Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 1:

﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾ (1)

The Surah al-Baqarah begins with the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾. These letters are huruf muqatta'a (disjoined letters), and the meaning of "disjoined" is that each letter is pronounced on its own. This is because letters have names (asma') and designations (musammayat). When people speak, they pronounce the designation of the letter and not its name. So when you say "kataba" (he wrote), you pronounce the designations of the letters. If you want to pronounce their names, you say "kaf, ta', ba'." The names of the letters can only be pronounced by someone who has learned and studied, whereas one who has not learned may pronounce the designations of the letters but does not pronounce their names. Perhaps this is the first thing that draws our attention. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was unlettered (ummi), who could neither read nor write, and therefore he knew nothing of the names of the letters. So when he came and pronounced the names of the letters, this is a miracle from Allah the Exalted, that this Qur'an was revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ). Had the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) studied and learned, it would have been an ordinary thing for him to pronounce the names of the letters. But come to any unlettered person who has not learned: he can pronounce the designations of the letters, saying "al-kitab" and "kub" and so on. But if you ask him to pronounce the names of the letters, he cannot tell you that the word kitab is made up of the letters kaf, ta', alif and ba'. These letters are indicative of the truthfulness of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in conveying from his Lord, and that this Qur'an is revealed by Allah the Exalted.

We find, in the openings of surahs that begin with the names of letters, that the letters are pronounced by their names, and you find the same word in another verse pronounced by its designations. So "Alif Lam Mim" at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah you pronounce by the names of the letters: alif, lam, mim. Whereas you pronounce them by the designations of the letters in the explanation of the surah in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ (Surah al-Sharh).

And in Surah al-Fil in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ (Surah al-Fil).

What made the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pronounce "Alif Lam Mim" in Surah al-Baqarah by the names of the letters, while pronouncing it in the two surahs al-Sharh and al-Fil by the designations of the letters? It must be that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) heard it from Allah just as Jibril (peace be upon him) conveyed it to him in this manner. Thus the Qur'an is originally oral transmission (sama'); you may not recite it except after you have heard it, so that you know that this one is read "alif lam mim" and the second is read "alim," even though the writing is the same in both. Therefore you must listen to a jurist (faqih) who recites the Qur'an before you recite it. What tires people is that they have not sat with a jurist, nor listened to a reciter, and then they want to read the Qur'an like any book. We say: no. The Qur'an has a special distinction; it is not like any book you read, because sometimes it comes with the name of the letter and sometimes with the designations of the letter. You cannot know this except by listening to a reciter who recites the Qur'an.

The Qur'an is always built on continuation (wasl) and not on pausing (waqf). If you read at the end of Surah Yunus, for example: ﴿wa huwa khayr al-hakimin﴾ ("and He is the best of judges"), you will not find a sukun on the nun, but a fatha, joined to the saying of Allah the Exalted, "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim." Had it not been joined, you would find a sukun on it.

So all the verses of the Noble Qur'an are built on continuation, except the openings of surahs consisting of letters, which are built on pausing. So you do not read at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah "alim" with a damma on the mim; rather you read alif with a sukun, lam with a sukun, and mim with a sukun. So each letter stands alone with a pause, even though pausing does not occur at the end of surahs or anywhere in the whole Noble Qur'an.

There are surahs in the Noble Qur'an that begin with a single letter, such as the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Sad. By the Qur'an, possessor of reminder﴾ (Surah Sad).

﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe﴾ (Surah al-Qalam).

We notice that the letter is not an independent verse, whereas "Alif Lam Mim" in Surah al-Baqarah is an independent verse, and "Ha Mim" and "'Ayn Sin Qaf" are independent verses, even though they are a expression of disjoined letters. There are surahs that begin with a verse of five letters, such as "Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad" in Surah Maryam. There are surahs that begin with four letters, such as "Alif Lam Mim Sad" in Surah al-A'raf. There are surahs that begin with four letters that are not an independent verse, such as "Alif Lam Mim Ra" in Surah al-Ra'd, joined to what follows it. Whereas you find a surah beginning with two letters that is an independent verse, such as "Ya Sin" in Surah Ya Sin, and "Ha Mim" in Surah Ghafir and Fussilat, and "Ta Sin" in Surah al-Naml. All of these are not joined to the verse that follows them. This shows us that the letters at the openings of surahs do not follow a fixed rule.

"Alif Lam Mim" consists of three letters, and you find it in six surahs as an independent verse: it is a verse in al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, al-'Ankabut, al-Rum, al-Sajdah and Luqman. "Alif Lam Ra" is three letters but not an independent verse; rather it is part of the verse in four surahs: Yunus, Yusuf, Hud and Ibrahim. And "Alif Lam Mim Sad," of four letters, is an independent verse in Surah al-A'raf, while "Alif Lam Mim Ra," of four letters, is not an independent verse in Surah al-Ra'd. So the matter is not a law applied generally, but a particularity in each of the letters.

If you ask what is the meaning of these letters, we say that the question is in its origin mistaken, because a letter is not asked about its meaning in the language unless it is a particle of meaning (harf ma'na). Letters are of two kinds: harf mabna (a letter of construction) and harf ma'na (a letter of meaning). The harf mabna has no meaning except to indicate a sound only. As for the particles of meaning, they are such as fi (in), min (from) and 'ala (upon). "Fi" indicates place (zarfiyyah), "min" indicates the starting point (ibtida'), "ila" indicates the endpoint (intiha'), and "'ala" indicates elevation (isti'la'). These are all particles of meaning.

Since the letters at the beginnings of surahs in the Noble Qur'an have departed from the rule of continuation, because they are built on sukun, there must be a wisdom in that. First, so that we know the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites a letter from the Book of Allah, he has for it a good deed, and the good deed is worth ten like it. I do not say that Alif Lam Mim is a letter, but Alif is a letter, Lam is a letter, and Mim is a letter." (1)

That is why they are mentioned in the Qur'an as independent letters, so that we know, as we worship by reciting the Noble Qur'an, that we take a good deed for every letter. If we recite "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim," we have a good deed for the ba', a good deed for the sin, and a good deed for the mim, so there are three good deeds for one word of the Noble Qur'an. And a good deed is worth ten like it. When we recite "Alif Lam Mim" and do not understand its meaning, we know that the reward of the Qur'an is for every letter we recite, whether we understand it or not. Allah the Exalted may place in these letters that we do not understand some of His secrets, a reward and recompense that we do not know.

He desires us, by reciting them, to obtain this reward.

The Noble Qur'an is not a miracle in eloquence alone, but contains a miracle in everything the human mind can approach. Every thinker who reflects on the words of Allah finds a miracle in the Noble Qur'an. The one who studied rhetoric saw the rhetorical miracle; the one who learned medicine found a medical miracle in the Noble Qur'an; the botanist saw a miracle in the verses of the Noble Qur'an, and likewise the astronomer.

If one of us wishes to know the meaning of these letters, we should not take them according to the measure of our humanity, but according to the measure of what Allah intends by them. Our abilities vary and our understandings are limited. Each of us possesses a key of understanding, each according to his knowledge. This is a simple key that opens once; another turns twice; another turns three times, and so on. But whoever has knowledge possesses all the keys, or possesses the key that opens all doors.

We should not exert our minds to understand these letters. The lives of people require of us at times that we set words that have no meaning for others, though they represent necessary things for us, exactly like the password that armies use, which has no meaning if you hear it, but for the one who set it, its price is life or death. So take the words of Allah that you understand by their meanings, and take the letters that you do not understand by what Allah intends by them. Allah the Exalted willed that their meaning remain in the unseen with Him.

The Noble Qur'an is not taken in one uniform pattern, so that we may be alert when we recite or write it. Thus, for example, you find "Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim" written without an alif between the ba' and the sin. Yet sometimes you find it written with an alif, in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾ (Surah al-'Alaq).

And the word "tabaraka" is sometimes written with an alif and sometimes without the alif. Had the matter been monotony in the writing of the Qur'an, it would all have come in one system. But it came in this manner so that the writing of the Qur'an and its wording would be a miracle.

We say to those who ask about the wisdom in the beginning of some surahs with letters: there is a wisdom with Allah for that, whether we understand it or not. The Qur'an was revealed to an Arab nation in which there were both believers and disbelievers. Yet we have not heard anyone criticise the letters with which the surahs begin. This is evidence that they understood them by their Arabic faculties. Had they not understood them, they would have criticised them.

I advise whoever reads the Noble Qur'an for worship not to occupy himself with thinking about the meaning. As for the one who reads the Qur'an to derive rulings from it, let him stop at the wording and the meaning. If you read the Qur'an for worship, read it with the secret of Allah in it. If you sat searching for the meaning, you would have confined the meaning of the Noble Qur'an to your own information, and you would have taken the meaning deficient, with the deficiency of human thought. But read the Qur'an with the secret of Allah in it.

If we searched the meaning of every word in the Noble Qur'an, we would have excluded from reading the Qur'an the unlettered and everyone who has not studied the Arabic language in depth. Yet you find an unlettered person who has not read a single word, and yet he memorises the whole Qur'an. If you ask how, we say to you: by the secret of Allah in it.

Speech is a means of conveying and understanding between the speaker and the listener. The speaker is the one who holds the initiative, and the listener is surprised by the speech, because he does not know in advance what the speaker will say. The listener's mind may be occupied with something else, so he does not take in the first words. That is why you may alert him with letters or sounds that have no purpose except to draw attention to the speech that will come after them.

If we do not understand these letters, the means of understanding and the miracles in the Noble Qur'an are endless, because the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and speech is an attribute of the speaker. That is why no human understanding can reach the ultimate limit of the meanings of the Noble Qur'an; it can only draw near to them, because the speech of Allah is one of His attributes, and an attribute in which there is perfection without end.

If you say that you have known every meaning of the Noble Qur'an, you have confined the meaning of the speech of Allah to your own knowledge. That is why these letters came as a miracle for you, so that you know you cannot delimit the meanings of the Qur'an by your knowledge.

A person's failure to understand things does not prevent him from benefiting from them. The villager, for example, benefits from electricity and television and what is broadcast by satellite, while he knows nothing about any of them. So why should Allah the Blessed and Exalted not have given us these letters, from which we take their benefit and derive benefit from their secrets, and through which Allah bestows upon us the grace He has deposited in them, whether the believing servant understands the meaning of these letters or not?

The giving of Allah the Exalted and His wisdom is beyond the capacity of human understanding. If a person were to let his thought and reflections hover around the meanings of these letters, he would find in them something new every day. Scholars have delved much into the research, and every scholar took from them according to the clarity of his mind, and none of the scholars claims that this is the truth intended by these letters; rather each of them says, "And Allah knows best what He intends." That is why you find a scholar saying that (Alif Lam Ra), (Ha Mim) and (Nun), which are letters at the openings of surahs, form the name al-Rahman. We say that this cannot represent a general understanding of the letters that begin some surahs of the Qur'an. But what tires or exhausts you in trying to find meanings for these letters?

If Allah the Exalted, who sent down the Qur'an, wanted us to understand their meanings, He would have stated them in a direct meaning, or clarified the meaning for us. For example, one of the scholars says...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 2:

﴿That is the Book; there is no doubt in it; a guidance for the God-conscious (muttaqun).﴾

In the second verse of Surat al-Baqara, Allah the Glorified and Exalted describes the Noble Qur'an as "the Book" (al-kitab). The word "Qur'an" means that it is recited, and the word "Kitab" means that it is not preserved only in the breasts (memorization) but is also written down in lines, and remains preserved until the Day of Resurrection. The description of it as "the Book" distinguishes it from all the books of this world, and distinguishes it from all the heavenly scriptures that were revealed before it. The Qur'an is the Book that gathers all the rulings of heaven, from the beginning of the messages until the Day of Resurrection. This is an affirmation of the elevated status of the Qur'an, its uniqueness, its heavenly origin, and a proof of the oneness of the Creator. From the dawn of history, scriptures carrying the curriculum of heaven were revealed to the earlier nations, but every book and every message that was sent down was time-bound, in its time and its place, performing its mission for a specific period and towards specific people.

The message of Nuh (Noah), peace be upon him, was for his people; likewise Ibrahim (Abraham), Lut (Lot), Shu'ayb (Jethro) and Salih, peace be upon them... All these were messages that had a limited time, exercising their mission in life, until the Book came, which is the Noble Qur'an, gathering the curriculum of Allah the Glorified and Exalted. Therefore, in the heavenly scriptures that were revealed before the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), good tidings were given that there would come a Messenger who would bear the final message to the world, and that all who believe in the curriculum of heaven must follow him. In this regard, the Truthful Lord, the Glorified and Exalted, says:

﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ (part of verse 157, Surat al-A'raf).

The Qur'an is the Book, because no distortion or alteration can reach it. The previous heavenly messages were entrusted by Allah to mankind, so they forgot some of it; and what they did not forget they distorted, and they added to it from the words of men, attributing to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, what they attributed unjustly and falsely. But the Noble Qur'an is preserved by the Supreme Creator, in confirmation of His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ (Surat al-Hijr).

The meaning of that is that no person should doubt this Book, because all that is in it of the curriculum of Allah has been preserved from the moment of its revelation until the Hour arrives, by the power of Allah the Glorified and Exalted.

The Majestic Lord says: ﴿There is no doubt in it, a guidance for the God-conscious.﴾

The miraculous quality (i'jaz) present in the Noble Qur'an lies in its style, in its truths, in its verses, in what it has related to us of the stories of the earlier prophets, in what it has corrected of the Torah and the Gospel, and in the knowledge it has brought which mankind did not know and still does not know until now. All of that makes the Qur'an free of doubt, because even if mankind and the jinn were gathered together, they could not produce one verse of the verses of the Qur'an. Therefore, whenever we contemplate the Qur'an and its style, we find that it is truly free of doubt, because no one can produce a verse, let alone the Qur'an.

This Book has risen above all books and above the perceptions of men; it clarifies the signs of the universe and the signs of the curriculum, and in every age it has miracles. The word "Book" with which Allah the Glorified and Exalted described the Qur'an, distinguishing it from all previous books, draws our attention to many meanings, which define for us some of the fundamentals of the curriculum that this Book came to convey to us. The first of these fundamentals is that the revelation of this Book necessitates praise of Allah the Glorified and Exalted. Read in Surat al-Kahf:

﴿Praise be to Allah, who revealed to His servant the Book and did not make therein any deviance. [He made it] straight, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward﴾ (Surat al-Kahf).

Allah the Glorified and Exalted draws attention to the fact that His sending down the Qur'an upon His Messenger (ﷺ) necessitates praise from all of mankind, because in it is the curriculum of heaven, in it is the mercy of Allah to His servants, in it is the good tidings of Paradise and the path to it, and in it is the warning against the Fire and what leads to it. This warning or admonition is a mercy from Allah the Exalted to His creation, because if He had not warned them, they would have done what necessitates punishment and would have made them abide in painful torment. But the Book that came to draw their attention to what angers Allah, so that they might avoid it, came with a mercy that necessitates praise, because it has shown us all the way to salvation from the Fire. Had Allah the Glorified and Exalted not sent down the Book, people would not have known the curriculum that leads them to Paradise, and none of them would have deserved the pleasure of Allah and His bounty in the Hereafter.

In Surat al-Kahf we find another affirmation: that the Book of Allah, which is the Noble Qur'an, no human being will be able to change even a single word of it. Read the saying of the Majestic Lord:

﴿And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord; there is no changer of His words, and you will not find other than Him a refuge﴾ (Surat al-Kahf).

Allah the Glorified and Exalted shows us that this Book came for the benefit of people and for the benefit of the servants, and that Allah does not need His creation. He is capable of compelling whom He wills to obedience, and it is not possible for any of Allah's creation to step outside the will of Allah in the universe of Allah. Read His saying, the Glorified and Exalted:

﴿Ta, Sin, Mim. These are the verses of the clear Book. Perhaps you would kill yourself [with grief] that they will not be believers. If We willed, We could send down upon them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain humbly subjected to it﴾ (Surat al-Shu'ara').

Allah the Glorified and Exalted brings the oath which draws our attention to the fact that every word in the Qur'an is from Allah, as Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, conveyed it to Muhammad (ﷺ), in His saying, the Glorified:

﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars. And indeed, it is an oath, if you only knew, that is great. Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an, in a Book well-protected, which none touches except the purified. A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'a).

Then the Truthful Lord draws our attention to that Book which is a curriculum for man on the earth. After He, the Majestic, made clear to us, beyond any room for doubt, that the Book is sent down from Him, and that it corrects the earlier books such as the Torah and the Gospel, which Allah had entrusted to mankind, and they distorted and altered them, this distortion nullified the mission of the divine curriculum with respect to these books. So came the Book to which no distortion or alteration could reach, to remain a curriculum from Allah until the Hour arrives. The first thing this Book brought is the faith at its summit: that there is no god but Allah, the One, the Unique. Allah the Glorified and Exalted says:

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. He has sent down upon you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming what was before it; and He revealed the Torah and the Gospel﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran).

Thus we know that the Book was sent down to affirm for us that Allah is One, the Unique, with no partner, and that the Qur'an comprises all that the heavenly laws contained of Torah, Gospel, and other books.

The Qur'an was sent down to distinguish between the truth that the earlier books brought and the falsehood that those entrusted with them added.

Then the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, defines for us our duty: that this Book is required to be conveyed to all people. Read His saying, the Glorified:

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad. A Book revealed to you, so let there be no discomfort in your breast concerning it, that you may warn thereby and as a reminder for the believers﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

The address here is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and every address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the Noble Qur'an includes an address to his entire community. The Messenger (ﷺ) was charged with conveying the Book to people, and we are charged with following the same method and conveying what came in the Qur'an to people, so that the reckoning will be just, and so that it may be said that they had conveyed the curriculum of Allah, and then they disbelieved in it or abandoned it. Thus conveying the Book is one of the fundamental duties which Allah the Glorified and Exalted has specified with respect to the Qur'an.

The Book contains a refutation of the arguments and falsehoods of the disbelievers. Read the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the wise Book. Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man among them, [saying], "Warn the people and give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a true standing with their Lord"? The disbelievers said, "Indeed, this is clearly a magician"﴾ (Surat Yunus).

In these noble verses, Allah the Glorified and Exalted draws our attention to two truths. The first truth is that the disbelievers take the humanity of the Messenger as an argument that this Book is not from Allah. The answer was: all the earlier Messengers were human beings, so what is the wonder that Muhammad (ﷺ) should be a human Messenger? The second point is that this Qur'an is written with the very letters that Allah created for us to write with, and yet the Noble Qur'an was sent down using these letters that all people know, being miraculous in that neither mankind nor the jinn, gathered together, can produce a single chapter of it. Then the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted, draws our attention to another point: that this Book is perfect in its verses, and that Allah then made it clear to His servants. Read His saying, the Majestic, in Surat Hud:

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses have been perfected and then presented in detail from before One who is All-Wise and Acquainted, [saying], "Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings"﴾ (Surat Hud).

These are some of the verses of the Noble Qur'an in which Allah the Glorified and Exalted wanted to draw our attention to the meaning of "the Book." Its verses are from Allah, the Wise, the Acquainted, and every verse in it is a miracle challenging mankind and the jinn. This Book must be conveyed to all people; the Book warns them not to worship anyone but Allah, so that the reckoning will be just in the Hereafter. Whoever is warned and obeys will have Paradise, and whoever disobeys will have the Fire, we seek refuge in Allah.

Then Allah draws our attention to the fact that this Book contains the stories of the earlier prophets from Adam, peace be upon him. The Majestic Lord says:

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an so that you might understand. We relate to you the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an, although you were before it among the unaware﴾ (Surat Yusuf).

Thus we find that the Noble Qur'an came to relate to us the best of stories concerning the earlier prophets and the events that occurred in the past. The Qur'an did not bring these stories for entertainment or amusement, but brought them for admonition and as a lesson of faith, because the Qur'anic story recurs in every time and place. Pharaoh is every ruler who transgressed in the land and set himself up as a god; Qarun is everyone whom Allah blessed and who attributed the blessing to himself, grew arrogant and disobeyed Allah; the story of Yusuf is the story of every set of brothers who harbored hatred toward a brother of theirs and conspired against him; and the People of the Cave are every group of youths who believed in their Lord, so that Allah spread for them of His mercy in this world and the Hereafter. There is one exception, the story of Maryam and 'Isa, peace be upon them both, which is a miracle that will not be repeated, and therefore Allah the Glorified and Exalted named its protagonists: He said "Isa ibn Maryam" and He said "Maryam bint 'Imran."

The Book which Allah the Glorified and Exalted sent down contains a draw of attention to the signs of Allah in His universe. Read His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Ra. These are the verses of the Book; and that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most of the people do not believe. Allah is He who raised the heavens without pillars that you see; then He istawa' (established Himself) above the Throne and subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term. He arranges the affair and details the signs that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord﴾ (Surat al-Ra'd).

Thus Allah has explained to us in the Book His signs in the universe and drawn our attention to them. The sky is raised without pillars that we see; the sun and the moon are subjected to serve man; and all these are signs that none of the creation of Allah can claim for himself or for another. There is no one, even on the Day of Resurrection, who can claim that he raised the sky without pillars, or that he created the sun and the moon and subjected them to serve man. If people reflected upon the signs of the universe they would believe, but they are heedless of these signs. Then the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted, defines the mission of this Book and how it is a mercy to all people, saying, the Majestic:

{Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book which We have sent down to you that you may bring mankind out of darkness into light, by the permission of their Lord, to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy. Allah — to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And woe to the disbelievers}

﴿Those who believe in the unseen (al-ghayb), establish the prayer, and spend from what We have provided for them.﴾ (3)

After Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made clear to us that this Book, the noble Qur'an, is ﴿guidance for the God-conscious﴾, meaning that it contains the method and the path for anyone who wants to place between himself and the anger of Allah a shield (wiqaya), He wished to make us know the attributes of these God-conscious (muttaqun) and who they are. The first attribute is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe in the unseen﴾.

What is the unseen (al-ghayb) that Allah made the first rank of guidance and of protection from the Fire and from the anger of Allah?

The unseen is everything that is absent from the objects of the senses. Sensible things, which we see and touch, no one disputes. For this reason it is said, "There is no 'where' with the eye," because what you see requires no further proof. But the unseen is not grasped by the senses; it is grasped by other than them.

As evidence for the precision of this definition, they have said that there are five apparent senses: hearing, sight, smell, taste and touch. But there are things perceived by other than these senses.

Let us suppose that in front of us are two suitcases, identical in shape and size. Can you, by your apparent senses, perceive which of them is heavier than the other? Can the five senses tell you which of the two suitcases is heavier? No. You must lift one of them, then lift the other, in order to know which is heavier.

By what did you perceive this weight? By the sense of muscular effort (hassat al-'adal). Because your muscles were strained when you lifted one of the two suitcases, and were not strained when you lifted the second. So you knew precisely which was heavier. Do not say "by touch," for if you touched one and then touched the other, you would not know which was heavier. So there is a sense of muscular effort by which you measure the weight of things.

Suppose you enter a cloth shop, and in front of you are two kinds of one fabric, but one of them is thinner than the other. As soon as you place the two cloths between your fingers, you perceive that one is fine and the other thicker. By what sense did you perceive this? Not by the sense of touch, but by the sense of discernment (hassat al-bayyina), whose judgment never errs.

And when you feel hungry, by what sense did you perceive that you are hungry? Not by the apparent senses. Likewise when you are thirsty: what is the sense by which you perceived that you need water? And when you are asleep, what is the faculty that wakes you from sleep? No one knows.

So there are faculties within the soul, which are the apparent senses, and there are perceptions within the soul, which are senses that none knows except their Creator. Therefore, when scholars come to set a definition of the human soul, we say to them: What do you know of this soul? You know only an outward aspect of the life of this world. But there are things within the soul that you do not know. There are perceptions of which a person knows nothing, and they are many and varied. Therefore whoever says that what is not perceived by the apparent human senses is unseen is mistaken, because there are many faculties and perceptions operating without our knowledge.

If a student is given an engineering exercise, solves it and arrives at the answer, do we say that he knew something unseen? Because the solution was unseen to him and then he reached it? No. Because there were premises and laws that led him to this solution. The unseen has no premises and no laws leading to it. And when the meteorological office announces that tomorrow will be a very windy rainy day, have you then known the unseen? No. Because they took premises and reached conclusions by them, and this is not unseen.

And if one of the charlatans comes and tells you that what was stolen from you is with so-and-so, has he known the unseen? No. Because it is a condition of the unseen that it not be known to someone like you, whereas what was stolen from you is known to someone like you. The thief and the one to whom the stolen goods were sold know who stole and what happened. The police, by means of premises, fingerprints and investigation, can reach the thief and the one who bought the stolen goods. And if a charlatan of those who enlist the jinn comes to you, and it is known that the jinn are hidden from us and distinguished by lightness and swiftness of movement, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says of Satan: ﴿Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you cannot see them﴾ (Al-A'raf 7:27).

It may be that this one enlisted from the jinn has seen something, or moved from one place to another, and so knows something you do not know. This is not unseen, because you were ignorant of it, but someone else knows it by the laws that Allah created for him. And the scientists who discover the secrets of the universe: is it said that they have been granted knowledge of the unseen? No. Because these scientists discovered an existing thing that has premises, and so they reached these results; it is not unseen.

But what is the unseen?

It is that which has no premises and to which no knowledge can attain, of any of Allah's creatures, not even the angels. Read the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, when He taught Adam the names, all of them, and presented them to the angels. He, exalted be His majesty, said:

﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them; then He presented them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful." (31) They said, "Glory be to You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the Knowing, the Wise." (32) He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." And when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing?" (33)﴾ (Al-Baqara 2:31–33).

The jinn too do not know the unseen. For this reason, when Solomon, peace be upon him, died, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had subjected the jinn to him, the jinn did not learn of his death until a creature of the earth ate his staff. Read His saying, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿So when We decreed for him death, nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. And when he fell, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating punishment.﴾ (Saba' 34:14).

So the unseen is that which none knows except Allah, glorified and exalted is He. Read the words of the Truth, exalted be His majesty:

﴿Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, (26) except to one whom He has approved of among messengers. Indeed, He sends before him and behind him guards.﴾ (Al-Jinn 72:26–27).

Thus the messengers do not know the unseen. But Allah, glorified and exalted is He, informs them of whatever unseen He wills, and this is a miracle for them and for those who follow them.

The summit of the unseen is faith in Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and faith in His angels, His books, His messengers, and faith in the Last Day. All these are unseen matters. When Allah, blessed and exalted is He, informs us of His angels, and we do not see them, we say: since Allah has informed us of them, we believe in their existence. And if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, informs us of the Last Day, then since Allah has informed us, we believe in the Last Day, because the One who informed us is Allah, exalted be His majesty. I believed in Him as God, and I used in this faith the rational proof that led me to believe that this universe has a god and a creator. What comes to me of Allah is the ground (haythiyya) of faith in Him, that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who says.

We must know that the existence of a thing is entirely different from the perception of that thing. You have a soul in your body that gives you life. Have you seen it? Have you heard it? Have you tasted it? Have you smelled it? Have you touched it? The answer, of course, is no. By which of the means of perception do you know that you have a soul in your body? By its effect in giving life to the body.

So you have known the soul by its effect, and the soul is a creature of Allah. How, then, do you wish, while you are unable to perceive a creature within your body and self, which is the soul, by its effects, to perceive Allah, glorified and exalted is He, by your senses?

When we believe in the supreme unseen, which is Allah, exalted be His majesty, we must believe in everything He informs us about, even if we do not see it. And Allah, blessed and exalted is He, out of mercy toward our minds, willed to bring the matter of the unseen closer to us, so He gave us, from the material universe, proofs that the existence of a thing and the perception of that existence are two entirely separate matters.

For example, germs exist in the universe, performing their function since the beginning of creation. People used to observe the effects of diseases on their bodies, such as rising temperature, fever and other things, and they did not know the cause. Then when science advanced, and Allah permitted His creatures to see the existence of germs, He made minds able to discover the microscope, which gives us a magnified image, because the visual power of the eye is too weak to perceive these minute creatures. When science discovered the microscope, we were able to see these germs, and know that they have a life cycle and reproduction, and other things that Allah reveals to us of knowledge as time advances.

Our inability to see a thing does not mean that it does not exist. Rather, the instrument of perception, which is sight, is incapable of seeing it, because it is extremely small. If you bring the microscope, this microbe is enlarged for you so that it enters the range of your means of sight, which is the eye. Our seeing germs and microbes is not evidence that they were created the moment we saw them; rather, they exist performing their function, whether we see them or not.

If someone spoke to us of microbes and germs before we saw them with our own eyes, would we have believed him? And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, left some of His creatures unable, in their time, to perceive some realities of the universe, so that man would advance and perceive them afterward, and it was supposed that his faith would increase when he perceived them, and that creatures would know by material evidence that what is unseen to them exists even though we do not see it.

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, has given us from His signs in the universe what makes us perceive that this universe has a creator. The sun, the moon, the stars, the earth, humans, animals and inanimate things: no one can claim to have created them, and no one can claim to have created himself or others. This universe, with this precise order, cannot have come into being by chance, because chance is events that are unarranged or unorganized. And if this universe had come into being by chance, the sun, the moon, the stars and the earth would have collided, and the night and day would have been thrown into disorder.

Rather, every sign in the universe confirms to us that there is a tremendous power that created, ordered and originated. So if a messenger comes to us informing us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who created this universe, we must believe him.

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿and establish the prayer﴾. The prayer is the continuation of allegiance of servitude to the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, and it never lapses from a person. A person prays standing; if he cannot, he prays sitting; if he cannot, he prays lying down. The prayer does not lapse from a person from the time of his obligation until the time of his death, five times every day.

Blessed and exalted is the Truth, who says: ﴿and from what We have provided for them they spend﴾. When we speak of provision, many people think that provision is wealth. We say: no. Provision is whatever one benefits from. Strength is provision, knowledge is provision, wisdom is provision, humility is provision, and everything in which there is movement of life is provision. If you do not have money to spend from, you have health with which to work to obtain money, and you give it in charity to the helpless and the sick. If you have forbearance, you spend it by protecting the fool from behaviours that may harm society and harm you. If you have knowledge, you spend it by teaching the ignorant. Thus we see that ﴿and from what We have provided for them they spend﴾ encompasses the entire movement of life.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 4:

﴿And those who believe in what has been revealed to you, and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain.﴾

The Almighty, glorified and exalted is He, in this noble verse gives us other attributes of the believers. After informing us that among the attributes of the believers are faith in the unseen, the establishment of prayer, and spending from what Allah has provided for them, He now moves on to other attributes.

These believers are: ﴿those who believe in what has been revealed to you﴾, that is, in the Noble Qur'an which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has sent down. And [﴿what was revealed before you﴾], and this phrase does not appear in the description of the believers except in the Noble Qur'an. This is because when Islam came, it had to confront two categories of people. The first category is the disbelievers, who do not believe in Allah or in any messenger who conveys from Allah. And there was another category of people: the People of the Book, who believe in Allah and believe in messengers from Allah and books from Allah.

Islam confronted both categories, because the People of the Book may have thought that they were already connected to Allah: they believe in Him, they receive books from Him, and they follow messengers, and this, in their view, is sufficient. We say: No. Islam came so that the disbeliever would believe in Him, and the People of the Book would believe in Him, and so that the religion would be entirely for Allah. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, in the books He sent down, informed of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), of his name and his attributes, and He asked the People of the Book who would come to recognise his message (ﷺ) to believe in him.

Allah, majestic in His majesty, gave the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the People of the Book, to the extent that they used to recognise him as they recognise their own sons. Indeed, their knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), of his time and of his attributes was certain knowledge. And the Jews of Madina used to say to the disbelievers: "The time of a Messenger is near; we will believe in him and kill you with the killing of 'Ad and Iram." But when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, they were the first to fight him and deny his prophethood. So the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) are present in the Torah and the Gospel. Therefore the People of the Book used to warn the disbelievers that they would believe in the new Messenger and, through him, rule over the Arabs. And read the words of the Truthful, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, and previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:89)

That is, the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) was not a surprise to the People of the Book; rather, they were awaiting it. They used to affirm that they would believe in it, as their books commanded them. But they refused to believe and denied the message when its time came.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿and of the Hereafter they are certain.﴾ We notice here that the phrase "and of the Hereafter" has come, because if you browse the Torah, which is the book of the Jews, or read the Talmud, you will find nothing about the Last Day. They took only the material matter from their books. And Allah, blessed and exalted is He, affirmed belief in the Last Day so that those who say "we believe in Allah, His books and His messengers" and do not turn to the Last Day would be known as not being believers. Had this attribute not come in the Noble Qur'an, they might have said that Islam agrees with what we have. But Allah, majestic in His majesty, wants to portray faith in its perfect form: that belief in Allah is the summit at the beginning, and belief in the Last Day is the summit at the end. Whoever does not believe in the Hereafter, and that he will meet Allah and be called to account by Him, and that there is a Paradise in which the believer is blessed and a Fire in which the disbeliever is punished, his faith will be deficient, and he will have drawn close to the disbeliever who made this world his goal and his aim.

The believer follows the way of Allah in this world in order to deserve the bounty of Allah in the Hereafter. Had the Hereafter not existed, the disbeliever would have had more share of life than the believer, because he took from this world what he desired and did not restrict himself to any way, but let his desires run free. Whereas the believer restricted his movement in life according to the way of Allah and exerted himself for that. Then both die, and there is nothing after that. So the disbeliever would be the winner of the pleasures and desires of this world, while the believer would take nothing, and the matter here would not be consistent with the question of faith. Therefore belief in Allah is the summit of faith at the beginning, and belief in the Hereafter is the summit of faith at the end.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 5:

﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.﴾ (2:5)

The words of Allah, "Those" (ulā'ika), point to those upon whom all the qualities that Allah, glory be to Him, describes in the two preceding verses apply. Those upon whom these qualities apply have reached guidance (hudā), that is, the path leading to faith. They have reached success (falāḥ), which is the goal of faith.

And the words of Allah, "Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful," include everyone.

But why did Allah, blessed and exalted, use "ulā'ika" twice? That is from the eloquence of the Noble Qur'an. And why did He join the two statements with one another? So that we know that in Islam there are not two faiths, but one faith, which results in one reward. Its means is guidance (hudā), and its end is success (falāḥ).

If you look at the obligations (takālīf), which are the guidance that leads to the goal, you find that Allah, glory be to Him, has elevated the one who is guided by the guidance. So that we know that guidance did not come to restrict your movement in life and to humiliate you, but came to raise you up.

Superficial people believe that guidance restricts a person's movement in life and prevents him from fulfilling his immediate desires. But in reality guidance raises a person, protects him from harm, from the anger of Allah, and from corrupting society, of which he would be the first to suffer. Therefore the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿upon guidance﴾.

"Upon" ('alā) indicates elevation. If you say, "You are upon the horse," you are above it. It is as if the one who is guided, when he binds himself to the method, is not humiliated, but rises up through guidance, and guidance takes him from good to good. This is the opposite of misguidance, which takes a person downward.

For this reason, when you read in the Noble Qur'an the words of Allah, the Exalted:

﴿And indeed, either we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ (part of verse 24, Surat Saba')

you see that what indicates height and elevation is used for guidance, and what indicates lowness and descent is used for error. The elevation is in guidance because the method restricts the movement of your life as an honour to you, for your loftiness and the exaltedness of your station, in that you do not take legislation from a human being, nor take movement from your own self, but you are raised so that you receive from Allah, glory be to Him. This is a great elevation. But regarding error, He said: ﴿in error﴾. And "in" (fī) indicates an enveloping containment. This is what Allah, glory be to Him, described in another verse, with His words, majestic is His majesty:

﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and his sin has encompassed him, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ (2:81)

"His sin has encompassed him", meaning he cannot escape from it, because he is enveloped in error. And as long as sin encompasses him, he finds no outlet, because it governs him. And as long as it governs him, he can never reach guidance at all. So when the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful﴾, He chose a word that has a worldly connotation that brings the meaning close to the hearer.

What is falāḥ? The general meaning is winning, and the mufliḥ is the winner. The meaning of the noble verse is: "those are the winners." And He said: ﴿they are the successful﴾, because falāḥ is derived from splitting the earth for sowing. From it the farmer (fallāḥ), whose trait is splitting the earth and casting seeds into it, is named.

The Truth, glory be to Him, used this word in relation to the Hereafter because He wants to bring us the thing together with its proof. There is a difference between a matter unseen by us that we do not know, and an unseen matter that is inferred from something witnessed.

Religion restricts your freedom in life in that you do or do not do. The method of Allah came to tell you: do such-and-such, and do not do such-and-such. Many people think that this is a restriction on the believer's movement in life and a burden upon him, because it has taken from him the freedom of his movement and restricted it.

When Allah, blessed and exalted, says to you, "Do not do," the superficial understand that He has constricted what you want to do. And when He says to you, "Do," they understand that He has constricted you in something you do not want to do. For example: when He asks you for zakat. In its outward appearance zakat is a decrease of wealth, though in its reality it is blessing and growth. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Charity does not decrease wealth; Allah does not increase a servant who pardons except in honour; and no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him." (1)

So when the Truth, glory be to Him, restricts your movement in life, do not think that this is a constriction upon you; rather, it is for your benefit. Because He has not commanded you alone, but the command is for people all together when He, majestic in majesty, says: "Do not steal." He has said it to all people, and therefore you are the winner. Because He restricted you, as an individual, from stealing from others, and He restricted millions of people from stealing from you. So Allah has not constricted you; rather He has protected your wealth from all people. He restricted you, as one person, from stealing from the property of others, and restricted millions of people from stealing from your property. So who is the winner? You, of course.

And His words, ﴿those are the successful﴾: "al-mufliḥūn" is from the root f-l-ḥ. If the land is barren, when we split it and sow it, it gives a great harvest. This process we have taken from father to grandfather. The land, when split and sown, gives abundant produce. And if this process has been taken from father to grandfather, the question arises: who taught Adam sowing and planting? We say: Allah, glory be to Him, taught him, as He taught him the names, and as He taught him what would enable him to undertake his task on earth.

The Truth, majestic is He, would not leave Adam in his life on earth without teaching him what would guarantee the continuation of his life and the life of his offspring. He taught him at least beginnings. Then these beginnings developed through what Allah revealed of His knowledge to His creation. After that, the earlier centuries came, and we were able to use modern, advanced machines that perform ploughing and sowing.

But the fixed truth that has not changed since the beginning of the universe and will not change until its end is that the task of man is to plough, place the seed in the earth, and water it. As for the growth of the crop itself, man has no part in it. Likewise, the fruit it produces is not the work of man. Allah, blessed and exalted, has alerted us to this truth so that we do not become deluded by our movement in life and say that we are the ones who sow. Read the Truth's words, majestic is He, in Surat al-Waqi'a:

﴿Have you considered what you plough? Is it you who grow it, or are We the growers? Were We to will, We would make it into debris, and you would remain astonished, saying, "Indeed, we are burdened with debt. Rather, we have been deprived."﴾ (56:63-67)

Thus the task of farming on the land has remained confined to ploughing, watering and sowing. When you cast the grain into the earth, Allah creates within it the nourishment that suffices it until it can take its nourishment from the earth. If you take a grain and moisten it, you find that a stem and roots have sprouted from it. From where did this growth come? From the very composition of the grain. Allah, blessed and exalted, has decreed in every grain the nourishment that suffices it so that it can feed itself from the earth. In proportion to the amount of nourishment required, the size of the grain is determined. When you place it in the earth, it first begins to nourish itself, so that a stem and roots grow for it, and two leaves through which it breathes. You have no part in all of this, and no work of yours is involved. The grain begins to take its nourishment from earth and air, to grow until it becomes a great tree producing fruit of the same kind as the seed itself.

From here came the word (al-mufliḥūn), so that the Truth, majestic is He, may give us, from visible material matters, what helps our limited minds understand the unseen. He likens the obligation and its reward in the Hereafter to seeds and farming. First, because when you cast one seed into the earth, it gives you many seeds.

And the words of Allah, glory be to Him:

﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven ears; in every ear is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ (2:261)

If the earth, which is itself created by Allah, gives you many times over what you gave it, then how about the Creator? And how much reward does He multiply for you in obedience? This is the reason the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: "and those are the successful," so as to draw our attention to the root of farming, which is something present that we see and witness every day.

Just as the obligation takes things from you in order to multiply them for you, so the earth took from you a grain and did not give you back what it took, but gave you for one grain seven hundred grains. Thus we can arrive, through a visible thing, at an explanation of an unseen thing.

(1) Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi from Abu Hurayrah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 6:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾

After Allah, the Exalted, spoke about the believers, their attributes, their reward in the Hereafter, and the great good that awaits them, He wanted to give us the opposite picture, that of the disbelievers. He showed us that faith came to dominate everyone, bringing them good in this world and the next. Thus there must be an evil that faith combats. Were it not for the existence of this evil, would there be any need for faith? The believing person protects himself, his society and his world from the evils that disbelief brings.

The disbelievers are of two kinds. One kind disbelieved in Allah at first, then listened to the words of Allah, received them with his sound nature, responded and believed. The other kind profits from disbelief, from tyranny, from injustice, from consuming the rights of people, and other such things. This kind knows that if faith comes, it will strip them of worldly status and of gains they achieve through injustice and aggression.

So those who stand against faith are those who benefit from disbelief. But what about those who were disbelievers and received the religion of Allah properly?

These are the ones whose hearts may open up, and so they believe. Kufr (disbelief) literally means covering, concealing. The meaning of kafara (he disbelieved) is "satara" (he concealed). And "kafara billah" means he concealed the existence of Allah, glorified is His majesty. Whoever conceals must be concealing something that exists, because concealment is an accident upon existence. The original state of the universe is faith in Allah. Then the disbelievers came trying to conceal the existence of Allah. So the original state is faith, then heedlessness came upon people and they concealed the existence of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, so that they might remain in their authority, their control, their exploitation, or their dominance over other human beings.

The word kufr itself indicates that faith came first and then disbelief came after. How?

Because the first creation, Adam, whom Allah created with His own hands, breathed into him of His spirit, made the angels prostrate to him, and taught him all the names.

The angels' prostration and the teaching of the names was a visible matter concerning Adam, and disbelief did not exist at that time. It was expected that Adam, after he descended to the earth and settled in it, would teach his children the method of worshipping Allah, since he descended carrying the method of "do" and "do not do." And the children of Adam were to teach their children the method, and so on.

But with the passage of time, heedlessness set in, the notion that faith restricts people's movement in the universe. So everyone who wanted to subject his life to desire without restraint took the path of disbelief. The intelligent person, when he hears the word kufr, must be alert that its meaning is concealment of an existent that is necessarily existent. How can a person disbelieve and participate in concealing what exists? Therefore you find that the Exalted says:

﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life, then to Him you will be returned? He is the one who created for you whatever is on the earth, all of it. Then He turned to the heaven and made it seven heavens, and He is Knowing of all things.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

Thus this question comes, and the disbeliever has no answer! Because Allah is the One who created him and brought him into existence. None of us can claim that he created himself or created others. Existence itself is evidence for the matter of faith. Therefore the Blessed and Exalted asks them: how do you disbelieve in Allah and conceal the existence of the One who created you? Creation is a settled matter belonging to Allah, the Exalted, and no one can claim it. No one can claim that he created himself. Your being existent necessitates faith in Allah, the Exalted, who brought you into existence. It is the very essence of proof for Allah. When a person looks around and finds that everything in the universe is subjected to his service and things respond to him, he may, over time, think he has control over this universe. Therefore he lives with the notion of the power of causes. He takes the causes while He is the one who causes them, and finds that they have given him and responded to him, and he does not turn to the Creator of causes, who made for them their laws so that they respond to man.

Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has pointed to this in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Nay, indeed man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient.﴾ (Surah al-Alaq).

That is because man plows the earth and it gives him fruit, so he believes that he is the one who subdued the earth and set its laws to give him what he wants. He presses the electric switch and the place is lit, so he believes that he is the one who created this electricity! He boards the airplane, and it moves him through the air, so he believes that he is the one who made it fly. He forgets the properties that Allah, the Exalted, placed in the atmosphere so that it could bear this airplane. He turns on the television and sees before him the events of the world, so he believes that this happened by his own power. He forgets that Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, placed in the atmosphere properties that made it carry sound and image from the farthest part of the world to its farthest part in a few seconds. Thus everything around us he thinks he has subdued by his own essence.

Whereas all of this is subjected by Allah, the Exalted, for the service of man, and He is the one who created and set the laws. We say to him: if you understood the meaning of the self-existence of things, your soul would not have suggested this to you. The self-existent thing is that which belongs to you in essence, does not change and never fails. What is not in your essence is what changes.

And if you look at your own "self" that has deluded and transgressed you, you will understand that the word "self-existence" means that you do not need anyone else, but everything comes from yourself. Yet throughout your whole life you have no self-existence, because everything around you changes without your will. You are a child, needing your father and mother at the beginning of your life. Then when you grow up and gain strength and events respond to you, you cannot make this period of youth and vigour last. Time holds power, but for a limited period. When you reach the stage of old age, you will need someone to take your hand and help you, perhaps even with your most basic needs, which are food and drink.

So you begin in childhood needing others, and you end in old age needing others. Even when you are in your youth, an illness may befall you that confines you from movement. If you had a true self, then repel this illness from yourself and say: I will not fall ill. You cannot.

Allah, the Exalted, created these changes so that pride would end in man himself, and he would know that he is strong and capable only by what Allah has subjected to him of the laws of the universe. So that we know that we are all in need of the Capable, who is Allah, the Exalted, and that Allah is self-sufficient above all His creation. He changes and is not changed. He causes death while He is ever-living. He makes strength after weakness, while He is always the Strong. What is with people perishes, but what is with Him, the Blessed and Exalted, never perishes. He is Allah in the heavens and the earth.

So you have no self-existence that would let you claim you subdued the universe by your capabilities, because you have no power to remain in one state and keep it from changing. How, then, do you disbelieve in Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and conceal His existence? Everything in the universe and in yourself is a witness and proof of the existence of the Exalted.

We said that disbelievers are of two kinds. One kind disbelieved in Allah, and when guidance came, it judged with its intellect, recognised the truth and believed. The other kind profits from disbelief, and therefore clings to it. Whatever faith and proofs of faith come to it, it obstinately persists in disbelief, because it wants to keep its worldly authority and its influence, which rest on injustice and tyranny. It will not accept being stripped of them, even by truth. This is the kind of which Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾

They did not disbelieve because a message from Allah, the Exalted, did not reach them, nor because they needed a messenger or prophet to draw their attention to the method of Allah. These people have made disbelief a craft and a way of life. They benefit from disbelief because it made them masters, and because they are distinguished from others by falsehood. And if the faith came that makes all people equal and rejects injustice, they would become ordinary individuals, distinguished in nothing.

This disbeliever who has taken disbelief as a path to the worldly status and glitter of this life: whether you warn him or do not warn him, he will not believe. He wants the world in which he lives. Indeed, these are the ones who oppose religion and fight everyone who has believed, because they know that faith will strip them of many privileges. Therefore their non-belief is not because the method of faith did not reach them, or because no one drew their attention to the signs of Allah on earth, but because their lives are established and built upon disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 7:

﴿Allah has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their sight is a veil; and theirs is a great punishment.﴾

Just as the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has given us the attributes of the believers, He gives us the attributes of the disbelievers. Some people may ask: if this is Allah's judgment upon the disbelievers, then why does the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) demand faith from them when Allah has sealed their hearts? The meaning of sealing the heart is a judgment that what is in the heart of disbelief does not leave it, and faith does not enter it.

We say that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is independent of the worlds. If some of His creatures become independent of faith and choose disbelief, then Allah helps them to remain independent and does not assist them in returning to faith. For this reason, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says in a hadith qudsi:

"I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than it; and if he draws near to Me a hand's span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running" (1).

The hadith qudsi has made clear that Allah, blessed and exalted is He, assists the believers toward faith, and that Allah, majestic in His majesty, as He assists the believers toward faith, does not concern Himself whether the servant comes to faith or does not come. For this reason we find the Qur'an precise and firm that those who disbelieved chose disbelief by their own will. Their choice of disbelief came first, before Allah sealed their hearts. The Creator, majestic in His majesty, is the most independent of partners from association, and whoever associates others with Him, He is independent of him.

Indeed, those who disbelieved, that is, who concealed faith in Allah and His Messenger, upon them Allah seals, by their disbelief, all instruments of perception: the heart, the hearing, and the sight. The heart is an instrument of perception that is not apparent. Allah placed the heart before the hearing and the sight in that verse because He wants to teach us the channels of perception. In the Noble Qur'an the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that you might give thanks.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl, 78)

Thus Allah teaches us that the channels of knowledge in a human being are hearing, sight and hearts. But in the noble verse we are concerned with, Allah placed the hearts before the hearing and the sight, because Allah knows that they chose disbelief, and this choice was before Allah sealed their hearts. And the sealing of the hearts means that no new perception enters them and no old perception leaves them. Whatever the eye sees or the ear hears, there is no benefit in it, because these hearts are sealed with the seal of Allah after their owners chose disbelief and persisted in it. Concerning them the Truth, majestic in His majesty, describes them:

﴿Deaf, dumb, blind; so they will not return.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 18)

But why have they lost all these instruments of perception? Because the veil has wrapped itself around the disbelieving hearts, so the eyes have become incapable of contemplating the signs of Allah, and the hearing has become unable to receive from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

So these, who chose disbelief, persisted in it, and disbelieved in Allah despite His messages, His messengers and His Qur'an, what does Allah do with them? He abandons them. And because He, glorified and exalted is He, is independent of the worlds, He facilitates for them the path they walked in and assists them upon it. Recite His saying, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his constant companion.﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf, 36)

He, majestic in His majesty, also says:

﴿Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend? They descend upon every lying sinner.﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 221-222)

And of the greatness of the knowledge of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, is that He knows the believer and knows the disbeliever, without His being, majestic in His majesty, interfering in their choice. When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sent Nuh (peace be upon him), and Nuh called to the method of Allah for nine hundred and fifty years, and before the flood came, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knew that none would believe in Nuh (peace be upon him) except those who had already believed. So Allah, blessed and exalted is He, commanded Nuh to build the ship so that the believers would be saved from the flood. Recite His saying, majestic in His majesty:

﴿And it was revealed to Nuh: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not grieve over what they have been doing. And construct the ark under Our eyes and Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned."﴾ (Surah Hud, 36-37)

Thus we see that from the greatness of the knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, He knows who will persist in disbelief and that he will die a disbeliever. And if this is the reality, why does Allah, blessed and exalted is He, command His Messenger (ﷺ) to convey to them the method and the Qur'an? So that they will be witnesses against themselves on the Day of Resurrection, so that these people do not come on the day of the great gathering and argue falsely. For if the guidance had reached them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had called them, they would have believed. But why does Allah, majestic in His majesty, seal their hearts? Because the heart is the place of beliefs. Therefore the matter is discussed in the intellect, and when the discussion ends and a person is fully convinced of it, it settles in the heart and does not return to the mind again, and it becomes creed and faith. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that grow blind.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 46)

When the heart is blind to the matter of faith, no eye sees the signs of faith, and no ear hears the speech of Allah. And those who chose disbelief over faith, for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has described the punishment as painful, as humiliating, and as great. The painful punishment is that which causes severe pain. The humiliating punishment is that which comes to those whom Allah raised in this world. Sometimes humiliation is more painful to the soul than the pain of punishment itself. Those who were the leaders of disbelief in this world, Allah, blessed and exalted is He, will bring them on the Day of Resurrection before those who followed them, and He will humiliate them. As for the great punishment, it is attributed to the power of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, because with human power force is limited, whereas with the power of Allah, majestic in His majesty, force is without limit, for every act is proportionate to its doer. The power of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is great in every act, and since the punishment is from Allah, majestic in His majesty, it is a great punishment.

1 Narrated by Imam Muslim in his Sahih, in the Book of Remembrance and Supplication.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 8:

﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.﴾

People in this worldly life are in three states: either a believer (mu'min), or a disbeliever (kafir), or a hypocrite (munafiq).

At the very beginning of the Noble Qur'an, in Surat al-Baqarah, Allah the Most Glorified and Exalted wanted to give us a description of all of mankind with respect to the method (manhaj), and that they are three categories. The first category is the believers. Allah the Most Glorified and Exalted made known their qualities in three verses, in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Those who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them; and those who believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, and of the Hereafter they are certain. Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.﴾

The second category is the disbelievers. Allah the Most Glorified and Exalted made known their qualities in two verses, in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, those who have disbelieved, it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe. Allah has sealed over their hearts and over their hearing, and over their vision is a veil; and for them is a great punishment.﴾

As for the hypocrites, their qualities came in thirteen consecutive verses. Why? Because of their danger to the religion, for it is the hypocrite who demolishes the religion, whereas the disbeliever, we guard against him and beware of him, because he declares his disbelief.

The hypocrite displays faith before you, but he conceals evil and disbelief. You may think him a believer, so you disclose your secrets to him, and he takes them as a weapon to stab the religion. Allah has created in man multiple faculties, but for a person to live in peace with himself, his faculties must be harmonious and not contradictory. The believer's faculties are harmonious, because he has believed in his heart and his tongue utters what he believes, so there is never any contradiction among his faculties.

It may be said that the disbeliever lives in peace with himself, for he has rejected faith and denied it with his heart and tongue and speaks accordingly. But the one who has lost peace with his faculties is the hypocrite. He has lost peace with his society and lost peace with himself. He says with his tongue what his heart does not believe; he shows other than what he conceals, and says other than what he believes, and he fears that people will expose him, so he lives in deep fear, and he believes that this condition is temporary and will end.

But this contradiction remains with him until the last day of his life in this world, and then it passes with him to the Hereafter, where it turns against him to lead him to the Fire. Read His saying, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them concerning what they used to do. And they will say to their skins, "Why have you testified against us?" They will say, "We were made to speak by Allah, who has made everything speak, and He created you the first time, and to Him you are returned."﴾ (Surat Fussilat)

So all their faculties turn against them in the Hereafter. The peace they used to wish for, they did not achieve either in their lives or in their Hereafter. The tongue of the hypocrite testifies against him, his hands testify against him, his feet testify against him, and his skins testify against him. What then remains for him?

Between him and his Lord there is contradiction; between him and himself there is contradiction; between him and his society there is contradiction; between him and his Hereafter there is contradiction; and between him and the disbelievers there is contradiction. His tongue says what is not in his heart. With what did the True, Glorified and Exalted describe the hypocrites? He, Exalted, said:

﴿And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah and the Last Day," but they are not believers.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah)

This is the first description of the hypocrites in the Noble Qur'an: they proclaim faith while disbelief is in their hearts. For this reason, all their faith is pretense. When they go to prayer, it is not recorded for them, because they perform it ostentatiously and do not offer it out of faith. When they pay zakat, it becomes a regret for them, because they spend it while disliking it, since in their assumption it is a loss from their wealth. They do not receive reward for it in the Hereafter. And when one of them is killed in a military campaign, grief and sorrow overtake them, because they have squandered their lives and did not offer them in the way of Allah.

Thus everything they do becomes wretchedness for them.

As for the believer, when he prays, or pays zakat, or is martyred in the way of Allah, he hopes for Paradise. But the hypocrites do all this while hoping for nothing. It is as though, by their hypocrisy, Allah the Most Glorified and Exalted has decreed for them wretchedness in this world and the Hereafter: they have neither in this world the enjoyment the believer has in what he does in the way of Allah, nor in the Hereafter the reward the believer hopes for from Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 9:
