﴿They seek to deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none but themselves, and they perceive not.﴾

The second attribute of the hypocrites comes next, an attribute that indicates their heedlessness and the foolishness of their thinking. They imagine that by their hypocrisy they are deceiving Allah, glorified and exalted be He. Can any human being deceive the Lord of the worlds?

Allah knows everything. He knows what we conceal and what we declare, He knows the secret and what is more hidden than the secret. Is there anything more hidden than the secret? We say yes. The secret is what you confide to someone else, so it is known to two: you and the one to whom you confided it. But what is more hidden than the secret is what you keep within yourself and tell no one, which remains in your heart and which you do not confide to any person. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says: ﴿And if you speak aloud, indeed He knows the secret and what is yet more hidden.﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 20:7).

There is no creature who can deceive its Creator, but out of their heedlessness they imagine that they can deceive Allah, majestic in His majesty. In this conduct of theirs there is no peace between them and Allah; rather, there is only abhorrence and wrath.

In their deception they also imagine that they are deceiving those who believe, by saying in front of them other than what they conceal. But this deception is a wretchedness upon them, because they live in constant fear. They are always in anxiety or dread lest the believers expose them, or overhear them in their private gatherings, where they speak words of disbelief and mock faith. Therefore, when they speak, they must first make certain that none of the believers can hear them, and second make certain that none of the believers will enter upon them while they are talking. Fear fills their hearts too, even when they are with the believers, so each one of them fears that a word will slip from him that exposes his hypocrisy and disbelief.

Thus there is no peace between them and the believers. The truth is that they deceive none but themselves. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, knows their hypocrisy, and the believers may also know this hypocrisy; and if they do not know it, Allah informs them of it. Read the word of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿And if We willed, We would show them to you, and you would surely know them by their marks; and you will surely know them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds.﴾ (Surah Muhammad, 47:30).

Did the hypocrites not come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in order to testify that he is the Messenger of Allah? Then Allah exposed them before His Messenger and sent down His saying, exalted is He:

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars.﴾ (Surah al-Munafiqun, 63:1).

The hypocrites came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) testifying to the truth of his message, and Allah, glorified and exalted be He, knows that this testimony is true and sincere, because He, majestic in His majesty, knows that His Messenger (ﷺ) is truthful in his message. Yet at the same time He testifies that the hypocrites are liars. How?

How can the words of Allah agree with what the hypocrites said, and yet they be liars?

We say: because the hypocrites said with their tongues what was not in their hearts. They testified with their tongues alone that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah, but their hearts denied that and rejected it. Therefore, although what the hypocrites said is a fact, they are liars, for they say with their tongues what is not in their hearts. Truthfulness is that speech corresponds to the reality within the heart, and these people lied, because in their testimony to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) they were not expressing a reality in their hearts; rather, their hearts contradicted what they said.

There are many verses in the Noble Qur'an in which Allah, glorified and exalted be He, exposes the hypocrites and informs His Messenger (ﷺ) of what they conceal in their hearts. Thus their deception of the believers, although it is the deception of a human being toward a human being, sometimes results in their tongues slipping, and so their reality becomes known. And if the tongue does not slip, then the clarification comes from Allah, glorified and exalted be He, to expose them. The outcome of all this is that they deceive no one, for Allah knows their secret and their open speech: sometimes Allah helps the believers against them so they expose them, and sometimes the tongues of the hypocrites slip so they expose themselves.

Thus the conduct of the hypocrite deceives none but himself, and he is the loser in this world and the Hereafter. When he performs an act of faith, Allah knows that it is hypocrisy; and when he tries to deceive the believers, he is exposed. The result is that they think they have achieved some benefit for themselves, whereas they have achieved for themselves nothing but manifest loss.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 10:

﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah has increased their disease. And for them is a painful punishment because they used to lie.﴾ (2:10)

Allah, glorified and exalted, likened what is in the hearts of the hypocrites to a disease. A disease first produces sickness and weakness, as if their hearts do not possess the health of faith that gives life to the heart and makes it strong and vigorous. Rather, they are sick hearts. Why are they sick? Hypocrisy has exhausted them, and their constant estrangement from everything around them has exhausted them too. They feel that they are living a life filled with lies. So the heart is disturbed, and this has made it sick. It cannot be cured except by the permission of Allah, and its remedy is true and sincere faith, which is what gives it healing. Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾ (17:82)

So faith and the Qur'an are the healing of hearts. Both are far from the hearts of these hypocrites, so the disease grows in their hearts over time, and by their hypocrisy and disbelief Allah increases them in disease. This is the third characteristic of the hypocrites: they are people of sick, diseased hearts, into which the light of faith does not enter. For this reason their hearts are weak, lacking the strength needed to recognize the truth. They are hearts fearful of everything around them, terrified in every step, disturbed between what is in the heart and what is on the tongue. The sick person is unable to do anything, and likewise these hearts are unable to speak the truth, unable to be sincere, and unable to see what is around them with that vision which accords and agrees with the innate faith (fitrah) that Allah placed in hearts. Therefore, when the hypocrites enter a battle within the ranks of the Muslim army, the first thing they seek is escape from the battle. They look for a hiding place in which to conceal themselves, or a place where no one can see them. Allah, glorified and exalted, describes them saying:

﴿If they could find a refuge or caves or a place to enter, they would turn to it while rushing headlong.﴾ (9:57)

Why? Because they are people of sick hearts, unable to withstand anything, and their disease makes them flee from everything and hide. Would that the matter stopped at this point! But awaiting them in the Hereafter is a painful punishment, other than the punishment they suffered from their sick hearts in this world. Because they lied against Allah and His Messenger, awaiting them in the Hereafter is a painful punishment, more severe than the punishment of the disbelievers. Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire.﴾ (part of 4:145)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 11:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers."﴾

Corruption on the earth is that you deliberately approach what is good and corrupt it. The least that is asked of you in this world is that you leave what is good in its goodness and do not interfere with it to spoil it. If you wish to rise in faith, then go to what is good and increase its goodness. But if you come to what is good and corrupt it, you have committed a double corruption. For God, glorified and exalted is He, has set right for you the foundations of your life in the universe, and you have not left them in the state of goodness in which they were created. Leaving them alone would in itself have been a distance from corruption. Instead, you came to them while they were good by God's creation, and you corrupted them. You did not receive the blessing granted to you by God by letting it perform its task in life, nor did you add to its goodness in performing its task; rather, you came to this task and corrupted it.

Consider a well from which people drink. It is a blessing for the necessity of their lives. You may, by God's means in God's universe, come and improve it, by lining its walls with stones so as to prevent the sand from collapsing inside it, or by bringing a rope and a vessel so as to help people reach its water. But if you come and fill it in, you will have corrupted the good in life.

So too are the hypocrites. God, exalted is He, sent down a method for the good life of man on earth, and these hypocrites have exerted all their effort to corrupt this method, by plotting against it and claiming that they believe in it, in order to stab Islam from within.

The enemies of Islam became aware that this strong, true religion cannot be affected by the stabbing blows of disbelief; rather, it confronts them and prevails over them. No battle has ever taken place between truth and falsehood without truth being victorious. The enemies of Islam tried to confront it for many years, but they failed. Then they realized that this religion can only be defeated from within, and that employing the hypocrites in corruption is the true method of dividing the Muslims. So they set out among the Muslims in name, to take them as the spear which they would aim against Islam. Sects and divisions appeared, and what they called secularism, leftism, and other things. All of this was carried out by the hypocrites within Islam, and they wrapped it in an Islamic wrapping, in order to corrupt the earth and wage war against the method of God.

When the believers draw their attention to the fact that they are corrupting the earth, and ask them to refrain from corruption, they claim that they do not corrupt but only reform. But what reform is there in not following the method of God and rebelling against it on any pretext whatsoever?

Thus Allah, glory be to Him, gives us His judgment upon them: just as they deceive themselves without realizing it, and imagine that they are deceiving Allah and the believers. Likewise, they cause corruption on the earth while claiming to be reformers. But in reality they are corrupters. Why? Because there is disbelief in their hearts and hostility toward the method of Allah. So if they undertake any action whose outward appearance is reform, its reality is corruption, exactly as they utter with their tongues what is not in their hearts.

The universe cannot be set right except by the method of Allah. Allah, the Almighty, is the One who created and brought into existence, and He knows best His creation, what corrupts it and what sets it right, because He is the Maker. No one knows the secret of what sets right His handiwork better than its Maker.

In worldly affairs, when we want to repair something, we turn to its manufacturer, for he is the one who can show us the true repair of that thing. If its manufacturer is not present in the same town, we turn to those whom the manufacturer trained in repair, or to what they call the "catalogue" (kataloog, the manual) that explains to us the way of repair. Without this, we do not repair; rather, we corrupt. Strangely, we follow this method in our worldly life, and then we come to the human being and the universe. Instead of turning to its Maker and Creator to take from Him the method of reform, He who knows best His handiwork, we turn to the creatures of Allah, and they set down for us methods that corrupt, whose outward appearance is reform, but which make matters worse. Strangest of all, we call this "success" and we call it "progress." But why do we not turn to the Maker or the Creator, who brought into existence and created? He, glory be to Him, knows best His creation and what sets it right and what corrupts it.

Since the Truth, glory be to Him, has judged the hypocrites to be the corrupters, that is a certain judgment. Everyone who tries to alter the method of Allah, or to obstruct its application under the pretext of reform, is a corrupter, even if he does not realize it, because if he truly wanted reform he would turn to what sets the universe right, which is the heavenly method sent down by the Creator and Maker of this universe. This method exists, has been conveyed, and is hidden from no one.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 13:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe as the people have believed," they say, "Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?" Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know.﴾

In the intention of the hypocrites, "the foolish" are the poor. But what is the meaning of foolishness (safah) linguistically? Safah means lightness of mind, folly, and recklessness in dealing with affairs. So, does the attribute of foolishness apply to the believers, who have believed in God? Or does it apply to those who have not believed in God? If you believe that those who have believed are the foolish, then why do you claim faith falsely, so that you might be foolish?

There is no doubt that there is a contradiction present in all the conduct of the hypocrites.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) calls them to faith, and the Muslims call them to faith, yet they describe those who believed as foolish, meaning poor people who own nothing, because the masters of Quraysh did not believe. They claim that those who believed acted in a foolish, reckless manner. But heedlessness is the disease that fills their hearts, preventing them from noticing an important truth: that they pretend to faith, claim to believe, and then describe the believers as foolish, if these people were foolish as you claim. So do you pretend to believe in order to become foolish like them?!

Logic does not hold up, and it shows the foolishness of the minds of the hypocrites. These minds did not realize that in describing the Muslims as foolish, they condemned themselves, because the hypocrites claim that they are believers. Thus all the conduct of the hypocrites contains contradiction, a contradiction with reason and logic. This contradiction arises from the contradiction among the faculties of the soul with one another. The tongue contradicts the heart, the action contradicts the creed, and pretending to faith burdens them with the hardship of faith without giving them any of its reward. Had they had minds, they would have noticed all of this, but they do not perceive it as they proceed along this path, the path of hypocrisy. They embody foolishness itself, with all that it carries of stupidity and levity, lack of attention to the truth, and the rashness with which they act. And God, glorified and exalted is He, when He described them as foolish, it was an accurate description of their state and way of life.

Thus does the Truthful (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, show us that every hypocrite has more than one life that he is anxious to protect. For life to be upright, it must be one coherent life, its parts consistent with one another. But look at these people: with the believers they say, "We believe," and they adopt the life of faith outwardly. That is, they play the part of believers, just as an actor on the stage performs a role entirely different from his own person. Their whole life is contrived and self-contradictory. So when they withdraw from those who believe, the Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils (shayatin)﴾.

Notice the precision of the Qur'anic expression. The shaytan is secret whispering. Truth is apparent and clear, while the method of the shaytan and his plotting happen in secret, because falsehood is hidden, and the soul never feels shame before truth, but it fears, dreads, and tries to conceal falsehood.

Let us take a simple example. A man is sitting with his wife in his home, and a visitor knocks at the door. What happens? The man goes calmly, opens the door to see who is knocking. If it is a friend or a relative, he honors him, welcomes him, and insists that he come in as his guest. His wife prepares the food or drink that will be served to the guest. Now take the same situation where a man is in his apartment with another man's wife, and a visitor knocks. A violent agitation occurs. The man looks for a place to hide the woman who is with him, or for a secret door to let her out by, or he tries to switch off the lights and suppress the sounds, hoping that the visitor will sense that no one is in the place and leave. Before he lets out that woman who is forbidden to him, he opens the door cautiously, looks right and left to make sure whether anyone sees him. When he finds no one, he hurries to push the woman outside, because she is a sin from which he wants to be rid. If he walks her out, he walks at a distance from her and keeps watching the road to make sure no one has seen him. When the two of them get into the car, they set off at top speed.

This is the difference between the method of faith and the method of the shaytan. The incident is one and the same, but what differs is the lawful and the unlawful. Observe how people behave with the lawful: in light, in safety. And how they behave with the unlawful: the method of the shaytan is in darkness and in secrecy, and they take great care that no one sees them. This is where the precision of the Qur'anic expression comes in: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils﴾.

The method of the shaytan requires seclusion, a place where no one sees you and no one hears you, because openness in the method of the shaytan becomes scandal. That is why the one who is not upright tries hard to conceal his deviation, and his effort to hide is itself a testimony from him that what he does is a crime and an ugliness, and that it is not right for anyone to know of it. As long as it is not right for anyone to see him in a certain place, know that he senses that what he does in this place is the work of the shaytan, which God does not approve of and is not pleased with.

We must know that values remain values, even for the deviant. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And when they meet those who believe, they say, "We believe"﴾ means that when they pretend to faith, they take the side of openness; indeed, they may have fabricated it. And what would have been expected, when they are alone with their devils, is that they would say: "We have not believed."

In the language there is the nominal sentence (al-jumla al-ismiyya, الجملة الاسمية) and the verbal sentence (al-jumla al-fi'liyya, الجملة الفعلية). The verbal sentence indicates renewal (tajaddud, التجدد), and the nominal sentence indicates stability (thubut, الثبوت). So the hypocrites, with the believers, say "āmannā" (آمنا), their faith is not stable, it wavers. But when they meet the disbelievers, if they had said "lam nu'min" (لم نؤمن), it would have taken on the quality of stability. Yet in the period between their meeting the believers and their meeting the disbelievers, disbelief is renewed in them. Therefore they said: ﴿Indeed we are with you; we were only mocking﴾.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 15:**

﴿Allah mocks them and extends them in their rebellion, wandering blindly.﴾

These hypocrites are a people with no power and no strength of their own. But Allah, glorified and exalted, is the Capable, the Mighty, and when He mocks them, the mockery is painful. If the hypocrite has shown with his tongue what is not in his heart, then Allah, glorified and exalted, deals with him in kind. He has an outward and an inward state: in the outward affairs of this world, He treats him as He treats the Muslims, but in the Hereafter, on the day when hidden things are laid bare, He places him in the lowest level of the Fire. He is not equated with the disbelievers, because the sin of the hypocrite is greater.

﴿Allah mocks them.﴾ Istihza' (الاستهزاء) is mockery and ridicule. On the Day of Resurrection they will come trying to cling to the outward appearance, and Allah, glorified and exalted, will then reveal to them their inward reality. The Exalted says:

﴿Woe to every slanderer, backbiter﴾ (Surah al-Humazah 104:1).

The humazah (الهمزة) is one who mocks people, even by a gesture. He sees a person afflicted with a defect in his foot, walking with a limp, and he tries to imitate him in a manner that provokes ridicule, either by gesture or by speech. There is hamz and humazah: hamz is mockery and ridicule of people, a sign of lack of faith. For we are all created by one God. This quality for which you mock a lame man, for example, is something he has no hand in, and he has no power or strength over it. A person did not create himself. In truth, you are mocking the creation of Allah, and whoever mocks the creation of Allah is a foolish person, because he has mocked a defect in the creation of Allah and has not appreciated the favour Allah has bestowed upon him. Likewise, he has mocked a defect without realizing that the Exalted has given that person qualities and distinctions that He perhaps has not given to him. Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people, perhaps they may be better than them﴾ (Surah al-Hujurat 49:11).

The total of every human being equals the total of every other human being, and that is the justice of Allah. So if I am better than a person in something, I should look for the deficiency in myself. If you mock a believer for something, then the mockery is not separate from the handiwork of Allah. Therefore, it is logical that when they said: ﴿We are only mockers﴾, Allah replied to them: ﴿Allah mocks them and extends them in their rebellion, wandering blindly﴾, meaning He increases them in this rebellion. Madd (المد) is to increase a thing. Sometimes you increase a thing from its own substance, and sometimes you increase it by adding something from elsewhere. You may take a thread and let it extend to its end, or you may join it to another thread, so that you have extended it with something from outside. So Allah increases them in their rebellion.

As for His saying ﴿yaʿmahun﴾ (يعمهون, wandering blindly): al-ʿamah (العمه) differs from al-ʿama (العمى). The difference lies in the last letter. Al-ʿama is blindness of the eyes, and al-ʿamah is blindness of insight, and yaʿmahun means they stumble about in confusion. For ʿamah gives rise to stumbling, whether sensory stumbling arising from blindness of the eyes, or stumbling in values and the way of life arising from blindness of insight. The Exalted says: ﴿For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ (Surah al-Hajj 22:46). So material blindness may not exist, but there may be blindness of insight. Read His saying, the Exalted:

﴿He said, "My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?" He will say, "Thus came to you Our verses, but you forgot them; and similarly, this Day, you are forgotten"﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha 20:125–126).

So the blindness of insight in this world blinds a person's sight to seeing the signs of Allah in His creation, and blinds him to faith and the way of life.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 16:

﴿Those are the ones who have bought misguidance in exchange for guidance, so their trade has not profited, nor were they [ever] guided.﴾

The Truth, glory be to Him, gives us another attribute of the hypocrites, describing them as those who have bought misguidance in exchange for guidance. As long as there is a purchase, there is a transaction, and a transaction requires a buyer and a seller. In the past, goods were bought with other goods, but now everything is bought with money. What did they buy?

These hypocrites bought misguidance, and at what price?! They bought it with guidance! In the Arabic language, the preposition bi (ب, "with/in exchange for") is attached to what is given up. When you buy something, you leave its price behind. So it is as if these people abandoned guidance and bought misguidance. But did they have guidance with them at the moment of the transaction?

The situation requires that they had guidance with them. For example, a person may be guided, then find that guidance does not bring him the worldly benefit he seeks, so he abandons it to buy misguidance, through which he achieves what he wants. The guidance that was with them may have been the guidance of fitrah (the innate human disposition to recognize the truth). So it is as if these people could have chosen guidance, but they chose misguidance.

Allah, glory be to Him, guides all people with the guidance of indication (hudā dalālah), so whoever chooses guidance, He increases him in it. Read His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ (part of verse 17, surah Fussilat).

As for the Truth's words, ﴿so their trade has not profited﴾: trade is selling and buying. The buyer consumes, and the seller may be a producer or an intermediary between producer and consumer. What is the seller's share of the sale and purchase? That he gains. If he gains, it is said that his trade has profited. If he neither gains nor loses, or if he loses and does not gain, then in both cases he has achieved no profit, and we say his trade has not profited.

So His saying, ﴿so their trade has not profited, nor were they [ever] guided﴾, indicates that they lost everything, because they did not profit. It is as if they achieved nothing of benefit, and they lost the guidance, that is, they lost the profit and the capital. Perhaps they did not gain and did not lose, but they offered guidance as the price for misguidance, so they did not profit, and the guidance was lost from them, that is, their capital.

As for the psychology of the hypocrite, if you want to define it, he is a person without dignity, without manliness, unable to confront, without strength, who tries to scheme in secret. For this reason his self-image is contemptible in his own eyes, even if he manages to hide his faults from people, for it is enough that he is a liar before himself for his self-image to be contemptible in his own eyes. On this the poet says:

If I do not come to baseness out of fear
of people, then people are more noble than my self.

Enough shame for a person is that he sees the fault of his own self,
even if he is hidden from jinn and humans.

So what matters is your opinion of yourself. And the division within the hypocrite is that he wants to hide his faults from people.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (*Tafsir al-Sha'rawi*, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 17:

﴿Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, unable to see.﴾ (2:17)

The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, wishes to bring the attributes of the hypocrites' disunity closer to our understanding, and so He strikes examples (*amthal*, sing. *mathal*) for us. A *mathal* is a likeness that brings the meaning near to us and gives us wisdom. The *amthal* form one of the ancient branches of Arabic literature.

A *mathal* is when something occurs and a brief, expressive saying is uttered about it, which people then adopt for every similar situation.

Let us give an example of this. A king wished to propose marriage to a girl from among the Arab women, so he sent a matchmaker named Isam to see this bride, ask about her, and report back to him. When she returned, he said to her, "What is behind you, O Isam?" meaning, what news have you brought? She said, "The churning has revealed the butter." Churning (*al-makhd*) is when one takes milk and churns it in a waterskin until the butter separates from the milk. The question and the answer have since become a *mathal*. You come to someone who is coming to you, hoping for news from him, and you say to him, "What is behind you, O Isam?"

Yet his name is not "Isam," and you did not send him to seek news, while you want to hear what he has to report.

When you want to depict, for example, the repulsion of hearts, and how, once they repel each other, they never reconcile, the poet wishes to bring this meaning near and says:

"When the hearts' affection repels, it is like a glass; its break cannot be mended." (i.e., cannot be repaired)

At the moment a glass breaks, you cannot repair it. And so that this meaning may be easy for you to grasp and understand readily and smoothly, you cannot picture or witness a battle between two hearts, because this is an unseen matter. So you bring something visible and strike it as an example, and thus the meaning becomes near, because you have likened it to something perceptible that you can understand and see.

God, glorified and exalted be He, has used examples in the Noble Qur'an on more than one occasion, to bring close to our minds the meanings of the unseen that we do not know and do not witness. Accordingly, He struck examples for us regarding the summit of faith, the oneness of God, glorified and exalted be He. He struck the example of His light, majestic in His majesty, which we do not witness, as it is unseen to us. He struck examples concerning the disbelievers and hypocrites, so that we might know the corruption of their creed and be alerted to it. He struck examples of what disbelief in blessings can do, and of tyranny against the truth, and other examples. God, exalted be He, said:

﴿And We have certainly diversified for the people in this Qur'an from every example, but most of the people refused except denial.﴾ (17:89)

God, majestic in His majesty, has struck examples for us in this world and in the Hereafter, in the precision of creation and the summit of faith. Yet people turn away from the wisdom of these examples and reject them, even though the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, struck them for us so that the meaning might be brought near to us, by way of likeness to material things we see in our worldly life. It was expected that these examples would increase people in faith, because they bring near to them meanings that are hidden from them. But instead they increased in disbelief!

Before we address the noble verse ﴿Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire; and when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, unable to see.﴾, we must speak of some of the examples struck in the Noble Qur'an, to see how God, glorified and exalted be He, has told us of unseen matters through worldly perceptible things:

God, blessed and exalted be He, has struck for us an example of the summit of faith, which is that there is no god but God, and how this is a mercy from God, glorified and exalted be He, for which we should prostrate in gratitude, because in it is protection for us from wretchedness. Yet God, blessed and exalted be He, desires mercy for His servants, but some people wish to bring misery upon themselves by associating partners with God, majestic in His majesty. Instead of taking the easy path of faith, they take the path of disbelief, hypocrisy, and associating partners with God, who owns everything in this world and the Hereafter. The Truth, majestic in His majesty, says:

﴿God presents an example: a man in whom are partners in dispute, and a man belonging entirely to one man. Are they equal in comparison? Praise be to God; but most of them do not know.﴾ (39:29)

In this perceptible image that we see, about which no two people disagree, God, blessed and exalted be He, wishes to bring near to our minds the picture of the one who worships God alone, and the picture of one who associates partners with God. He gives us the example of a servant owned by partners, a man owned by ten, for instance, and these ten partners are not in agreement, but rather are "disputing," meaning they differ. And another man is owned by one master. Which of them is at rest, living in mercy? Obviously, the one owned by a single master is in blessing and mercy, because he follows one command and one prohibition, obeys one Lord, and seeks the pleasure of one master. As for the one owned by partners, even if they were in agreement, each of them would have a command and a prohibition, and each would have a demand. So what if they disagree? One partner tells him, "Come," while another says, "Do not come." One partner orders him to do one thing, and another orders him to do the opposite. He is perplexed as to which one to please and which to anger. Thus his life becomes wretchedness and contradiction.

God, glorified and exalted be He, wishes to bring the picture close to us, in a matter that is the summit of certainty, which is faith in the One, the Unique. He wants us to touch this picture through an example we see and witness, and to see God's overflowing mercy upon His servants. The Truth, glorified be He, proceeds to draw our attention to think for a little while about an example He strikes for us in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿God presents an example of two men: one of them is mute, unable to do anything, and he is a burden on his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path?﴾ (16:76)

In this noble verse, the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, asks us to think about a material, perceptible example: which of them is better? Is it that idol which the disbelievers worship, which never brings them any good at all, since it cannot benefit itself, so how could it bring good to others? Rather, it is a burden on those who take it as a god. They must place it, carry it from one place to another if they wish to change its shrine or relocate, and if it falls and parts of it are shattered, they must repair them.

So, beyond the fact that it brings them no good, it is a burden upon them that causes them hardship and requires from them care and attention.

Is the worship of such an idol better, or the worship of God, glorified be He, from whom comes all good and all blessings, who commands justice and does not favor one of His servants over another, and who gives His servants the straight path, which has no crookedness, and which leads to Paradise in the Hereafter? God, glorified and exalted be He, explains through this example the foolishness of the thinking of the polytheists who worship idols and abandon the worship of God, blessed and exalted be He.

Thus these two examples give us a clarification of the matter of oneness and divinity. Then God, glorified and exalted be He, brings another example, striking for us an example of His light, this divine light that illuminates the world and the Hereafter, illuminating believing hearts. He wishes to strike for us an example of this light with a material, perceptible thing, and so He says, majestic in His majesty:

﴿God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly star, lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. God guides to His light whom He wills. And God presents examples for the people, and God is Knowing of all things.﴾ (24:35)

It is as if God, glorified and exalted be He, wishes us to know, through a perceptible comparison, that the likeness of His light is like a niche (*mishkah*). The *mishkah* is the recess (*al-taqah*), which is a hollow in the wall of a rural house, and we place the lamp in this recess. So the lamp is not in the whole room, but its light is concentrated in this recess, so it is strong within this narrow space. But the lamp is in a glass, which protects it from the air on every side, so the light becomes stronger, pure, with no smoke in it, just as glass reflects rays, thereby increasing their concentration. The glass is not an ordinary one, but "a pearly star," meaning it is luminous in itself, as if it were a star. Its fuel is from a blessed tree, which fills it with light; it is neither eastern nor western, meaning light fills it from the center and comes out pure. The oil shines by itself without fire touching it, so it is "light upon light." Would any part of this niche, which is small in area, be dark? Or would all of it be filled with strong light?

This is not the light of God, blessed and exalted be He, beyond comparison and description, but merely an example to bring it near to minds. It is as if God's light illuminates every corner and every spot, leaving no place dark. It is light upon light. One of the poets wished to praise the caliph(1) and it was customary to liken the caliph to prominent persons with good qualities. So he said:

"The bravery of 'Amr with the generosity of Hatim,
in the forbearance of al-Ahnaf, in the intelligence of Iyas."(2)

All those whom the poet struck as examples were famous for these qualities: 'Amr was famous for courage and bravery, Hatim was famous for generosity, al-Ahnaf is proverbial for forbearance, and Iyas is a blaze of intelligence. Here one of those present(3) stood up and said, "The Amir is greater than everything with which you have compared him." Abu Tammam immediately responded:

"Do not deny my striking for him, besides Him, an example
unique in generosity and valor.
God has struck, for His light, a lesser example
from the niche and the lamp."(4)

Ahmad ibn al-Mu'tasim and those present were amazed at his intelligence, and he ordered that his reward be doubled.

God, glorified be He, strikes for us an example of what believers will witness in Paradise, and so He says, majestic in His majesty:

﴿The likeness of Paradise which the righteous are promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey.﴾ (From verse 15 of surah Muhammad)

This is not Paradise itself, but it is an example by which God, glorified and exalted be He, brings the picture close to us with things present in our lives, because human minds cannot grasp more than this. Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. For this reason there are no words in life that express what is in Paradise. Read His saying, exalted be He:

﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ (32:17)

If the soul does not know, then no words exist to express what is in Paradise. And an example, once its use spreads among people, becomes called a *mathal*. If you see a person conceited about his strength, and you want to make him understand that you are stronger than him, you say to him, "If you are a wind, then you have met a whirlwind." Yet there is no wind or whirlwind in what occurs between you two; rather, the intended meaning is the idea, without being bound to the literal sense of the words.

So the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, wishes to give us a picture of what is inside the hearts of the hypocrites, of turmoil, instability, and hesitation in receiving God's method. At the same time, what happens in their hearts is hidden from us, and God wished to bring this meaning close to us, so He said: ﴿Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire﴾, meaning he tried to kindle a fire. Whoever tries to kindle a fire must have a goal: the goal may be warmth, may be cooking, may be light, or may be something else. The important thing is that there be a purpose for kindling the fire.

The Truth, glorified and exalted be He, says: ﴿And when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, unable to see.﴾ That is because of the bewilderment that filled their hearts. They had heard from the Jews that the time of a new prophet had come, so they decided to believe in him. But their belief was not out of desire for faith; rather, it was an attempt to obtain worldly security, because the Jews were threatening them, saying, "The time of a prophet has come; we will believe in him, and we will kill you with him, as the 'Ad and Iram were destroyed." So these hypocrites wanted to protect themselves from this killing that the Jews threatened them with, and so they imagined that

1 He is Abu Tammam.
2 He is Ahmad ibn al-Mu'tasim.
3 He is Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi.
4 From the *Diwan* of Abu Tammam, with the commentary of al-Tabrizi.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 18:

﴿Deaf, dumb, and blind, so they will not return.﴾

So Allah, glorified and exalted, after informing us that these hypocrites wronged themselves, and that He took away the light of faith from their hearts, so that they do not see the signs of Allah, wanted to draw our attention to the fact that it is not sight alone that has gone. Rather, all their faculties have been disabled. Hearing has been disabled, so they are deaf. Speech has been disabled, so they are dumb. Sight has been disabled, so they are blind. These are the instruments of perception in a human being. Consider His saying, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts, so that you might give thanks.﴾ (Surat al-Nahl: 78)

Thus, their being in darkness, unable to see, means that the other means of perception have also been disabled. Their ears have become deaf, so they do not hear the method of truth. Their tongues have been disabled from conveying what is in their hearts. Their eyes do not see the signs of Allah in the universe. Thus the instruments of their perception of Allah's guidance are disabled in them.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so they will not return﴾, it means that these means will not come back to them so that they may perceive the light of Allah in His creation. Perception is not present in them. Therefore, do not hope that they will ever return to the method of faith. Creed has become corrupted in their hearts, so they do not distinguish between immediate harm and what is a deferred benefit. The light of guidance would have made them see the path to Allah, so that they walk with clear proof and do not stumble. But when the light came to them, they rejected it and turned away from it. It is as if they turned away from everything that would guide them to the path of Allah!!

So Allah, glorified and exalted, in this noble verse, has given us another description of the hypocrites: that the instruments of perception which Allah, majestic in His majesty, created are disabled in them. Therefore, insisting on guiding them and exerting effort with them will not bear fruit, because Allah, blessed and exalted, by their hypocrisy and wrongdoing, has disabled the means of guidance through which they could have returned to the path of truth.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 19:

﴿Or like a rain-cloud from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder and lightning. They put their fingers in their ears against the thunderclaps, for fear of death. And Allah encompasses the disbelievers.﴾

The Word of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Or like a rain-cloud from the sky﴾. Ṣayyib is the rain. Allah, blessed and exalted, sends down water, and by it life stands up, in confirmation of His saying, majestic is His majesty: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ (Qur'an 21:30).

It is self-evident that we know that the sending down of rain is from the power of Allah alone, the Glorified and Exalted. The process of rain involves creation according to a precise measure, and it involves processes that take place every day, also according to measure, and it involves factors that none can control except Allah, the Glorified and Exalted. The matter of rain was prepared for the earth at the time of creation, so that three-quarters of the earth became water and a quarter dry land. Why? Among the wisdom of Allah in this creation is that evaporation should be easy and possible, for the wider the surface of the water, the easier the evaporation; and when the surface is narrow, evaporation becomes harder. If we take a cup full of water and place it in a closed room for a day, then return to it, we find that the volume of water has decreased by a few centimetres or less. If we take the water of this cup and spill it in the room, it disappears within a short period. Why? Because the surface of the water has become wide, so evaporation happened quickly.

When Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, created the earth, He placed in the creation the wisdom of rain: that the area of water should be wide so that evaporation happens easily. He made the rays of the sun, which carry out evaporation from the surface of the water, and this was done with precise measure, so that the rains do not drown the earth or cause drought in it. Then He subjected the wind to drive the clouds to where Allah wishes the rain to fall, and the cold mountain peaks so that the clouds strike them and the rain falls. All of this is with precise measure in the creation and in every stage of the rain.

Since water is that by which there is life on earth, Allah has set forth for us the parable of it, just as He set forth for us the parable of fire and its light. These are all material examples to bring closer to our minds what is unseen to us. Water gives us life.

But these hypocrites did not turn to this good which descends upon them from the sky without any toil or effort on their part. Rather, they turned to secondary things, which they should have welcomed, because they are harbingers of good for them. Before rain descends from the sky, there must be some darkness in the cloud that brings the rain, which veils the rays of the sun if it is day, and conceals the light of the moon and stars if it is night. This darkness is a harbinger of good and of water.

They did not turn to the good with which Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, filled the earth. Rather, they turned to the darkness and recoiled from the good. Likewise the sound of thunder and the light of lightning. Thunder is received by man through the ear, which is the instrument of hearing, and lightning is received by the eye. The sound of thunder is strong, stronger than the capacity of the ear. Therefore, when a person hears it he is startled, and tries to prevent the ear from receiving it, by placing his fingertips in his ears.

These hypocrites did not place the fingertips, but as Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, said: ﴿They put their fingers in their ears﴾, and He did not say "their fingertips." This is hyperbole in depicting the effect of the thunder upon them, as if each one of them, from his fear and terror, tries to put his whole finger into his ear, to protect himself from this frightening sound. As if they are exaggerating in their fear of the thunder.

We note here that the discourse is not about one individual, but about many, because He, the Glorified and Exalted, says ﴿their fingers﴾. We say that when an address is to a group, it means an address to each individual in it. If a teacher says to the students "take out your pens," it means that every student takes out his pen. If the head of a group says "board your cars," it means that each one boards his car. Therefore the meaning of ﴿they put their fingers in their ears﴾ is that each one of them puts his two fingers in his two ears.

Why do they do that? They do it out of fear of death, because thunder and lightning are sometimes accompanied by thunderbolts, and so, out of their exaggerated fear, each one of them feels that a thunderbolt will kill him. As if they receive the blessing of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, without its reality. They do not see the true blessing in that this rain comes to them with the means of the continuation of life, but they take the outward appearance of the lightning and thunder. Likewise the hypocrites: none of them can endure patiently the desires of his soul and its impulses. He wants that immediate gain and does not look to the true good which Allah has promised to His believing servants in the Hereafter. He looks at the obligations as if they were hardship and a matter that burdens the self with some toil, and he neglects the reality of the reward of the obligations in the Hereafter, and how they will provide for them everlasting bliss, exactly as a person looks at the rain as darkness, thunder and lightning, and forgets that without this rain it is impossible for his life to continue.

They take these phenomena as if they were everything, whereas in reality they come for a short time and then disappear. They are brief like the life of this world, temporary. But their view of them is temporary and material, because they believe in nothing but this world and have neglected the Hereafter. They neglected that water which remains for a long time, and they noticed those temporary phenomena that come with the rain, and they feared them, and their fear of them made them unable to perceive the good in the rain. And the hypocrites want to take the good of Islam without performing the duties of this religion!!

Then the Truth, the Glorified and Exalted, draws our attention to an important matter: that their fear of the loss of the enjoyments of this world and its dominion will not avail them anything, because Allah encompasses the disbelievers. Encompassing (ihāṭah) means complete control over a thing, such that it has no means of escape. The power of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, encompasses the disbelievers and non-disbelievers alike.

So, their not turning to the true benefit, which is the way of Allah, does not give them the ability to escape the power of Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, in this world and in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 20:

﴿Lightning almost snatches away their sight. Whenever it lights up for them, they walk in it; and when darkness falls over them, they stand still. And if God willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight. Indeed, God is over all things competent.﴾ (2:20)

Almighty God wishes to draw our attention to the fact that lightning, whose duration is momentary and brief, is what captures their attention. Had they believed, the light of faith and Islam would have illuminated their path. But their hearts are filled with the darkness of disbelief, so they do not see the path of light. "Lightning almost snatches away their sight" means it takes it without their will. "Snatching" (khatf) means that the one who snatches does not wait for permission, and the one from whom something is snatched has no power to prevent the snatcher. Snatching is not the same as usurping (ghasb). Usurping is taking a thing despite its owner.

But what is the difference between taking (akhdh), snatching (khatf), and usurping (ghasb)? Taking is when you ask the owner for a thing and he gives it to you, or you seek his permission; that is, you take the thing with the permission of its owner. Snatching is when you take it without the will of its owner and without him being able to prevent you.

Usurping is when you take a thing against the will of its owner, by using force or otherwise, such that he becomes unable to prevent you from taking it.

Let us give an example of this, and to God belongs the highest likeness. If a child enters a sweet shop and snatches a piece of candy, the shopkeeper has no power over the snatcher, because the event is beyond the capacity of the one snatched from; it is sudden and unexpected, so he cannot prevent the snatching. As for usurping, it is that the shopkeeper is alert but does not have the power to prevent what is happening, and if he tries to resist, the one who takes the thing despite him must be stronger than him. That is, the strength of the usurper is greater than that of the one usurped from.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lightning almost snatches away their sight﴾.

We must be mindful of His saying ﴿almost﴾ (yakād): the lightning comes close to snatching away their sight, and a human has no power to prevent this lightning from seizing the attention of the sight.

And His saying ﴿Whenever it lights up for them, they walk in it﴾.

That is, they walk according to the measure of the worldly light that the lightning gives them. There is no light in their hearts. Therefore, when darkness falls over them, they stop, because they have no light.

And His saying ﴿And if God willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight﴾.

Some orientalists claim that this contradicts the noble verse that says ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind; so they will not return﴾ (2:18). How can they be deaf, dumb, and blind? That is, the channels of perception in them do not function, and we are speaking here of spiritual blindness. Then the Blessed and Exalted says ﴿And if God willed, He would have taken away their hearing and their sight﴾, even though they are deaf, dumb, and blind?

We say: the saying of the Truth, exalted is He, ﴿deaf, dumb, blind﴾ means they do not see God's signs and the certainty of faith, and do not hear the verses of the Qur'an and comprehend them. Thus the means by which they perceive spiritual matters are disabled. But their means of perceiving sensory matters remain as they are. The hypocrite who does not believe in the Day of Resurrection does not see the punishment awaiting him in the Hereafter.

And if God, exalted is He, willed to take away their hearing and their sight, with respect to sensory things, He would have been able to, for He is competent over all things. But He, exalted is He, did not will that, so that they would not come arguing on the Day of Judgment that, had they had sight, they would have seen God's signs, and had they had hearing, they would have contemplated the Qur'an. God therefore left them their sight and hearing, to be a proof against them: that they had sight but turned away from God's signs toward things that bring them immediate benefit in the world, however much they bring God's anger; and that they had hearing with which they hear everything, from plans of conspiracies against Islam, to undermining faith, and other things. So when God's verses are recited to them, they do not hear them. And concerning this, God, exalted is He, says:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you; until, when they leave your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?"﴾ (part of 47:16)

That is, they hear but do not understand, and the light does not enter their hearts, so it is as if they are deaf to God's signs, not hearing them.

The Truth, exalted is He, wishes to give us the example of the hypocrites, that they do not turn to the true values of life, but take only its outward appearance. They desire immediate benefit, and the darkness of their hearts does not let them see the light of faith. Rather, the glitter of the world dazzles them, although it is fleeting and momentary, so it snatches away their sight. And since there is no light in their hearts, when the world departs from them, darkness surrounds them from every direction, because they do not believe in the Hereafter. Although God, exalted is He, if He willed, would have taken away their hearing and sight, since they do not use them in the required faithful manner. These means of perception are supposed to increase us in faith, but these people see only the enjoyment of this world and hear only the whispering of Satan. Thus the faith-based function of the means of perception has ceased, as if these means did not exist.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 21:

﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous.﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted is He, related to us the attributes of the hypocrites in thirteen verses and gave us their outward characteristics, and He gave us examples of what happens in their hearts so that the believers may recognize them, outwardly and inwardly, and be wary of them and not feel secure with them. He has shown us how the hypocrites did not only disbelieve in Allah as God; they concealed His existence, yet they also disbelieved in Him as Lord (rabb). The Lord's provision is guaranteed for everyone He created, believer and disbeliever alike, for He, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who summoned them into existence and created them. Therefore He, glorified is He, guarantees their sustenance and their lives.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, does not deprive any of His creatures of the gift of His lordship in this world. The sun shines upon the believer and the disbeliever. The rain falls upon the one who says "there is no god but Allah" and upon the one who concealed His existence. The air is breathed by the one who establishes the prayer and by the one who has never bowed in prayer even once in his life. Food is eaten by the one who loves Allah and by the one who denies the blessings of Allah. This is because these are gifts of lordship that Allah, exalted is He, gives to all His creatures in this world.

As for the gifts of divinity (uluhiyyah), they are for the believers in this world and the Hereafter.

So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, draws the attention of His creation to the fact that the gift of lordship from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to them is sufficient for them to believe in Allah and worship Him.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, addresses people in the Noble Qur'an, that Book "falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it," the address must be to people in every time and place, from the revelation of the Noble Qur'an until the Day of Resurrection.

The address of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, concerns the supreme matter of faith, which is submission to one God without partner.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿who created you and those before you﴾ means that among the requirements of worship is that Allah is the Creator of all people. As we have said, there is no doubt in the matter of creation, because no one can claim that he created himself or created this universe. Rather, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, asks us to acknowledge the direct causality in our existence: the father and the mother are here a cause of the existence of the human being. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents. Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them [so much as] "uff," and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 23).

Thus we see that the Truth has honored causality in the originator, although He, glorified and exalted is He, is the Originator who created everything. Yet Allah honors the work of the human being, even though he is only a cause, for wealth is Allah's wealth, He gives it to whomever He wills. Yet we find the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, urging charity, saying:

﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ (part of verse 245, Surah al-Baqarah).

It is as if He, glorified is He, has honored the human being's work in acquiring wealth, although the wealth is Allah's wealth. So He, the Supreme Creator, said: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ Thus the mercy of the Truth toward creation becomes manifest.

Allah says: ﴿that you may become righteous.﴾ Righteous (tattaqun) from what? From the attributes of majesty (jalal) of Allah. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has attributes of majesty and attributes of beauty (jamal). The attributes of majesty are "the Compeller (al-Jabbar), the Subduer (al-Qahhar), the Proud (al-Mutakabbir), the Strong (al-Qawi), the Able (al-Qadir), the Powerful (al-Muqtadir), the Harmful (al-Darr)," and others among the attributes of majesty.

So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wants us to place between ourselves and the attributes of His majesty a shield, so that we do not anger Allah and He does not deal with us through the consequences of His attributes of majesty, and that we hold fast to the attributes of the beauty of Allah: the Merciful (al-Rahim), the Loving (al-Wadud), the Forgiving (al-Ghaffar), the Accepter of Repentance (al-Tawwab). If we succeed in that, we have salvation from the Fire, which is one of the armies of Allah and among the instruments of His majesty.

Nevertheless, we must be mindful that when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says ﴿O mankind﴾ He is addressing all people. If the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wishes to address the believers, He says: ﴿O you who believe﴾, meaning, O you who have believed in Allah as God and have entered into a covenant of faith with Him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 22:

﴿Who made the earth a bed for you, and the sky a canopy, and sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you. So do not set up rivals to God while you know.﴾

Having shown us that the bounty of His lordship, which He bestows on all His creatures, believer and disbeliever alike, should suffice for people to believe, all of them, He began to show us signs of the bounty of lordship and to draw our attention to them, so that whoever has not believed, when he reads these signs, faith may enter his heart. God, glorified and exalted, draws our attention to the creation of the earth in His saying, ﴿Who made the earth a bed for you﴾.

The earth is the place in which people live, and no one can claim that he created the earth or brought it into existence. It is therefore a sign of lordship which does not require intellectual effort for us to take heed of it, because it is an obvious matter settled for God, glorified and exalted. His saying, ﴿a bed [firash]﴾, suggests that He prepared the earth for mankind in a comfortable preparation, just as you spread on the ground something you sit or sleep on, so it becomes a bed that comforts you.

We inherit the earth generation after generation, and it is suitable for all our lives, from the time the earth was created until the Day of Resurrection, it will remain a bed for man.

Some people may say that if you sleep on the ground, it may be uncomfortable, with pebbles or other things beneath you that bother you. We say that the first man used to sleep on it comfortably, so the necessity of sleep is possible on the earth.

When civilization advanced and luxury increased, the earth remained a bed, despite the soft things that were found upon it. It is as if God, the Exalted, prepared it for us in a preparation that suits every generation. Every generation has been made comfortable in living by the advance of civilization, and God, glorified and exalted, has revealed of knowledge that by which the earth is made pliable to Him and made a bed.

We observe that God, glorified and exalted, says in another verse:

﴿He made for you the earth a cradle﴾ (part of verse 10, Surah al-Zukhruf).

The mahd is the bed of the infant, and it must be comfortable, because if an infant finds in his bed anything that troubles him, he does not possess the means by which he can make himself comfortable, and therefore the mother prepares the place where her child sleeps, so that he sleeps a comfortable sleep. But He who prepares the earth for all His creatures is God, glorified and exalted; He makes it a bed for His servants. And if you read His saying, glorified and exalted:

﴿It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its broad paths and eat of His provision﴾ (part of verse 15, Surah al-Mulk).

the meaning of that is that God, glorified and exalted, made the earth obedient to man, giving him everything he needs.

God, glorified and exalted, turns to the sky and says: "and the sky a canopy [binā']." Binā' indicates firmness and cohesion. That is, the sky, which is above you, you see nothing holding it up so that it does not fall upon you. It is a firm, solid ceiling. God confirms this meaning with His saying:

﴿And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission﴾ (part of verse 65, Surah al-Hajj).

And in another verse He says:

﴿And We made the sky a protected ceiling﴾ (part of verse 32, Surah al-Anbiya').

The purpose of all these verses is that we may be reassured, as we live on the earth, that the sky will not collapse upon us, because God preserves it.

So among the signs of God, glorified and exalted, in the earth is that He made it a bed, that is, prepared and comfortable for human life. And the preservation of the sky by His power, glorified is He, so it remains in its place, not threatening the inhabitants of the earth or frightening them that it may fall upon them. Then He brought another sign:

﴿And sent down from the sky water, and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾

It is as if God, glorified and exalted, placed in the earth the means of sustaining life, and did not leave man on the earth without providing him the means of continuing his life. The rain descends from the sky, and the sky is everything that is above you and shades you. Thereby crops and fruit grow, and this is provision for us. People differ concerning the matter of provision. Provision is what one benefits from, not merely what one obtains. You may gain abundant wealth but not spend it or benefit from it, so this is not your provision but the provision of another, and you remain a guardian over it, not spending a single piece of it until you deliver it to its owner. In the view of most people, provision is wealth. The Messenger, peace be upon him, said: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' Do you have from your wealth, O son of Adam, anything but what you eat and consume, what you wear and wear out, or what you give in charity and thus make go on?" (1)

This is the provision of wealth, and it is part of provision. But there is the provision of health, the provision of a child, the provision of food, the provision of blessing. Every blessing from God, glorified and exalted, is provision, not wealth alone.

God, glorified and exalted, wants by this noble verse to draw our attention to reflect a little on Him who created this universe, so that we know that before He created man, He created for him the elements of his survival. But this preparation did not stop at material life. Rather, just as He prepared for us the means of our material life, He prepared for us the means of our spiritual life, or the values in existence. And if you read in Surah al-Rahman His saying, glorified and exalted:

﴿The Most Merciful. Taught the Qur'an. Created man. Taught him eloquence.﴾ (Surah al-Rahman)

you will find that the Qur'an gives us the values of life, without which the whole world becomes worthless. Because the world is a test or examination for a coming life in the Hereafter. If you do not take it for its task, that it is the path which leads you to Paradise, its value is entirely wasted.

And the world gives you nothing but punishment in the Hereafter.

God, glorified and exalted, has linked provision in this verse to the sky, saying: ﴿and brought forth thereby fruits as provision for you﴾.

To draw our attention to the fact that provision comes only from above. God, glorified and exalted, gave the example of water because it is direct provision, perceptible to us, and water descends from the sky in its purest form, distilled. Everything that comes to us from the sky has elevation. It descends to increase the ascent of the life of values, a process which, if men wanted to carry out, they could not, because it would cost millions of pounds, to give us water that would not suffice a single family. But God, glorified and exalted, sent down from the sky water in its purest form, so that by it fruits may grow, which guarantee the continuation of life in this universe. And after we understand all these blessings, and the miracle in them, and comprehend them, the Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿So do not set up rivals to God while you know.﴾

"Andād" is the plural of nid, and nid is the equal or the like. Any mind with a grain of thought keeps away from such a thing, and does not make for God any likeness or equal, nor associate anyone with God. God is one in His power, one in His might, one in His creation, one in His essence, and one in His attributes.

There is no comparison between the attributes of God, the Exalted, and the attributes of creatures. God gave each of us a mind with which to think. If this matter were presented to the mind, it would reject it entirely, because it does not accord with reason or logic. Therefore the Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿while you know﴾.

That is, you know this well with your minds, because the nature of the mind rejects this entirely. Who can claim that he created you and those before you? And who can claim, even falsely, that he is the one who made the earth a bed, and made the sky a protected ceiling, or sent down rain and caused crops to grow? No one. So you know that all reason belongs to God alone, and since there is no opponent and none could exist, the matter is settled for the Blessed and Exalted.

And God, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And among the people are those who take, besides God, equals [andād], loving them as they love God; but those who believe are stronger in love for God﴾ (part of verse 165, Surah al-Baqarah).

Why did these people take equals for God? Because they want a religion without a method. They want to satisfy the innate faith that God created in them, while at the same time following their desires. When they considered this, they found that the best way was to choose a god without a method, who asks nothing of them. Therefore every deviant call finds that it permits what God has forbidden and releases man from all the obligations of faith, such as prayer, zakat, jihad, and others.

As for those who believe, they know that God, glorified and exalted, set His method for the benefit of man: God does not benefit from our prayer, nor from our zakat, nor from the method of faith at all, but we are the ones who benefit from God's mercy, from His blessings, and from His Garden in the Hereafter.

Because those who believe know this, they love God with intense love, while those who disbelieve, despite all they claim, in the hour of hardship turn to God, glorified and exalted, as the sole refuge and shelter. Read His saying, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing; but when We remove his harm, he continues on as if he had never called upon Us for harm that touched him﴾ (part of verse 12, Surah Yunus).

Why do they not call upon the equals? Because a person never deceives himself at the hour of peril, and because these people know by their minds that there can be no equals to God. But they take them for worldly purposes. When danger comes, he turns to God, glorified and exalted, because he knows with certainty that He alone removes harm. The barber who treats people with quackery: if his son falls ill, he hurries him to the doctor, because he deceives himself; but he cannot deceive himself.

Al-Asma'i was once standing at the Ka'bah, and he heard a Bedouin supplicating and saying: "O Lord, You know that I am disobedient to You, and it was Your right over me that I should not call upon You while I am disobedient. But I know that there is no god but You, so to whom shall I go?" Al-Asma'i said: "O man, God will forgive you for the goodness of your request."

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, and Ahmad in the version of Muslim, with its chain through Mutarrif from his father.

Having made clear to us that those who take rivals besides God rely on no logic or reason, but rather on immediate worldly desires, God, glorified and exalted, wanted to present the challenge concerning the Noble Qur'an, the everlasting miracle of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so as to prove to them that if God, glorified and exalted, made the creation of the universe a tangible miracle, the Qur'an is a method that is miraculous in a profound way. God, majestic in His majesty, said:

﴿And if you are in doubt﴾. The address here is to every disbeliever and hypocrite who is not a believer, because those who believe in God and His Messenger have no doubt in their hearts. Rather, they believe that the Qur'an is revealed by God and conveyed to Muhammad (ﷺ) through revelation sent down from heaven.

Al-rayb (doubt) is doubt. God's words ﴿if you are in doubt﴾ mean: if you are in doubt. From where does this doubt come, when the miracle surrounds the Qur'an and its Messenger (ﷺ)? What are the justifications for doubt, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) neither read nor wrote, and was not known for eloquence or poetry among his people, such that he could bring from himself this miraculous speech, which the masters of Arab poets, who were trained in eloquence and language, could not match with a single verse? This is one point. The second is that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) never lied, and no lie was known of him before he was commissioned as a messenger. Rather, they used to call him (ﷺ) "the Truthful, the Trustworthy." Those who called the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by these titles are the same ones who accused him that the Qur'an is not from God. Would the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, be truthful with people and lie about God? This is impossible.

No one among the masters of Arabic rhetoric could have brought the speech that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought, which is the Qur'an. And the knowledge revealed in the Noble Qur'an was not known to any human at that time. So how did the unlettered Prophet bring this miraculous speech and this knowledge that no human knows? If he had sat with a teacher or read the books of ancient civilizations, they would have said: perhaps he derived it from them. But he did not do that.

So from where did doubt enter their hearts? Undoubtedly it entered through the gate of falsehood, and falsehood has no proof. Without doubt, they exposed themselves, for they did not doubt the Qur'an, but they wanted it to be sent down upon a leader of the chiefs of Quraysh. Read the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted:

﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of great standing from the two cities?"﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf).

These doubters did not find an argument to confront the Qur'an with, so they said, "He is a sorcerer." But does the bewitched have will in the presence of the sorcerer? If he were a sorcerer, why did he not bewitch you? They also said, "He is a madman." But the madman acts without logic: he laughs without cause, he weeps without cause, and he strikes people without cause. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted, answered them with His words:

﴿Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe. You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman. And indeed for you is a reward never cut off. And indeed you are of a great moral character.﴾ (Surat al-Qalam).

Can a madman be of great moral character? Thus, all the causes of doubt, or the reasons that stir suspicion, do not exist and are not available. There is not a single genuine cause that would make them doubt that the Qur'an is not from God. Yet they are the ones who said, as the Truth, blessed and exalted, narrates to us:

﴿And when they said, "O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ (Surat al-Anfal).

So all causes of doubt are absent, and the causes of certainty are present, yet they doubted and were uncertain. As for God's words, glorified and exalted:

﴿from what We sent down upon Our servant﴾.

The Qur'an existed in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) before man was created. When the time came for it to take up its mission in the universe, it descended from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven all at once, and then God, glorified and exalted, sent it down upon His Messenger (ﷺ) according to what the events and occasions required.

Thus His words ﴿nazzalna﴾ (We sent down) mean: it was sent down from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven all at once. And His words ﴿anzala﴾ (He sent down) mean: He sent it down to Muhammad (ﷺ) as verses, according to the demands of events and occasions.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿upon Our servant﴾, and this requires a pause. God, majestic in His majesty, has slaves ('abid) and has servants ('ibad). Every creature of God in His universe is a slave of God, glorified and exalted; they cannot step outside God's will or His determination. These are the slaves. But the servants ('ibad) are those whose desires have become united with what God, glorified and exalted, wills. They have abandoned their worldly choice, so as to become obedient to God by their own choice; that is, they have become equal with those who are compelled, in that they have chosen God's method and left every choice that contradicts it.

These are the servants. If you read the Noble Qur'an, you find that God, glorified and exalted, refers to the servants as the righteous among mankind, and the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me and believe in Me that they may be guided.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah).

This is not for every creature of God, but for the servants: those who, when God says to them "do," they do, and when God says "do not," they do not. That is, they do not oppose God's method, glorified and exalted, through their power of choice. Therefore, in jihad, the Truth, glorified and exalted, does not call the mujahidin slaves; rather, He, majestic in majesty, says:

﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they went through the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.﴾ (Surat al-Isra').

Some orientalists who seek to attack the Noble Qur'an say that the word "servants" ('ibad) was used to describe the non-believer in God's words: ﴿Did you misguide these My servants, or did they themselves stray from the way?﴾ (part of verse 17, Surat al-Furqan).
