We say: you have not understood that this is the moment of reckoning in the Hereafter, and in the Hereafter we are all servants, because we are all compelled; no one has choice in the Hereafter. Human choice ends at the moment of death agony, and then the human becomes compelled.

So we are all servants in the Hereafter, but the difference between slaves and servants lies only in the worldly life. Servanthood is the highest rank of nearness to God, the Exalted, because you come to God obediently, carrying out His method by your own choice. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was offered to be a king-messenger or a servant-messenger, and he chose to be a servant-messenger. If we wish to know the meaning of servanthood, we read in Surat al-Isra':

﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed.﴾ (part of verse 1, Surat al-Isra').

We see that this is at the highest degree of God's bounty, glorified and exalted, upon His Messenger (ﷺ), in the great miracle that did not happen to any human before him (ﷺ), whether he was a messenger or not, and will not happen to any human after him. That is because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ascended through the seven heavens in spirit and body, then returned to the earth. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) surpassed the station of Gabriel, passing beyond the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), which is the place where the knowledge of God's creation, of humans and of the nearest angels, comes to an end. The humanity of the Messenger was a great subject of dispute from the time heavenly messages began, and until our present age. Read His words, exalted is He:

﴿The eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, "We see you as nothing but a human like us."﴾ (part of verse 27, Surat Hud).

And His words:

﴿So they said, "Shall we follow a single human from among us? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness."﴾ (Surat al-Qamar).

And His words:

﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has God sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ (Surat al-Isra').

And His words:

﴿And if you obey a human like yourselves, indeed you would then be losers.﴾ (Surat al-Mu'minun).

So the humanity of the Messenger was taken as an argument by those who did not want to believe, while the Messenger is a conveyor from God, and he must be of the same kind as the people to whom he was sent. He must have lived among them for a period before the mission and become known for trustworthiness and truthfulness, so that they could not call him a liar. At the same time, he is a model. Therefore he must be of their kind, because he will apply the method practically before them. Had he been of another kind, they would have said, "We cannot bear what You have charged us with, O Lord, because this Messenger of God is created from a substance other than ours and is compelled to obedience."

So the humanity of the Messenger is necessary. Whoever tries to give the Messenger a non-human attribute is only trying to diminish the perfections of God's messages, and God, glorified and exalted, is not incapable of turning humans into angels. Read His words, exalted is He:

﴿And if We willed, We would have made from you angels upon the earth, succeeding one another.﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf, verse 60).

So the humanity of the Messenger is part of the completeness of the mission.

Then comes the challenge from God, glorified and exalted: ﴿then produce a surah like it﴾. What is required is that the Arabs produce a surah like what the Noble Qur'an brought. The witnesses whom God calls upon are weak witnesses, witnesses from among humans, not a testimony from God about the unseen. God, glorified and exalted, placed in this verse most of the doubts so that we may examine them, and so that we may afterwards arrive at the essence of the Qur'anic miracle.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, proceeded gradually in the challenge with the disbelievers. He asked them to produce something like the Qur'an, then asked for ten surahs like it, and then escalated the challenge, asking for a single surah. The descent in the challenge from the whole Qur'an to ten surahs, to one surah, is evidence against those he challenged. They could not produce something like the Qur'an, so He says: then produce ten surahs. They cannot, and their position becomes a cause for mockery, so He says: then produce a surah. This is the ultimate contempt for those whom God, glorified and exalted, challenged, and a proof that they are unable to do anything. The word ﴿bi-mithlihi﴾ (like it) means that the Truth, glorified and exalted, asks for a likeness and does not require the text of the Qur'an itself. This is an excess and an increase in showing the incapacity of the people who do not believe in God and who doubt the Qur'an. God's words: ﴿and call your witnesses﴾.

Its meaning is that God, glorified and exalted, in addition to the challenge, demands that they bring their witnesses themselves and present the verse to them, so that these witnesses may judge whether what they have brought is like the Qur'an or not. Is this not a display of the utmost strength of God, glorified and exalted, since He did not stipulate witnesses from among the angels, nor witnesses from among those known for truthfulness who testify to the truth? Rather, the Truth, glorified and exalted, left it to them to bring whatever witnesses they wished, and these witnesses will not be able to testify that the words of these doubters are equal to a surah of the Qur'an.

God, glorified and exalted, asked them to bring any witnesses partial to them, and He extended it to all kinds of creatures on earth, saying: ﴿besides God, if you are truthful﴾. But beware of saying, "God bears witness that what we have brought is like the Qur'an," because you would then have lied against God and claimed something God, glorified and exalted, did not say.

But what is the meaning of His words: ﴿if you are truthful﴾? Truthful in what? And what is truthfulness? Truthfulness is the opposite of falsehood, and truthfulness and falsehood are each relative. We all know that there is speech that is not beneficial. If you say "Muhammad" and remain silent, the listener will ask you, "What do you mean by your saying Muhammad?" His asking is a sign that he has gained nothing. But if he asks you, "Who is with you?" and you answer, "Muhammad," it is as if you are telling him that you have a Muhammad with you. This is one word, but you understood it in the sense you took from the questioner's speech. Therefore do not say a single word; rather, say beneficial speech. So beneficial speech is that which keeps the hearer silent about it.

Every speaker, before uttering speech, has a mental relation to what he will say, which he expresses by a verbal relation. But there is also an external relation to what he says, which represents reality.

Ai a

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 24:

﴿And if you do not, and you will never do, then fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.﴾ (2:24)

After Allah, glorified and exalted be He, spoke of the proofs on which the doubters of the Noble Qur'an rely, proofs that rest on neither reason nor logic, He challenged them to bring a surah like the Qur'an, and to seek help from whomever they wish besides Allah, because the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and Allah, glorified be He, is its speaker. Since they attempt to cast doubt on the claim that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and that it was sent down from Allah, let them seek help from whomever they wish to bring forth a verse like it, for the challenge here cannot be fulfilled unless they enlist all powers other than Allah, glorified and exalted be He.

Then, after this, the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, brings the outcome before the challenge is even completed, because Allah, glorified be He, knows that they will not do it and will not be able to do it.

His saying, glorified be He, ﴿And if you do not, and you will never do﴾ means that He has judged them to fail at the time the Qur'an was revealed, and after its revelation until the Day of Resurrection, because nothing is hidden from His knowledge. He is All-Knowing of everything. The phrase "if you do not" (lam taf'alu), when it comes, may stir doubt, for we know that the conditional particle *in* ("if") implies doubt, since the matter, for it to be realized, depends on a condition. If you say, "If you study, you will succeed," there is doubt in the matter. But if you say, as the Truth says, ﴿When the help of Allah comes, and the victory﴾ (110:1), this means that the help of Allah is certainly coming.

*In* is a particle, and *idha* ("when") is an adverb of time, and every event needs a place and a time. So when you use a conditional particle, this means that you are bringing it close to the element that constitutes the act and the event. If you want to express something that will certainly happen, you say *idha*; and if you want to cast doubt on it, you say *in*. Allah, glorified be He, said ﴿fa-in lam taf'alu﴾, and because the act is possible to occur, He wished to weigh the side that prevents it, so He said ﴿wa-lan taf'alu﴾ ("and you will never do"). This is a matter of choice. If you speak of a matter of choice and then judge that it will never happen, it is as though your power were what prevented it from being done. It cannot be said that you forced it not to happen. No: you knew it would never happen. Their preparations cannot enable them to do it.

These are among the matters within the informative statements of the Noble Qur'an concerning the unseen realities about which it gives news. When Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them﴾ (27:14), this means that they affirm them in their hearts, but their tongues do not acknowledge it. And His saying, exalted be He, ﴿fa-in lam taf'alu wa-lan taf'alu﴾ means that the doubt is manufactured within their souls; they do not want to believe, and therefore they bring up a fabricated pretext for not believing. Their thinking has settled on not believing, and as long as this is what you have decided, you will keep searching for fabricated excuses for not believing.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿So fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾.

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, wants to draw our attention to another image of the helplessness of these disbelievers. They sought out excuses to justify their unbelief, and they pretended to doubt the Noble Qur'an. He says to them: if you truly had power and self-determination, then prevent yourselves from entering the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, just as you prevented yourselves from believing in this world.

This is a warning from Allah. He granted them self-determination in this world, and they did not choose under compulsion; rather, they chose not to believe by the will of choice that Allah gave them. But there is a time in which there is no choice, and that is the Hereafter. So try to protect yourselves in the Hereafter from the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. But no one will have any choice then. Allah, glorified be He, says on that Day:

﴿To whom belongs the dominion this Day? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16)

And He, majestic is His majesty, says:

﴿The Day when no soul will avail another soul in anything, and the command that Day will be with Allah.﴾ (82:19)

So your will, which prevented you from believing, will not protect you that Day from the punishment of the Fire. Read His saying:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you are to it bound to come.﴾ (21:98)

Why are they and what they worship (mentioned together)? Because the worshipper hopes for the benefit of the one worshipped. So when each of them sees the other in punishment, the anguish will be greater. Therefore, the stones and idols they worshipped will be with them in the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. This is not a punishment for the stones and idols, for they are a creation subdued to Allah and glorifying Him; rather, these idols and stones will be content as they burn those who disbelieved in Allah, and they will say: "You worshipped us, while we are more worthy of worship by Allah than those who seek forgiveness at dawn."

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿prepared for the disbelievers﴾. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, informs them while they are in this world that the Fire has been prepared for the disbelievers. His saying, exalted be He, "the Fire prepared for the disbelievers," is an assurance of utmost reassurance for the believer and a terror of utmost terror for the disbeliever. His saying ﴿prepared﴾ means that it already exists in fact, even though we do not see it, and that it is created, even though it is hidden from us.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Paradise was displayed to me, and if I had wished, I would have brought you a cluster from it."

This is evidence that it already exists.

When the believer knows that Paradise already exists and that faith will lead him to it, he feels happiness and longs for Paradise. When he hears the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿Those are the inheritors, who will inherit Paradise; they will abide therein forever.﴾ (23:10–11)

As you recite this noble verse, you know that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, will place you in Paradise to take what was meant for others, because inheritance comes to you from someone else. Allah's knowledge, glorified and exalted be He, preceded the creation of all people. Before He created, He prepared for each of His creatures a seat in the Fire and a seat in Paradise. Those who will enter the Fire to abide therein, their seats in Paradise will be empty, and Allah, glorified and exalted be He, will give them to the believers to inherit, atop their seats and dwellings in Paradise. And when the Truth, glorified be He, says ﴿prepared﴾, it is indeed already existing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 25:

﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds: that for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom as provision, they say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in semblance; and for them therein are purified spouses, and they therein are abiding.﴾ (2:25)

After Allah, glorified and exalted, explained to us the fate of the disbelievers who cast doubt upon the Qur'an in order to take that as an excuse for not believing, He said: If you have chosen not to believe, using the choice I gave you in the world, then in the Hereafter you will not be able to protect yourselves from the Fire, and you will have no will of your own.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, presents the opposite picture. Whenever the noble Qur'an mentions Paradise, Allah follows it with the opposite picture, which is punishment by the Fire; and whenever it mentions the Fire with its torment and its blaze, it mentions Paradise after it. This juxtaposition has an effect in driving faith into souls. When a person reads a surah about punishment and then comes to bliss, he knows that he has succeeded twice. The one who is drawn away from the Fire and does not enter it has achieved a success and a blessing; then, if he enters Paradise, that is another blessing. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, says:

﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into the Garden has indeed triumphed﴾ (part of 3:185).

He did not say, "Whoever is admitted into the Garden has triumphed," because merely being drawn away from the Fire is a great triumph... in the Hereafter. After the reckoning, the Sirat is laid over Hell, and the believers and the disbelievers cross over it. The believers traverse the straight path, each according to his deeds: some of them pass as swiftly as lightning, and some pass more slowly, and so on, while the disbelievers fall into the Fire. But why do the believers pass over the Sirat? Allah, exalted is He, said:

﴿And there is none of you but will come to it. That is upon your Lord a decree that must be carried out. Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it on their knees﴾ (19:71-72).

Because merely seeing Hell is a great blessing for the believers: when they see the terrible torment from which faith saved them, each of them feels the blessing of Allah upon him, that He saved him from this torment. The people of the Fire and the people of Paradise see one another. When the people of Paradise see the people of the Fire, they feel the immense blessing of Allah upon them, because He saved them from it; and when the people of the Fire see the people of Paradise, they feel the immense anger of Allah upon them, that He deprived them of His bounty. So this sight is a bliss for the people of Paradise and an increase in torment for the people of the Fire. Allah, exalted is He, says:

"And give good tidings" (wa-bashshir). Glad tidings (bushra) is the announcement of something pleasing that is coming but whose time has not yet arrived. So when you give a person good news, you announce to him something pleasing that is coming. The glad tidings here come after the warning to the disbelievers.

Warning (indhar) is the announcement of a frightening matter whose time has not yet arrived.

But glad tidings sometimes appear in the noble Qur'an while intending the disbelievers. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Woe to every sinful liar, who hears the verses of Allah recited to him and then persists arrogantly as though he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (45:7-8).

The glad tidings here are sarcastic, from Allah, exalted is He. The Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to increase the punishment of the disbelievers, for when they hear the words "so give them tidings," they assume they will hear something pleasing, and then the painful punishment comes to add grief upon grief.

The Truth, exalted is He, says: ﴿And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ Glad tidings here is information of good coming to the believers, and faith is the inner reserve from which behavior arises. For whoever believes in a cause works for it: the student studies because he believes he will succeed, and every behavioral action must have a doctrinal source. Faith means that the movement of life harmonizes with what is in the heart, in accordance with the will of Allah, exalted is He; and the order of life can only stand upon faith... So righteous deeds have faith as their source. For this reason the noble Qur'an says:

﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ (103:1-3).

And in another verse: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah, does righteousness, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ (41:33).

But is it enough to announce that I am a Muslim? No, rather this declaration must be accompanied by acting in accordance with the will of Allah, exalted is He.

The Truth, exalted is He, wants to draw our attention... to the fact that our saying "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah" must be accompanied by action in accordance with the methodology of Islam. Our utterance of the testimony does not add anything to the dominion of Allah. Allah, blessed and exalted, testified to His own oneness of divinity, and this is the testimony of the Essence to the Essence. Then the angels testified by witnessing, since they see Him, glorified and exalted is He. Then those possessed of knowledge testified by evidence, by what Allah, majestic in majesty, has opened to them of knowledge. Concerning this the Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge, [that He is] maintaining [creation] in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (3:18).

But the Truth, glorified and exalted, wants the believers to act upon the methodology... Why? So that the movement of life does not conflict but supports itself. And as long as the movement of life is upright, it becomes a life that is mutually supportive and strong. When Islam spread across the regions of the earth, the goal was not merely that people believe for the sake of belief; rather, the movement of life must harmonize with the methodology of Islam. If the movement of life departs from the methodology of Islam, then it does not serve the cause of religion whether people believe or do not believe. For this reason faith and righteous deeds must be stated together: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ "Righteous deeds" (al-salihat) is the plural of "salihah," and salihah is that which is upright in accordance with the methodology, whose opposite is corruption. When a person encounters existence, the least of righteous deeds is that he leaves the righteous as it is in its righteousness or increases it in righteousness.

The Truth, blessed and exalted, gives glad tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds of gardens beneath which rivers flow. "Gardens" (jannat) is the plural of "jannah," and it is plural because they are many and varied. Within each garden there are levels more than in this world. Read His saying, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿See how We have preferred some of them over others; and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference﴾ (17:21).

The gardens themselves are varied: there are the Gardens of Firdaws, the Gardens of Eden, and the Gardens of Bliss. There is the Abode of Eternity, the Abode of Peace, and the Garden of Refuge. There is 'Illiyyun, which is the highest and best of the gardens, and the highest of what is in them is enjoying the vision of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He. This is a bliss that far surpasses any bliss of food and drink in this world. Food and drink for the people of Paradise are not out of hunger or thirst, but only out of desire and enjoyment. Allah, majestic in majesty, in this verse promises something unseen. Therefore, in order to bring the meaning near to the human mind, it is necessary to use words that are witnessed and existent, that is, referring to a reality we witness. Read His saying, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do﴾ (32:17).

So what exists in Paradise is not known by any soul in this world, and there is no word in language that expresses it, nor any faculty of knowledge such as hearing or sight that has perceived it. For this reason the Truth, blessed and exalted, used words that correspond to our minds and perception, saying: ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow.﴾ Yet there are other verses that say "rivers flow beneath them" (tajri tahtaha al-anhar). What is the difference between the two? "Rivers flow beneath them" means the water springs from a distant place and passes beneath them. But His saying, ﴿beneath which rivers flow,﴾ suggests that the rivers spring up beneath them, so that no one fears that the water coming from afar will be cut off or dry up. This is an added reassurance to the believers that the bliss of Paradise is lasting and eternal.

And as long as there is water, there is greenery and a beautiful sight, and there must be fruit. In His saying, ﴿Whenever they are provided with a fruit therefrom as provision, they say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in semblance﴾, there is a discussion of the fruit of Paradise. The fruit of Paradise differs from the fruit of this world. In this world you must go to the fruit and bring it, or someone else brings it to you. But in Paradise the fruit comes to you: as soon as you desire it, you find it in your hand. You may think there is a resemblance between the fruit of this world and the fruit of Paradise, but the fruit in Paradise is not like the fruit of this world, neither in its taste nor its smell. The people of Paradise see its fruit and speak, saying, perhaps this fruit is the mango or the fig that we ate in this world. But in reality it differs completely: the shape may be similar, but the taste and everything else is different.

In this world every food has waste that a person expels. But in the Hereafter food has no waste; a person eats as he wishes without needing to expel waste, because the fruits of this world differ from those of the Hereafter in their composition.

So in Paradise the rivers differ, the fruits differ, and provision in Paradise comes from Allah, glorified and exalted, who says ﴿to a thing: "Be," and it is﴾, and no one performs any work.

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And for them therein are purified spouses, and they therein are abiding.﴾

A wife is the enjoyment of a person in this world if she is righteous, and a source of distress to him if she is not. There are distresses a wife can place in her husband's life that make him wretched in his life: such as being sharp-tongued or constantly quarrelsome, or not giving attention to her husband, or trying to stir him up by making him suspicious of her. In the Hereafter, however, all these distresses vanish by the command of Allah. The wife in the Hereafter is purified from everything her husband dislikes in her, and what he did not love in this world disappears. The believers in the Hereafter are purified from all the defects and troubles of this world, and first among them rancor and hatred. Read His saying, majestic in majesty:

﴿And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [as] brothers, upon couches facing each other﴾ (15:47).

So the standards of this world will vanish, and everything you dislike in this world you will not find in the Hereafter. If anything has troubled your life in this world, it will vanish in the Hereafter. The Truth, blessed and exalted, gave the example of wives because a wife is her husband's enjoyment in this world, and she is the one who can turn his life into bliss or into hell.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they therein are abiding,﴾ means there is no death in the Hereafter, and death will never exist there at all; rather there is eternal abiding, either in Paradise or in the Fire.

After the Blessed and Exalted Lord spoke of Paradise and gave us a parable that brings close to us the immense forms of bliss that a person will enjoy in Paradise, He wished to clarify for us the faith-based path that every believer must follow. This is because Allah, glory be to Him, does not impose worship on a disbeliever. But the person who has consented to enter faith in Allah, majestic in His majesty, has entered into a covenant of faith with Allah, blessed and exalted. Since he has entered this covenant of faith, he receives from Allah His method of "do" and "do not do." He must apply this method without asking about the wisdom behind everything, because faith is belief in the unseen. If the thing itself is hidden from us, how can we want to know its wisdom?

The wisdom of any faith-based obligation is this: it proceeds from Allah, glory be to Him. Since it proceeds from Allah, it has not come from an equal of yours with whom you could debate. It comes from a God to whom obedience is owed by you, because He is God and you are His worshipper. It is enough that Allah, glory be to Him, said "do," so that we do. And it is enough that He said "do not do," so that we do not do.

The wisdom is hidden from you, but the command's coming from Allah is itself the wisdom, and it is what makes obedience obligatory. I pray because Allah prescribed prayer, not as a kind of physical exercise. I perform ablution because the Blessed and Exalted Lord commanded us to perform ablution before prayer, not as a kind of cleanliness. I fast because Allah commanded me to fast, and not so that I may feel the hunger of the poor. For if prayer were exercise, we would have replaced it with exercise in the sports fields. And if ablution were cleanliness, we would bathe before every prayer. And if fasting were so that we would feel hunger, it would not have been obligatory on the poor to fast, since they already know the meaning of hunger.

So every obligation from Allah we perform because Allah has prescribed it, and we do not perform it for any other reason. And everything that comes to us from Allah, in the form of the Qur'an, we receive as the speech of Allah, and we do not receive it in any other manner. This is the faith that Allah wants us to hold fast to, and that should be the conduct of our lives.

That is an introduction that had to precede our understanding of the noble verse: "Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even of] a mosquito or what is more than that" (2:26). When Allah gave the parable of the mosquito, the disbelievers received it in its worldly sense without perceiving its true meaning. They said: how can Allah give the example of a mosquito, that weak creature, which you can kill by striking it with anything or with your palm, so that it dies? Why did the Blessed and Exalted Lord not give as an example the elephant, which is huge in body and very strong, or the lion, which is stronger than a human? Instead He gave us the mosquito as an example, and they said: "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" (2:26). They did not realize that this mosquito, tiny in size, is a miracle of creation. For in this small size Allah, glory be to Him, placed all the organs necessary for its life. It has two eyes, and it has a very fine proboscis, yet it is able to pierce a person's skin and break the blood vessels beneath the skin in order to suck a person's blood.

The mosquito also has legs, wings, a reproductive system, and everything necessary for its life. All of this is in this tiny size. The smaller a thing is, the greater the precision of creation it requires.

We observe in our human life that, for example, when man invented the clock, it was so large that it needed a big place. As civilization advanced and man progressed in his industry, civilization, and development, the size became small and fine, and clockmaking continued to become more delicate, until it became possible to make a watch the size of a ring or smaller. When the invention of the radio began, its size was large, and now it has become so refined that you can place it in your pocket or smaller. In all industries, as they advance, their size shrinks, because that requires skilled craftsmanship and scientific progress.

Thus, when Allah gave the mosquito and what is beyond it as an example, that is, what is smaller than it in size, the Blessed and Exalted Lord wanted to draw our attention to the precision of creation. The more subtle a thing is and the smaller its size, the more precise creation it requires. But the disbelievers did not take the meaning in this way. They took it in the simple worldly sense, which does not represent the truth.

When Allah, glory be to Him, gave this example, the believers received it as the speech of Allah. They received it through the logic of faith in Allah, and they affirmed it, whether they understood it or not, because the believer affirms everything that comes from Allah, whether or not he knows its wisdom. Consider the words of the Blessed and Exalted Lord:

"And We had certainly brought them a Book which We detailed with knowledge, as guidance and mercy for a people who believe. Do they await except its fulfillment? The day its fulfillment comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: 'The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So do we have any intercessors to intercede for us, or could we be returned so that we may do other than what we used to do?' They have lost themselves, and what they used to invent has gone astray from them" (7:52–53).

Everyone who affirms the Qur'an does not seek its interpretation or the wisdom in its verses. That is why the disbelievers said: "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" The reply of the Blessed and Exalted Lord comes: "He misleads many by it and guides many by it, and He does not mislead by it except the defiantly disobedient" (2:26).

Who are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqin)? They are those who break the covenant of Allah. The first thing in fisq is that the fasiq breaks his covenant. It is said: "fasaqat al-ruṭba," meaning the skin separated from the fruit. When the fruit or the unripe date is red, its skin clings to the fruit so that you cannot pull it off. But when the fruit or date becomes ripe (ruṭab), its skin darkens and separates from the fruit, so that you can pull it off easily. This is the fasiq who has moved away from the method of Allah. He strips away from it easily and smoothly, because he is not attached to it. When you move away from the method of Allah, you are not bound by His commands and prohibitions. So you do not perform the prayer, for example, and you do what Allah has forbidden, because you have departed from His religion.

What made fisq exist is that man was created with choice, able to act or not to act. Through this choice, man corrupted the order of the universe. Everything that has no choice in it, you find performing its task with high precision, like the sun, the moon, the stars, and the earth. All of them follow a precise order that does not break down, because they are subjugated. Had man not been created with choice, it would have been impossible for him to commit fisq, to move away from the method of Allah, and to cause corruption on the earth. But this choice is the foundation of all corruption.

Having explained to us the concept of faith, that we receive from Allah and implement His judgment even if we do not know the wisdom behind it, so that everything that comes from Allah we take with the logic of faith, which is that Allah has said it, and not with the logic of disbelief and doubt. Everything from Allah has the wisdom that it proceeds from the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. The Truth, blessed and exalted, has told us that the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun) are those who turn away from the method of Allah. The Truth wished to show us the attributes of the defiantly disobedient, and He specified them in three attributes:

First: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification.﴾

Second: ﴿And sever what Allah has commanded to be joined.﴾

Third: ﴿And cause corruption in the earth.﴾

Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, specified their judgment, saying: ﴿Those are the losers.﴾ The loss they have reached is from their own deeds, because they abandoned the method and began legislating for themselves according to the desires of the soul. For this reason the Truth, exalted is His majesty, says about them:

﴿Those are the ones who have bought error in exchange for guidance, so their commerce has not profited, nor were they guided.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah).

So they are the ones who chose, and they are the ones who bought error and paid its price from the guidance of Allah. It is as if they had concluded a losing transaction, because the guidance of Allah is what leads us to eternal life and to a bliss that does not cease. The Truth, glorified and exalted, gives us the image in His saying:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties [in exchange] for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. [It is] a promise binding upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in the transaction you have made. That is the great achievement.﴾ (Surat al-Tawbah).

So the believers sold their properties and their lives to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and they were truthful in their covenant. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, they sold the guidance of Allah and bought with it the error of this world. The Truth, glorified and exalted, has mentioned to us the first attribute of the defiantly disobedient: that they have no covenant. Not only with people, but they have no covenant with Allah either. Whenever they make a covenant with Allah, they break it. And Allah loves fulfilment of covenant. For this reason He, exalted is His majesty, says:

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner until he reaches maturity. And fulfill [every] commitment. Indeed, the commitment is ever [that about which one will be] questioned.﴾ (Surat al-Isra').

And He, exalted, says:

﴿And We found not for most of them any fidelity to covenant; and indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

What is the binding covenant that Allah took from His servants, which they broke? It is the first faith, the innate faith present in each of us. Allah, glorified and exalted, took a covenant from all of mankind, and some of them fulfilled it and some of them broke it.

Allah, glorified and exalted, has mentioned to us in the noble Qur'an that there is a binding covenant between Him and the offspring of Adam. So He, exalted is His majesty, said:

﴿And [recall] when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] - lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware."﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

Thus Allah took a covenant from the offspring of Adam that they would believe in Him, and He made them testify that He is their Lord. Heedlessness then came into the hearts with the passing of time, so they broke the covenant and took gods besides Allah. So the first attribute of the defiantly disobedient is that they break the covenant of Allah. And one who breaks a covenant with a human being, such conduct is not accepted by the Truth, glorified and exalted, even with disbelievers and non-believers. Read His saying, blessed and exalted:

﴿except those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists and then they have not been deficient toward you in anything or supported anyone against you. So complete for them their treaty until their term. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.﴾ (Surat al-Tawbah).

Thus we see that the Truth, blessed and exalted, when He announced His disavowal, and the disavowal of His Messenger (ﷺ) and of the believers, from every polytheist disbelieving in a great matter of faith, forbade the disbelievers and hypocrites, in it, from approaching His Sacred House in Makkah, yet He, exalted is His majesty, respected the covenant even with the polytheists, and commanded the believers to fulfil it. So if this is the believer's way with every disbeliever and polytheist, that if you have made a covenant with him, fulfil it until its term, then how about the polytheists who have made a covenant with the Supreme Creator and then break His binding covenant? They have betrayed the method of Allah and His covenant. And if they have no covenant with Allah, glorified and exalted, will they have a covenant with the creation of Allah?!

So the defiantly disobedient have as their first attribute that they have no covenant with their Creator, and no covenant with people. For this reason we never feel safe with them.

Then comes the second attribute of the defiantly disobedient, in His saying:

﴿And sever what Allah has commanded to be joined.﴾ What Allah has commanded to be joined is the kinship tie (silat al-rahim). Allah, exalted, has commanded us to join our kinship ties, for we are all children of Adam. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in the Farewell Pilgrimage: "All of you are from Adam, and Adam was from dust."

Thus we see that there are human bonds to which Allah, glorified and exalted, draws our attention. These bonds begin with the family, then widen to include the neighbourhood or the quarter, then widen to include the state and society, then widen to include all believers, then widen to include the whole world. This is the human brotherhood to which the Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to draw our attention.

But the reminder here is not confined to the human side; it also records that what they did is disobedience and opposition to the command of Allah, exalted. Allah commanded that we join the ties of kinship, and these people came and opposed and disobeyed what Allah had commanded, and severed this connection. So the matter involves opposition to a method and disobedience to one of the commands of Allah, glorified and exalted. Kinship-joining creates a kind of social solidarity among human beings. If a person is struck by a calamity, his relatives hasten to stand with him in his trial, and each of them tries to ease his burden. This cohesion within the family makes it strong in facing events, and none of its members feels lost in this universe, because he is bound to his family and bound to his quarter or village. Thus resentment disappears from society, and family disintegration disappears.

And perhaps if we look at Western societies, which are afflicted with family disintegration, we find that each of them has lost his way and deviated because he feels lost. So he turns to drugs, or to alcohol, or to fornication, and other vices that we see. A lost generation. Who lost it? The absence of kinship-joining. And if we speak of the deviations we see among the young today, we do not blame the young, but we blame the fathers and mothers who abandoned their sons and daughters and neglected the kinship tie. So a generation grows up suffering from psychological complexes without limit. The son who loses the atmosphere of the family loses the balance of his life. And Allah, glorified and exalted, wants believers to be united, loving one another, free of all the complexes that wreck life. Thus the absence of kinship-joining loses entire generations.

Then we come to the third attribute of the defiantly disobedient, in His saying: ﴿And cause corruption in the earth.﴾ We say: everything in the universe is created according to a system: "[who] créated and proportioned, and who determined and [then] guided" (cf. Surat al-A'la), meaning that everything has a guidance that it must follow. But man came into the domain of choice and corrupted the matter of righteousness in the universe.

It is among the mercy of Allah that He placed in His creation a kind of creature that acts compelled, in order to regulate the movement of the higher universe. The sun, the stars, the earth, and the whole universe except humans and jinn, proceed according to a precise system. Why? Because they proceed without any choice of their own. And the Truth, exalted is His majesty, has informed us that, in order for the balance of our life to be upright, let us judge ourselves by the method of Allah, just as the compelled universe is governed by the method of Allah. The meaning of human choice is not that we should turn away from the method of Allah, because Allah has the attribute of compulsion. He could create us compelled, but He gave us choice so that we would come to Him out of love, not out of compulsion. You love desires, but you love Allah more, so you restrict yourself by the method of Allah. So choice was not given to us so that we would corrupt the earth, but it was given to us so that we would come to Allah, glorified and exalted, obedient, not compelled.

For this reason each of us is free to believe or not to believe. This choice demonstrates the beloved-ness of Allah, glorified and exalted, in our hearts. But man, instead of taking choice in order to come to Allah out of love, and thereby attain the greatest reward, took it in order to corrupt the earth.

Corruption is to shift the domain of "do" and "do not": you place this in the place of that. The balance then is reversed, meaning that in what Allah said "do," you do not do it, and in what He said "do not," you do it. You have made the balance of your life upside down. Why? Because we are not governed by a universal rule that organizes people's lives. Each person will set a rule for himself, and each will not do what is incumbent upon him, so collision occurs in life. And every corruption creates ugliness in existence. Suppose you are walking along the road and see a building recently constructed, whose pipes have leaked water. When you see that, you are hurt, because there is ugliness in existence, in a person's lack of trustworthiness in his work. So when a single worker corrupts by lacking sincerity in his work, the universe loses a blessing that Allah loves, namely that you see a beautiful thing and say: "Allah..."

So every person who is not trustworthy in his work corrupts the universe. And every person who is not trustworthy in his character corrupts the universe, and transgresses against the sanctities and property of others. This makes the universe ugly, so that there is no one who feels safe regarding his honour and his wealth.

The aggressor wished to achieve what benefits himself quickly, but he has caused corruption in the universe. Likewise, when a merchant cheats people, and when a person acquires wealth by plunder and theft, Allah then opens for him the worst channels of wealth in existence. He has taken regret through corruption in the earth.

Corruption in the earth is to take a thing out of its balance: you exceed in your desires, you exceed in your greed, you exceed in punishing people, and you exceed in transgressing against the rights of others. And corruption in the earth is that a method is implemented other than the method of Allah.

The absence of the method of Allah means that each of us becomes a slave of his whims. When affairs go according to people's desires, the movement of life brings them misery and evil instead of happiness and security. What we see today of people's complaints is a sign of corruption, because it means that people suffer and no one moves to remove the causes of these complaints. This existence will not be set right, nor will it be freed from corruption, except if we govern by a method that has no whim. And the one who has no whim is the Creator of mankind, the Establisher of the balance of the universe.

And the first manifestations of corruption are that matters are entrusted to those who are not qualified for them, because if authority is given to those who are not its people, then await the Hour, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"When authority is entrusted to those who are not its people, then await the Hour."(1)

Why? Because society then becomes built on hypocrisy and disorder of affairs, not on excellence and sincerity. The one who excels at hypocrisy is the one who reaches the highest ranks, while the one who perfects his work reaches nothing. The result is that a group of ignorant hypocrites are the ones who manage affairs without knowledge. Corruption in the earth is that truth is lost, values are lost, and society becomes a goal: every person wants to achieve his whim regardless of the rights of others. And whoever works and does not reach his right feels there is no benefit in work, so the whole society turns into a group of non-producers.

Corruption in the earth is that we make our minds the ruler, so we do not reflect on the balance of the universe that Allah created, but proceed with our minds planning, so we cut down trees and throw factory waste into rivers and so spoil them, and bring poisonous chemicals with which we spray crops or water channels and rivers, as is happening now, filling it with poison and then eating it, and then we find pollution has filled the universe. The ozone layer has suffered clear damage that exposes the life of human beings on earth to great dangers. The waters of rivers are spoiled and no longer fit for drinking or irrigation. Good departs from the world gradually. And corruption in the earth is that injustice spreads and life becomes an endless chain of misery. And corruption in the earth is that you...

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Hurayrah.

How can you disbelieve in God, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life again, then to Him you will be returned? (28)

In the language, "kayfa" (how) is used to ask about a state. Almighty God used it in this noble verse not as a real question, but to call attention to a strange matter that should not have happened. After all that God related in earlier verses of clear proofs about the creation of the heavens and the earth and the creation of people, proofs that no one can deny or refute, how can you disbelieve in God after these clear proofs? Your disbelief has no proof or logic behind it. A question may be used as a rebuke, as when you say to a man, "How can you curse your father?" or it may express wonder at something someone has done that they should not have done. Both meanings meet. Whether the intent is rebuke or wonder, the meaning is the same: this is something that should not have come from you. Then Almighty God brings other proofs that no one can deny or lie about, so He says, Exalted is His majesty: ﴿And you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die.﴾

Here the discussion moves to the origin of life and death. After God explained what the disbelievers, the defiant, and the hypocrites do of corruption on earth, and of severing what God commanded to be joined, the argument rose to a discussion of life and death. God's saying ﴿You were dead and He gave you life﴾ is a matter that does not admit dispute. They may have been able to argue about not following the method, or about severing what God commanded to be joined, but the matter of life and death no one can dispute. God created us from nothing, and no one has ever claimed that he created people or created himself. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to people and said that the One who created you is God, no one could refute him, and no one will be able to, because we truly were not existing in the world, and God is the One who brought us into being and gave us life.

As for God's saying ﴿then He will cause you to die﴾, no one doubts that he will die. Death is decreed for all people. Creation from nothing is established by proof, and death is established by sensory observation and witnessing.

The matter of death is our way of confronting any atheist. If they say that reason is enough to manage life, and that there is nothing called the unseen, we say: the One who governs creation in bringing into being is the One who governs it in death. The worldly life is a stage between two brackets. The first bracket is that God creates us and brings us into existence, and the journey of life proceeds to the second bracket, in which our humanity goes out and our life stops, which is death. That is, in the journey of life we are from God and return to Him. So the movement of worldly life is a beginning from God in truth and an end in death.

When they spoke about test-tube babies, which is a process for treating infertility more than anything else, they depicted it in a jahili (pre-Islamic ignorance) manner. All that happens is that they take an egg from the mother's womb, in which the vagina is blocked or does not allow natural fertilization. They take this egg from the mother's womb, fertilize it with the husband's sperm, and then implant it in the mother's womb.

They took what is from God's creation: the mother's egg and the man's sperm. All they do is the process of fertilization, yet they call it test-tube babies, as if the test tube could create a child! The truth is other than that. The mother's egg and the man's sperm are from God's creation, and they did not create anything. We say to them: if you possess life and death, then prevent one person from dying, instead of spending thousands of pounds on treating infertility, which may or may not succeed. Keep one person alive, and you will not be able to.

Death is a sensory, observed matter. Therefore, it is out of God's mercy toward the human mind regarding unseen events that God has brought them close to us through something observed. How? When a person looks at himself while he is alive, he does not know how God gave him life and how He created him. God, Exalted is His majesty, mentioned to us the unseen of creation in the noble Qur'an, saying that He created man from dust, from clay, and from black mud altered, then breathed into him of His spirit.

And recite the saying of the Almighty: ﴿If you are in doubt about the Resurrection, indeed We created you from dust.﴾ (from verse 5, Surah al-Hajj)

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿And We certainly created man from an extract of clay.﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun)

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We created them from sticky clay.﴾ (from verse 11, Surah al-Saffat)

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿And We certainly created man from clay, from black mud altered.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr)

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down in prostration to him.﴾ (Surah Sad)

So the Almighty, blessed and exalted, informed us of a stage of creation that we did not witness, but death is something witnessed by all of us. Since it is witnessed by us, the Almighty brings it as proof of the stages of creation that we did not witness. Death is the undoing of life, and God, blessed and exalted, informed us of life's stages, but they are unseen, which we did not witness.

But He who created said: I created you from dust, from clay, from black mud altered, from clay like pottery. Water is poured onto dust and it becomes clay. We leave the clay and its color changes and it becomes clay-stone (salsal). The salsal dries and becomes black mud altered; then He shapes it into the form of a human, and the Almighty, blessed and exalted, breathes the spirit into it, and it becomes a human being. Then comes death, which is the undoing of life. Undoing anything comes in the opposite order to its building.

The building of a structure begins from the bottom up, and its demolition begins from the top down. Therefore, the last stage of a journey is the first step on the path of return. If you are traveling to Alexandria, the first place on the return journey is the last place you reached.

The first thing that leaves the body is the spirit, and it was the last thing that entered it. Then the body hardens and becomes like altered black mud. Then it rots and becomes like clay-stone. Then the water in it evaporates and it returns to dust. Thus death is the undoing of the form of life, in agreement with the stages that the Almighty, blessed and exalted, has explained to us.

As for His saying: ﴿then to Him you will be returned﴾, that is, God, blessed and exalted, will resurrect you in order to call you to account. The disbelievers, the atheists, and the proponents of material philosophy have tried to deny the matter of resurrection, and in this they have brought nothing new. Rather, they came with the same words that the people of the first jahiliyya said. Recite His saying about what the people of the first jahiliyya said: ﴿And they say, "There is nothing but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time."﴾ (from verse 24, Surah al-Jathiyah)

The wish of the disbeliever and of the one who wrongs himself is that there be no resurrection or reckoning. As for those who wonder at this, we say to them: God, who brought you into existence from nothing, is able to return you when you were existing. He, Exalted is His majesty, says: ﴿And it is He who originates creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (Surah al-Rum)

Bringing into existence what was already existing is easier than bringing into existence from nothing, without an existing model. And God, Exalted, responds to the disbelievers, saying: ﴿And he presents for Us an example and forgets his own creation, saying, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation."﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin)

Thus the resurrection is easier for God than the beginning of creation. Everything is written with God, Exalted, in a clear Book, and what the earth has taken of the human body, He will return on the Day of Resurrection, so that it may come back anew.

The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of man. Recite His saying: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know.﴾ (from verse 57, Surah Ghafir)

And God's saying, ﴿then to Him you will be returned﴾, is reassurance for the one who believes. Since to Him we return and from Him we began, life begins from God and ends with God. So let us make it entirely for God. We must note that God, blessed and exalted, has hidden death from us in time, place, cause, and lifespan. He did not hide it in order to conceal it, but hid it so that we anticipate it at every moment. This is a wide announcement of death so that people hasten to righteous deeds and to reward, because there is no certain lifespan in this world. The young person is not secure about his lifespan, nor the youth, nor the elderly. Therefore each of us must hasten to good deeds, so that death does not surprise him and he dies while disobedient.

We note that God has given the story of life in a single verse. Returning to God, which is a certainty for the believers, obligates them to the method, so they live on what is lawful. Their commitment to this is what leads them to the path of Paradise, and it reassures them about their children after the parents have departed from the world.

The deed of the righteous man is reflected in his children after him. Recite His saying, Exalted: ﴿And let those fear [Allah] who, if they were to leave behind them weak offspring, would fear for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ (Surah al-Nisa')

Thus the one committed to the method is reassured about meeting his Lord and reassured about his recompense. But the one who does not believe in the Hereafter received life from God and wasted it on what does not benefit. Then afterward he finds nothing but reckoning and the Fire. Recite the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿As for those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a lowland which the thirsty one takes for water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing; and he finds Allah with him, so He pays him in full his account. And Allah is swift in account.﴾ (Surah al-Nur)

That is, the disbeliever will be surprised in the Hereafter by God, whom he never imagined would call him to account for what he did.

As for His saying ﴿وإليه ترجعون﴾ (and to Him you will be returned), it is read in two recitations (qira'at): with a damma on the taa, and with a fatha on the taa. In the first, the verb is ﴿تُرْجَعون﴾ (turja'un, passive), meaning that we are compelled to return, so the return to God is not by our will. This applies to the disbelievers who wish they would not return to God. In the second, ﴿ترجِعون﴾ (tarji'un, active), there is volition, and it applies to the believers because they wish to return to God.

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, on surah 2, verse 29:

﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth. Then He turned to the heaven and made it seven heavens; and He is Knowing of all things.﴾

In this verse Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, reminds us that He is the One who created all that is on the earth, all of it. This verse came after His saying ﴿He gave you life, then He causes you to die, then He gives you life again, then to Him you will be returned﴾, to draw our attention to the fact that everything on the earth belongs to Allah, majestic is His majesty, and that we own nothing except by a temporary ownership, and that what we have in this world will pass to others, and so on.

When Allah, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, created life and said ﴿You were dead, then He gave you life﴾, it was as if life needs a continuous supply from the Creator to the creature so that it can continue. So, for life to continue, the supply of blessings must continue. But blessings remain for the duration of life, and at death the human being's connection to the blessings of this world ends. Therefore, a person must be mindful that things are subjected to him in this world to serve him, and that this subjection is not by anyone's power but by the power of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted. A human being does not know how creation took place, nor what its stages are, except what Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, informs us of. He, majestic is His majesty, says: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor was I one to take misleading ones as helpers﴾ [Surat al-Kahf: 51].

Since they did not witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, we must take that from Allah. What Allah tells us about the creation of the heavens and the earth, and about our own creation, is the truth, and whatever comes to us from other than Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is misguidance and falsehood. Today we find many studies about the formation of the heavens and the earth and the creation of man, and all of them will never reach a certainty; rather, they will remain theories without proof. That is why Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, said ﴿nor was I one to take misleading ones as helpers﴾, meaning that there will be those who will come and mislead, and say, "This is how the heavens and the earth were created, and this is how man was created." These misleaders who bring things that are known only to Allah, came to establish the method of faith. For if these misleaders had not come, and had they not said, "The earth was created in such-and-such a way and the sky in such-and-such a way," we would have said that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, had informed us in His Mighty Book that there would come those who would mislead about the creation of the universe and the creation of man. But their coming is itself proof of the truthfulness of the Qur'an, which informed us of their coming centuries before they came.

Benefiting from a thing does not require knowing its secrets. For example, we use electricity although we do not know what it is. Likewise we live on the earth and benefit from all its phenomena and everything Allah has subjected for us. Our not knowing the secret of creation and origination does not deprive us of this benefit. It is knowledge that does not benefit, and ignorance that does not harm. The universe is subjected to serve man, and subjection means making it submissive; the phenomena of the universe do not rebel against man. If there are phenomena in the universe that rebel by the decree of Allah, such as floods, volcanoes and natural disasters, we say that this happens to draw our attention, glory be to Him and exalted, to the fact that everything in the universe does not serve us by its own nature, nor by our control over it, but serves us by Allah's command to it. Otherwise, if creatures served you by their own nature, then have power over them when they rebel against serving you. Everything in the universe is subject to the absolute power of Allah. Even causes and effects are subject to the absolute divine power. Causes and effects in the universe do not go beyond the will of Allah.

Therefore, when water rebels in a flood, and the winds rebel in a storm, and the earth rebels with earthquakes and volcanoes, this is only so that man may know that it is not within his power to control the universe in which he lives. Read His saying, glory be to Him and exalted:

﴿Do they not see that We created for them, from what Our hands have made, livestock, and they are their owners? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat.﴾ [Surat Ya-Sin: 71-72]

A human being is incapable of subduing an animal except by Allah's subjecting it to him. And it is remarkable that you see animals perceive what the human being does not perceive in the universe. They sense the earthquake before it happens and flee from the place of the earthquake, while the human being cannot, with his intellect, understand what is about to happen.

And the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿He created for you all that is on the earth﴾ encompasses all the kinds of the earth. Therefore, a human being cannot originate anything except from something existing. That is, the human being has not invented anything in the universe. For if you take a grain of wheat: from where did we get it? From last year's harvest... and the harvest of the previous world. From where did that come? From the harvest of the year before that. And so the sequence of things continues until you reach the first grain of wheat. From where did it come? It came by direct creation from Allah. And likewise, all the fruits of the earth, if you trace them back to the first fruit, are by direct creation from Allah, glory be to Him and exalted. And if you try to reach the origin of human existence, you will find by logic and reason that the beginning of creation was a male and a female, created by direct creation from Allah. For you are from your father, and your father is from your grandfather, and your grandfather from his father, and so on until you reach the creation of the first human being. We find that it must be a direct creation from Allah, glory be to Him and exalted. What applies to the human being applies to animals, plants and inanimate things. For everything, if you trace it back to its origin, you will find that it must begin with a direct creation from Allah, glory be to Him and exalted.

Some people ask about progress and civilization and these new inventions: is there not creation by man in them? We say: there is creation from something existing. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has disclosed from His knowledge to mankind what they can use, with the materials Allah created in the earth, to advance and make new things. But we have never found, nor heard of, a human being who created matter from nothing.

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is the One who created everything in this universe from nothing. Then after that the creatures multiplied by laws Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, subjected for them. But all this development is due to the fact that Allah created the creatures and gave them the property of reproduction and mating so that life continues generation after generation. And all of Allah's creation that you see in the universe now, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has placed in it laws of causes that give it the continuity of life from generation to generation until the universe ends. So if a person says to you, "I cultivate by my intelligence and knowledge," say to him: "You bring the seed that Allah created, and place it in the earth that Allah created, and Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, sends down water on it from the sky, and it sprouts by Allah's power, who placed in it its nourishment and the manner of its growth." So all that happens is that you plough the earth and throw the seed. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿Have you considered what you plough? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the Growers?﴾ [Surat al-Waqi'ah: 63-64]

It is true that a human being ploughs the earth and throws the seed, and perhaps tends the crop with care and irrigation. But there is no act of creation in what he does. Rather, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is the Creator of everything. And if you were cultivating by your own power, then bring a seed not created by Allah, and earth not created by Allah, and water not sent down by Allah from the sky. And of course you will not be able to... But what is the source of the things that have been newly produced?

We say there is a difference between a thing's existence in potential and its existence in actuality. For example, the palm is a seed that was existing in potential; it was a kernel. Then it was planted and became existing in actuality. And you have no action in either state: you did not, by your power, create the kernel which is the seed, nor did you, by your act, make the kernel grow to become a palm tree in actuality. Moreover, there are things hidden in the universe that Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, created at the beginning of creation, then left them hidden in the universe until He disclosed them to whoever seeks their secrets in His universe.

And every discovery has a birth. If we take, for example, what is beneath the soil, or the treasures existing below the surface of the earth: they remained hidden until Allah guided the human being to them and taught him how to extract them. The human being did not invent, for example, or create petroleum or minerals; rather, all of these were hidden in the universe until the time came when they must perform their role in life. So the Truth guided us to them. The fact that a thing was absent from us does not mean that it did not exist, nor that it came into existence at the moment of our discovering it. The thing that is happening now, and the thing that will happen after years, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, created all its elements and deposited them in the earth at the moment of creation. And the human being, by what Allah discloses to him of knowledge, can combine these elements, but he cannot create them or originate them. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾.

When Allah, majestic is His majesty, says "istawa" (He turned/established Himself), we must understand everything related to the Essence of Allah in the sense that ﴿there is nothing like Him﴾ [Surat al-Shura: 11]. The Almighty "istawa" (established Himself) and kings "istawa" on their thrones, and you "istawa" on your chair. But because we are governed by the principle ﴿there is nothing like Him﴾, we must know that the istiwa' of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is nothing like anything. Allah is Living, and you are living: is your life like His life? Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, knows, and you know: is your knowledge like His knowledge? Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is capable, and you are capable: is your capability like His capability? Of course not. So when you come to "istawa", do not try to understand it at all in the human sense. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, knows what is in the earth and what is in the heaven. He, glory be to Him, knows the place with all its atoms, and those present in this place or dwelling, with all their atoms. And you know the outward matter... And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth until the Day of Resurrection, and after the Day of Resurrection. So He, majestic is His majesty, is not like anything. Your intellect cannot fully grasp an act related to the Essence of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, for your intellect falls short of comprehending it. Therefore say "Glory be to Allah", there is nothing like Him, in every act related to the Essence of Allah: ﴿He turned to the heaven﴾. This statement is the speech of Allah, so the speaker is Allah, mighty and majestic.

Some people say, "We received the Qur'an and memorized it." We say to them: the One who preserved the Qur'an is Allah, glory be to Him and exalted. And since He preserved His speech, He, majestic is His majesty, knows that the whole of existence will never contradict the Noble Qur'an. And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, preserved the Qur'an to be a proof for Him against people. And since Allah, majestic is His majesty, is the Creator and the Speaker, there is no truth in the whole universe that conflicts with the Noble Qur'an. Read His saying, glory be to Him and exalted:

﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian.﴾ [Surat al-Hijr: 9]

This is from the greatness of Allah, that He preserved His speech so that it would be a proof against people. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, had His attributes existing before the existence of the objects of those attributes. He, majestic is His majesty, created because He is the Creator. It is as if the attribute of creation existed first; otherwise, how did He create His first creation if He was not Creator? And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, is the Provider before anyone existed to be provided for. Otherwise, by what power did Allah provide for His first creation? Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, created this universe with the perfection of His attributes, and He bore witness that there is no god but Him before any of Allah's creation bore witness that there is no god but Allah. Read His saying, exalted:

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice.﴾ [Surat Al 'Imran: 18]

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, bore witness that there is no god but Him before any of His creatures existed to bear witness to the oneness of His divinity. He bore witness that there is no god but Him before He created the angels, so that they might bear witness, by witnessing, that there is no god but Allah. And "those of knowledge" bear witness by knowledge. So the witness of the Essence to the Essence, in His saying "Allah bears witness that there is no god but Him", is the one that is relied upon, and it is the strongest of witnesses; for Allah has no need of His creatures to extend the witness.

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted: after He created the earth and created the heaven, and the matter was settled for Him, He said ﴿and He is Knowing of all things﴾, meaning that not an atom of His dominion is hidden from His knowledge. He knows every atom of the earth, every atom of people, and every atom of the universe. The universe does not act except by His permission and His will. Read His saying, exalted:

{O my son, indeed if it is the weight of a mustard seed, and should be within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.}

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 30:

﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed I will make upon the earth a successive authority." They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know."﴾ (2:30)

After the True One, glorified and exalted is He, informed us that He created everything that is in the universe, He wished to tell us about those whom He created to populate this universe. Thus, the story with which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, began the stories of the Qur'an is the story of Adam, the first of creation. This story appears many times in the Noble Qur'an, to show us why the True One, glorified and exalted is He, told us this story. It also comes to show us the truthfulness of the conveying of the message from Allah. Recite His saying, exalted is He:

﴿We relate to you their story with truth﴾ (part of 18:13).

The word "al-haqq" (the truth) that appears here is to show us that there are stories, but without truth. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wished to remove His stories from the circle of stories that people circulate, or the stories of history, because these may contradict reality and come without truth. There are stories told in the world that have no reality, but are rather of the category of imagination.

The word "qissa" (story) is derived from "qass al-athar" (tracing the trail), meaning that the tracker (qassas al-athar) in the desert follows the traces he sees on the sand until he reaches his goal, when he reaches the end of the trace. Since we have known that Allah relates the truth, we know that all the stories of the Noble Qur'an are events that actually occurred, and every story in the Qur'an contains a lesson or something important that the True One, glorified and exalted is He, wants to draw our attention to. Sometimes a story is to strengthen the Prophet (ﷺ) and to strengthen the believers. Recite His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And all that We relate to you of the news of the messengers is that by which We strengthen your heart﴾ (part of 11:120).

Every story strengthens the heart of the Messenger and the believers in the situations in which events shake them. The stories of the Qur'an are not for killing time, but the supreme aim of the story is to strengthen and benefit the movement of faithful life. If we look at the stories of the Noble Qur'an, we find that they speak of things that have passed and become history. History links events to their times, and it may be the history of a person rather than of an event, but the person is an event of the events of the world. If you read the history of every event, you will find that it expresses the viewpoint of its narrator. All historical stories were written from the viewpoints of those who narrated them. Therefore, one story differs according to the narrator.

But the stories of the Noble Qur'an are the true stories. The lesson in the stories of the Noble Qur'an is that they convey to us events in history that recur over the passage of time. Pharaoh, for example, is every ruler who wants to be worshipped on earth. The People of the Cave, for example, are the story of every faithful group that fled from the tyranny of disbelief and withdrew to worship Allah. The story of Yusuf (peace be upon him) is the story of every brotherhood among whom Satan has sown discord, making them harbor malice toward one another. The story of Dhu al-Qarnayn is the story of every reforming ruler to whom Allah, glorified and exalted is He, gave the means in the world and established him in the earth, so he acted according to Allah's method and in what pleases Allah. The story of Salih is the story of every people who asked Allah for a miracle, so He fulfilled it for them, and they disbelieved in it. And the story of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) is the story of every people who cheated in the scale and the measure.

Thus, all the stories of the Qur'an are stories that recur in every age. Even in the time in which we live, you find more than one Pharaoh, and more than one People of the Cave who flee with their religion, and more than one Qarun who worships wealth and gold, and thinks that he has become independent of Allah. Therefore, the characters of the stories of the Qur'an came unnamed, except for one story, the story of 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary) and Maryam bint 'Imran (Mary daughter of 'Imran). Why? Because it is a miracle that will not be repeated. Therefore Allah made her known to us, saying "Maryam bint 'Imran" and said "'Isa ibn Maryam," so that the matter would not be confused, and any woman would claim that she conceived without a man, like Maryam. We say: No. The miracle of Maryam will not be repeated. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, specified her by name, saying: 'Isa ibn Maryam, and Maryam bint 'Imran. As for the rest of the stories of the Noble Qur'an, they came unnamed.
