Allah, exalted is He, did not tell us who Pharaoh of Moses was, nor who the People of the Cave are, nor who Dhu al-Qarnayn is, nor who the owner of the two gardens is, and so on through what came in the Noble Qur'an, because these stories are not intended to be about a specific person whose story is not repeated with anyone else. Some people busy themselves with who Pharaoh of Moses is, and who Dhu al-Qarnayn is, etc. We say to them: you will reach nothing, because Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has related the story to us without clarifying the persons, so that we know that the intended meaning is not a specific person, but rather the wisdom of the story.

The stories in the Qur'an are not repeated. Some of them come in some verses and some in other verses, but the snapshot is different. Each verse gives us new information, so that if you gather all the verses mentioned in the Noble Qur'an, you will find before you a complete and integrated story. Each verse adds something new.

The greatest story in the Noble Qur'an is the story of Moses (peace be upon him). The Qur'an always reminds us of it, because its events deal with the story of the worst of mankind in history. On every occasion, Allah reminds us with a snapshot from the lives of these people. Recite His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Nurse him; and when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear or grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers."﴾ (part of 28:7).

And in another verse, the True One, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿When We inspired to your mother that which is inspired, "Cast him into the chest, then cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his."﴾ (parts of 20:38-39).

The superficial understanding supposes that this is repetition, and we say no. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We inspired to the mother of Moses, "Nurse him; and when you fear for him, cast him into the river"﴾.

This snapshot shows that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, prepares the mother of Moses in faith for the event. But when the event occurs, the story changes in a rapid pattern: ﴿cast him into the chest, then cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank.﴾ Words suited to the moment the event occurs. The first verse showed us that the mother of Moses nursed him before she placed him in the chest, and that she would cast him into the river when a danger occurs and she fears for him from being killed. In it is reassurance for her: that she should not fear or grieve, because Allah will deliver him. And in it are two glad tidings: that Allah will return him to his mother, and that Allah has chosen him as a messenger.

We come to the second verse, which completes this snapshot for us, saying ﹛cast him into the chest﹜. Here we know that the mother of Moses will place him in a chest, which was not mentioned in the previous verse. Then after that we learn that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, issued His command to the water to throw the chest onto the bank. This was not mentioned in the previous verse. We also know that the one who will take him is Pharaoh, and that there will be mutual enmity between them. Thus we see that the two verses of the story complete each other, and there is no repetition. In the second verse, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wants to establish that there will be mutual enmity between Moses and Pharaoh, just as Pharaoh's enmity to Allah, exalted is He, and to Moses was established, so He said: "an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his." But enmity is not settled unless it is mutual. Then a third verse comes to complete the picture, in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up to be for them an enemy and a grief﴾ (part of 28:8).

Thus the noble verse has shown us how the enmity between Pharaoh and Moses would be settled until Pharaoh is destroyed. Because if a person is an enemy to you, and you meet enmity with kindness, the enmity subsides after a little while. So these verses are not repetition, but verses that complete the story and give us the complete and integrated picture.

But why did the story of Moses not come complete like the story of Yusuf? Because Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wants to establish by it our Prophet (peace be upon him) and the believers. So here is one snapshot and here is another snapshot, to accomplish what is required of strengthening without disruption, because the verses give us the story complete.

Likewise the story of Adam came to us in multiple verses, to give us in their totality a complete story. At the same time each verse has a wisdom that the time in which it was revealed needed. The True One, glorified and exalted is He, relates to us the beginning of creation, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are all the children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust."(1)

And the True One, glorified and exalted is He, wants to make us know how creation began. And the story of Iblis's enmity toward Adam and his offspring. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, spoke about the first of mankind. He made us know his name, which is Adam (peace be upon him). He spoke about the material from which he was created. He spoke about the method that He set for Adam. He told us about the discussion that took place with the angels. He also informed us that Adam would be a successor on earth. And that He taught him all the names, to lead his life's movement. And He taught us the logic of knowing things, and knowing their names. He told us about the dialogue that took place between Iblis and his Lord when he refused to prostrate. He showed us Iblis's argument for refusing to prostrate, and Iblis's plan and his entry into the hearts of believers through seduction and whispering, and other things. So there are many things that the story of Adam addresses, and even if a human wanted to write the history of Adam, he could not bring all these snapshots. But the True One, glorified and exalted is He, made each snapshot come for strengthening.

The noble verse that we are concerned with did not come in al-A'raf, nor in al-Hijr, nor in al-Isra', nor in al-Kahf, nor in Ta-Ha. And by this we know that there is no repetition. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, informed His angels that He is placing a successor on earth. Here we must pause: Was Adam created as an individual, or did Allah create him with all his offspring hidden within him until the Day of Resurrection? If we read the Noble Qur'an, we find that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿And We had certainly created you and [then] fashioned you; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾ (part of 7:11).

The address here is to everyone: to Adam and his offspring. So it is as if He, glorified and exalted is He, indicates that the first origin of creation is Adam, and that the characteristics of created beings from his offspring are hidden in him by inheritance until the Hour is established. That is, at the time Adam was created, there were in him the particles from which all creation would be taken. This is about this, until the Hour is established. I have said that each one of us has in him a particle or a part of Adam. Adam's children took from him, and the generation after them took from the living microbe that Adam deposited in his children. Those after them also took from the living part that was created originally with Adam. And likewise those after them, and those after them. And life must be a continuous link. Each of us takes from the one before him and gives to the one after him. And if there were a missing link, life would stop. For example, if a man died before he married, he would have no offspring after him, and the link of life would stop. So the continuity of the link of life is proof that it is a connected life that has not stopped. And since life from the time of Adam until our present day has been connected, there must be in each of us a particle of Adam, who is the beginning and origin of life. And life then passed in connected links to our present day, and will continue until the Day of Resurrection.

So I am now alive, because I arose from a living microbe from my father, and my father took his life from a living microbe from his father. And so on until you reach Adam. So you are created from a living particle in which life has not stopped since Adam until our present day. And if it had stopped, you would have no existence.

So the lives of those living now are connected to Adam. No death has come upon them. And those who will live at the time of the Hour, their life is also connected to Adam, the first of creation. And the True One, glorified and exalted is He, when He commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, they prostrated to Adam and to his offspring until the Hour is established. And the offspring of Adam were hidden in his back, and they witnessed the first creation. So the saying of the True One, glorified and exalted is He, ﴿We had certainly created you and [then] fashioned you﴾ contains a new part of the story of creation.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels﴾, meaning that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, asks our master Muhammad (peace be upon him) to say that when Adam was created, He created him as a successor on earth. The speech here does not mean that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, consults anyone in creation, as evidenced by His saying ﴿Indeed I will make﴾. So it is a matter already settled, m

(1) Narrated by al-Bazzar from Hudhayfah with a good chain (isnad).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 31:

﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them; then He presented them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful."﴾

So God, glory be to Him and exalted, answered the angels with this noble verse, because He had taught Adam all the names. The word "kulluha" (all of them) conveys comprehensiveness (al-ihatah), and the meaning of comprehensiveness is knowing everything about these names.

Here a question arises: Did God, glory be to Him and exalted, teach Adam the names from the moment of creation until the Final Hour, since God says "all of them"? What, then, is the status of those names belonging to inventions that will come into being many centuries after Adam's creation?

We say: when God, glory be to Him and exalted, taught Adam the names and distinguished him over the angels, He gave that which is lower an element that distinguished it from a creature of a higher element. Adam was created from clay, and the angels were created from light. The capacities of human beings cannot give the lower anything more than the higher. But God alone, glory be to Him, is the One who gives this, to remind us that what we receive is not by our own capacities but by His power, glory be to Him. Therefore you find Solomon, who was a king and a prophet, whom God gave a kingdom that none after him should possess, and whom He distinguished above His creation. The hoopoe came to Solomon and said: ﴿I have comprehended that which you have not comprehended, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news.﴾

How can the hoopoe, a weak and limited bird, comprehend what Solomon, the prophet-king who ruled over humans and jinn, did not comprehend? Because God, glory be to Him and exalted, dislikes arrogance among His creatures. Therefore He brings a sign that distinguishes the lower from the higher, so that all of them know that all their capacities are not from themselves but are from God. Then Moses, who was a messenger and prophet, learned from al-Khidr, who was a righteous servant, what he had not known.

God, glory be to Him, created the named things (al-musammayat), even though we do not know their existence, and He made the angels receive the names of these named things from Adam. Some people ask about the means by which the Most Generous Creator taught Adam, peace be upon him. The teaching of the Creator differs from the teaching of creatures, because the Creator teaches by inspiration (ilham): He casts into Adam's heart the names of all the named things, of every creature in the universe.

Thus the first scene, of Adam with the angels, is that all the named things had already been brought into existence and God had inspired them to Adam. The evidence is that the angels did not recognize these named things, while Adam knew them. At this point we must pause. Speech is the product of hearing, and language is the product of environment. God, glory be to Him and exalted, taught Adam the names, and this knowledge could only come about if Adam had heard from God, glory be to Him and exalted, and then pronounced it. For if you bring an Arab child and leave him in London, for example, he speaks English fluently and does not understand a single word of Arabic. And the reverse is true: if you bring an English child and leave him in an Arab country, he speaks Arabic and knows nothing of English. Therefore language is not heredity, nor race, nor environment; rather, it is imitation that a person hears and then pronounces. If a person hears nothing and is deaf, he cannot pronounce a single letter. So if Adam pronounced these names, he must have heard them from God, glory be to Him and exalted.

Remarkably, the method by which God, glory be to Him and exalted, taught Adam is the same method that humanity follows to this day. You do not teach a child by narrating actions to him; rather, his teaching must begin with names and named things. You say to him: "This is a cup, this is a mountain, this is a sea, this is the sun, this is the moon." After he learns the named things, he can then come to know the actions, and his education progresses thereafter.

In this way we become acquainted with the first origin of speech, and the completeness of God's power, glory be to Him and exalted, taught Adam the names.

Here we pause to answer two questions. The first: if God, glory be to Him and exalted, taught Adam all the names, did they include the names of what would be newly invented in the world? We say: even if Adam learned the names he needs for the essentials of existence and uses in the requirements of his life on earth, then when something new emerges, Adam's children use names derived from the foundations and names they have learned. Whatever names come into existence and enter the language are not from nothing; rather, they come from the language in which people speak and write.

Likewise, everything in this universe, if you trace it back to its origin, you will find its origin is from God. If humanity were traced back to its origin, it would have to arrive at the fact that the first human was created by God, glory be to Him and exalted. And if you trace knowledge back to its origin, since every science needs a teacher, we say to you: who taught the first teacher? Is it not self-evident that knowledge began with a teacher whom God, glory be to Him and exalted, taught, and that this was the first teacher? Thus the one who taught the names to Adam is God, glory be to Him and exalted, and He taught them to his children, and his children taught them to their children, and so on.

The second question: if God is the teacher of speech, why have languages differed on earth and become many kinds of tongues and dialects?

We say: the diversity of historical periods and the spread of humans over the earth caused each group of people to draw closer to one another so that they would have one language. Every existing language is derived from an older language. French, English and Italian are derived from Latin. Hebrew and Syriac are related to the Arabic language. The dialects spoken by the Arab world, which has one language, differ; even the dialect of Algeria or Morocco, for example, is different from the Egyptian or Sudanese dialect. But when we speak Arabic, some of us understand one another, and the language of all of these people is originally the language of the Qur'an, which is Arabic. But in the periods of historical weakness that passed over the Arabs, the Arab lands became isolated from one another, and each society proceeded to take language as a social marker, so understanding among the different dialects collapsed.

Thus God, glory be to Him and exalted, taught Adam all the names, then presented them to the angels and said to them: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful﴾? That is, God, glory be to Him and exalted, honored Adam in knowledge and gave him a knowledge He did not give to the angels. Then He made Adam the one who teaches them the names of named things they had not known. This is evidence of the completeness of God's power, glory be to Him and exalted, who does what He wills in His dominion. As we have said, distinguishing the lower from the higher is accomplished only by God's act alone. To bring this closer to the mind: suppose a weak person wants to carry a heavy load and cannot. If a strong person helps him, he cannot give him some of his strength to carry the load, but he can help him by carrying it for him. As for the One who can make the weak person strong so that he can carry the heavy load, it is God, glory be to Him and exalted. A human cannot give another human some of his strength, but God alone is capable of making the weak strong and the strong weak.

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿if you are truthful﴾: could the angels have been lying? The angels are a creation of light who glorify God and do what they are commanded. We say that His saying ﴿if you are truthful﴾ refers to what you have judged by analogy regarding events, or what you have said as a conjecture about the unseen.

Had the angels based their judgment on the judgment of another kind that existed on earth, such as the jinn for example, who were created before humans, the Exalted would say: you have erred in this analogy of yours, or: if you are truthful in what you have predicted of the unseen. None knows the unseen except God, exalted is He. Thus both analogies missed the mark.

This is not a criticism of the angels; rather, it is a correction of them and an instruction to us that the angels do not know the unseen. Therefore, when they made analogies or judged the unseen, they missed the mark, because God alone is the Knower of the unseen. What prompted the angels to say or to harbor this statement is their great love for God, exalted is He, and their intense aversion to corruption in His dominion.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 32:

﴿They said, "Glory be to You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise."﴾ (2:32)

This noble verse makes clear to us that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the First Teacher in the universe. And if every knowledge has a teacher, then the First Teacher must be Allah, glorified and exalted is He. And although we witness in our age various kinds of sciences, these sciences arise from the interaction of the intellect that Allah, exalted is He, bestowed upon man, with the materials that Allah placed in the universe, through the logic and knowledge that Allah taught to man. All inventions and innovations took their existence from antecedents that preceded them. Water, for example, has existed since eternity, and the sun, as an energy, evaporates water to form clouds from it. So when man uses thermal energy to evaporate water and uses steam as an energy source, there is a civilisational leap in the sciences called the Age of Steam, which is what powered trains and machines in factories. And other things besides.

This progress in knowledge stems only from the existence of knowledge and energy, and to these is added the mental capacity of man granted to him by the Creator, which led him to think about using the energy produced by steam. When man came to observe a fallen tree rolling toward the earth because its trunk is cylindrical, he took from the system of that tree what he used to make the wheel, which was an important development in the history of knowledge.

Thus the cylindrical trunk of the tree gave man the idea of the wheel. When man developed the use of steam and made a train that runs on steam, this development is a child of previous knowledge concerning the energy produced by evaporating water, and of how to make a wheel. Every knowledge stems from earlier knowledge, and is linked to capacities that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has bestowed upon man.

Therefore, when Islam came to present empirical or material knowledge, it came to draw our attention to the signs of the Creator in the universe, and asked us to reflect on these signs and to exercise our intellect and perception upon them. Consider the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it?﴾ (Surah Yusuf 12:105).

Thus Allah, majestic in His majesty, draws our attention to His signs in the heavens and the earth, so that we may exercise intellect and perception upon them, and derive from them what gives us civilisation. The Qur'an requires us to continue the knowledge that Allah taught to Adam. And if the history of the sciences conveys to us reports of peoples who were not believers and yet preceded us in knowledge and deduction, then it was incumbent upon us, the believers, to reflect on the signs of Allah, exalted is He, on the earth. Newton, who noticed the force of the earth's gravity, was observing an apple falling from the top of a tree and striking the ground, and he arrived at the law of gravitation.

And if we wish to take a glimpse of the knowledge of Allah that He taught us, it suffices that we look at the date pit: in this small pit is a complete palm tree. Once the pit is placed in the earth, the palm tree grows and comes into being.

To clarify all of this, we say that every knowledge is built upon theories. The first theory leads to the second, and the second leads to the third, and so on. But the beginning of all these sciences did not start with a theory; rather, it started with what they call axioms (al-badihiyyat, self-evident truths), that is, things that need no proof. These are the things Allah created in the universe, and upon these axioms the theories were built one after another. So if you wish to trace them back to their origin, you will ultimately arrive at the fact that the first knowledge is from Allah, glorified and exalted is He: the First Teacher taught it, and the first fruit was created by Allah. And all of man's discoveries from the beginning of life until the Hour is established exist potentially, like the palm tree within the pit, awaiting reflection and action so that they become discovery in actuality. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, who is the First Teacher, has placed in His universe much knowledge.

The verse of the poet Ahmad Shawqi comes to mind, when he said:

Glory be to You, O Allah, the best of teachers, who taught the first generations by the pen.
You sent Moses with the Torah as a guide, and the son of the virgin taught the Gospel.
And You caused the spring of eloquence to gush forth in Muhammad, who gave drink of the hadith and handed down the Revelation.

Shawqi, in these verses, expresses that all knowledge is ascribed to Allah alone. Thus it becomes clear to us that the saying of the angels, ﴿Glory be to You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise,﴾ contains an acknowledgment that all knowledge ultimately returns to Allah. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the source of knowledge and wisdom. As for His saying, glorified and exalted is He, ﴿the All-Knowing, the All-Wise﴾: "al-'Alim" (the All-Knowing) means the One who knows everything, whether hidden or manifest, and all knowledge comes from Him. As for "al-hikma" (wisdom), it is originally applied to the piece of iron placed in a horse's mouth to bridle it so that the rider can control it, since the horse is a pampered and skittish animal that needs training, and the piece of iron placed in its mouth makes it more obedient to its master. It is as though the attribution of the description "al-Hakim" (the All-Wise) to the Creator, glorified and exalted is He, means that He, majestic in His majesty, governs the creatures so that they do not move without guidance and without understanding.

Wisdom means that a purpose is set for every movement, so that movements harmonise with one another and the universe becomes governed by the Truth, before which falsehood cannot stand, from before it or behind it. The All-Knowing and All-Wise is the One who assigns to every being its frame and limits. Wisdom is that everything performs what is required of it with skill. In jurisprudence, wisdom is the deduction of the sound ruling; in poetry, it is weighing words according to the metres (al-mafa'il); in medicine, it is knowing the diagnosis of the disease and the remedy that treats it; in engineering, it is designing a hospital according to the needs of the patient and the doctor, the treatment equipment, the pharmacy stores, and so on, or designing a home for comfortable living. The wisdom of building a house, for example, differs from the wisdom of building a palace or a place of work.

The whole universe was created by an All-Wise, All-Knowing Creator. The Creator, glorified and exalted is He, placed in it everything in its place to perform its task. To describe Allah, exalted is He, as All-Wise requires that He be All-Knowing, because His knowledge is what makes Him create everything with wisdom. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has given each of His creatures knowledge in proportion to its need. It is not in the nature of the angels to know what that human will do, whom Allah will appoint as His successor on earth; rather, they exist for another task. And Allah distinguished man with intellect so that he may discover, from the signs of Allah in the universe, what suits the needs of his life. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who decreed and then guided.﴾ (Surah al-A'la 87:1–3).

So everything has been created according to a measure, and every creature is made easy for what Allah has guided it to.

﴿He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." So when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen (ghayb) of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing?"﴾

Allah, glorified and exalted, intended to respond to the angels' objection concerning the creation of Adam and his being a khalifa (vicegerent) on the earth, and that Allah, in His wisdom, has what is hidden from them. Therefore they did not grasp this wisdom. Before Allah created Adam and made him a vicegerent on the earth, He already had knowledge of everything that would happen from Adam and his descendants until the Hour. As for the angels, after the Hour, they had no knowledge of that, because this is not their task. As we have said: everyone is made easy for that for which he was created. Therefore, the Truth, glorified and exalted, wished to give the angels the picture that you have judged Adam either from the experience of another species that lived on the earth, or from conjecture about the unseen. Both measures are invalid. Therefore Allah, glorified, at this moment distinguished Adam over the angels, so He taught him the names of all things. Then He asked the angels to inform Him of these names. But they said, "Glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what You have taught us." And since Allah had not taught them the names, they do not know them. So Allah asked Adam to inform them of the names of these things, and he informed them. But he did not inform them by his own essence, nor by his own rule, nor by a knowledge he had on his own. Rather, he informed them by the teaching of Allah, glorified and exalted, to him. And concerning this Allah, exalted, says:

﴿We raise by degrees whom We will, and over every possessor of knowledge is one who knows more.﴾ (Part of verse 76, Surah Yusuf.)

So Adam's knowledge of the names was by the will of Allah, glorified and exalted. And this will alone is what made Adam, at that time, know what the angels did not know. Here the Truth, glorified and exalted, responded to the angels' statement that Adam would cause corruption on the earth. So Allah reminded them by His saying: ﴿Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning that Allah, glorified and exalted, alone knows the unseen. The unseen here is the absolute unseen (al-ghayb al-mutlaq). There is also a relative unseen (ghayb nisbi). For example, my wallet may be stolen and I do not know who stole it, so it is unseen to me. But it is known to the thief, and to the one who facilitated the method of theft by guarding the way for him so that no one would surprise him while he steals. Or an important decision may have been issued regarding me, such as a promotion, a dismissal, or a verdict, which has not reached me. So I do not know it, but the one who issued the decision or verdict knows it.

This relative unseen is not considered unseen. But the absolute unseen is that which has no preceding indications pointing to what will happen. This is the unseen that surprises you and surprises everyone around you without any preliminary signs. This unseen is known only to Allah alone. As for His saying: ﴿and I know what you reveal and what you have been concealing﴾, it gives us a pause here. Did the angels actually say to Allah, glorified and exalted, ﴿Will You place in it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we glorify You with praise and sanctify You?﴾ Did the angels say it aloud, or did they say it within themselves without uttering it? His saying ﴿and what you have been concealing﴾ gives us a sign that the angels perhaps said this secretly and did not reveal it. In any case, whether they said it aloud or said it secretly, Allah knows it, because Allah, majestic in His majesty, encompasses everything. We do not want this point to stir up dispute. Why? Because in both cases, whether openly or in concealment, the matter is equal with the knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted. So there is no need for argument, because there is no disagreement.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 34:

﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis. He refused and was arrogant, and he was among the disbelievers.﴾

God, exalted is He, issued His command to the angels to prostrate to Adam. This matter gave rise to a lengthy debate. Some people said: "How can the angels prostrate to other than God? Prostration belongs to God alone." Others said: "Does the prostration of the angels to Adam mean that they worshipped him?" Another group said: "Prostration to other than God is not permissible under any circumstances." We say to these: you have not grasped the meaning. God, glorified and exalted, after He distinguished Adam over the angels with the knowledge of the names, commanded them to prostrate to Adam. Here we must know that prostration to Adam was obedience to the command of God, and not worship of Adam. It was God, glorified and exalted, who commanded the angels to prostrate, and Adam did not command them, nor does he have the right to command them. So the command to prostrate here came from God, glorified and exalted. Whoever obeyed Him was an worshipper; whoever did not obey Him was a disobedient one; and whoever returned the command to the One who commanded was a disbeliever.

To understand the meaning of worship, we say: worship is obedience to the commands of God and avoidance of His prohibitions. So, when God says to me, "Do," I do; and when He says, "Do not," I do not. For worship is the obedience of a creature to its Creator in His commands and prohibitions. That is why, when we go on pilgrimage (Hajj), we kiss the Black Stone in the Ka'bah, and we stone the stone that represents Iblis at Mina. We kiss a stone and we stone a stone. This is the meaning of worshipping God and following His method: as we are commanded, we act. Nothing is sacred to us except the command of God and His method. The angels here did not prostrate to Adam; rather, they prostrated in obedience to God's command to prostrate to Adam. There is a great difference between prostrating to a thing and prostrating in obedience to the command of God. Prostration in obedience to the command of God, glorified and exalted, is not considered a departure from the method, because the foundation is obedience to God. Did all the angels prostrate to Adam? No. Rather, the angels who had a task with him prostrated, and that task God, glorified and exalted, clarified in His saying:

﴿But indeed, over you are guardians, honorable and recording, who know whatever you do.﴾ (Surah al-Infitar)

And His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Not a word does he utter except that with him is an observer, ready.﴾ (Surah Qaf)

And His saying, glorified is He:

﴿And those who arrange (affairs) by command.﴾ (Surah al-Nazi'at)

So there are among the angels those who will record a person's deeds, every word he says and every action he does, and they write these actions down. And among them are those who protect him from the devils, and among them are those who carry out the decrees of God on earth. All of these have a task with the human being. But the command to prostrate did not include those exalted angels, the bearers of the Throne, the guardians of the heavens, and others who have no task with the human being. That is why, when Iblis refused to prostrate, God said to him:

﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?"﴾ (Surah Sad)

God's saying, "were you among the exalted," means: you were among the exalted angels who were not included in the command to prostrate. Thus, the command to prostrate to Adam was like God's command to us to prostrate toward the qiblah in prayer. We do not prostrate to the qiblah itself, but we prostrate in obedience to God's command to prostrate toward the qiblah. The angels who were included in the command prostrated in obedience to the command of God, glorified and exalted, but Iblis refused to prostrate and disobeyed the command of God.

Some people say that Iblis was not among those whom God commanded to prostrate, because the command included only the angels, and Iblis is not an angel but is of the jinn, as the Noble Qur'an relates to us in His saying:

﴿Except Iblis; he was of the jinn and defied the command of his Lord.﴾ (part of verse 50, Surah al-Kahf)

We say: that Iblis was of the jinn is what caused him to disobey the command to prostrate. Had Iblis been of the angels, who are compelled to obedience, he would necessarily have obeyed God's command and prostrated. But because he was of the jinn, who have choice in whether to obey or disobey, this is what enabled him to disobey the command to prostrate. Therefore, as for those who take from the noble verse that Iblis was of the jinn and so was not included in the command to prostrate, we say to them: God, the Truthful, has informed us of Iblis's kind so that we understand through which gate he entered into disobedience. For he entered through the gate of choice granted to humans and jinn in this worldly life alone. Had God, glorified and exalted, willed that Iblis be compelled to obedience, he would not have been able to disobey. But his disobedience came from the fact that he was created with choice, and choice is the gate through which he entered into this disobedience. This is a truth we must understand. That is why the Truthful, glorified and exalted, answers anyone who may come to think that the command to prostrate did not include Iblis because he was of the jinn, with His saying, glorified and exalted:

﴿He said, "What prevented you from not prostrating when I commanded you?"﴾ (part of verse 12, Surah al-A'raf)

Iblis's disbelief and his eternal abode in the Fire lay in his returning the command to the One who commanded, and his saying:

﴿"Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-Isra')

The presence of Iblis among those higher than him, namely the angels, was a greater reason for prostration. For once the command had been issued to those above to prostrate, it applies to those below as well.

Iblis, as related in the narrations, was called "the peacock of the angels," and he used to strut with pride among them. This pride or arrogance is what led him into disobedience. And because Iblis was created with choice, he was proud of his choice to obey God, before his vanity led him to disbelief and disobedience. That is why, as soon as God issued the command to prostrate to Adam, Iblis refused out of arrogance, and did not strive against himself to obey God. So Iblis's disobedience was disobedience at its peak, for he returned the command to the One who commanded and thought himself better than Adam, and did not commit to obeying God. His vanity continued to lead him from one disobedience to another. So God expelled him from His mercy and made him accursed. When Iblis knew that he had been expelled from God's mercy, he asked God, glorified and exalted, to let him remain until the Day of Judgment, and Iblis swore by the might of God that he would lead the children of Adam astray. He specified the directions from which misguidance would come. He said:

﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf)

We note here that the directions relative to the human being are six: right and left, front and back, above and below. But Iblis mentioned only four. As for the last two, namely above and below, Iblis cannot approach them. As for below, it is the place of prostration and submission to God; and as for above, it is the place where prayer and supplication ascend. Iblis cannot approach these two places. Thus we see that Iblis did not merely refuse to prostrate; rather, he returned the command to the One who commanded, and this is the beginning of disbelief. Then he continued in his error, threatening Adam and his descendants that he would lead them astray from the path of God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 35:

﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance wherever you will; but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers."﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted be He, had created Adam and commanded the angels to prostrate to him, and after the disbelief and disobedience of Iblis occurred, Allah, majestic in His majesty, willed that Adam should carry out his mission on the earth. But before he carried out his mission, Allah placed him in a practical trial concerning the method (manhaj) that man would follow on the earth, and concerning the seduction to which he would be exposed from Iblis. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, out of His mercy, did not will that Adam begin his mission in existence on a theoretical basis, because there is a difference between theoretical speech and trial.

Something may be said to you and you agree with it in theory, but when the action comes you do nothing. Thus the period Adam spent in Paradise was a practical application of the method of servitude ('ubudiyyah), so that when he went out to his mission he did not go out with a theoretical principle, but with a practical method in which he encountered [the distinction between] "do" and "do not", the lawful and the unlawful, the seduction of Satan and disobedience. Then afterwards he learns how to repent, seek forgiveness and return to Allah. And so that the children of Adam would know that Allah does not close His door in the face of the disobedient, but opens to him the door of repentance.

Allah, glorified and exalted be He, caused Adam to dwell in Paradise. Some people say: it is the Paradise of eternity (jannat al-khuld) into which the believers will enter in the Hereafter. Others have said: if Adam had not disobeyed, we would be living in Paradise. We say to them: No. The Paradise of the Hereafter is for the Hereafter, and no human lives in it for a period of time and then after that is expelled from it. Rather, as Allah, exalted be He, has informed us, it is the Paradise of eternity; everyone who enters it lives in eternal bliss.

So what is the Paradise in which Adam and Eve lived? This Paradise is the Paradise of trial, or the place in which the trial of applying the method took place. When we read the Noble Qur'an we find that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, has applied the word "jann" (garden, from the root meaning concealment) to the gardens of the earth. The word "jannah" comes from "jann", which means concealment, because in it there are dense trees that conceal whoever lives in it so that no one sees him. And in it are fruits that give him continuity, giving him the continuation of life so that he does not need to go out from it. And in the Noble Qur'an we find His saying, exalted be He:

﴿Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to pick its fruit at morning, and did not make exception [by saying, "If Allah wills"].﴾ (Surah al-Qalam)

This is the story of the brothers who owned a garden of the gardens of the earth, but they withheld the right of the poor, the needy and the orphan, so Allah took away the fruit of the whole garden and burned its trees. And there in Surah al-Kahf is the story of the owner of the two gardens, in His saying, exalted be He:

﴿And present to them a parable: two men, for one of whom We had made two gardens of grapevines and surrounded them with date palms and placed between them fields of crops.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf)

It is the story of that man to whom Allah gave two gardens. Instead of thanking Allah, exalted be He, for His blessings, he disbelieved and denied the Resurrection and the Reckoning. And in Surah Saba', read His saying, exalted be He, about the people of Saba', whom Allah guided and for whom He made clear the straight path, but they preferred disbelief. And read His saying, blessed and exalted be He:

﴿There was for Sheba in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and the left. "Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him; a good city and a forgiving Lord." But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam and replaced their two gardens with two gardens producing bitter fruit and tamarisk and some lote-trees, a little. That We repaid them for their disbelief; and do We repay except the ungrateful?﴾ (Surah Saba')

Thus we see that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, in the Noble Qur'an has applied the word "jannah" to the gardens of this world, and did not confine it to the Paradise of the Hereafter.

So when Adam, to whom Allah, glorified and exalted be He, said:

﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise﴾ (part of verse 19, Surah al-A'raf)

it is not the Paradise of eternity, but a Paradise in which the trial of applying the method would be carried out. Therefore one should not say: how did Iblis enter Paradise after he disobeyed and disbelieved? Because this is not the Paradise of eternity, and you must pay close attention to this, so that it is not said that the disobedience of Adam is what expelled mankind from Paradise. For before Allah created Adam, He defined his mission, saying:

﴿And [mention] when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority (khalifah)."﴾ (part of verse 30, Surah al-Baqarah)

So Adam was created for the khilafah (vicegerency) on the earth, and whoever of his offspring is righteous enters the Paradise of eternity in the Hereafter, and whoever enters the Paradise of eternity lives in bliss forever.

And the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, says: ﴿and eat therefrom in [ease and] abundance wherever you will﴾. So Allah, glorified and exalted be He, supplied the Paradise in which Adam and Eve dwelt with everything that guarantees the continuation of their life, just as He created all the blessings that guarantee the continuation of the life of Adam and his offspring on the earth before human life began on the earth. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has the bounty of lordship (rububiyyah); He is the One who created, the One who brought into existence from nothing, and therefore He guaranteed for His creatures what gives them the continuation of life on the earth: water, air, food and blessings that cannot be counted or enumerated. So it is as if Allah had supplied the Paradise in which Adam and his wife dwelt with all the factors of the continuation of their life before they dwelt in it, just as He supplied the earth with all the means of the continuation of human life before Adam descended to it. So His saying, exalted be He: ﴿O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise﴾.

This is the period of training in applying the method. And "sakan" (dwelling, rest) is the place where a person finds rest and always returns to. You may travel for periods, and all the countries you pass through during your journey are not considered a dwelling until you return to your house; that is the dwelling. A man toils and struggles in life, and wherever he goes he returns again to the place where he lives in order to rest there. And His saying, ﴿and do not approach this tree﴾ is the completion of the method. There is a command and a prohibition: "do" and "do not". ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise﴾ is a command; ﴿and eat therefrom in abundance﴾ is a command; ﴿but do not approach this tree﴾ is a prohibition. This is the first method that teaches man obedience to Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and abstention from what He has forbidden. All the messages of heaven and the methods of Allah on the earth are commands and prohibitions: do such-and-such, and do not do such-and-such.

Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, guaranteed Adam life, and not only life but abundance (raghadan), that is, permitted, without toil, in ease and without hardship. We also notice here that what is permitted is abundant and what is prohibited is scarce. Everything in Paradise of food and drink is permitted to Adam, and there is only one restriction: one tree out of the thousands of trees that were in Paradise; only one tree was forbidden.

And if you look at the method from heaven to earth you find that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has permitted in it blessings that cannot be counted or enumerated, and has restricted in it the least of the least. What Allah has forbidden us concerning the blessings of the earth is the least of the least, just as in Adam's Paradise there was one tree and the rest that was permitted is abundant. And if we take the wording of the expressions, we find that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, when He says ﴿We said, O Adam﴾ uses the pronoun "nā" (we), the plural pronoun, although Allah is One, the Unique. They call it the "nūn of majesty" and the "nūn of greatness".

So every event in which the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, uses the "nūn of majesty" and the "nūn of glorification" — because every action requires multiple attributes to be completed. If you want to do something, it requires of you strength, it requires of you knowledge, it requires of you power, it requires of you wisdom. So there are many attributes present that the act requires.

But when the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, speaks of the testimony of tawhid, He says "Indeed, I am Allah," and does not say "Indeed, we are Allah," because He, majestic in His majesty, intends tawhid. In the place of tawhid He uses the singular pronoun, the One, the Unique. But at the beginning of events He uses the pronoun of majesty and greatness. Read His saying, exalted be He:

﴿And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are expanding it.﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat)

And when the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, wished to praise Ibrahim He said: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was a nation (ummah)﴾. What is the meaning of "ummah"? It means one who combines the attributes of goodness that are not combined in an individual but are combined in a nation. So in a nation the attributes of goodness are gathered: this one is distinguished by truthfulness, that one by courage, and another by forbearance. So the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, wished to say that Ibrahim was a nation, that is, he was one who combined the attributes of goodness.

And in His saying ﴿We said, O Adam﴾, "Adam" is a proper name for the named one who is the first of God's creation from mankind. "Uskun" (dwell) requires two elements: tranquility and reassurance. This is the meaning of "uskun": providing tranquility and reassurance, and from it is taken the name "maskan" (dwelling). And the word "maskan" has been applied to the wife. If the place in which you dwell lacks one of these two elements, namely tranquility and peace, it is not called a dwelling. And the wife has been called "sakan" as in His saying, exalted be He:

﴿And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you might find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy.﴾ (part of verse 21, Surah al-Rum)

Because tranquility, mercy and blessing are found in a righteous wife. And the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿And pray for them; indeed, your prayer is a comfort (sakan) for them.﴾ (part of verse 103, Surah al-Tawbah)

That is, rest, reassurance and mercy. A person wants in his home that life be restful for him from the toil of work and the clamour of life. And the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, says: ﴿Dwell, you and your wife﴾. It would have been possible to say "uskun wa-zawjuka" (dwell, and your wife), because the subject of an imperative verb is always implicit. But He, glorified be He, said ﴿uskun anta wa-zawjuka﴾. And beware of thinking that "anta" is the subject of the verb "uskun". Rather it is a pronoun that came to separate "uskun" from "zawjuka", so that the noun is not conjoined to the verb.

We must note that the word "zawj" (spouse) is applied to the individual together with his like. Therefore He did not use the feminine ta' (زوجتك, "zawjatuka"). "Uskun anta wa-zawjatuka" would be the feminine form. Because the legal command from Allah applies equally to male and female. And read His saying, exalted be He:

﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer﴾ (part of verse 40, Surah Ghafir)

So the two are equal in this respect. What did Allah, glorified and exalted be He, provide for Adam and his wife in this Paradise? Read His saying, blessed and exalted be He:

﴿Indeed, it is [granted] to you that you will not be hungry therein or be naked, and that you will not be thirsty therein or be exposed to the sun.﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, verses 118–119)

These are the elements of life that Allah provided for Adam and his wife in the Paradise of practical faith-trial and obligation. Thus we see from the attributes that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has given us for this Paradise that it is not the Paradise of the Hereafter. Firstly, because there is obligation in it, in His saying ﴿and do not approach this tree﴾; and the Paradise of the Hereafter has no obligation in it. And the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, permitted Adam and Eve to eat as they wished from the Paradise. And the Paradise contains many varieties. Therefore He said ﴿wherever you will﴾.

You cannot offer a person one or two kinds and say, "Eat whatever you want," because he has only a narrow field of choice in front of him, and the small number of kinds makes the soul weary. Therefore there must be many and numerous kinds.

Then came the prohibition, in His saying: "but do not approach this tree", meaning do not draw near to its place. But why did the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, not say "and do not eat from this tree"? Because Allah, majestic in His majesty, out of mercy toward Adam and his wife, did not want them to fall into the seduction of disobedience. For if He had said "do not eat from this tree", it would have been permitted for them to approach it, and then its beautiful appearance would attract them and they would approach its fruit, which its pleasant fragrance and attractive colour would tempt them toward. Then the seduction would occur, and under this enticement their hands would extend to the tree to eat from it.

But Allah, exalted be He, knows that when something is forbidden to the human soul and it does not protect itself from what surrounds it, that makes it more likely not to do it. So when Allah forbade wine, He did not say "wine has been forbidden to you," for then we would have sat in wine gatherings with those who drink it, or traded in it, and all this would be an enticement to drink wine. Rather He said: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, verse 90)

This noble text has led us to keep away from the places where wine is found, so we do not sit with those who drink it, and we do not trade in it, lest we fall into disobedience. So if you see a place where there is wine, stay away from it immediately, so that...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 36:

﴿So Satan caused them to slip from it, and removed them from that in which they had been, and We said: "Go down, some of you enemies to others, and for you on earth will be a dwelling place and provision for a time."﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted, had settled Adam and his wife in Paradise, and had informed them of what is lawful and what is unlawful, Satan began his task: the task of his terrible enmity toward Adam and his descendants. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿So Satan caused them to slip﴾, meaning that Satan set about his task and brought them to a slip, which is a stumble or a fall. How did this happen, when Allah, the Exalted, had advised Adam and his wife not to follow Satan, and had made known to them that he is their enemy? In His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not get you both out of Paradise, for you will be distressed﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 117).

So the enmity was declared and forewarned. Let us suppose it had not been declared. Did Adam not witness the occasion on which Iblis disobeyed Allah's command and did not prostrate to Adam? Did he not know the extent of Iblis's arrogance toward him, in his saying ﴿I am better than him﴾ and his saying ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ All of this should have alerted Adam that Iblis would never bring him any good.

The Truth, glorified is He, did not suffice with the natural indications that arose from Iblis's position in refusing to prostrate. Rather, He informed Adam that Satan is an enemy to him and to his wife. The Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿So Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been﴾. From what did He remove them? From the pleasant life, the abundance of blessing in Paradise, and from the calm and assurance that their provision comes to them without toil. Therefore the Truth will come in another verse and say: ﴿so let him not get you both out of Paradise, for you will be distressed﴾.

Here we must ask: why did He not say "you two will be distressed" (fatashqa)?

This is a notice from the Truth, glorified is He, toward the task of the woman and the task of the man in life. The task of the woman is to be a rest for her husband when he returns to his home; she removes his fatigue and his hardship. As for the task of the man, it is work, until he provides food and shelter for his wife and children. Work is fatigue and movement.

Thus the Truth, blessed and exalted, drew our attention to the fact that the man's task is to toil and to be distressed, and then he comes to his family, where there is tranquility, rest and assurance.

If this is the reality, why does the world come to change this order? We say that the world is what exhausts itself and exhausts the world. The woman's work is a distress for her; her task is the home, and she has no time for anything else. If she works, that is at the expense of her children, her home and her husband. From here distress arises in society: children are lost, the husband flees to a place where there is a woman who gives him the rest he needs, and society ends in chaos.

Adam should have been alert to the fact that Iblis regarded himself as the cause of his expulsion from the mercy of Allah; so he should not have accepted from him advice or speech, and should have been cautious. How did Satan cause Adam and his wife to slip? Allah, the Exalted, explained this to us, but not in Surah al-Baqarah; rather in another verse. He, the Exalted, said:

﴿Then Satan whispered to them to reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts, and said: "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels or become among the eternal"﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 20).

So Iblis said, falsely, that whoever eats from this tree becomes an angel and becomes eternal, not dying. The whispering of Satan is accomplished through false speech to beautify disobedience, and Satan is not concerned with what sin is committed; he wants you disobedient in any way. But the self, when it whispers to you toward sin, wants a particular thing. This is the difference between the whispering of Satan and the whispering of the self. Satan wants you disobedient by any sin; if you refrain on one side, he comes to you from another side. He said to Adam: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ But this attempt did not succeed, so he said to them: ﴿Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become angels or become among the eternal﴾. And it escaped Adam that if this were true, Iblis would have eaten from the tree, and he would not have asked the Truth, glorified is He, to grant him respite until the Day of Religion.

What made Adam fall into disobedience? It was heedlessness or forgetfulness. The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no determination﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 115).

Is forgetfulness a disobedience, such that the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so erred﴾ (part of verse 121, Surah Ta-Ha)?

Yes, forgetfulness was a disobedience among earlier nations. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "My nation is pardoned for error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do" (1). "He forgot and disobeyed" carry one meaning.

And His saying, the Exalted:

﴿He said: "Go down, some of you enemies to others, and for you on earth will be a dwelling place and provision for a time"﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 24).

This descent is the beginning of man's coming down to the earth to undertake his task in this world. Since the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿and for you on earth will be a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾, it is therefore a life limited by its appointed time and according to its measure.

As for those who say that there must be a human being whom we call a redeemer, who ransoms the world by his crucifixion or otherwise, for the sin that Adam committed: we say to him, you have not understood anything about Allah, because the story here is of an error that occurred and was corrected. There is a difference between error (khata') and sin (khati'ah). Error is corrected, but sin is punished. Adam erred, and Allah corrected him, and he received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance. So there is no sin after Allah taught him repentance and he turned to Allah. Then what did Adam do, that we should say we deliver the world from Adam's sin, that he ate from the tree? And are all the sins of the world only eating?

Who caused killing and the shedding of blood, adultery, rape, backbiting and slander?

If their speech were correct, there would necessarily be no sin on earth, since the redeemer who ransomed the world from sin has been found. But sin remains. And who said that sin is inherited, so that the whole world inherits Adam's sin? And Allah, the Exalted, says: "No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another."

As for the saying of the Truth, glorified is He, ﴿and We said: Go down, some of you enemies to others﴾, the enmity here is between Satan and man. The enmity is also between the devils of mankind and the believers, and this enmity leads us to activity and alertness.

The orientalists oppose Islam, but their opposition gives us activity to research and to investigate, so that we may respond to them. The soldiers of Satan from mankind oppose the believers, and their enmity gives us immunity so that we do not err and do not become heedless. So as long as you have an enemy, try to surpass him by every means.

Perhaps human civilization does not advance as quickly as it advances in time of war, for in war each opponent tries to overcome his opponent, and all forces are mobilized to surpass other states scientifically. These advances and inventions may be for destruction and killing, but after the war ends they are directed to human advancement on earth. The splitting of the atom was reached by them in wars; the rockets by which man reached the moon were the result of a war; and the various scientific advances that took place in America and the Soviet Union had as their basis the enmity of each camp for the other.

As for His saying: ﴿Go down, some of you enemies to others﴾: descent may be from a higher place to a lower place, and descent may be figurative, as when you say, "This man has come down in my estimation since he did such-and-such." He did not descend from a higher place to a lower place, but he descended in his worth. Distances do not mean nearness or farness: a person may sit beside you while you feel nothing of him, and another may be hundreds of miles away yet be closer to your heart than the one sitting beside you. Whether the descent was material or immaterial, it occurred so that Adam might undertake his task on earth. And enmity between faith and disbelief continues.

Thus, after Adam's disobedience, he and Eve descended from Paradise to live their lives on earth. And His saying, ﴿Go down﴾, means that Adam, Eve and Iblis descended to the earth after the test of faith was completed.

Allah, the Exalted, made clear to Adam, in practice, that Iblis is his enemy, who does not wish him good, and that he is a liar in everything he promises man. Allah has defined the worldly life as a limited life, its capacities limited and its enjoyments limited, in His saying: ﴿and for you on earth will be a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾.

That is, no one will remain on earth except to the extent of the lifespan Allah has decreed for him, and then he dies. Thereby Allah warned Adam and his descendants not to take life as their goal, because its enjoyment is small and its duration short.

1 (Narrated by al-Tabarani from Thawban).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 37:

﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He turned to him in forgiveness. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ (2:37)

Adam and Eve descended to the earth to carry out their mission in the universe. Before they began this mission, God, glorified and exalted is He, let them undergo a practical experience of applying the methodology (manhaj) and of the seduction of Satan. He warned them that Satan is an enemy to them. After the disobedience had occurred, it was necessary for God, exalted is He, to legislate repentance as a mercy to His servants. The legislation of repentance is not a mercy to the disobedient one alone, but a mercy to the whole society. For if a person disobeys and knows that there is no repentance for him, and that he is condemned to abide forever in the Fire, he persists in his criminality, because as long as he has no hope of salvation from the punishment of the Hereafter, he persists in disobedience, since there is no hope of forgiveness or repentance.

Who will suffer in this case? It is the society in which that disobedient one lives. The believers will be the most afflicted of people, because they are people of goodness and tolerance, and because God, blessed and exalted is He, has commanded them to pardon and to forgive. Read His saying, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 24:22)

And His saying:

﴿And that you pardon is nearer to righteousness. And do not forget graciousness between you.﴾ (part of 2:237)

There are many verses in the Noble Qur'an that urge the believers to pardon. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My Lord commanded me with nine things, and I command you with them: to be sincere in secret and in public; to be moderate in wealth and in poverty; to pardon him who wrongs me; to give to him who deprives me; to maintain ties with him who cuts me off; that my silence be contemplation, my speech remembrance, and my gaze be a lesson." (1) 

So if repentance had not been legislated, the whole society would suffer, especially the believers who were commanded to meet aggression with forgiveness and wrongdoing with pardon. Therefore the legislation of repentance by God, exalted is He, is a mercy to all people. God, majestic in His majesty, legislated repentance first; then, after He legislated it, the disobedient one repented; then, after that, God accepts the repentance or does not accept it, according to His will. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Then He turned to them so they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ (part of 9:118)

Adam received words from his Lord, and He turned to him in forgiveness. Is there a sin after Adam's repentance and God's acceptance of this repentance? Some people say that Adam disobeyed and Allah accepted his repentance, while Iblis disobeyed and Allah made him abide forever in the Fire. We say: you have not understood what Adam did. He ate from the forbidden tree, and when he knew that he had erred and disobeyed, he did not persist in disobedience, nor did he return the command to the One who commanded. Rather, he said: "O Lord, Your command and Your methodology are true, but I did not master myself, so forgive me."

Adam acknowledged his sin, acknowledged his weakness, acknowledged that the methodology is true, and sought repentance from God, glorified and exalted is He. But Iblis returned the command to the One who commanded. He said: ﴿I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾, and he said ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾, and he said ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾, and he said ﴿I will surely take control of his descendants, except for a few﴾. So Iblis here returned the command to the One who commanded; he did not acknowledge his sin, and he does not say, "O Lord, my weakness overcame me, and You are the Truth and Your word is the Truth." Rather, he returned the matter to God, exalted is He, and was obstinate, saying, "I will do such and such, and I will do such and such." And this is disbelief in God.

Beware of returning the command to God, glorified and exalted is He. If you do not pray, do not say, "What is the benefit of prayer?" If you do not pay zakat, do not say, "The legislation of zakat is an injustice to the wealthy." If you do not apply the law of God, do not say, "This Shari'ah no longer suits the modern age." For by that you would have disbelieved, and we seek refuge in God. But say, "O my Lord, the obligation of prayer is true, the obligation of zakat is true, and the application of the Shari'ah is true, but I do not master myself, so have mercy on my weakness, O Lord of the worlds." If you do this, you will only be a disobedient one.

The difference between the disobedience of Adam and the disobedience of Iblis is that Adam acknowledged his disobedience and his sin, while Iblis returned the command to the One who commanded. So Adam had disobeyed, and Iblis had disbelieved, and we seek refuge in God. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He turned to him in forgiveness.﴾ As for these words that Adam received, the scholars wished to specify them. What are these words? Is it Adam's saying as mentioned in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:23)

This noble verse indicates to us that Adam's sin was not a sin of arrogance but a sin of heedlessness, whereas Iblis's sin was a sin of arrogance against the command of God. When Adam disobeyed, a humility occurred in him, so he said: "O my Lord, Your command not to approach the tree is true, but I did not master myself. So Adam acknowledged the right of God in legislation, whereas Iblis objected to this command and said:

"Shall I prostrate to one You created from clay?"

The words that Adam received from God, glorified and exalted is He, may be: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾. Or they may be: "O Allah, there is no god but You, glory be to You, my Lord, and praise be to You. Indeed, I have wronged myself greatly, so forgive me, O best of forgivers," or "accept my repentance, O best of those who accept repentance," or he said: "Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah." The point is that God, glorified and exalted is He, inspired Adam with words through which he draws near to Him, whether this noble verse or other words.

If we look at God's teaching Adam words so that He might turn to him in forgiveness, we find a vital principle in the life of society. For God, glorified and exalted, as we said, if He had not legislated repentance and had not given us the good news that He would accept it, then whoever committed a single sin would never return from disobedience, and the whole world would suffer.

God, glorified and exalted, created us as choosers and did not create us as compelled. Compulsion establishes the attribute of power for God, but God, glorified and exalted, wants us to come to Him out of love and not out of compulsion. Therefore He created us as choosers, and placed in us a capacity that can disobey and obey. And as long as there is choice, a person chooses this or that.

God did not create humans who choose good all the time, nor humans who choose evil at all times. Among the good there are those who fall into evil once, and among the wicked there are those who do good once. The servant was not created to choose absolute good, or to choose absolute evil. Therefore sometimes we forget, or we are heedless, or we disobey. And as long as the servant is exposed to sin, God, glorified and exalted, legislated repentance, so that the servant does not despair of God's mercy and repents to return to God. And it has come in wisdom: "The disobedience that leaves one humbled and broken is better than the obedience that leaves one proud and arrogant."

Thus, when Adam descended to begin his mission in life, he did not carry any sin on his shoulders. He had erred, and God taught him words of repentance, so he repented, and God accepted his repentance. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾, the word "tawwab" indicates that God, exalted is He, does not take His servants to account for a single sin, because even if He repents of a single sin of each of His servants, He would be Tawwab. Intensiveness in the attribute comes from two directions: first, that the matter recurs several times from a small number of persons, or from one person; or that the matter occurs once but from many persons.

For example, if you say: "So-and-so is a great eater," he may be a great eater because he eats a large quantity of food, and so he is called a great eater. He does not exceed in the number of times the normal meals of a human being, but he eats a large amount, so we call him a great eater; he eats, for example, ten loaves at breakfast, and the same at lunch, and the same at dinner.

A person may also be a great eater when the same act is repeated, such as eating ordinary quantities of food but eating fifteen times a day, for example. God, glorified and exalted, is Tawwab because His creatures are many. If each of them sinned once, the number of their sins which God would forgive would be an enormous quantity. And if someone is found who sins several times a day, God, exalted is He, is also Tawwab toward him if he repents and turns to Him.

So sometimes intensiveness comes in the act, even if it is done by one person; and sometimes intensiveness comes in the act because those who do it are many individuals.

Thus Adam committed one sin, which required that God be Tawwab; but the descendants of Adam after him would be a numerous creation, so the intensiveness comes from the side of number.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾: Our master 'Umar was approached by a woman screaming and shouting because her son had been caught stealing. She said to 'Umar: "My son did not steal except this time." 'Umar said to her: "God is more merciful to His servant than to take him at the first time. He must have stolen before... and I challenge that there is a criminal who is caught the first time." The word tawwab indicates that he is caught after two or three times; God conceals His servant once and again, but if he increases and persists in disobedience, God stops him at his limit. This is the meaning of tawwab.

And the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is Tawwab through His mercy, because there is someone who pardons and keeps reminding you of the pardon, to the point that the one pardoned says: "I wish you had punished me and had not reminded me of the pardon every hour." But the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is Tawwab and Merciful. He turns to the servant, and has mercy on him, erasing his sins from him.

1 (Narrated by Razin).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 38:

﴿We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve."﴾ (38)

The Truthful, Exalted One says in this verse: ﴿We said, "Go down from it, all of you"﴾. In Surah Ta-Ha He, may His majesty be exalted, says ﴿He said, "Go down from it, both of you, all together"﴾, when addressing with the plural form. The address was to all the progeny of Adam hidden in his loins, a command to all of them to descend: Adam, Eve, and the progeny. Because each one of us, until the Hour arises, is a part of Adam. Therefore we must attend to the word of the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿And We certainly created you and then formed you; then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾ (from verse 11 of Surah al-A'raf).

We observe here that the address is in the plural form. The Truthful, Exalted One did not say, "I created you, then I formed you, then I said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam'." It is as if the Truthful, Exalted One wants to draw our attention to the fact that at the moment of creation all the progeny of Adam were hidden in his loins. He created them all, then He formed them all, then He commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam. Were we present then? Yes, we were present in Adam. Therefore the Truthful, Exalted One says ﴿Go down﴾ so that we know this address is directed to Adam and all his progeny until the Day of Resurrection.

Once He says ﴿Go down from it, both of you, all together﴾, because here begins the bearing of responsibility for Adam. At this moment, the moment of descent to the earth, the method of God begins its mission in life. As long as there is a method and individual application, responsibility is individual, and the plural does not come here.

So the Truthful, Exalted One says ﴿Go down from it, both of you, all together﴾. We observe that the command to descend here is in the dual. Then He, Blessed and Exalted, says "all together", in the plural. We say that since this is the beginning of the obligation, there are two parties who will confront one another: the first party is Adam and his spouse, and the second party is Iblis. They are three, but in the battle of faith they are only two sides: Adam, Eve and their progeny are one side, and Satan is another side. It is as if God, Exalted, wants to draw our attention to the fact that this descent relates to the method and its application on earth. In the method, Adam and Eve are keen on obedience, while Iblis is keen to lead them to disobedience.

In His saying, Exalted: ﴿And when guidance comes to you from Me﴾, we observe that God, Glorified and Exalted, after Adam went through the trial and fell into disobedience, taught him the words of repentance and advised him that if he becomes heedless he should repent, and God, Glorified and Exalted, will accept his repentance.

Thus the Truthful, Exalted One wants Adam and Eve to dwell on the earth and begin their mission in life, and God guides them to good, in confirmation of His saying: ﴿And when guidance comes to you from Me﴾. Guidance (hudan) has two meanings: it means indicating the good, or indicating the path that leads to the good. There is also guidance which is assistance in faith and increase in it. Read His saying: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their righteousness﴾ (17) (Surah Muhammad).

Guidance here in the noble verse means indicating the path of good. Therefore the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted One says: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance, no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾.

What is fear and what is grief? Fear is that you expect an approaching evil which you have no power to repel, so you fear it. Grief is that you lose something you love and desire. The Truthful, Exalted One says in this verse: whoever walks on the path of faith which I have shown him, and which I have sent down in My method, no fear will be upon them, meaning no good will escape them so that they grieve over it, because all good is in God's method. Whoever follows the method never fears that anything will happen.

This gives us an important matter in society. The one who has committed no violation, does fear reach him? Never. But the one who commits a violation you always find fearful, lest his affair be exposed, and he is surprised by an evil he has no power to repel.
