The upright person does not live in fear, because fear has two causes. Either a sin for which I am the cause, and the one walking on the straight path has done nothing whose exposure he fears; or a matter in which I have no part, which my Creator brings about, and this must be for a wisdom. I may have grasped it or not grasped it, but I accept it. So whoever follows the guidance of God does not fear and does not grieve, because he has not sinned, has not broken a law, has not deceived a person, or concealed a crime. So he fears nothing, and even if a sudden event meets him, his heart is at peace. Those who follow God do not fear, and no fear is upon them. As for His saying: ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, it is because the one who lives obedient to God's method has nothing that makes him grieve, for his will in this state submits to the will of his Creator. Everything that happens to him from God is good, even if on the surface it appears otherwise. His faculties are harmonious, and he is at peace with the universe and with himself. The universe hears from him nothing but glorification, obedience and prayer, and all of it is mercy. So he is at peace with himself, at peace with his Lord, and at peace with society.

Society is always happy with the believing person who does not corrupt the earth, but does every good. The believer is a breath of beauty shining in the universe, a blessing of goodness and contentment with all people. And as long as a person is like this, he will never lose what pleases him. If events befall him which God has brought upon him, he meets them only with gratitude, even if he does not know their wisdom. Beware of objecting to God regarding a judgment.

Therefore he says: "My Lord, I praise You for all Your decree and all Your destiny, the praise of contentment with Your judgment and certainty in Your wisdom."

A person reacts to events, but there is a difference between reacting to events alone and reacting to events together with the wisdom of the one who brings them about. Therefore the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, teaches us precision when he said: (The eye sheds tears and the heart grieves, and we say nothing except what pleases our Lord, and indeed, O Ibrahim, we are saddened by your separation.)(1)

Look at faith as it receives events: the eye sheds tears, and the heart is not hard like a stone, but has tenderness. The heart humbles itself before God, acknowledging His wisdom and will.

God, Glorified and Exalted, does not want us to receive events with grief alone, but with grief together with faith. God does not prevent you from grieving, but you must not separate the event from its Causer and His wisdom in it. Therefore, when you go to a bone doctor who breaks your bone in order to set it, does he do you good or harm? Of course he does you good, even though it hurts you.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Ibn Majah and Ahmad, and this is the wording of al-Bukhari.

Almighty Allah, after informing us that when Adam descends to the earth he will receive from Allah a method (manhaj) for the movement of his life, said: whoever follows it will leave his life fear and sorrow behind, and will become secure in this world and the Hereafter. Allah wanted to give us the opposite picture. The ruling in the previous verse concerned those who were guided, and the ruling in this verse concerns those who disbelieved. The Blessed and Exalted Allah says: ﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs﴾. Disbelief, as we have explained, is an attempt to conceal the existence of Allah, the Necessarily Existent. And the attempt to conceal this existence is a declaration that Allah exists. For you do not try to conceal a thing unless it has existence first.

A thing that has no existence does not need to be concealed, because it is not present in our minds. Our minds do not understand or grasp except what exists. The mental image comes first, and then the name or verbal expression comes after it. Therefore, if a person speaks to you about something that has no existence, you do not understand it, and you cannot comprehend it unless it is likened to something that exists, such as being told: "like this mountain," or "like this lake," or "like the disc of the sun," or other things, until you are able to understand. You do not understand what does not exist unless it is likened to something that exists.

Everything must have existed first. Then afterwards the linguistic academies of the world gather to search for a word that expresses it, after it has come to exist in the mental image. For example, there was no name for the rocket before the rocket existed, nor for the spaceship before it was invented, nor for laser rays before they were discovered. So all of this existed first, and the name was assigned to it afterwards.

Those who disbelieve try to conceal the existence of Allah, and concealing the existence of Allah, glory be to Him, is an affirmation of His existence, because you do not conceal a thing that does not exist. Thus disbelief becomes an affirmation of faith.

Your intellect cannot understand a name unless the meaning exists in your mind. And you will not find any language of the languages of the world that lacks the name of Allah, the Exalted. Rather, Allah, may His majesty be exalted, though He is unseen to us, when His name is mentioned, the young and the old understand it, the ignorant and the learned, the one who has traveled the world and the one who has never left his house. All of these understand Allah through the innate nature of faith that He placed in all our hearts.

So those who disbelieve try to conceal the existence of Allah, the Exalted. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and denied Our signs﴾, the sign (ayah) is the wondrous, striking thing. There are in the universe cosmic signs such as the sun, the moon, the stars, the earth, the mountains, the seas, and other things. These are called signs, a thing beyond human capacity, which Allah the Exalted created to be a sign in His universe and to serve mankind.

And there are the signs, which are miracles. When Allah sends a messenger or prophet to his people, He, glory be to Him, breaks the laws of the universe for him in order to prove to his people that he is a prophet sent from Allah, the Exalted. These signs are intended for those who witness them, because they come to strengthen the believers in the messengers, who pass through a crisis in which they need strengthening, and as an indication of the truthfulness of the prophet's message to his people. The term "signs" is also applied to the verses of the Noble Qur'an, the miraculous speech of Allah, in which He, glory be to Him, placed what confirms the truth of the message, until the Day of Judgment.

Allah, glory be to Him, speaks to us in His signs about how man was created, about the method of heaven for the earth, and other things.

Those who deny the signs of Allah are the disbelievers, they are the polytheists, and they are those who reject Islam and fight the religion. Allah the Exalted has specified their destiny. But is denial a lack of ability to understand? We say that sometimes denial is deliberate, as happened to the people of Pharaoh when Allah afflicted them with calamities, diseases, and the lesser punishment so that they would believe. Yet, despite their certainty that these signs were from Allah, the Exalted, they did not acknowledge them. The Majestic Lord says:

﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ (Qur'an 27:14)

The signs in the universe are many. If we paid attention to them, we would believe. They do not need thought; rather, Allah, out of mercy to us, made them manifest so that people may perceive them, all people. Yet some, despite that, deny the signs of Allah, and these are the ones who want to follow the desires of the self. Allah, glory be to Him, gathered the disbelievers and deniers of Allah's signs into one punishment. The Majestic Lord said: ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire﴾. The companion (sahib) is one who is fond of his companion, likes to sit with him, and spends his most pleasant times with him. So His saying, the Exalted: ﴿companions of the Fire﴾ is evidence of the Fire's love for them; it rejoices at them when they enter it, just as a friend rejoices in his friend, and it never wants to part from them.

For this reason, read the saying of Allah, glory be to Him:

﴿The Day We say to Hell, "Are you filled?" and it says, "Are there more?"﴾ (Qur'an 50:30)

Thus we see the extent of the passion between the Fire and the disbelievers. The Fire accompanies them everywhere, and this companionship is not repugnant to the Fire; rather, it is a companionship the Fire loves. When the Fire burns every disbeliever, sinner, and hypocrite, it is happy, because it punishes those who disbelieved in Allah's method and denied His signs in the worldly life. The same is true of Paradise: Paradise also loves the companionship of everyone who believed in Allah, sincerely worshipped Him, and applied His method. Read His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves to their Lord, those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein forever﴾ (Qur'an 11:23)

That is, Paradise accompanies the believers, loves them, and stays with them, just as the Fire accompanies the disbelievers and deniers. And just as the Fire is happy when it burns the disbeliever, Paradise is happy when it bestows pleasure upon the believer. Then the Almighty says: ﴿they will abide therein forever﴾, meaning that the punishment there is constant, does not change, does not slacken, and is not lightened; rather, it continues forever. Read His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿Those are the ones who have bought the worldly life at the price of the Hereafter, so their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be helped﴾ (Qur'an 2:86)

Thus we know that Allah, glory be to Him, sent down the method to the earth with Adam, and that Adam descended to the earth with guidance, to apply the first method of heaven on earth. It is as if Allah, glory be to Him, never left man for a single moment on earth without giving him the method that shows him the path of guidance and the path of misguidance. Along with the method, repentance was legislated, and the acceptance of repentance was legislated, so that man would not despair and would not feel that if he erred or forgot, his destiny would be Hell. Rather, he would feel that the doors of heaven are always open to him, and that Allah who created him is merciful to him: if he errs, He opens for him the doors of repentance and forgives his sins, so that every person feels Allah's care for him on earth, from the very beginning of life.

So the method is available to whoever wants to believe, repentance is open to everyone who errs, and Allah, glory be to Him, warned Adam and his descendants that whoever obeys and believes will live a good life in this world and the Hereafter, while whoever disbelieves and denies will face everlasting punishment.

Allah made Adam aware of his enemy Iblis and asked him to beware of him. So what did the children of Adam do? Did they receive Allah's method with obedience or with disobedience? And did they adhere to the teachings of Allah, or did they cast them behind their backs?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 40:

﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and fulfil My covenant, and I shall fulfil your covenant, and fear Me alone.﴾ (40)

After Allah related to us the story of creation and how it began with Adam, and the enmity of Iblis toward Adam and its cause, He related to us the first test of the (divine) method (manhaj) in one of the Gardens, and how Adam was put to the test, so Satan seduced him and he disobeyed. Then he descended to the earth armed with the method of Allah, and protected by repentance from being tyrannical. The mission of Adam on the earth began..

Indeed, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wished to present to us the procession of the messages (risalat) and how the children of Adam received the method of Allah with disbelief and disobedience. Allah, majestic is His majesty, chose the story of the Children of Israel because it is the most abundant of stories in miracles, and the prophets of the Children of Israel are among the most numerous of the prophets sent to a single nation. This does not mean that they are preferred; rather, because they were the most disobedient and sinful of nations, they had the most prophets. Whenever they emerged from one miracle, they deviated; then another miracle would come to them, and they would deviate again. Thus Allah, because of their wrongdoing, decreed that they be scattered across the earth and then gathered again in one place, so that they might taste the punishment and retribution as recompense for their disobedience and disbelief. For this reason the story of the Children of Israel took that enormous size in the Book of Allah, and in strengthening the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Moses (peace be upon him), whom Allah sent to the Children of Israel, is among the Messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-azm). Therefore you find in it education (tarbiyah) first, and education second..

We must pay attention to the saying of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿O Children of Israel﴾. For the Truth, majestic is His majesty, when He wants to address all of mankind, says: ﴿O Children of Adam﴾, and read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer﴾ (part of verse 31, Surah al-A'raf).

And His saying, glorified is He:

﴿O Children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you﴾ (part of verse 11, Surah al-A'raf).

Why does Allah, exalted is He, address us with His saying: "O Children of Adam"? Because He wants to remind us of a blessing upon us from the beginning of creation, since these blessings concern Adam and his descendants. Allah, exalted is He, created Adam with His own Hands, commanded the angels to prostrate to him, and prepared for him a universe full of everything that guarantees the continuation of his life, not only the necessities but also the luxuries. Then the Truth trained him for what he would be exposed to of Satan's seduction, and made him understand that Satan is his enemy. Then He taught him the words of repentance so that He might accept his repentance, and bestowed upon him blessings that cannot be counted or enumerated.

So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wants to remind us of all of that, so that we might be ashamed to commit disobedience after all this honouring of man. When we remember the blessings of Allah upon us, we feel shame at meeting these blessings with disobedience.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has taught us a knowledge by which He distinguished us from His angels. Therefore it was necessary that we remain thankful and worshipping throughout our lives in this world. But we notice that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, began this noble verse with His saying: ﴿O Children of Israel﴾. Why? And who is Israel?

Isra'il is derived from two words: Isr and Il. (Isr) means "servant who is chosen" or "elect." (Il) means "God" in Hebrew. So the meaning of the word is "the chosen one of God" (safwat Allah), and the choosing here is for Ya'qub, not for his descendants..

When we look at Israel, who is Ya'qub, how he took this name, we find that he took the name because he was afflicted by Allah with a great affliction, by which he deserved to be a chosen friend of Allah. When Allah, exalted is He, calls the people of Moses by His saying: "O Children of Israel", He wants to remind them of Israel's station with Allah, what he faced, and what he bore in his life. So remember what he enjoined upon you when death attended him.. Read the saying of the Blessed and Exalted:

﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are submitting."﴾ (133) (Surah al-Baqarah).

Then comes the saying of Ya'qub after that.. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿O my sons, indeed Allah has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except while you are Muslims.﴾ (part of verse 132, Surah al-Baqarah).

That is the bequest with which Ya'qub enjoined his sons. In it there is knowledge and in it there is admonition: knowledge that Allah is one God with no partner, and that the religion is Islam; and admonition and reminder that Allah chose the religion for them, so let them be keen upon it until death.

This bequest came when Ya'qub was attended by death, and at the hour of death a person is truthful with himself, truthful with his Lord, and truthful with his descendants. So when He, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿O Children of Israel﴾, He wants to remind them of Israel, who is Ya'qub, and how he bore affliction and remained patient, and his bequest to them at the hour of death.

Indeed, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, reminds the sons of His favour upon the fathers, perhaps they will be admonished or be ashamed of disobedience, just as there is a righteous servant whose sons have transgressed against themselves.

It is said to them:

"Are you not ashamed? You are the sons of so-and-so, the righteous man. It is not proper that you commit what angers Allah…" ﴿O Children of Israel﴾

Israel is Ya'qub son of Ishaq, and Ishaq is son of Ibrahim, and Ibrahim begot Ishaq and Isma'il. And our Messenger (ﷺ) is of the descendants of Isma'il. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour upon you﴾. But when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, addresses the Muslims, He does not say "remember the favour of Allah"; rather He says: ﴿Remember Allah﴾, because the Children of Israel were materialistic and worldly.

So the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, was saying to them: since you are materialistic and worldly, then remember Allah's material favour upon you.

But we, the Muslims, are a non-material nation.

There is a difference between a person being with the favour and being with the Bestower. The materialists love the favour, while the non-materialists love the Bestower and live in His company.

Therefore, the address to the Muslims is: ﴿Remember Allah﴾, because we are with the Bestower, whereas His address to the Children of Israel was: ﴿Remember the favour of Allah﴾.

The sacred hadith says: (I am worthy that I be feared, so let no god be associated with Me; whoever fears to associate a god with Me, he is worthy that I forgive him)(1).

So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is worthy of worship even if He had not created Paradise and Hellfire. For this reason the believers are the people of affliction from Allah. Why? Because affliction from Him is a favour. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, boasts to His angels about His servants and says: "They worship Me for My own sake." The angels say: "Rather, they worship You for Your favour upon them." He says to them: "I shall withdraw it from them, and they will still love Me.." And among My servants are those whose supplication I love, so I test them until they say, "O Lord," for their voices are loved by Allah, glorified and exalted is He. Therefore, when He tests a servant in his health, for example, and removes from him the favour of well-being, you find that the ignorant one looks at this with a look of dissatisfaction. But the one who is deep in knowledge looks to the saying of Allah in the sacred hadith: that Allah, mighty and majestic, says on the Day of Resurrection: "O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me." He says: "O Lord, how could I visit You, and You are the Lord of the worlds?" He says: "Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was sick and you did not visit him? Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him?"(2) So if the believer loses the favour of well-being, he should not despair, for Allah, exalted is He, wants him to live in the company of the Bestower, and that throughout the period of his illness he is in the company of Allah, exalted is He.

Therefore, when the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾, its meaning is: if you are not believers for My own sake, then be ashamed to commit disobedience with My favour which I bestowed upon you. The favour is mentioned here because the Children of Israel worship Allah for the sake of His favours.

﴿Remember My favour﴾. Remembrance (dhikr) is guarding against forgetfulness, because the routine of life makes us forget the Cause of the favours. The sun rises every day; how many of us remember that it rises only by the permission of Allah, and so thank Him? The rain falls every period; who among us remembers that Allah sends down the rain, and so thanks Him? Remembrance is by the tongue and by the heart. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is unseen and hidden from us, and His greatness lies in His being hidden. But the favours of Allah, glorified is He, point to Him for us.. So by remembrance He is always in our minds, and by His favours, His remembrance and thanks are always present.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, asked the Children of Israel to remember only the favour which He bestowed upon them. It was obligatory for them to obey Allah and so remember the Bestower, because the remembrance of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, places you in a firm refuge, where no harm or evil reaches you.

The remembrance of Allah the Bestower gives us the movement of life in everything. The remembrance of Allah produces humility (khushu') in hearts, reduces sins, benefits all people, and makes the movement of life upright. When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Remember My favour﴾, its meaning is: remember Me even through the favour which I bestowed upon you. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and fulfil My covenant, I shall fulfil your covenant﴾, the covenant ('ahd) is the pact (mithaq). Read His saying, glorified and exalted is He:

﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot, and We found in him no determination.﴾ (115) (Surah Ta-Ha).

So the covenant is a binding matter between the servant and his Lord. What is the covenant which Allah wants the Children of Israel to fulfil, so that Allah may fulfil His covenant to them?

We say: is it the covenant of the fitrah? The covenant of the fitrah, as we have said, is to believe in Allah and thank Him for His favours. And as we have said: if a person descends to a place where there is no one, then sleeps and rises and finds a table laden with favours before him, will he not ask himself: who made this? If he thinks a little, he will know that it must have a maker, especially since creation here is beyond the capacities of human beings. If Allah, glorified and exalted is He, sends a messenger who says that Allah is the One who created and brought into being, and no claimant or opponent appears, because bringing about these favours is beyond human power, the matter is settled for Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

So the remembrance of Allah and thanking Him is obligatory by the sound fitrah, needing no complications or philosophies. And fulfilling the covenant of Allah, that we worship Him and thank Him, is the fitrah of faith in response to the favours He has given us. Yet the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, is found to say:

﴿And fulfil My covenant, I shall fulfil your covenant﴾ (part of verse 40, Surah al-Baqarah).

And in another verse:

﴿So remember Me, I will remember you﴾ (part of verse 152, Surah al-Baqarah).

And in a third verse:

﴿If you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet﴾ (part of verse 7, Surah Muhammad). What is this matter which the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to draw our attention to in these noble verses? Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wants us to know that He has placed in our hand the key to Paradise. In the hand of each one of us is the key to the path that leads him either to Paradise or to Hellfire. Therefore, if you fulfil the covenant, Allah fulfils His; if you remember Allah, He remembers you; if you support Allah, He supports you..

The sacred hadith says: "And if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running"(3). Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to alert us that the key is in our hands. So when we begin with obedience, the giving of Allah is without limits; when we draw near to Allah, He draws near to us; and when we distance ourselves from Him, He calls us. This is the faith of the fitrah.

Is this the covenant intended by Allah, glorified is He, in His saying: ﴿Fulfil My covenant, I shall fulfil your covenant﴾, or is it the covenant which Allah took from the prophets, that they should convey to their peoples that when a messenger comes confirming what they have, they must believe in him and support him? The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, took from all the prophets the covenant concerning the Messenger of Islam, our master Muhammad (ﷺ).. Or is it the covenant which Allah took through Moses (peace be upon him) from the scholars of the Children of Israel, who received the Torah, recited it, wrote it down and memorised it: a covenant that they would not conceal anything from it.. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those given the Scripture, [saying], "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they threw it behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is what they purchase.﴾ (187) (Surah Ali 'Imran).

The aim of this covenant is that they should not conceal what was revealed about Islam in the Torah, and should not hide the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that it brought. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has given the attributes of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) in the Torah and in the Gospel.. Read His saying, exalted is He:

{And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming…

2 Narrated by Muslim from Abu Hurayrah..
3 Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Tawhid, and by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi..

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 41:

﴿And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you, and do not be the first to disbelieve in it, and do not exchange My signs for a small price, and fear Me alone.﴾ (41)

After Allah, glorified and exalted, reminded the Children of Israel of the covenants they had made upon themselves, [He reminded them] of not altering or changing the Torah, whether by concealing things or adding things. He also reminded them of their covenant regarding belief in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whose attributes Allah, glorified and exalted, mentioned in the Torah. So much so that the Jewish rabbi Ibn Salam used to say to his people in Medina: "I recognised him when I saw him just as I recognise my son, and my recognition of Muhammad is even stronger." That is, he was reminding his people that the attributes of the Messenger ﷺ present in the Torah should not lead them to misidentify him.

The Truthful, Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you﴾. Because the Qur'an confirms the Torah, and the intended Torah here is the genuine Torah before they distorted it. So the Qur'an does not agree with what they possess of the altered or changed Torah; rather, it agrees with the Torah that contains no falsehood.

Then the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿and do not be the first to disbelieve in it﴾. We have said that the Jews were not the first to disbelieve in Muhammad ﷺ; rather, the Quraysh had disbelieved in him in Mecca. The intended meaning in this noble verse is: the first disbeliever in him from among the People of the Book. Why? Because the Quraysh had no connection with the heavenly methodology, and they knew nothing of the earlier scriptures. But the rabbis of the Jews knew the truth of the message, and they used to seek victory through the Messenger of Allah ﷺ over the people of Medina, saying: "The time of a messenger has come, whom we will believe in, and we will kill you with the killing of 'Ad and Iram." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came, instead of hastening to believe in him, they became the first to disbelieve in him.

Allah, glorified and exalted, did not surprise the People of the Book with the coming of Muhammad ﷺ; rather, He alerted them to it in the Torah and the Gospel. Therefore they should have been the first of the believers, not the first of the disbelievers, because the one who came is someone they knew.

As for His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿and do not exchange My signs for a small price﴾: when the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted speaks of the transaction of faith, He uses the words purchase, sale and trade. Read His saying, exalted be He:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise﴾ (part of verse 111, Surah at-Tawbah).

And in another verse He says:

﴿Shall I direct you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? [You should] believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives﴾ (part of verses 10–11, Surah as-Saff).

Indeed, the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted used the words transaction, purchase and sale afterwards in His saying:

﴿O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer on the day of Friday, then proceed to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade﴾ (part of verse 9, Surah al-Jumu'ah).

We know that trade is an intermediary between the producer and the consumer. The producer wants to sell his product, and the consumer needs this product. Profit is a process that lasts a period and may be shorter or longer, depending on the movement of the goods and the demand for them, whether fast or slow. Allah, glorified and exalted, used the act of trading to show us that it is the shortest path to benefit. Trade is carried out by the hand of man: he buys the goods and sells them. But with Allah, you will be taken from some of your own freedom so that He may give you something more lasting and more expansive than it.

As we have said: if we compare the world with its limited lifespan, how many years is each of our lives? Fifty... sixty... seventy!! We find that the world, however long it lasts, will end, and the intelligent person is the one who sacrifices the temporary and finite period so that he may have a share in the eternal period. In this way, this transaction is profitable.

The bliss of this world is according to human capacities, and the bliss of the Hereafter is according to the capacity of Allah, glorified and exalted. A person comes and says: "Why should I constrict myself in this world? Why should I not enjoy?" We say to him: No... what you will receive of punishment and retribution in the Hereafter is not equal to what you took from this world. So the transaction is then a losing one. You purchased something transient and paid for it a price of eternal bliss. And Allah, glorified and exalted, says to the Jews: ﴿and do not exchange My signs for a small price﴾, meaning: do not give up the signs of faith that were given to you in order to take in exchange a small price. When a person takes less than what he gives, that is a reversal of the transaction, and loss always comes from a reversal.

It is as if the verse says: you give up the signs of Allah, which are His complete methodology, to take a commodity of the goods of this world, whose value is small and whose time is short. This is a reversal of the transaction.

Therefore the Qur'anic expression came as a counterpart to this reversal. In transactions, prices are always paid and goods are taken. But in this case that the verse speaks of, in His saying ﴿and do not exchange My signs for a small price﴾, the price that should be paid has been made the thing purchased, and this is folly and error.

Allah says ﴿and do not exchange My signs for a small price﴾, meaning: do not accept the transaction. The thing you should have sacrificed, do not make it the price. Because in this case you have made the price into a commodity. As long as you are going to buy the signs with the price, you have made the signs of Allah a price in order to obtain worldly gains. Would that you had made them a precious price; rather, you have made them a cheap price.

You have disowned your covenant with Allah so that your wealth or your position may remain for you!! But if a person sacrifices some of the pleasures of this world in order to take the enduring pleasures of the Hereafter, then this is the profitable transaction. This is because a person in this world is blessed according to his conception of bliss, but in the Hereafter he is blessed according to Allah's conception of bliss.

Some who do not want to bind themselves to the methodology of Allah hasten for the gains of the transaction in a foolish haste. They want enjoyment, whether lawful or unlawful. We say to each of them: if you believe in the Hereafter or do not believe, the transaction is a losing one, because in both cases you will be punished in the Fire. It is as if you have purchased a passing enjoyment with your faith and your religion, and made disbelief and disobedience of Allah the price. Thus you have reversed the verse, and made what should have been purchased with the methodology of Allah, which is the bliss of the Hereafter, into something sold... and sold for what? For transient bliss! When a person takes less than what he gives, this is a reversal of the transaction.

So it is as if the verse says: you give up the signs of Allah and what they give you of the good of this world and the next, in order to take a transient commodity of the goods of this world, whose price is small. The price is always of material things such as gold, silver and others, and they are not commodities. Suppose you have a treasure of Qarun in gold, and you are in an isolated place and hungry. Would you not give this treasure to someone who would give you a loaf of bread, so that you do not die of hunger? Therefore wealth must not be an end or a commodity. If you make it an end, you will have much wealth but you will not buy anything with it, because wealth is your goal, and society is corrupted. Wealth is a sincere slave, but a wicked master. It is your slave when you spend it; but when you hoard it and grasp at it, it makes you miserable and sick, because you have become its servant.

This noble verse gives us an idea about the Jews, because the axis of their lives and their activities is wealth and gold. Allah, glorified and exalted, has forbidden usury (riba), because with money, usury turns it into a commodity. A hundred is taken for a hundred and fifty, for example... and this corrupts society, because it is supposed that wealth increases through labour. When the increase of wealth becomes without labour, the movement of life is corrupted. The poor grow poorer and the rich grow richer. This is what we see in the world today.

Poor countries grow poorer because they borrow money, and its interest accumulates upon them until the interest exceeds the debt itself. And as time passes, the interest increases, so the debt multiplies and repayment becomes impossible. Rich countries grow richer, because they pay back the loan and recover it at many times its value.

And when Allah, glorified and exalted, says ﴿and do not exchange My signs for a small price﴾, we must not understand that the signs of Allah can be bought at a higher price... No, because however high the price rises, it will be small and very small, since it is set against the signs of Allah. And the signs of Allah are beyond any price. So the transaction is a losing one, whatever its value.

And the saying of the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted: }and fear Me alone{. In the previous verse He said: }and fear Me alone{ [Surah al-Baqarah 2:40], which is a warning. But ﴿and fear Me alone﴾ is an actual reality. His saying ﴿and fear Me alone﴾ [in verse 40] is a warning and caution regarding what will come in the Hereafter. But ﴿and fear Me alone﴾ [in verse 41] means: beware of the attributes of majesty of Allah. The attributes of majesty are those connected with the might and punishment of Allah. Among these attributes are the Compeller (al-Jabbar), the Subduer (al-Qahhar), the Proud (al-Mutakabbir), the Capable (al-Qadir), the Avenger (al-Muntaqim), the Humiliator (al-Mudhill), and other attributes of majesty.

Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Fear Allah﴾ and He says ﴿Fear the Fire﴾. How? We say: Allah, glorified and exalted, wants us to place between ourselves and the Fire, which is one of the soldiers of the punishment of Allah, glorified and exalted, a shield. He wants us to place between ourselves and the punishment of the Fire a shield. And He also wants us to place between ourselves and the attributes of majesty of Allah a shield. So His saying ﴿and fear Me alone﴾ means: place between yourselves and the attributes of majesty of Allah a shield, so that a great punishment does not befall you. And how do we place between ourselves and the attributes of majesty of Allah a shield? By making our deeds in this world conform to the methodology of Allah, glorified and exalted. Thus, piety (taqwa) is required in this world...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 42:

﴿And do not mix the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth while you know [it].﴾

After Almighty Allah warned the Jews not to sell their religion for a small price, namely wealth or worldly influence, He said: ﴿And do not mix the truth with falsehood﴾. The root is labasa (تلبس), derived from libas (اللباس), the clothing we wear. Labs (اللبس) means covering or obscuring, that is, hiding the truth and not showing it. Clothing is a covering for the body that conceals it, so its details are not made clear.

The truth (al-haqq) is the fixed, decreed matter that does not change. Suppose we witnessed something happen, and then each of us related what occurred. If we are truthful, our accounts will match reality. But if someone tries to change the reality, each of them will have a different version. Thus the truth is constant and does not change.

In the Torah there are verses that the Jews did not distort, and there are verses that they did distort. Every verse that relates to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), describing him and stating that he is the final Prophet, they distorted. The verses that do not relate to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) they did not distort. It is as though they mixed the truth with falsehood. What made them introduce falsehood and try to hide the facts? The first motive: to buy with the signs of Allah a small price. Falsehood (al-batil) is that which has no reality, and therefore the gates of falsehood are many, while the gate of truth is one.

Allah, glorified and exalted, wants to inform us that the Jews placed falsehood in the Torah that Allah had not commanded, and concealed the truth about the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). But did they do this by mistake, inadvertence, or forgetfulness? No, they did it knowingly. Consider, for example, the saying of the Almighty to the Jews:

﴿And enter the gate prostrating and say, "Hittah (forgiveness)," and We will forgive you your sins and increase the doers of good.﴾ (Qur'an 2:58)

Hittah means: remove from us, O Lord, our sins. The Jews came and changed Allah's words: instead of saying hittah, they said hintah (wheat). Whoever hears this word may not notice and may think they said what Allah commanded them, though in reality they had distorted it. Likewise, when they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they would say, "Ra'ina" with their tongues, while it was supposed to be "ra'ina" (our shepherd, i.e., attend to us). They said "ra'ina" from ra'una (foolishness). Allah, exalted is His majesty, alerted the believers to His Messenger (ﷺ) not to say as they said. He said:

﴿Do not say "ra'ina," but say "unzurna" (look upon us).﴾

That is, abandon this word entirely. This is mixing the truth with falsehood. So the Jews mixed the truth with falsehood. A person does not mix the truth with falsehood unless he is unable to confront the truth, because inability to face the truth is a weakness that drives him away from it toward falsehood, since the truth burdens its bearer, and a person cannot force himself to the truth.

As for His saying, ﴿and conceal the truth while you know﴾, it means they do this deliberately and not out of ignorance. A person may conceal a truth while not knowing that it is the truth, but if you know it, that is the calamity, because you hide it intentionally and deliberately. Or [the phrase] "while you know" may mean that the Jews, being People of the Book, know what painful punishment will befall them in the Hereafter because of their concealing the truth. They are not ignorant of what will happen in the Hereafter, yet they proceed with their deed knowing it is wrong, so the punishment will be just.

Establishing the prayer is well known. It begins with the takbir (the opening "Allahu Akbar") and ends with the taslim (the closing greeting of peace). Its conditions and elements include standing, bowing (ruku') and prostration (sujud). But the Truth says, ﴿And give zakat and bow with those who bow﴾. This may mean that He wants them to join the assembly of faith that unites them, because their prayer had no bowing in it. Thus He wants them to believe in Muhammad (ﷺ). And they should not think that their faith in Moses (peace be upon him) exempts them from submitting to what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought. They say, "Our religion is sufficient for us." Islam came only for those who have no religion, namely the disbelievers and polytheists. So He says to them: ﴿bow with those who bow﴾.

Almighty and Exalted God wants to draw their attention to the fact that their prayer will not be accepted from them unless it contains bowing. The prayer of the Jews has no bowing in it, though it has prostration. In both cases, Almighty and Exalted God draws their attention to the necessity of believing in the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

When the Almighty and Exalted God said, ﴿and do not trade My verses for a small price﴾, He wants to draw their attention to the fact that the opposite is what is required, and that they should have bought faith and chosen the profitable bargain. That will not happen except if they believe in the final Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ). This is the only path to the pleasure of Almighty and Exalted God.

God, Almighty and Exalted, wants to demolish their arrogance toward the new religion, so He commanded them to pray as the Muslims pray, and to give zakat as the Muslims give zakat. They should not believe that their faith in Moses and the Torah will be accepted from them after the new Messenger has come, the one they were commanded to believe in. Rather, if they were truly believers in them both, their faith in Moses and the Torah would require them to believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), because the Torah commands them to do so. So their not believing in Muhammad (ﷺ) amounts to disbelief in the Torah and a violation of its teachings.

Prayer, as we have said, is the servant's awareness of standing before his Lord. When the servant stands before God, all arrogance within himself must disappear, and humility, submissiveness and lowliness before God enter in its place. The arrogant person is heedless of seeing his Lord, who stands before him. Their not believing in this Prophet, and their standing before God in prayer as it must be performed, as God prescribed it from above the seven heavens, is in fact a refusal to submit to the commands of God.

After that comes zakat, because the believing servant must direct the movement of his life toward beneficial work that benefits him and those who cannot move in life. Almighty and Exalted God, when He demands that we strive on the earth, does not demand that this be only according to our needs; rather He demands that our movement exceed the needs of our lives, so that this movement extends to include the life of one who is unable to move in life. Thus society expands to embrace everyone, rancor and envy are removed from it, and souls are purified.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 44:

﴿Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people while you forget yourselves, and you recite the Scripture? Will you not then reason?﴾ (44)

After God drew the attention of the Jews to the fact that their disbelief in Islam is disbelief in the Torah, because the teachings of the Torah command them to believe in the new Messenger, and they had been given the descriptions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his time in the Torah, and were commanded to believe in him. The Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people while you forget yourselves﴾. The Jews used to announce the coming of a new Messenger and declare that they would believe in him. But when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and was not from their own people, they disbelieved in him, because they wanted the dominance to belong to them, by the new Messenger coming from among them. When he came from the Arabs, they knew that their dominance would vanish and their economic supremacy would end, so they disbelieved in the Messenger and in his message.

We must point out that although these verses were revealed concerning the Jews, their meaning is not restricted to them alone. Rather, they apply to all the People of the Book and to all who do not believe. The lesson lies in the generality of the subject, not in the specificity of the cause.

The statement also applies even to Muslims who "sell the signs of God for a small price." These are the preachers of sedition whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw, whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire. He asked: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "The preachers of sedition. They adorn for every oppressor his oppression, and they make the religion of God serve the desires of people. Whereas the principle is that the desires of people should submit to the religion of God. These are the ones who, under the banner of renewal, seek to give people an argument for escaping the method of God. They justify what occurs and do not reflect on the reckoning of the Hereafter."

The religious scholars who carry the method of God do not have the task of justifying what others do. The method of God can never submit to human desires. Those who do so must repent, return to God, and try to make up for what they have done, because returning to the truth is better than persisting in falsehood.

The saying of the Truthful and Exalted: ﴿Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people while you forget yourselves﴾ gives us another method of the callers to God. The one who enjoins good and forbids evil, and carries the method of God, wants to bring out the one who does not believe from the movement of falsehood to which he is accustomed. Bringing the unbeliever out of the movement of falsehood is a hard matter for his own self, because it is a departure from what he has become used to, a distancing from what he has been familiar with, and an acknowledgment that he was upon falsehood. Therefore he keeps his eyes open toward the one who has shown him the path of faith, to see whether he applies that to himself or not. Does the one who forbids evil practice what he says? If he practices it, he knows that the caller is sincere. If he does not practice it, that becomes an excuse for him to return to the falsehood that controlled the movement of his life.

Religion is a word that is said and a conduct that is performed. When the word is separated from the conduct, the call is lost. God, Glorified and Exalted, says:

﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of God is that you say what you do not do﴾ (Surah As-Saff).

Why? Because whoever sees you doing what you forbid him knows that you are deceptive and dishonest. What you do not accept as conduct for yourself, you cannot preach to others. Therefore we read in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿Indeed, there has been for you in the Messenger of Allah an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in Allah and the Last Day and remembers Allah often﴾ (Surah Al-Ahzab).

The method of religion alone is not sufficient unless it is put into practice. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never commanded his Companions to do anything without being the first to do it. The Muslims took from him the example in word and deed. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), whenever he wished to legislate a matter in Islam, would bring his family and relatives and say to them: "It has occurred to me to command such and such, and by Him in whose hand my soul is, whoever of you opposes it, I will make him an example to the Muslims." By this, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab closed the doors of sedition, because he knew where it comes from.

In the Islamic call, scholars must be a model so that people's affairs may be set right. In all the sciences of this world, example is not required, except in religion. If you are told of a brilliant chemist and told that he drinks wine or does such and such, you say: "What is it to me about his conduct? I take the science of chemistry from him because he is brilliant in it, but his conduct is no concern of mine." And so with all the scholars of the earth, except the scholar of religion. If there is a scholar who shows you the straight path, and you receive the sciences of your religion from him, and then you learn that he drinks wine or steals, do you listen to him? Never. Because he falls from your sight immediately, and you do not love to hear him or sit in his gathering, however great his knowledge. You will say: "Enough of your deceit!" Thus the scholar of religion must be a model. He does not forbid an evil and commit it, nor command a good and fail to carry it out. People's eyes are all open to what he does. Islam spread by the scientific method before it spread by the method of conduct, and the greatest number of Muslims embraced this religion through a behavioral example that led them to it. Those who spread Islam in China were mostly merchants who adopted the morals of Islam, and so they attracted many around them, and they embraced Islam. Therefore the Truthful, Exalted, says:

﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to God and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"﴾ (Surah Fussilat).

The first condition is calling to God, and the second condition is righteous deeds. His saying "Indeed, I am of the Muslims" did not attribute the virtue to himself or his own essence, but attributed the virtue to Islam.

But tell me: what benefit is there in saying that we are Muslims while we act like non-Muslims? So His saying, Exalted: ﴿Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people while you forget yourselves﴾ reminds that the Jews say what they do not do. Had they truly believed in the Torah, they would have believed in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and in Islam, because that is a command in the Torah. But they forgot themselves, so they are the first to oppose the Torah, because they did not follow it. They recite their Book, which commands them to believe in the new faith, and although they are certain of the truthfulness of the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they do not believe. Had they possessed even a particle of reason, they would have believed in what their Book, which they recite, requires of them. But they do not think with their minds; rather they desire exaltation on earth. And the verse, as we have said, does not apply to the Jews alone, but to everyone who follows this conduct.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 45:

﴿And seek help through patience and prayer. And indeed it is difficult, except for the humble (khashi'un).﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted, showed that faith is a model, and after He drew our attention to the fact that the Torah obligates the Jews to believe in Muhammad, peace be upon him, Allah, glorified and exalted, calls for seeking help through patience and prayer. The meaning of seeking help through patience is that arduous events will occur, and that the matter will not be easy but will require effort. Patience (sabr) means compelling the self to bear a difficult matter. Since they had become accustomed to trading the signs of Allah for a small price, for they had reversed the transaction, making Allah's signs a price for the enjoyments of this world, and they had purchased with them their pleasures and desires, and since they had become accustomed to usury (riba) and other means of unlawful gain, they must seek help through patience if they wish to return to the path of faith.

As we have said, the matter is not restricted to the specific cause but is general in its subject, for it is addressed to everyone. Every believer who enters the path of faith needs to seek help through patience, to compel himself to bear the hardship of the path and its obligations, and to restrain himself from the desires that Allah, glorified and exalted, has forbidden.

Some scholars have interpreted patience in the noble verse as fasting. It is as if Allah, the Exalted, commands them to swallow and endure the pain of hunger. The hardship of faith and prayer, as we have said, is humility, submission and abasement before Allah, which puts an end to their arrogance, so that they would believe in a religion that was not revealed to any of the rabbis of the Jews. Allah, the Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And indeed it is difficult, except for the humble.﴾

In His words ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer﴾, the Truth calls for seeking help through two things: patience and prayer. The context of the verse would require that it say "and indeed they [both] are" (wa-innahuma), but the Qur'an says "and indeed it is difficult" (wa-innaha la-kabira). So is the intended reference to one of them only, prayer alone, or patience?

We say: when two matters are joined together such that affairs are not set right except by both of them together, they constitute a single remedy. Consider His words, exalted is He:

﴿They swear to you by Allah in order to please you, but Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they were believers.﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 62)

He said "that they should please Him" and did not say "that they should please them." From this same interpretation we understand: there is no separate right for Allah and a separate right for His Messenger, but Allah and His Messenger meet upon one right. Likewise His words, exalted is He:

﴿And when they see a transaction or a diversion, they break away toward it and leave you standing.﴾ (Surah al-Jumu'ah, 11)

It should have said "toward them both," but trade and diversion are one action: that which preoccupies the believers from worship and remembrance. ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer﴾, because the remedy lies in patience together with prayer. Patience is great, for the self must bear it, and so is prayer, because both take from the movement of a person's life. Patience is required here so that they endure abstaining from the delights of this world and its adornments, and prayer combats arrogance in the self. It is as if the faithful prescription cannot be divided: patience is not complete without prayer, and prayer is not perfected except through patience.

As for His words, exalted is He, ﴿except for the humble (al-khashi'in)﴾: what is the meaning of khushu'? Khushu' is submission to one whom you see as above you without dispute. People differ in worth and gifts, and each one tries to boast of his superiority and talents, saying: "I am better than so-and-so," or "you are better than so-and-so." Thus it is possible for a person to be arrogant because of what he possesses. But a person submits to one who has a need that he can fulfil, for if he is arrogant toward him, he will make his worldly life miserable. For this reason Allah, glorified and exalted, gave people gifts in common and humility in common. Every one of us needs the other: this is humility in common. And every one of us is distinguished by what others cannot attain: these are gifts in common. This is with regard to human beings; as for Allah, glorified and exalted, humility is due to Him who created, bestowed and brought into being.

Humility makes a person call to mind the greatness of the Truth, glorified and exalted, and know his own insignificance before the Truth, glorified and exalted, and the extent of his helplessness before the Creator of this universe. He knows that all that he has can be taken away by Allah, exalted is He, in a moment, for we live in a world of change. Therefore let us submit to the One who does not change, for everything a person obtains is from Allah and not from himself. To those who are deluded by the existence of causes we say: worship and humble yourselves before the Giver and Creator of causes, for causes do not act by themselves. Allah, glorified and exalted, makes the days alternate (duwal), that is, circulated among people. A person boasts of his strength; one stronger than him comes and defeats him. A person boasts of his wealth; this wealth is lost in a moment. Consider His words, exalted is He:

﴿If a wound touches you, a wound has already touched the people like it. And these days We alternate among people, that Allah may know those who believe and take martyrs from among you. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers.﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 140)

Therefore we must understand that the person who exalts himself through causes will come to a time when causes do not give to him. When a person reaches, in his own eyes and in the eyes of people, the rank of perfection, he becomes deluded by himself. We say to him: do not be deceived by the perfections of your self, for if they exist now, they will change tomorrow. Humility belongs only to Allah. Allah, the Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And indeed it is difficult, except for the humble.﴾ Who are the humble (al-khashi'un)? The khashi' is one who obeys Allah, refrains from what is forbidden, is patient with the decrees of destiny, and who knows with certainty within himself that the matter belongs to Allah alone and to no other power. So he humbles himself before the One who created him and created this universe for him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 46:

﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord, and that to Him they will return.﴾

After Allah, the Exalted, has made clear to us that patience and prayer are a heavy burden except upon those whose hearts are humbled before Allah, the one who turns to them with love, faith and desire. He wished to let us know who the humble ones (al-khashi'un) are. So He, majestic is His majesty, said: ﴿Those who think that they will meet their Lord﴾.

What is ẓann (supposition, assumption)? We have previously spoken about the nisba (attribution, a proposition). We said there is a proposition to which I am firmly committed and which reality confirms. When I say, for example: Muhammad is diligent. If there is a person named Muhammad who is diligent, then I have affirmed a fact. This is a proposition held with certainty on condition that I am able to prove the truth of what I say. But if I am certain of the proposition without proof of the truth of what I say, then this is taqlid (blind imitation). Like your six-year-old son who says, for example: There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. But his small mind cannot prove that; rather he is imitating his father or his teachers.

If you are certain of a thing that has no existence in reality, then this is jahl (ignorance). And the ignorant person is worse than the illiterate person, because the ignorant person believes in a claim that has no reality and defends it. As for the illiterate person, he does not know, and when he learns, he believes. Therefore, with regard to the ignorant person, falsehood must first be removed from his heart so that truth may enter. And if the matter is not held with certainty, and existence and non-existence are equal, then that is shakk (doubt). If one of the two sides outweighs the other, that is ẓann (supposition). The Exalted says: ﴿Those who think﴾, and He did not say: Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord. Why did the Exalted not use the word yaqin (certainty) and replace it with ẓann? Because mere supposition that you will meet Allah, the Exalted, is enough to make you adhere to the method. How much more so if you are certain. Mere supposition is sufficient.

If we wish to give an example of this, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, we say: Suppose you are walking on a road, and a person comes and tells you that this road has thieves and highwaymen. Merely this statement makes you not walk on this road unless you are armed and accompanied by one or two people. You do this out of precaution. So mere supposition has moved us to precaution. Thus His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They think that they will meet their Lord﴾, the mere fact that the matter is more probable is sufficient to follow the method of Allah, so that you protect yourself from a great punishment.

Al-Ma'arri says at the end of his life: "The astrologer and the physician both claim / that bodies are not resurrected. I say to you both: / If your saying is true, I am not a loser, / but if my saying is true, the loss is upon you both."

So every one who denies the Hereafter is a loser. The human soul must take precaution for meeting Allah, and must acknowledge that there is a resurrection and work for it.

The Exalted says: ﴿Those who think that they will meet their Lord and that to Him they will return﴾. Returning to Allah, the Exalted, is a matter of certainty. Since you have come into this world created by Allah, you will inevitably return to Him. This day must be guarded against with great caution, and we must watch for it, because it is a tremendous day. The Exalted says:

﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she nursed, and every pregnant one will drop her load, and you will see people as intoxicated, but they are not intoxicated; rather, the punishment of Allah is severe.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj)

And He, majestic is His majesty, says:

﴿Then how will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, on a Day that will make children grey-haired?﴾ (Surah al-Muzzammil)

If this is our state on the Day of Resurrection, how is mere supposition not enough for us to hold fast to the method of Allah? We take precautions against worldly events that are worth nothing compared to the terrors of the Day of Resurrection. Here, the supposition that we will meet Allah, the Exalted, is enough for us to take a thousand precautions on His account.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 47:

﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and that I preferred you over the worlds.﴾ (2:47)

Some people claim that there is a repetition of the seven verses in which the Children of Israel were earlier reminded. We say: no, these verses have not been repeated. They are His, exalted is He, saying:

﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and fulfil My covenant, and I shall fulfil your covenant, and fear Me alone. And believe in what I have sent down, confirming what is with you, and do not be the first to disbelieve in it, and do not exchange My signs for a small price, and fear Me alone. And do not mix the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth while you know. And establish prayer, give zakah, and bow with those who bow. Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people and forget yourselves, while you recite the Book? Then will you not reason? And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is difficult except for the humble, who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that to Him they will return.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah)

All these seven verses address the Children of Israel concerning the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The description of his attributes and his time was present in the Torah, and they are reminded that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a favour to them and to all mankind. And if Allah has preferred the Children of Israel by sending messengers to them, that does not mean that they may deny Allah's favour upon them through the final Messenger. And since the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were mentioned in the Torah, and they were asked to believe in him and support him, their non-belief in him is disbelief in the Torah. Likewise, the Gospel gave glad tidings of Muhammad (ﷺ) and asked them to believe in him; so their non-belief in him is disbelief in the Gospel.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿remember My favour which I bestowed upon you﴾ means: remember that I placed in your Book that which confirms the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ) in his prophethood. The meaning is: remember My favour, that I preferred you over the worlds of those contemporary with you at the time of the revelation of Musa's message, and I made prophets from among you.

Since the Truth, glory be to Him, has preferred them over the worlds, how then does He bestow favour upon them? We say: the bestowal here is for the sake of intense rebuke of them. For Allah, glory be to Him, because of the intensity of their disobedience and disbelief, made from them apes and swine and those who worship the Taghut.

Read His saying:

﴿And you have known those among you who transgressed in the Sabbath, so We said to them: Be apes, despised and driven away.﴾ (2:65)

And His saying:

﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah cursed and upon whom He was angry, and made from them apes and swine, and those who worship the Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way.﴾ (5:60)

So Allah, glory be to Him, shows us how the Children of Israel disbelieved in their prophets and killed them, though Allah had given them much good. But they broke the covenant, and so deserved punishment. They did not make Allah's favour upon them a cause of their sincerity and their faith in Him, glory be to Him, and their affirmation of His method, and their affirmation of the final Messenger who was mentioned to them in the Torah. It was necessary for them to believe in Allah and to remember His many favours which He bestowed upon them.

The Truth wants to draw our attention to the fact that since He has bestowed favour upon them, they should not think that they are not obliged to believe in Muhammad, upon him be peace. Rather, they had to understand that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to correct their Book and to clarify for them the correct path, so it was obligatory upon them to support him. Favour cannot continue together with disbelief in it. And lest we think that Allah, glory be to Him, was harsh with them by making them scattered peoples throughout the whole earth, and then gathering them in one homeland to be killed, read His saying:

﴿And We said after him to the Children of Israel: Dwell in the land.﴾ (17:104)

Which land is that which Allah, glory be to Him, asked the Children of Israel to dwell in? Since the Truth, glory be to Him, said ﴿Dwell in the land﴾, it is the land, all of the land. Would the whole earth be a homeland for the Jews? Of course not. But Allah, glory be to Him, decreed for them that they be dispersed in the earth, so there will be no state for them except when Allah wills to gather them in one place, then He will set over them His believing servants. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book that you will surely cause corruption in the earth twice, and you will surely become arrogant with great arrogance. So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they went through the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled. Then We gave back to you the return over them and provided you with wealth and children and made you more numerous in manpower.﴾ (17:4–6)

This is the first time the Muslims have defeated the Jews. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then We gave back to you the return over them﴾. Since the Truth, glory be to Him, said "over them", it is over the Muslims, because they are the ones who defeated the Jews. And His saying, ﴿and provided you with wealth and children﴾ means that they will prevail over the Muslims, and this is what is happening now, and what we have witnessed and what we are witnessing in the recent period. That is, the reinforcement and strength come to them from outside and not from themselves.

We see that Israel is founded upon bringing Jewish immigrants from other countries, and bringing money and aid from other countries too. That is, all this comes to them as reinforcement from outside. Israel cannot survive except by the immigrants coming to it and by the aid that reaches it. So reinforcement must come from outside. If there is a battle and a commander requests reinforcements, it means he wants men who come to him from outside the battlefield to become a reinforcement and strength for this army. His saying, ﴿and made you more numerous in manpower﴾: *nafir* is the loud voice that draws attention. We see now that Israel controls the media and propaganda in the world, and that its voice is loud and heard. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter came, to disgrace your faces and to enter the mosque as they entered it the first time﴾. The meaning is that al-Masjid al-Aqsa will be lost from the Muslims and will come under Jewish rule, then the Muslims will come and fight them and enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, in the time of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. And Allah says: ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter came, We brought you as a mixed crowd﴾. *Lafif* is the gathering of heterogeneous elements, which repel themselves and those around them. Since Allah, glory be to Him, has decreed that fighting occur between the Jews and the Muslims, in which the Muslims regain al-Masjid al-Aqsa, it was necessary that He gather them in one place, because if they remained as scattered communities in every country of the world, isolated from the societies in which they live, that would have required the Muslims to fight the whole world. But Allah, glory be to Him, will bring them from every country to the place where Bayt al-Maqdis is, so that the Muslims may fight them and enter the mosque as they entered it the first time.

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, reminds the Children of Israel of His favours upon them, and of their disobediences and disbelief, so that no one says that Allah, glory be to Him, was harsh with them, when it was they who disbelieved, and they who disobeyed and spread corruption in the earth, so they deserved this punishment from Allah, glory be to Him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 48:

﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be helped.﴾

The words of the Exalted, ﴿And fear a Day﴾: He reminds them of this Day, which is the Day of Resurrection, on which nothing benefits a person except his deeds. And the Truthful and Exalted asks them to place between themselves and the attributes of His majesty, on that Day, a shield (wiqayah).

Indeed, there is another verse that says:

﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah) [2:123].

This verse occurs twice, and the beginnings of the two verses agree. But the first verse says: ﴿nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it, nor will they be helped﴾, and the second verse: ﴿nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped.﴾ Is this a repetition? We say no. The matter requires understanding. The two verses agree in their opening, in the words of the Exalted: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all﴾.

In the first verse, intercession is mentioned first and he said: "will not be accepted." The second postpones intercession and says: "will not benefit." In the first verse, intercession is placed first, and compensation comes later; in the second verse, compensation is placed first and intercession is postponed. In the first verse: "nor will intercession be accepted from it." In the second verse: "nor will intercession benefit it." The intended meaning of the words of the Exalted, ﴿fear a Day﴾, is the Day of Resurrection, of which He, the Glorious and Exalted, said: ﴿The Day when no soul will avail another soul at all, and the command that Day belongs to Allah﴾ (Surat al-Infitar) [82:19].

And the words of the Exalted, ﴿no soul will avail another soul at all﴾: how many souls are here? They are two: a soul for a soul. There is a first soul and a second soul. What is the first soul? The first soul is the one that recompenses (al-jaziyah). The second soul is the one for which recompense is made. And since there are two souls, the words of the Exalted, ﴿intercession will not be accepted from it﴾: is it from the first soul or the second?

If you consider the meaning, the meaning is that a righteous person will come on the Day of Resurrection and say: "O Lord, I will pay on behalf of so-and-so, or I will free so-and-so, or I will settle the right of so-and-so." The first soul, that is, the recompensing soul, tries to bear on behalf of the soul for which recompense is made.

To bring the meaning closer, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude, let us suppose that a ruler became angry with one of the people and decided to take the most terrible revenge upon him. A friend of this ruler comes and tries to pay on behalf of the one who has incurred anger. By this man's standing with the ruler, he tries to intercede for the third party. In this case, either his intercession is accepted or it is not. If it is not accepted, he will say to the ruler: "I will settle what is owed on his behalf," that is, he will pay a ransom for him, and this will not happen unless the intercession has failed.

So if the matter is on the Day of Resurrection and with Allah, the Exalted, a righteous person comes to intercede with Allah, blessed and exalted, for a person who has transgressed against himself, then this intercessor must be one of the righteous so that his intercession is accepted before the Truth, majestic in His majesty. And recite His words, glorified be He:

﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ (part of 2:255).

And the words of the Exalted:

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not intercede except for one whom He approves, and they are, out of fear of Him, apprehensive.﴾ (Surat al-Anbiya') [21:28].

The righteous person tries to intercede for one who has transgressed against himself, but his intercession is not accepted, nor is compensation taken from him, and no other bargaining is permitted. Thus one speaks of compensation in recompense only when intercession has failed.

Here the pronoun returns to the recompensing soul, that is, the one who comes forward to intercede with Allah. So the Truthful and Exalted says: ﴿nor will intercession be accepted from it﴾, so no other bargaining is accepted from it. And He says, glorified be He: ﴿nor will compensation be taken from it﴾. This is the natural order of events.

In the second verse, Allah, blessed and exalted, speaks of the soul for which recompense is made before it seeks intercession from others and asks Him to intercede for it. It must be that its devices have run out and its means have become unavailable. So it is compelled to turn to another. In this there is an acknowledgment of its helplessness. It says: "O Lord, what shall I do so that I may atone for my sins?" and it is not accepted from it. Then it goes to those from whom intercession is accepted, and their intercession is not accepted. If we wish to give an example of this from the Noble Qur'an, recite the words of the Truthful, blessed and exalted:

﴿If only you could see when the criminals will bow their heads before their Lord, [saying]: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us that we may do righteousness; indeed, we are certain."﴾ (Surat al-Sajdah) [32:12].

These are the ones who seek compensation from Allah, that He may return them to the world so that they may atone for their misdeeds and do righteous work that saves them from punishment, for good deeds erase bad deeds.

So what was the response of the Truthful and Exalted to them? He, majestic in majesty, said:

﴿So taste [the punishment] for your forgetting the meeting of this your Day; indeed, We have forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.﴾ (Surat al-Sajdah) [32:14].

They offered to atone for their misdeeds by asking to return to the world to do righteousness, but Allah, the Exalted, did not accept this offer from them. Recite His words, blessed and exalted: ﴿Do they await except its outcome? The Day its outcome comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth. So are there any intercessors for us to intercede for us, or could we be returned so we might do other than what we used to do?" They have lost their souls, and what they used to invent has strayed from them.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf) [7:53].

These people first sought intercession and it was not accepted, so they entered another stage, which is compensation, and it was not taken, in fulfilment of the words of the Exalted: ﴿nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it.﴾ Thus we see the difference between the two verses. There is no repetition in the Noble Qur'an.

But the verse we are dealing with concerns the recompensing soul, or the one who wishes to intercede for one who has transgressed against himself: ﴿So intercession will not be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it.﴾ And the second verse: ﴿Compensation will not be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it.﴾ That is, the pronoun here refers to the soul for which recompense is made. It first presents compensation: ﴿Return us that we may do righteousness﴾, and it is not accepted from it, so it seeks intercessors and finds none, and intercession does not benefit it.

All the verses we have cited from the Noble Qur'an relate to the Day of Resurrection. However, there is another example in the words of the Exalted:

﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and for them.﴾ (part of 6:151).

And the second verse, in His words, glorified be He:
