﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty; We will provide for them and for you.﴾ (Surat al-Isra') [17:31].

Some people say that ﴿We provide for you﴾ in the first verse and ﴿We provide for them﴾ in the second is a matter of beauty of style. We say no. The words of the Exalted, ﴿do not kill your children out of poverty﴾, mean out of existing poverty. And as long as poverty exists, a person does not want children so that his poverty will increase. Therefore the Truthful and Exalted said to him: ﴿We provide for you and for them.﴾ That is, the coming of children will not increase you in poverty, because you have your provision and they have their provision. That they have their provision does not mean that this will diminish your provision. For the father there is a provision and for the child there is a provision. As for the second verse: ﴿do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾, it is as if poverty does not yet exist, but he fears that if children are granted to him, poverty will come to him. The Truth says to him: ﴿We will provide for them and for you.﴾ That is, their provision will come to them before your provision.

So when you read the words of Allah, glorified be He: ﴿Fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all﴾, repeated in the two verses, do not think this is repetition. For the ending of one is: ﴿nor will intercession be accepted from it, nor will compensation be taken from it﴾, and the other: ﴿nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it.﴾ The pronoun differs in the two cases. In one it returns to the recompensing soul, so it places intercession first and postpones compensation. But for the soul for which recompense is made, compensation comes first and after it intercession.

The Truthful and Exalted says:

﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all.﴾ (part of 31:33).

That is, a person cannot be recompensed on behalf of another person, however close the kinship. A son cannot avail his mother or father, nor can a father avail his children. And recite His words, blessed and exalted:

﴿The Day a man will flee from his brother [34], and his mother and his father [35], and his wife and his children [36], for every man among them, that Day, will be a matter that preoccupies him. [37]﴾ (Surat 'Abasa) [80:34–37].

And the words of the Truthful and Exalted: ﴿nor will compensation be accepted from it﴾ and ﴿nor will compensation be taken from it.﴾ Compensation (al-'adl) is the equivalent. For example, the one who has transgressed against himself says: "O Lord, I did such-and-such and I transgressed against myself, so return me to the world that I may do righteousness." The word "'adl" is sometimes pronounced with a kasra on the ʿayn ('idl), and it is the equivalent of a thing of its own kind: cloth is equalled by cloth like it, gold by gold like it. "'adl" with a fatha on the ʿayn (ʿadl) is the equivalent of a thing but of a different kind. And "'adl" means truth, and justice is only between two opponents. It means fairness and it means truth. Truth is the thing that is fixed and does not change, and it means that you do not favour one side at the expense of another. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, sat with his companions, he would distribute his gaze among all those sitting, so that it could not be said that he was concerned with one of them over the others.

We must know what the soul (nafs) is. When the word "nafs" occurs in the Noble Qur'an, understand that it has a connection with the spirit (ruh). When the spirit joins matter and gives it life, the soul comes into being. Matter alone, before the spirit joins it, is subdued and submissive, glorifying Allah. So do not say "the spiritual life and the material life," for the spirit glorifies and matter glorifies. But when the spirit meets matter and life begins and desires stir, disorder begins. Death results in the spirit leaving the body. The spirit goes to its realm of subjection, and matter goes to its realm of subjection. This allows us to understand the words of the Truth, glorified be He:

﴿On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do.﴾ (Surat al-Nur) [24:24].

Why do they testify? Because they are no longer subjected to the human being to follow his commands in obedience and disobedience. Your senses are subjected to you by the command of Allah in the worldly life, and they glorify and worship. So if they obey you in disobedience, they curse you, because you compelled them to disobedience, and they come on the Day of Resurrection and testify against you. And Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it [7] and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness [8].﴾ (Surat al-Shams) [91:7–8]. The terms "material life" and "spiritual life" have become common among people, because spiritual life differs from the spirit that is in your body. And it applies to the angels, in confirmation of the words of the Exalted:

﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down.﴾ (Surat al-Shu'ara') [26:193].

And the words of He, majestic in majesty:

﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command.﴾ (part of 42:52).

This is the spirit in which there is purity and clarity. And the words of the Exalted: ﴿nor will they be helped.﴾ That is, if Allah, the Exalted, decrees the punishment upon them, no one can help them or halt their punishment. This cannot happen, for the whole matter belongs to Allah.

The Quranic verse is about to be followed by the translation of the commentary. [Translation begins]

After Allah, glory be to Him, warned the Children of Israel of a Day on which no intercession will avail, He wished to remind them of His favour upon them and His blessings.

His saying, Exalted is He, "إذ" (*idh*, "when") is an adverb (*zarf*, an adverbial noun of time or place). We have previously said that the *zarf* is of two kinds, because every event needs a time in which it occurs and a place in which it occurs. When I say to you, "Sit in your place," this *zarf* refers to place. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, addresses His servants, "Remember when you did such-and-such," the meaning is: remember the time when you did such-and-such, a *zarf* of time. And the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when We delivered you﴾, meaning: remember the time when He delivered you from Pharaoh.

The verse we are concerned with occurs three times in the Noble Quran. His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And [remember] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive; and in that was a tremendous trial from your Lord.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:49).

﴿And [remember] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with terrible torment, killing your sons and keeping your women alive.﴾ (Part of verse 141, Surah al-A'raf).

And the saying of His Majesty in Surah Ibrahim:

﴿[Remember] when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive.﴾ (Part of verse 6, Surah Ibrahim).

The difference between the first and second is His saying in the first verse, ﴿slaughtering your sons﴾, and in the second, ﴿killing your sons﴾. Also, ﴿najjaynākum﴾ ("We delivered you") in the first verse, and "anjaynākum" ("We delivered you," with the causative form) in the second. What is the difference between *najjā* and *anjā*? This is the point that deserves pause.

In Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And [remember] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh﴾. The speech here is from Allah. But in Surah Ibrahim we find: ﴿Remember the favour of Allah upon you when He delivered you﴾.

The speech here is the speech of Musa, peace be upon him. What is the difference between the speech of Allah, Exalted is He, and the speech of Musa?

The speech of Musa relates the speech of Allah. When Allah, Exalted is He, bestows favour upon His servants, He bestows upon them the pinnacles of blessing, and He does not bestow favour through small blessings. When Allah, blessed and exalted, bestowed favour upon the Children of Israel, He said: ﴿We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who slaughtered your sons and kept your women alive.﴾ He did not speak of the torment that the people of Musa were suffering at the hands of the people of Pharaoh. They would take them as hired labourers on the land to plough, in the mountains to hew stone, and in the houses to serve. Whoever had no work, they would impose the *jizya* (poll tax) upon him. For this reason the Jews would feign weakness and go about in old clothes, so that Pharaoh would be lax in collecting the *jizya* from them. This is the meaning of the saying of the Truth, Exalted is He:

﴿And humiliation and misery were stamped upon them﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-Baqarah).

That is, they would pretend to be destitute and display humiliation so that they would not pay the *jizya*. But the Truth, Exalted is He, did not bestow favour upon them by saying He had saved them from all this torment. Rather, He bestowed favour upon them with the pinnacle of blessing, which is the deliverance of the sons from slaughter and the keeping alive of the women. For in that state their women and their men would have been humiliated, for the woman would find no man to protect her and would be led astray.

Between the word *najjā* and the word *anjā* there is a great difference. *Najjā* is used at the time the torment descends, while *anjā* means that the torment is kept away from them. The first is for rescue from a torment, and the second means that the torment of Pharaoh is removed from them entirely. So Allah's favour upon them came in two stages: a stage in which He rescued them from a torment that had fallen upon them, and a second stage in which He removed them from the people of Pharaoh, thereby preventing the torment from reaching them.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿afflicted you with terrible torment (*yasūmūnakum sū' al-'adhāb*)﴾. What is *al-sū'*? It is that which comprises many kinds of torment, such as flogging, forced labour, and work in arduous tasks. What is the meaning of *yasūm*? It is said: *sāma fulān khaṣmahu*, meaning he humiliated him, oppressed him, and pressed him hard. The word *sām* is derived from *sām al-māshiya*, meaning he left the livestock to graze freely; hence it is called *sām*, that is, left unattended. When it is said that Pharaoh afflicted the Children of Israel with a terrible torment, the meaning is that their whole life was humiliation and torment.

You find that when Allah, Exalted is He, speaks of the rulers of Egypt from among the Pharaohs, He speaks of ancient Pharaohs who lived in the time of 'Ad and the time of Thamud. Read His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿By the dawn, and ten nights, and the even and the odd, and the night when it passes. Is there in that an oath for one of understanding? Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which was not created in the land, and Thamud who carved out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh of the stakes, who transgressed in the lands and made much corruption therein?﴾ (Surah al-Fajr 89:1–12).

That is, Allah, blessed and exalted, brought the civilisation of the Pharaohs and the ancient Egyptians after 'Ad and Thamud, and this is evidence that the civilisation of 'Ad and Thamud was ancient. Allah, Exalted is He, described 'Ad as "the like of which was not created in the lands," meaning that their civilisation was more advanced than the civilisation of the ancient Egyptians.

Some people may ask how Allah, Exalted is He, describes 'Ad as "the like of which was not created in the lands," when there are today many advanced civilisations.

We say: Allah has revealed to us the civilisation of the Pharaohs and their monuments, but He has hidden from us the civilisation of 'Ad. We have found in the civilisation of the Pharaohs things that we have not yet attained, such as their skill in embalming the dead and preserving bodies, and the building of the pyramids, and other things. Since the civilisation of 'Ad was more advanced than that of the Pharaohs, it must have reached secrets that remain hidden from the world until now. But we know nothing of them, because Allah has not revealed their remains to us.

The Truth, blessed and exalted, spoke of the Pharaohs by the name "Pharaoh," and in the time of Musa He spoke of them as "the people of Pharaoh." But the period between the times of Yusuf and Musa, the king of Egypt was not named Pharaoh; rather he was called *al-'Azīz*, who was the minister, while his superior was the king. The Truth, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me."﴾ (part of verse 50, Surah Yusuf).

So the ruler in the time of Yusuf was called a king and not Pharaoh, whereas the rulers of Egypt before and after Yusuf were titled Pharaoh. This is because before the time of Yusuf, peace be upon him, the Hyksos, who were of the people of the Children of Israel, ruled Egypt. They raided Egypt and defeated the Pharaohs, and ruled Egypt for years until the Pharaohs gathered and drove them out.

What is remarkable is that this history was not known until after the discovery of the Rosetta Stone and the deciphering of the hieroglyphic script. The Hyksos kings were shepherds who had occupied Egypt for a period. For this reason, in the story of Yusuf, peace be upon him, we see the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me."﴾

Thus we learn that the Noble Quran narrated precisely the story of each ruler in his own time. It described the Pharaohs as Pharaohs. Then came the Hyksos, and there was no Pharaoh, but there was a king. And when Musa came, the Pharaohs had returned to rule Egypt. If this matter was not known to us until the beginning of the fifth century (of the Hijri era? the nineteenth century CE), when the French discovered the Rosetta Stone, the Quran had already recorded the correct history of it fourteen centuries ago. This is a miracle added to the great miracles of the Noble Quran concerning a matter that was unknown at the time of the Quran's revelation and has since become known, so that we find the Quran brought it in its correct and sound place.

Having spoken of the difference between *najjaynākum* and *anjaynākum*, we now speak of the difference between ﴿slaughtering your sons (*yadhbaḥūna abnā'akum*)﴾ and ﴿killing your sons (*yaqtulūna abnā'akum*)﴾. Slaughter is not the same as killing. Slaughter necessarily involves the shedding of blood, and slaughter is usually carried out by cutting the arteries at the neck, whereas killing may be by slaughter or by other means, such as strangling or drowning. All of this is killing, and it does not require that blood be spilled.

The Truth, Exalted is He, wishes to draw our attention to the fact that when Pharaoh wished to take revenge on the offspring of the Children of Israel, he took two forms of revenge. One was revenge because they had been allies of the Hyksos and had helped them occupy Egypt. For this reason the Hyksos king had appointed Yusuf as vizier, so it was as if the Hyksos had been loyal to the Children of Israel. When the Pharaohs were victorious, they took revenge on the Children of Israel by every means of vengeance: they killed them and burned their houses over them.

As for the matter of slaughter in His saying, ﴿slaughtering your sons﴾: Pharaoh saw in a dream a fire that blew from the direction of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and burned all the Egyptians, and none was saved from it except the Children of Israel. When Pharaoh asked for the interpretation of the dream, the soothsayers (*kahhān*) told him: a boy will come forth from the offspring of Israel, and the end of your kingdom will be at his hands. So he ordered the midwives (*qawābil*, the *dayāt*) to slaughter every male newborn of the Children of Israel. But the people of Pharaoh, who had grown accustomed to power, said to Pharaoh: the Children of Israel are about to become extinct, and they perform the services for us. So he made the slaughter a yearly practice: in one year they would slaughter, and in the following year they would spare the male infants. Harun was born in a year in which there was no slaughter, so he was saved, and Musa was born in a year in which there was slaughter, and what happened, happened.

Thus the cause of the slaughter was Pharaoh's fear of losing his kingdom, and the slaughter was imposed so that the people of Pharaoh would be certain that the newborn had died. Had they done it by any other means, such as throwing him from the top of a mountain, striking him with a heavy stone, or stabbing him with a sword or spear, he might have survived death. But slaughter makes them certain of his death at once, so that no one escapes.

The Truth says: ﴿They afflict you with terrible torment, slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive.﴾ The word *ibn* (son) applies to a male, but *walad* (child) applies to both male and female. For this reason, the slaughter was only of males, while the women were left alive.

But why did the Truth, blessed and exalted, not say "slaughtering your sons and keeping your daughters alive," instead of "keeping your women alive"? The Truth, Exalted is He, wishes to draw our attention to the fact that the purpose of this was to keep the female element alive, so that the people of Pharaoh could enjoy them. Therefore He did not say "daughters" but said "women." That is, they wanted them for pleasure, as a means of humiliating the Children of Israel. A man's manhood is destroyed only when he sees immorality being committed against his women.

The Truth, Exalted is He, says: ﴿And in that was a tremendous trial from your Lord.﴾ What is the trial? Some people say that the trial is evil. But Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned.﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya 21:35).

So there is a trial through good and a trial through evil. The word "trial" (*balā'*) is not what frightens; what frightens is its outcome, because a trial is an examination or test. If you pass it and succeed, it is good for you; if you do not carry it out, it becomes a burden upon you. The Truth, Exalted is He, says of His friend Ibrahim:

﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them, He said, "Indeed, I will make you an imam for the people."﴾ (part of verse 124, Surah al-Baqarah).

Ibrahim succeeded in the test. The trial came to the Children of Israel from two directions: the trial of evil, through their torment, their subjugation, and the slaughter of their sons; and the trial of good, through their being delivered from the people of Pharaoh. The Children of Israel succeeded in the first trial: they endured the torment and oppression, and it was a tremendous trial. In the second trial they did things that we will address at their proper time.

[Translation ends]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 50:

﴿And when We parted the sea for you and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on.﴾

Again, ﴿And when﴾. Deliverance comes as a means. This means is mentioned in the noble verse. Musa (Moses) and his people set out, and they were six hundred thousand, as the reports say. Pharaoh learned of their departure, so he went out after them at the head of an army of a thousand thousand (one million). When the people of Musa saw them, as the noble Qur'an narrates to us:

﴿They said, "We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us."﴾ (part of verse 129, surah al-A'raf).

And Musa said to them, as came in the Mighty Book:

﴿It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and then He will see how you act.﴾ (part of verse 129, surah al-A'raf).

When the people of Pharaoh came with their enormous number, opposing the people of Musa, and the two groups came in sight of each other, meaning they saw them with their own eyes, the people of Musa said, "Indeed, we are overtaken."

This is a logical statement. Before them was the sea, and behind them Pharaoh and his soldiers. But when events leave the realm of causes for the power of the One who causes, they are not subject to the causes of the cosmos. Therefore Musa said to them with full confidence: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.﴾

In this way the matter was transferred from causes to the Causer, blessed and exalted is He. By the logic of events, Pharaoh and his soldiers would overtake them. But by the logic of the Truth, glorified is He, He will prepare for them a path of salvation.

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, revealed to Musa that he should strike the sea with his staff, and it parted. Thus the law of water, which is its spreading out and fluidity, ceased. The sea split, and each part of it became like a mountain. The water particles held together with one another to form two great mountains, between which was dry land through which the Children of Israel passed.

This is the meaning of His exalted saying: ﴿And when We parted the sea for you﴾. And "parting" (al-farq) is the separation between two things. And if the sea was split, where did the wet mud at the bottom of the sea go? They said that Allah sent a wind that passed over it and dried it. Therefore the Truth, majestic is His majesty, said: ﴿a dry path in the sea﴾.

It is said that when Musa and his people were crossing the sea, they asked about the rest of their brethren. Musa told them that they were on other paths parallel to ours. They said, "We want to be reassured about them." So Musa raised his hand to the sky and said, "O Allah, help me against their bad manners." Then Allah revealed to Musa that he should strike the partitions with his staff, and an opening appeared between each path. So they could see one another.

When Musa, peace be upon him, saw Pharaoh and his army heading toward the sea to cross it, he wanted to strike the sea so that it would return to its flowing state, so that the people of Pharaoh would not reach them. But Allah revealed to him:

﴿And leave the sea as it is (rahwan); indeed, they are an army to be drowned.﴾ (surah al-Dukhan, 24).

That is, leave the sea as it is, until the people of Pharaoh follow you, thinking that they are able to take the same route and walk in it. When the first of them is near your shore and the last of them is at the other shore, I will return the water to its flowing. Thus I will have saved and destroyed with a single cause. So the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to bestow favor upon the Children of Israel by informing them that He saved them from punishment and destroyed their enemy. The gift was two gifts: a gift of granting, by saving them, and a gift of taking away, by destroying their enemy.

As for His exalted saying: ﴿while you were looking on﴾ in this verse, the Truth, majestic is His majesty, did not speak of Pharaoh, but spoke of the drowning of the people of Pharaoh. Why? Because the people of Pharaoh were those who helped him in his tyranny, his oppression, and his transgression. They were the instrument he used to torture the Children of Israel.

And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wanted the Children of Israel to see the people of Pharaoh drowning, so they stood watching them. When you see the downfall of your enemy, the bitterness in your heart departs. ﴿while you were looking on﴾ may carry another meaning: that some of you look at others while you do not yet believe that you have escaped this great trial. At the same time you are reassured as you watch them drowning, with none of them escaping, so that no doubt enters your hearts that some of them might have survived and would return with an army to pursue you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 51:

﴿And [recall] when We appointed for Moses forty nights; then you took the calf [for worship] after him, while you were wrongdoers.﴾

The word of Allah, glorified and exalted be He: ﴿And [recall] when We appointed for Moses forty nights.﴾ This appointment was for giving Moses the method (manhaj). When Allah, glorified and exalted be He, spoke to Moses at the side of the Mount (al-Tur), it was to inform Moses, peace be upon him, that he was a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, and that He had sent him to deliver the Children of Israel from the tyranny of Pharaoh and his torment. And that He would support him with signs and miracles, so that Pharaoh and his people would be convinced that Moses was a messenger from Allah, blessed and exalted be He. This came after Moses had been charged with the message and had gone to Pharaoh, and after what happened with the magicians, then the deliverance of Moses and his people, when Allah, majestic in majesty, split the sea for them. This was at a time when the method (manhaj) had not yet been revealed. Therefore, as soon as Allah, glorified and exalted be He, delivered Moses and his people and drowned Pharaoh, it was necessary that Moses be informed of the method. The appointment comprised forty nights. These forty nights were first determined as thirty, then the Truthful One, glorified and exalted be He, completed them with ten more.

And recite His words, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was complete as forty nights.﴾ (part of verse 142, surah al-A'raf).

When religion speaks of time, it always speaks in nights. The reason is that you cannot determine time precisely by the day: the sun rises and sets and then rises again. If you look at the disk of the sun, you cannot tell at what point of the month we are: at its beginning, its middle, or its end. But when night comes, merely by looking at the moon you can determine the time. If the moon is a crescent, we are at the beginning of the month; if it is full, we are in its middle, and so on.

There are precise measures regarding the moon, and the measurement of time in the custom of people; the ordinary person can tell you the time approximately by nights, and the Bedouin in the desert will tell you, "This moon is so-and-so nights old."

In the logic of religion, we reckon everything by the entry of night. So this is the night of the first of Ramadan, in which we pray the taraweeh; and the night of the 'Eid, in which we do not pray the taraweeh; and the night of the middle of Sha'ban; and the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj.

In all the measures of religion, the night does not follow the day except in one thing, the Day of 'Arafah. So we do not say "the night of 'Arafah," but "the day of 'Arafah." Thus the night is the beginning of time in religion. And time with Allah, its duration is twelve months for each year. The Gregorian year differs from the Hijri year, and the reason is that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, distributed His mercy over His creation. For if religious seasons followed the solar calendar, Ramadan, for example, would come in a fixed month that does not change; people would fast it in summer in certain regions and in winter in certain regions, and it would never vary. Ramadan would always come in summer and heat for some people, and in winter and cold for others.

But because the Hijri year is based on the reckoning of the crescent, this means that all of Allah's breaths of grace in His creation come in every season and every time: you find Ramadan in summer and in winter, and likewise the standing at 'Arafat and likewise all the good religious occasions. For the Hijri year is eleven days shorter than the Gregorian year, and the difference amounts to a year every thirty-three years.

And the Truthful One, glorified and exalted be He, says: ﴿then you took the calf [for worship] after him, while you were wrongdoers.﴾

He wishes to test the Children of Israel and to show us their disbelief in the blessings of Allah. Allah had delivered them from the family of Pharaoh, and they had scarcely crossed the sea when they saw a people worshipping idols, and they said, as the noble Qur'an relates to us:

﴿O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods.﴾ (part of verse 138, al-A'raf).

This happened immediately upon their coming out of the sea safe. Moses, peace be upon him, took the leaders (nuqaba') and went to the appointed time with his Lord, and he left his brother Aaron with the Children of Israel. And the Children of Israel, when they were in Egypt and serving the women of Pharaoh's family, had taken from them some jewelry and gold secretly. Although Pharaoh and his people were rebellious against Allah, blessed and exalted be He, this does not justify stealing their women's jewelry. We do not repay one who disobeys Allah regarding us by disobeying Allah regarding him, becoming equal to them in sin; rather, we repay one who disobeys Allah regarding us by obeying Allah regarding him.

When Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, was informed that a man had cursed him, he sent him a letter in which he said: "O my brother, do not be extravagant in reviling us, and leave room for reconciliation, for we do not repay one who disobeys Allah regarding us with anything more than obeying Allah regarding him."

The Children of Israel had stolen some of the jewelry of Pharaoh's women, and Allah made it a trial to mislead them, and Satan made it appealing to them to fashion from it a calf that they would worship. It was made for them by Musa al-Samiri, whom Jibril had raised. He took the jewelry and melted it to shape it into a calf that had a lowing sound, and said to them, "This is your god and the god of Moses." Do you know why Allah, glorified and exalted be He, tested them with the calf?

Because the gold from which the calf was made had a haram origin, and what is haram never produces any good at all. We must take a lesson from this incident: that haram turns against its owner as evil and ruin. If your food is haram, it enters into the formation of your cells, and haram settles in your body. When haram enters the body, your conduct inclines toward what is haram; haram troubles the body and drives it toward sins.

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Allah is good and accepts only what is good, and Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, so He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds﴾ [23:51], and He said: ﴿O you who have believed, eat of the good things We have provided you and be grateful to Allah, if it is Him you worship﴾ [2:172]." Then he mentioned the man who travels far, disheveled and dusty, who raises his hands to the sky, saying, "O Lord, O Lord," while his food is haram, his drink is haram, his clothing is haram, and he is nourished with haram; so how could his supplication be answered?(1)

The same thing happened to the Children of Israel: they stole the gold of Pharaoh's family, and it turned against them as wrongdoing. Allah said of them: ﴿Then you took the calf [for worship] after him, while you were wrongdoers.﴾

Allah's promise to Moses, as the scholars say, was thirty nights; completing the thirty nights would bring him what was promised. The word wa'd (promise) is the announcement of something pleasing, and wa'id (threat) is the announcement of something evil. If you hear a promise, know that what follows will be good; and if you hear a threat, know that what follows is evil, except for one verse, His words, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿The Fire Allah has promised those who disbelieve.﴾ (part of verse 72, surah al-Hajj).

Is the promise here good, or has the meaning changed? We say: if the Fire is the one promised, then it is evil; but if the Fire is the one who promises and the disbelievers are those promised to it, then it is good for the Fire, because the Fire rejoices in the torment of the disbelieving servants of Allah. We know this joy from His words:

﴿The Day We will say to Hell, "Are you full?" and it will say, "Are there any more?"﴾ (Qaf, 50:30). A person seeks more only of something he loves. The Fire, like everything else, is subjected to Allah and glorifies Him, and it dislikes the disobedient; but it is not commanded to burn them in this world. In the Hereafter, however, it will be joyful while burning the disobedient and the disbelievers.

(1) Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 2, verse 52:

﴿Then We pardoned you after that, that perhaps you might give thanks.﴾ (56)

God, glorified and exalted is He, bestows His favour upon the Children of Israel once again, even though they had committed a sin of the gravest kind. Yet God pardoned them, because He wishes to preserve the element of good among people. He wants His creation to know that He is a Lord who is Merciful. He opens the doors of repentance one after another, so that the cells of evil in the human soul may be erased.

When a person commits a sin, he slips away from the matter of faith. Had repentance and pardon not been prescribed by God, people would have multiplied their disobedience and drowned in it, because if there were no repentance, and every single sin led to the Fire, and punishment were to reach the human being, then he would persist in disobedience. This is not what God, glorified and exalted is He, wishes for His servants.

In the noble hadith:

"Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His servant than any one of you who, having lost his camel carrying his provisions, food and drink, in a barren desert, despairs of finding it, then comes upon it standing beside him." (1)

The meaning of the hadith: a man has a camel carrying his wealth, his food, his drink, and everything he owns. This camel wanders off into a barren desert. Its owner searches for it and does not find it. He has lost it, and with it all the means of his life. Then he looks and sees it in front of him. How will his joy be? Obviously, without limit. This is how God, may He be exalted, rejoices at the repentance of His believing servant, and even more than that.

When God, blessed and exalted, opens the door of repentance, He wants the movement of the world to continue. Suppose a soul was heedless once, or its desire led it once to disobedience, or Satan whispered to it as happened with Adam and Eve. Were there no repentance and forgiveness, all of these would have turned into devils. Indeed, acts of goodness come from those who have been excessive against themselves; these people do much good and act righteously in abundance, in confirmation of the words of God, the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ (Surah Hud, part of verse 114)

And His saying, majestic is His majesty:

﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them growth through it.﴾ (Surah At-Tawbah, part of verse 103)

So God, glorified and exalted is He, accepting the repentance of the Children of Israel, although they had disbelieved by worshipping the calf, is because God wishes to preserve good in His creation. The Children of Israel worshipped the calf before the method was revealed to them, which is the Torah. But after the method and the Torah were revealed to them, did they repent and reform, or did they persist in their disobedience and obstinacy?

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 53:

﴿And when We gave Moses the Book and the Criterion, that you might be guided.﴾

Almighty and Exalted God here reminds the Children of Israel that, after He had shown them many miracles, rescued them from the people of Pharaoh, and parted the sea for them, they should have believed with a true faith that was free of any kind of hesitation. This is because they saw and witnessed, and their witness was ʿayn al-yaqīn (certainty of sight). That is, they saw with their own eyes what happened.

But did this witnessing manage to erase hypocrisy and disbelief from their hearts? No. They remained obstinate throughout their history. They did not accept anything easily.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) warns his community not to be like the Children of Israel, a people who made things hard for themselves, so that Allah made them hard for them. This applied to the story of the cow, which they were ordered to slaughter so that they could identify the killer in a murder that nearly stirred up wars among them. They began asking what it was and what its color was, and so on, which we will discuss when we come to the noble verses concerning this event. Had they slaughtered any cow, it would have sufficed them, because it is enough that Almighty and Exalted God tell them, "Slaughter a cow," and they would slaughter any cow. Lack of specification is easier for them. But they asked and kept on asking, so He made it hard for them by specifying a particular cow in itself. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave me alone with what I leave you, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. So when I command you to do something, do of it what you are able, and when I forbid you from something, leave it." (1)

As for Almighty and Exalted God's words, ﴿And when We gave Moses the Book and the Criterion﴾, it is as if the giving of the Book and the Criterion to Moses was a blessing that his people must remember, and that they should receive God's method as a blessing. A person should not take the divine obligation from the angle of what restricts his movement or what it withholds from him. That is because when God forbids you theft, He forbids all people from stealing from you. So if He takes from you the freedom to steal, He has taken from all people the freedom to steal your property. This is a great protection for you.

What is the Book, and what is the Criterion? The Book is the Torah; it is what makes the method clear. The Criterion refers to the things by which God distinguishes truth from falsehood. The word "Criterion" is applied once to the Torah, because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and it is also applied to everything that distinguishes between truth and falsehood. For this reason the Day of Badr was called the Day of the Criterion, because it separated truth from falsehood. Thus God's method and His Book show us where the truth is and where falsehood is, and distinguish between them.

(1) Narrated by Muslim.

Al-Sha'rawi says: Allah, blessed and exalted, reminds the Children of Israel of the story of worshipping the calf. It was a grave deviation from the way of Allah, and a violation of the highest principle, the worship of Allah alone. What happened was that Musa (peace be upon him) went to the appointed meeting with Allah, taking with him the chieftains of his people, to receive the method and the Torah. Allah, glorified be He, informed him that his people had gone astray and worshipped other than Allah. Musa returned in the height of anger, seized his brother Harun by his head and beard, dragging him, and said to him: ﴿I was only the one who had left you in charge of them, so that they would not go astray.﴾ Harun (peace be upon him) said: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize my beard or my head. I feared that you would say, "You have caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word."﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha).

The trial of the calf-worship was caused by al-Samiri. Al-Samiri, whose name was Musa al-Samiri, was born by his mother in the desert, and when she died, Jibril (Gabriel) took charge of him and raised him. Jibril (peace be upon him) would come to him on a horse, bringing him what he needed of food and drink. Musa al-Samiri would see Jibril's horse, and whenever it walked on the earth, dust would fall from it, and the earth would become green and vegetation would grow after that dust. He became certain that there was a secret in the horse's hoof. So he took a handful of dust from the horse's trace and placed it into the calf made of gold, and it began to make a lowing sound as though it were alive.

Do not be surprised that the one behind the trial finds assistance from the means, so that he may tempt people with it, because Allah, blessed and exalted, wishes to test His creation. The one who carries the call to truth must be specially prepared by Allah, glorified be He. Before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) moved to Madinah, he and the Muslims faced many afflictions. The event of the Isra' and Mi'raj came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after the means of this world had abandoned him in Makkah, and he went to al-Ta'if to call its people, and they set their slaves and foolish ones against him, and they pelted him with stones until his blessed feet bled. He raised his hands to the sky with the well-known supplication: "O Allah, to You I complain of the weakness of my strength, the scarcity of my resources, and my humiliation before the people."

This was not for the Messenger alone, but for the believers with him as well, to the point that Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, the pampered youth of Quraysh, who had clothing, wealth and slaves beyond counting, was seen after his acceptance of Islam wearing a donkey's hide, so that Allah, the Truth, might test in the heart of Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr his love for faith: whether he loved this world more or loved Allah and His Messenger more. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say to the Companions: "Look at what faith has done to your companion."

Allah, blessed and exalted, must purify and test those who will carry His call to the whole world. They must be patient in the face of trials, strong before the opponents of the call, and ready to bear burdens and pains, because this is the proof of sincerity in faith.

Therefore you find that every call to error brings benefit to its owners. The call of communism benefits the members of the central committee, while the people wear cheap clothes and live in cramped houses. Those gentlemen who spend without accounting are the members of the central committee. This is the call of falsehood. The opposite is the call of truth: the owner of the call is the first to pay and the first to sacrifice. He does not benefit from what he says; rather, on the contrary, he sacrifices for what he says. So falsehood brings gain to the owner of its call. If you see a call that showers its followers with gifts, know that it is a call of falsehood. Had it not given generously, no one would have followed it.

The noble verse we are discussing is a rebuke from Musa (peace be upon him) to his people, whom Allah had saved from the people of Pharaoh and whose enemy He had destroyed, yet they took the calf as a god. When did this happen? At the time when Musa had gone to the appointed meeting with his Lord to bring the method. They took the calf as a god. Did they wrong Allah, glorified be He, or did they wrong themselves? They wronged themselves, because they brought themselves to the place of destruction without gaining anything.

The wrongdoer is of various kinds: a wrongdoer in something above, that is, at the summit, and a wrongdoer in what the summit requires. The wrongdoing at the summit is the one who makes a partner with Allah, and therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong.﴾ (Part of verse 13, Surah Luqman).

The relationship between shirk (association of partners with Allah) and wrongdoing is that you have brought as a partner for the One who created and provides one who creates nothing and provides nothing. And how can that which you have made a god be worshipped? Worship is the obedience of the worshipper to the one worshipped. So what did this calf that you worshipped besides Allah tell you to do? Therefore you are wrongdoers with the wrong of the summit. The other wrong is wrongdoing in what the summit has legislated, by taking people's rights and violating them. In both cases the wrong does not fall upon Allah, glorified be He, but upon yourself. Why? Because you believed in Allah or did not believe. He will remain Allah, the Strong, the Capable, the Mighty. Your faith or your lack of faith will not diminish anything of His dominion. Then you come on the Day of Resurrection and He punishes you. So it is as if the wrong fell upon you. If you take people's rights, you may enjoy them for days, weeks or years, then you die and leave them and receive the punishment. So it is as if you wronged yourself and gained nothing.

Therefore the Truth, majestic in His majesty, says: ﴿They did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (Part of verse 57, Surah al-Baqarah).

The wronging of people returns upon themselves, because none of Allah's creation can wrong Allah, glorified be He. His words ﴿So turn in repentance to your Creator﴾: the Truth, blessed and exalted, said in the previous verse ﴿We pardoned you﴾, and then this verse says ﴿so turn in repentance to your Creator﴾, because repentance (tawbah) is the root of forgiveness. You repent of your sin, resolve never to return to its like, and Allah accepts your repentance and pardons you. It was possible that Allah would seize them for this sin and destroy them as He did with the earlier nations. But since Allah legislated for them to repent, this is grace from Allah and pardon. Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿So kill yourselves﴾. Look at the precision of the obligation and the precision of the reason in His words, the Exalted: ﴿So turn in repentance to your Creator and kill yourselves.﴾ Allah, glorified be He, says to them: I have not overcome you with a creator who created you or took you from Him; rather, I am the One who created you. But the Creator (al-Khaliq) is one thing and the Maker (al-Bari') is another. Khalq means bringing a thing into existence from non-existence, while bara' means shaping it into a straight form and in the best proportion. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿He who created and proportioned, and He who determined and guided.﴾ (Surah al-A'la).

From here we know that creation is one thing and proportioning is another. Bari'ukum is derived from bara' al-sahm (the straightening of an arrow), and straightening an arrow requires precision and skill.

His words, exalted be He, ﴿So kill yourselves﴾: because the One who created you and proportioned you, you disbelieved in Him and worshipped other than Him. So it is as if, in this state, you must return to Him the life He gave you. When the command of Allah, blessed and exalted, came down, Musa had the Children of Israel stand in rows, and he told them that whoever had not worshipped the calf would kill whoever had worshipped it. But when they stood to carry it out, Allah had mercy on them by sending a cloud of mist to cover them so that they would not find hardship in carrying out the killing. It is said that they killed seventy thousand of themselves.

When this happened, Musa and Harun cried out to their Lord, and they said: "Weep, weep," meaning: cry, perhaps Allah will pardon them. They stood weeping before the Wailing Wall, and Allah had mercy on them.

His words, exalted be He, ﴿So kill yourselves﴾: because these souls, with their desires and their disobedience, were what made them rebel against the method.

Indeed, the legislation here of killing is the expiation (kaffarah) of the sin. Because the one who worshipped the calf and took another god besides Allah, by offering himself to be killed, this is a confession from him that the calf he worshipped was false. And by this he returns his soul, which had rebelled against the way of Allah, to correct worship. This is the harshest kind of expiation: that he kill himself as proof of his faith that there is no god but Allah, and as remorse for what he did and a declaration of it. So killing here is a sincere testimony of return to faith.

His words, exalted be He, ﴿That is better for you with your Creator﴾: meaning this repentance is the most sincere kind of repentance, and it is better, because it saves you from the punishment of the Hereafter. His words, glorified be He, ﴿Then He turned to you in forgiveness. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾: the first repentance is that He legislated expiation for you, and the second repentance is when He accepts your repentance and pardons you with an everlasting pardon.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 55:

﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will not believe you until we see Allah openly," so the thunderbolt seized you while you were looking on.﴾ (55)

After Allah had accepted the repentance of the people of Musa following their worship of the calf, they returned once again to their obstinacy and their materialism. They wanted a material god, a god they could see. But from the greatness of God is that He is unseen, that eyesight cannot perceive Him. Consider His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision, and He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 103)

That Allah, glorified and exalted, is beyond human perception is part of His greatness, majestic is He. But the Jews, who believe only in the material and the perceptible, have minds and hearts that cannot encompass that Allah, glorified and exalted, is above matter and above sight. This materialistic outlook is a foolish outlook. Allah, blessed and exalted, has also drawn our attention to the question of seeing Him openly in this world, through His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And within yourselves. Will you not then see?﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 21)

That is, Allah, majestic is He, has placed the supreme proof of the existence of God, whom eyesight cannot perceive, in the soul of each of us. This is the soul present within the body. Man is created from matter into which the soul was breathed, so life, movement and sensation came to stir within it. Therefore, all the life in your body does not return to the matter you see before you, but to the soul, which you cannot perceive except through its effects. When the soul departs, life goes, and the body becomes a corpse.

If this soul within your body, which gives you life, cannot be perceived by you although it exists within you, how then do you wish to perceive Allah, glorified and exalted? You should first have asked Allah to make you perceive the soul within your body. But Allah, glorified and exalted, said that it is of the command of Allah. Consider His saying, majestic is He:

﴿They ask you about the soul. Say, "The soul is of the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little."﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 85)

If this soul is a creation of Allah which you cannot perceive, how then do you hope to see its Creator? Observe the precision of the Qur'anic expression in His saying, glorified is He: "حتى نرى الله جهرة" (until we see Allah openly). The word "نرى" (see) is used to mean knowledge, for example:

﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾ (part of verse 43, Surah al-Furqan)

That is, "have you known". But the word "جهرة" (openly) came to negate mere knowledge and to demand a vision that is manifest and clear, perceived by their senses. This is evidence that they adhere to materialism, which is the foundation of their lives. We say to these people that your question is marked by stupidity. For you, when you ask to see Allah openly, and it is supposed that Allah, blessed and exalted, has a concept in your minds, you want to see Him so that you may compare the concept with the existing reality. That would be the case if the question were, in the first place, whether you know that God exists or does not exist. What encouraged them to say what they said was the request of Musa, peace be upon him, that Allah, glorified and exalted, let him see Him. Consider His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿He said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You." He said, "You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it should remain in its place, then you will see Me." But when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Musa fell unconscious.﴾ (part of verse 143, Surah al-A'raf)

We must know that the question of seeing Allah in this world is one that is perceptible, and that there is no way to it while a human being is in his human body, because this body has laws governing its perceptions. But on the Day of Resurrection we will be created with laws that differ. In this world, the waste of food must leave our bodies; in the Hereafter there is no waste. In this world time governs us; in the Hereafter there is no time, for a person remains young forever. So there is a change.

The measures there are not the measures of this world. In this world, by your preparation and your body, you cannot see Allah. In the Hereafter, your preparation and your body will permit Allah, glorified and exalted, to manifest Himself to you, and this is the supreme bliss of the Hereafter. You now live among the traces of Allah's power, and in the Hereafter you will live the life of one who looks upon Allah, blessed and exalted. On this the Truth, majestic is He, says:

﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord.﴾ (Surah al-Qiyamah, 22-23)

Man in this world has invented instruments that enable him to see what he cannot see with his naked eye. He sees minute things through the microscope and distant things through the telescope. If the work of man in this world has enabled him to see what he could not see, then consider the power of Allah in the Hereafter. And if a person's eyesight weakens, the doctor asks him to use glasses; but if he goes to a more skilled doctor, the doctor performs a surgical operation on his eye, by which he dispenses with glasses and sees without them. So what then of the preparation of the Truth for creation, and of the power of Allah, which has no limits, to re-create the eye such that it can enjoy His noble Countenance?

Allah, blessed and exalted, settled the matter with Musa, peace be upon him, by showing him human incapacity, for the mountain, with its strength and might, could not bear the light of Allah, so He made it crumble. It is as if Allah wished to make Musa understand that Allah, blessed and exalted, withheld from him the vision out of mercy, for if this happened to the mountain, what could have happened to Musa? If Musa fell unconscious at the sight of the One who manifested Himself to him, how then would it be if he saw the Manifest One?

When a person is unable to perceive something in this world because he is created with these capacities, his inability to perceive is itself a perception, for the inability to perceive is part of the greatness of Allah, glorified and exalted. When the people of Musa asked him to let them see Allah openly, the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on. When they dared such audacity against Allah, the thunderbolt seized them. The thunderbolt is either a fire that comes or a punishment that descends. What matters is that it is a calamity that engulfs them all. And the thunderbolt struck Musa as well.

Verse 56:

﴿Then We revived you after your death, that you might be grateful.﴾

Al-Sha'rawi continues the account of those who said, ﴿Show us Allah openly,﴾ and so the thunderbolt ﴿seized them﴾. Moses, peace be upon him, was also struck by the thunderbolt, when he asked to look upon Allah. But there is a difference between the two cases. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And Moses fell down in a swoon. Then, when he recovered, he said, "Glory be to You! I have turned to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers."﴾ (part of verse 143, Surat al-A'raf).

However, the matter was not the same with the people of Moses. With Moses, Allah said, ﴿when he recovered (fa-lamma afaqa)﴾, meaning that the thunderbolt struck him with a kind of fainting. But with the people of Moses, He said, ﴿Then We revived you after your death,﴾ as if the people of Moses had actually died from the thunderbolt. Moses recovered on his own, whereas those among his people who were struck by the thunderbolt died and were then raised up, ﴿that perhaps they would be grateful.﴾

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 57:

﴿And We shaded you with the clouds, and sent down upon you the manna and the quails. Eat of the good things with which We have provided you. They did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.﴾

God, glory be to Him, wishes to bestow His favours upon the Children of Israel, with His blessings and His miracles. He shows us that, despite all these blessings, the Children of Israel persisted in their obstinacy and their stubborn insistence. After the Children of Israel asked to see God openly, the thunderbolt struck them down. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, raised them up again, so that they might give thanks.

The Truth, majestic is His majesty, mentions to us other blessings of His upon the Children of Israel. He said: "Remember when you were in the desert, where there was no shade to shelter you from the harsh heat of the sun, and no place to take shelter, for there is no water and no vegetation in the desert. So God, glory be to Him, shaded you with the clouds," meaning that the clouds came as a mercy from God, glory be to Him. Then after that, the manna and the quails came.

The manna is red drops that gather on the leaves of trees between dawn and sunrise. It is still found today in Iraq. In the early morning, people bring white sheets and spread them beneath the trees, then shake the trees vigorously so that the drops on the leaves fall onto the sheets. They gather them, and it becomes one of the most delicious kinds of sweets, with the taste of cream and the sweetness of bee honey. It is a pleasant, nourishing sweet that is easy to digest and quickly absorbed by the body. God, glory be to Him, made it for them the fuel of their lives, providing them with energy while they were in the desert. As for the quails, they are birds from the sky, and it is said that they are the quail (samman). They come to them in great flocks, whose source they do not know, and they remain on the ground until they catch them, slaughter them and eat them.

So Allah, blessed and exalted, has provided them with this good sustenance: a cloud that protects them from the heat of the sun, a source that gives them the fuel of movement, and quails as food for them. All of this comes to them from the sky without any effort on their part. But because of their lack of faith in the unseen, they wanted material things, and they feared that the manna and the quails would one day cease for them, so what would they do?

Had they truly been believers, they would have said: "The One who provided us with the manna and the quails will not abandon us." But the Truth, majestic is His majesty, sends them their food daily from the sky, and instead of meeting this blessing with gratitude, they met it with ingratitude.

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves﴾, the Truth, glory be to Him, speaks for the third time about the wrongdoing of the people of Moses. In the first instance He said ﴿and you are wrongdoers﴾. In the second verse He said: ﴿you have wronged yourselves﴾. And in this verse He said: ﴿They did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves﴾.

I have already said that no one can wrong God, because God, glory be to Him, remains in His power, might and greatness. It does not diminish if all the people of the earth disbelieve, and it does not increase if all the people of the earth believe. The power of God remains and His word stands. But it is we who wrong ourselves, by casting ourselves into destruction and into a punishment from which there is no escape, without having given it anything in return.

Indeed, the world, as we have said, is a realm of change. The blessing you are in is leaving you. Either you leave it through death, or it leaves you and departs from you. You go out of this world carrying only your deeds. Everything passed away, and your sins remain, which you carry into the Hereafter. Therefore, whoever disobeys God and rebels against His religion has wronged himself, because he has led it to everlasting punishment out of desire for influence or wealth that vanished after a short time and did not last. It is as though he wronged it by depriving it of eternal bliss and giving it a brief, hasty desire.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 58:

﴿And [recall] when We said: Enter this town and eat from it wherever you wish, in ease, and enter the gate prostrating, and say, "Hitta" [remission], and We will forgive you your sins and increase [reward] for the good-doers.﴾

From this noble verse we learn that the Children of Israel rejected the provision of heaven, the manna and the quails, even though it was a provision of the highest rank: high in quality, for it was sweet, pure, and delicious food sent down to them directly from the sky; and high in abundance, for it came to them without labour or toil, in enormous quantities sufficient for them with more to spare. They asked Moses for the food of the earth that they plant with their own hands and see before them every day, for they feared that one day they would wake up and find no manna and quails. The Exalted Lord completes the story for us in a later verse:

﴿And when you said, "O Moses, we will not endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its greens, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions." He said, "Would you exchange what is better for what is less? Go down to Egypt, for you will have what you asked."﴾ (part of verse 61, surah al-Baqarah)

So Allah, exalted is He, continues to remind the Children of Israel of His blessings and of how they met them with ingratitude. He reminds them of their deliverance from the torment of the people of Pharaoh; He reminds them of the sea that split open for them so that they walked through it, then the water closed back over the people of Pharaoh and drowned them; and He reminds them how they worshipped the calf afterwards. It was possible that Allah would destroy them for their sins, as He destroyed the earlier nations, but He pardoned them. Then He reminds them of His favour upon them in giving them the Book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood; and He reminds them that they asked to see Allah openly, so they were struck down and died, then Allah resurrected them. And He reminds them how He shaded them with clouds from the scorching heat of the sun, and provided for them with manna and quails. Then He reminds them that they asked for the food of the earth, and He responded to them.

In this verse, the Blessed and Exalted Lord says: ﴿فكلوا منها حيث شئتم رغدا﴾ ("eat from it wherever you wish, in ease"). In another verse He says: ﴿رغدا حيث شئتم﴾ ("in ease, wherever you wish"). The difference in meaning is that His saying ﴿حيث شئتم رغداً﴾ indicates that there are many kinds of food. Whereas "ورغداً حيث شئتم" implies there is one single kind and the people are hungry, so they eagerly approach the food. When the Majestic Lord says "eat in ease", the addressee here is of two types: a person who is not hungry, for whom many varieties of food are prepared to tempt him to eat, so in this case ﴿حيث شئتم﴾ is placed first, and it is said: "eat from it wherever you wish, in ease." But if the person is hungry, he is content with any food, so it is said: "in ease, wherever you wish."

The matter in the noble Qur'an is not a matter of advancing or delaying words, but the meaning does not hold without this change.

His saying ﴿ادخلوا هذه القرية﴾ ("enter this town"): the town here is Bayt al-Maqdis, or Palestine, or Jordan. The Blessed and Exalted Lord says: ﴿وادخلوا الباب سجدا وقولوا حطة نغفر لكم خطاياكم وسنزيد المحسنين﴾.

When the Majestic Lord addressed them, He made clear to us that they were not in a state of severe hunger such that they would eat anything, so He said: ﴿فكلوا منها حيث شئتم رغداً﴾, meaning you will find in it many varieties of food that will tempt you to eat even if you were not hungry. His saying ﴿وادخلوا الباب سجداً﴾ means: enter the gate while you are in utmost humility. ﴿وقولوا حطة﴾ means: remove from us our sins, O Lord. However, even in the command they altered its content and distorted the truth with falsehood, and this is a characteristic of theirs. Therefore they entered the gate not prostrating; they entered it crawling on their buttocks, even though what Allah commanded them was less burdensome than what they did. It is as if the disobedience did not come from Allah's commands being hard, but from a desire to oppose the Creator's command; instead of saying "hitta", meaning "remove our sins from us, O Lord," they said "hintah", and "hintah" is wheat, so that they bent the word to their purposes. It is as if the matter was not an inability to obey, but a desire to disobey.

Although the Blessed and Exalted Lord promised them forgiveness, mercy, and increase for the good-doers, they disobeyed and rebelled. His saying ﴿وسنزيد المحسنين﴾ comes in the noble verse:

﴿لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾ ("For those who did good is the best reward and more" — part of verse 26, surah Yunus).

That is, they will have a reward like what they did, multiplied manifold. And what is the increase? That they will see Allah on the Day of Resurrection. This is the increase that has no parallel in this world.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 2, verse 59:

﴿So those who did wrong substituted a word other than that which had been said to them, so We sent upon those who did wrong a punishment from the sky for what they were defiantly disobeying.﴾

Al-Sha'rawi: In this noble verse, God Almighty explains to us how the Jews were a people of disobedience despite God's blessings upon them. Had God Almighty imposed on them a duty they could not bear, because it was burdensome for them, they would have had an excuse. But God, blessed and exalted, does not impose any duty except that which is within a human being's capacity or less than it. So He, majestic in His majesty, says:

﴿God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] what it has earned.﴾ (part of verse 286 of Surah al-Baqarah)

God, blessed and exalted, did not command the Children of Israel to enter this town, which is said to be Jerusalem, and it is said to be a town in Palestine or a town in Jordan, except in response to their own request. It was they who asked Moses to ask God to let them enter a valley with crops, so that they could eat from what the land produces and be at ease about their food, because they feared that a day would come when manna and quails would no longer descend upon them from the sky. When God answered their request and said to them, "Enter the gate prostrating, and say, 'Ḥiṭṭah' (a plea for the removal of our sins)," the Children of Israel altered the word: instead of saying ḥiṭṭah, they said ḥinṭah (wheat). They also altered the manner of entering: instead of entering prostrating, they entered on their backs, crawling. This was out of desire for opposition. So God sent upon them a punishment from the sky for what they were defiantly disobeying, that is, they were turning away from God's way and not applying it, out of desire for opposition and persistence in obstinacy.

The Qur'anic verse is at the head of this passage: ﴿And when Moses prayed for water for his people, We said: Strike the rock with your staff, and there gushed forth from it twelve springs. Every people knew its drinking place. Eat and drink of God's provision, and do not go about the earth causing corruption.﴾ (2:60)

Its meaning: remember when Moses sought water for his people. This appears, as we have explained, in several verses, such as His words:

﴿And when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who inflicted on you the worst torment﴾ (7:141).

And His words:

﴿And when We appointed for Moses forty nights﴾ (2:51).

And His words, majestic is He:

﴿And when you said: O Moses, we will not believe you until we see God plainly﴾ (2:55).

We have said that all of these are blessings with which God bestowed favour upon the Children of Israel, and He, glorified and exalted, reminds them of them, either directly or through the tongue of Moses, peace be upon him. God wishes to remind the Children of Israel that when they wandered in the desert, He shaded them with clouds, and He gave them drink when they asked for water. The scarcity of water among the Children of Israel had reached such a point that they could not find anything to drink. A person begins to dry up when there is no water to irrigate his crops; then the water decreases and he cannot find water for his livestock; then it decreases further and he cannot find anything to drink. This is the peak of drought or barrenness.

Moses, peace be upon him, asked God, blessed and exalted, for water. One does not ask God for water unless the means have run out and the last drop of water has come to an end. Water is the source of life, which God sends down from the sky, pure, clean, and fit for drinking, irrigation, cultivation, and watering livestock.

God, glorified and exalted, made three quarters of the earth water and one quarter dry land, so that the surface area of water exposed to evaporation by the sun's rays is very large, and evaporation occurs easily. If you bring a cup of water and leave it in a closed room for two or three days, then return and find it less by a qirat or two qirats, but if you take the water in the cup and pour it onto the floor of the room, it dries before you leave the room. Why? Because the surface area of the water here is large, so evaporation takes place quickly and requires no time. This is the same principle that operates in the universe. God, blessed and exalted, made the water surface three quarters of the earth so that evaporation takes place quickly and easily, so clouds form and rain falls. We take from it what we need, and the rest becomes springs in the earth, in confirmation of His words, blessed and exalted:

﴿Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth?﴾ (39:21).

These springs go to places the rain does not reach, and people drink from them what we call wells or groundwater, and their livestock drink from them. When drought occurs, people go out, men, women, children, and elders, humbling themselves before God that He may send them rain. When we seek intercession through our infant children and the weak, God sends us rain.

Some people say that rain falls according to fixed scientific laws: vapour rises from the seas and becomes clouds in the upper layers of the atmosphere, then falls as rain. These are the fixed laws of its descent.

They say that the cloud must be at such and such a height in metres to reach the coldness of the atmosphere that makes it fall as rain, and that the cloud must be fertilised. We say that all of this is linked to variables. The wind blows or does not blow, and carries the cloud to a high cold region or does not carry it, and so on.

Thus every fixed thing is carried upon a variable. You may know the fixed laws, but the variable laws cannot be predicted, and therefore God, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And if they had remained steadfast upon the way, We would have given them abundant water to drink﴾ (72:16).

So the factors of rainfall are not subject to fixed laws. Rather the variable is the decisive factor, driving the cloud to the cold regions and to the required height. We must be mindful that there are fixed laws in the universe and laws that change, and that the changing law is what produces change.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Moses prayed for water for his people﴾ indicate that there is one who is asked for water (mustasqa, with the qaf open) and one who asks (mustasqi, with the qaf kasra). The one who asks, with the qaf kasra, is the one who humbles himself before God that He may send down rain. As for the one who is asked, with the qaf open, he is God, glorified and exalted, who sends down rain.

This situation is specific to God, blessed and exalted. There are no reservoirs of water, and there is no water on the earth, from rivers, wells, or springs, and no refuge except God. So one must seek intercession with God, blessed and exalted.

From Anas, may God be pleased with him, that when the people suffered drought, Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, would seek rain through al-Abbas ibn al-Muttalib, may God be pleased with him, and he said: "O God, we used to seek intercession with You through our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and You gave us rain; and now we seek intercession with You through the uncle of our Prophet, so give us rain." He said: "And they were given rain."¹

Some people say this is evidence that the dead cannot be sought for help, on the basis that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, did not seek intercession through the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after his death, but sought intercession through the uncle of the Messenger of God. We say: and through whom did Umar seek intercession? Did he seek intercession through al-Abbas or through the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He sought intercession through the Prophet's uncle, and by this we take the proof that intercession (tawassul, seeking a means of approach) is not restricted to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but extends to his relatives.

Here a question arises: why was the matter transferred from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to the uncle of the Messenger? We say: because the Messenger of God has passed away and no longer benefits from water, but his uncle al-Abbas is alive and benefits from water. Therefore the intercession was through the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It would not have been logical for them to seek intercession through the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was dead and did not need water. As for those who want to take intercession through people of standing, we say to them that the hadith is against you, not for you, because it establishes that intercession is permissible through one who is connected to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

We must speak of how the Truth, glorified and exalted, after the Children of Israel met His blessing with ingratitude and denial, still gave them water. We say: it is the merciful prophethood that was the cause of mercy descending upon the Children of Israel, mercy after mercy. Moses' desire for the mercy of God was boundless, and therefore the supplications of Moses, peace be upon him, for his people kept coming, and the response from God kept coming.

For the meaning to be complete, it should have been said: "And when Moses asked his Lord for his people, he said: O Lord, give them drink." But this was not stated; it was omitted, and the response came after it: ﴿And when Moses prayed for water for his people, We said: Strike the rock with your staff...﴾ So His words "O Lord, give my people water" and God's response to him are omitted because they are understood. The Qur'an therefore presents the essential points and leaves out the points that are understood, relying on people's intelligence. Just as in Surat al-Naml: the hoopoe went and saw the queen of Sheba and her throne, returned to Solomon and informed him. Solomon asked the hoopoe to deliver a letter to the queen of Sheba and her people, and said:

﴿Take this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then withdraw from them and see what they will return. She said: O chiefs, a noble letter has been delivered to me﴾ (27:28–29).

So Solomon ordered the hoopoe to deliver a letter to Bilqis and her people. The verse that follows has her say: ﴿O chiefs, a noble letter has been delivered to me.﴾ All the details were omitted: that the hoopoe took the letter, flew to the queen of Sheba, and dropped the letter before her throne; that Bilqis, queen of Sheba, picked up the letter and read it; that she summoned her people and began to recount to them the story of the letter. All of this was omitted because it is understood.

Moses said: O Lord, give my people water. And God, glorified and exalted, said to him: If you want water for your people... all of this is omitted. Then comes the noble verse: ﴿Then We said: strike the rock with your staff.﴾

﴿Strike the rock with your staff⦆ has a pause for us. A person, when he asks God for water, asks Him to send down rain from the sky. And the Truth, blessed and exalted, was able to send down rain from the sky upon the Children of Israel. But God, majestic is His majesty, wanted a miracle. He said: I will supply you with water, but of the same kind as that which withheld water from you, namely the rock beneath your feet.

I will not give you water from the sky, but God, glorified and exalted, wanted the Children of Israel to see the extent of the miracle, so He gave them water from the rock beneath their feet.

But who is affected by the striking: the rock or the staff? The staff is what is affected and shattered, while nothing happens to the rock. Yet God, glorified and exalted, wanted that with one strike of the staff the rock would split. Therefore the poet says:

O you who mock the varieties of fate,
you rebuke yourself, not fate.
And O you who struck the stone with a staff,
did the staff strike, or the stone?

The gushing of water from the staff's strike is evidence that the staff merely pointed to the rock, and water burst forth from it. And even if the staff were of iron, could it make water spring from the stone?

So the Truth, glorified and exalted, wants to draw our attention to the fact that it was possible for water to descend from the sky, but God willed it to be a compound blessing, so that they would know that He can bring water out of hard rock, and that the springing of water is one of the things included in "Be!" (kun). Here we must consider the obstinacy of the Children of Israel. They said to Moses: suppose we are in a place with no rock; from where will the water spring? We must take the rock with us so that when we are thirsty we can strike it with the staff. They forgot that there is what happens through causes and what happens through the word "Be!" Therefore you find, for example, great physicians perplexed about treating a patient, and then he is healed at the hand of a newly graduated young doctor. Does this young doctor know more than his professors who taught him? The answer, of course, is no.

A student does not surpass the teacher who taught him. Healing does not come through causes alone, but through the power of the One who causes. Therefore the time of healing came at the hand of this young doctor: God revealed the disease to him and inspired him with the cure.

God, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Then there gushed forth from it twelve springs.﴾ Why twelve springs? Because the Jews lived in a state of isolation.
