Each group among them was called a "sibt" (tribe), with a leader like a tribal chief. And the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Every people knew its drinking place.﴾ That is, every tribe or group went to its own drinking place. The springs gushed from the rock and spread out branching to all the tribes, each in its own place. When they had taken what they needed, Moses struck the rock and it dried up. Therefore we know that the rock gave them water according to their need. The lower side of the rock, the side touching the ground, and the upper side, which was struck with the staff, produced nothing; but from each of the remaining four sides there gushed three springs.

There is something in language called the homonym (al-lafz al-mushtarak, a word with several meanings). It is used for multiple meanings. If you say "the people watered their animals from the 'ayn" ('ayn here means a spring of water). If you say "the prince sent his 'uyun in the city," it means he sent his soldiers. If you say "I bought it for an 'ayn," it means for gold. If you say "he looked at me with an 'ayn shadhr," it means with his eye. So the word 'ayn is used for many things, and its meaning here is the flowing spring of water.

His words: ﴿Every people knew its drinking place⦆ mean that each tribe knew its own place that it must keep, so that none of them would lose water. But a person, when he is compelled, commits to what God requires of him and remains dutiful. When God relieves his distress and blessing returns to him, he returns to his rebellion. Therefore the Truth, majestic is He, says in it: ﴿Eat and drink of God's provision, and do not go about the earth causing corruption.﴾ That is, let your thanks for the blessing not be the spreading of corruption on the earth. And read His words, exalted is He:

{Certainly there was for Sheba in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and on the left. Eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him: a good land and a forgiving Lord. But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam and replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a little lote-tree...} (34:15–16).

¹ Narrated by al-Bukhari.

﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will not endure one kind of food. So call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions." He said, "Would you exchange what is lower for what is better? Go down to a city, for you will have what you ask." And humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them, and they returned with anger from Allah. That was because they had been disbelieving in the signs of Allah and killing the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.﴾ (61)

This noble verse is also one of the verses that remind of the blessings of Allah, the Exalted, upon Musa and upon the Children of Israel. We have already touched on the meaning of "one kind of food" when mentioning al-Man wa-al-Salwa (the manna and the quails). We said that the repeated descent of the manna and quails every day made the food one single kind. The word "wahid" (one) is the first of the numbers. When another like it is added to it, it becomes two; when another like it is added, it becomes three. Thus the origin of number is the one. The "wahid" indicates the singularity of an individual and does not indicate oneness in the sense of uniqueness. So when we say "Allah is Wahid," this means that there is nothing like Him. You are not "wahid" and not "ahad," because you are composed of parts, just as there are those who resemble you. The sun in our system is "wahid," but it is not "ahad," because it is composed of parts and interacts. Allah, the Exalted, is "Wahid," there is nothing like Him, and "Ahad" is not composed of parts. For this reason, among His Most Beautiful Names is "al-Wahid al-Ahad." We do not say that the name is repeated; rather, the first indicates individuality, and the second negates division.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We will not endure one kind of food﴾. We note here that the food is described as "one" although it consists of two kinds, al-Man and al-Salwa. But it was "one" because of the monotony of its descent. The food used to come to them from the sky. But their obstinacy towards Allah made them unable to endure it, so they said, "How do we know that it will not stop coming?" They wanted food that they would grow with their own hands and that would be before their eyes all the time. As if these miracles were not sufficient to give them confidence in the continuation of Allah's provision. They want to see; they want to see. Did they not say to Musa: ﴿Show us Allah openly﴾?

What did they ask for? They said: ﴿So call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth grows﴾. ﴿Call upon your Lord for us﴾ means ask from Allah. Because supplication (du'a') is a type of request, when you turn to Allah asking Him to give you, you call upon Him with the humility of the one who calls before the might of the one called upon. If the request is from the lower to the higher, it is called du'a'; if it is from an equal to an equal, it is called talab (request); and if it is from the higher to the lower, it is called amr (command).

The Children of Israel asked Musa to call upon Allah, the Exalted, to bring forth for them foods from what the earth grows. They enumerated the kinds of foods desired and said: ﴿from its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions﴾. But these are all types that indicate that whoever eats them is of the class of slaves. It is known that the family of Fir'awn enslaved the Children of Israel. It appears that the Children of Israel loved the life of slavery and developed a taste for it.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wanted to raise their status, so He sent down upon them al-Man and al-Salwa. But they preferred the food of slaves. The word "baql" (herbs) is not meant only as vegetables, but as every plant that has no stalk, such as lettuce, radish, kurrat (leeks), and arugula. Al-Qithaa' is the qiththa, a type of cucumber. Al-Fawm is wheat or garlic (thawm). Lentils and onions are well known. Before answering them, Allah, the Exalted, wanted to rebuke them, so He said: ﴿Would you exchange what is lower for what is better?﴾

When we hear the word "istibdal" (exchange), know that the letter "ba'" (bi) is attached to what is left behind. You say, "I bought the garment with a dirham." That means you took the garment and left the dirham.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿what is lower for what is better﴾. That is, they left what was better, which is al-Man and al-Salwa, and took what is lower. Here "lower" (dana) does not mean base (dana'a), because what the earth produces of Allah's blessings cannot be described as base. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, creates through causes and creates through direct command. What Allah creates by direct command, through His word "Be!" (kun), is better than what comes through causes. Because direct creation has no attribute of yours in it; it is pure giving from Allah. As for creation through causes, you may have a role in it, such as plowing the land or sowing seeds. What comes purely from Allah without your causes is close to the giving of the Hereafter, in which Allah gives without causes but by His word "Be!" For this reason, the Lord, Glorified and Exalted, says:

﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that with which We have provided pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 131).

So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, describes the provision of this world as a trial, and describes the provision of the Hereafter as better than it. Although the provision of this world and the Hereafter, and every provision in this existence, even unlawful provision, is from Allah, Majestic in His Majesty, there is no provider except Allah. But what makes provision unlawful is people's hastiness regarding it, so they take it by an unlawful way. Had they been patient, it would have come to them lawful.

We say that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is the One who provides, but He called a provision a trial and called another provision better than it. That is because provision from Allah without causes is higher and more excellent in rank than provision that comes through causes.

So when the Lord, Glorified and Exalted, says: ﴿Would you exchange what is lower for what is better?﴾, the meaning is: Would you exchange what is direct provision from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, which is al-Man and al-Salwa coming to you by "Be!", close to the provision of the Hereafter, for what is lower in rank, which is the provision of causes in this world? The Children of Israel did not answer this rebuke. Allah, the Exalted, said to them: ﴿Go down to a city, for you will have what you ask﴾. This is not said to them except because they insisted on asking, although the Majestic, Exalted One had shown them that what He sends down to them is better than what they ask for.

We note here that "Misr" came with tanwin (nunation). But the word Misr, when it occurs in the Noble Qur'an, does not occur with nunation. Among the honor of Misr is that it is mentioned more than once in the Noble Qur'an. We note that when Misr is meant as the Nile valley, it never comes with nunation. Read His saying, the Exalted:

﴿And settle your people in Misr in houses﴾ (part of verse 87, Surah Yunus).

And His saying, Majestic in His Majesty:

﴿Does not the kingdom of Misr belong to me, and these rivers flow beneath me?﴾ (part of verse 51, Surah al-Zukhruf).

And His saying, Glorified:

﴿And the one who bought him from Misr said to his wife, "Make his residence comfortable"﴾ (part of verse 21, Surah Yusuf).

And His saying, Blessed and Exalted:

﴿Enter Misr, if Allah wills, in security﴾ (part of verse 99, Surah Yusuf).

The word Misr is mentioned in the four verses above without tanwin. But in the verse we are dealing with: ﴿Go down to a Misran (a city)﴾, with tanwin. Is this Misr the same as the Misr mentioned in the verses referred to? We say no. Because the thing that is diptote (prohibited from tanwin) due to definiteness and feminine form, if it is a place or a location: at times you observe it as a region, and it remains feminine; at times you observe it as a place, and it becomes masculine. If it is a region, it is a proper noun prohibited from tanwin. If it is a place, it has definiteness but no feminine form. And at times there is definiteness and importance, but Allah has made it take tanwin in the Noble Qur'an, like the words Nuh, Lut, Shu'ayb, Muhammad, and Hud.

All these names were supposed to be diptote, but they took tanwin. So in the Noble Qur'an it is said Nuhan, Lutan, Shu'ayban, Muhammadan, and Hudan. So is it possible that the Misr in His saying, ﴿Go down to a Misr, for you will have what you ask﴾ is the Misr in which they lived under the rule of Fir'awn? His saying, ﴿Go down to a Misr﴾, may mean any city of the cities. It may also be the Misr in which Fir'awn lived. The word Misr is applied to every place that has a mufti, an amir, and a judge. It is derived from "iqtita'" (cutting off), because it is a place that cuts off the extension of the empty land. But what is established in the Noble Qur'an is that the Misr that is not given tanwin is the proper name of the Misr in which we live. As for Misran, which takes tanwin, it means every valley in which there is cultivation.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them﴾. Dhilla (humiliation) is the hardship that leads to breaking. It may be lifted from you if you are under the protection of another, who honors you by saying that you are under his protection. Allah, the Exalted, says about the Children of Israel:

﴿Humiliation has been stamped upon them wherever they are found, except by a rope from Allah and a rope from the people﴾ (part of verse 112, Surah Ali 'Imran).

A rope from Allah, as happened when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant with them in Madina, and they lived under the protection of the covenant. So "a rope from Allah" means at the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or the believers who follow him. And "a rope from the people" means under the protection of a strong state, such as the United States of America. If you make a covenant with them, they are honored; if you leave them, they are humiliated.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and humiliation was stamped upon them﴾. "Duribat" means it was impressed with a strong impression, by a strong stroke that makes the writing stand out on coins. That is why it is said "duribat fi Misr," meaning it was minted with a strong stroke. It humiliated them and remained prominent, which they cannot erase. As for "maskana" (poverty), it is a breaking in appearance.

The People of the Book used to pay the jizya (poll tax), and the jizya was taken from the wealthy. They used to wear dirty clothing and stand in a position of humiliation and disgrace so that they would not pay the jizya.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and they returned with anger from Allah﴾. That is, Allah's anger upon them because of their sins and disobedience, until anger became, because of their great disobedience, as if it were one of their characteristics. Why? ﴿That was because they had been disbelieving in the signs of Allah and killing the prophets without right﴾. That is, they disbelieved in the blessings and did not give thanks; they disbelieved in the signs and sold them for a small price. And they did not stop there, but they killed the prophets of Allah without right.

The prophets are not the same as the messengers. Prophets are a behavioral model (uswa sulukiyya), but they do not bring a new method. As for messengers, they are prophets in that they are a behavioral model, and messengers because they brought a new method. For this reason every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger. Allah, the Exalted, protects His prophets and messengers from sin, but He protects His messengers from being killed, so that their enemies cannot prevail over them. The coming of prophets is a necessity, because they are behavioral models that make it easy for people to commit to the method. The Children of Israel had prophets sent to them so that they would follow them, and they killed them. Why? Because they exposed their lies, their corruption, and their failure to commit to the method. For this reason you find that the disbeliever, the disobedient, and the uncommitted become jealous of and hate the one committed to the method of Allah, and try to remove him from their path, even by killing. So Allah's anger upon them was due to their disobedience, their transgression against the prophets, and the sins they committed.

After the Almighty spoke about the Children of Israel and how they disbelieved in His blessings, He wished to present to us the reckoning of the nations that preceded the nation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Day of Resurrection. This verse appears in Surah al-Ma'idah as well, but with a slight difference in order. In Surah al-Ma'idah it reads: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabians and the Christians...﴾ (from verse 69 of Surah al-Ma'idah).

That is, in Surah al-Ma'idah al-Sabi'un (the Sabians) precede al-Nasara (the Christians). The grammatical case (i'rab) also differs. In al-Baqarah it is al-Sabi'in (in the accusative form, with the ya'), while in al-Ma'idah it is al-Sabi'un (in the nominative form, with the waw). Another verse appears in Surah al-Hajj:

﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabians and the Christians and the Magians and those who associated others with Allah – Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is over all things a witness.﴾ (Surah al-Hajj, 17).

The three verses appear similar, yet there are many differences. What is the reason for the repetition found in the verses, for the placing of al-Sabi'in once before and once after, and for its being nominative when placed first? In the first two verses (al-Baqarah and al-Ma'idah) comes: ﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does righteous deeds – for them is their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.﴾ As for the verse in Surah al-Hajj, it adds: ﴿the Magians and those who associated others with Allah﴾, and the statement that follows differs: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection.﴾

When Allah created Adam and sent him down to populate the earth, He sent down with him guidance. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer﴾ (from verse 123 of Surah Ta-Ha).

It is taken for granted that Adam conveyed the method (of worship) to his children, and they conveyed it to their children, and so on. Then life occupies people, heedlessness overtakes them, the greed and avarice of worldly life afflict them, and they follow their desires. Thus it was necessary, out of Allah's mercy toward His creation, that Messengers should come to remind, to warn, and to give good tidings.

The noble verse says: ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾, meaning the faith of innate nature (fitrah) that descended with Adam to the earth. After that came religions which people disbelieved in, and so they were destroyed from the face of the earth, such as the people of Noah, Lot, Pharaoh, and others. Religions also came which have followers until now, such as Judaism, Christianity and Sabianism. Allah the Exalted wishes to gather all that came before into the message of Muhammad, peace be upon him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to purify the state of faith on earth.

So, those who believed first were with Adam or with the Messengers who came after him to address the ailments that had occurred. Then came those who named themselves Jews, those who named themselves Christians, and those who named themselves Sabians. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wishes to inform them that all of this has ended. Whoever believes in Muhammad (ﷺ), there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve. It is as if his message, peace be upon him, came to purify all the previous religions. Every person in the universe is obligated to believe in Muhammad, peace be upon him. He has called all people to believe in his message. Even if a person has remained from the time of Adam, or from the time of Idris, or Noah, or Abraham, or Hud, and those who were attributed to Judaism, Christianity and Sabianism, all of these are obligated to believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) and to affirm the religion of Islam. Islam gathers the earlier beliefs on earth and centers them in one religion. Those who believe in this religion: ﴿there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve.﴾ And those who do not believe have fear, and upon them is grief. This is an announcement of the unity of a new religion, in which everyone on earth is organized until the Hour is established. As for those who remained upon what they were upon, and did not believe in the new religion, Allah will not judge between them except on the Day of Resurrection. Therefore, the verse that contains the reckoning and judgment on the Day of Resurrection includes everyone who did not believe in the religion of Muhammad, peace be upon him, including the Magians and those who associated others with Allah.

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wished to remove the suspicion of one who follows a religion that preceded Islam and remains upon it after Islam has come, thinking that this religion benefits him. We say to him that Allah the Exalted has settled this matter in His saying:

﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ (from verse 85 of Surah Al 'Imran).

And His saying, majestic is His majesty:

﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam﴾ (from verse 19 of Surah Al 'Imran).

So the final purification of the procession of faith and the messages in existence has been settled. Whoever believed in Muhammad, peace be upon him, will not fear nor grieve on the Day of Resurrection, and whoever did not believe, Allah, blessed and exalted is He, says to him: ﴿Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ So, those who believed are those who inherited faith from the time of Adam. Those who were Jews are the followers of Moses, peace be upon him. The name came from their saying: ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾, meaning we have returned to You. The Christians, plural of Christian (naṣrānī), are attributed to al-Nasirah, the town where Jesus, peace be upon him, was born. Or (the name comes) from the saying of the disciples (al-Hawariyyun): "We are the helpers of Allah," in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿So when Jesus perceived disbelief from them, he said, "Who are my helpers for Allah?" The disciples said, "We are helpers of Allah. We have believed in Allah, and bear witness that we are Muslims."﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 52).

As for the Sabians, the scholars have differed concerning them. Some said they are the followers of Noah, but they altered (his religion) after him and worshipped, besides Allah, intermediaries in the universe such as the sun, the moon, and the stars. Or the Sabians are those who moved from the religion that was contemporary with them to the new religion. Or they are a group of rational people who said: "What our people are upon does not satisfy the intellect. How can we worship these idols when we make them and repair them?" So they abstained from worshipping the idols of the Arabs, and the Arabs said of them that they had "sabi'a" (turned away) from the religion of their fathers, meaning they abandoned it and believed in the new religion. Whatever the intended meaning of the Sabians, they are everyone who turned away from his religion to another religion.

We observe that Allah the Exalted placed the Sabians in Surah al-Baqarah later and in the accusative form, and in Surah al-Ma'idah earlier and in the nominative form. We say that this discussion enters the rules of grammar. The verse says: ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾. We know that (inna) makes the noun accusative and the predicate nominative. So alladhina (those who) is indeclinable, being a relative pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna. ﴿And those who were Jews﴾ is conjoined to alladhina amanu and is therefore also accusative. Al-Nasara is also conjoined to the noun of inna. Al-Sabi'in is also conjoined and accusative, marked by the ya' because it is a masculine sound plural.

We come to His saying: ﴿whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾. This is correct in Surah al-Baqarah both grammatically and in order. The Sabians came after the Christians because they are a small group that does not represent a large multitude like the Christians. But in the verse of al-Ma'idah, al-Sabi'un came first and in the nominative form, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews﴾. Alladhina amanu is the noun of inna, and alladhina hadu is conjoined. And al-Sabi'un: by grammatical analysis it should have been said wa al-Sabi'in. After it, al-Nasara is conjoined. But the word (al-Sabi'un) came between the Jews and the Christians, and its grammatical case was broken in a manner that the apparent structure does not require. So the Arabs are linguistically sensitive: whenever a listener hears al-Sabi'in, which is conjoined to the noun of inna, come in the nominative, he turns with a forced glance to know the reason.

When Abu Ja'far al-Mansur assumed the caliphate, he stood on the pulpit and made a lahn (a mistake in speech), meaning he erred in pronouncing a word. There was a Bedouin Arab sitting there, and his ears were offended. Al-Mansur erred a second time, and the Bedouin moved his ears in astonishment. When he erred a third time, the Bedouin stood up and said: "I testify that you have been given this matter by decree and destiny," meaning that you do not deserve this. This is what the Arab does when he hears it, he moves his ears. So when a word comes in the nominative when it should be in the accusative, this makes him realize that Allah has a wisdom and a cause. What is the cause?

As for alladhina amanu, their matter is understood. And alladhina hadu, their matter is understood, and al-Nasara, their matter is understood. But as for al-Sabi'un, these were not followers of a religion, but rather they took a different path. So this verse came to draw our attention that this purification also includes the Sabians, so it placed them first and in the nominative to draw the ears to them strongly. Allah the Exalted joins faith with action, which is why He always says: ﴿believed and did righteous deeds﴾, because faith, if it is not accompanied by action, has no benefit. And Allah wants faith to control the movement of life through righteous action. So He commands every believer to do righteous deeds, and for these there is no fear in this world, nor will they grieve in the Hereafter.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah (2), verse 63:

﴿And [remember] when We took your covenant and raised the mount above you, [saying], "Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it, that you may become righteous."﴾

Allah, glorified and exalted is He, once again bestows favour upon the Children of Israel through the blessings He conferred upon them, and reminds them of their denial of those blessings. But we observe that when the Noble Qur'an speaks about the Jews, it addresses them in the direct mode of address. So are those who lived at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, upon whom Allah, blessed and exalted, took the covenant, addressed with the intent of their fathers and forefathers who lived at the time of Musa, peace be upon him?

We say: it was required of every grandfather or father that he convey to his descendants what the matter of faith had come to. So when Allah bestows favour upon them by saying that He destroyed the people of Pharaoh and rescued them, He bestows favour upon them because He rescued their fathers from slaughter. Had He not rescued them, these contemporary Jews would not have come into existence at the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. They were hidden in the loins of their fathers. And for Allah to rescue them, the chain of life had to remain continuous. Whenever the life of a father ends before he marries and has children, at that very moment the life of his descendants ends as well. The same applies to the words of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿And [recall] when Musa asked for water for his people﴾. It is a favour upon the Jews contemporary with the revelation of the Qur'an, because if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had not rescued their fathers from death by thirst, they would have died without descendants.

Thus every favour upon the Jews in the era of Musa is a favour upon their descendants in the era of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him. And Allah, glorified and exalted is He, took from the Jews the ancient covenant, and had it not been for this covenant, they would not have believed, nor would their descendants have believed.

As for His words, ﴿and We raised the mount above you﴾: that is, Allah, blessed and exalted is He, reminds them that after they were saved and Allah drowned Pharaoh and his people, Musa went to the appointed time with his Lord to receive the Torah from Him. The Children of Israel then worshipped the calf. When Musa returned with the Torah and the tablets, they found its teachings burdensome for them, and said: "We cannot bear this obligation," and they considered not adhering to it and not accepting it.

The obligation (taklif) comes from the One who imposes it, who is Allah, glorified and exalted is He. Yet they say that Allah imposed upon them what they cannot bear, whereas Allah, majestic in His majesty, does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. This is the principle of faith laid down by the Truth, majestic in His majesty. Some people think the meaning of the noble verse:

﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ (part of verse 286, Surah al-Baqarah).

They think that we are placing ourselves as judges over Allah's imposition: if we believe we can bear this obligation, then it is from Allah, and if by our own judgment we believe we cannot bear it, we say Allah did not impose this on us because it is beyond our capacity. But the correct judgment is: did Allah impose this matter upon you or not? If Allah has imposed it, then He knows that it is within your capacity, because Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. We now hear outcries saying that the age can no longer bear it, and that the conditions of the world, the speed of its movement, and the speed of its events are a justification that it is not within our capacity to perform some obligations. Perhaps this obligation was within capacity in the past, when life was simple, its movement slow, and its problems limited.

To whoever repeats this speech we say: the One who imposed it upon you long ago is Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and He knows that you are able to perform the obligation at the time of its descent, and after thousands of years from its descent until the Hour arrives. The proof of this is that there are those who perform the obligation and volunteer more than it, seeking the station of excellence (ihsan). There are those who pray the obligatory prayers, which are the obligation, and add to them the sunnah prayers, and there are those who stand in night prayer, continually drawing near to Allah, blessed and exalted is He, through voluntary acts of the same kind as what was obligated. There are those who fast Ramadan and voluntarily fast at the beginning of the Arabic months, or every Monday and Thursday throughout the year, or in the months of Rajab and Sha'ban. There are those who perform Hajj once and those who perform it many times. There are those who keep to the limits of zakat and those who give more in charity than it requires.

Therefore, all the obligations which Allah has imposed upon us are within our capacity and less than our capacity. It cannot be said that the age has changed, for we are the ones living in this age, with all its changes, performing the obligations and adding to them without any hardship. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, raised the mount above the Children of Israel out of mercy for them, just as a doctor holds the scalpel to remove pus that has formed within the body, because the body is not sound without this.

Therefore, when Allah, glorified and exalted is He, willed by His grace and mercy to benefit the Children of Israel despite their reluctance, He raised above them the mountain of Tur, which is located in Sinai, and said to them: accept the obligation or the mountain will be brought down upon you. Just as Allah, blessed and exalted is He, destroyed those who disbelieved, rejected faith, and opposed the messengers before them. Some may say that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, compelled the Jews to accept an obligation, while He says:

﴿There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become clear from error﴾ (part of verse 256, Surah al-Baqarah).

And His words:

﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ (part of verse 29, Surah al-Kahf).

We say: Allah, majestic in His majesty, did not compel anyone to accept the obligation. Rather, out of His mercy, He gave them the choice between the obligation and a punishment that would befall them and destroy them, and this punishment is that the mount of Tur be brought down upon them. So the matter involves no compulsion, but it involves choice. He gave those before them the choice between faith and destruction, and they did not believe until destruction befell them. But when the Children of Israel saw the mountain above them, they humbled themselves, prostrating on the ground. Their prostration is evidence that they accepted the method. Yet while they were prostrating, they kept looking at the mountain above them, fearing that it would fall upon them. That is why the prostration of the Jews to this day is on one side of the face, while the other side looks upward, out of fear that the mountain would collapse upon them. If you asked a Jew why he prostrates in this manner, he would tell you: "I carry the Torah," and he sways, trembling. We say that they trembled at the moment Allah raised the mount of Tur above them, so in every prayer they took the same posture, and those who witnessed them among their children and descendants believed it to be a condition of prostration among them. Thus their prostration became on one side of the face, and their gaze toward something above them that they fear. That is, the picture that occurred to them at the moment the mount of Tur was raised is still with them until now.

In this noble verse the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿And [recall] when We raised the mount above you﴾. In another verse, the Lord, majestic in His majesty, speaks of the same event: ﴿And [recall] when We shook the mountain over them as though it were a canopy, and they thought it would fall upon them: "Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it that you may become righteous" [7:171]﴾ (Surah al-A'raf).

﴿Nataqna﴾ (We shook/uprooted): it is as if the mountain were a stake in the ground that We wanted to pull out, so We shake it right and left until it can come out of the earth. This shaking, quaking and pulling is the *natq*. The mountain is exactly like a stake that needs shaking, jolting and pulling until it comes out of its place. When this image occurred, they humbled themselves, prostrated, and accepted the method.

The Lord, glorified and exalted is He, says: ﴿Take what We have given you with determination﴾. Taking is usually the counterpart of giving: you take from a giver. The obligation is a taking from Allah so that through it you give a movement of righteousness into the universe. Thus every taking must be followed by a giving: you take from the generation that preceded you and give to the generation that follows you, but you do not give it as it is; you must add to it. This addition is what builds civilizations.

His words, ﴿with determination﴾: that is, do not take the obligation with laxity. A person usually takes firmly what is beneficial to him. Therefore, the nature of Allah's methods is to be taken with strength and certainty, so that they yield much good with strength and certainty. When you take Allah's method with strength, you have been entrusted with it, your breast has been expanded, and you want to take more. That is why you find in the Noble Qur'an, "They ask you about such-and-such," which is evidence that they loved the obligation and knew it was beneficial, so they wanted more benefit.

Since the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said ﴿Take what We have given you with determination﴾, they came to love the obligation, and it was no longer burdensome to them.

His words, ﴿and remember what is in it that you may become righteous﴾: remember what is in it, that is, what is in the method, that it addresses every matter of life; and know the ruling on these matters. ﴿That you may become righteous﴾ means that you obey Allah and fear His punishment and chastisement on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 64:

﴿Then you turned away after that. But for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would surely have been among the losers.﴾

After the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, explained to us how He commanded the Jews to remember the method (manhaj) and not to forget it. Merely remembering the method would have led them to believe in Islam and in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because it is written in their Torah and his attributes are mentioned there. What did the Jews do?

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Then you turned away after that﴾, meaning: you turned away from the method of Allah, forgot it, and paid it no attention. ﴿But for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would surely have been among the losers﴾. What is grace (fadl) and what is mercy (rahmah)? Grace (fadl) is an increase beyond what one deserves. It is said to you, "This is your right, and this is grace from me," meaning an addition to your right.

On the authority of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Be steadfast, strive to be near (to perfection), and rejoice, for no one will enter Paradise by his deeds alone." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His forgiveness and mercy." (1)

If you ask how this is so, and how it is that no one enters Paradise by his deeds, we say: yes, because all the deeds of this world do not equal one of the blessings of Allah upon His creation. You remember the deed and do not remember the grace. Everyone who enters Paradise does so by the grace of Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He. Even the martyrs, who gave their lives, which is all they possess in this world. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted is He, says of them:

﴿Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and rejoicing for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 170)

If these martyrs, who are in the highest ranks of Paradise, entered Paradise by the grace of Allah, then what of those who are lower than them in reward? Allah, glory be to Him, has grace over all His servants. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of mankind are not grateful.﴾ (part of verse 243, Surah al-Baqarah)

As for mercy (rahmah), it is what opened the way to turn toward the forgiveness of sins. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, wants to draw our attention to the fact that, but for this grace toward the Children of Israel, and but for His opening for them the door of mercy and forgiveness so that they might return once more to their covenant and their method, they would have been among the losers, upon whom a manifest loss would have fallen in this world and the Hereafter. But Allah, blessed and exalted is He, by His grace and mercy, led them to the religion which Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, preserved by His power from any distortion. He lifted from them the burden of preserving the Book and the heavy load that results from that in this world. He showed them mercy through the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whom He sent as a mercy to the worlds, in confirmation of His saying, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds.﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 107)

He gave them the grace of this final religion, which settled the question of faith in this universe. Together with this mercy and this grace, by sending down to them in the Torah the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the time of his mission, He opened for them a door so that they would not become among the losers. But they abandoned this door just as they turned away from their religion.

1 "Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Ahmad, Ibn Majah and al-Darimi."

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 2, verse 65:

﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ﴾ (٦٥)

After Allah, may His majesty be exalted, showed us how He opened the door of grace and mercy to the Jews, and they abandoned it, He wished to show us some of what they did in opposing Allah's commands and evading them by trickery. Allah, blessed and exalted, has commands regarding religion and commands concerning worldly affairs. He does not want us to treat any of His commands, whether related to religion or to this world, with a lack of seriousness, or to prefer one command over another. For this reason, you find in Surat al-Jumu'ah, for example, the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted:

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَاةِ مِن يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ فَاسْعَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَذَرُوا الْبَيْعَ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ ﴿٩﴾ فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلَاةُ فَانتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَابْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ (Surat al-Jumu'ah).

These are two commands, one concerning religion and the second concerning this world, and both are part of Allah's method. Allah does not want you to trade and work during the prayer time, nor to leave your work without cause and remain in the mosque after the prayer. When the prayer is called, go to the mosque; when the prayer is concluded, go out to seek provision. There are two days of the week mentioned by name in the Qur'an, namely Friday (yawm al-Jumu'ah) and Saturday (yawm al-Sabt), while the days of the week are seven, and five of them are not mentioned by name in the Qur'an: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. Friday is the festival of the Muslims, in which their gathering in the mosques and the performance of congregational prayer were legislated. We note that the name Friday was not derived from a number. The days of the week are named after numbers except Friday and Saturday. Thus you find Sunday (al-Ahad) named after one, Monday (al-Ithnayn) after two, Tuesday (al-Thulathā') after three, Wednesday (al-Arbi'ā') after four, and Thursday (al-Khamis) after five.

It would have been expected that Friday be named after six, but it was not named so. Why? Because it is the day on which the system of the existence of the universe was completed. So Allah, blessed and exalted, named it al-Jumu'ah (the gathering) and made it a festival for us. The festival is the gathering of the whole universe on this day, the gathering of Allah's blessing in the creation of the universe and its completion on that day. So the believers in Allah gather in a gathering of celebration for the completion of the creation of the universe for them. As for Saturday (al-Sabt): the letters ba' and ta' indicate the meaning of cutting off. It is said sabata and yasbutu sabtan when his work ceased. We note that the creation of the heavens and the earth was completed in six days, in confirmation of His saying, exalted be He:

﴿هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ (part of verse 4, Surat al-Hadid).

The completion of creation was on Friday, and on the seventh day, which is Saturday, everything had settled and the creation of the universe had been finished. For this reason it has sabat, that is, this day is called sabat, because in it the movement ceases after the completion of creation.

When the Jews wanted a day of rest, Allah gave them Saturday. The Truth, blessed and exalted, wanted to test them on this day, and the test (ibtila') is their examination. They lived by the sea, and their work was fishing. The test came on this day, when Allah forbade them to work and made the fish they hunted come to them, their fins appearing, while they had been searching for them all week and perhaps not finding them. On Saturday they came to them, appearing on the surface of the water, approaching them to tempt them. Read His saying, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿وَاسْأَلْهُمْ عَنِ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ حَاضِرَةَ الْبَحْرِ إِذْ يَعْدُونَ فِي السَّبْتِ إِذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ حِيتَانُهُمْ يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعًا وَيَوْمَ لَا يَسْبِتُونَ لَا تَأْتِيهِمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَبْلُوهُم بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ ﴿١٦٣﴾﴾ (Surat al-A'raf).

Thus the surface of the sea fills with fish and whales on Saturday. When Sunday morning comes, they disappear far away. They wanted to make Saturday a festival for themselves in which they would do nothing, but at the same time they wanted to obtain these fish and whales. They devised something called deep pits (al-hiyad al-'amiqah) to evade Allah's command not to work on this day, and at the same time to obtain the fish. These pits the fish enter easily, and because they are deep, it cannot get out of them. They leave it to spend the night, and in the morning they catch it. This was a trick on their part to oppose Allah's command. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, does not love those who resort to trickery regarding any of His commands.

Allah, exalted be He, says: ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ﴾. This is a well-known story among the Jews, and it is widely transmitted (mutawatir): the grandfathers teach it to the fathers and the fathers to the grandchildren. It is not new to them, although the addressees are the Jews contemporary with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Therefore, when we hear ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمْ﴾, meaning "you certainly know," it means that the story is known to you, as if it were among the stories of the heritage that they pass down to one another.

As for His saying, ﴿الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ﴾: the object here is one... here the trick is mentioned, that they transgressed Allah's command to rest on Saturday. In reality they did not hunt on Saturday, but they evaded what was forbidden by setting traps for the whales and fish. In doing so they were foolish. What was forbidden was that they take possession of the fish by hunting on Saturday, but they took possession of them by trickery and traps. As for His saying, ﴿اعْتَدَوْا﴾, it means they transgressed the limits of Allah that were set for them. Usually, when Allah forbids something, His saying follows the prohibition:

﴿تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا﴾ (part of verse 187, Surat al-Baqarah).

Because He wants to prevent you from being tempted, so that you do not fall into disobedience, He says to you, "Do not approach." But the Children of Israel transgressed the ruling of Allah while displaying obedience, and they were disobedient. They thought they could deceive Allah by claiming to be obedient while they were disobedient. Allah's judgment against them was issued: ﴿فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ﴾.

Usually you do not command a person to do something unless he is able to do it. The command here is that they become apes. Are they able to carry it out, and to change their form into apes? It is a command within the power of Allah alone. How then does He say to them, "Be apes"?

We say that the one commanding here is the very one who is able to make them apes. This command is called a compulsory (taskhiri) command. He did not say to them, "Be apes," so that they would become apes by their own will. Rather, as soon as He, glorified be He, said "Be apes," they were. This shows the submission of the one commanded to the command, while he has no choice. Even if he did not want it, it would not be necessary that they had heard the words of Allah or that He had spoken to them, because if what was required of them were the carrying out of what they had heard, it might have been necessary. But with the mere issuing of the command, and before they became aware or knew anything, they were apes.

The scholars have differed on how these Jews turned into apes. How were they transformed (maskh)? Some of them said that the transformation took place while they did not know it. When they found themselves changed into a creature lower than the human, they did not eat or drink until they died. Some scholars said that when a human is transformed, he does not reproduce, and therefore once they were transformed they did not reproduce until they became extinct. Why did they not reproduce? Because Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ﴾ (part of verse 164, Surat al-An'am).

And if they had reproduced, the children would have borne the burden of their fathers' sin, and this is rejected by Allah. So it is by the mercy of Allah that they did not eat, drink or reproduce. They remained for a period and then became extinct through diseases and plagues, and this is what happened to them.

Some people may say: if they were transformed into apes, then where did the Jews who exist now come from? We say to them that not all the Jews were disobedient. Rather, there was a minority among them who disobeyed and were transformed, while the majority remained, so that their descendants reached us today. Other scholars have said that there is a verse in Surat al-Ma'idah that says:

﴿قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُم بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذَٰلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِندَ اللَّهِ ۚ مَن لَّعَنَهُ اللَّهُ وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهُمُ الْقِرَدَةَ وَالْخَنَازِيرَ وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ شَرٌّ مَّكَانًا وَأَضَلُّ عَن سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ ﴿٦٠﴾﴾ (Surat al-Ma'idah).

So this is the case of a people upon whom Allah's anger fell, and He transformed them into apes and swine and worshippers of the Taghut (tāghūt, every being or person who exceeds the limits in tyranny and oppression). Allah, may His majesty be exalted, has informed us that the Jews were transformed into apes, but He did not tell us that they were transformed into swine. Were they transformed into apes? Then after that the anger of Allah increased against them and they were transformed into swine? Did Allah move them from humanity to animality in character, will and form?

We say that first we must consider the animality into which Allah moved them. We find that the ape is the animal that always has its private parts exposed, and its private parts have a distinctive color different from its body, and it is not disciplined except by the stick. Likewise the Jews did not accept the method except when the mountain of Sinai (Tur) was lifted above them. What they are in now is not a transformation of form but a transformation of character (maskh khuluq). The swine does not feel jealous over its females, and this is a characteristic found in the Jews. As for worshippers of the Taghut: the Taghut is every person who transgresses the limit in aggression and oppression, and the worshippers of the Taghut are those who obey every tyrant, helping him in his oppression, and they themselves are like that.

So this process of transformation, whether it took place once or in two stages, is a formal matter. But Allah, glorified and exalted be He, gave us, in the verse we mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah, the moral characteristics of the Jews. It is as if they were transformed in character and transformed in morals.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 66:

﴿So We made it a deterrent punishment for what was before it and what was after it, and an admonition to the God-fearing.﴾

God, blessed and exalted, wishes to draw our attention to the fact that, after He made them (the Jews) a warning example in their bodies and their morals: ﴿And We made them a deterrent punishment for what was before it﴾, i.e., what was with it, ﴿and what was after it﴾, i.e., what came after it. "Nakal" (deterrent punishment) is a severe penalty. A penalty must arise from criminalization first. This is the Islamic principle and the legal principle. Men of law say: there is no penalty except by criminalization, and no criminalization except by text. Before you punish, you must state that this act is a crime and its penalty is such-and-such. In that case, when any person commits it, he deserves the penalty. As long as this is the situation, there must be legislation.

Legislation does not mean that God legislated the punishment. Rather, it means an attempt to prevent the crime through intimidation so that no one commits it. If the crime occurs, the penalty must be imposed, because imposing it is a lesson to others and a deterrent from committing it. This deterrence is called "nukul" (deterrence), and from it comes "al-nukul fi al-yamin" (refraining from an oath), i.e., retracting it.

So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We made it a deterrent punishment﴾, i.e., We made them a deterrent and a strong punishment, so that none of the Children of Israel would return to a violation of this kind. ﴿And a deterrent punishment for what was before it﴾, i.e., a penalty which, when those who witnessed it narrate it, suffices so that they never approach this disobedience. It becomes for them an admonition they never forget. ﴿And what was after it﴾ means We made them something the generations of the Children of Israel inherit, generation after generation, just as a father tells his son, so that no one in the future returns to such an act, because of the severity of the punishment. ﴿And an admonition to the God-fearing﴾, i.e., an admonition to all people to whom God, blessed and exalted, conveys what happened to the Children of Israel and the punishment He inflicted on them, so that they protect themselves from the evil of the torment on the Day of Resurrection, in which there will be forms of torment far more severe than this.

However, we must draw attention to the fact that the principle "there is no penalty except by criminalization, and no criminalization except by text" is a divine principle. Therefore God, exalted is He, says:

﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ (part of verse 15, Surah al-Isra').

That is, the Messenger comes first to criminalize these acts. If any of God's creation commits them, the penalty becomes due upon him. Hence, everything said about retroactive laws contradicts the law of God, blessed and exalted, and His justice. There is nothing in the justice of heaven that could be described as retroactive.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 67:

﴿And when Musa said to his people, "Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow." They said, "Do you take us in mockery?" He said, "I seek refuge in Allah from being among the ignorant."﴾

We touched upon this noble verse at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, because the surah is named after this (cow). We note here that Allah, glorified and exalted, used the particle "wa-idh" (and when), meaning "and remember": ﴿And when Musa said to his people, "Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow."﴾ He did not say why He commanded them to slaughter the cow. We must read the verses up to the end of the story to know the reason, in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And when you killed a soul and then disputed over it, but Allah was to bring out that which you were concealing. So We said, "Strike the dead body with part of it." Thus Allah brings the dead to life and shows you His signs that you might reason.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah)

In all matters it is presumed that a command is preceded by its cause. But this is the greatness of the Noble Qur'an, for asking about the cause first means that the command comes from someone equal to you. If a person tells you, "Do such-and-such," you ask him "Why?" so that you may obey and carry out the command. So it is the command from an equal whose cause you ask about. But a command from one who is not your equal, such as a father's command to his son, a doctor's to his patient, or a commander's to his soldiers, such a command is not asked about its cause before its execution, because the one who issued it is wiser than the one to whom it was issued. And if every servant (mukallaf) who came to Allah's command asked first about its cause, he would have done the command for the sake of its cause, as if he had done it for the sake of the cause. From here faith disappears, and it becomes equal whether the person is a believer or not, and the execution of the command would be without reward from Allah.

Faith makes the believer receive the command from Allah obediently, whether he knows its cause or not, and he carries it out because it comes from Allah. Therefore the execution of any act of faith is done because the command comes from Allah. And every obligation that comes, the cause of its occurrence is faith in Allah. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, begins every obligation with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, meaning, O you who have believed in Allah as Lord, God and Creator, take from Allah and act, because you have believed in the One who commanded you.

In these verses under discussion, Allah, exalted is He, wanted to make this clear to us. He brought the command to slaughter the cow first, and the cause in the verses that related to us the cause of the story. And when you worship Allah, everything you do is obedience to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, whether you know the cause or not. For you perform the prayer because Allah, blessed and exalted is He, commanded you to pray. So if you performed the prayer as exercise, or as a means of waking early, or as movements needed for suppleness of the joints, your prayer would be without reward or recompense. If you want exercise, go to one of the gyms and let one of the trainers train you so that the exercise is done according to its principles. And if you want physical fitness, there are a thousand ways to achieve it. And if you want to worship Allah as Allah commanded you, then let your prayer be the one Allah prescribed for you because Allah prescribed it. And likewise all the other acts of worship.

Fasting is not a feeling of the sensation of hunger, nor is it a method of dieting, but it is an act of worship. If you do not fast in execution of Allah's command to fast, you have no reward. And if you make for fasting any cause other than worship, it is a fast that Allah does not accept, for Allah is the most self-sufficient of partners from partnership. Whoever associates anyone with Him, Allah leaves his deed to the one he associated. And likewise all acts of worship.

This is the faith-based understanding that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wanted to draw our attention to in the story of the Cow of the Children of Israel. Therefore He did not bring the cause or reason first, but brought the story, then informed us at its end of the reason. Whether Allah informs us of the reason or not, this does not change our faith in the reality of what happened. Indeed the story has wisdom, even if it is hidden from us, for it exists.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to slaughter a cow﴾, Allah, blessed and exalted is He, gave the command first to test the strength of the faith of the Children of Israel, and the extent of their carrying out the obligation without hesitation or delay. But instead of doing that, they began bargaining and dawdling: ﴿And when Musa said to his people﴾. The word "qawm" (people) is applied only to men. Therefore the Noble Qur'an says:

﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them.﴾ (Part of verse 11, Surat al-Hujurat)

So "qawm" means men, because they are responsible for the affairs of their families and their women. Therefore the Arab poet says:

"And I do not know, nor do I think I know, whether the people of Hisn are men or women."

Guardianship (qawwamah) belongs to men, and a woman's life is built on modesty in her home, and men stand for her with what she needs of affairs. It is presumed that the woman is a source of rest for her husband, her home and her children, and in this she has a greater task than the task of men.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you﴾: the command (amr) is a request for an act. If the one commanding is higher than the one commanded, we call it a command (amr); if he is equal to him, we call it a request (iltimas); and if it is directed upward, we call it a supplication (raja' and du'a'). However, we must pay attention to His saying, exalted is He, on the tongue of Zakariyya:

﴿There Zakariyya prayed to his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring."﴾

(Part of verse 38, Surat Al 'Imran)

Is this a command from Zakariyya? Certainly not, because it is a supplication, and supplication is a request from the lower to the higher. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah commands you﴾: if a person of even minimal intelligence were asked to slaughter a cow, would this need clarification? Had they slaughtered a cow, everything would have been completed without any effort. Since Allah had asked them to slaughter a cow, all that was incumbent upon them was execution.

But look at their stupidity even in questioning. They wanted to do anything to nullify the obligation. They said to Musa, their prophet, "You are mocking us." That is, they denounced that Allah, blessed and exalted is He, would obligate them to slaughter a cow without any specification, so they accused Musa of mocking them, as if they saw the matter as difficult for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, that it could not be resolved merely by slaughtering a cow. When Musa heard their words, he was astonished. Is there a prophet who mocks one of the obligations of Allah, blessed and exalted is He? Would the prophet of Allah convey to them a command of Allah, majestic is His majesty, as a jest?

Here Musa realized that these Jews were ignorant: ignorant of their Lord, of their Messenger, and ignorant of their Hereafter, and that they were trying to take everything by their own measures and not by the measures of Allah, glorified and exalted is He. So he turned to the heavens seeking refuge in Allah from these ignorant people, who, when ease comes to them, want it difficult, and when ease comes to them, want it hard, and who ask Allah to trouble them, to make them hard-pressed, and to make everything in their lives difficult and burdensome.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 68:

﴿They said: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what she is." He said: "Indeed, He says she is a cow neither old nor virgin, but between that, so do what you are commanded."﴾ (2:68)

Their question shows the deficiency of faith (iman) in their hearts. They did not say "call upon your Lord" (rabbana), but "call upon your Lord" (rabbuka), as if He were only the Lord of Musa. This manner of speech recurred many times among the Children of Israel, to the point that they said, as the Noble Qur'an relates to us:

﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here.﴾ (part of 5:24)

The dialogue between them and Musa continued for a long time. They would direct a question to Musa, he would call upon Allah, and the answer would come to him from Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He. Instead of carrying out the command and the matter ending, they would direct another question, Musa would call upon his Lord, the answer would come to him, and the answer would lead to a question from them that was out of place. Then Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, cuts off the means of disputation from them by giving them attributes of a cow that apply to only one cow. It is as if they made things hard for themselves, so Allah made them hard for them.

As for the question of the Children of Israel: Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, says: ﴿They said: "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what she is."﴾ It is a question with no meaning and no place, because Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, had told them that it is a cow, and He did not say, for example, that it is an animal in general, so there was no room for the question. Thus the Truth, Blessed and Exalted is He, says to them: ﴿Indeed, she is a cow neither old nor virgin.﴾ The word "fāriḍ" (old, past-bearing age) in the language means "wide," and what is meant by it is a cow that is no longer young. But what is the connection between a cow's age and "wide"? A cow is frequently subjected to pregnancy, and it is essentially for milk and breeding. Since she has been frequently pregnant, the place of the milk in her becomes wide. That is, her belly grows wider with each new pregnancy. When a cow's belly is wide, it is known that she is old, has given birth many times, and has become fāriḍ.

The word "bikr" (virgin) has several meanings: among them, that no stallion has mounted her; among them, that she is a virgin who has given birth once; and among them, that she has given birth several times but this does not show on her because she is young in age.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿but between that⁠﴾, it means middle between all these attributes. Then the Truth, after that, rebukes them, saying: ﴿so do what you are commanded﴾, meaning: enough of disputing; carry out Allah's command and slaughter the cow. But they did not stop, for they wished to keep debating.

I will translate this passage faithfully.

They sought another question: "What is its colour?" It is as if Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, when He spoke to them about the cow, opened the doors for them to ask, "What is its colour?" Yet He, glorified and exalted, had said to them: ﴿So do what you are commanded﴾. But they did not do so; rather, they asked, "What is its colour?" ﴿He said, "Indeed, He says it is a yellow cow."﴾ Yellow is one of the colours. Then He, majestic is His majesty, said: ﴿Bright in its colour﴾, meaning intensely yellow. Then He said: ﴿It pleases the beholders﴾, meaning that everyone who looks at it is pleased by its freshness, its cleanliness, its fine appearance, and the harmony of its body.

Describing the cow as yellow is a known colour. Regarding colours, you cannot specify a colour except by seeing it. For this reason, the sensible perception of colours must precede knowing them, and after that you bring the required colour. Therefore it is not said merely "yellow," because you cannot pin it down, since yellow has endless degrees. Mixing colours gives you an endless number of its shades. Hence those who work at painting houses cannot paint an apartment in one colour unless they prepare the whole mixture of the colour at once, so that the paint comes out entirely in a single shade. But if you asked him to paint the apartment in the same colour, on condition that he paint one room each day, he would not be able to do so. So when you hear "yellow," the yellow colour comes to your mind; but when you hear "bright" (fāqi'), each colour has a description suited to it that gives us the precision of the required colour. "Fāqi'" means intensely yellow.

I think the matter has now become clear: it is a cow whose colour is bright yellow, pleasing to the beholders. The Children of Israel should have been content with that, but they returned to the question once again.

They said, "Call upon your Lord for us to make clear to us what it is, for the cow has become confused to us, and indeed we, if Allah wills, will be guided."

Although what was said to the Children of Israel was perfectly clear about the cow, its age, its form, its colour and its appearance, Allah the Exalted wished to discipline them, so He made them look at the cows. One of them says, "This is it," and another says, "No, rather it is in such-and-such a place," and a third says, "No, rather it is in such-and-such a location." So they returned to Musa, asking him to go back to his Lord so that He might make it clear to them, because the cow had become confusing to them. Here they remembered Allah, whom they had forgotten and whose command they had not carried out since He told them, "Slaughter a cow," and then said to them, "Do what you are commanded" (﴿افعلوا ما تؤمرون﴾). So they asked Him for guidance after they had strayed and lost their way because of their obstinacy and contentiousness. And the answer came from Allah the Exalted.

**Who Bears the Responsibility in This Verse**

*(This is not part of the passage; I'm leaving the heading out. Translation begins below.)*

Actually, to be clear: here is the translation.

﴿He said, "He says it is a cow that is neither broken to plough the earth nor to water the tilth, sound and without blemish." They said, "Now you have brought the truth," and they slaughtered her, though they had almost not done it.﴾ (2:71)

﴿A cow that is not broken﴾... The dhalul cow is the cow that has been trained and made docile, which performs its task without tiring, just as a trained horse does not tire its rider because it has been broken in. Sayyidina Isma'il was the first to break horses and tame them. God, glorified and exalted, gave them the first description of the cow: that she was not trained. No one had led her or made her work. She roamed according to her own nature and disposition in the fields without a driver.

﴿That plows the earth﴾: that is, she had not been used to plough or cultivate the land.

﴿Nor waters the tilth﴾: that is, she had not been used to operate the water-wheels for irrigating crops.

﴿Sound, with no blemish in her﴾: that is, free of defects, her ears not pierced, and bearing none of the marks by which people distinguish their cattle. Her leg was not lame, and she was free of spots and colours other than the bright yellow.

The word ﴿lā shiyata fīhā﴾ (*lā shiyata fīhā*): that is, "there is nothing in her" (*shiyah* here means a mark or blemish, and the phrase means "no spot or mark of any kind on her").

Whoever reflects on the description of the cow as it comes in the verses sees the difficulty and strictness in choosing her attributes, as though the Truth, blessed and exalted, wanted to requite them for their deeds. The Children of Israel found only one cow that fit these specifications, so they said, ﴿Now you have brought the truth﴾, as though what Moses had said before had been outside the bounds of truth. They slaughtered the cow, but only reluctantly, because they had been eager not to slaughter her, out of their eagerness not to carry out the command. They wanted to stall God, glorified and exalted. God tells us that the mark of the believers is that they hasten to carry out His obligations. Consider His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous﴾ (Surat Al ʿImran, 3:133).

This eagerness of the believers in carrying out their duties is evidence of their love for obligation, because you hasten to do what the one you love asks of you. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿and they had almost not done it﴾, shows us that they tried to delay the execution and drag their feet.

We must notice that the Children of Israel's slowness in carrying out the command served another matter of faith. The cow that God asked of them, because they did not carry out the command as soon as it was given, became a rare cow that is not repeated. The specifications given to them in the end applied only to a single cow, so that its owner could control its price and sell it at the highest prices.

The story is that there was among the Children of Israel a righteous man who was scrupulous about lawful sustenance, truthful in speech, and sincere in his true faith in God. When death approached him, he had a cow, and he had a wife and their young son. What could he do, since he owned nothing but the cow? He turned to God and said, "O God, I entrust this cow to You for my son," and then he released her into the pastures. He did not appoint anyone to look after her, but entrusted her to God, entrusting her to the trustworthy hand of God over all things. Then he said to his wife, "I own nothing but this cow, and I trust no one with her except God. I have released her into the pastures."

When the boy grew up, his mother said to him, "Your father left you a deposit with God, which is a cow." He said, "O mother, where can I find her?" She said, "Be like your father: he put his trust in God and made a deposit; you put your trust in God and reclaim it." The boy said, "O God, Lord of Abraham and Lord of Moses, return to me what my father deposited with You." Then the cow came to him, having become a cow, and he took her to show his mother. As he walked along, the Children of Israel saw him. They said, "This is the cow that the Lord asked for." They went to her owner and asked to buy her. He said, "For how much?" They said, "For three dinars." He went to consult his mother, and they feared she would refuse, so they offered him six dinars. His mother said, "No, do not sell her." The son said, "I will not sell her except for her hide filled with gold," and they paid him what he asked.

Thus we find that the righteousness of the father causes God to be a guardian over his children, watching over them and making their affairs easy for them.

The story of the slain man is that a wealthy man from the Children of Israel had no child to inherit from him. He had relatives, each of whom wished to seize the wealth of this man. Wealth and gold were the life of the Children of Israel. So the son of his brother plotted against this wealthy man and killed him in order to inherit him and take over his wealth. But he wanted to put the accusation away from himself, so he carried the body and threw it at the gate of a neighbouring village, so that its people would be accused of killing the wealthy man. In the morning the people of the village rose and found the body of the wealthy man in front of their village. They found that he was a stranger to the village, so they asked, "Who is he?" until they reached his nephew. The people of the slain man gathered and accused them of killing him, and the most zealous in the accusation was the slayer, his nephew.

As for His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and when you killed a soul and disputed about it﴾ (ﷺ) — the word "idara'tum" (إدارأتم) comes from "al-dar'" (الدرء), which is the thing when it comes to you and each one repels it from himself. "Idara'tum" means that each of you wants to push the crime away from himself, so each one says, "It is not I."

It is not necessary that anyone accuse someone other than himself. The important thing is that he push it away from himself.

The people of the two villages tried, the village of the slain man and the village in front of which the body was found, each to push the suspicion of the crime away from itself, and perhaps to attribute it to the other. There was no conclusive evidence that favoured a specific accusation. Rather, the evidence was lost, and therefore it was impossible to direct an accusation at one person rather than another, or at one village rather than another.

At that time the legislation stipulated that if a slain person was found at the gate of a village and his killer could not be identified, then the village of the slain man and his people would take fifty men of the notables of the village in whose vicinity the body was found, and they would swear the oath that they did not kill him and did not know his killer. If the notables and leaders were fewer than fifty men, the oaths were repeated until they amounted to fifty oaths, and they swear that they did not kill him nor know his killer, whereupon the public treasury (بيت المال) bears the blood-money (diyah) of the slain man.

But God wanted something else. He wanted to answer the denial of the Children of Israel of the Last Day through this crime, and to make the dead man stand before them and utter the name of his killer, and to let them see the Resurrection while they were alive. Therefore the Exalted, the Glorified, said: ﴿And Allah is the Bringer-forth of what you were concealing﴾. That is, the Children of Israel, or those who committed the crime, planned it so that it would remain in the folds of concealment, and no one would know anything of it. Therefore the young man came and killed his uncle without anyone seeing him. Then he carried the body secretly in the darkness of the night and went out with it, and no one turned to him. Then he went to a neighbouring village, threw the body at its gate while its people were asleep, and returned.

All these steps, in his opinion, would make the crime obscure, never to be uncovered, and its secret known to no one. But God, blessed and exalted, willed otherwise. He willed to expose the crime in a manner that admits no dispute, and at the same time to answer the denial of the Children of Israel of the Resurrection, by showing them the Resurrection while they were alive.

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 73:

﴿So We said: "Strike him with part of it." Thus Allah brings the dead to life, and shows you His signs, that you may understand.﴾

Disagreement broke out among the Children of Israel, and a great strife was nearly provoked. They resolved to turn to Musa (ʿalayhi as-salam) so that he would ask Allah, blessed and exalted is He, to reveal to them the riddle of this crime and to point them to the killer. The command came from Allah, subhanahu wa taʿala, that they should slaughter the cow. Had they slaughtered any cow at all, the problem would have ended. But they kept asking what its color was and what its form was, and so on, as we have related, until they arrived at the cow that the righteous man had entrusted to Allah until his son grew up. So they bought it and slaughtered it. Then Allah commanded them to strike him with part of it, meaning that they were to strike the slain man with a piece of the slaughtered cow after its blood had flowed and it had died.

Consider the greatness within the story: a part of a dead thing is struck against a dead man, and he comes to life. The matter was thus arranged by the Truth in a way that leaves them no room for doubt ever. For if Allah had brought him to life without striking him with a part of the cow, they would have said: "He had not died; there was life in him, and he woke up after a fainting spell." Instead, Allah commanded them to slaughter a cow until it died, to give them a lesson in faith in Allah's power, since they were materialists who believe only in material things. And they were to take a part or parts of it and strike the slain man with it, so that he would come to life, speak the name of his killer, and then Allah would cause him to die again.

The Truth, majestic in His majesty, says: ﴿Thus Allah brings the dead to life, and shows you His signs, that you may understand.﴾ So that the Children of Israel, while still alive, might see how Allah brings the dead to life, and know that a human being does not remain alive by the causes of life, but by the will of the Cause of life, who says: "Be," and it is.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 74:

﴿Then your hearts hardened after that, so that they became like stones, or even harder. For indeed, among stones there are some from which rivers gush forth, and indeed, among them there are some that split open so that water comes out of them, and indeed, among them there are some that fall down out of fear of Allah. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾ (74)

Why did the Exalted say "hearts" and describe them as hardening, and did not say "souls" (nufus)? Because the heart is the seat of tenderness, mercy and compassion. If we make the heart abundant in the remembrance of Allah, it becomes filled with mercy and compassion. The heart is the organ that settles the problems of life. When the heart is inhabited by certainty (yaqin) and faith (iman), every limb (jarihah) carries within it the leaven of faith.

So that we may know the strength, capacity and breadth of the heart's ability to hold faith, Allah, the Exalted, clarified this meaning in His Mighty Book, where He says:

﴿Allah has sent down the best of speech, a Book consistent and repeating.
