The skins shiver therefrom of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whom He wills. And whoever Allah leaves astray – for him there is no guide.﴾ (Surah al-Zumar, 23)

Thus we see that the skins shiver from the terror of the threat of the Fire, and merely from reading what the Qur'an mentions about it. Then comes mercy, and in this state the skins do not merely soften; the hearts must soften too, because they are what give the flash of faith to all the limbs of the body.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart." (1)

So the heart is the source of certainty and the outlet of faith. Just as faith is in the heart, hardness and disbelief are in the heart. When the heart forgets the remembrance of Allah, it hardens. Why? Because it believes there is nothing but this worldly life and nothing but matter, so it tries to obtain from it the utmost it can and by any means. Thus it produces nothing but injustice, tyranny and the seizing of the rights of the weak, and it never lets go of these, because they are the ultimate end of its life, with nothing after them.

It finds a person dying of hunger before it, and does not give him a loaf of bread. When faith leaves the heart, mercy leaves it, and all the faith of the limbs leaves it as well. The flash of faith that is in the hand departs, so the hand reaches out to theft and what is forbidden. The flash of faith that is in the eye departs, so the eye looks at everything Allah has forbidden. The flash of faith that is in the foot departs, so the foot never walks to the mosque, but walks to the tavern and to theft, because, as we said, the heart is the storehouse of faith in the body.

Blessed and Exalted Allah likens the hardness of their hearts when He says: ﴿Then they are like stones, or even harder.﴾ Stones are the hard thing that our senses perceive, familiar to us and familiar to the Children of Israel too, because they had a great experience with stones when they wandered in the desert, when they were thirsty and Moses would strike the rock with his staff for them.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, draws their attention to the fact that their hearts should have been soft and tender even if they were as hard as stones. But their hearts exceeded this hardness, so they did not become as hard as stones, rather they became harder.

But how can hearts be harder than stones? Do not look at the softness of the material of the hearts; look at how they perform their task.

The mountain's hardness is required, because its task is to be a firm, strong stake for the earth. But this hardness is not required of the heart, and is not its task. As for the hearts of the Children of Israel, they are harder than the mountain. What is required of hearts is softness, and what is required of stones is hardness. Every attribute is created for a creature and required for a task. The swallow, for example, is crooked; this crookedness enables it to perform its task in the most perfect manner. So the crookedness of the swallow is straightness for its task. When hearts become corrupt and depart from their task, they become harder than stones, and become the complete opposite of their task.

Then the Truth, Blessed and Exalted, says:

﴿And indeed, among stones there are some from which rivers gush forth, and indeed, among them there are some that split open so that water comes out of them﴾ (part of 74, Surah al-Baqarah).

Here Allah reminds them of the mercy found in stones, which they had witnessed, when Moses struck the rock with the staff and springs gushed forth from it. That is a sensible example they had seen. The Truth, majestic in His majesty, says to them: mercy reaches stones, so rivers gush from them and water comes out of them. And He, glorified, says: ﴿And indeed, among them there are some that fall down out of fear of Allah.﴾

So stones are touched by softness and mercy and water comes out of them. But your hearts, when they harden, are not touched by softness or mercy, so they never soften and never humble themselves. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, sent down the Torah to you and gave you of His bounty, mercy, covering and abundant forgiveness. It was required that your hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah.

But what is the difference between rivers gushing from stones and their splitting so that water comes out of them? When stones gush forth, water comes out of them. We go to the place of water to take what we need. But when rivers gush from them, the water comes to us while we are in our places. There is a difference between a gift you go to and a gift that comes to you. As for the falling of the stone out of fear of Allah, that happened when Allah manifested Himself to the mountain and made it crumble to dust. Read His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble to dust, and Moses fell down unconscious﴾ (part of 143, Surah al-A'raf).

The Exalted reminds them how the mountain, when Allah manifested Himself to it, descended and collapsed out of fear of Allah. Thus He does not give them examples from what happened to others, but gives them examples from what happened to them.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do,﴾ it means: remember that nothing is hidden from Allah, Glorified and Exalted, that He knows everything you know, and that you will meet Him on the Day of Resurrection and will need His mercy and forgiveness. So do not let your hearts harden, lest Allah expel you from His mercy just as your hearts were emptied of His remembrance.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 75:

﴿Do you then hope that they will believe in you, when a group of them used to hear the Word of Allah and then distort it after they had understood it, while they knew?﴾

The Truthful and Exalted One gives us here wisdom, in what He relates to us about the Children of Israel and their stories, because they would have a role with the Muslims in Madinah, then in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), then in al-Masjid al-Aqsa. So He relates to us how they wearied their Prophet and how they disobeyed their Lord, and how they met blessing with disobedience and mercy with denial. And if this has been their stance, O Muhammad, toward Allah and toward their Prophet, then do not hope that they will believe in you or enter into Islam, even though the Torah in their possession calls them to believe in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

These verses carry the greatest consolation for the Noble Messenger, and they demand that he not grieve over the disbelief of the Jews in him, because his duty is only to convey. Yet the eagerness of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that all the people of the earth—Jews, Christians and disbelievers—should believe, does not mean that he had failed to understand his mission. Rather, it means that he perceived the sweetness of the responsibility from his Lord, such that he wanted to guide every creature of Allah on earth. So Allah reassures him and says: do not believe that they will believe in you. And their non-belief does not mean that you are not truthful; their denial of you should not affect you. So do not hope, O Muhammad, that they will believe in you.

What is greed (ṭam')? Greed is the soul's desire for something that is not its right, even if it is beloved to it. The original principle for the rational person is that he should not hope except for what is his right. A person sometimes wants to make his life luxurious and live in affluence, but with the movement of his life as it is. We say to him: if you want to expand your luxury, you must expand the movement of your life; for if you live in luxury relying on the movement of others' lives, you will corrupt the balance of life's movement on earth. In other words, if you want to live a balanced life, live according to the measure of your own life's movement, for if you do otherwise, you steal, bribe and corrupt. So if you have greed, let it be for what you are capable of.

Thus the phrase "Do you then hope" here determines that we should not hope except for what we are able to do. Are we able to make these Jews believe? Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: this is an added matter beyond what you were charged with, because your duty is only to convey, and even if it is beloved to your soul, their conduct toward Allah does not give you hope that you will reach the result you desire.

This verse also contains consolation for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding what he would meet from the Jews, and it gives him the spiritual charge that makes him confront their non-belief with strength and resolve. For he was expecting it, so he would not grieve, nor would his soul be consumed by regrets, because Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, had placed in his soul the anticipation of what would happen from them. So when their conduct came in line with what was anticipated, that would be something the soul could bear.

And the Truthful and Exalted One says: ﴿and a group of them used to hear the Word of Allah﴾. Observe the precision and exactness: "a group of them," not all of them. From this the scholars derived the principle of preserving probability (ṣiyānat al-iḥtimāl), which is avoiding generalization, such that you do not say that they are all like this. You must leave room for the possibility that some person will believe, or will deviate, or will oppose. Here, a group of the People of the Book recognized the qualities of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, from the Torah and the Gospel, and when he was sent, they believed in him; these did not distort the Word of Allah. Had the Qur'an delivered the ruling in general terms, the view of the disbelievers toward Islam would have changed, and they would have said: this religion has said about us that we distorted the Book of Allah, but we did not distort it, and we are awaiting His Messenger. So that ruling would seem imprecise, and something would have to be wrong, because Allah who revealed this Qur'an is not hidden from anything and knows what is in all our hearts. But because the Noble Verse says that a group of them used to hear the Word of Allah and then distort it, the speech is without generalization and applies precisely in every case.

And the Majestic One, may His majesty be exalted, says: ﴿then distort it after they had understood it, while they knew﴾. This is a compound sin: they heard the Word of Allah, understood it, and knew the punishment for disobedience, and then they distorted it. They read it in the Torah and read the description of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, so that they recognized him as they recognize their own sons. Then they distorted the Word of Allah while knowing. Distortion (taḥrīf) means changing the meaning of a word. They used to say "as-sa'm 'alaykum" (death be upon you) instead of "as-salāmu 'alaykum" (peace be upon you). And the matter did not stop at distortion; it went further, to the point that they brought speech of their own and claimed that it was from the Torah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 76:

﴿And when they meet those who have believed, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with one another, they say, "Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you, so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord? Then will you not reason?"﴾ (76)

These are images of the hypocrisy of the Jews. People are divided into three: believers, disbelievers, and hypocrites. The believer is in harmony with himself and with the universe in which he lives. The disbeliever is in harmony with himself but not in harmony with the universe, and the universe curses him. The hypocrite is not in harmony with himself nor with the universe. This verse gives us an image of hypocrisy and how the hypocrite is not in harmony with himself nor with the universe. He says what he does not believe, and inwardly he believes what he does not say. The whole universe curses him, and in the Hereafter he is in the lowest level of the Fire.

This verse resembles a verse we discussed at the beginning of this surah, namely the words of the Exalted:

﴿And when they meet those who have believed, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you; we were only mocking."﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 14)

In the first verse the role belonged to the Jews, and there were hypocrites from among non-Jews, whose devils were from the Jews. Here the role is of the Jews, and the hypocrites are from the Jews. Almighty and Exalted God says: ﴿And when they meet those who have believed, they say, "We believe"﴾. Is belief speech? Belief is certainty in the heart, not words on the tongue. Belief is inferred from conduct, and no person follows the path of the believers out of hypocrisy or show without it appearing. He says "I believe" hypocritically, but his conduct is not the conduct of a believer. Therefore their conduct is what exposes them.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when some of them are alone with others, they say, "Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you?"﴾

And in another surah the Truth says:

﴿And when they meet you, they say, "We believe." But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage.﴾ (part of verse 119, Surah Al 'Imran)

And in Surah al-Ma'idah He, glorified be He, says:

﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe," while they had entered with disbelief and they had left with it.﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah al-Ma'idah)

Here are four images of the hypocrites, all of which involve the display of false belief. In the first verse: ﴿And when they are alone with their devils, they say, "Indeed, we are with you"﴾; in the second: ﴿when some of them are alone with others, they say, "Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you?"﴾; in the third: ﴿they bite their fingertips at you out of rage﴾; and in the fourth: ﴿they had entered with disbelief and they had left with it﴾.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent, the Jews would say to the believers, "This is your prophet; he is present with us in the Torah, and his attributes are such-and-such." At that time the rabbis of the Jews would forbid them from this and say to them: ﴿Do you talk to them about what Allah has opened to you, so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord?⁠﻿ So it seems they knew the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but they wanted to conceal them. What is strange is that they say, "what Allah has opened to you." If this is an opening from Allah, then they have no merit in it; and had Allah willed to open it to them, their hearts would have believed.

His saying, ﴿so that they may argue with you about it before your Lord⁠﻿ indicates that the Jewish hypocrites, the disbelievers, and every creature on earth know that they are created by Allah, and that Allah is the One who created them. And since they know this, why do they disbelieve in their Creator? ﴿So that they may argue with you about it⁠﻿ means that their argument against you would be strong before Allah. But they did not say "before Allah"; they said ﴿before your Lord⁠﻿. And argument (muhaajjah) means that two parties meet, each having a different point of view, and a debate is held between them in which each party presents its proof. Read His saying:

﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship?⁠﻿ (part of verse 258, Surah al-Baqarah)

This is the debate that took place between Abraham (peace be upon him) and Nimrod, to whom Allah had given kingship. What did Abraham say?

﴿When Abraham said, "My Lord is He who gives life and causes death."⁠﻿ (part of verse 258, Surah al-Baqarah)

This was Abraham's argument in calling to Allah, and Nimrod answered him with a false argument. He said, "I give life and cause death." Then he brought one of his soldiers and said to his guards, "Kill him." When they moved toward him, he said, "Release him." Then he turned to Abraham:

﴿He said, "I give life and cause death."⁠﻿ (part of verse 258, Surah al-Baqarah)

A sterile argument, because the one whom Nimrod ordered killed was alive, and his life was from Allah. Nimrod, when he said "kill him," did not cause his death; rather he ordered his killing. And there is a difference between death and killing. Killing is that the structure of the body is destroyed so that the soul leaves it, because it is no longer fit to sustain it. Death is that the soul leaves the body while its structure is sound and not destroyed. The One who causes death is Allah alone, and therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Muhammad is not but a messenger; messengers have passed on before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?⁠﻿ (part of verse 144, Surah Al 'Imran)

And if Nimrod had killed this man, he could not have restored him to life. But Abraham (peace be upon him) did not want to enter into such a sterile debate, in which the contest of proof against proof could allow argument even if false. Therefore he brought the decisive proof which Nimrod could not dispute:

﴿Abraham said, "Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." So the one who disbelieved was overwhelmed. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.⁠﻿ (part of verse 258, Surah al-Baqarah)

This is the meaning of muhaajjah. Each side brings its proof, and since they argue with you before your Lord, and they believe that the matter will not pass before Allah in peace, for He is the Lord of all and will give the oppressed justice against the oppressor. If this is the truth, then are you working for the benefit of yourselves? The answer is no. If you knew what is right, you would not have fallen into this error. So this is not an opening (from Allah).

His saying, ﴿Then will you not reason?⁠﻿ is a logical conclusion of the verse, because one who acts as they act and speaks as they speak does not have reason. Whoever says ﴿they would argue with you before your Lord⁠﻿ believes that he has a Lord, and then does not believe in this God nor fear Him, cannot possibly be characterized by reason.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 77:

﴿Do they not know that Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal?﴾ (77)

Allah makes clear to us that He knows their affair and what they do. They thought that Allah was heedless when some of them withdrew privately to one another and said: ﴿Do you tell them what Allah has disclosed to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord?﴾ Allah knows and hears. And when the hypocrites meet the believers, they say, "We believe," ﴿but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage﴾. This is a bodily reaction; no words are spoken, but there is a reality that is seen. Nevertheless, it is not a secret.

What is the secret and what is the open? The open matter is that which comes out from you to someone who has the faculty of hearing, so that he may hear you. The open matter comes out from you to someone who has the faculty of sight, so that he may see you. If it is a movement without sound, its instrument is the eye; if it is with a sound, its instrument is the ear. These are the original means of perception.

As for His saying, ﴿He knows what they conceal and what they reveal﴾: would it not have been more appropriate for Him, glory be to Him, to say "He knows what they reveal and what they conceal"? And if He knows what we conceal, does He not know what we reveal? Undoubtedly He knows. But this is a precision of Qur'anic eloquence, because the speaker is Allah, glory be to Him.

We know that Allah is Unseen (ghayb), and unseen means hidden from our senses. Since Allah is Unseen, He knows the hidden unseen. Perhaps the apparent open has other laws. For example, if there is a person in the house who says, "I know what is in the house and what is outside the house": if he said "I know what is in the house," we would say to him, "You are inside it, so there is nothing strange in that." But you are hidden from what is outside, so how do you know it?

Since Allah is Unseen, His saying "what they conceal" is closer to His unseenness, while "what they reveal" is what needs pausing over. Do not think that Allah, blessed and exalted, because He is Unseen, knows only what is hidden and concealed. No. He knows the witnessed and the absent. Therefore, the fitting order, since Allah is unseen from our sights and we cannot perceive Him, is that He says "what they conceal" first.

What is the meaning of "what they conceal"? The secret is what you have not whispered to another, because whispering something to another no longer makes it a secret. Rather, the secret is what you keep within yourself and do not whisper to anyone among people. If the secret is what you keep in yourself, then the open is what you proclaim openly. It is open as long as two people have known it. Openness is clear among people and secrecy is hidden among them. When Allah, glory be to Him, informs us that He is Unseen, that does not mean that He knows only the unseen. He knows the secret and the open.

Allah, majestic in His majesty, says in the Noble Qur'an:

﴿He knows the secret and what is more hidden﴾ (Qur'an 20:7).

If the secret is what you conceal within yourself and has a reality inside you, then "what is more hidden" means that Allah knows you will do it before you do it, and He knows it will come from you before it comes from you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 78:

﴿And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Book, except for wishful fancies, and they are only conjecturing.﴾

Almighty Allah continues to speak about the People of the Book. Having explained to us those who said: ﴿Do you speak to them of what Allah has opened to you, so that they may argue with you before your Lord?﴾, He, glorified is He, moved on to another group, those He named the unlettered (ummiyyun).

The most sound statement about the ummi is that he is as his mother bore him, meaning that he knows nothing of the culture and knowledge of existence from the moment he emerged from his mother's womb. Accordingly, the ummi in the absolute sense is one who acquires nothing of the culture of the existence around him, regardless of whether it is said "as his mother bore him", because it is common in societies that those who know are the elite, not the common people. In any case, all the meanings converge in the definition of the ummi.

As for His saying, ﴿And among them are unlettered people﴾, you notice that there were camps of unlettered people who confronted the Islamic call. The first camp was the polytheists in Makkah, and the second camp was the People of the Book in Madinah. The term "People of the Book" applies to the followers of Musa and the followers of the Messiah, but in the Arabian Peninsula there was a negligible number of Christians, and there was a community (of Jews). What is intended by His saying, ﴿And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Book, except for wishful fancies﴾, is the Jews who had a community in Madinah. Since the Truth, glorified is He, said ﴿And among them are unlettered people﴾, this means that there must be among them non-unlettered people. These are the ones about whom Allah's statement in the following verse comes:

﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands﴾ (part of verse 79, surah al-Baqarah).

Here Allah, blessed and exalted is He, divided the Jews into categories. Among them is a category of unlettered people who do not know the Book, and what their rabbis tell them is all they know. Had these people known what is in the Torah of the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they would have believed in him. Here "the Book" refers to the Torah. Allah, glorified is He, did not negate from them knowledge altogether, but He negated the distinction of knowledge, for He said they do not know except wishful fancies, as if they know those fancies from the Book.

But what are the amani (wishful fancies)? They are pronounced once without shaddah on the ya' and once with shaddah on the ya'. If it is without shaddah, it is the plural of umniyyah (amniyyah); if it is with shaddah, it is the plural of umniyyah with shaddah on the ya'. You find the word umniyyah in the Noble Qur'an in His saying:

﴿It is not by your wishful fancies, nor by the wishful fancies of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ (part of verse 123, surah al-Nisa').

This is regarding the plural. As for the singular, in His saying:

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished (tamanna), Satan threw into his wish (umniyyatihi)﴾ (part of verse 52, surah al-Hajj).

What is the umniyyah? The umniyyah is a thing that a person loves to happen, but its occurrence is impossible. So it will not happen and will have no existence. Therefore they said that among the meanings of tamanni is the fabrication of things. The poet who said: "Oh, would that youth would return one day, so that I might tell it what old age has done", is it possible for youth to return? Of course it is impossible; this is something that will not happen. And the poet who said: "Would that the stars would draw near to me, so that I might string them as a necklace of praise for you, and my pleasure would not be in your words", will the stars descend from the sky and come to this poet, so that he may string them as verses of poetry to his beloved? So among the meanings of tamanni is lying and fabrication.

Some orientalists have interpreted the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished (tamanna)﴾ (i.e., recited): ﴿Satan threw into his wish﴾ (i.e., into his recitation). Of course Satan would not throw into the recitation of the Messenger anything but lies, slander and disbelief. Read His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Is for you the male and for Him the female? That, then, is an unjust division.﴾ (surah al-Najm).

The enemies of Islam said: since the names of the gharaniq have been mentioned in the Qur'an, and they are the idols that the disbelievers used to worship, among them al-Lat and al-'Uzza and Manat the third, the other, then the intercession of these idols is hoped for in the Hereafter. This is a statement that does not agree with the logic of the whole religion, which calls to worship Allah alone. The orientalists concluded from this that the religion indeed calls to worship Allah alone, and so Satan must have thrown into the wish of what the Messenger of Allah said. Then Allah, glorified is He, made His verses firm, saying:

﴿They are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ (part of verse 23, surah al-Najm).

They intend by this to cast doubt on the possibility that Satan could throw some of his ideas into the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But Allah, glorified is He, abrogates what Satan throws and makes His verses firm.

Indeed, Allah, majestic is His majesty, has not left His revelation to the play of Satan. Therefore we will examine the verse away from everything that has been said. We say: if you pay attention to the saying of Allah, ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished﴾, if we say tamanna means "recited", then Allah abrogates what Satan throws, then Allah makes His verses firm. So He, glorified is He, will not leave His Messenger to err. By this we have established that everything the Messenger arrives at is correct, and that everything that has reached us from the Messenger is firm. So we are reassured that there is nothing Satan could throw into the wish of the Messenger that reaches us without being abrogated.

If we say: Allah abrogates what Satan throws, then what made you know what Satan threw, since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told you only what is firm? Then who is the Messenger? A human being to whom a method was revealed from heaven and who was commanded to convey it. And who is the Prophet? A human being to whom a method was revealed but who was not commanded to convey it. Since he was not commanded to convey it, it is specific to that Prophet, and the Prophet is a behavioral exemplar, because he applies the method of the Messenger before him, so he has brought nothing new.

The noble verse uses the two words messenger or prophet. If the meaning of Satan's wish is correct regarding the Messenger, it is not correct regarding the Prophet, because the Prophet does not recite anything. Since the Prophet is mentioned in the noble verse, tamanni must have a meaning other than recitation, because the Prophet did not bring words to recite to the people. It is as if he would recite firm speech in which there is no wish of Satan, that is, his recitation. Tamanni does not come with the meaning of Satan's recitation. The wish of the Messenger and the Prophet is that they succeed in their mission: the Messenger as a conveyor of the method of Allah, the Prophet as a behavioral exemplar. The meaning here differs: the Messenger's wish is that the method of Allah be conveyed, and Satan tries to pull the method out of people's hearts. This is the meaning. And Allah, glorified is He, when He makes His verses firm, supports faith so that the method of Allah prevails on earth and people's movement is organized. This is the meaning.

The word tamanni in this noble verse means that the Messenger or Prophet loves that his method prevail on earth, and Satan throws up obstacles, and Allah makes His verses firm and supports the truth. The verse must be understood in this sense. Thereby what the orientalists claim is completely negated, namely that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was reciting what was revealed to him, Satan could intervene and put words into the revelation. Impossible.

As for His saying, ﴿And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Book, except for wishful fancies﴾, its meaning is that there come people who know nothing of the Book except by conjecture, so these unlettered people believe them without knowledge. Allah, glorified is He, wanted to draw our attention to the fact that many religious schools of thought on earth arise from those who convey them. There are people who entrust others to tell them what the religious rulings have concluded, so the unlettered or uneducated person asks a scholar about a ruling of the legal rulings, then takes the ruling from him and applies it without debating it, because his knowledge ends at asking for the fatwa. The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ (part of verse 164, surah al-An'am).

That is, no one carries another's sin on the Day of Resurrection. Then He says:

﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ (part of verse 25, surah al-Nahl).

Some people think the two verses contradict each other. We say no. Whoever commits a sin is held accountable for it. And whoever misleads others with an incorrect fatwa, by which he makes lawful what Allah has forbidden, bears his own sins and the sins of the one he misled. So he has a burden because he went astray, and a burden because he led another astray. Moreover, more than that.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, without that diminishing their rewards in any way; and whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing their sins in any way." (1)

We must be alert to the gravity of issuing fatwas in religion without knowledge. The worst a worldly fatwa can lead to is that it makes you lose a deal, but a fatwa in religion will last a long time.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿They are only conjecturing﴾, and conjecture, as we have said, is a probability that is not certain. If tamanni, as it occurs in the language, means recitation, then these unlettered people know the Book only as reading of the tongue without understanding. Therefore Allah, glorified is He, said about the Jews:

﴿The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not bear it is like that of a donkey carrying books﴾ (part of verse 5, surah al-Jumu'ah).

Thus we see that there is a category that carries the Torah while knowing nothing of it. Allah, majestic is His majesty, said its likeness is that of a donkey, but worse than a donkey, because the donkey's task is to carry loads, whereas a human's task is not to carry what he does not understand, but rather he must read the Book and know what is required of him.

1 (Narrated by Ahmad and Muslim from Abu Hurairah).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 79:

﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands, then say, "This is from Allah," that they may trade it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn.﴾ (79)

This noble verse comes concerning the second category of the Jews, the counterpart of the Ummiyyun (the unlettered). They are either unlettered people who do not know the Scripture, or they know it but alter it, writing it with their own hands and saying, "This is from Allah." For this reason, Allah, blessed and exalted, threatened them, saying, "Woe to them," and the verse began directly with the threat of recompense.

We note that the word "wayl" (woe) in the language is used together with "wayh" and "ways," and all of them mean destruction and punishment, and they are used to express regret over a person's heedlessness of the punishment. Read His saying, exalted be He:

﴿O woe to us! What is this Book that leaves out nothing small or great but has enumerated it!﴾ (Part of verse 49, Surah al-Kahf)

And His saying, majestic is His majesty:

﴿O woe to us! We were in heedlessness of this.﴾ (Part of verse 97, Surah al-Anbiya)

These cries of woe express regret at the time of seeing the punishment. It is said that "wayl" is a valley in Hell into which a person plunges for forty autumns, and we seek refuge in Allah. The Truth, blessed and exalted, warns those who write the Scripture with their own hands that their punishment on the Day of Resurrection will be multiplied, because everyone who commits a sin as a result of their distortion of the Scripture will be their partners and will carry their punishment with them on the Day of Resurrection, and their punishment will be multiplied many times over.

Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands.﴾ Would it not have been sufficient for Him to say, "Woe to those who write the Scripture," and the meaning would be understood? Write the Scripture with what? With their hands. We say: No. This is because the act may be accomplished by command and may be accomplished by doing. The head of state, for example, calls one of his ministers and says to him, "Did I not write to you a letter about such-and-such? Why did you not carry it out?" He did not write this letter with his own hand, but they wrote it by his command, and heads of state rarely write letters with their own hands.

Allah, glorified and exalted, wishes here to show us the extent to which these people deliberately commit sin. They are not content, for example, merely to tell others, "Write." Rather, out of their concern to falsify and distort the words of Allah, glorified be He, they do it with their own hands, to make certain that the matter has been done exactly as they wish. So it is not a passing whim, but is with premeditation and deliberate planning. By this they wish to buy "a small price," which is money, or what is called temporal authority: they rule, and they have influence and dominion.

In the past, when the People of the Book disagreed about something, they would go to the priests, monks and others to judge between them. Why? Because when people disagree, they want to shelter behind something that preserves their pride if they are mistaken. That is, "I will not be defeated before him, nor will he be defeated before me," but rather they say, "We have accepted the judgment of so-and-so." So if we were to resort to the legislation of heaven to judge between us, there would be no victor and vanquished, or defeated and triumphant. When you and I submit to the judgment of Allah, each of us is content with the outcome of that judgment.

But the rabbis of the Jews and the clergy of the Christians began to issue contradictory rulings, each according to his own interest and desire. Therefore the judgments in similar cases conflicted, because judgment was no longer by justice; rather, judgment became subject to the desires, interests and affairs of men. When they write the Scripture with their own hands and say, "This is from Allah," they only want to bestow upon what is written a sanctity that makes a person accept it without discussion. In this way they become the legislators in the name of Allah, writing what they want and recording it in writing. When the People of the Book sensed the conflict in the rulings of religion caused by what the monks and rabbis had added, they began to demand the liberation of judgment from the authority of the Church.

But why do these people write the Scripture with their own hands and say, "This is from Allah"? The Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿that they may trade it for a small price.﴾ We have said that a person does not buy the price; rather he pays the price and buys the goods. But here you pay in order to receive a price: you give up the method and judgment of Allah, changing and altering it, to take a temporary price. Allah, glorified be He, gives you in the Hereafter, but you sell it for little. Every price, however great it is, that you take in exchange for the method of Allah is considered a small price.

And the Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written.﴾ The noble verse began with His saying: ﴿So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands.﴾ Then came His saying: ﴿So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn.﴾ So at the moment of writing there is woe and punishment; at the moment of selling the bargain there is woe and punishment; and what they earn is woe and punishment.

This matter spread in the writing of indulgence certificates which were sold in the churches to whoever paid more. The Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And woe to them for what they earn.﴾ The word "kasb" (earning) indicates an action of your limbs that brings you good or benefit. There is "kasaba" and there is "iktasaba": "kasaba" brings a beneficial thing, and "iktasaba" brings a harmful thing. But in this noble verse the Truth, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿And woe to them for what they earn,﴾ and in another verse He said: ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed (kasaba sayyi'atan).﴾

Why was this usage employed? We say that this is not natural earning; rather it is an artificial effort in earning, that is, acquisition (iktisab). We must understand that with regard to the limbs of a person, there is speech, action and work. Some people believe that there is only speech and work. We say no: there is speech, which is the work of the tongue; there is action, which is the work of the other limbs besides the tongue; and there is work, which is when speech agrees with action. Therefore Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Greatly hateful in the sight of Allah is that you say what you do not do.﴾ (Surah al-Saff)

So there is speech, action and work. When a person uses his limbs properly, he does what is suitable for him. But if he moves from what is suitable to what is unsuitable, to what angers Allah, then his limbs do not act naturally but contrive; their faculties collide with one another. A person who opens his safe to take from his own money is at ease and fears nothing; but a person who opens someone else's safe is anxious, and all his conduct is contrived. A person with his wife is in harmony in a natural condition, unlike when he is in a contrary situation. It is a state of contrivance. Everyone who earns something unlawful contrives it, and therefore it is said of him that he "iktasaba." Except when he becomes hardened and the unlawful no longer disturbs him, or those we call habitual criminals: in this case he does the thing without contrivance, because he has become accustomed to it. Those who have reached the point where they write with their own hands and say it is from Allah, sin no longer disturbs them, and therefore Allah threatened them with punishment twice in a single verse.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 80:

﴿And they say, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days." Say, "Have you taken a covenant with Allah, so that Allah will not break His covenant? Or do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"﴾

Here Allah, glorified and exalted, exposes the thinking of these people. Satan has made falsehood appear attractive to them, so that they believe they have actually gained, that they have taken worldly wealth and status and achieved success with it, because they will be punished in the Hereafter only with a light, brief punishment. For this reason Allah, blessed and exalted, exposes what they say to one another. What did they say? ﴿They said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days."﴾

Al-massu (المس) means a light touch, or something coming close to something else. Yet neither of the two perceives the other except with a faint perception that is barely noticed. If you come to a person and place your fingertips on his hand, it is said that you "touched" (massastu), but through this mere touch you cannot sense the warmth of his hand or the softness of his skin. Real contact (al-lams), however, gives you a sensation of what you touch. ﴿They said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days."﴾ Thus they took the very least of the punishment, and then the very least of the time, saying "a few counted days." Something that is said to be "counted" (ma'dud) is few; whereas that which cannot be counted is many. For this reason, when Allah speaks of His blessings, He says, glorified is He: ﴿And if you should count the favour of Allah, you could not enumerate them.﴾ (part of verse 18, Surat an-Nahl). The very act of setting out to count implies that the thing can be counted. If it were not possible, no one would set out to count it, and we do not see anyone attempting to count the grains of sand or the drops of water in the seas. The blessings of Allah, glorified and exalted, both manifest and hidden, cannot be counted, and therefore no one sets out to enumerate them. When you hear the phrase "counted days," know that it means a few days. For this reason we see in Surat Yusuf the words of the Truth, exalted is His majesty:

﴿And they sold him for a low price, a few counted dirhams.﴾ (part of verse 20, Surat Yusuf).

Their saying "The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days" is evidence of their stupidity, because the duration of a touch is nothing but a moment. Rather, these are wishful fancies which Satan placed in their minds, so that the reply from Allah would come in His words, glorified is He: ﴿Say, "Have you taken a covenant with Allah, so that Allah will not break His covenant?"﴾ Meaning: if that is a promise from Allah, then Allah does not break His promise. Allah commands His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to say to them: you are not the ones who judge or decide what Allah, glorified and exalted, will do to you. Rather, it is He, exalted is His majesty, who judges. So if He has given you a covenant, Allah does not break His covenant.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do you say about Allah that which you do not know?﴾ Here is the courtesy of prophethood and the magnificent character of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Instead of saying, "Do you fabricate lies against Allah? Or do you lie about Allah? Or do you invent about Allah what He has not said?", He said: ﴿Or do you say about Allah that which you do not know?﴾ The one who fabricates speech knows that he is fabricating. He is the first to know the falsehood of what he says. He may have an argument and convince those before him so that they believe him, but he still knows that what he said is invented, even though they believed him. For this reason the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, says: "I am only a human being, and you bring disputes to me. Perhaps one of you is more eloquent in his argument than another, and I judge for him according to what I hear. So whoever I award something of the right of a Muslim, it is only a piece of the Fire, so let him take it or leave it" (1).

Thus the one who invents a thing knows that it is invented. And these Jews are the first to know that their saying, ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days,﴾ is an invention. But to whom do they say about Allah what is a slander and a lie? They say it to the unlettered (al-ummiyyin) who do not know the Book.

1 (Narrated by Malik, Ahmad, al-Bukhari and Muslim).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 81:

﴿Nay, whoever earns an evil deed and his sin has encompassed him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ (2:81)

God, glorified and exalted be He, wanted to make clear their lie. So the Qur'an came saying: ﴿Nay﴾ (bala). It is a particle of response, exactly like "na'am" (yes), but "bala" is a response particle used in negation. That is, it negates what came before it. They said: "The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days," and the Messenger of God asked them: "Have you taken a covenant with God, or do you say about God what you do not know?" Then the Qur'an came to say: ﴿Nay, whoever earns an evil deed and his sin has encompassed him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ The beginning of the answer with "bala" negates what they said, because "bala" comes after a negation, while "na'am" comes after an affirmative answer. If a person says, "You have nothing with me," and you say "na'am," its meaning is that it is true that you have nothing with me. But if you say "bala," that means you have something or things with me. Therefore, after their saying ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days﴾, had "na'am" come after it, their statement would have been true; but "bala" negated it, and the speech that followed it confirmed the negation:

﴿whoever earns an evil deed and his sin has encompassed him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ They said the Fire would not touch them; He said that it would not merely touch you, but you would abide in it eternally. God's words ﴿companions of the Fire﴾: companionship requires a kind of attachment, in which there is a pull between the two companions. This means there will be a pull between them and the Fire.

Here we observe that the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, said ﴿earns (kasaba) an evil deed﴾, whereas the context would call for "iktasaba" (acquires). But because they thought they had earned it, as we explained in the previous verse. As for His words ﴿and his sin has encompassed him﴾: encompassing in such a way that there is no outlet for escaping from the sin, because it surrounds him. The most suitable interpretation of His words ﴿earns an evil deed and his sin has encompassed him﴾ is that what is meant is shirk (associating partners with God), because shirk is what encompasses a person and there is no forgiveness for it. God, exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.﴾ (part of 4:48, Surat al-Nisa').

Therefore, these people were not merely disobedient; rather they were disbelievers and polytheists. The proof is His words ﴿they will abide therein eternally﴾. Those who commit minor or major sins and repent from them do not abide eternally in the Fire; but the one who associates partners with God and disbelieves in Him is the one who abides eternally in the Fire. Every person who does not believe in our master Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a disbeliever, because God, glorified and exalted be He, said:

﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers.﴾ (85) (Surat Al 'Imran).

Therefore, I have said there is a difference between the person who commits a sin because he cannot control himself, then regrets and repents, and the person who rejoices in sin. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon God for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon after.﴾ (part of 4:17, Surat al-Nisa').

There is the one who regrets the sin, and for him there is repentance; and there is the one who rejoices in sin, and this one increases in sin.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 82:

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds - they are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide forever.﴾

When Allah, glorified and exalted, mentions in the Noble Qur'an the punishment and the Fire, He follows it with its counterpart, which is the bliss and the Garden. This is because comparison shows us the difference and gives the believer a feeling of happiness, because he has been drawn away from the punishment of the Hereafter. And that is not all: he has entered the Garden to abide forever in bliss. For this reason, Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into the Garden has indeed triumphed﴾ (part of verse 185, Surah Al ʿImran).

So, success in the Hereafter is not of one degree but of two degrees. The first degree of success is that a person is drawn away from the Fire, even if only as far as al-A'raf, and this is a great success. It is enough that you pass over the Sirat (bridge) laid over the Fire and see the various kinds of punishment in it, and then after that you are saved from all this terror. That alone is enough to be a great success, because the disbeliever at this moment wishes he were dust so that he would not enter the Fire. So the believer's passing over the Sirat and seeing the Fire is a blessing, because he feels what he has been saved from. Then, if he passes beyond the Fire and enters the Garden to enjoy everlasting bliss, that is another success. For this reason, Allah, blessed and exalted, was keen to give us both stages. He did not say: "Whoever is drawn away from the Fire has succeeded," nor "Whoever is admitted into the Garden has succeeded," but He said ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into the Garden has indeed triumphed﴾. This noble verse came after the verses about punishment to give us the comparison.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 83:

﴿And when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel: "Worship none but Allah, and be good to parents and to near relatives and orphans and the needy, and speak to people good words, and establish prayer and give zakat." Then you turned away, except for a few of you, and you were averse.﴾ (2:83)

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, took eight things from the Children of Israel. The first is the mithaq (covenant), which is the firmly tied pact, bound with precision. It is the covenant of fitrah (innate nature) or the covenant of the dhar (the seed of Adam), in confirmation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves, "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we testify."﴾ (7:172)

There is another covenant that Allah, exalted is He, took from all His messengers: that they should give good news of the mission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that they should ask their followers to believe in him when he is sent, or that they should not conceal what is in their scriptures and should not alter it. The mithaq is everything in which there is an obligation from Allah. That is because you enter into a contract of faith with Allah, exalted is He, that He will do what He commands and you will leave what He has forbidden. This is the mithaq.

The word mithaq appears in the Noble Qur'an with a heavy description, in the relationship between a man and a woman. Allah, exalted is He, says:

﴿And if you wish to replace one wife with another, and you have given one of them a great amount, do not take anything from it. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin? And how could you take it when you have gone in to one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?﴾ (4:20-21)

We say yes, because this mithaq makes lawful for the woman things that are not lawful except through it: things that are not lawful for her father, or her brother, or any person other than her husband. When a man enters upon his daughter and her leg is uncovered, he hurries to cover it. But if her husband enters upon her, there is nothing wrong. So it is a heavy covenant, because it enters the areas of nakedness (awrah) and makes the awrah permissible for the husband and wife. For this reason the Blessed and Exalted Truth says:

﴿They are garments for you and you are garments for them.﴾ (2:187)

Each of them covers, conceals and shields the awrah of the other. A father is not made happy by the transfer of his daughter's guardianship to someone else, except that the transfer of this guardianship is to her husband. He feels anxious when the girl grows up and is not married.

The Truth says: ﴿And when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel: "Worship none but Allah"﴾. This covenant included three conditions: ﴿Worship none but Allah﴾, meaning you worship Allah alone, and you believe in the Torah and in Moses as a prophet. Why? Because worshipping Allah alone is the peak of faith. But you do not determine the method of His worship, exalted is He. Rather, it is the One worshipped who determines the method of worship, not the worshipper. You must adopt the method revealed by Allah, which is the Torah, and believe in it. Then, after that, you believe in Moses as a prophet, because he is the one to whom the Torah was revealed, and he is the one who will explain to you the path of correct worship. Without these three conditions, the worship of the Children of Israel is not sound.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and be good to parents﴾, because they are the direct cause of your existence. They raised you when you were small, and they cared for you. His saying: ﴿good (ihsan)﴾ means more than what is obligatory. This is because you may perform a thing only to the extent required of you. The one who performs the prayer, for example, merely to the required extent has indeed fulfilled it. But the one who performs supererogatory prayers and stands in the night prayer has entered the realm of ihsan (excellence), meaning that his giving exceeds what is obligatory. Allah, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good. They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness, and in their wealth there was a right for the one who asks and the deprived.﴾ (51:15-19)

Thus we see that ihsan is more than what is obligatory: in prayer, in glorification (tasbih), and in charity. Allah, blessed and exalted, wants you to give to your parents more than what is required of you or obligatory upon you.

His saying: ﴿and near relatives﴾. Allah determines for us here the second rank with respect to ihsan. Allah, majestic in His majesty, has enjoined upon us to be good to our parents and to care for our relatives. If each one of us did this, no one in society would be found who is in need, poor, or destitute. Allah wants a society with no poverty and no spite. This cannot be achieved except through mercy and ihsan toward parents and relatives, so that every needy person in society has someone who sponsors him.

Allah, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and orphans﴾. The orphan is one who has lost his father while still a child who has not reached the stage of manhood. This applies to humans. As for animals, the orphan is one who has lost his mother, because in animals motherhood means staying with the young, and because the father is not known in animals but the mother is known. The orphan who has lost his father has lost the one who supports him, the one who strives for him, and the one who defends him. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted is He, made the mother the one who raises and cares, and the father the one who struggles to provide the family's needs. But the situation has now reversed, and for this reason Shawqi, may Allah have mercy on him, says:

"The orphan is not the one whose parents have both departed from life and left him humbled,
Rather, the orphan is the one for whom no mother has attended, nor a father who is occupied."

The orphan becomes broken because he has lost his father, and so he has no helper. If we see in the Islamic society that every orphan is cared for with the care of a father by all the men of society, that makes a father not fear to leave his son after his death. Thus society's care for the orphan first guarantees the protection of his right, because if he is an orphan and has wealth, all people covet his wealth, since he cannot protect it. This is the first point. The second is that this mutual solidarity removes spite from society and makes every person content about his children.

His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿and the needy (masakin)﴾. In the past we used to say that the masakin are those who own nothing at all with which to sustain their lives, until the noble verse in Surat al-Kahf was revealed:

﴿As for the boat, it belonged to needy people who worked on the sea.﴾ (18:79)

So we learned that the miskin may own something, but he does not own what suffices him. This is a kind of social solidarity that must exist in society so that the whole society is mutually supportive. If you are poor or needy, and something comes to you from a rich man that helps you in your life, you will wish good for him, because that good reaches you. But if this rich man gives you nothing, he grows richer while you grow poorer, and the result is that his spite toward you increases.

The Truth, exalted is He, says: ﴿and speak to people good words (husna)﴾. The word husna with a damma on the ha' is used in the sense of hasan with a fatha on the ha'. The hasan is what the Shari'ah has deemed good. Scholars have differed: is the hasan what the Shari'ah deems good, or what reason deems good? We say: what reason deems good, in matters where no text from the Shari'ah's approval exists, because reason may differ regarding one and the same thing. This one considers it good and that one considers it ugly. Allah, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a manner that is best.﴾ (16:125)

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and speak to people good words﴾. Then came His saying, majestic in His majesty: ﴿and establish prayer (salat)﴾. We have discussed the meaning of establishing prayer and what makes it acceptable to Allah. There is a difference between your saying "pray" and your saying "establish prayer". "Establish prayer" means: pray, but a prayer at the level that is demanded of you. And establishing the prayer, as we have said, is the pillar that never falls away from a person.

The Truth says: ﴿and give zakat﴾. Regarding zakat: when Allah, glory be to Him, says ﴿and near relatives, orphans and the needy﴾, we say that relatives, orphans and the needy have a right in zakat as long as they are poor. So that all of us may feel that we live in a complete, faithful environment, in which each of us tries to help the other. Zakat is essentially given to the poor even if he is not an orphan or a relative. For every poor person has rights and care. If there are poor relatives or orphans, they have two rights: the right of kinship and the right of poverty. And if he is an orphan, he has the right of the orphan and the right of the poor.

After the Truth, exalted is He, mentioned the eight elements of the covenant, He said: ﴿Then you turned away (tawallaytum)﴾. Tawalla means: turned away, or did not obey, or did not listen. Allah, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Then you turned away, except for a few of you, and you were averse.﴾ This is the actual history of the Children of Israel, because some of them turned away and did not obey the covenant, and some of them obeyed.

The Qur'an did not launch a campaign against the Jews; rather, it launched a campaign against those among them who opposed. For this reason it respected reality and said: ﴿except for a few﴾. This is what is called, with respect to human beings, the law of preserving possibility (qanun siyanat al-ihtimal).

The Truth, majestic in His majesty, speaks with the fairness of the Creator toward the created. Therefore He did not say "then you turned away" but said "except for a few". "Tawallaytum" means "you were averse", but Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Then you turned away, except for a few of you, and you were averse.﴾ We want to take the precision of expression. If we want to explain tawalla, its meaning is: turned away, or rejected the command. But if we look at the Qur'an carefully, we find that when a believer meets an unbeliever in battle, Allah, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Whoever turns his back to them on that day, unless he is maneuvering for battle or joining another company, has indeed earned anger from Allah.﴾ (8:16)

So tawalli is turning away, and the Truth, exalted is He, in this noble verse shows us that turning away occurs with different intentions. The fighter on the day of battle turns away, not with the intention of fleeing the battle, but with the intention of going to fight in another place or to help his brothers whom the enemies have overwhelmed. This is turning away, but not with the intention of fleeing the battle; rather, with the intention of fighting in a manner more suitable for victory.

Suppose a man owes you money, and you see him coming down the road, so you turn away from him. You did not turn away from him out of hatred, but out of mercy, because you do not want to touch his dignity. So there is a turning or aversion that is not with the intention of aversion. Allah, glory be to Him, wants to draw our attention to the fact that these Jews turned away with the intention of aversion, and did not turn away with any other intention. That is, they turned away while deliberately intending to turn away, and for no other purpose.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 84:

﴿And when We took your covenant: "You shall not shed your blood, nor expel yourselves from your homes." Then you acknowledged it, while you were witnessing.﴾ (84)

We have said that "idh" (when) here means "remember," and that the covenant (mithaq) is the solemn, binding pledge. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿You shall not shed your blood﴾: Allah, blessed and exalted, had already mentioned in the covenant the worship of Allah alone, ﴿and to parents, kindness, and to kinsfolk, orphans, and the needy﴾, ﴿and speak to people good words, and establish the prayer﴾, and so on to the end of what came in the noble verse. All of these are commands, meaning, all of them are "do." They are part of completing the covenant. Allah says in this noble verse what you do not do. Worship, as we have said, is obeying the commands and refraining from the prohibitions, or what the covenant forbade:

﴿You shall not shed your blood﴾, meaning: no one of you should shed the blood of his brother; some of you should not shed the blood of others. But why did Allah say ﴿your blood﴾? Because after it He says ﴿nor expel yourselves from your homes﴾. The law of faith addresses the community of believers as one unit.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the believers in their mutual love, compassion and mercy is like the likeness of a single body: when one of its limbs complains, the rest of the body responds to it with wakefulness and fever." (1)

So the community of faith is as one unity. And Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿So when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from Allah, blessed and good﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah an-Nur).

But if I am the one entering, how can I greet myself? It is as though Allah is addressing the believers on the basis that they are one unit. On this basis He, glorified, says: ﴿You shall not shed your blood﴾, meaning: do not kill yourselves. "Safk" (shedding) means the pouring out of blood. "Dima'" (blood) is the fluid present in the body that is necessary for life. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿nor expel yourselves from your homes﴾ means: none of you should expel another from his home.

Then He linked the believers among the Children of Israel with His saying: ﴿Then you acknowledged it, while you were witnessing.﴾ "Aqrartum" means you confessed. ﴿While you were witnessing﴾: testimony (shahadah) is the reporting of what one has witnessed. A judge questions witnesses because they saw the incident, so they relate what they observed. When you relate what you have witnessed, it is as though those who heard it have made what occurred a matter witnessed and actual for them, whereas the false witness alters the facts.

Allah, the Truthful, exalted is He, addresses the Jews contemporary with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), reminding them of what their earliest forefathers did and their stance regarding the taking of the covenant when the Mount of Tur was lifted above them, a matter that is well known. The Qur'an wants to say to them: you altered and changed in matters you know. What came in accordance with your desires, you implemented; what did not come in accordance with your desires, you did not implement.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 85:

﴿Then you are those who kill yourselves, and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting [their enemies] against them in sin and aggression. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, while their expulsion was forbidden to you. Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part? So what is the recompense for those of you who do that except disgrace in worldly life; and on the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the severest punishment. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾ (85)

The Truth, exalted is He, addresses the Jews to expose them, because they applied from the Torah what suited their desires, and did not apply what did not please them. He says to them: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ He reminds them that they agreed to the covenant and acknowledged it.

This verse was revealed when a Jewish woman committed adultery, and they wanted not to carry out the prescribed punishment upon her by stoning. They said: "Let us go to Muhammad," thinking that he would exempt them from the punishment found in their Book, or that he did not know what was in their Book. When they went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he told them: "This ruling is present with you in the Torah." They said: "In our Torah it is that the face of the adulterer and the adulteress is smeared with filth and they are paraded among the people." The Messenger of Allah said to them: "No. The verse of stoning is present with you in the Torah. Leave." So it was as though, when they supposed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would lighten one of the prescribed punishments of Allah, they went to him to ask his ruling.

The Truth, exalted is He and Most High, says: ﴿Then you are those who kill yourselves﴾. That is, after the covenant was taken from you that you would not do so, you kill yourselves. One of you kills another, or the one who kills will himself be killed, so it is as though he killed himself. The Truth, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then you are those who kill yourselves﴾. Why did He use this phrase "you are those" (ha'ulaa')? Because it is a signal to alert us, so that we turn our attention to the ruling.

And His saying: ﴿and expel a party of you from their homes﴾, and He warned them by His saying: ﴿and do not expel yourselves from your homes﴾ (2:84). This came in the covenant. What is the ruling to which the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wants to draw our attention? We say: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emigrated to Medina, he moved from a house of polytheism to a house of faith. The meaning of "house of faith" is that there were believers who had preceded him. There were people of Medina who had believed. The Muslims had emigrated before that to Abyssinia, but that was an emigration to a house of safety and not a house of faith. But when the Pledge of al-'Aqaba took place, and a group came from Medina and pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and believed in him, the Messenger sent with them Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr to teach them their religion. The emigration of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, came upon an existing leaven of faith. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, he spoiled the Jews' plan for their lives. The Jews were represented by the Banu Qaynuqa', the Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qurayza. In Medina there were the Aws and the Khazraj, and between them there were constant wars before Islam came. The Jews divided themselves into a group with the Aws and a group with the Khazraj, so as to ensure the enmity continued. Whenever the fighting calmed, they incited one of the two camps against the other so that fighting would resume anew. They remained so until now, and this is their nature.

The one who created communism is a Jew, and the one who created capitalism is a Jew. The one who stirs enmity between the two camps is a Jew. The Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qaynuqa' were with the Khazraj, and the Banu Qurayza were with the Aws. When the Aws and the Khazraj clashed, each of them had Jewish allies. When the battle ended, what used to happen? The captives of the Banu al-Nadir and the Banu Qaynuqa' would be helped by the Banu Qurayza to free them, even though they were the ones who caused this capture. If the Aws won and took captives from the Khazraj and their Jewish allies, the Jews would come and work to release the Jewish captives, because they had a text saying that whenever a captive from the Children of Israel is found, his capture must be ransomed.

The Truth, exalted is He, says to them: your deeds, in that you fight one another and shed your blood, do not accord with the covenant that Allah took from you, but are rather worldly interests. ﴿You kill yourselves﴾ and Allah forbade you this: ﴿and expel a party of you from their homes﴾, and Allah forbade you this: ﴿supporting [their enemies] against them in sin and aggression. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, while their expulsion was forbidden to you.﴾ This is what used to happen in Medina in the wars between the Aws and the Khazraj, as we have explained. The word "asara" (captives) is the plural of "asir" (captive), and it is irregular, because the analogical plural would be "asra."  That is why we see in another verse the saying of Allah, exalted is He:

﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted slaughter upon the land﴾ (part of verse 67, Surat al-Anfal).

But the Qur'an used "asara." Language sometimes comes in a form other than what its analogy requires, to draw your attention to some meaning. Thus "kaslan" (lazy) becomes "kasala" (plural). The "kasala" are those whose movement is low. The captive too: you have restricted his movement. So the plural "asara" for "asir" is a sign of the restriction of movement, like "kasala." The Noble Qur'an came with "asara" and "asra," but when it used "asara," it wanted to draw our attention to the restriction of movement, like "kasala." The existence of "asra" means a war has occurred, a war that requires encounter and close combat, and each one wants to kill his enemy.

This word "asr" (capture) was taken in order to calm the frenzy of the encounter. So it is as if Allah wanted to protect the people from the ferocity of their souls at the time of war, and so He said to them: take them captive. Do not kill them unless you are compelled to kill. But take them captive, and in this there is an interest for you, because you will take ransom from them. This is one of the legislations of mercy, because if capture were not permitted, then whenever two fighters met, one of them would have to kill the other. Therefore it is said: take him captive, unless his presence is a danger to your life.

And the saying of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, while their expulsion was forbidden to you.﴾ Each group of Jews was with its ally from the Aws or the Khazraj, and it would expel the defeated from his homes and take the homes. After the war ended, they would ransom them, that is, take ransom from them to return to them their homes and children.

Why do the Jews divide themselves in this way? It is not a faith-based division, but a division of worldly interest. Why? Because it is not reasonable, while you are People of the Book, that you divide yourselves into a group with the Aws and a group with the Khazraj, and there be among you sin and aggression.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿supporting [their enemies] against them in sin and aggression﴾. "Tuzahiruna 'alayhim" means you cooperate against them, while you are people of one religion. "Bil-ithm" (in sin): ithm is the foul thing of which people are ashamed. "Wal-'udwan" (and aggression): that is, transgression with ferocity. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, while their expulsion was forbidden to you﴾, that is, you expel them from their homes and take the ransom to return it to them.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ That is, you take the matter on the basis of worldly interest, and you divide yourselves with the Aws and the Khazraj. You do this while you believe in a God, a Messenger and a Book. It is impossible that your religion or your Prophet ordered you to do this.

Then the Truth, exalted is He, says: ﴿So what is the recompense for those of you who do that except disgrace in worldly life﴾. That is, you did that and opposed [the covenant] in order to reach worldly glory, but you did not reach it. Allah will afflict you with disgrace in this world. That is, the recompense will not be delayed until the Hereafter, but disgrace will come upon you, which is humiliation and abasement in this world. And what of the Hereafter? Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the severest punishment﴾. The disgrace in this world befell them at the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers. The Banu Qaynuqa' were expelled from their homes in Medina. Likewise the Banu Qurayza were slaughtered after they broke the covenant and betrayed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims. Thus Allah, exalted is He, does not delay the recompense for some sins until the Hereafter, and the recompense for oppression in this world is not postponed to the Hereafter, because the wronged person must see the downfall of his oppressors so that the order of the universe is set right, and people know that Allah exists and that He, exalted is He, lies in wait for every oppressor. The disgrace of this world came to the Jews swiftly. ﴿On the Day of Resurrection they will be sent back to the severest punishment﴾.

People may ask: is the disgrace in this world not enough to spare them the punishment of the Hereafter? We say no, because the disgrace did not reach them as a prescribed punishment, and it was not the result of establishing Allah's limits upon them. For disgrace, when it befalls a person as a prescribed punishment (hadd) of Allah's limits, spares him from the punishment of the Hereafter. Whoever steals and has his hand cut off, and whoever commits adultery and is stoned: these have received a punishment of Allah's limits, so they will not be called to account in the Hereafter. As for oppressors, the matter is different. That is why we find people who committed a sin in this world insisting that the prescribed punishment be carried out on them, so that they may be saved from the punishment of the Hereafter, even though no one saw them, knew of them, or witnessed against them. And so that someone does not come and say: why does the disgrace that befell the oppressors in this world not spare them the punishment of the Hereafter? We say: in the disgrace of this world they were not held to account for their crimes. Harm and punishment befell them, but the severest punishment awaits them in the Hereafter. How light is the punishment of this world, which is within human power, compared to the punishment of the Hereafter, which is within the power of Allah, exalted is He; and as this world ends in death for a human being, in the Hereafter there is no death, but rather eternal punishment.

Then the Truth, exalted and majestic is He, says: ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do﴾. That is, do not suppose that Allah, exalted is He, is heedless of anything in His dominion. He is not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep, and He encompasses all things.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 86:

﴿Those are the ones who have purchased the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter. So their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be helped.﴾

Allah, glory be to Him, mentions for us the reason for the failure and misguidance of these people: they purchased the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter. They made the Hereafter the price for their desires and their influence in this world. They looked only at this world. A person's looking at this world, and comparing it with the Hereafter, makes you seek the reward of the Hereafter in everything you do. Your lifespan in this world is limited.
