Do not say the age of the world is a million, two million, or three million years. The age of the world, as far as you are concerned, is the duration of your stay in it. When you leave the world, it has ended for you. Leaving the world happens through death, and death has no fixed causes. For this reason, Islam does not make the world the goal, because our life in it is uncertain. There is one who dies in his mother's womb, one who lives an hour or a few hours, and one who reaches a senile old age. So turn toward the Hereafter, for in it there is bliss, life without death, and enjoyment according to the power of Allah.

But the failure of these people is that they purchased the worldly life with the Hereafter. Therefore the Truth says concerning them: ﴿So their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be helped.﴾ "Their punishment will not be lightened" means they must not feel secure that the punishment in the Hereafter will be eased for them, or that its degree will be reduced, or its duration shortened, or that there will come a day when it does not come. As for His saying ﴿nor will they be helped﴾: help (nusra) comes in two senses. It comes in the sense that one is not overcome, and it comes in the sense that there is a power that takes his side, i.e., supports him. As for being overcome, Allah, glory be to Him, prevails over His affair, so no one possesses for himself any benefit or harm, while Allah possesses benefit and harm for all His creatures. Blessed and exalted is He, able to subdue His creatures as He wills. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

﴿Say: I possess not for myself any benefit or harm, except what Allah wills.﴾ (Qur'an 7:188)

As for the matter of someone supporting him, who can support anyone against Allah? Consider His saying, glory be to Him, concerning Noah (peace be upon him):

﴿And O my people, who will help me against Allah?﴾ (Qur'an 11:30)

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So their punishment will not be lightened.﴾ This is a matter that has not yet occurred but will occur in the future. Allah, glory be to Him, speaks of it in the form of the present tense. We say that all events of the universe that will happen are, with Allah, already completed and decreed. Therefore we find in the Noble Qur'an His saying, glory be to Him:

﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it.﴾ (Qur'an 16:1)

"Has come" is a past-tense verb, and "do not seek to hasten it" is a future imperative. How can Allah, glory be to Him, say "has come" and then say "do not seek to hasten it"? It is future for us. As for Allah, blessed and exalted, since He has said "has come," this means it has happened. No one can prevent any of Allah's affairs from occurring. So the punishment is coming to them, it is coming, and it will not be lightened for them, because no one can lighten it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 87:

﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book, and We followed him with messengers. And We gave ʿIsa, son of Maryam, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. Is it that whenever a messenger comes to you with what your souls do not desire, you become arrogant? Some you denied, and some you kill.﴾ (2:87)

After Allah, glorified and exalted, explained to us what the Jews did with their Prophet Musa, peace be upon him, He wished to show us what the Children of Israel did after their Prophet Musa. He wished to show us their attitude toward a messenger who came to them from among themselves. Many messengers came to the Children of Israel, because their deviations from the method were many. But the noble verse mentions ʿIsa, peace be upon him, because the two great religions that preceded Islam are Judaism and Christianity. But we must know that before the coming of ʿIsa, and between the message of Musa and the message of ʿIsa, peace be upon them both, there were many messengers, among them Dawud, Sulayman, Zakariyya, Yahya, and others. It was as if, in every period, the Children of Israel would drift away from religion, commit transgressions, and disobedience would spread among them. Then Allah would send a messenger to straighten the balance of their way of life. Yet they would return again to their disobedience and wickedness, so Allah would send a new messenger to remove falsehood and the desires of the self from society and to implement the Law of Allah. But after him they would return again to disobedience and disbelief.

Allah, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿We certainly gave Musa the Book﴾. The speaker is Allah, majestic in His majesty. The Book is the Tawrah (the Torah): ﴿and We followed him with messengers﴾. Allah, blessed and exalted, has shown us the attitude of the Children of Israel toward Musa, and their attitude toward the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, the seal of the Prophets and Messengers. But He has not shown us their attitude toward the messengers who came after Musa, up to ʿIsa, son of Maryam. Allah, glorified and exalted, wants to draw our attention to the fact that He did not leave the matter to the Children of Israel after Musa, to act only by the Book that was sent with him. Rather, He followed that with messengers. When you hear ﴿wa-qaffayna﴾ ("and We followed"), it means: We made some follow others, each succeeding the one before him. ﴿Qaffayna﴾ is derived from qafa, and qafa al-shay' means to come after it. You say qafawtu fulanan, meaning I walked behind him, close to him.

Allah wants us to notice that the message of Musa did not stop at Musa and his Book. Rather, He, glorified is He, sent messengers and prophets to remind and to warn. We have said before that the multitude of prophets among the Children of Israel is not a testimony in their favour, but a testimony against them. They boast that they are the nation with the most prophets, and they consider that a privilege for themselves, but they have not understood. The abundance of prophets and messengers is a sign of the abundance of the nation's corruption, because messengers only come to rescue humanity from corruption and sickness and to save it from misery. Whenever messengers and prophets multiply, that indicates that the people have deviated as soon as the messenger has departed from them. That is why there had to be a new messenger, just as a patient in a dangerous condition has many doctors without benefit. Also, so that Allah, glorified and exalted, could establish the proof against them on the Day of Resurrection, He did not leave them a period of heedlessness. Rather, messengers kept coming to them one after another, at short intervals.

When we look at Yusha', Ushmawil, and Shamʿun; Dawud and Sulayman, Shuʿayb and Irmiya; Hizqil, Ilyas, al-Yasaʿ, Yunus, Zakariyya and Yahya, we see a long procession that came after Musa, so much so that no period passed without a prophet or messenger. And so that we distinguish between the prophet and the messenger, we say: the prophet is sent, and the messenger is sent. Both are sent from Allah, but the prophet does not bring a new legislation. Rather, he is sent upon the method of the messenger who preceded him. Read His saying, glorified is He:

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ (22:52).

So the prophet is also sent, but he is a behavioural model for implementing the method of the messenger who preceded him.

Did Allah, glorified and exalted, relate to us the stories of all the messengers and prophets He sent? Read His saying, blessed and exalted:

﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you; and Allah spoke to Musa directly﴾ (4:164).

So there are messengers and prophets who were sent to the Children of Israel whom we do not know, because Allah did not relate their news to us. But the noble verse we are discussing mentions only ʿIsa, peace be upon him, as being among the messengers with the most followers. When Allah, blessed and exalted, sent ʿIsa, He supported him with signs and clear proofs that establish the truth of his delivery from Allah. That is why He, majestic in majesty, said: ﴿And We gave ʿIsa, son of Maryam, the clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit﴾. ʿIsa, son of Maryam, peace be upon him, came to respond to the materialism that dominated the Children of Israel and made them acknowledge only the material and the perceptible. Their minds and hearts were closed to the unseen, to the point that they said to Musa: ﴿Show us Allah openly﴾. When the manna and quails came to them as provision from Allah, they feared it would be cut off from them because it was an unseen provision, so they asked for the plants of the earth. Therefore, there had to come a messenger whose whole life and method were matters of the unseen. His birth was an unseen matter, his death was an unseen matter, his ascension was an unseen matter, and his miracles were unseen matters, so that he might lead them from the tyranny of materialism to the purity of spirituality.

His beginning was that he came not through the ordinary path of material reproduction, which takes place among people through a man, a woman, and a sperm cell. Allah, glorified and exalted, wanted to remove from the minds of the Children of Israel the notion that material causes govern Him; rather, He is the one who governs causes. He is the one who creates causes, and when He says "Be," it is. This is regardless of the familiar materiality of the universe. In the matter of creation, Allah, majestic in majesty, wanted minds to understand that His will is the cause and is the agent. Read His saying, glorified is He:

﴿To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He creates what He wills. He bestows females on whom He wills, and bestows males on whom He wills, or He pairs them, males and females, and He makes whom He wills barren. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent﴾ (42:49-50).

So it is as if Allah, glorified and exalted, made maleness and femaleness the cause of procreation, but He made the absolute power dominant over causes. A man and a woman may marry, but they do not have children. So the causes themselves seem incapable of doing anything except by the will of the Causer.

Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And We gave ʿIsa, son of Maryam, the clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit﴾. Why did the Truth, blessed and exalted, say ﴿and supported him with the Holy Spirit﴾? Were not the rest of the messengers and prophets also supported by the Holy Spirit?

We say: Here the support of ʿIsa with the Holy Spirit is mentioned because the Spirit would accompany every matter concerning him, his birth, his miracles, and his death. The Holy Spirit is Jibril, peace be upon him, who never left him. ʿIsa, peace be upon him, came in a manner contrary to the familiar practice of people and the nature of humans, which made him constantly exposed to attack. Therefore, revelation had to be in his company, never leaving him, so that his awe upon the people would repel them from him. When the Qur'an speaks of his being raised to heaven, the scholars differed: was he raised to heaven alive, or did he die and then was raised to heaven? We say: If we knew whether he was raised alive or died, what would change in our method? Nothing. And when it is said that it is strange for a human to be raised to heaven, remain there for this period, and then die, we say that ʿIsa, son of Maryam, did not deny death. He will die as all humans die. But was his birth natural? The answer is no. Then why are you surprised if his death was not natural? He was created from a mother without a father. If it happened that he was raised to heaven alive and will descend to earth, what is strange about that? Did our Messenger, ﷺ, not ascend to heaven alive? Then he descended to us afterward, alive. This happened to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. So the principle exists. Why then do you consider unlikely the ascension of ʿIsa and his descent at the end of time? The difference between Muhammad, ﷺ, and ʿIsa is that Muhammad did not remain long in heaven, while ʿIsa remained. The disagreement over the period does not invalidate the principle.

It is narrated from Ibn al-Musayyib that he heard Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, say that the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, the son of Maryam will surely descend among you as a just ruler; he will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizya, and wealth will overflow until no one accepts it."(1)

This hadith is in Sahih al-Bukhari. Allah made him an example for the Children of Israel. Read His saying, glorified is He:

﴿He is only a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾ (43:59).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave ʿIsa, son of Maryam, the clear proofs﴾. The clear proofs are the miracles, such as healing the born-blind and the leper, raising the dead by Allah's permission, and other miracles. They are the matters clear and evident as proof of the truth of his mission.

But if we reflect on these miracles, we find that some of them are attributed to the power of Allah, like raising the dead, which came after it "by Allah's permission," and some of them are attributed to his miracle as a messenger. It is well known that as a messenger he was supported by Allah with miracles that break the laws of the universe. But there is a difference between a miracle that gives a messenger insight, and a miracle that must be performed each time directly by Allah. Read the noble verse:

﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel: "I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I create for you from clay the form of a bird, then breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission, and I heal the born-blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by Allah's permission, and I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers"﴾ (3:49).

Thus we see in the noble verse that while ʿIsa's telling people what they eat and store in their houses was a disclosure from Allah, the raising of the dead each time was by Allah's permission, and it was not a disclosure nor an inherent miracle of ʿIsa, peace be upon him. Every messenger was supported by the Holy Spirit, who is Jibril, peace be upon him, but Allah supported ʿIsa with the Holy Spirit always, being with him. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We supported him with the Holy Spirit﴾. ﴿Wa-ayyadnahu﴾ ("and We supported him") is derived from strength, and its meaning is: We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit in every matter.

The word "rooh" (spirit) has two meanings. The first is that which enters the body and gives it movement and life. The other is the spirit of values, which makes movement beneficial and useful. That is why Allah, glorified and exalted, called the Qur'an a spirit. Read His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit of Our command﴾ (42:52). The Qur'an is a spirit. Whoever does not act by it, the movement of his life is without values. So everything connected with the method is a spirit.

As for "al-Qudus" (the Holy), this word comes once with a damma on the qaf and sukun on the dal, and once with a damma on the qaf and a damma on the dal. Both pronunciations are correct, and they convey purity and freedom from everything that blemishes and disgraces. Al-Qudus means free from every flaw.

His blessed and exalted saying: ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger comes to you with what your souls do not desire, you become arrogant﴾. His saying, ﴿Afa-kullama﴾ ("Is it that whenever"): there is a conjunction and there is an interrogative; it means: "Do you disbelieve? Whenever a messenger comes to you with what your souls do not desire, you become arrogant." That is, the Jews made themselves legislators besides Allah, and they wanted to legislate for their messengers. So when a messenger came with what opposed their desires, they denied him or killed him.

His saying, ﴿with what your souls do not desire﴾: there is hawa with a fatha on the waw, and hawa with a kasra on the waw. Hawa with a fatha on the waw means to fall downward. Hawa with a kasra on the waw means to love and to desire. The two words meet: the first means descent, and the second is love of desire, and desire leads to descent. That is why Allah, glorified and exalted, when He legislates, says "ta'alaw" (come up), meaning rise up from your fallen position. So the method came to protect us from falling. And the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, gives us this meaning, and how religion protects us from desiring and falling into Hell. He said: "The likeness of me and my nation is like a man who kindled a fire; the moths and the insects began to fall into it..."(1)

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Mazalim, Muslim in al-Iman, Abu Dawud in al-Malahim, al-Tirmidhi in al-Fitan, Ibn Majah in al-Fitan, and Ahmad in al-Musnad.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 88:

﴿And they say, "Our hearts are wrapped (ghulf)." Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.﴾ (88)

Allah, glorified and exalted be He, mentions for us how the Children of Israel justified their non-belief, their killing of the prophets, and everything else that occurred from them. So what did they say? They said, "Our hearts are ghulf." The word ghulf is derived from ghilaf (covering) and taghlif (wrapping). There is ghulf with the lam sukun (ghulf) and ghulf with the lam damma (ghulf), like kitab and kutub. ﴿Our hearts are ghulf⦆ means they are covered, and contain enough knowledge and more, so it is as if they are saying, "We have no need for the words of the messengers." Or, ﴿Our hearts are ghulf⦆ means they are covered and sealed, meaning that Allah has stamped upon their hearts and sealed them so that no ray of guidance can penetrate them and no ray of disbelief can exit from them.

If Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has done this, did you not ask yourselves: why? What is the cause? The Truth, blessed and exalted be He, replies to them, saying: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.﴾ The word "rather" (bal) confirms to us that their statement is not correct. They do not have enough knowledge that would make them not need the method of the messengers. Rather, they are cursed and expelled from the mercy of Allah, so no rays of light or guidance penetrate their hearts. But this is not because Allah sealed them without cause; rather, it is a recompense for the fact that light and guidance came to them, and they first obstructed it with disbelief. Therefore they became expelled from the mercy of Allah, because whoever obstructs faith with disbelief is expelled from the mercy of Allah, and no ray of the rays of faith reaches his heart.

Here we must pay attention to the fact that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, did not begin with them with the curse. Some people who want to escape responsibility for disbelief, hoping it will save them from punishment on the Day of Resurrection, say that Allah, glorified and exalted be He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills⦆ (part of verse 8, Surah Fatir). That is the argument of the disbelievers who think it will save them from punishment on the Day of Resurrection. They want to say that Allah misguides whom He wills, and since Allah has willed to misguide me, what is my fault? And can I prevent the will of Allah? We say to them: when Allah restricts one of the absolute matters, we must resort to the restriction. Allah, blessed and exalted be He, says:

﴿And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people⦆ (part of verse 37, Surah at-Tawbah).

And He, glorified be He, says:

﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people⦆ (part of verse 19, Surah at-Tawbah).

And He, majestic be His majesty, says:

﴿And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people⦆ (part of verse 24, Surah at-Tawbah).

The Truth, glorified be He, has informed us that He withholds His aid to guidance from three types of people: the disbelievers, the wrongdoers, and the defiantly disobedient. But did He, glorified be He, withhold the aid of guidance first, or did they commit misguidance that made them not deserve the guidance of Allah? A person who confronted Allah with disbelief, who disbelieved in Allah, refused to listen to the signs of Allah and His messengers, refused to reflect on the universe of Allah, refused to reflect on His creation, on himself and on who created him, and refused to reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth — he rejected all of this completely, and proceeded to make for himself the path of misguidance and legislate disbelief for himself. Because he did that first, and because he began with disbelief even though Allah, glorified and exalted be He, placed in the universe and in himself signs that would make him believe in Allah, yet he refused. He is the one who began, and Allah, glorified and exalted be He, sealed his heart.

The wrongdoer wrongs people and does not fear Allah; they remind him of the power and might of Allah, but he pays no attention; Allah seals his heart. Likewise the defiantly disobedient person, who leaves no wrong unless he commits it, no sin unless he perpetrates it, and no disobedience unless he hastens to it — Allah does not guide him. Did you want these people to begin with disbelief, wrongdoing and defiance, and persist in it, and then Allah guides them? Would He guide them by compulsion or force, when Allah created us as chooser? Of course not; that would nullify human choice in whether a person obeys or disobeys.

The Truth, blessed and exalted be He, has established the absoluteness of His power in what we are subjected to: in our bodies, whose internal organs operate by compulsion from Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and not by our will, such as the heart, breathing, the circulation of the blood, the stomach, the intestines, and the liver. All of this and more is subject to Allah, majestic be His majesty. We cannot order it to act and it acts, or order it not to act and it does not act. And Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has established the absoluteness of His power in the events that occur to us in the universe: this one falls ill, that one is struck by a car, this one is struck by a stone, this one falls, and this one is assaulted by a person. All the things that happen to you, you have no say in, and you cannot prevent them. What remains is that which proceeds from you, and most important of it is applying the method of Allah in "do" and "do not do." This is a choice you have.

Indeed, Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has granted you this choice so that the reckoning in the Hereafter will be just. If you choose disbelief, Allah does not compel you to faith; if you choose wrongdoing, Allah does not compel you to justice; if you choose defiance, Allah does not compel you to obedience. He respects your choice, because He gave you this choice in order to hold you accountable for it on the Day of Resurrection.

Allah has established for Himself the absoluteness of power, that He guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills. But He, glorified be He, said that He does not guide the disbelieving people, nor the wrongdoing people, nor the defiantly disobedient people. So whoever wishes to step outside the guidance of Allah, let him disbelieve, wrong, or be defiant; in this case he is the one who has chosen, and the punishment of Allah becomes due upon him. Therefore the disbelievers among the Children of Israel said that Allah sealed their hearts so they are not guided, but they are the ones who chose this path and walked in it, so they chose non-guidance.

This question has provoked great dispute among the scholars, but in reality it does not deserve this dispute. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, said: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief⦆. Cursing (la'n) is expulsion and distancing from the mercy of Allah, and it is accomplished by the power of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, because the expulsion is proportionate to the strength of the one who expels.

For example, your small son pushes a stone in front of him; the force of his push is proportionate to his age and strength, and the older one is stronger still. So if the one who expels is Allah, glorified and exalted be He, there is no measure of the strength of cursing and expulsion that the human mind can know.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief⦆, meaning Allah expelled them because of their disbelief. Allah, blessed and exalted be He, does not court people so that they will believe, nor does He want the messengers to exhaust themselves in compelling people to faith. Rather, the duty of the messenger is delivery, so that the reckoning will be true and just. Read His words, majestic be His majesty:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers. If We willed, We could send down upon them from the sky a sign, and their necks would remain bowed to it.﴾ (Surah ash-Shu'ara, 3-4)

That is, they would not be able to avoid faith if We wanted them to be believers by compulsion. But We want them to be believers by choice, and the faith of the servant is what benefits him. Allah does not benefit from the faith of mankind. Our saying "There is no god but Allah" does not support the throne of Allah; whether we say it or not, there is no god but Allah. But we say it so that it may testify for us on the Day of Resurrection, and to save us from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection and from the anger of Allah.

His words, exalted be He: ﴿for their disbelief⦆ give us an important matter: that He, blessed and exalted be He, is the most self-sufficient of partners from partnership. Whoever associates anyone with Him, it belongs to the one who associated. Therefore the Truth, majestic be His majesty, says in the sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners from partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his partner."(1)

The testimony of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, to Himself for divinity is the testimony of the Essence to the Essence, as in His words:

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He⦆ (part of verse 18, Surah Al 'Imran).

So Allah, glorified and exalted be He, before He created any creation who would testify that there is no god but Allah, testified for Himself to divinity. Let us read the noble verse:

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice⦆ (part of verse 18, Surah Al 'Imran).

Allah, glorified and exalted be He, testified for Himself with the testimony of the Essence to the Essence. The angels testified by observation, and those of knowledge by evidence. The Truth, blessed and exalted be He, says: ﴿so little is it that they believe⦆. When you say "little of such-and-such happens," you mean here to preserve the possibility, because it is possible that one of them will return to his senses and believe, so Allah keeps the door open for these people. That is why we find that those who were excessive against themselves in their youth may come at the end of their lives and repent. Outwardly they were excessive against themselves, but when they repented, acknowledged their sins, and returned to the path of truth, Allah accepted their faith. Therefore Allah, majestic be His majesty, says: ﴿so little is it that they believe⦆, meaning that the majority remain upon their disbelief, and the minority are those who return to faith.

1 Narrated by Muslim.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 89:

﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, though before that they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved; but when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾ (89)

After Allah, glorified and exalted is He, explained to us that the Children of Israel said that their hearts were "ghulf" (wrapped, covered), so that no ray of guidance or faith could enter them, He, blessed and exalted, wished to give us another picture of their disbelief: that He sent down a Book confirming what was with them, and yet they disbelieved in it. Had this Book been different from the one they possessed, we would have said that the matter involves disagreement. But before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and the Qur'an was revealed to him, they used to believe in the Messenger and in the Book that was mentioned to them in the Torah. They used to say to the people of Madinah, the people of the time of a Messenger: "We will believe in him, follow him, and kill you with the killing of 'Ad and Iram."

The Jews lived in Madinah, and with them were the Aws and the Khazraj. Whenever disputes arose between them, the Jews would threaten them with the coming Messenger. So when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, they disbelieved in him and in what was revealed to him of the Qur'an.

Through their disbelief, the Jews became one of the causes of the victory of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because when the Messenger (peace be upon him) was sent, the Aws and the Khazraj said, "This is the Prophet with whom the Jews have threatened us," and they hastened to pledge allegiance to him. Thus it was as if the Jews, without realising it, were made by Allah to serve the victory of Islam.

The Messenger (peace be upon him) used to go to people in Ta'if, and would wait for the tribes arriving in Makkah during the season of Hajj to present the call to them, and they would turn him away and persecute him. When Allah willed that the call of Islam spread, people came to Makkah, and with them the Aws and the Khazraj came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he did not go to them. They announced their allegiance to him, their belief in his message, and the spreading of his call, without the Prophet (peace be upon him) asking them for that. Then they invited him to live among them in the abode of faith. All this took place when Allah willed to support Islam through the Hijrah to Madinah and to support it through those who followed him.

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿And they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved﴾. That is, before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, they used to seek victory by saying that the time of a Messenger whom they would believe in and follow had drawn near. But when the Messenger came, they denied him and disbelieved in his message.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿over those who disbelieved﴾, that is, the disbelievers of Madinah from the Aws and the Khazraj who had not yet become Muslims, because the Messenger had not yet come. Allah, the Exalted, gives us the complete picture in His saying: ﴿But when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾

Thus we see that the Children of Israel had a compound obstinacy: the Messenger whom they had awaited and been given good news of came to them, but pride seized them, although they were certain of the coming of the new Messenger and his attributes were present with them in the Torah. Yet they refused to believe, and for that they deserved the curse of Allah. And the curse, as we have said, is expulsion from the mercy of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 90:

﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls: that they should deny what God has sent down, out of insolence that God should send down His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants. So they have incurred wrath upon wrath. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.﴾

When the Jews refused to believe in the Messenger of God (ﷺ), God cast them out of His mercy. He shows us that they are: ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls.﴾ The word ishtara (to buy) was discussed earlier, and we said that normally we pay a price and take the goods we want. But the disbelievers reversed this completely and made the price into the goods. However, we must first speak about the difference between shara and ishtara. Shara means "sold." Read the words of the Mighty and Majestic:

﴿And they sold him for a paltry price, a few dirhams counted out, and they were among those who had no desire for him.﴾ (Surah Yusuf)

The meaning of the noble verse is that they sold him for a small price. Ishtara means "bought," but ishtara may also come to mean shara, because sometimes you are in need of goods and you have money, so you go and buy the goods with your money, and this is the sound situation. But let us suppose you need a necessary item, such as medicine, for example, and you do not have money, but you have other goods, such as a watch or a fine pen. So you go to the pharmacy and give the man goods in exchange for goods. In this case the price has become something bought. Thus sometimes the sale is a purchase and sometimes it is a sale.

And the Truth, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls.﴾ It is as if He is reproaching them for claiming intelligence and shrewdness, and for believing in materialism whose foundation is buying and selling. If they truly mastered this, they would have known that they had concluded a losing transaction. The winning transaction would have been to buy their souls in exchange for affirming what God sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ). But they sold their souls and bought disbelief, so they lost the deal, because they received disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter. God, glorified and exalted, brings some of the punishment into this world so that the balance of affairs is kept straight even for those who do not believe in the Hereafter. When someone who does not believe in the Hereafter sees a worldly punishment fall upon a wrongdoer, he fears injustice and keeps away from it, lest the punishment of this world befall him, and he knows that in this world there are measures of reward and punishment. And so that corruption by those who do not believe in God or the Last Day does not spread in the earth, the Truth, blessed and exalted, established retaliation (qisas) in this world. Read the words of the Majestic One:

﴿And in retaliation there is life for you, O people of understanding, that you may be God-fearing.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah)

In His retaliation, God draws the attention of both believer and unbeliever to the punishment of the life of this world. Thus, for the usurer who sucks the blood of people, a calamity befalls him after which he has nothing left to spend. Therefore we say: O Lord, this people has been deceived by Your forbearance and has been slow to await Your Hereafter, so seize them for some of their sins with the seizure of the Mighty, the Powerful, until the balance is restored.

God, blessed and exalted, has placed the downfall of wrongdoers, transgressors and tyrants in this world, making it a lesson for those who do not take heed of God's method. You find a man who turned away from his religion, and the world turned toward him with its luxury, glory and fame, and then you find him in the last days of his life living on the charity of benefactors. And you find a woman whom wealth deceived, who set out to gather from every place, lawful or unlawful, and the world gave to her generously. In the last days of her life the world leaves her, and she cannot find the price of medicine, and she dies, and people gather money to cover the expenses of her funeral. All these events and others are a lesson to people. That is why they happen before the eyes of all, and a large number of people know of them, either because they are published in newspapers or because they are spread among the people of the neighbourhood, who pass them around. The point is that they become famous.

And you find, for example, that the Jews, who were the leaders of the city, the merchants of war and weapons, end up being expelled from their homes, their wealth seized and their women taken captive. Is this not disgrace?

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿out of insolence (bagyan)﴾. Bagy is transgressing the limit, and God has set a limit for everything; whoever transgresses it has committed bagy. The limits God has set are rulings; sometimes they are commands and sometimes prohibitions. Therefore the Truth says concerning commands:

﴿These are the limits of God, so do not transgress them.﴾ (part of verse 229, Surah al-Baqarah)

And He says concerning prohibitions:

﴿These are the limits of God, so do not approach them.﴾ (part of verse 187, Surah al-Baqarah)

But what was the cause of their insolence? Their insolence was envy of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that the message should come to him, and that the Messenger should be from the Arabs. The Jews believed, because of the multitude of their prophets, that they were the ones who had inherited God's messages to the earth. When the Torah and the Gospel came, giving glad tidings of a final Messenger, they said that he would be from among them. Prophethood and message would not depart from them, for they were the chosen people of God. Therefore they used to declare that they would follow the coming Prophet and support him. But they were surprised that he was not from among them. Then pride and envy filled them, and they said: since he is not from us, we will not follow him, but will fight him. The messages were removed from them because they were not worthy of them, and God had to punish them for their disbelief and disobedience and place the message in another nation. The Almighty says:

﴿If He wills, He will take you away and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for God.﴾ (Surah Fatir, 16-17)

God tested them with many messages, but, as we read in the previous verses, they denied a group of the prophets, and whomever they did not deny, they killed. Therefore it was necessary that God take these messages from them and place them in another nation, so that the Arab nation would be the seal of the messages of heaven to earth. That is why they transgressed.

As for His saying, exalted be He: ﴿out of insolence that God should send down His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants.﴾ From here we know that messages and the choosing of messengers are a bounty from God, which He bestows on whom He wills. When God gives us free rein and empowers us with means, we do not step outside His will but submit to it. We know that there is no inherent self-existence in this universe, so that a person may not be deceived by himself. For the world champion in a particular game is the peak of human perfection in that game, but this perfection is not inherent in him, because another may overcome him, and because some obstacle may befall him that makes him unfit for championship. In any case, his championship does not last, because it is not inherent in him, and He who granted it to him, God, will grant it to another whenever He wills. Therefore a person must know that human perfection is changeable and lasts for no one, and that everyone who reaches the summit descends afterward, because we live in a world of change, and whoever rises must descend. Perfection belongs to God alone, and God guards His perfection by His own essence.

So the Jews envied the Messenger of God; they envied the descent of the Qur'an upon the Arabs. The Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿So they have incurred wrath upon wrath. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.﴾ God, Majestic and Exalted, tells us that He was angry with them twice.

The first anger was that they did not carry out what was in the Torah, so God was angry with them. The second anger came when a messenger came to them, who was mentioned in their Torah and whom they were required to believe in, but they disbelieved in him. It was required that they believe, so that God would be pleased with them. Therefore God was angry with them again when they disbelieved in the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

As for His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment.﴾ The punishment in the Noble Qur'an is described as painful, described as great, and described as humiliating. Painful means one who is punished feels intense pain. But suppose the one being punished bears up and tries not to show pain, lest people gloat over him. God brings upon him a great punishment that he cannot bear, for the greatness of the punishment makes him unable to endure it. So if the person was among those who led disbelief in the world and stood against God's religion, fighting it and leading their people, God, blessed and exalted, brings upon them a humiliating punishment, and this is more painful to the soul than pain itself. Just as, if a man who is the strongest in the region, whom everyone fears, is struck down by your hand and thrown to the ground, you have in that case humiliated him before the people, so that he can no longer act tyrannically or arrogantly toward any of them. This is more painful to the soul than the pain of the punishment itself. Therefore the Truth, glorified be He, says:

﴿Then We will surely draw out from every faction whichever of them was most insolent toward the Most Merciful. Then We are most knowing of those most deserving of it to burn therein.﴾ (Surah Maryam, 69-70)

And His saying, Majestic is He:

﴿Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble.﴾ (Surah al-Dukhan, 49)

That is the humiliating punishment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 91:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down," they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us," and they reject what is besides it, while it is the truth, confirming what is with them. Say, "Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?"﴾ (2:91)

Almighty Allah here makes clear to us the position of the Jews, regarding their refusal to believe in the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), even though they were commanded to do so in the Torah. He, majestic is His majesty, says: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Believe in what Allah has sent down"﴾, meaning: when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called them to believe in Islam and to believe in the Qur'an, they rejected that. ﴿And they say, "We believe in what was sent down to us"﴾, meaning: we believe in the Torah, ﴿and they reject what is besides it﴾, meaning: what was sent after it.

We know that kufr (disbelief) is concealment (sitr). Had Muhammad (ﷺ) come contradicting what they had, they might have said: "He came to demolish our religion, and therefore we reject him." But he came with the truth, confirming what is with them.

So when they disbelieve in the Qur'an, they also disbelieve in the Torah, because the Qur'an confirms what came in the Torah.

Here Allah, blessed and exalted, establishes against them the conclusive proof: your this disbelief and your conduct against every prophet who came to you... and if you were truly receiving faith with an open heart, then tell us: why did you kill the prophets of Allah? Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Why then do you kill the prophets of Allah before?﴾ Is there in your book, the Torah, any permission for you to kill the friends of Allah? It is as if Almighty Allah had taken the proof from their saying: ﴿"We believe in what was sent down to us," and they reject what is besides it﴾. If this is true, and you believe in what was sent down to you, then bring us from what was sent down to you, which is the Torah, anything that permits you to kill the prophets, if you are believers in the Torah. Of course, they could not answer, because they had disbelieved in what was sent down to them. So they are liars in their saying "we believe in what was sent down to us," because what was sent down to them did not command them to kill the prophets. Thus they disbelieved in what was sent down to them, and they disbelieved in what was sent down to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.

The Qur'an brings us the conclusive proof that silences the mouths of the disbelievers and affirms that they are incapable and unable to produce proof in debate. Here we must take note of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why then do you kill the prophets of Allah before?﴾ His saying ﴿before﴾ is a reassurance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that their killing of the prophets has ended, and at the same time it is a termination of the hopes of the Jews that they might kill Muhammad (ﷺ). Allah wishes to remove fear from the hearts of the believers concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), by making clear that what befell the earlier messengers from the Children of Israel will not befall the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Thereby the Qur'an cut off the path of return for anyone who wishes harm to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because that was a past covenant and it has ended. And if they plot to kill him (ﷺ), they will not succeed and will not reach their goal.

After the revelation of this noble verse, the Jews did not retreat from their plotting, nor did they cease their aggression in killing messengers and prophets. They tried to kill the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) more than once. Once, while he was in their quarter, they threw a stone upon him, but Jibril (peace be upon him) warned him, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) moved from his place before the stone was thrown. Another time they put poison for him, and other attempts all failed.

So His saying ﴿before﴾ means: if you are thinking of getting rid of Muhammad (ﷺ) by killing him as you did with your prophets, then We tell you: you will not be able to kill him.

This verse was sufficient to cast despair into their souls so that they would cease their method of killing the prophets, but they persisted in their attempts. At the same time, the verse was a strengthening for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers: that the Jews, however much they plot, Allah will not enable them over anything. His saying ﴿if you are believers﴾ means: in what was sent down to you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 92:

﴿And We certainly brought Moses to you with clear proofs; then you took the calf [for worship] after him, while you were wrongdoers.﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted is He, explained to us their refusal to believe in what was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on the pretext that they believe only in what was revealed to them, He made clear to us that this pretext is false, and that by their very nature they are disbelievers and deniers. So He said, glorified is He: ﴿And We certainly brought Moses to you with clear proofs﴾. That is, Moses, peace be upon him, was supported by Allah with many clear signs and miracles, which were sufficient to fill your hearts with faith and make you worship none but Allah. He split the sea for you, and you passed through it while you were looking and seeing. That is, the miracle was not hidden from you; it happened before your eyes and you witnessed it. But as soon as you crossed the sea and Moses went to meet Allah, as soon as that happened, you took the calf as a god besides Allah and worshipped it. So how can you claim that you believed in what was revealed to you? Had you believed in it, you would not have taken the calf as a god.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wants to refute their argument that they believe in what was revealed to them, and to show us that they did not even believe in what was revealed to them. So He brought the account of the killing of the prophets. Had they truly believed in what was revealed to them, let them produce what would permit them to kill their prophets, but they are liars. As for the second argument: if you believe in what was revealed to you, then tell us how, when Moses came to you with the clear signs, namely the staff that turned into a serpent, the white hand without harm, and the sea that We split for you so that you might be saved from the people of Pharaoh, and the slain man whom Allah revived before your eyes after you struck him with part of the cow you had slaughtered, many signs, yet as soon as Moses left you and went to meet his Lord, you worshipped the calf. So your saying "we believe in what was revealed to us" is untrue. Neither do you believe in what was revealed to you, nor do you believe in what came after you. All these arguments have as their purpose the absence of faith in the first place.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then you took the calf after him, while you were wrongdoers﴾. Taking the calf in itself is not a sin if you take it for tilling or for slaughter, to eat its meat. But the sin is taking the calf as an object of worship. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿you took the calf﴾. That is, this is a matter that was witnessed; you did not worship the calf in secret but openly worshipped it. Therefore it is a matter that needs no witness or testimony, because it happened publicly and before all the people. And the mention of this story of the calf is so that they would feel their guilt toward Allah, just as a person commits a mistake and then time passes over it, and whenever we want to reproach him we remind him of what he did. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿while you were wrongdoers﴾. That is, wrongdoers in your faith, wrongdoers toward the right of Allah by your disbelief in Him.

﴿And when We took your covenant and raised Mount Sinai above you, [saying], "Hold firmly to what We have given you and listen." They said, "We hear and we disobey," and they were made to drink the calf into their hearts because of their disbelief. Say, "Wretched is what your faith enjoins upon you, if you are [truly] believers."﴾

After Allah, glory be to Him, had reminded them of their disbelief in worshipping the calf, which was a form of severe reproach and a reminder of their kufr, He wished to rebuke them once more and to remind them that they had believed only out of fear that Mount Sinai (Jabal al-Tur) would fall upon them. The mountain would not have fallen on them, because Allah does not compel anyone to faith. But as soon as they saw Jabal al-Tur above them, they believed. Their situation is like that of a child whom the doctor has prescribed a bitter medicine so that he may be cured. Therefore, Allah's raising of Jabal al-Tur above them was so that they would accept the covenant and the methodology (manhaj). It cannot be said that He did this by coercion so that they would believe. It is the compulsion of one who loves. Allah wants His creation not to live without a heavenly methodology, so He raised the mountain above them to demonstrate His might and power, blessed and exalted is He, so that when they sensed this tremendous power and what it could do to them and to them alone, they believed. It was as if, when they perceived the power of Allah, they believed, exactly like the small child who opens his mouth to take the bitter medicine while hating it. But did you give him the medicine in aversion to him, or did you give it to him out of the utmost love and compassion for him?

Allah, glory be to Him, wants to draw their attention to the fact that He left no means unused so that the Children of Israel would receive the correct methodology of Allah. We say that He left no means unused without employing it. But the instinct of arrogance and obstinacy prevented them from continuing in faith. This is exactly like saying to a father that the medicine is bitter and has not brought about a cure, and his child is still sick. He replies, "What more can I do? I forced him to drink the bitter medicine, but he was not cured."

As for Allah's words, ﴿your covenant﴾: is the covenant from them, or is it the covenant of Allah? Certainly it is the covenant of Allah. But the Majestic One addressed them by saying ﴿your covenant﴾ because they had become a party to the contract. Since they had become a party, the covenant became theirs. We must affirm that raising Jabal al-Tur above the Jews was not to compel them to accept the covenant, so that it could not be said they were forced into it. They followed Musa (Moses) before the mountain was raised above them, so they must have taken his methodology by their own choice and applied it by their own choice. Allah, glory be to Him, did not keep the mountain raised above their heads wherever they were throughout their lives so that it could be said they were coerced. If they had been coerced only for the moment the mountain was above them, then after that miracle ended there would have been nothing compelling them to apply the methodology. The matter is that Allah, blessed and exalted, when He sees disobedience among His servants, may frighten them and may seize them with a lesser punishment, so that perhaps they will return to their faith. This comes from Allah's love for His servants, because He wants them to be believers.

However, the Jews are a materialistic people who believe only in matter. Allah, blessed and exalted, wanted to show them a material sign upon their hearts that would make them humble and return them to the remembrance of Allah. There is no coercion in this, because, as we have said, when the miracle ended they could have returned to disobedience. Yet it was a sign that pushes toward faith.

As for His words, ﴿Hold firmly to what We have given you with strength﴾: because what is taken with strength is given with strength, and taking with strength indicates the taker's love for what is taken. As long as the believer loves the methodology, he will fulfil its requirements with strength. A person, when he takes something he does not love, always takes it with lethargy and negligence.

As for His words, ﴿and listen; they said, "We hear and we disobey"﴾: speech (qawl) is the action of the tongue, while action (fi'l) is the action of all the limbs apart from the tongue. There is qawl, fi'l and 'amal. Qawl is to utter with your tongue; fi'l is for your limbs to carry out; and 'amal is for speech to match action. They ﴿said, "We hear and we disobey"﴾: they heard what Allah, glory be to Him, had said to them, and they disobeyed it. But on what is ("we disobey") coordinated? It is not coordinated with ﴿We hear﴾, but with ("they said"). They said "We hear" in speech, and "we disobey" in action. This does not mean that they said with their tongues "we disobey" in action. The problem arose from coordinating "we disobey" with "we hear", so one thinks they uttered both words. No. They said "We hear," but they did not carry it out, so they did not act. Allah, glory be to Him, wants them to hear with the hearing of obedience, not the mere hearing of any kind. But they heard and did nothing, so their not acting was itself disobedience.

As for His words, ﴿and they were made to drink the calf into their hearts﴾: the Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to portray for us their materialism. Love is a non-material matter, since it is not perceptible. The expression would normally have been "they drank the love of the calf." But the One speaking is Allah, who wants to give us the clear and complete picture that they drank the calf itself, that is, the calf entered their hearts.

But how can the calf enter such a narrow place as the heart? Allah, glory be to Him, wants to draw our attention to pervasiveness in everything through the word "drink" (ushribu), because it describes the drinking of water, and water permeates the entire body. The image expresses how materialism had seeped into the hearts of the Children of Israel, as if the calf had entered their hearts and permeated them as water enters the body, even though material things do not enter the heart.

The Truth, Majestic is He, says: ﴿and they were made to drink the calf into their hearts because of their disbelief﴾. It is as if disbelief itself gave them the calf to drink. They disbelieved first, and because of their disbelief the calf entered their hearts and sealed them.

As for His words, ﴿Say, "Wretched is what your faith enjoins upon you, if you are [truly] believers"﴾: they said, "We believe in what was revealed to us, and we do not believe in what came after it." Say: does your faith enjoin you to this? This is a style of mockery in the Noble Qur'an directed at them, like His words:

﴿Expel the family of Lut from your town; they are people who keep themselves pure.﴾ (part of verse 56, Surat al-Naml)

Does purity justify expelling the family of Lut from the town? Certainly not. It is a style of mockery and reproach. The truth is that their faith does not enjoin them to this; rather, it enjoins them to believe in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). Read His words, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿And prescribe for us in this world good, and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You." He said, "My punishment — I afflict with it whom I will; but My mercy encompasses all things. So I will decree it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses, who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that were upon them. So they who have believed in him, honored him, supported him, and followed the light which has been sent down with him — it is those who will be the successful.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf, 7:156–157)

This is what their faith enjoins: that they believe in the unlettered Prophet, Muhammad (ﷺ). Allah, blessed and exalted, knows what faith enjoins upon them, because it comes from Him, Majestic is He. Therefore, when they try to deceive Allah, Allah, glory be to Him, mocks them and says to them: ﴿Wretched is what your faith enjoins upon you, if you are [truly] believers.﴾ His words, ﴿if you are [truly] believers﴾, are evidence that they are not believers. Rather, shirk and disbelief, or the calf they worshipped, still remain in their hearts.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 94:

﴿Say: If the Last Abode with Allah is specially for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.﴾

Allah, glorified and exalted, wants to expose the Jews, and to make clear that their faith is not sound, that they have distorted and altered [the Scripture], and that they have bought with the signs of Allah a small price. He, glorified be He, wants us to know that these Jews did not do this out of ignorance, nor were they deceived; rather, they know that they changed and altered, and they know that they brought words and attributed them to Allah, glorified and exalted, falsely and with slander. For this reason, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is commanded to expose them before the people and to make their lie clear with decisive proof. So He says: ﴿Say: If the Last Abode is yours﴾. "Say" is addressed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning: say to them, O Muhammad. This statement would only be made if the Jews had claimed that: ﴿the Last Abode with Allah is specially for them﴾.

That which is khalis (pure, unmixed) is what is clear, without turbidity or partner: that is, the thing that belongs to you alone, in which no one shares with you and no one contends with you. So Allah, glorified and exalted, says to His Messenger (ﷺ): If the Hereafter belongs to them alone with Allah, with no one sharing it with them, then it was incumbent upon them to wish for death so that they might go to everlasting bliss. For as long as the Last Abode is theirs, and as long as they are certain of entering Paradise alone, what is it that keeps them in this world? Do they not wish for death as the Muslims wished for martyrdom, so that they might enter Paradise?

These are not the only fabrications of the Jews against Allah, glorified and exalted. Consider the saying of the Majestic, the Mighty:

﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ (part of verse 111, Surat al-Baqarah).

Who said this? The Jews said of themselves that none would enter Paradise except those who were Jews, and the Christians said of themselves that none would enter Paradise except those who were Christians. Each of them said that Paradise is specifically theirs. Their statement has posed us a riddle in matters of creed: who will enter Paradise alone, the Jews or the Christians? We say: Allah, glorified and exalted, has answered this question with His saying, the Majestic, the Mighty:

﴿And the Jews say: The Christians are not upon anything; and the Christians say: The Jews are not upon anything﴾ (part of verse 113, Surat al-Baqarah).

This is the truest statement that the Jews and the Christians said about one another. The Jews are not upon anything, and the Christians are not upon anything. Each of them is truthful in what he says about the other. In the noble verse we are discussing, the Jews said that the Last Abode is exclusively theirs. We will take them at their word and say to them: why do they not hasten and wish for death? It would be expected that they long for the Hereafter, since it is exclusively theirs. Therefore Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾. But these are false wishes, according to the Jews and the Christians alike. Consider His saying, glorified be He:

﴿And the Jews and the Christians say: We are the sons of Allah and His beloved. Say: Why then does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings of those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and to Him is the final return﴾ (18, Surat al-Ma'idah).

So they imagine that, however many sins they commit, Allah will not punish them on the Day of Resurrection. But the justice of Allah refuses this. How could He punish human beings for their sins and not punish the Jews for the sins they have committed? Rather, He would admit them to Paradise in the Hereafter. And how could Allah, glorified and exalted, make Paradise in the Hereafter exclusively for the Jews, when He has prescribed His mercy for the followers of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the believers in the message of Islam, and has informed the Jews and Christians of this in their books? Consider His saying, glorified and exalted:

﴿And prescribe for us in this world good, and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned back to You. He said: My punishment I afflict with whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things. So I will decree it for those who fear Allah and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses. Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ (verse 156 and part of verse 157, Surat al-A'raf).

If this is the reality present in their books, and the Truth, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers﴾ (85, Surat Al 'Imran).

How then do the Jews claim that the Last Abode will be exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection? But the Truth, majestic is He, exposes their lie and confirms to us that what they say is something they themselves are the first to know is false.

Qur'an 2:95: ﴿And they will never wish for death, because of what their hands have sent forward. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾

They will never wish for death at all; rather, they fear it. When Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed this verse, He placed the matter of the whole of faith in the hands of the Jews, such that they could, if they wished, cast doubt upon this religion. How? Was it not possible, when this verse was revealed, for a number of Jews to come and say: "Would that we were dead! We wish for death, O Muhammad. So pray to your Lord that He cause us to die"? Was it not possible for them to say this? Even if hypocritically, even if ostentatiously, in order to demolish this religion? But even this they did not say, and it did not occur to them. Look at the miraculous nature of the Qur'an in His words, glorified is He: ﴿and they will never wish for it﴾.

Allah, glorified is He, has issued a final judgment regarding a voluntary matter concerning an enemy who opposes Islam. He said that this enemy, namely the Jews, will never wish for death. It was possible for them to perceive this challenge and say: "Rather, we do wish for death and we ask Allah for it." But even this did not occur to them, because when Allah, blessed and exalted, decides a voluntary matter, He strips the enemies of the religion of those thoughts that they could use to demolish the religion. Thus these thoughts never occur to them at all, just as Allah, glorified is He, had challenged them earlier in His words, exalted is He: ﴿The foolish among the people will say: "What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they had been facing?"﴾ (part of 2:142).

This noble verse was revealed before they said it, as evidenced by the use of the particle sin (س) in His words "will say". Allah, majestic in His majesty, described them as foolish. Nevertheless, they did say it. Had their minds been alert, they would have remained silent and said nothing. In that would have been a challenge to the Noble Qur'an: they would have said, "Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has said: ﴿The foolish among the people will say﴾." But no one said anything. Where are these foolish ones, and why did they not speak? This would have been considered a challenge to the Noble Qur'an in a matter in which they had freedom of choice. But because Allah is the Speaker and Allah is the Doer, that never occurred to them at all, and they did indeed speak.

In the noble verse we are discussing, the Qur'an challenged them to wish for death, and they did not wish for it. The logical expectation, since the Last Abode is exclusively theirs, was that they would wish for death. Allah challenged them: if they were truthful, they would have wished for it, so as to go to everlasting bliss. But the Truth had already decreed in advance that this would not happen from them. Why? Because they are liars and know that they are liars. Therefore they flee from death and do not wish for it.

Look, for example, at the ten who were given the glad tidings of Paradise. ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, in the battle of Hunayn, while being martyred, was reciting: "Now I shall meet the beloved, Muhammad and his companions." He was happy because he had been struck, and he knew, as he was being martyred, that he was going to Paradise, to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions. Thus is confidence in the reward and the glad tidings of Paradise. ʿAbdullah ibn Rawaha was fighting while reciting and saying: "How good is Paradise and its nearness, / Good and cool, and its drink." And the Imam ʿAli, may Allah honour his face, entered the battle of Hunayn wearing a light tunic without armour, which would not repel an arrow or the thrust of a spear, so much so that his son al-Hasan said to him: "O my father, this is not battle attire." ʿAli, may Allah ennoble his face, replied: "My son, your father does not care whether he falls upon death or death falls upon him." And our master Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman was reciting while dying: "A beloved who came upon a camel, no gain without regret." So those who trust in their afterlife love death.

And at the Battle of Badr, one of the Companions asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, is there nothing between me and Paradise except that I fight these men and they kill me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) answered: "Yes." And the Companion had some dates in his hand, which he was chewing. He considered it too slow to remain far from Paradise until he had eaten the dates, so he threw them from his hand, entered the battle, and was martyred.

These are the ones who trust in what is with Allah in the Hereafter. But the Jews, when the Noble Qur'an challenged them with His words: ﴿So wish for death, if you are truthful﴾, they fell silent and did not answer. Had they wished for death, the breath of each of them would have stopped while swallowing his saliva, and they would all have died. Someone may say: "Is wishing by the tongue alone? Perhaps they wished in their hearts." We say: what is wishing? We say that wishing is to say of a thing you love, "Would that it happened." So it is speech. Suppose it is an act of the heart; had they wished in their hearts, Allah would have seen it and caused them to die immediately. But since the Truth, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿and they will never wish for it﴾, they will never wish for it, whether by tongue or by heart. Because their claim that Paradise with Allah is exclusively theirs resembles their statement which the Qur'an relates to us in His words, exalted is He:

﴿And they said: "The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days." Say: "Have you taken a covenant with Allah, so that Allah will not break His covenant? Or do you say about Allah what you do not know?" (80)﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

And His words, exalted is He: ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾ — that is, their evil deeds make them fear death. As for the owner of righteous deeds, he rejoices at death. That is why we hear that so-and-so, when he died, his face was like the full moon, because his deeds were righteous. At the moment of death, a person knows with certainty that he is dying. When a person falls ill, he hopes for recovery and considers death remote. But at the moment of the death-rattle, a person becomes certain that he is dying, and he reviews his life as in a rapid film. If his deeds were righteous, his features relax and he rejoices, because he will be blessed in the Hereafter with eternal bliss. For in that hour, as the soul leaves the body, a person knows his destiny, either to Paradise or to the Fire, and he is received either by angels of mercy or by angels of punishment. The one who obeyed Allah is given good news by the angels of mercy. But the one who disobeyed and did what displeases Allah reviews the film of his deeds and finds it a film of evil, while he is facing Allah, and there is no opportunity for repentance or for changing his deeds. When he sees that his destiny is the Fire, his features contract and his soul is seized in that state. So it is said: "So-and-so died with a blackened face and contracted features."

Thus, the one who did evil in his worldly life never wishes for death at all, whereas the owner of righteous deeds rejoices at meeting Allah.

However, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade wishing for death, saying: "None of you should wish for death nor call for it before it comes to him, unless he is confident in his deed."(1)

We say that the forbidden wishing for death is the wishing of despair and the wishing of protest against calamities. That is, one wishes for death because he cannot bear the decree of Allah in a calamity that has befallen him, or he wishes it in protest against the decrees of Allah in his life. This is the forbidden wishing for death. As for the owner of righteous deeds, it is recommended for him to wish to meet Allah. Read His words at the end of Surah Yusuf:

﴿My Lord, You have given me from the kingdom and taught me from the interpretation of narratives. Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous (101)﴾ (Surah Yusuf).

And the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): i.e., do not wish for death out of impatience with what befalls you of Allah's decree, but rather be patient with Allah's decree. And His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ — because Allah knows their wrongdoing and disobedience. It is this wrongdoing and disobedience that makes them fear death and not wish for it.

(1) Related by Ahmad in al-Musnad from Abu Hurayrah.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 2, verse 96:

﴿And you will surely find them the most avid of people for life, and of those who associate others with God. One of them wishes he could be given a life of a thousand years, but being granted such a life will not remove him from the punishment. And God is All-Seeing of what they do.﴾

After God exposed their lies, in that they could never wish for death because they are wrongdoers, and as long as they are wrongdoers, death is a frightening matter for them, and they are the most avid of people for life, so much so that their eagerness exceeds that of those who associate others with God. The polytheist is eager for life because he believes this world is the ultimate goal. The Jews are more eager for life than the polytheists because they fear death due to their previous evil deeds. Therefore, whenever their lives are prolonged, they think they are far from the punishment of the Hereafter. Life does not make them face the punishment, and therefore they rejoice in it.

The Jews do not care whether they live in humiliation or in wretchedness, or any kind of life at all. What matters is that they live in whatever life. But why are they more eager for life than the polytheists? Because the polytheist has no Hereafter; this world is his entire concern and his entire life. Therefore he wishes his life to be prolonged at any price and in any form, because he believes that after it there is nothing, and he does not know that after it there is punishment. The Jews are more eager for their lives than the polytheists are.

As for His saying, ﴿One of them wishes he could be given a life of a thousand years﴾: al-wadd (ود) means love. That is, they love to live a thousand years or more. But suppose he lived a thousand years or even more than that: would it remove him from the punishment? No. Length of life does not change the end.

Since the end is death, the one who lived a few years and the one who lived thousands of years are equal. As for His saying, ﴿yu'ammar﴾ with a fatha on the ʿayn and a shadda on the mīm, it is said that it is always in the passive voice (mabniyy li-l-majhūl). It would not be correct to say yu'ammar with a kasra on the mīm, because life is not in anyone's hand but in God's hand. God is the One who gives life and the One who ends it. Since life is not the possession of any human being, the verb is in the passive voice.

Life (al-ʿumr) is the span of time a person passes between his birth and his death. The root of the word is taken from ʿimārah (cultivation/building), because the body is made populated by life; when life ends, the body becomes scattered remains and ruin. As for His saying, ﴿a thousand years﴾: why was the thousand mentioned? Because it was the limit of what the Arabs knew of counting.

This is why the man who was taken captive in war, the sister of Khosrow, said: "How much will you take and leave me?" He said: "A thousand dirhams." They said to him: "For how much did you ransom her?" He said: "For a thousand." They said: "If you had asked for more than a thousand, they would have given it to you." He said: "By God, if I knew anything above a thousand, I would have said it." Thus the thousand was the highest number among the Arabs. This is why they used to say "a thousand thousand" and did not say "a million."

As for His saying, ﴿and he is not one to remove him from the punishment by being granted life﴾: its meaning is that even if he lived a thousand years or more, he would not escape the punishment. As for His saying, ﴿and God is All-Seeing of what they do﴾: that is, He knows what they do, and He will punish them for it, whether they live a thousand years, more, or less.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 97:

﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel – for indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah, confirming what came before it, and as guidance and good tidings for the believers.﴾ (2:97)

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wishes to draw our attention to the fact that the Jews did not merely kill the prophets, distort the Torah, and sell the signs of Allah for worldly status. Rather, they also took the angels as enemies. Indeed, they harboured enmity towards the closest of the angels to Allah, the one who brought down the revelation of the Qur'an, namely Gabriel (peace be upon him). They said: "Gabriel is our enemy."

The address here is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Jurya, one of the rabbis of the Jews, sat with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: "Who is it that brings the revelation down to you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Gabriel." The Jew said: "If it had been anyone else, we would have believed in you. Gabriel is our enemy, for he always brings down punishment and torment, whereas Michael brings down mercy, rain and fertility." Also, he is their enemy because they believed that Bayt al-Maqdis would be destroyed by a man named Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar), so they sent someone to kill him. The Jew met a young boy and the boy asked him: "What do you want?" He said: "I want to kill Bukhtnassar, because in our Torah he is the one who will destroy Bayt al-Maqdis." The boy said: "If it is decreed that this man will destroy Bayt al-Maqdis, you will not be able to overcome him, because what is decreed is carried out, whether we are pleased or not. And if it is not decreed, then why would you kill him?" That is, the child said to him: if Allah has decreed in the Book that Bukhtnassar will destroy Bayt al-Maqdis, then no one can prevent the decree of Allah, and you will not be able to kill him to prevent the destruction of Bayt al-Maqdis at his hands. And if this is not true, then why would you kill a soul without guilt? So the Jew returned without killing Bukhtnassar. When he went back to his people, they said to him: "It was Gabriel who appeared to you in the form of a child and persuaded you not to kill this man."

It is related that our master ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab had land on the upper part of Madinah. Whenever he went to it, he would pass by the Jewish schools and sit with them. The Jews thought that ʿUmar's sitting with them expressed his love for them, so they said to him: "We love you, we respect you, and we hope for you." ʿUmar understood their intention and said: "By Allah, I did not sit with you out of love for you, but I wished to increase my understanding of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to learn from you what is in your Book about him." They said: "And who will inform Muhammad of our news and secrets?" ʿUmar said: "It is Gabriel, who descends to him from the heaven with your news." They said: "He is our enemy." ʿUmar said: "What is his standing with Allah?" They said: "He sits on the right of Allah, and Michael sits on the left of Allah." ʿUmar said: "Since the matter is as you have said, neither of them is an enemy of the other, for they have one standing with Allah. Whoever is an enemy to either of them is an enemy to Allah. Your enmity to Gabriel and your love for Michael will not benefit you, because their standing with Allah is exalted."

Their enmity towards Gabriel (peace be upon him) confirms their materialism. They measure the matter by human standards: the one who sits on the right of a lord and the one who sits on his left compete for rank with him.
