But this is the world of humans; with the angels there is nothing of this kind. With Allah is that which enables Him to give high rank to whomever He wills without diminishing the other. Moreover, Allah, glorified and exalted, has the name al-Haqq (the Truth), and what Gabriel brings down is truth, and what Michael brings down is truth, and truth does not dispute with truth. ʿUmar said to them: "You are worse in disbelief than donkeys." Then he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and before he had even reached him, the Messenger said: "Your Lord has agreed with you, O ʿUmar." And the words of Allah, blessed and exalted, were revealed: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel – for indeed he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah, confirming what came before it, and as guidance and good tidings for the believers.﴾ ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, after that my faith is firmer than a mountain."

So their saying "Michael is our beloved and Gabriel is our enemy" is one of material considerations, while Allah, blessed and exalted, says to His Messenger (ﷺ): they are enemies of Gabriel because he has brought it down upon your heart by the permission of Allah. And since it has come down from Allah upon your heart, it is no concern of theirs. It confirms what is before them of the Torah, and it is guidance and good tidings for the believers. So which of these elements do you deny in Gabriel? Your enmity towards Gabriel is enmity towards Allah, glorified and exalted.

Thus God, glorified and exalted, has given the ruling. He said that enmity toward the messengers is like enmity toward the angels, which is like enmity toward Jibril and Mika'il, which is like enmity toward God. The Truth, glorified and exalted, brought the angels in general, then mentioned Jibril and Mika'il by name.

The matter is not divided into parts; it is one single issue. Whoever is an enemy to the angels, to Jibril and Mika'il, and to the messengers of God, is first and last an enemy to God, because there is no division among them. They all revolve around the Truth, and the one Truth contains no hostility. Hostility arises only from the clash of desires and appetites, and this happens in worldly affairs.

The noble verse establishes the unity of the Truth among God, His angels, His messengers, Jibril and Mika'il. Whoever opposes one of these opposes them all, and he is an enemy of God, glorified be He. The Jews are enemies of God because they disbelieved in Him, and enemies of the messengers because they denied them and killed some of them.

Thus the Truth, glorified and exalted, wishes to draw our attention to the unity of the Truth in the religion. Its source is God, majestic in His glory. His messenger from among the angels is Jibril, and His messengers from among mankind are the messengers and prophets whom God sent. Mika'il descends with goodness and fertility, because faith is the foundation of the existence of life. Whoever is an enemy to the angels, the messengers, Jibril and Mika'il is a disbeliever, because the verse did not say that enmity toward these is merely enmity. Rather, God ruled that they are disbelievers. God, glorified and exalted, did not inform Muhammad (ﷺ) of this ruling only; He commanded him to proclaim it, so that people everywhere would know it and know that the Jews are disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 99:

﴿And We have certainly sent down to you clear signs, and none disbelieves in them except the defiantly disobedient.﴾

God, glorified and exalted is He, then moves on to affirm the truthfulness of the message of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and that the signs in it are so clear that every person who has reason and wishes to believe will believe in them. But those who desire deviance and wickedness are the ones who do not believe.

What is the meaning of "clear signs"? The ayah (sign) is the wondrous matter, and it is wondrous because it is miraculous (mu'jiz). The signs are the miracles of the Messenger, which indicate the truthfulness of his conveying from God. They are also the ayat (verses) of the Noble Qur'an. "Clear" (bayyinat) means that they are matters that are evident, on which there is no disagreement, and which need no explanation.

﴿And none disbelieves in them except the defiantly disobedient.﴾ Fisq (defiant disobedience) is departing from obedience, and it is derived from ar-rutbah: the unripe date, before it becomes ripe, whose skin you cannot pull off; but when it becomes rutab (ripe dates), you find that the skin moves away from the fruit, so it is said: "the date fisqat (has split out of its skin)." Therefore, whoever departs from the method of God is called fasiq.

The meaning is that the signs with which God, glorified and exalted is He, supported Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, are manifest before the disbelievers and need no proof. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, who did not read a single word in his life, brings this Qur'an, miraculous in its wording and its meaning: this is a manifest miracle that needs no proof. And the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, whom the whole world cannot tempt to abandon this religion, however much they give him, is evidence that he is a man of principle and a message from heaven. And the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, who, by a Qur'an revealed from heaven, reports the outcome of a war that will take place after nine years, and who informs the disbelievers and hypocrites of what is in their hearts and exposes them, and who foretells coming events and the laws of the cosmos, and other things that the miraculous Qur'an contains of every kind of miraculousness, scientific, astronomical and cosmic: all of these are clear signs with which the Qur'an challenges the disbelievers. They are all clear signs, which none can disbelieve in except the one who wants to depart from the method of God and do what his soul desires.

The miraculousness in the cosmos, in the Qur'an, and in the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, all of this requires only impartial thought, so that we may know that this Qur'an is from God, filled with miracles in language and knowledge, and that it will remain a miracle for every generation that brings new understanding.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 2, verse 100:

﴿Is it not that whenever they make a covenant, a party of them casts it aside? Indeed, most of them do not believe.﴾

After Allah, the Exalted, has shown that the religion of Islam, and its Book the Qur'an, contains such clear signs that belief in it requires nothing more than a pause for reflection by the intellect, the hostile stance that the Jews take toward Islam becomes contrary to all the covenants that were taken from them, contrary to innate faith, and contrary to their having covenanted with Allah not to conceal what came in the Torah about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), contrary to their pledge to believe in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and contrary to what Moses asked of them, that they believe in Islam when the Messenger comes, in confirmation of the saying of the Exalted:

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom, and then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him." He said: "Do you affirm and accept My burden on this condition?" They said: "We affirm." He said: "Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses."﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran)

Thus we know that Moses (peace be upon him), upon whom the covenant was taken, conveyed it to the Children of Israel, and that the Children of Israel knew this covenant well at the time of the sending of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they had precise descriptions of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him). But they broke it, as they broke many covenants. Among them was their pledge not to work on the Sabbath, and how they circumvented the command of Allah by setting up fish traps into which they would enter but from which they could not get out; this was a trick against the command of Allah. Then there was their covenant to believe in Allah as one God, the One, the Unique, and then they worshipped the calf. And there was their saying to Moses (peace be upon him), after Allah commanded them to enter a valley with crops, because they wanted to eat from the plants of the earth instead of the manna and quails that came to them from the sky. They said to Moses: ﴿So go you and your Lord and fight, we are sitting right here.﴾ And there are many other covenants concerning war, captives and worship. Even when Allah, blessed and exalted, raised Mount Sinai above them and terror entered their hearts, and they thought it was about to fall upon them, and this was only a supposition and not a reality, because Allah, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿And they thought that it was about to fall upon them.﴾ And as soon as they moved away from Mount Sinai, they broke the covenant.

Then they broke their covenant and pact with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he migrated to Medina, namely at the Battle of the Trench, and when they wanted to open a path for the disbelievers to strike the armies of the believers from behind.

As for the saying of the Exalted: ﴿a party of them casts it aside﴾, we have said that this is called the principle of preserving possibility, because among them were those who kept the covenants, and among them were those who were true to what Allah had covenanted with them, and among them, for example, were those who wanted to embrace the new religion and believe in Muhammad (peace be upon him).

So they are not all of them, lest it be said that this applies to Jews in general, for among them were people who did not break the covenant. Allah, blessed and exalted, wants to open the door before those who wish to believe, so that they do not say: "Allah has passed an absolute judgment against us, while we want to believe and preserve the covenant." But those who kept the covenant were few, and therefore the Truthful, Glorified One said: ﴿Indeed, most of them do not believe.﴾ That is, the party that breaks the covenant and breaks faith is the majority of the Children of Israel.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 101:

﴿And when there came to them a messenger from Allah, confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs, as though they did not know.﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted is He, spoke about the Jews who broke the covenants concerning belief in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), breaking them while they knew, Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when there came to them a messenger from Allah, confirming what was with them﴾. That is, what came in the Qur'an confirms what came in the Torah, because the Qur'an is from Allah and the Torah is from Allah. But they distorted the Torah, concealed parts of it, altered and substituted within it, hiding what they wished to hide. Therefore the Noble Qur'an came to reveal what they had concealed and to affirm what they had not concealed and had not tampered with.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs﴾. We have said that there is a book they first cast away, which is the Torah. When the final Book, which is the Noble Qur'an, came to them, they cast it behind their backs as well. What is the meaning of nabadha (to cast away)? The meaning is to throw something far away from oneself. So what was in their book concerning the attributes of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) they cast away far off, and the announcement of the coming of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) they cast away as well. For they used to seek victory through him over those who disbelieved, saying: "The time of a prophet has come, we will believe in him and kill you with the killing of 'Ad and Iram."

As for His saying: ﴿a party﴾, it means a group cast away, and another group remained that did not cast away the Book. The proof is that Ibn Salam, one of the rabbis of the Jews, affirmed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and believed in him, and Ka'b al-Ahbar, and Mukhayriq, embraced Islam. Had the Qur'an generalized and not said "a party," it would have been said that it was unjust to those who believed.

As for His saying: ﴿behind their backs﴾. Casting away may be in front of you, and when it is in front of you, you see it constantly, and perhaps it tempts you to turn toward it. But they cast it behind their backs, meaning they put it behind them so that they would forget it completely and not turn to it.

As for His saying: ﴿as though they did not know﴾. That is, they feign that they do not know of the glad tidings of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his attributes. His saying: ﴿as though﴾ is evidence that they do know it with certainty. For if they truly did not know, the Real, glorified is He, would have said: "a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs" while they did not know. So they know with certainty, but they feigned ignorance. And we must take note that nabadha may be followed by its opposite, as you say: "he cast away such-and-such and followed such-and-such." They cast away the Book of Allah, but what did they follow?

Almighty Allah informs us that a group of the Jews rejected the Book of Allah and followed what the devils recited. The word *nabadha* (cast aside) is matched by *ittaba'a* (followed), so *wa-ittaba'u* means they took as their guide, following what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. The context would normally call for *ma talathu al-shayatin* (what the devils recited), but Allah wants us to understand that this following continues to this day, as if they had not restricted the matter to a particular time.

To this very moment there are Jews who follow what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon. Since the contemporary Jews have approved of and adopted the deeds of their ancestors who followed the devils, it is as if they themselves did it.

The Truthful, Glorified One says: ﴿And they followed what the devils recited﴾. But the devils recited and then passed away. The Jews' invoking what the devils recited until now is evidence that they believe in it and accept it as true. The devils are the rebellious among the jinn, and the jinn include the disobedient, the obedient and the believers. Read His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among us are the righteous, and among us are those below that; we were in divided ways﴾ (Surat al-Jinn, 11).

And His saying about the jinn: ﴿And among us are the Muslims, and among us are the deviators﴾ (Surat al-Jinn, 14, part of the verse).

So among the jinn are believers and unbelievers, and among the believing jinn are obedient and disobedient ones. The devils are the rebellious chiefs of the jinn who rebel against the method of Allah. Every rebel against the method of Allah we call a devil, whether from the jinn or from mankind. For this reason the Truthful, Glorified One says: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorated speech as deception﴾ (Surat al-An'am, 112, part of the verse).

So the devils are those who rebel against the method of Allah. His saying: ﴿And follow what the devils recited over the kingdom of Solomon﴾ means what the devils used to recite during the days of Solomon's kingdom.

But what is the story of Solomon's kingdom and the devils? Before the coming of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah had empowered the devils to listen to the commands of heaven as they were descending to earth. They would listen to the commands received from the angels, convey them to the leaders of disbelief, and add to them some lies and superstitions. Some of it would be true, but most of it was false. For this reason Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you﴾ (Surat al-An'am, 121, part of the verse).

Before the revelation of the Qur'an the devils would eavesdrop, but at the sending of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) all of that was prevented, so that the devils could not place their superstitions into the method of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or into the Qur'an. For this reason the Truthful, Glorified One says: ﴿And we used to sit in it on seats for listening, but whoever listens now finds a watching flame﴾ (Surat al-Jinn, 9).

That is, the devils had seats in the heavens where they sat to listen to what descended from heaven to earth to be carried out. But when the Qur'an was revealed, Allah, glorified and exalted, sent the meteors, which are burning stars. So when the devils try to listen to what descends from heaven, a meteor falls upon them and burns them. For this reason, when common people see a meteor burning swiftly in the sky, they say: "An arrow of Allah at the enemy of the religion." It is as if the matter is in people's minds, causing them to say: "An arrow of Allah at the enemy of the religion," meaning the devil.

Read the saying of the Blessed, Exalted One: ﴿And we touched the sky and found it filled with severe guards and meteors﴾ (Surat al-Jinn, 8).

﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾ (Surat al-Jinn, 10).

That is, the matter became confused for the devils, because they could no longer steal hearing. So they did not know whether what descended from heaven was good or evil. Observe the precision of the Qur'anic expression in His saying: ﴿And we touched the sky﴾. It is as if they had ascended until they reached the sky, to the point that it became close to them, so that they almost touched it.

So Allah, blessed and exalted, in this situation, which is the Jews' following what the devils recited over Solomon's kingdom of magic, enchantments and things that harm and do not benefit, wished to absolve Solomon of all of this. So He, majestic in His majesty, said: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve﴾.

The logic would have required that Allah, glorified, first mention the account of the devils before absolving Solomon of the disbelief they wanted to spread. But Allah wanted to negate the accusation of disbelief from Solomon and affirm it upon everyone who followed the devils, so He, majestic in His majesty, said: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved﴾.

So it is the devils who spread disbelief. And how did the devils disbelieve, and with what did they tempt their followers into disbelief? Allah, glorified, says: ﴿But the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic and what was sent down upon the two angels at Babylon, Harut and Marut. And they did not teach anyone until they said, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve." And they learned from them that by which they cause separation between a man and his wife. But they could not harm anyone thereby except by permission of Allah. And they learned what harmed them and did not benefit them. And they had already known that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter﴾.

What is the story of all this? The Jews cast aside the covenant of Allah and followed what the devils recited in the days of Solomon, and they wanted to attribute everything in Solomon's reign to magic and the work of devils. Thus the Jews wanted to deceive people into believing that Solomon's method was from magic and from devils. The Truthful, Glorified One wanted to absolve Solomon of this lie. Solomon, peace be upon him, when prophethood came to him, asked Allah, glorified and exalted, to give him a kingdom that He would not give to anyone after him. Read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me; indeed You are the Bestower." So We subjected to him the wind, blowing by his command gently wherever he directed. And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound in shackles﴾ (Surat Sad, 35–38).

Thus Solomon was given sovereignty over mankind, the jinn and the creatures of Allah, such as the wind, the birds and other things. When Solomon took the kingdom, the devils were filling the earth with disbelief through magic and its books. So Solomon took all the books of magic, and it is said that he buried them beneath his throne. When Solomon died, the devils found the hiding place of the books of magic, took them out and spread them among the people. Their allies among the rabbis of the Jews said that these books of magic were what Solomon used to control mankind and the jinn, and that they were his method, and they spread them among the people. So Allah, glorified and exalted, wanted to absolve Solomon of this accusation, and of having ruled by magic and spread disbelief. He, majestic in His majesty, said: ﴿And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic﴾.

What is magic? The word is derived from *sahar*, which is the last hours of the night and the first emergence of day, when darkness mixes with light and everything becomes unclear. Thus magic is something that makes you imagine that something is happening when it is not. It rests on two things. The first is bewitching the eye, so that you see what is not real as if it were reality, but it does not change the nature of things. For this reason the Truthful, Glorified One said concerning the magicians of Pharaoh: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people and frightened them, and they produced a great magic﴾ (Surat al-A'raf, 116, part of the verse).

So the magician controls the eye of the one who is bewitched so that he sees what is not real and what is not true, and the eye of the bewitched becomes subject to the will of the magician. Therefore magic is imagination and not reality. Read the saying of the Truthful, Glorified One:

﴿He said, "Rather, throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him, because of their magic, to be moving﴾ (Surat Ta-Ha, 66).

So since the Almighty said: ﴿It appeared to him﴾, then they were not moving. So magic is imagination. And what is the evidence that magic is imagination? The evidence is the confrontation that took place between Moses and the magicians of Pharaoh. The magician bewitches the eyes of people, but no one bewitches the eyes of the magician himself. When the magicians and Moses came, read His saying:

﴿They said, "O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw." He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him, because of their magic, to be moving﴾ (Surat Ta-Ha, 65–66).

When the magicians threw their ropes and staffs, it appeared to the onlookers that they were snakes moving. But did it appear to the magicians that they were snakes? Of course not, because no one had bewitched the eyes of the magicians. So what they threw remained, in their own eyes, ropes and staffs. When Moses threw his staff, read the saying of the Blessed, Exalted One:

﴿And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only the plot of a magician, and a magician does not succeed wherever he comes.' So the magicians fell down in prostration, saying, 'We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses'﴾ (Surat Ta-Ha, 69–70).

Here the reality of magic becomes evident. Why did the magicians prostrate? Because their ropes and staffs remained as they were, ropes and staffs, since no one had bewitched their eyes. But when Moses threw his staff, it turned into a real snake. So they knew this was not magic but a miracle from Allah, blessed and exalted. Why? Because magic does not change the nature of things, and they were certain that Moses' staff had turned into a snake, while their ropes and staffs remained as they were, even though it had appeared to the people that they had turned into snakes.

So magic is imagination, and the magician sees the thing as it truly is, therefore he is not afraid. Whereas the bewitched, who are the people, imagine that the nature of the thing has changed. For this reason the magicians prostrated, because they knew that Moses' miracle was not magic but something beyond human capacity.

Magic, then, is imagination, and the devils have the ability to take on any form, and we cannot perceive the devil in his true form. But when he takes a form, we can see him in a physical shape. If he takes the form of a human, we see him as a human; if he takes the form of an animal, we see him as an animal. In this case he is governed by that form. So if he takes the form of a human and you shoot him, he dies; if he takes the form of an animal and you run him over with your car, he dies, because the form governs him by its law. This is the secret of why he remains in his form only for a moment and then disappears within seconds. Why? Because he fears that the one who sees him in that form will kill him, especially since the law of transformation governs him. For this reason, when the devil took the form of a man before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "I had intended to tie him to a pillar of the mosque so that the children of Medina could look at him. But I remembered the saying of my brother Solomon: 'My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not befit anyone after me.' So I left him." (The hadith is not recorded in the collections.)

And by the mercy of Allah toward us, when the devil takes a form, the form governs him. Otherwise they would have terrified us and made our lives a hell. Allah, glorified and exalted, made the universe stand on balance so that none oversteps against another. To illustrate: if we were in a village and none of us owned a weapon, balance would prevail. But if one of us acquired a weapon, claimed he did so to defend the people of the village, and then used the weapon to dominate the villagers and impose levies on them and other things, the balance would be upset, and this is what Allah does not accept.

Magic leads to the disruption of balance in the universe, because the magician seeks help from a power higher in its element than man, namely the devil, who is created from fire, light in movement, able to take forms and so on. When a person seeks and learns how to subjugate the jinn, he claims he does so to spread good in the universe, but this is not the truth, because this drives him to tyranny. What disturbs the security of the world is the lack of equality among people. A person (the text breaks off here).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 103:

﴿And if only they had believed and feared Allah, a reward from Allah would have been better, if they had known.﴾

Almighty Allah opens before His servants the doors of repentance and mercy. He has made clear to them that sorcery is disbelief (kufr), and that whoever practises it will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as a disbeliever and will abide forever in the Fire. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, also told them that if they refrained from learning sorcery in order to distinguish themselves over others through harm and injury, that would be better for them with Allah, blessed and exalted be He. This is because the two angels who were sent down to teach sorcery, Allah said of them: ﴿And they teach no one until they say, "We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve."﴾

So the practice of sorcery is disbelief. Had they believed in this matter, and that they would be entering into disbelief, and had they feared Allah, that would have been a reward (mathuba) for them with Allah and good in this world and the Hereafter. But what is the mathuba? It is the reward (thawab) for righteous deeds, and its counterpart is the punishment (iqab) for evil deeds. It is derived from thaba, meaning "returned." For this reason, the one who relays the words of the imam in prayer is called the muthawwib (the one who repeats the call), because the imam says "Allahu akbar," and the relayer repeats it in a loud voice so that those worshippers who cannot hear the imam's voice may hear it. This is called the tathwib (repetition), meaning the repeating of what the imam says so that those who did not hear what the imam said have a greater opportunity. As we have said, it is derived from thaba, meaning "returned," because when a person does a righteous deed, the good of that deed returns to him. So do not think that a righteous deed goes out from you and does not come back. Rather, it must return to you with good.

When we consider the precision of the Qur'anic expression, ﴿a reward from Allah is better﴾, we find that the word mathuba is derived from the same root as the word thawb (garment), whose plural is thiyab. In former times, people would take the wool of sheep to make their clothes. A man would bring what he had of sheep, shear their wool, and then give it to another to spin and weave into a garment, and return it to its owner. It was as though what he had sent of wool came back to him as a garment. For this reason it was called mathuba, because good returns to you so that you benefit from it with a high benefit. Likewise, the reward for a righteous deed returns to you with a high benefit.

So from thawb comes thawab (reward), and Allah, glorified and exalted be He, taught us that the garment is for covering the nakedness. A righteous deed covers the moral and psychological ailments in a person. About this the True One, blessed and exalted be He, says:

﴿We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts and as an adornment; but the clothing of righteousness, that is best.﴾ (part of verse 26, surah al-A'raf)

It is as though there are two garments: one to cover the nakedness, and the second to shield a person from punishment. The garment of righteousness is better than the garment that covers the nakedness. His saying, exalted be He: ﴿a reward from Allah is better﴾. Consider the reward that comes from Allah. If a reward that comes to you from one who made it beautiful, embroidered, and of bright colours is so, what then of the reward that comes to you from Allah? It is the summit of beauty. Allah is the One able to return the reward by His powers, so the return is high, and very high, such that the reward is multiplied again and again.

However, we must pay attention to the saying of Allah, exalted be He: ﴿And if only they had believed and feared﴾. We have said that the meaning of ittaqa (to fear/be mindful) is that they place between themselves and the attributes of majesty (sifat al-jalal) of Allah a protection (wiqaya). For this reason we have said that some people ask: how does Allah, blessed and exalted be He, say ﴿Fear Allah﴾, and say, glorified be His majesty, ﴿Fear the Fire﴾? We say that the meaning of "Fear Allah" is: place between yourselves and the attributes of majesty of Allah a protection. ﴿And fear the Fire﴾ means: place between yourselves and the punishment of the Fire a protection, because the Fire is among the consequences of the attributes of majesty. Therefore His saying ﴿Fear Allah﴾ is equivalent to "Fear the Fire." When the True One, blessed and exalted be He, said ﴿fear﴾, He used it in a general sense, and the omission of the object here is intended to generalise. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, wants to draw our attention to the fact that the sorcerers, if they had believed that learning sorcery is a trial that leads to disbelief, and had feared Allah and dreaded His punishment in the Hereafter, that would have been better for them. For this reason He, majestic be His majesty, said: ﴿a reward from Allah is better﴾.

When you hear the word khayr (good), the word sharr (evil) comes to mind, because good is opposed by evil. But in some cases, khayr has no opposite evil, but is opposed by a lesser good. The word khayr is the only word in the Arabic language whose noun form equals the comparative form (af'al al-tafdil). You say: "This one is excellent (fadil) and that one is surpassed (mafdul 'alayh)." The word khayr is a noun of preference, so one says: "That is better than such-and-such," meaning that one of the two gives more than the other. When the word khayr is not followed by "better than such-and-such," its counterpart is sharr. So when you say "So-and-so is better than so-and-so," both share in good, but to different degrees. Good is what brings you benefit, but the measure of benefit varies among people. One looks at immediate benefit, and another looks at deferred benefit. In outward appearance, each of them wanted good.

To bring this closer to the mind, let us say there are two brothers: one wakes early to go to his school, and the second sleeps until midmorning, then leaves the house to sit in a café. The first loves good for himself, and the second loves good for himself too; the disagreement is in the evaluation of good. The lazy one loves immediate good, so he gives himself his share of sleep, entertainment, and not working. The diligent one loves deferred good for himself, so he exerts himself and toils through the years of study, so that afterwards he may rest and achieve a distinguished future.

The farmer who ploughs and goes to his field at dawn, irrigates, sows the seed, and toils, at the end of the year receives an abundant harvest and much good. The farmer who sits in the café all day has given himself the good of rest, but at harvest time he reaps regret.

So all people love good, but their outlook and measures differ. Some want the pleasure of today, and some work for the pleasure of tomorrow. When Allah, blessed and exalted be He, commands us to good, the good may be burdensome to body and soul, but the end is everlasting enjoyment in the Garden of Eternity. So true good is what the Sharia has brought. Why? Because good is that beyond which there is nothing further. You are born, then you grow up, then you graduate from university, then you attain the highest positions, then you die, then you are resurrected, then you enter Paradise, and after that there is nothing but eternal abiding in bliss.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿if only they had known﴾. Allah negates knowledge from them, whereas in the preceding verse He affirmed knowledge for them when He said: ﴿And they had certainly known that whoever purchased it would have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ We say that knowledge which does not govern a person's conduct is as though he had known nothing.

Because this knowledge will be a proof against its possessor on the Day of Resurrection, and he would have wished he had never known it. Consider the words of the poet:

They were provided, yet they were not provided with the generosity of a hand;
it is as though they were provided, and yet they were not.
They were created, yet they were not created for noble deeds;
it is as though they were created, and yet they were not.

It is as though knowledge was never established for you, because you did not benefit from it. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says: ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾ (part of verse 6, surah al-Rum).

﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life...﴾ Thus Allah negated from the people true knowledge, and affirmed for them worldly, apparent knowledge. And His saying, majestic be His majesty:

﴿The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah and then did not take it up is like the example of a donkey carrying volumes. Wretched is the example of the people who deny the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (surah al-Jumu'ah, verse 5)

That is, they carried the Torah as knowledge, but they did not carry it as a method and practice. These sorcerers knew that whoever practises sorcery becomes a disbeliever, yet they did not act upon what they knew.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 104:

﴿O you who have believed, do not say, "Ra'ina," but say, "Unzurna," and listen. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.﴾

This is an address to the believers, because the noble verse begins: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. When the Truth addresses the believers with His words ﴿O you who have believed﴾, we know that faith here is the basis of responsibility (taklif). Allah does not hold a disbeliever or a non-believer accountable, and He does not command a responsibility except to those who have believed. So long as the servant has believed, the responsibility for his movement in life has become his obligation before his Lord, and for this reason He reveals to him the method of life. As for the disbeliever, Allah does not assign him anything.

Therefore, His words ﴿O you who have believed﴾ are a command to whoever has believed in Allah and been content with Him as God and Legislator. His words ﴿O you who have believed﴾ are an address to the believers, and His words ﴿do not say, "Ra'ina"﴾ are a prohibition, as though "Ra'ina" was a saying that was current among them, and Allah wants to forbid them from it. Faith obliges them to listen to the prohibition of Allah.

What is the meaning of "Ra'ina"? We say in our colloquial language, "Ra'ina," meaning: protect us, watch over us, and take us by the hand, and all of this is derived from the root of care (ri'aya) and the shepherd (ra'i). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock."(1)

The root derives from the shepherd of sheep, because the shepherd of sheep must lead them to places where there is grass and water, that is, to pasturing places, and must be a guard over them lest one of them stray or get lost and the wolves of the deserts devour it, and must provide them with rest so that they do not become exhausted and perish on the way.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I used to tend sheep for the people of Makkah for a few qirats."(2)

But why did the Truth, glory be to Him, replace the word "Ra'ina" with the word "Unzurna"? In Hebrew and Syriac, the word "Ra'ina" exists among the Jews and its meaning is foolishness (ra'una). For this reason, whenever they heard the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say "Ra'ina," they used it as a means of insulting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while the Muslims did not know anything. Therefore Allah, glory be to Him, commanded the believers to abandon this word, so that the Jews would not find a means to conceal their insults, and He commanded them to say: "Unzurna."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿and listen﴾. Here Allah points to the difference between the Jews and the believers. The Jews said, "We hear and we disobey," but Allah says to the believers, "Listen" with the listening of obedience and the listening of implementation.

Sa'd ibn Mu'adh heard one of the Jews say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "Ra'ina," and Sa'd was among the rabbis of the Jews and knew their language, so when he heard what he had said, he understood his intent. He went to the Jew and said to him: "If I hear you say it once more, I will strike off your neck." The Jew said: "Do you not say it to your Prophet? Is it forbidden to us and permitted to you?" Then the noble verse was revealed saying: ﴿Do not say, "Ra'ina," but say, "Unzurna."﴾ If we reflect on the word "Ra'ina" and the word "Unzurna," we find the meaning is one, but "Unzurna" conveys the meaning and has no counterpart in the language of the Jews which signifies insult to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And His words, the Exalted: ﴿And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment﴾, meaning: those who say "Ra'ina" as an insult to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will have a painful punishment.

(1) Narrated by Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi from Ibn Umar.
(2) Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 105:

﴿Those who disbelieve, among the People of the Book and among the polytheists, do not wish that any good should be sent down upon you from your Lord. But Allah singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾ (2:105)

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, revealed to the believers the enmity that the People of the Book, the Jews, and the polytheists, who disbelieved because they rejected belief in Muhammad (peace be upon him), harbour towards them. He draws their attention to the fact that the Jews and the polytheists dislike good for the believers. So be wary of every matter that comes from them, and know that they do not want any good for you. His words, exalted is He: ﴿do not wish﴾, meaning do not love. Wadd (love/affection) means the inclination of the heart towards one it loves. Wadd differs from ma'ruf (kindness). You do a kindness to those you love and to those you do not love, but you only wish well (wadd) for those you love. Therefore Allah, blessed and exalted, said:

﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers or their sons or their brothers or their kinsfolk﴾ (Surah al-Mujadilah 58:22, part of the verse).

Then, after that, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, comes to speak about parents:

﴿But if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, but keep them company in this world with kindness﴾ (Surah Luqman 31:15, part of the verse).

Some orientalists claim there is a contradiction between the two verses. How is it that Allah, glorified and exalted, says: do not show love to those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger, and then comes and says that if your parents try to make you associate partners with Allah, then keep them company in this world with kindness? Of course, parents who try to push their son into disbelief are waging war against Allah and His Messenger. How is this contradiction resolved?

We say: you have not understood the meaning. A person does kindness to those he loves and to those he does not love, as we said. You may find a person in distress and give him a sum of money as a kindness, even though there is no relationship between you and him. But wadd is only with those you love.

So: "ma yawaddu" means the love of the heart. That is, the hearts of the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists do not love good for you. They dislike that any good should be sent down upon you from your Lord. Indeed, in reality they do not want any thing from your Lord to be sent down upon you that is called good. And good is the revelation of Allah, His method, and the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).

His words, exalted is He: ﴿min khayr﴾ (any good), meaning any thing that is called good. When you go to a person and ask him for money, he says: "I have no money," meaning I do not own money, though he may possess a pound or two, and this is not considered money that can meet what you want. And you go to another man for the same purpose and say, "I want money," and he says: "I have no money," meaning I do not have even a single piastre, I have no amount at all that could be called money, even several piastres. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wants us to understand that the People of the Book, the disbelievers and the polytheists are united in their hatred of the believers, to the extent that they do not want any thing from your Lord sent down upon you that is called good.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿from your Lord﴾, indicate the source from which good comes from Allah. It is as if they do not love that any good from Allah should be sent down upon the believers, namely the method and the message. Then the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿But Allah singles out for His mercy whom He wills﴾, meaning that good is not subject to the desire and wishes of the disbelievers. Allah sends down good to whomever He wills. Allah has apportioned among people the affairs of their worldly life. So how can the disbelievers demand that Allah subject His method to their will? Read the words of the Blessed and Exalted:

﴿They said: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man of the two cities?" Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in rank, so that some of them may take others in service. But the mercy of your Lord is better than what they accumulate﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf 43:31-32).

The disbelievers objected to the revelation of the Qur'an upon Muhammad (peace be upon him), saying: if it had been sent down upon a great man of the two cities. So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, responds to them: you do not apportion the mercy of Allah; rather, Allah apportions your life in this world among you.

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, in the verse we are discussing, says: ﴿But Allah singles out for His mercy whom He wills﴾. When you read the word yakhtass (singles out), you understand that something has been specified for one thing rather than another. That is, I have specified so-and-so with this thing: ﴿Allah singles out for His mercy whom He wills﴾, that is, He gives mercy to whomever He wills so that he may carry out his mission, or sends down His mercy upon whomever He wills. So these disbelievers have no right to control the will of Allah, and their envy and hatred of the believers does not give them the right to control the mercy of Allah. Therefore Allah wished to respond to them that this religion will spread, the believers in it will increase, Allah will open through it regions and nations, people will enter it in multitudes, and He will make it prevail over all religions.

If we reflect on the causes by which any enemy overcomes one who opposes him, we find that they are either clear, visible causes, or cunning and deception, such that the enemy shows his enemy that he loves him while plotting against him in secret until he gains power over him and kills him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) migrated to Madinah secretly. Why? Because Allah wanted to say to the Quraysh: you will not be able to overcome the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), not even by cunning, deception and nocturnal plotting. They plotted by night to kill him, and they brought from every tribe a young man so that his blood would be lost among the tribes. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) went out and put dust on the heads of the young men. Allah wanted them to know that they would not be able to overcome the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) through cunning, nocturnal plotting and deception, nor through open hostility.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾. Fadl (bounty) is the amount in excess of your essential need.

For this reason the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever has an extra mount, let him give it to one who has no mount, and whoever has extra provisions, let him give it to one who has no provisions" (1).

And an extra amount of wealth is any wealth beyond his need. This is regarding bounty in relation to human beings. As for Allah, glorified and exalted is He, everything in the universe of Allah now and in the Hereafter is the bounty of Allah, because it exceeds His need. Allah does not need His creation, nor any of His blessings that have preceded or will come. Therefore He said: ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾, meaning the possessor of immense bounty that exceeds His need. For perhaps I may have a surplus, but I keep it because I will need it in the future. True bounty is that which comes from Allah. Therefore Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the Possessor of great bounty, because He does not need His creation or His universe. For Allah, glorified is He, existed before anything existed, and He will remain after nothing exists. This is what is called great bounty.

(1) Narrated by Muslim in Luqatah, Abu Dawud in Zakah, and Ahmad in the Musnad.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 106:

﴿Whatever a verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent?﴾ (106)

But what is the reason? The reason is that the People of the Book and the polytheists do not wish any good for the believers in their religion, because they sensed that what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought in his time was better than what Moses brought and what remained until the time of Muhammad (ﷺ)... and better than what Jesus brought in the time of Muhammad (ﷺ). This does not mean that we are trying to belittle what the earlier messengers brought... but we affirm that the earlier messengers brought, in their own times, the best that was found in those times. Every message that preceded the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to a specific people and for a specific time. Then a new Prophet came to abrogate what was in the previous message for a specific people and a specific time. Consider the words of Jesus (peace be upon him) when he was sent to the Children of Israel, as the Noble Qur'an relates to us:

﴿And confirming that which was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.﴾ (50) (Surah Al 'Imran).

It is as if Jesus (peace be upon him) came to abrogate some rulings of the Torah, and to make lawful for the Children of Israel some of what Allah had forbidden them. As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), being the Seal of the Messengers, he was given all good, because his religion is for all the worlds and remains until the Day of Resurrection.

Thus we see that the believers in the messengers, whenever a new messenger came, moved from good to good... and in what the messages agree upon, they moved to a similar good; and in what relates to the method of life, they moved to an increase in good. In the messages of heaven as a whole there are common matters in which there is no difference between one messenger and another, namely the matter of faith in one God, One, Who has absolute perfection... exalted in His essence, exalted in His attributes, and exalted in His actions. All of this is a common measure among the messages. But life, in its development, contains matters that did not exist and were not confronted in the age before. If we say that a message, in its doctrinal value, remains, it still cannot confront the matters of life that the ages after it will bring, except for Islam, because it came as a seal religion that does not change or alter until the Day of Resurrection. Yet some say: and what about the saying of Allah, Exalted be He:

﴿He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus: Establish the religion and do not be divided therein. Difficult for the polytheists is that to which you invite them. Allah chooses for it whom He wills and guides to it whoever turns back [to Him].﴾ (13) (Surah Ash-Shura).

We say that this applies to one thing: the matter fixed in the messages of heaven, which is the core of belief and faith in the One God. As for matters of life, we find rulings in this movement according to the expansions that have occurred in it. Therefore, when Muhammad (ﷺ) came, he gave things with which to address matters that did not exist in the time of the earlier messengers. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Whatever a verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾... The word "naskh" (abrogation) means removing a verse that existed and bringing another verse in its place, as one says "the sun abrogated the shade" (nasakhat al-shams al-zill), meaning the shade existed and then the sun came and erased it and took its place. And one says "I copied the book" (nasakhtu al-kitab), meaning I transferred it into multiple forms, and "old age abrogated youth" (nasakha al-shayb al-shabab), meaning the young man became an old man.

And His saying, Exalted be He, ﴿or cause to be forgotten﴾ has multiple meanings. It may mean that Allah causes the person to forget and become heedless of it, so it is lost from his memory or he leaves it for something else. The scholars differed on this question, and this difference arose because one of them observes one aspect and another observes a different aspect, and both seek the truth. We come to abrogation in the Noble Qur'an. A group said there is no abrogation in the Qur'an at all. Why? Because abrogation implies al-bada' (a change of mind) with respect to Allah. What is al-bada'? It is that you issue a ruling, then application comes and proves the ruling's inadequacy to confront the matter, so the ruling is changed. This is impossible with respect to Allah, Exalted be He. We say to them: of course this meaning is rejected, and it is impossible to attribute it to Allah, Blessed and Exalted. But we say that abrogation is not al-bada'; rather, it is the removal of a ruling and the bringing of another ruling. We say to them: when Allah issued the ruling at first, He knew that this ruling had a limited time in which it would end, and then a new ruling would take its place. But circumstances and gradualness require that this happen gradually. This does not mean that Allah, Exalted be He, ruled on something and then a different reality came and proved that the ruling was inadequate, so Allah changed the ruling. This is not correct.

Why? Because when Allah first issued the ruling, He knew that the ruling had a time or would be applied for a period, and after that it would be abrogated or replaced by another ruling. So the plan that set this ruling set it on the basis that it would end and a new ruling would take its place.

This is not like the reality of human beings. The rulings and laws of humans are amended because the reality of application proves the ruling's inadequacy to confront the matters of reality, since when people set the ruling they knew some things and other things were hidden from them. Then reality came to reveal what was hidden, and the ruling had to be abrogated or amended. But the matter with Allah, Exalted be He, is not like this. The command of Allah made the ruling time-bound from the moment the first ruling came.

For example, when Allah directed the Muslims to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem)... Was it the case with Allah that the qibla would remain toward Bayt al-Maqdis as long as Islam existed and until the Day of Resurrection? Then it became clear to Him, Exalted be He, to direct the Muslims to the Ka'bah? No... this was not the picture. Rather, it was in the law of Allah that the Muslims would first turn toward Bayt al-Maqdis for a period, and after that they would turn toward the Ka'bah until the Day of Resurrection.

Therefore, reality did not compel the plan to change the qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah...

Rather, it was in His knowledge and in His law that He would change the qibla after a period to the Ka'bah. Perhaps there is a faith-based purpose in this: that the reason for matters is that they come from Allah. Turning toward Bayt al-Maqdis or turning toward the Ka'bah does not cost the believers any additional effort of faith, nor does it place new obligations upon them. The same effort I exert to face east I exert to face west. But the test of faith is that the reason for the command is that it issues from Allah. So if Allah says "face Bayt al-Maqdis," we face it; if He says "face the Ka'bah," we face it. No thing is holy in itself, but holiness lies in Allah's command concerning it.

And when Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, they did not prostrate to Adam's essence, but they prostrated in obedience to Allah's command to prostrate to Adam. Allah, Exalted be He, chose the honored Ka'bah as His house and sanctuary on earth, and the Ka'bah took its lofty station among the Muslims not because it is a spot in some place where Abraham and the prophets came and people performed Hajj to it, but its station came from the fact that it is the House of Allah by Allah's choosing. All the mosques on earth are houses of Allah by the choosing of the creatures of Allah, but the only mosque that is the House of Allah by Allah's own choosing is the Ka'bah. Therefore, all the mosques that are by the choosing of the creatures of Allah must face the mosque that is by Allah's choosing. But the greatest faith-based reason is that we believe the issuing of the command from Allah is the basis for following this command without seeking its worldly causes.

So if Allah, Exalted be He, says: the prayer is five times a day... without seeking the cause or saying "why five? let us reduce them"... we pray five times a day because Allah said so. Likewise zakat, likewise fasting, likewise Hajj: all are performed in obedience to Allah. Thus the change of the qibla was carried out as a test of faithful obedience to Allah. Allah is present in every place, so no one should come and ask "why the Ka'bah? Is Allah present only in the Ka'bah?" We say no, He is present in every place; but He commanded us to face the Ka'bah. We do not face it because we believe that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is present in this place alone, but in obedience to Allah's command that our qibla be toward the Ka'bah.

Perhaps the change of the qibla gives us the philosophy of the abrogation of verses. Why? Because no circumstances arose, no realities emerged, and no hidden things appeared that made facing Bayt al-Maqdis difficult or surrounded by problems or otherwise; rather, the change of the qibla came because Allah, Exalted be He, willed that the Muslims face Bayt al-Maqdis for a period and then face the Ka'bah until the Day of Resurrection.

Therefore, every abrogated verse was, in Allah's knowledge, going to be applied for a specific period and then changed. Each of the ruling that would be abrogated, the time it would take, and the ruling that would come after it was known to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and decreed from eternity and before the beginning of the universe. Also, Allah wished to draw our attention through facing Bayt al-Maqdis first, because Islam is a religion that encompasses all religions, and Bayt al-Maqdis would become one of the sacred places of Islam, and no one could claim that the Muslims would have no standing regarding Bayt al-Maqdis. Therefore Allah, Exalted be He, took His Messenger (ﷺ) by night journey from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis, to establish that Bayt al-Maqdis has sanctity in Islam and that it is among the sacred places before Allah. From here the facing toward Bayt al-Maqdis came as the first qibla, then Allah abrogated the qibla to the Ka'bah. The Truth, may His majesty be exalted, says: ﴿Whatever a verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it.﴾ That is, abrogation occurs either when Allah brings something better than this verse or brings something similar to it. And was there something better than the abrogated verse which Allah did not send down? We say no. The meaning is that the abrogated verse was good in its time, and the second ruling was an increase in good after a period of time. Both are good in their time and in their rulings. And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed the noble verse:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims.﴾ (102) (Surah Al 'Imran)

But who can fear Allah as He should be feared? That is difficult for the Muslims. Therefore, when the verse was revealed they said: none of us is able to fear Allah as He should be feared. So the noble verse was revealed:

﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able and listen and obey and spend; it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful.﴾ (16) (Surah At-Taghabun)

Is the one who fears Allah as He should be feared better, or the one who fears Allah as much as he is able? Of course "as He should be feared" is better than the measure of ability. But Allah, Exalted be He, says: ﴿We bring one better than it﴾...

We say: you have not understood from Allah... ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ in the first verse or ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ in the second verse... Which of the two is better? We say the criterion is the outcome. When you want to establish something, you must first look at its outcome.

To bring the meaning closer to minds, we will strike an example, and to Allah belongs the highest example. Suppose there is a merchant who sells goods at a fifty percent profit. Then another merchant comes and sells the same goods at a fifteen percent profit. What happens? People will of course flock to the one who sells goods at fifteen percent profit and buy from him all they want, and the merchant who sells at fifty percent achieves a greater profit per item... but the one who sells at fifteen percent achieves a smaller profit per item, yet with the increase in the quantity sold, the profit in the end is greater.

And the one who applies the noble verse ﴿Fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ achieves greater good in his work, but he cannot fear Allah as He should be feared except in very limited actions.

So the good here is greater, but the work to which the verse applies is limited.

As for His saying, Exalted be He, ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾, it has defined the taqwa

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 107:

﴿Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? And you have not, besides Allah, any protector or helper.﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted be He, had shown us that there are verses abrogated in the Qur'an, He wished to make clear to us that He has absolute power over His creation, doing whatever He wills. For this reason the noble verse begins with: ﴿Do you not know﴾. This expression is called the interrogative of rebuke or affirmation (al-istifham al-istinkari aw al-taqriri), because the listener finds only one answer, that he acknowledges what Allah, blessed and exalted, has said, and says: "Yes, O Lord, You are the Truth, and Your word is the Truth."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Do you not know that Allah – to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. Dominion (al-mulk) requires an owner and requires something owned. It also requires the power to sustain this dominion and to prevent its end. It is as if Allah, the Truth, glorified and exalted, wants to show us that He has the power and possesses the capacity. Man has no power of ownership, nor the capacity to preserve what he owns. Man does not possess the power to act in the universe. If he wants, for example, to build a building, he may not find the land. If he finds the land, he may not find the worker who will build. If he finds the worker, he may not find the building materials. If he finds all of this, the government or the state may come and forbid building on this land, or the land may belong to another person, so lawsuits are filed and the building is never completed.

And the Truth, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Do you not know that Allah – to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. That is, everything in existence belongs to Allah, and He disposes of what He owns by His power. For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emigrated to Madinah, the Jews possessed wealth and had knowledge of some worldly sciences, so they became dominant in Madinah and began to scheme against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims. Allah, blessed and exalted, reassured His Messenger that absolute power in the universe belongs to Allah alone, and that if they had dominion, it would not last, because Allah strips dominion from whomever He wills and gives it to whomever He wills. Therefore, when the Day of Resurrection comes and Allah destroys the earth and everyone upon it, He, glorified be He, says:

﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ (Qur'an 40:16).

The Majestic answers by the testimony of the Essence to the Essence, saying:

﴿For Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (Qur'an 40:16).

Since Allah alone is the Owner, He is able to strip the Jews and others, and the whole world, of what they possess. The scholars relate that the 'asas (the night patrol, the soldiers who walk at night to check on people's conditions) found a man walking at night. When they approached him, he ran, so they chased him until he reached a ruined place to hide in. The patrol came forward and seized him, and there they found the body of a slain man in the place. They said to him: "You are the killer, because you ran when you saw us, and because you are now present in the place where the body of the slain man is." So they took him to be judged, and he said to them: "Give me a respite so I may pray two rak'ahs to Allah." They granted him respite, and he prayed, then raised his hands to the sky and said: "O Allah, You know that there is no witness to my innocence except You. You have commanded us not to conceal testimony, so I ask You by that, in Your own Self." While they were in that state, a man approached and said: "I am the killer of this slain man, and I confess to my crime." The people were amazed and said: "Why do you confess to your crime when no one saw you and no one accused you?" He said to them: "By Allah, I did not confess; rather, a voice came and made my tongue speak what I said." When the killer confessed to what he had done, the victim's guardian, who was his father, stood up and said: "O Allah, I call You to witness that I have pardoned the killer of my son from his debt of blood and retaliation."

Look at the absolute power of the Truth, glorified and exalted. The killer wanted to hide, but look at the precision of the question from the questioner, or the innocent accused. He prayed two rak'ahs to Allah, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us that when a matter distresses us, we should turn to prayer, for there is no door before us except this one. After he prayed, he asked Allah: "You have commanded us not to conceal testimony, and no one will testify to my innocence except You, so I ask You by that." After that, what happened, happened.

This story shows us that we are in the grip of Allah, whether we wish or do not wish, whether by means or without means. Why? Because to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and He is over all things Powerful.

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿And you have not, besides Allah, any protector or helper﴾. The walī (protector) is one who loves you and is loyal to you, and the naṣīr (helper) is one who has the capacity to give you victory; the helper may be other than the protector. The Truth, blessed and exalted, says: I am your protector and helper, that is, I love you and I will help you against those who oppose you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 108:

﴿Or do you wish to question your Messenger as Moses was questioned before? And whoever exchanges disbelief for faith has certainly strayed from the even way.﴾

Then the Truth, exalted is His majesty, moves the Muslims, after having made clear to them that He is their Protector and their Helper, to the conduct of the People of the Book, the Jews, with their messengers, so that they may avoid such conduct. He, exalted is His majesty, says: ﴿Or do you wish to question your Messenger as Moses was questioned before?⦆ The Truth says to the believers: "Or do you wish to question the Messenger of God as the Jews questioned Moses?" God did not will to liken the Muslims to the Jews, so He said: ﴿as Moses was questioned before﴾. It was possible for Him to say: "Or do you wish to question your Messenger as the Jews questioned Moses?" But God did not want to liken the Jews to the believers in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is an honour from God to the believers, by declaring them far above imitating the Jews. The Jews did question Moses, peace be upon him, and they said, as the Noble Qur'an relates to us:

﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven. But they had asked Moses for something greater than that, when they said: "Show us God openly," and the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf after clear proofs had come to them, yet We pardoned that, and We gave Moses clear authority.﴾ (Surah al-Nisa', 153)

The People of the Book and the disbelievers also questioned the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the Noble Qur'an relates to us:

﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth."﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 90)

﴿"Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you have claimed, or you bring God and the angels before us as a guarantee, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe your ascent until you bring down to us a Book we can read." Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 92–93)

Blessed and exalted is God, who urges the believers to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as the People of the Book and the disbelievers asked him, and He tells them that the Jews asked Moses for something greater than that. After they had seen the miracles, and God had split the sea for them, and they crossed the sea while witnessing the miracle, it was not hidden from them; rather it was manifest to them and clear, decisively indicating the existence of God, exalted and high is He, and the greatness of His power. Despite this, the Jews said to Moses: "We will not believe you until we see God openly," meaning that these miracles did not suffice them. It is as though, in their materialism, they wanted to see in their worldly life Him whom the eyes cannot perceive. And as soon as they had crossed the sea, they wanted Moses to make for them an idol to worship, and they worshipped the calf despite all the signs they had witnessed.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever exchanges disbelief for faith has certainly strayed from the even way.⦆ We have said that the particle "bi" (with, in exchange for) in His saying ﴿bil-iman﴾ (for faith) always introduces what is abandoned. For example, you say "I bought this for so many dirhams," meaning you gave up the dirhams and took the goods. Its meaning is that disbelief is taken and faith is abandoned. The Jews took disbelief and abandoned faith when they said to Moses: ﴿Show us God openly﴾. And His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿has certainly strayed from the even way﴾.

What is going astray? It is to take a path that does not lead you to your goal. ﴿The even way (sawa' al-sabil)﴾: sawa' means the middle, and "sawa' al-sabil" is the middle of the road. God, blessed and exalted, says:

﴿So he looked down and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 55)

That is, in the middle of the Fire, meaning he is at equal distance from its two edges. The middle of the road is its center. Before the use of modern technology, the edges of a road or path were rough, of the same nature as the earth before it was levelled, meaning unfit for travel. For this reason, walking in the middle of the road keeps you away from hardship and difficulty. God wants the believers in Him to walk on the levelled road, or in the middle of the road, because it is safer for them. In it they will not go astray to right or left, but will walk on the method of God and faith. The path of faith is always levelled and does not lead them to disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 109:

﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after you have believed, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them. So pardon and overlook, until Allah brings His command. Indeed, Allah is Competent over all things.﴾

This noble verse deals with events that occurred after the Battle of Uhud. In the Battle of Uhud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed the archers not to leave their positions at the foot of the mountain, whether the Muslims were victorious or defeated. When the signs of victory appeared, the archers became covetous of the spoils, so they disobeyed the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah defeated them. However, the disbelievers did not achieve victory, because victory is for you to seize a land and remain in it.

After the battle, these disbelievers set off back to Makkah, so much so that when the Muslims went out to confront them the next day, they found no one. The Jews of Madinah exploited this development. When they met Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Tariq and others, they said to them: "If you are truly believers, why were you defeated? Return to our religion and leave the religion of Muhammad." Hudhayfah said to them: "What does your religion say about breaking covenants?" He meant what the Torah says about the Jews breaking their covenants with Allah and with Musa. Then he said: "I will not break my covenant with Muhammad as long as I live." As for Ammar, he said: "I have believed in Allah as Lord, I have believed in Muhammad as Messenger, I have believed in the Book as an imam, I have believed in the Ka'bah as qiblah, and I have believed in the believers as brothers, and I will remain upon this as long as I live."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed of what Hudhayfah and Tariq ibn Yasir had said, he was pleased with that. But the Jews were exploiting what had happened at Uhud in order to shake the faith in the hearts of the Muslims, just as they had exploited the change of the qiblah from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah to shake faith in hearts. They said: "If the qiblah facing Bayt al-Maqdis was false, why did you turn toward it? And if it was correct, why did you abandon it?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back after your belief﴾.

Observe the precision of the Qur'anic expression in His saying: ﴿of the People of the Book﴾. It is as though only some of them were trying to turn the believers away from their religion. There was, however, a small group who were contemplating belief in Muhammad (peace be upon him). Had Allah, glorified is His majesty, passed judgment on all the People of the Book, He would have closed the way before this small group to believe. That is, the Jews wish to turn you away from your religion, and these are the majority, since Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Many of the People of the Book﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿after your belief, disbelievers﴾: disbelievers in what? In what you have believed, or in what your religion requires of you. They do not do this on principle, nor out of conviction, nor for your benefit, but rather: ﴿out of envy from themselves﴾. Their religion commands them to the opposite; it commands them to believe in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ). Therefore, they do not carry out what the Torah commands them when they refuse to believe in Islam. What drives them to try to turn you away from your religion is envy (hasad). Envy is wishing for the removal of a blessing from one whom you dislike. His saying: ﴿out of envy from themselves﴾ means that this matter comes from their own selves, because they envy the Muslims for the blessing of faith, and wish that this blessing would be removed, the blessing that made the Muslims brothers, loving one another, united and bound together, while they are factions and parties. There is, however, envy that stems from the standpoint of religion, and this is permissible.

Hence the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no envy except in two: a man whom Allah has given wealth and has empowered him to spend it in truth, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom, so he judges by it and teaches it to the people." (1)

It is as though envy is forbidden outside these two cases. These Jews envied the Muslims for their religion, and this envy comes from their own selves; the Torah and their books do not endorse it. As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿after the truth has become clear to them﴾: that is, after they had become certain from the Torah of the person of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and that he is the final Prophet.

As for His saying the Exalted: ﴿So pardon and overlook until Allah brings His command﴾: what is pardon (al-'afw) and what is overlooking (al-safh)? It is said: "The wind effaced (ʿafat) the trace," meaning it wiped it out and removed it. When a person walks on sand, his foot leaves a trace, then the wind comes and effaces the trace, meaning it removes it. Therefore, pardon means that you erase from yourself the trace of any offense, as though nothing had happened. Overlooking (al-safh) means folding up the pages of this matter: do not keep it in your mind and do not let it preoccupy you. As for His saying: ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾: this situation regarding the Jews and what they do to the believers will not continue, because Allah, glorified is He, has prepared a command for them, but this command has not yet come at its appointed time and its moment. When it comes, everything will change. Therefore Allah says to the believers: you will not remain like this, but rather a day will come when you take them to account for their crimes, and this day will not be far off. When Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾, then the command of Allah must certainly come, because this is a matter that touches the very essence of faith. It is never said "until Allah brings His command" and then this command does not come. Rather, the command of Allah is undoubtedly executed, and He will surely give you victory over them. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Competent over all things﴾: Allah has absolute power over His dominion. Therefore, when He says that He will bring a command, that command will certainly be realized and accomplished. There is no power in this universe except the power of Allah, glorified is He, and no might except His might, glorified is His majesty, and no action except what He wills.

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Knowledge, Muslim in the Book of Travellers' Prayer (Salat al-Musafirin), Ibn Majah in the Book of Zakat, and Ahmad in his Musnad.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 110:

﴿And establish prayer and give zakat. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has explained that the utmost wish of the People of the Book is that they might return us to disbelief, and that this is out of envy, Allah, blessed and exalted be He, wished to make clear to us what it is that the People of the Book dislike. He said that what troubles them is the balance of justice and truth that we follow: the method of Allah, glorified and exalted be He. Therefore Allah commands the believers to remain steadfast, to hold firmly to faith, and to devote themselves to the obligations (taklif), for this is the best response to them.
