Among the obligations brought by Islam are some that require only a period of time and a little action, such as the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, giving zakat, fasting in Ramadan, and pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to make his way to it.

The testimony that there is no god but Allah is said once in a lifetime. Zakat and fasting are performed once a year. Hajj is performed once in a lifetime by the one who is able. But there are acts of worship that are repeated every day to give the believer a charge of certainty and faith, and to lift him from his worldly life to Allah, through saying "Allahu akbar" five times a day. This is the act of worship that never lapses. A person may be healthy or sick: the believer can pray standing, pray sitting, and pray lying down, and can perform the rites of prayer in his heart. Therefore this was the first act of worship mentioned in His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And establish prayer﴾, meaning: and turn attentively to the calls of your Lord to prayer. When the voice of the muezzin rises with his saying "Allahu akbar," this is a call to turn towards Allah: a turning at a known hour so that you may stand before Him, glorified and exalted be He, and be in His presence, and Allah gives you aid. For this reason the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say: "When a matter distressed him, he would pray." (1)

The meaning of "a matter distressed him" is that its causes constrained him, so that he found no way out and no path except to turn to Allah. When this happens, a person performs ablution and prays two rak'ahs beyond the obligatory prayer, then supplicates for whatever he wishes, and Allah relieves his distress. Thus ﴿establish prayer﴾ is the appropriate response to all their attempts to strip you of your religion. This obligation, prescribed to declare the loyalty of faith to Allah, is every day five times: we leave everything in this world and turn to Allah through prayer. It is the pillar of the religion and its foundation.

As for His saying, exalted be He, ﴿and give zakat﴾: giving zakat only happens when one has something beyond one's needs. It is as if Allah, glorified and exalted be He, wants us to strive in the earth to earn what we need, the needs of those we support, and to have surplus. Thereby Muslims emerge from the economic domination of the Jews by which they subjugate the Muslims.

When the believer gives zakat, it means that his activity has expanded to include his own need and the need of others. Therefore even the poor find in the surplus of the Muslims' wealth what suffices their need, and do not go to the Jew to borrow at interest. For this reason Allah, glorified and exalted be He, wants the Muslims to be complete, such that their wealth suffices the rich and the poor among them, those able to work and those unable to, and Allah, blessed and exalted be He, increases the wealth of the Muslims by more than what is taken out of it as zakat. Therefore the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

"Charity does not decrease wealth, and Allah does not increase a servant who pardons except in honour, and no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him." (2)

Zakat (zakah, purification and growth) was so named because in its outward appearance it is a loss, but in reality it is an increase. Usury (riba) outwardly appears as an increase, but in reality it is a loss. On this Allah, majestic in His majesty, says:

﴿Allah eliminates usury and gives increase for charities﴾ (part of verse 276, Surah al-Baqarah).

Then the Truthful, glorified be He, says: ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves, you will find it with Allah.﴾ Therefore the believer must be reassured that the movement of his life is reward and recompense with Allah, blessed and exalted be He. If he prays, he has a reward; if he gives zakat, he has a reward; if he gives charity, he has a reward; if he fasts, he has a reward; if he performs Hajj, he has a reward. Everything he does of Allah's method has a reward, and not a reward proportionate to the deed, but many times over the deed. Read His saying, exalted be He:

﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾ (261, Surah al-Baqarah).

Thus we know that every movement in the method of Allah has not only a reward with Allah, glorified and exalted be He, but a reward multiplied many times over. It is a reward not by human capacities but by the power of Allah, glorified be He. Therefore it is multiplied not only in number of times but also in power. It is as if the believer has no reward in the Hereafter, yet if he is given in this world, he is given an equal gift; but the believer alone has the gift of the Hereafter many times over. It is a gift that does not vanish like the gifts of this world, but remains and endures.

The good you do will not be stored for you with yourself or with one who may deny it, saying "You have nothing with me." Rather, Allah will store it for you. So consider the tranquility of the deed being in the trustworthy hand of Allah, in His will, from which nothing is hidden, and in His power, which multiplies many times over. You will find it at the moment you are most in need of it, which is the time of reckoning.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted be He, says: ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ That is, do not think that anything is hidden from Allah, or that anyone can deceive Allah. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, is Seeing of everything: not only of what is outward in you, but of what you conceal within yourself and do not reveal to any of Allah's creation. He knows everything. Read His saying, glorified and exalted be He:

﴿Our Lord, You know what we conceal and what we declare, and nothing is hidden from Allah on earth or in heaven﴾ (38, Surah Ibrahim).

Thus we are reassured that Allah is Seeing of everything. Consider His saying, majestic in His majesty, ﴿they do﴾, so that you understand the importance of action.

(1) Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud from Hudhayfah. In another narration: when a matter distressed him, he would turn to prayer.
(2) Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi from Abu Hurayrah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 111:

﴿They said: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians. Those are their wishful thoughts. Say: Produce your proof, if you are truthful.﴾

After Allah, blessed and exalted, explained how every deed performed within the methodology of God has a reward, a reward that is lasting, firm, multiplied with Allah, and preserved by the power of Allah, the Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, He wished to respond to the claims of the Jews and Christians, who try to instil despair in the hearts of the believers through falsehood and discouragement, so that they might turn away from Islam. Therefore, Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, has informed us of what they have fabricated.

Read His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians.﴾ In this noble verse, the contradiction between the statements of the Jews and the Christians becomes apparent. We have already mentioned how the Jews said, "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews," and the Christians said, "None will enter Paradise except those who are Christians." Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, exposes the contradiction in a verse that will come in His saying, blessed and exalted:

﴿The Jews say: The Christians have nothing [valid] to stand on, and the Christians say: The Jews have nothing [valid] to stand on﴾ (part of verse 113 of Surat al-Baqarah).

This means that they contradicted themselves in their statements. The Christians said that they alone would enter Paradise, and the Jews said the same. Then they said: None will enter Paradise except those who are Jewish or Christian. Then the Jews said, "The Christians have nothing to stand on," and the Christians said, "The Jews have nothing to stand on." People say: "If you are a liar, then be a good memorizer," because the one who lies has contradictory statements, since he forgets, as long as he has said something other than the truth. That is why you find that the investigator or the judge keeps asking the accused different questions until his statements contradict one another, and so he knows that he is lying. If you narrate an event as it happened, you narrate it a hundred times without any disagreement in the details. But if you lie, you contradict yourself.

Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, says: ﴿Those are their wishful thoughts.﴾ What are wishful thoughts? They are that you attach yourself to a wish for which there is no basis in reality that leads you to its fulfilment. But if the wish rests on a deed that leads you to achieving the wish, that is something else.

Some people say that wishing, even if it is not fulfilled, relaxes the soul. The soul may find rest when it attaches itself to a false hope, and it lives for days in a kind of happiness, even if it is an imaginary happiness. We say that the shock that will strike the person afterwards will destroy him. Therefore, there is never any rest in falsehood. Daydreams are not fulfilled, because they do not rest on a foundation of reality, and they give a person only a kind of distance from the truth. That is why the poet says:

*If the wish is true, it is the best of wishes;*
*and if not, we have lived with it a pleasant time.*

That is, if wishes are real, or rest upon reality, they are the best of wishes, because they remain with you. But if they are not real, the poet says:

*We lived with them a pleasant time,*
*wishes of the night of Hassan, as if*
*Layla gave us to drink from them, on thirst, cool water.*

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are their wishful thoughts﴾ shows us that wishful thoughts are the desires of fools, because they are not fulfilled. The Truth, Subhanahu, says: ﴿Say: Produce your proof.﴾ What is proof? Proof is evidence. You do not ask for proof except from a person with whom you have entered into argument and with whom your viewpoints differ. You do not ask for proof unless you are certain that your interlocutor is lying, and that he will not find evidence for what he claims.

Suppose a person claimed that you owe him money, and asked you to return it to him, while you had not taken any money from him. In this case you ask him to produce evidence: the promissory note you wrote him, or the cheque, or the receipt of deposit. At the very least, you ask him for witnesses that you took the money from him. But before you demand evidence from him, you must be certain of yourself, and that he is indeed lying and that you took nothing from him.

So His saying, the Truth, Subhanahu: ﴿Produce your proof﴾ is a statement from Allah confirming that they are liars, and that if they wished to bring evidence, they would not find in the books of Allah, nor in the words of His messengers, anything that confirms what they claim. And if they add it, that would be a fabrication against Allah, and there would be a decisive proof that this is not the word of Allah, but of their own inventions.

Thus there is no proof for what they say. And if there were any proof, even if in this statement there were a part of the truth, Allah, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, would not have demanded evidence from them.

So you do not say "Produce your proof" unless you are certain that there is no proof for what they say, because you have returned the matter to him regarding what he claims, and he wishes to establish it and does everything in pursuit of obtaining proof. Allah would not say ﴿Produce your proof﴾ unless He, Subhanahu wa Ta'ala, knew that they were lying. That is why He said: ﴿if you are truthful﴾, meaning: if you are certain that what you say is correct, because Allah knows with certainty that you are lying.

Yes, indeed! Whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good, for him is his reward with his Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.

After Allah, blessed and exalted, exposed the falsehood of the Jews and demanded evidence for their claim that none will enter Paradise except Jews and Christians, He came with the reality of the matter to inform us, may His majesty be glorified, of who will enter Paradise. He said: "Yes" (bala).

When you read "bala," know that it is a particle of response, and it must be preceded by a statement and a negation. If a person says to you, "I have no debt upon you," and you reply "Yes" (na'am), you have confirmed that he owes no debt. But if you say "Yes" (bala), that means he does owe you a debt and that he is lying in what he said. Thus "bala" comes as an answer to establish the negation of what preceded it.

They said, ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾. When Allah says to them "Yes" (bala), this means that their statement is not correct, and that others than these will enter it. And it does not mean that every Jew and every Christian will enter Paradise, because Allah, glorified and exalted, has ruled, when Islam came, that whoever does not submit will not enter Paradise. Read His saying, may His majesty be glorified:

﴿And whoever desires other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran, 85).

Why did Allah, glorified and exalted, not say that neither Jews nor Christians will enter it? Because the Qur'an is eternal (azali). What does "eternal" mean? It means that it addresses matters from the beginning of creation until the Day of Resurrection. If He had said, "None will enter Paradise except one who believes in Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace," this would have been an overreach, because there were those who believed in Moses during his mission, were contemporaries of him, followed him, and whose religion was good, and who died before reaching Muhammad, peace be upon him. Will such a person not enter Paradise and be rewarded for his good deeds? No. He enters, and his station is according to his deeds, and he is rewarded with the best reward. Likewise, among the Christians were those who believed in Jesus during his lifetime, were contemporaries of him, carried out his teachings and method, and then died before Muhammad, peace be upon him, was sent. Will such a person not enter Paradise? No, he enters, and his station is according to his work, and he is rewarded with the best reward. But after Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, and Islam came and the Qur'an was revealed, whoever does not believe in the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, will not enter Paradise, and indeed will not see it. For this reason, the word of Allah came precise, wronging none of His creatures.

So His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good﴾ means: none will enter Paradise except one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good. One may submit his face to Allah while being a hypocrite, who shows something other than what he conceals. We say that the hypocrites were not doers of good, but were doers of evil, because they had two personalities: a believing personality before people, and a disbelieving one in reality, or in their hearts.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿whoever submits his face to Allah﴾ indicates that everything submitted to Allah, because the face is the most noble thing in a human being. In it is discernment, in it is identity, in it is individuality, and it is the highest part of the body. When they defined man, they said he is a rational animal, meaning a thinking animal, and some said he is an animal of upright stature, meaning his stature is raised. The raised stature above the rest of the body is the face. Man is raised above the rest of the earth's kinds, so he is raised above the other kinds, and his face is raised above the rest of him. So if he submits his face to Allah, he has submitted the noblest thing in him to Allah. For this reason it was said: the closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating. Why? Because he brings the face with which Allah elevated and honored him, and placed it level with his feet, so that the most complete thing in him is brought down to the lowest thing, and nothing remains with him by which he can display pride before Allah.

The Truthful, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿then for him is his reward with his Lord﴾. The phrase "his reward with his Lord" shows that Allah did not make us compelled, but imposed obligation upon us and made us free to act or not act. If we act, we have a reward. And since the obligation is from Allah, glorified and exalted, it is logical that the reward be with Allah, and that there be no fear or grief. For fear is of something that will happen, and grief comes over something that has already happened. Neither of these occurs when our reward is with Allah.

When a person has a right with his equal, he may fear that the equal will deny this right, or covet it, or need it and so claim he has no entitlement to it. But Allah, glorified and exalted, is free of the worlds. For this reason He does not covet what is in our hands of good, because it is from Him, nor does He covet what we have of wealth, because He has the treasuries of the heavens and the earth.

Allah, glorified, does not deny any of our rights, because He gives us from His bounty and increases us. Therefore, with what is with Allah there is no fear for it; rather, it is multiplied and increases. And there is no grief over what is with Allah, because a person grieves when some good escapes him, but what is with Allah remains; it does not escape you and you do not escape it. There is nothing with Allah, glorified and exalted, over which you grieve because it has passed. For this reason the saying of the Truthful, glorified and exalted, is: ﴿and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾, the most precise description that can be given of the state of the believers in the Hereafter: that they will be joyful with what is with Allah, with no fear or grief among them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 113:

﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything," while they recite the Scripture. Likewise said those who have no knowledge the same as their statement. So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they used to differ.﴾ (2:113)

We say: the truest of what the Jews and Christians have said is that each group accused the other of being "not upon anything." The Jews said, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians said, "The Jews are not upon anything." What is remarkable is that both groups are People of the Book: the Jews are People of the Book and the Christians are People of the Book. Yet each of them accuses the other of having no faith, and thereby they become equal to the polytheists (mushrikun).

Those who say that the People of the Book are "not upon anything" are the polytheists: they say the Jews are not upon anything and the Christians are not upon anything. And the Jews say the polytheists are not upon anything, and the Christians say the polytheists are not upon anything. Then the Exalted and Glorified says: ﴿Likewise said those who have no knowledge the same as their statement﴾. Thus we have three groups confronting the Islamic call: a group that believes in no heavenly method and no divine message, and these are the polytheists; and two groups that have faith, prophets and books, namely the Jews and the Christians. Therefore the Exalted and Glorified says: ﴿Likewise said those who have no knowledge the same as their statement﴾, meaning those who know no religion, know no God, and know nothing of the heavenly method. They have united in speech with the Jews and the Christians, and their statement has become one.

It was expected that the People of the Book, who have a connection with heaven, books sent down from Allah, and messengers who came to them for guidance, would be distinguished above the polytheists. But those who know and those who do not know have become equal. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Likewise said those who have no knowledge the same as their statement﴾. Since the three groups have said the same thing about one another, the scale of the disagreement between them is great, not small, because each one accuses the other of having no religion.

Who judges this great disagreement? Only Allah judges it, for He knows everything, and He is the One able to separate them with truth. And when is the time of this separation or judgment? Is it in this world? No. The world is an abode of testing, not an abode of reckoning, accountability, or the settling of matters of faith. Therefore the judgment between them takes place on the Day of Resurrection, in the sight of all of creation.

The Exalted and Glorified says: ﴿So Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they used to differ.﴾ The meaning of "judgment" here is not the clarification of who is mistaken and who is correct, for all three groups are mistaken. And all three groups, in their denial of Islam, have left the framework of faith. The judgment will come on the Day of Resurrection to make this clear and to confront the opponents with punishment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 114:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein and strives for their destruction? Those would not have entered them except in fear. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.﴾

Having shown us the position of the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists toward one another and toward Islam, and how these three groups confront Islam with hostility and accuse one another of falsehood, each group charging the others with being upon baseless belief, the Exalted, Majestic is He, wished to warn them against war against Islam and against opposing this religion, so He said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein﴾. The mosques of Allah are the places in which prostration to Allah takes place. Prostration is the sign of submission and the sign of servitude, as we have explained, because you place the most noble thing in you, which is your face, upon the earth, in submission to Allah and humility before Him.

Before Islam, it was not possible for the followers of any religion to pray except in a place specific to their religion, a designated place in which prayer is not permitted anywhere else. Then Allah brought Islam and made the whole earth a mosque and made it pure (ṭahūr). The meaning of the whole earth being a mosque is an expansion for the servants of Allah in the places where they meet their Lord and in the places where they worship Him, so that you can meet Allah in any place and at any time, because He does not specify for you a particular place in which prayer is valid only there. If you wish to pray two units (rak'ah) to Allah beyond the obligatory prayers, such as the prayer of thanks, the prayer of guidance (istikhārah), or the prayer of fear, or any of the voluntary prayers which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us, you can perform it at any time. It is as if you meet Allah, glory be to Him, wherever and whenever you wish.

Since Allah, blessed and exalted is He, has bestowed favour upon His Messenger (ﷺ) and upon his community by making the earth for them a mosque and a means of purification, He only intends to widen the circle in which the servants meet their Lord.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been given five things which were not given to any prophet before me: I was helped with awe for a distance of a month's journey; the earth was made for me a mosque and a means of purification, so whichever man of my community is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray; spoils were made lawful for me, which were not lawful for anyone before me; I was given intercession; and every prophet used to be sent to his people specifically, while I was sent to all mankind." (1)

But why did Allah single out the community of Muhammad with this blessing? Because Islam came in tandem with the ascents of the intellect and the ambitions of this world. Whenever the intellect advances in worldly sciences, it uncovers laws and overcomes obstacles, and it brings forth innovations and inventions that captivate people's minds and draw them away from religion, so they worship causes instead of the Creator of causes.

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wishes to make their worship of Him always easy, so as to protect them from this trial. He, majestic is He, wants us, when we see television, for example, transmitting events from the farthest parts of the earth to the farthest parts, and from the moon to the earth at the very moment they occur, to prostrate to Allah for His blessings which He has revealed to us, wherever we may be. The properties of the atmosphere have existed in the universe since Allah created the heavens and the earth. No one among the creatures of Allah placed them in the universe of Allah in these days; rather they were created together with the creation of the universe. Allah willed that we should not perceive their existence and use them until these days. So we must prostrate to Allah in gratitude for His blessings, which have disclosed to us secrets in the universe that we did not know. These secrets show us the precision of creation and bring us closer to the matters of the unseen.

So if we are told that on the Day of Resurrection all of Allah's creation will stand and witness the reckoning, and that each one of them will see the reckoning at the moment it occurs, we do not marvel and say, "This is impossible," because the important events of the world we now see all at the moment they occur, while we are at ease, sitting in our homes before the television. That is, we see them all at one time without effort. If this is the capacity of humans for humans, then how about the capacity of the Creator of humans?

When we see the secrets of Allah's laws in His universe, we must prostrate to the greatness of the Creator, glory be to Him, who placed all this knowledge and miraculous design in the universe. This prostration requires that the whole earth be mosques, so that you, in your place, can prostrate to Allah in gratitude, and you do not have to go to another place which may be distant or whose road is arduous, so that this would make you forget the gratitude to Allah and prostration to Him. Allah, glory be to Him, has willed to widen for the believers in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the circle of meeting with their Lord, because there are things which the Muhammadan message will come to reveal to the creatures of Allah at their appointed time. Whenever a secret of the secrets of existence is uncovered, man becomes deluded by himself. And since arrogance has entered the human soul, Allah must place in the universe what counterbalances this arrogance.

Things were the opposite of this before the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ). Affairs were natural: when the rains were withheld and the springs and wells dried up, they had no recourse but to turn to the sky with the prayer for rain (ṣalāt al-istisqā'). Likewise in every matter that was difficult for them to face. But now, after Allah has disclosed to His creatures some of His secrets in His universe, there are more than one means by which a person can confront a number of the crises of the universe. These means have led humans to believe that they are capable of solving their problems far from Allah, glory be to Him, by their own efforts. Thus dependence on creation began instead of dependence on the Truth. Therefore the word of the Truth, glory be to Him, was revealed:

﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is in a glass, the glass as if it were a pearly star lit from a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things. [He is lit] in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned﴾ (from verse 35 and verse 36 of Surah al-Nur).

What are these houses in which people see the light of Allah, blessed and exalted is He? They are the mosques. Those who maintain the mosques and who are constant in prayer therein are the ones who see the light of Allah. So when a people come who dare against them and prevent the name of Allah from being mentioned therein, it means that the believers who maintain these mosques are weak in faith and weak in religion, so their enemies have become bold against them. For if they were strong, their enemy would not dare to prevent the mention of Allah's name in the mosques of Allah, or to strive to ruin them so that they are demolished and the Friday prayer is no longer established in them. But at the moment someone appears to ruin one of the houses of Allah, the people rise to prevent him and to restrain his hand; that is when faith is strong. If they leave him, then the believers have been humiliated before their enemy. Why? Because the unbeliever who wishes to extinguish a place where the light of Allah shines upon His creatures lives within the movement of evil in existence, which grows and strengthens whenever non-believers are able to prevent the name of Allah from being mentioned in His house and to ruin it.

As for the word of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿Those would not have entered them except in fear﴾. That is, these unbelievers were not permitted to enter the mosques of Allah except in fear that the believers, the people of the mosque and those who pray in it, would seize them. If they enter without fear, it means that the restraint of faith in the souls of the believers has weakened.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is more unjust﴾. Its meaning is that there is no one more unjust than the one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned therein. That is, this is the great injustice, the injustice of the highest degree. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and strives for their destruction﴾, that is, for their removal, or for their remaining unfit for the performance of worship. Striving for the ruin of a mosque is demolishing it.

The Exalted concludes the noble verse with His words: ﴿For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾. That is, Allah will not leave them, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Rather, disgrace will befall them in this world. Disgrace is the ugly thing that you dislike people seeing you in. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾ is a manifestation of Allah's jealousy for His houses. Look at what Allah made them taste in this world in regard to the Jews of Madinah who used to strive for the ruin of the mosques of Allah: their wealth was taken and they were expelled from their homes. That is an event, and this is the meaning of His saying, "disgrace in this world." As for the Hereafter, the enemies of Allah will be reckoned with a severe reckoning for their arrogance toward the mosques of Allah, glory be to Him. But at the same time, the believers who remained silent about this and were lax in supporting the religion of Allah and defending the houses of Allah will also face a painful punishment.

I warn every believer not to be lax or weak before those who try to prevent the mention of Allah in His mosques, for in that case he is committing their very sin and perhaps more. Allah will not leave him on the Day of Resurrection, but will drive him to the Fire.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim and al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Jabir.

Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 115:

﴿To Allah belong the east and the west; so wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah. Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted be He, had explained the recompense of those who ruin the mosques of Allah and demolish them, and who prevent His name from being mentioned in them, and the punishment that awaits them in the Hereafter, He wished to remind us that enforcing this in a complete and total manner is an impossible undertaking, because the whole earth is a mosque. To ruin it would mean to ruin the whole earth, for Allah, blessed and exalted, is present in every place. Wherever you are, you will find Allah turning toward you with His manifestations.

As for His saying, ﴿Then there is the Face of Allah﴾, it means: there is the Face of Allah. And His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾, means: do not feel constricted about a place where you meet your Lord, for Allah is All-Encompassing, present in every place in this universe and in every place beyond this universe. But when Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says, ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾, it does not mean only specifying the direction of the east or the direction of the west. Rather, it extends to all directions: its east and its west, its north and its south, the northeast and the southwest, and every direction you can imagine.

But why does the verse mention only the east and the west? Because all other directions are determined by the rising and setting of the sun. There is a northeast, a southeast, a northwest and a southwest. Moreover, east and west are known to people by their innate nature: no one is ignorant of where the sun rises or where it sets, for you see a sunrise and a sunset every day. When Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says, ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾, its meaning is not to restrict ownership to these two directions, but what is known as *ikhtisas bil-taqdim* (specification through prior mention). You say, "I wrote with the pen and I came by the car," meaning that writing is specifically by the pen and coming is specifically by the car. This is what is known as *ikhtisas* (specification): this belongs to such-and-such and nothing else has a share in it. Therefore, the meaning of ﴿To Allah belong the east and the west﴾ is that ownership belongs to Allah, glorified and exalted be He, and no one shares it with Him. And the changing of the qibla from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah does not mean that Allah, blessed and exalted, was in Bayt al-Maqdis and then turning toward the Ka'bah does not mean that Allah, majestic in majesty, is in the Ka'bah.

The unification of the qibla means no more than that Muslims have one direction in prayer, and that is evidence of the unity of purpose. You must distinguish between a direction in prayer and a direction outside prayer. In prayer, we all face a specific place that Allah has chosen for us to face in prayer. People pray throughout the whole world facing the Ka'bah. The Ka'bah's place is one and does not change, but our direction toward it from the regions of the earth does change. One faces north, one faces south, one faces east, and one faces west. Each of us faces a different direction according to the spot on the earth where he is located, yet we all face the Ka'bah. Despite the difference of our directions, we meet in facing one single place.

Allah, majestic in majesty, wants us to know that when we say, ﴿To Allah belong the east﴾, we should not assume that "the east" is a single direction. Rather, the east varies with the place: every place on earth has an east and a west. When the sun rises in one place, at the same time it sets in another place. It rises for me and sets for others; after a minute it rises for one people and sets for others. If you look at east and west in relation to the apparent rising and setting of the sun, you find that the east and the west never cease on the surface of the earth. In every minute there is a rising and a setting.

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Encompassing﴾, it means that He is vast enough for all His dominion; nothing preoccupies Him from anything else. For this reason, when Imam 'Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, was asked, "How does Allah reckon all people at one time?" he said, "Just as He provides for them all at one time."

Thus, nothing preoccupies Allah from anything else, and He needs nothing in His work. His work is only ﴿Be, and it is﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 116:

﴿And they say, "Allah has taken a son." Exalted is He! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him.﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted, made clear that everything in the universe belongs to Him, and that nothing preoccupies Him from anything else, He wished to refute those who tried to give Allah a helper in His dominion, those who said, "Allah has taken a son." Allah, blessed and exalted, responded to them: why would He take a son when to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, all devoutly obedient to Him? The response is focused on three points.

His saying, ﴿Exalted is He﴾, means He is far exalted above having a son.

His saying, ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾: if this is His dominion, and if the whole universe is His creation and subject to Him, then what need has He for a son?

His saying, ﴿all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾, means that everyone in the heavens and the earth worships Allah, majestic in His majesty, and acknowledges His divinity.

The matter of Allah having a son is mentioned nineteen times in the Noble Qur'an, together with the refutation of it. Because it is a matter at the very summit of belief, it has been repeated, and the refutation of it repeated, again and again. If you look at those who said this, you will find several statements. There is the saying of the polytheists, and read the Qur'an:

﴿Surely they say, out of their own falsehood, "Allah has begotten." And indeed they are liars. Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾ (Surat al-Saffat).

And the saying of the Jews, as the Qur'an relates to us:

﴿And the Jews said, "Ezra is the son of Allah."﴾ (part of verse 30, Surat al-Tawbah).

And the saying of the Christians:

﴿And the Christians said, "The Messiah is the son of Allah."﴾ (part of verse 30, Surat al-Tawbah).

Then, in the story of the creation of Jesus, peace be upon him, from Mary without a father, Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Indeed you have brought forth something monstrous. The heavens nearly rupture from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son. There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant.﴾ (Surat Maryam).

Allah, glorified and exalted, wants us to know that this claim is a grave, abhorrent, reprehensible and detestable assertion. Surat Maryam treated the matter at length: a treatment in which every kind of creation in the universe other than man takes part, the reaction of the heavens, the earth, the mountains and other creatures of Allah, which curse everyone who says this. Indeed, as if feeling the enormity of the crime, the heavens nearly rupture, that is, fall in small pieces; the earth splits, that is, is torn apart; and the mountains collapse, that is, fall down as dust. All this is because of the horror of what was said and the falsehood of what was said, for this claim is a fabrication against Allah. All these verses came in Surat Maryam, which gave us the miracle of Jesus' creation. The matter also appeared in several other surahs.

The question here is: what is the suspicion that led them to say "Allah's son"? What drove them to resort to this fabrication? The Qur'an says of Jesus son of Mary: he is a word of Allah which He cast to Mary. We say to them: we are all a word, "Be!"

Why have you been tested concerning Jesus son of Mary with this test? Allah, glorified and exalted, explains the matter, saying:

﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾ (Surat Ali 'Imran).

His saying "like the likeness of Adam" is merely to match the opponent's argument. But the miracle in Adam is stronger than in Jesus, peace be upon him. You were tested with Jesus because the element of fatherhood is absent. In Adam both the element of fatherhood and the element of motherhood were absent. So the miracle is greater. It would have been more fitting for you to be tested with Adam instead of Jesus. And strangely, you did not mention the test in Adam, yet you mentioned the test in what has an element absent from one of the two absent elements in Adam. It was necessary that you attribute this matter to Adam, but you did not do so.

As for the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, Allah told him that the matter is not one of denial, but that it is a false claim. Read His saying, blessed and exalted:

﴿Say: "If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers."﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf).

That is, it would not harm Allah, glorified and exalted, to have a son, but Allah, majestic in His majesty, has not taken a son. It is not possible for people to worship something that did not belong to Allah; rather they invented and fabricated it.

Allah, majestic in His majesty, says: ﴿And they say, "Allah has taken a son. Exalted is He! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth"﴾. His saying, ﴿Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, gives Allah, glorified and exalted, ownership of everything in the universe, and ownership contradicts sonship. Why? Because ownership means that everything in the universe is from Allah's creation; everything is created by Him without any opponent. And since He is its creator and originator, that thing cannot be part of Him, because the one who creates something is an agent, and the agent has a product, and the product is never of the same kind as the agent. Have you ever seen someone make a craft out of his own flesh? The one who makes a car, for instance: did he make it from his own flesh or from human flesh? Likewise the airplane, the chair, the clock, and the television. Are these manufactured things of the same kind as the one who made them? Certainly not.

Therefore, since it is ownership, it is not said to be of the same kind as its maker, and it is not said that the agent brought into existence something of his own kind, because the agent never brings into existence something of his own kind. Every agent brings into existence something lesser than himself. So His saying "Exalted is He" is a declaration of His transcendence, blessed and exalted. Why? Because a son is taken to preserve the life of his father, which the reality of the universe does not guarantee for him: he carries his name after he dies and inherits his property. So he is for the preservation of his kind, and one who wants the preservation of his kind is not satisfied with having just one son.

Suppose, for the sake of argument, that He had one son. It would be expected that this son belongs to Him. But we have not seen children of those who claim he is the son of Allah. And before the son exists, what was Allah, glorified and exalted, doing when He had no son? And what new thing came upon Allah and His universe after He supposedly took a son? Nothing changed in existence. Therefore the existence of a son for the deity gave Him no manifestation of power, because the universe before the supposed son came into existence and after it has not changed in any way.

So what is the reason for taking a son? Help? Allah's power is not diminished. Guarantee of life? Allah's life is eternal. He is the One who created life, He grants it, and He is living and does not die. So what need has He for any guarantee of life? The Truth, blessed and exalted, is one to whom things submit, meaning He is capable of bringing a thing into manifestation according to His decree. He, majestic in His majesty, possesses the perfection of attributes from eternity, and by the perfection of His attributes He created and brought this universe into being. Therefore He has no need of any of His creatures, because at the moment of creation He had all the attributes of the power to create. Indeed, before He created, He had all the attributes of the Creator, and by these attributes He created. Allah, glorified and exalted, was Creator before anyone existed to subdue Him, and was Ever-Relenting before anyone existed to repent to Him. By these attributes He brought into being, created, provided, subdued, and relented toward His creatures.

So this whole universe added no attribute of perfection to Allah; rather Allah, by the perfection of His attributes, is the One who brought it into being. Therefore Allah, glorified and exalted, says in a sacred hadith: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were to stand in one open place and ask Me, and I gave each person his request, that would not diminish what I have of dominion any more than a needle diminishes when dipped in the sea."(1)

Then, if Allah, glorified and exalted, had a wife and a son, who came into existence first? If Allah, glorified and exalted, existed first and then brought into being the wife and the son, then He is the Creator and they are the created. And if each of them brought himself into being, then they are three gods, not one God. So the son is either a created being or a god. The first perfection of Allah was not increased by the son in anything, and hence his existence has no value. When the Truth, blessed and exalted, presents this matter, He presents it at length in many surahs of the Noble Qur'an, the first of which is Surat Maryam, in His saying:

﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son."﴾ (Surat Maryam).

He, glorified and exalted, is far above resemblance to His creation, neither in essence, nor in attributes, nor in actions. Everything you see in existence, Allah is other than it. And everything that occurs to your mind, Allah is other than that. His saying, ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾: this is a matter that contradicts taking a son, because everything in the heavens and the earth is subject to Allah.

His saying, ﴿all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾, means: submissive. This confirms for us that the universe, in the hand of Allah, is subject to the command of Allah, submitting willingly or by compulsion.

(1) Narrated by Muslim in the book of righteousness (al-birr), and narrated by Ahmad.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 117:

﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ (2:117)

After Allah, blessed and exalted, explained that their saying "Allah has taken a son" is a fabrication against Allah, the Truth wanted to draw our attention to some of His capabilities. So He, majestic is His majesty, said: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾. That is, He created the heavens and the earth, and everything in them, as a creation without any prior model. That is, there was no heaven, earth, angels, jinn, or human beings before them. Then Allah, glorified and exalted, brought into existence things similar to them in form, size, or power. That is, He, glorified is He, did not resort to what we call a mould.

The one who makes a glass cup first makes a mould into which the molten raw glass is poured, and in the end identical cups come out. Every manufacturing process other than that of Allah is carried out on the basis of making the mould first, and only after that does production begin. For this reason, the real cost lies in preparing a good mould that gives us an image of what we want. The one who bakes a loaf of bread, for example, may not use a mould, but he imitates something that already existed. The shape of the loaf and its material already existed, and he imitates them each time. However, he cannot give exact sameness in weight, shape, or roundness. Rather, there is variation in the imitation, and perfection in the craft is not attained.

When Allah, majestic is His majesty, created the creation from Adam until the Hour is established, He made the creatures similar in everything: in the composition of the body and its form, in the head, the two feet, the two hands, the two eyes, and the other members of the body, with precise sameness in form and function, such that every organ performs its task in life. But this sameness was not produced upon a mould; it was produced by the word "Be." And despite the similarity in creation, each of us differs from the other by a difference that enables you to distinguish him by knowledge and by sight. By knowledge, each of us has a fingerprint and a voiceprint that voice-recording experts can identify, and a scent print that we may not distinguish but that trained dogs can. They smell a thing and then hasten to show you its owner, even if he were among a thousand people. And a genetic signature makes the body recognise its own parts: if you bring a cell from another body, it rejects it; and if you bring a cell from the same body, it unites with it and heals its wounds.

If this is some of what science has reached, there is much more that we may reach which confirms to us that, despite the resemblance of billions of persons, each one has what distinguishes him alone, and it is not repeated in all of Allah's creation. This is the miraculous nature of creation and a proof of the all-encompassing power of Allah in His dominion.

Allah, glorified and exalted, gives us the general meaning in the Noble Qur'an: that this is among His signs, that it did not happen by chance, nor came about by an unplanned way, but is prepared by the power of Allah, glorified is He. So He, majestic is His majesty, says:

﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and your colours. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.﴾ (Surah ar-Rum, 30:22)

This difference represents to us the all-encompassing power of Allah, glorified is He, in creating without a model. Every creature differs from the one before it, the one after it, and those around it, although in general form they are alike. And if you gathered all people from the time of Adam until the Day of Resurrection, you would find them in one form, and each of them differs from the other. There are not two humans among the creation of Allah such that each is an exact copy of the other. This is the precision of workmanship, and this is what we understand from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Originator (Badi')﴾. Precision gives wisdom, and manifestation in multiple forms gives power. For this reason, after we die and our elements scatter in the dust, Allah will gather us on the Day of Resurrection. The miracle of this gathering is that each person will be raised from those same elements, in that same image and that same form which he had in this world. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, said:

﴿We have known what the earth diminishes of them, and with Us is a preserved record.﴾ (Surah Qaf, 50:4)

So Allah, glorified and exalted, by the all-encompassing power of His bringing into being, has created us; and by the all-encompassing power of His re-creation, He revives us after death, in our form, our flesh, our attributes, and every atom within us. Is there any precision after that?

If we brought the most skilful and proficient craftsmen and said to him: "Make for us something you excel at." Then when he made it, we said to him: "Make its like." He cannot produce a model like it with the same specifications, because he lacks the precise measures that would provide him with the same specifications with which he made it. He can give us a similar model, but not exactly as he made it. But Allah, glorified and exalted, takes back His creation, and at the hour of resurrection or the hour of their raising, He returns them with the same components they had, without addition or subtraction. This is because Allah, majestic is His majesty, does not create according to fixed moulds, but says to a thing: "Be," and it is.

The noble verse says: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

﴿Be (kun)﴾ occurs frequently in the Noble Qur'an. In the language there is a thing called the homonym (al-mushtarak al-lafzi): a word that is one but whose meanings differ according to context. For example, the word qada (قضى) has several meanings, and it has a meaning that gathers all its meanings. Sometimes the Truth uses it in the sense of "finished" or "ended," in His saying:

﴿So when you have completed your rites, remember Allah as you remember your fathers or with a greater remembrance.﴾ (part of 2:200)

Meaning: when you have finished the rites of Hajj.

And at another time He, glorified is He, says:

﴿So decide what you will decide. You only decide regarding this worldly life.﴾ (part of 20:72)

The meaning is: do what you wish. And in another verse Allah, exalted is He, says:

﴿And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair.﴾ (part of 33:36)

The meaning is that when Allah says something, the believers are not left the right of choice. And at another time, majestic is His majesty, Allah depicts the disbelievers in the Hereafter, when they are in the Fire, wishing to be relieved of the punishment by death.

Read His saying, glorified is He:

﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us." He will say, "Indeed, you will remain.﴾ (Surah az-Zukhruf, 43:77)

Here "liyaqḍi 'alayna" means: let Him cause us to die.

And another meaning in His saying:

﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided.﴾ (part of 14:22)

That is: when the matter has ended and the reckoning has occurred. And in another place His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So when Musa had fulfilled the term and set out with his family﴾ (part of 28:29).

"Qaḍā al-ajal" here means: completed the term. And in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And He will judge between them with justice, and they will not be wronged.﴾ (part of 10:54)

That is: He will judge and decide between them. And His saying, majestic is His majesty:

﴿And We conveyed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you will cause corruption in the land twice.﴾ (part of 17:4)

Meaning: We informed the Children of Israel in their Scripture.

So "qaḍā" has multiple meanings determined by context. But there is one meaning in which all the meanings meet, and that is "decided," that is "judged," and this is the mother meaning.

Thus the meaning of His saying: ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ is: when He judges a judgment, it comes to be. And we must note the Truth's saying: ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be."﴾ The meaning of "He says to it" is that the matter exists with Him, exists in His knowledge, but has not reached our knowledge. That is, it is not a new matter, because since Allah, glorified is He, said "He says to it," as if majestic is He addresses something existent. But this existent is not in our knowledge, and we know nothing of it; rather it exists in the knowledge of Allah, glorified and exalted. For this reason it has been said that Allah has matters which He manifests but does not originate: they are present with Him, because the pens have been lifted and the scrolls have dried, but He manifests them to us, we who do not know them, so that we come to know them.

﴿And those who do not know say, "Why does Allah not speak to us, or why does no sign come to us?" Likewise said those before them, similar to their words. Their hearts have become alike. We have made the signs clear for a people who are certain.﴾

When the Exalted says ﴿those who do not know﴾, He means that they know nothing of the Book of Allah, because they are disbelievers. These people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that Allah speak to them. To be spoken to by Allah means to hear words from Allah, the Exalted, just as Musa heard the speech of Allah.

And what did they want from the speech of Allah, blessed and exalted is He? Did they want Allah to tell them that He had sent Muhammad as a messenger to convey to them the way of the heavens? It is as if all the miracles with which Allah supported His Messenger (ﷺ), foremost among them the noble Qur'an, were not sufficient to convince them. Yet the Qur'an is an inimitable speech, and it was brought by an unlettered messenger. They asked him about matters that had happened, and Allah revealed them to him in detail. The Qur'an came to challenge them concerning future events and the secrets of the human soul. This would have been enough for them had they used their minds, but they wanted obstinacy. Whenever a sign came to them, they denied it and asked for another sign. Allah, the Exalted, has informed us that human nature cannot receive from Allah directly. Recite His saying, the Exalted:

﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger who reveals by His permission what He wills.﴾ (Part of verse 51, Surat al-Shura).

So humans, even the one chosen by Allah and qualified to receive from Allah, are not spoken to by Allah except through revelation, or the inspiration of a thought (ilham, inspiration cast into the heart), or from behind a veil as He spoke to Musa, or by sending a messenger who conveys the way of Allah to the people. As for direct contact, the humanness of creation prevents it.

Then the Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿or a sign come to us﴾. The signs that the disbelievers ask for, and that Allah, the Exalted, brings and fulfills for them, they do not believe in; rather, they increase in disbelief and obstinacy. Allah, whose majesty is great, says:

﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her by it.﴾ (Part of verse 59, Surat al-Isra).

So the signs that the disbelievers ask for in order to believe do not make them believe; rather, they increase in disbelief, even if they know with certainty that these signs are from Allah, the Exalted, as happened to the family of Pharaoh. Recite the saying of the Truthful, the Exalted:

﴿So when Our signs came to them as visible, they said, "This is clear magic." And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance. So see how was the end of the corrupters.﴾ (Surat al-Naml, verses 13–14).

Thus their request that Allah speak to them or that a sign come to them was out of obstinacy and disbelief. The Truthful, the Exalted, says: ﴿Likewise said those before them, similar to their words.﴾ The Children of Israel said to Musa, "Show us Allah openly." Those who do not know said, "Why does Allah not speak to us?" But those who said, "Show us Allah openly," had knowledge, because they believed in the Torah. So those who know and those who do not know became equal. Therefore Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Their hearts have become alike.﴾ That is, the hearts of those who were submissive to the way and the hearts of those who do not submit to a way have become alike in one logic.

If it had been said that "those who do not know" said this, but not "those who know," the matter would have been easier, and we would say that their ignorance is what prompted them to say what they said. But what excuse did those who had knowledge and had a Book have for saying, "Show us Allah openly"? So there is something common between them: their hearts have become alike in desire. The source of every behavioral movement or bodily action is nothing but the heart, from which the motives of action proceed. As long as the heart is not sincere to Allah, the one who knows and the one who does not know are equal.

Then the Truthful, the Exalted, says: ﴿We have made the signs clear for a people who are certain.﴾ What is certainty (yaqin)? It is the settling of a matter in the heart in a way that admits no doubt and no shaking. The matter cannot come out again to the intellect to be debated anew, because it has become certainty. Certainty comes from the report of one you trust, whose reports become certainty for you. So if Allah says something, it is certainty. And if the Messenger (ﷺ) says something, his speech is true. This is why, as part of the authenticity of faith, when it was said to our master Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), "Your companion says that he was taken up to the seventh heaven and went to Bayt al-Maqdis in a single night," he said, "If he said it, then he has spoken the truth."

His certainty arose from the report of one he trusted, and this we call knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin). It may rise further to become eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin), when you see the thing with your own eye after having heard of someone else's sight of it. Then you enter into the reality of the thing, and it becomes truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). So certainty is knowledge when it comes from the report of one you trust; it is eye of certainty when the matter has been witnessed with the eye; and truth of certainty is that you enter into the reality of the thing. Allah, the Exalted, explains this in His saying:

﴿Competition in increase distracted you until you visited the graves. No! You will know. Then no! You will know. No! If you knew with certainty of knowledge, you would surely see the Hellfire.﴾ (Surat al-Takathur, verses 1–6).

This is the first stage, that knowledge of certainty comes to us from Allah, the Exalted. Then the second stage comes in the saying of the Blessed and Exalted:

﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.﴾ (Surat al-Takathur, verse 7).

That is, you will see Hell with your own eyes on the Day of Resurrection. This is knowledge of certainty and eye of certainty. After that comes truth of certainty, in His saying, the Exalted:

﴿But if he is of the deniers, the astray, then a welcome of boiling water, and burning in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the truth of certainty.﴾ (Surat al-Waqi'a, verses 92–95).

The believer, may Allah protect him, is spared from witnessing the Fire as truth of certainty. He will see it as he passes over the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), but the disbeliever is the one who will truly burn in it, in certainty of reality. The People of the Book said to their prophets things that match the words of those who do not believe. The Jews said to Musa: ﴿We will not believe you until we see Allah openly.﴾ And the Christians said to Isa: ﴿Is your Lord able to send down to us a table from the heaven?﴾ He said: ﴿Fear Allah, if you are believers.﴾ Thus the believers in the Book encouraged the unbelievers to ask to see Allah and to ask for material miracles.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 119:

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And you will not be questioned about the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾ (119)

Here we must note that when God, glorified and exalted is He, tells us about a matter of His action, He always uses the plural of majesty, which we call the "nun of the speaker" (nun al-'azamah). We observe that kings and heads of states use the plural of majesty, saying "we, so-and-so, have decreed what follows." It is as if the majesty in a human being has harnessed various talents to carry out the decision issued by the head of state. Police, judiciary, the state and the armed forces take part in its execution if it is a decision of war. Multiple talents from different groups join together to carry out the decision. God, blessed and exalted is He, possesses absolute perfection. Everything that is necessary for execution is among the attributes of God, glorified and exalted is He. So when God, majestic in His majesty, speaks of an act that requires the perfection of talents from God, blessed and exalted is He, He says "Inna" (We):

﴿Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian.﴾ (9) (Surah al-Hijr; al-Sha'rawi's citation is Surah al-Hijr 15:9, given here as "Surat al-Hajj" in the source)

But when God speaks of His sole divinity and of His worship alone, He uses the singular pronoun, such as His saying, glorified is He:

﴿Indeed, I am God; there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.﴾ (14) (Surah Ta-Ha)

He does not say "fa'budna" (worship Us). Thus, in every act God, glorified is He, uses the plural of majesty, and in every command related to worship and monotheism He uses the singular. This is so that we understand that the act from God is not the product of His power alone, nor His knowledge alone, nor His wisdom alone, nor His mercy alone, but rather every act of God's acts is one in which the attributes of absolute perfection of God are integrated.

The nun of majesty comes to draw our attention to this truth, to make clear to the intellect the integration of attributes in God. For you may have power but not knowledge, may have knowledge but not power, or may have knowledge while wisdom is absent from you. Thus the integration of attributes is required.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth﴾ means: We have sent you as a messenger with the truth. The truth (al-haqq) is the established thing that does not change and does not contradict itself. If you see an event before you and then are asked to relate what you saw, you narrate what happened. If you are asked after a period to narrate it again, you narrate it with the same details. But if you are lying, your statements will contradict one another. That is why it was said: "If you are a liar, then be a good rememberer." The truth does not contradict itself and does not change. Since the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent with the truth, he is obligated to convey it to people, and the truth will remain truth until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾. Good tidings (bushra) is the announcement of something that pleases you, whose time is coming. Warning (indhar) is the announcement of something that distresses you, whose time is coming, which you may perhaps be able to avert. A bringer of what? And a warner of what? He brings good tidings to those who believe of the bliss of Paradise, and warns the disbeliever of the punishment of the Fire. Good tidings and warning require a method of conveying. For the one who believes in it, it is good tidings to him; and for the one who does not believe, it is a warning to him.

Then the Truth, majestic in His majesty, says: ﴿And you will not be questioned about the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾ That is, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not responsible for those who will throw themselves into the Fire and punishment. He is not responsible for their guidance; rather, his duty is only to convey. Read His saying, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps if they do not believe in this discourse.﴾ (6) (Surah al-Kahf)

And He, majestic in His majesty, says:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself that they are not believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them from the heaven a sign, so their necks would remain humbled before it.﴾ (3-4) (Surah al-Shu'ara')

So if God, glorified is He, had wanted us to believe by compulsion and force, not one of creation could have disbelieved. But He, blessed and exalted is He, wants us to come to Him with hearts that love Him, not with hearts forced into faith. God, glorified is He, created people free to believe or not to believe, and it is not for a messenger to compel people to believe by force, because if God had willed, He would have compelled all His creation.

As for the companions of the Blazing Fire, they are the people of the Fire. "Al-Jahim" is derived from "al-juhuh" (blazing, ferocity). "Jamahat al-nar" means the fire raged, i.e., it became agitated; when you see a fire blazing, it is said "jamahat al-nar," meaning its flame has become intensified such that it consumes everything that reaches it and never subsides.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to reassure His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that his heart should not be preoccupied with those who disbelieved, because he has warned them. This is his duty, and this is the mission with which God has charged him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 120:

﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion. Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance." And if you followed their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have from Allah no protector or helper.﴾

The Jews used to enter upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a manner of meanness and deceit. They would say, "Make peace with us," meaning: tell us what is in our book, so that we may see whether we follow you or not. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, wanted to cut off from the Jews the path of plotting and scheming against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, by declaring that neither the Jews nor the Christians would follow your religion. Rather, they wish that you would follow their religion. You want them to be with you, and they hope that you will be with them. So Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿And the Jews will never be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their religion.﴾

We note here the repetition of the negation, so that we understand that the pleasure of the Jews is not the pleasure of the Christians. Had the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, said, "And the Jews and the Christians will never be pleased with you," without "nor," it would mean that they are united in one pleasure, or in agreement. But they are divided, as evidenced by Allah, exalted is He, saying:

﴿And the Jews say, "The Christians are not upon anything," and the Christians say, "The Jews are not upon anything"﴾ (part of verse 113, Surat al-Baqarah).

Therefore it is not correct to say, "Nor will the Jews and the Christians be pleased with you." Allah, glorified is He, wants to say: "The Jews will never be pleased with you, and the Christians will never be pleased with you." If you were to satisfy the Jews, the Christians would not be pleased with you; and if you satisfied the Christians, the Jews would not be pleased with you.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿until you follow their religion.﴾ The millah (religion, creed) is the dīn (religion), and it was called millah because you incline toward it, even if it is false. Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿Nor are you worshipers of what I worship. Nor am I a worshiper of what you have worshiped. Nor are you worshipers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion.﴾ (Surat al-Kafirun).

So He made for them a religion while they were disbelievers and polytheists. But what protects us from following the millah of the Jews or the millah of the Christians? The Truth, may His majesty be exalted, says:

﴿Say, "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is [the only] guidance"﴾ (part of verse 73, Surat Al 'Imran).

The Jews distorted their religion, and the Christians distorted theirs. But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has with him the guidance of Allah. Guidance (hudā) is that which brings you to the goal by the shortest route, or it is the straight path, considered the shortest of the ways to the goal. The guidance of Allah is one path, whereas human guidance is that each person has a guidance springing from his own desire.

Hence these are many scattered and multiple paths that lead you to misguidance. But the guidance that leads to the Truth is one guidance: the guidance of Allah, mighty and majestic is He.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿if you followed their desires﴾ is an indication from Allah, glorified is He, that the millah of the Jews and the millah of the Christians are human desires. The plural of hawā is ahwā', and hawā is what the self desires in falsehood, far from the Truth. Therefore Allah, may His majesty be exalted, says: ﴿And if you followed their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, you would have from Allah no protector or helper.﴾

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, says to His Messenger: if you followed the crooked path, full of desires without right, whether it is the path of the Jews or the path of the Christians, after the guidance has come to you from Allah, then you would have from Allah no protector to take charge of your affairs and guard you, and no helper to support you.

This address to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ requires us to pause and reflect on how Allah addresses His Messenger ﷺ, whom He chose. When Allah directs this address to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, the intended meaning is the community (ummah) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the followers who will come after him, those whose hearts may incline toward the Jews and the Christians. As for the Messenger, Allah protected him from following them.

Allah, glorified is He, wants us to know with certainty that what He did not accept from His Messenger ﷺ, He cannot accept from anyone of his community, however high his standing. This is so that no one comes after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ claiming knowledge and saying, "We will follow the millah of the Jews or the Christians in order to draw them to us." We say to him: No. What Allah did not accept from His beloved and Messenger, He will not accept from anyone.

The citing of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as an example here is intended to show that following the millah of the Jews or the Christians is absolutely rejected under any circumstances. Allah, glorified is He, has set forth His Messenger as an example in order to cut off from those with ulterior motives every way of toying with this religion under the pretext of rapprochement with the Jews and the Christians.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 121:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recitation. It is they who believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it, it is they who are the losers.﴾

After Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had explained that the Jews and Christians had distorted their books, He wished to make clear that among the Jews and Christians there are those who did not distort their books, and that these believe in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and in his message, because they recognize him from the Torah and the Gospel.

Had Allah not mentioned this verse, [one might have thought that] those who read the Torah and the Gospel in their true form, and who consider believing in the message of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would say: "How can this condemnation apply to all Jews and all Christians when we intend to believe in Islam?" This is what is called the principle of probability, meaning that there is a significant number, however small, of Jews or Christians who consider embracing Islam as the religion of truth. There was indeed a group of Jews, forty in number, who came from Sinai with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib to bear witness before the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that they had read the undistorted Torah and had believed in his message. Allah wished to honour them and to honour every one of the People of the Book who would believe, so He, exalted is His majesty, said:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it with its true recitation﴾ (part of verse 121, surah al-Baqarah).

That is, they recite it as it was revealed, without distortion or alteration, so they know the realities pure and unmixed with human desires, and without the distortion which is the transfer of something from truth to falsehood.

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿It is they who believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it, it is they who are the losers.﴾ We observe that the noble Qur'an frequently employs comparison, to honour the believers and to instil regret into the hearts of the deniers, because comparison always makes clear the difference between two things.

Allah, glorified is He, wishes to inform those to whom He has given the Book, and who did not distort it and believed in it, that they will attain the blessing that will lead them to everlasting bliss, which is the blessing of Islam and faith; in contrast to those who distort the Torah and the Gospel, whose fate is manifest loss and abiding in the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 122:

﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and that I preferred you over the worlds.﴾ (2:122)

If we return to what we said when we addressed verse (40) of Surat al-Baqarah, and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Children of Israel, remember My favour which I bestowed upon you, and fulfil My covenant, and I will fulfil your covenant, and fear Me alone.﴾ (2:40)... Then, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, did not end the discourse with the Children of Israel in this round before reminding them of what He had begun with them. He, glorified is He, does not conclude speaking with them in this round until He has given them a final reminder of His blessings upon them and His preferring them over many of His creatures. Among the greatest manifestations of this preference is the verse in the Torah that gives good tidings of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and that is a great preference.

The reminder here of the blessing and of the favour is a rebuke to the Children of Israel, that they did not believe in the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, even though he is mentioned among them in the Torah. They should have taken this reminder seriously and hastened to believe in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, because it is a great preference from Allah, glorified and exalted is He, to them. And Allah, majestic is His majesty, said, when the Jews were seized by the quaking, and Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord for mercy, as the noble Qur'an narrates to us:

﴿And prescribe for us in this world good, and in the Hereafter; indeed, we have turned to You." He said, "My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things. So I will decree it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses.
