﴿Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes were Jews or Christians? Say: Are you more knowing, or is God? And who is more unjust than one who conceals a testimony he has from God? God is not unaware of what you do.﴾ (2:140)

The Jews and the Christians claimed that the prophets before Moses and Jesus were Jews or Christians. So the Jews claimed that they were Jews, and the Christians claimed that they were Christians. God, glorified and exalted is He, refutes them with His words: ﴿Say: Are you more knowing, or is God?﴾

The question here has only one answer, because they will not be able to say, "We are more knowing than God." We have said that when a question is posed in the noble Qur'an, its answer must be confirmed by what the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, intends, and there is only one answer to it. Therefore His words, ﴿Are you more knowing, or is God?﴾, the answer is that God is without doubt more knowing, and this is a reality.

Thus, by the question, God has in effect informed us about the matter. But note in the noble verse the mention of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes. The constant mention of Ishmael together with Isaac and Jacob indicates the unity of the faith's message from God, because Ishmael was among the Arab nation, while Isaac and Jacob were among the Children of Israel.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, speaks of the unity of the source of faith for His creatures, since there is no connection between Ishmael being for the Arabs and Isaac being for non-Arabs and the unity of the divine method. Therefore you read the saying of the Truth, exalted is He:

﴿They said: We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac, one God; and to Him we are submitting.﴾ (part of 2:133)

The God who sent Ishmael is the God who sent Isaac: one God, the One. And as long as God is one, the method of faith must be one. If disagreement occurs, the disagreement comes from humans who distort the method in order to achieve their desires and gains. ﴿Every soul earns only for itself﴾; your lineage to them will not benefit you, nor will it add anything to you in the Hereafter. If they were believers, then your disbelief and your saying "we are descended from Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac" will not benefit you. And if they were otherwise, it will not harm you at all.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 141:

﴿That is a community that has passed away; theirs is what they earned, and yours is what you have earned. And you will not be questioned about what they used to do.﴾ (2:141)

Some people say that this verse is repeated, since a verse preceding it says:

﴿Or were you witnesses when death approached Ya'qub, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Ibrahim and Isma'il and Ishaq, one God, and to Him we are Muslims." That is a community that has passed away; theirs is what they earned, and yours is what you have earned. And you will not be asked about what they used to do.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:133–134)

Some superficial readers say there is repetition in these two verses. We say: you have not understood the meaning. The first verse tells the Jews that your lineage to Ibrahim and Ishaq will not intercede for you before Allah on account of what you have distorted and altered in the Torah, and on account of what you do that is other than what Allah has legislated. So know that it is your deeds for which you will be held to account before Allah, not your lineage.

As for the verse we are discussing, they said that Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq were Jews or Christians. Allah, blessed and exalted, does not argue with them; rather He says to them, let us suppose — and this is an incorrect supposition — that Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq were Jews or Christians, this will not be an excuse for you, because for them is what they earned and for you is what you have earned. So do not take that as an argument against Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Do not say that we used to think Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq were Jews or Christians, meaning that they were not upon the religion of Islam, because this is an unacceptable argument. Are you more knowing, or is Allah, glorified is He, who testifies that they were Muslims?

Beware of saying that there is repetition. The context of the first verse says that you have no intercession on the Day of Resurrection through your lineage to Ibrahim, Isma'il and Ishaq. The context of the second verse says that you have no argument on the Day of Resurrection in your saying that they were Jews or Christians. So your lineage to them will not benefit you, and Allah will not accept your argument. Thus the meaning is entirely different, touching two different situations on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 142:

﴿They will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they had been facing?" Say, "To Allah belongs the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path."﴾

This verse was revealed to settle the matter of the turning of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the believers toward the Ka'bah instead of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). This is the first abrogation (naskh, the replacement of one ruling by another) in the noble Qur'an. God, glory be to Him, wanted to give it the appropriate attention, because it would become a source of doubt and fierce dispute from everyone who opposes Islam: the Quraysh disbelievers would take it as a pretext for doubt, and likewise the hypocrites and the Jews. God, blessed and exalted, wanted to define the matter before these doubts occurred. So He, majestic is His majesty, says: ﴿The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they had been facing?"﴾ The letter sīn here (in sayaqūlu) confirms that they had not yet spoken. That is why He, glory be to Him, said ﴿will say the foolish﴾. Before the change of the qiblah took place, the Truth, exalted is He, said: this process will cause a violent upheaval that the skeptics will exploit.

Although God, glory be to Him, said ﴿the foolish will say﴾, meaning that they did not say it until after this verse was revealed, this indicates that they are truly foolish. For God, majestic is His majesty, informed His Messenger (ﷺ) in a Qur'an that is recited and prayed with, and that does not change or alter until the Day of Resurrection, saying: ﴿The foolish among the people will say.﴾ Had they refrained from speaking and not commented on the change of the qiblah, that would have been a casting of doubt upon the noble Qur'an, because in that case they could have said: "A Qur'an that God sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ) does not change or alter until the Day of Resurrection." He said: ﴿The foolish among the people will say what has turned them away from their qiblah﴾, and no one said anything...

But because they were truly foolish, and foolishness is ignorance, recklessness and levity, they said it. They, who were disbelievers in the Qur'an and wanted to demolish this religion, were among those who claimed to affirm faith, whose actions testify to the truth of the Qur'an. For God, glory be to Him, said: ﴿The foolish will say,﴾ and they indeed said it. The disbelievers of Makkah said about the Ka'bah that it is "our house and the house of our fathers," not the House of God. So God turned His Messenger at the beginning of Islam and directed him toward Bayt al-Maqdis. At that point the Jews said: "He has made foolish our religion and follows our qiblah." God, glory be to Him, wanted Islam to encompass every religion before it, so that sanctity belongs to all. For this reason He made His Messenger (ﷺ) travel by night from Makkah to Bayt al-Maqdis, so that Bayt al-Maqdis would enter the sacred places of Islam, because it had become contained within Islam.

God did not will to make the qiblah the Ka'bah at the outset, because they used to hold it sacred as the house of the Arabs, and they used to place their idols in it. Placing idols in the Ka'bah was a testimony that it had sanctity in itself. Sanctity did not come to it through their idols; rather, they wanted to protect these idols, so they placed them in the Ka'bah. Why did they not place them elsewhere? Because the Ka'bah is sacred without idols.

When God, glory be to Him, said: ﴿The foolish among the people will say, "What has turned them away from their qiblah, which they had been facing?"﴾ the word "walla" means He turned it aside and returned it. The qiblah they had been facing was Bayt al-Maqdis. Here the Truth brings a comprehensive answer: the commands of God that concern faith are not tied to a reason; rather, the reason for compliance with what God, glory be to Him, commands us is that God is the One who commands. Had the Truth, blessed and exalted, explained to us the cause or reason for changing the qiblah, the command would not have been a test of faith in the hearts, because faith and worship are obedience to the One worshipped in what He commands and what He forbids. God says to you: "Glorify this stone," which is the Black Stone in the Ka'bah, and you glorify it by touching and kissing it. He says to you: "Stone this stone, which symbolizes Iblis," and you stone it with pebbles. God, glory be to Him, does not say "why?" For if He had said "why," faith here would have been lost, and the matter would have become one of persuasion and conviction.

When I say to you, "Do not eat this because it is bitter, and eat that because it is sweet," the reason is clear. But God, blessed and exalted, says: "Eat this and do not eat that." If you eat what He has forbidden, you are sinful, and if you refrain, you are obedient and rewarded.

So the faith-based reason is that the command proceeds from God, glory be to Him. If you refrain from drinking wine because it is harmful to health or damages the liver, there is no reward for you; and if you refrain from eating pork because it contains a large amount of cholesterol and has many harms, there is no reward for you. But if you refrain from drinking wine and eating pork because God has forbidden them, then this is worship and this is reward.

God, glory be to Him, wanted to respond to these foolish people, so He said: ﴿Say, "To Allah belongs the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path."﴾ That is, when you turn toward Bayt al-Maqdis, or turn toward a particular direction, the Ka'bah has no sanctity in itself; rather, the command of God, blessed and exalted, is what gives it this distinction. So when we turn toward Bayt al-Maqdis, we turn toward it in obedience to God's command, and when God, glory be to Him, says turn toward the Ka'bah, we turn toward it in obedience to God's command.

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿He guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ The sirāṭ (path) is the straight road with no crookedness in it, so that it is the shortest distance to the goal. God, glory be to Him, directed us to Bayt al-Maqdis, and that is a straight path we follow; He directed us to the Ka'bah, and that is a straight path we follow. The matter belongs to God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 143:

﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels. And indeed, it was difficult except for those whom Allah guided. And Allah would never let your faith go to waste. Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to the people.﴾ (2:143)

When you see "kadhalika" (thus), there is a comparison. Almighty Allah wants us to be mindful of His blessing in making us a justly balanced nation (ummah wasatan). Every law that Allah prescribes falls under the heading of blessings upon the believers. And if turning toward the Ka'bah is a test of certainty of faith in the souls of the Muslims, then His making us a balanced nation is a blessing from Him. As long as we are balanced (wasat), there must be extremes, so that the middle can be defined: this is one extreme, then the middle, then another extreme. The middle of a thing is its midpoint, or what lies between the two extremes.

But what is the meaning of "a balanced nation"? It is balance in faith and creed. There are those who denied the existence of the true God, and there are those who went to excess and multiplied gods. This extreme is wrong, and that extreme is wrong. As for us, the Muslims, we say: there is no god but Allah alone, without partner, One, the Eternal. This is one of the self-evident truths of this universe, because Allah, blessed and exalted, created the universe and created everything in it, and He, glorified be He, said that He created. No one has come, nor will anyone come, claiming creation. Therefore the claim belongs exclusively to Allah, blessed and exalted. Had there been multiple gods in this universe, each one of them would have claimed creation. For this reason, Allah, majestic in His majesty, says:

﴿Allah has not taken any son, nor was there with Him any god; for then each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others.﴾ (part of 23:91)

That is: the creation would have been in conflict and the universe would have been in disorder. So Islam is a religion balanced between atheism and the multiplicity of gods. Furthermore, there are people who go to excess in materialism and neglect spiritual values, and people who neglect matter and believe only in spiritual values.

The reality of life is that materialists dominate the spiritualists because they have wealth and power. Islam came as a balance: in it are both matter and spirit. Beware of saying that the spirit is better than matter, or that matter is better than the spirit. Matter alone and spirit alone are both subjugated, worshipping and glorifying Allah, exalted be He. But when matter mingles with spirit, the self (nafs) comes into being, and the self is the one that has choice: it obeys or disobeys, worships or disbelieves, God forbid.

Almighty Allah wants the believers to live the materiality of life with the values of heaven. This is the moderation of Islam: it did not take the spirit alone nor matter alone, but established the materiality of life guarded by the values of heaven. So when Allah tells us that He will make us a balanced nation that combines the good of both extremes, we know that the religion came to protect mankind from the desires of mankind.

Blessed and exalted Allah wants us to investigate the material aspects of the universe in a way that produces progress, prosperity and strength for humanity. What is material and laboratory-based is something on which people do not disagree. But what involves the desires of people, heaven will set its law for you. If you live by desires, you will be miserable; if you live by the theories of heaven, you will be happy.

Some may ask: has communism, which came more than half a century ago, elevated its peoples or not? We say: look at it now. It built what it claimed as advancements upon lies and falsehood. Then it declined, and then it collapsed completely. Just as communism collapsed, capitalism will collapse, because they are two contradictory extremes, whereas we are a balanced nation. For this reason Allah, glorified be He, has given us the good of this world and the next.

The Almighty says: ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾. That is, the proof will be in your favour in the future, and the world will be compelled to return to what your religion legislates. Almighty Allah said ﴿a balanced nation (ummatan wasatan)﴾ and did not say "wasat" with a kasrah on the waw (meaning midpoint), so that it could not be said that these capitalists and communists will return to the truth entirely. Rather, some of them will lean slightly toward this side or that, so that a meeting takes place. For this reason, when they say, "We will take the wealth of the rich and distribute it among the poor," we say to them: and when a poor person comes in the future, from where will you give him, after you have eliminated the rich?

I heard from a person who has experience in politics and government that he said: "The one who worked with me and squandered all his wealth on wine, gambling and women was better than me, because I kept my money and developed it, and they said you are a feudal lord and confiscated it, whereas those who wasted never had anything done to them." I said: Almighty Allah wants you to develop your wealth, because if you do not develop it and pay on it zakat of 2.5%, then the wealth will be exhausted within forty years. But if you develop your wealth and they come to the product of your work and take it on the claim that you are a feudal lord, they are destroying work in society, because if you are going to take the product of someone's labour without right, why would he work? Islam came to expand the sphere of life's movement and to guarantee the property of the one who moves, so that zakat is taken from his wealth and the one unable to work is helped, so that he does not harbour resentment against society. This is the middle way.

As for the Almighty's saying ﴿that you may be witnesses over the people﴾: it is as though Almighty Allah informed us that a battle will take place in the universe, and it will be decided only by the testimony of this nation. Right or capitalism is in error, and communism is in error. But the method of Allah, which established the scales of justice for the universe and for human life, is the correct one. Then the Truth, blessed and exalted, informs us that the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, will be a witness over us. Did our work and our movement conform to what He sent down to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and what the Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace, conveyed to us? Or did we follow our desires and deviate from the method?

The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, will be a witness over us on this point. That verse, although it gave good news to the balanced nation that the world would return to its rule, that can only happen if the testimony of truth and justice prevails within it.

As for the Almighty's saying ﴿And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn back on his heels﴾: this is a return to the change of the qiblah from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah. Allah, blessed and exalted, does not favour one direction over another. For this reason, those who face the Ka'bah will differ in their directions according to the location of their countries relative to the Ka'bah: this one faces east, this one faces northeast, and this one faces southwest.

There is not, with Allah, one direction preferred over another. But Allah, glorified be He, made the change of the qiblah a test of faith, not a knowledge of cognition but a knowledge of witnessing, because Allah, glorified be He, knows, but He, majestic in His majesty, wants the human being to be a witness against himself on the Day of Resurrection. It is a test of faith, so that Allah may know the extent of your faith, and who will obey the Messenger in what came to him from Allah, and who will turn back on his heels. The matter of changing the qiblah was going to cause a violent shake of faith in the Muslims themselves, so Allah knows who will persist in his faith and in following the Messenger of Allah, and who will refuse and turn away from the religion of Islam.

As for the Almighty's saying ﴿And indeed, it was difficult except for those whom Allah guided﴾: Allah here intends the knowledge that will be a witness over people on the Day of Resurrection. The process of trial or testing in changing the qiblah is a arduous process, except for the believers who welcome every obligation, because they know that faith is obedience and they do not look into the reason behind things.

But the disbelievers, the hypocrites and the Jews did not let the change of the qiblah pass so easily. They said: if the qiblah was the Ka'bah, then your prayers during the days you faced Bayt al-Maqdis were lost; and if the qiblah is Bayt al-Maqdis, then your prayers will be lost while you face the Ka'bah.

We say to them: do not isolate a ruling from its time. The qiblah of Bayt al-Maqdis was for its time, and the Ka'bah comes in its time. Neither has transgressed against the other. Some believers died while praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and the doubters rose and said their prayers were not accepted. Allah, glorified be He, replied with His saying: ﴿And Allah would never let your faith go to waste﴾, because those who died while praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis were obedient to Allah and believed in Him, so Allah will not waste their faith.

As for the Almighty's saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to the people﴾: that is, remember that you believe in a Lord who is Kind, who does not intend hardship for you, and Merciful, who keeps affliction away from you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 144:

﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven. So We will surely turn you to a qibla that you will like. So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it. Indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.﴾ (2:144)

We know that "qad" (قد) is for emphasis and confirmation, and "nara" (نرى) is a present-tense verb, which indicates that the event is taking place at the time of speaking. The Almighty gives us a picture of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that he loved and longed to face the Ka'bah instead of Bayt al-Maqdis. The Messenger (peace be upon him) had become accustomed to receiving revelation from above, so it was as though he (ﷺ) would direct his gaze toward the sky at the moment revelation came. This happens only when his heart was attached to the hope that revelation would come with the change of the qibla. So it was as though this matter preoccupied him.

Allah, the Glorified, informs His Messenger (ﷺ) that He has seen the turning of the face of His noble Messenger toward the heaven, and He responded to him by directing him to the qibla that He loves. Does this mean that the qibla on which the Messenger (ﷺ) was, namely Bayt al-Maqdis, was not one he was pleased with? We say no. Rather, pleasure always relates to emotion, and there is a difference between the love of emotion and the love of reason. For this reason, no one says that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not pleased with the qibla of Bayt al-Maqdis. Rather, he would face Bayt al-Maqdis while his heart's emotion was directed toward the Ka'bah. This shows obedience and commitment.

Allah says to His Messenger (peace be upon him): "So We will surely turn you to a qibla that you will like", meaning, that you love with your emotion. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was looking forward to this change, so it was as though his emotions (ﷺ) turned to set down the preliminaries of the transfer.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾. By "the face" is meant the whole self, and the word "shatr" (شطر) means direction, while "shatr" also means half. Both meanings are correct, because when a person is in a place he becomes the center of a circle which ends at something called the horizon, which is the range of sight. And it seems to you there that the sky has come down upon the earth.

Each one of us has a circle according to his sight: when a person rises, the circle widens; and if his sight is weak, his horizon is smaller, and he is at the center of a circle half of which is in front of him and half behind him.

So whoever says that "shatr" means half is correct, and whoever says that "shatr" means direction is correct.

And His saying, ﴿So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾, means: make your face toward the direction of the Sacred Mosque, or make the Sacred Mosque within the half of the circle that is in front of you. In past times, worship was performed in specific places, until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, and Allah made the entire earth a mosque for him.

The mosque is the place of prostration, and since prostration is the utmost submission to Allah, the place in which we pray was called a mosque. But there is a difference between a place where you prostrate and a place you make restricted to the prayer to Allah and in which you do nothing else. The mosque is designated for prayer and worship. As for the place where you prostrate and carry on the movement of your life, it is not called a mosque except for the hour you prostrate in it. The Ka'bah is the House of Allah, by Allah's choosing; and all the mosques of the earth are houses of Allah by the choice of the creatures of Allah. For this reason, the House of Allah, by Allah's choosing, is the qibla for the houses of Allah by the choice of the creatures of Allah.

His saying, ﴿And wherever you are﴾, means: wherever you may be. ﴿Turn your faces toward it﴾. This is because the verse was revealed while they were in the mosque of Banu Salamah in Madinah, and the Muslims then turned toward the Sacred Mosque. Lest anyone think that the change applies only to that mosque and only to the time the verse was revealed, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾. And His saying, Majestic is His majesty: ﴿Indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.﴾ means: those who were given the Scripture, and who try to cast doubt upon following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), know that the Messenger of Allah is the final Messenger, and they recognize his attributes which were mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel. They know that he is the one of the two qiblas. Had the Messenger (ﷺ) not turned from Bayt al-Maqdis to the Ka'bah, they would have said: the Torah and the Gospel say that the final Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), prays toward two qiblas, so why has it not come true? And that would have been more conducive to doubt.

So, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord, because they find in the Torah that the Messenger who will come will turn toward Bayt al-Maqdis and then turn toward the Sacred House. Thus this change, with respect to the People of the Book, is a confirmation of their faith in the Messenger (peace be upon him), and not a cause of shaking their certainty.

His saying, ﴿And Allah is not unaware of what they do﴾, means: the Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to reassure His Messenger (ﷺ) that their doubting neither advances nor delays anything. Their stance is not a seeking of proof, but obstinacy. They do not want proof or a faith-based argument; they want only to be obstinate.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 145:

﴿And even if you were to bring those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qibla, nor are you to be a follower of their qibla, nor are some of them followers of the qibla of others. And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, then you would indeed be among the wrongdoers.﴾

Following the qibla is an outward manifestation of faith in the religion. So as long as you have believed in your religion, follow your qibla... If you do not believe in your religion, you will not follow your qibla.

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And if you were to bring﴾. As soon as you hear "wa-la-in" (wa, lam and in), this is an oath. It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted, swore that if the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were to bring the People of the Scripture every sign, they would not believe in his religion nor follow his qibla. Why? Because they do not seek evidence, nor do they wish to be convinced of the truth of the new religion. Had they wanted evidence or conviction, they would have found it in their own books, which informed them about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he is the final Prophet, and described his attributes to them. So the evidence is with them, but they take the matter with foolishness, obstinacy and arrogance.

As for His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Nor are you to be a follower of their qibla﴾. It is as if, when the change of qibla came, Allah informed us that the Muslims would never return again to facing Jerusalem, and that Allah would not turn them to a third direction. And so that Allah, glorified and exalted, would teach us that the Jews and the Christians would be on one side and we would be on another side, and that there is no meeting point between us and them. He, glorified, said: ﴿Nor are some of them followers of the qibla of others.﴾ So the disagreement over the qibla continues until the Day of Resurrection. And the saying of the Truth: ﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, then you would indeed be among the wrongdoers.﴾ When Allah, glorified and exalted, addresses His Messenger and beloved Muhammad (ﷺ) with this verse, while He knows that Muhammad, the infallible Messenger, could never follow their desires, we say that what is intended by this verse is the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Allah addresses His community through his person, saying: ﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, then you would indeed be among the wrongdoers.﴾ What are the desires of the People of the Scripture? They are that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) should make a truce with them, or that he should say that what they have distorted in their books was revealed by Allah. Thus they make the desires of their souls something to be followed. So it is as if Allah, glorified and exalted, wants to draw the attention of the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to the fact that whoever follows the desires of the People of the Scripture and what they have distorted will be among the wrongdoers, whatever his degree of faith. And if Allah, blessed and exalted, will not accept this from His Messenger and beloved, how could He accept it from any individual of the community of Muhammad (ﷺ)?

The address here touches a summit of the summits of faith whose corruption would ruin the whole creed. Allah, glorified and exalted, wants us to know that He does not tolerate it nor accept it, even if it came from His Messenger, and even though it will not happen. Rather, so that we know that it is utterly rejected by Allah at any level of faith, even at the summit, and so that the community of Muhammad stays entirely far from such an act.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 146:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognise it as they recognise their own sons. But indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know it.﴾

Allah, blessed and exalted, says: those who were given the Book before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recognise him. Recognise what? Do they recognise the matter of the change of the qibla, or do they recognise the matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, his mission and his message, which they try to cast doubt upon? Allah, glorified and exalted, explains this to us in His saying:

﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what was with them, though before that they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, yet when there came to them that which they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:89)

So it is as if the Jews and Christians recognise the message of Muhammad ﷺ, and it is written in the Torah and the Gospel that he is the truth and that they are required to believe in him. When Ka'b al-Ahbar was sitting, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was present, and 'Umar asked him: "Did you recognise him, O Ka'b?" That is, did you recognise Muhammad ﷺ, his message and his attributes? Ka'b, who was one of the rabbis of the Jews, said: "I recognise him as I recognise my son, and my recognition of Muhammad is stronger." When they asked him, "Why?", he said: "Because as for my son, I fear that my wife may have betrayed me concerning him. But as for Muhammad ﷺ, his attributes are mentioned with such precision in the Torah that we cannot mistake him."

Thus the People of the Book recognise the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they recognise his time and his message. Those among them who embraced Islam and believed did so out of conviction. As for those who did not believe and disbelieved in what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought, they recognised it but concealed what they knew. Therefore Allah, glorified and exalted, says of them: ﴿But indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know it.﴾ When you say "he concealed the thing", it is as if the thing by its nature wants to appear and spread. The truth by its nature must appear and spread, but denying the truth and concealing it requires effort.

Those who investigate delicate matters try to prevent force from concealing the truth, so they keep the one they interrogate from sleeping until his strength collapses and he speaks the truth. Speaking the truth requires no effort, whereas concealing the truth is what requires effort and strength; not speaking the truth is an arduous process. But Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿while they know it﴾, meaning they are not ignorant, but have knowledge of the reality. And the truth is from Allah, so can these people conceal it? Of course not; it must appear. When falsehood and lies spread, they are like the pain that occurs in the body. People dislike pain, but pain is one of the soldiers of healing, because it makes you feel that something in the body has become diseased, so you turn to it with the means of restoring health.

The most dangerous diseases are those not accompanied by pain, and you do not feel them until the time of treatment has passed. The truth always prevails over its affair, which is why there is no battle between two truths. Falsehood, however, has battles between falsehood and falsehood, and between truth and falsehood, because there is only one truth while falsehood is many.

Battles between truth and falsehood end quickly with the defeat of falsehood. But what is prolonged is a battle between two falsehoods, and therefore the wars of the modern age drag on and exhaust the world. The wars of the Second World War, for example, still have their effects extending until now in the Cold War and other lesser wars. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ says:

("None of you truly believes until his desire is in accordance with what I have brought.")(1)

(1) Narrated by al-Daylami in Musnad al-Firdaws.

The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.

The truth is from Allah, glorified and exalted. And since it is from Allah, do not be among those who doubt that the truth will prevail. But the truth needs a force to protect it, and as the poet says: "The sword, though it boast of its jewelled hilt, does nothing except in the hand of a hero." What use is a sharp sword if there is no strong hand to strike with it? We often waste the truth because we do not provide it with the strength by which it prevails.

As for His saying, exalted be He: ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾. The mumtari (the doubter) is one who doubts whether a thing will happen. Doubt (shakk) means that there is no probability that outweighs another; that is, the two possibilities are equal. But the truth is from Allah, and there is no probability opposing it. Therefore, we should not doubt, nor enter into barren disputation about the victory of the truth.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 148:

﴿For each there is a direction towards which he turns. So race to [all] good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth all together. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾

Allah, glorified is He, willed that man be free in choice. Hence he has the choice to believe or not to believe, to support the truth or to support falsehood, to do good or to do evil. All these are trials which Allah willed to give to man in this world, such that he is able to act or not to act. But this will not remain forever; this choice exists in the life of this world.

However, the humanity of man ends at the hour of death agony. At the confrontation with death and the end of life, man becomes subdued and no longer free to choose. He possesses nothing for himself and cannot say, "I will not die now." His humanity and his control over himself have ended, even his limbs bear witness against him.

So in this worldly life, each one chooses the direction he turns towards: this one chooses disbelief and that one chooses faith; this one chooses obedience and that one chooses disobedience. As long as man has choice, each one has a direction different from the other. And the one whom Allah guides turns towards good deeds as if racing to them. Why? Because he does not know when he will die, and therefore whenever he races to a good deed, that is a good deed he adds to his account.

What is required of the believers in this worldly life is that they race to good deeds before their term comes, and that none of them think he will escape from Allah, because as He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth all together.﴾ That is, there is no place where you can hide from the knowledge of Allah, blessed and exalted; rather He knows your places, all of you, one by one, and He will bring you all together, in confirmation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And [mention] the Day We will remove the mountains and you will see the earth prominent, and We will gather them and not leave behind from them anyone.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf)

And His saying, glorified is He:

﴿So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.﴾ (Surah adh-Dhariyat)

That is, the Truth, majestic is His majesty, wants us to know with certainty that we cannot flee from His knowledge, nor from His decree, nor from His punishment. The only open path before us is to flee to Allah, and there is no refuge from Allah except to Him. Therefore no disbeliever or sinner should think that he will escape from Allah, nor think that he will not exist on the Day of Resurrection, or that he will not be called to account, or that he can hide.

The vanity of this world may overtake some people, so they think they are secure from Allah and that they will never meet Him. We say to them: you will be surprised in the Hereafter when you know that the Reckoning is true, the Garden is true, and the Fire is true. You will be astonished by what will befall you. And whoever does not believe and does not hasten to good will meet disgrace and painful punishment. Allah advises us to believe and to race to good deeds, so that we may be saved from His punishment, and He tells us that not one of you will escape, nor a single particle of your body, from standing before Allah for reckoning. Therefore Allah concluded this noble verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ That is, Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is not overcome by anything, and nothing goes out of His obedience. He, glorified is He, is competent over all things.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 149:

﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾

We must reflect on how many times the Noble Qur'an emphasized the matter of the change of the qiblah. It emphasized it three times in close succession, because the change of the qiblah caused a violent shock in the souls of the believers, and the Most High wants this effect to be removed, and He confirms the change of the qiblah with a confirmation that establishes it in faith.

He brought it in three verses, which is the least of the plural: one for the one who faces the Ka'bah while inside the Mosque, the second for the one who faces it while outside the Mosque, and the third for the one who faces it from all directions.

As for His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾, it is a response to the hypocrites, the Jews, and the Christians, who tried to cast doubt on Islam by confronting the Muslims with the matter of changing the qiblah, on the basis that it is a matter that should not have occurred, because there is no added obligation in it and no additional hardship that would increase the reward of the believer. The effort that the believer exerts in facing the Masjid al-Aqsa is the same effort he exerts in facing the Sacred House. For if you turn in your prayer to the right or to the left, to the east or to the west, that does not add hardship to you. So what is the reason for the change?

We say to them: this is not a valid argument for casting doubt on the change of the qiblah, because facing the Sacred Mosque is obedience to Allah. And since Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has commanded it, we must obey with faithful obedience. The Lord, Majestic in His majesty, says: ﴿And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾ That is, what you have done in changing the qiblah is the truth that has come to you from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is not unaware of your deeds, such that you would have turned toward the Sacred House without His knowledge. Rather, Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal. So be assured that you are upon the truth, and turn your faces toward the Sacred Mosque, and know that Allah, Glorified, encompasses you in all that you do.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verse 150:

﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque; and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, so that people will have no argument against you, except those of them who do wrong. So do not fear them, but fear Me, and so that I may complete My blessing upon you and that you may be guided.﴾

Allah, blessed and exalted is He, affirms to His Messenger (ﷺ) that he and the Muslims should face the Sacred Mosque (al-Masjid al-Haram), whether they are in Medina, outside Medina, or anywhere else on earth. That is their qiblah in every prayer, regardless of the place where they pray.

As for His saying, ﴿so that people will have no argument against you﴾: "the people" here refers to the hypocrites, the Jews, and the Christians. An argument about what? Because the Muslims had been facing Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and then they turned toward the Sacred Mosque. Neither Bayt al-Maqdis nor the Sacred Mosque has holiness in itself, as we have said. Rather, we obey the command of the Supreme Commander, who is Allah. Allah, blessed and exalted, applied the word ﴿wrongdoers﴾ to the hypocrites, the Jews, and the Christians, and described them as "those who did wrong." So who is the wrongdoer? The wrongdoer is one who denies the truth, or changes its direction, or turns truth into falsehood and falsehood into truth. Wrongdoing (zulm) is transgressing the limit. It is as if He, glory be to Him, described them as having exceeded the truth and denied it. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So do not fear them﴾, meaning do not fear those who did wrong: ﴿but fear Me, and so that I may complete My blessing upon you and that you may be guided.﴾ That is, fear is for Allah alone, and the believer does not fear any human being, because he knows that all power belongs to Allah. Therefore he proceeds with every deed with a heart that dreads no one except the truth.

As for His saying, glory be to Him, ﴿and so that I may complete My blessing upon you and that you may be guided﴾: the completion of blessing is faith, and the completion of blessing is carrying out what faith requires. So if Allah guides us to faith, this is part of the completion of His blessings upon us. For faith to be sound and accepted, I must fulfill its demands and persist in carrying out Allah's obligations for us, so that we do not let the obligations lapse. For obligation is a blessing; without it our lives are not put right, and the blessings of obligation from Allah, glory be to Him, do not follow one another unless we approach the method with love. When you come to the method, it may be burdensome, but if you remember the reward of every act of obedience, you will become humble and will love obligation, because you know righteous deeds by their reward and sin by its punishment. Therefore Allah, blessed and exalted, said:

﴿Seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is burdensome except for the humble, who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that to Him they will return.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah 2:45–46)

So the humble (al-khashi'un) are those who link obedience with reward and disobedience with punishment and torment. For the one who turns away from obedience because it is hard has separated obedience from reward, so it became heavy; and the one who goes to disobedience has separated disobedience from punishment, so it became easy. Thus it is part of the completion of blessing that Allah keeps us performing what faith requires. That is why, at the Farewell Pilgrimage, the noble verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion.﴾ (part of verse 3, Surah al-Ma'idah)

This was an announcement that the mission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was complete, and that the legal obligations had ended. But those who find obligation burdensome, you will find them saying to you: "Corruption has spread, and Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity." As if he rules that this is within his capacity and that is not, and takes obligation according to that judgment. We say to him: Has Allah imposed obligation or not? If He has imposed it, then the obligation is within your capacity, for when He, glory be to Him, finds hardship, He commands ease, such as permitting the shortening of the prayer for the traveler, and permitting the breaking of the fast in Ramadan for the sick and the traveler. He, glory be to Him, has defined what is within your capacity.

As for His saying, ﴿and that you may be guided﴾: guidance is the straight path that leads to the goal, and it is the shortest route. The goal of this life is that you reach the bliss of the Hereafter. Allah has given you in this world the means to govern the movement of your life, but this is not the purpose of life. Rather, the purpose is that we go to a life without means, and this is the greatness of the power of Allah, glory be to Him. Allah, majestic in His majesty, comes to teach us in the Hereafter that He created us to live in this world by means, and in the Hereafter to live in His care without means.

So His saying, ﴿and that you may be guided﴾, means: so that you may take heed and recognize the goal required of you. Let none of you think that the life of this world is the goal, or the end, or the aim, so that he works for this world, taking from it whatever he can, lawfully or unlawfully, regarding it as the only enjoyment created for him. We say: No. In that case he has gone astray and has not been guided, for if he had been guided, he would have known that the true life of a human being is in the Hereafter, and he would have known that the bliss of the Hereafter, which will not escape you and which you will not escape, should be our aim in the life of this world. So we should work as much as we can to attain bliss without means in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 151:

﴿As We have sent among you a messenger from yourselves, reciting to you Our verses, purifying you, and teaching you the Book and wisdom, and teaching you what you did not know.﴾

God, exalted is His majesty, after telling us about the guidance to His method and to His path, told us about His blessing upon us by sending a messenger who recites to us the verses of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the one through whose hands would come the summit of blessings, which is the Qur'an and the final religion.

God's words: ﴿a messenger from yourselves﴾ mean not of another kind. Rather, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a messenger from among you, whom you knew before he was charged with the message and before he brought the proof. Why? Because he was known for his great character, his noble speech, his trustworthiness, and everything that increases a person in elevation, exaltation and respect. The first to believe in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were those who knew him better than others, such as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Sayyida Khadija, and his cousin ʿAli ibn Abi Talib. They believed without asking for proof, because they took faith from their knowledge of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was charged with the message. They had never known him to lie at all, so they said: one who does not lie to people cannot lie to God, and so they believed. God, glorified and exalted, in His mercy sent to them a messenger from among them, unlettered, so that his Lord would teach him. Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted, said:

﴿There has certainly come to you a messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer; [he is] concerned over you and to the believers, kind and merciful.﴾ (Surah al-Tawba, 9:128).

God, exalted, says: ﴿reciting to you Our verses and purifying you.﴾ The verses are the noble Qur'an, and purification (tazkiyah) is cleansing, and there must be a defilement from which He cleanses them. So He purified them from the worship of idols, from the burying of daughters, from wine, gambling and usury. Tazkiyah also means removing what is harmful, as if he came to them with benefit and removed harm from them.

God's words: ﴿and teaching you the Book and wisdom.﴾ The Book, in its unrestricted sense, refers to the noble Qur'an, and wisdom (hikmah) is placing a thing in its proper place. The Book gives you obligation: either it commands you to do something or forbids you from something. So it revolves between doing and abstaining. Wisdom is that you do the act which brings you good and prevents evil from you. The word is derived from al-hikmah (the bridle), the iron piece placed in a horse's mouth to control its movement in going and stopping, so that every movement fulfills its purpose. Wisdom also means the sayings of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in confirmation of God's words:

﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom﴾ (part of verse 34, Surah al-Ahzab, 33:34).

God, glorified, says: ﴿and teaching you what you did not know.﴾ Because you are an unlettered nation. If the world dazzles you with its civilization, you will dazzle them with the illuminations of faith that make you superior to them. Everything that comes to you from heaven is above all the civilizations of the earth. Therefore ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: "What would ʿUmar be without Islam?"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 2, verse 152:

﴿So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.﴾

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So remember Me﴾ mean that all these blessings and favours upon you must not be forgotten. You should live always in remembrance of the One who has bestowed His favours upon you. Allah the Exalted desires that His servants remember Him, and whenever they remember Him and give thanks to Him, He increases them.

And Allah the Exalted says in a hadith qudsi:

{ "I am as My servant thinks I am, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than it. If he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running." }(1)

This is the desire of the Generous to give, on the condition that we are worthy of receiving, because He wishes to give you more and more. So His words ﴿remember Me﴾ mean: remember Allah in everything: in His blessings, in His giving, in His covering, in His mercy, in His forgiveness.

One of the righteous says: I heard, from among those who heard from my beloved, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that when you approach drinking water, divide it into three. Before the first sip, say "In the name of Allah," drink it, then say "Praise be to Allah." Begin the second sip, say "In the name of Allah," and after finishing it say "Praise be to Allah." Then say "In the name of Allah," drink the third sip, and conclude it with your saying "Praise be to Allah." As long as this water is in your belly, not a single atom of your body will tempt you to disobey Allah. Try it one day for yourself: say "In the name of Allah," drink, say "Praise be to Allah," and repeat it three times, and you will have received the blessing by remembering the Giver and kept away from yourself your own power and strength, and you will have ended the blessing with the praise of Allah. But why water? Because water in the belly satisfies more than anything else.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾. Thanking God for a blessing causes Allah the Exalted to increase you in it. Recite His words, blessed and exalted is He:

﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ (part of verse 7, Surat Ibrahim).

And gratitude to Allah removes conceit from yourself, so that means do not deceive you, and you do not say, "I was given it because of knowledge from myself." ﴿And do not deny Me﴾ means do not conceal the blessings of Allah, but keep them always on your tongues. For every blessing of Allah, if you receive it with your saying "What Allah wills; there is no power except with Allah," you will never see any harm in the blessing, because you have fortified the blessing with the protection of the Giver. You have given Allah His due in His blessing. If you do not do this, and leave it as though it were from you and you were its originator, forgetting the Giver, who is Allah the Exalted, then the blessing will leave you.

(1) Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ahmad in his Musnad, with varying wordings.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 2, verse 153:

﴿O you who have believe, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾

Allah, glorified and exalted, asks us to seek help through patience and prayer. Help in what? In everything Allah requires of us: in His obligations and His methodology, we seek help in these through patience and prayer. But why patience? Because patience is restraining the self from being distressed by anything that happens, and it takes various forms according to how far people advance in worship.

For example, Imam ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about the right of the neighbor. He said: "Do you know that you should not harm him?" They said, "Yes." He said: "And that you should bear patiently with his harm." So it is not only required of you that you not harm your neighbor, but that you bear patiently with his harm. Patience is what helps you to do what Allah has commanded you and to avoid what He has forbidden you.

Allah has forbidden you from things that are among the desires of the self, and has commanded you to do things that involve hardship, and these need patience. If you take the methodology of Allah as an act of worship, you will afterward take it as a habit. One of the righteous says in his supplication: "O Allah, I ask You not to leave me to myself, for I fear, O Lord, that You will not reward me for obedience because I have come to desire it." Glory be to You, You commanded us to fight our desires... Look at obedience: from the abundance of love for Allah, it has become desirable and beloved to the self. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say to Bilal at the time of the adhan:

("Give us rest with it, O Bilal.")

He did not say, as some people say, may Allah protect us, "Relieve us of it." For there are those who tell you that prayer is like a mountain on the shoulders, and that you will rest from it. We say to them: you rest with it, not from it, because you are standing before Allah, the One who imposes obligation. As long as a person is standing before his Lord, every difficult matter becomes easy.

One of the worshippers says: "I do not confront Allah with my servitude, but I confront Him with His lordship, so I find rest, because He is my Lord and the Lord of the worlds." The one who has a father to help him does not bear worry; how much more so the one who has a Lord who helps and supports him.

The word of the Truth, glorified be He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾ That is, He asks you to face life in the company of Allah. If you faced problems in the company of someone whose strength you trust, you would face matters with courage; how much more so if you are in the company of Allah, and everything in existence is subject to Allah. Can anything dare to stand before you while you are with Allah?

Events do not fill creation with terror and panic except at the moment of escaping the protection of their Lord. Whoever lives under the protection of his Lord, Satan does not dare against him, for Satan is the whisperer (khannas). What is the meaning of khannas? If you forget Allah, he becomes bold against you, and if you remember Allah, he withdraws and weakens; he has no power. He does not enter into battle with Allah, the Exalted, but enters into battle with the creatures of Allah who forget Allah and turn away from Him. The Noble Qur'an says:

﴿He said: "By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them."﴾ (Surah Sad).

Since Allah, glorified and exalted, is with the patient, we must surely love patience. And how could we not love that which causes Allah to be with us? The Lord, majestic in His majesty, says in the Hadith Qudsi:

("O son of Adam, I was ill and you did not visit Me." He said: "O Lord, how could I visit You, when You are the Lord of the worlds?" He said: "Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was ill and you did not visit him? Did you not know that if you had visited him, you would have found Me with him?")(1). One of the righteous says: "O Allah, I am ashamed to ask You for healing and well-being, lest that be renunciation of my company with You." So we must love patience, because it keeps us always in the company of Allah.

Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾ And we want Allah, glorified be He, to be with us always. This verse does not let a person despair, no matter how much hardship he encounters in the course of his life.

1 Related by Imam Muslim in his Sahih.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 2, verse 154:

﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive.﴾

Almighty Allah knows that the enemies of faith and its adversaries will confront the Muslims with severe hardship. It will threaten them not only in their wealth but also in their souls, so Allah, mighty and majestic, wished to give the believers immunity against these events. He enjoined on them patience and prayer, with which they confront every event that shakes them violently. He told them that the matter may reach killing, to martyrdom in the way of Allah. He wished to reassure them that martyrdom is the highest level of faith that a believing person can reach in this world, so He, glorified be He, said: ﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead."﴾

Killing is the most severe thing that can befall a person. You may be afflicted in your wealth, your child, your provision or your health, but to be afflicted in your very self, so that you are killed, is the greatest calamity. Allah, glorified be He, called death a calamity, and consider His saying, exalted be He: ﴿If you are traveling in the land and the disaster of death strikes you﴾ (part of verse 106, Surah al-Ma'idah).

Blessed and exalted be Allah, He wished the believers to understand that the one who is killed in the way of Allah does not die, but Allah grants him a new hue of life containing blessings beyond counting or enumeration. He, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And do not say of those who are killed in the way of Allah, "They are dead." Rather, they are alive, but you do not perceive.﴾

What is the appearance of the life they live? Life for us is manifested in movement. And what is the movement of the one who was killed in the way of Allah? Its movement, in relation to non-believers, the enemies of Islam and faith, is that life is not taken from him, because he goes to a happier life, and death transports him to something better than what he was living in. So if the disbelievers have killed him, they have taken nothing from him; rather they have moved him to a greater blessing than the one he was living in. As for the believers, his martyrdom protects for them the method of Allah so that it reaches them until the Hour is established.

All the battles in which the believers are martyred are but a continuous chain to protect the movement of faith in existence. The greatness of life is not that I move, but that I make those after me move. When a believer is martyred, his influence remains in existence for every movement that moves after him. Every movement to protect faith is inspired by him and by what he did, and takes from his faithful conduct a motive to fight and to be martyred. Thus the movement is continuous and the process is continuous. As for the disbeliever, life ends for him at death, but another life awaits him when Allah resurrects all people and then brings death, and it dies. When death itself dies, life becomes deathless, either in Paradise or in Hell.

Allah, glorified be He, wants us to know that whoever is killed in the way of Allah is alive with his Lord; he passes from the life of this world directly to the life of the Hereafter, and the death of the intermediate state (barzakh) until the Day of Resurrection is not written for him as it is for one who dies a natural death and not as a martyr. Because this is the life of the martyrs, Allah, glorified be He, has concealed its details from us, since it belongs to the life of the Hereafter, and it is unseen to us. He, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿But you do not perceive.﴾ And since we do not perceive it, it must be a life higher than our worldly life.

The one who is martyred, in the custom of people, has had his soul taken from him, but in the reckoning of Allah he has received a new life. When we open the grave of one of the martyrs, we find his body as it was, and we say that he is dead before us. You must be aware that at the moment you open it, he has moved from the realm of the unseen to the realm of the witnessed. Allah, glorified be He, said: ﴿alive with their Lord﴾ and did not say "alive in the realm of the witnessed." So he is alive as long as he is in the realm of the unseen, but if you open and uncover it, you find a body in its grave, because he has moved from the realm of the unseen to the realm of the witnessed. As for how: we have said that the unseen has no "how," so you will not know it, and it is not required of you to know it.

When we perform a surgical operation on a patient, the doctor gives him anesthesia (al-bang) so that he loses consciousness and sensation, not so that he dies, and then begins the operation, and the patient feels no pain at all.

The body does not sense, because it is the thing on which the operation is performed, and life remains in it in the form of pulse and breath, but it does not feel. Rather, it is the conscious soul that has departed that feels pain.

When there is pain in your body and you sleep, the sensation of pain ceases; it is as though pain is not a matter of organs but is tied to consciousness. In sleep you pass into another world whose laws are different. Scientists have examined the human brain while a person sleeps and found that it cannot do more than seven seconds of work in which it sees a dream that one keeps recounting for hours. So when the Truthful, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed they are alive with their Lord﴾, this life must be taken as by the power of Allah and from Him. Allah, mighty and majestic, wished to bring close to us the matter of resurrection and the Day of Judgment through the example of sleep.

Consider the saying of the Truthful, glorified be He: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. He retains those for which He has decreed death and sends the others back until an appointed term﴾ (part of verse 42, Surah al-Zumar).

So it is as though the Truthful, mighty and majestic, gives the martyrs an everlasting, eternal life because they died in His way. Since He, exalted be He, said: ﴿but you do not perceive﴾, do not try to grasp it with your perception and sense, for you will not grasp it. And the martyr must be killed in the way of Allah, and not for any worldly purpose, but so that the word of Allah may be the highest.

We know that mere trial is not evil. Evil lies in falling through the trial. Every trial is a test and an examination, and no one says that examinations are evil. They become evil only from the viewpoint of the one who did not bear the hardships of work to reach success. For the one who exerted effort and won first place, examinations are good. So His words, ﴿and We will surely test you﴾, mean: We will set for you an examination that will purify the heroism of the new faith.

Before this verse, the Almighty mentioned the summit of trials, which is that a person attains martyrdom in the way of God, and He mentioned the reward of the martyr, which is that he remains in a form of life with his Lord. This was a prelude to the lesser trials. The summit of trial, within the limits of our understanding, is the loss of life. God wanted to give the believers immunity in what falls short of life: immunity from fear, hunger, the loss of wealth, the loss of lives and the loss of fruits. Everything short of a person's life is a matter of comfort compared with the loss of life itself. Whoever does not lose his life will face trials in what falls short of his life, namely the trials of fear, hunger, the loss of wealth, a shortage in the number of believing brothers, and likewise a shortage in fruits. All of these are things a person loves, and the obligation comes to ask the believer to leave some of what he loves. These trials fall within the scope of the continuation of obligation. The first of these trials is fear. Fear is the disturbance of the soul and its failure to feel secure from the anticipation of something harmful. The soul has many faculties, and when fear afflicts it, it suffers from a lack of harmony. Fear is a weakness that is not necessary, because if you want to secure yourself against something that frightens you, you need to strive with your means to prevent what frightens you. But if you surrender to disturbance, you will not be able to confront the frightening matter with all your faculties, because you will face it with some of your faculties in a state of weakness and turmoil. Yet at the time of fear you need the stability of your psychological faculties, so that you can supply your soul with what secures you from this fear. If your disturbance exceeds its limit, then you have thereby aided the source of fear against yourself, because you will not confront the matter with all your strength or all your thinking.

So to the one who fears fear, we say: you are assisting the source of fear against yourself. Your fear and disturbance will not prevent the fearful matter. Therefore you must occupy yourself with what prevents the frightening matter, and leave the frightening matter until it happens. Do not live in its terror before it comes to you. The bane of people is that they live in calamities before they occur, and by doing so they prolong the duration of calamities for themselves. A calamity may come, for example, after a month, so why do you lengthen the life of the calamity by dreading it and fearing to confront it? If you leave it until it happens, you will have shortened its distance. Know that when a calamity comes, the Almighty, the Exalted, in His mercy sends down gentleness along with it. So if you live in the calamity before it happens, you are living in the calamity alone, isolated from the gentleness that accompanies it. But if you remain patient and seeking reward, able to confront any difficult matter, you will not live in the calamity without the gentleness.

The call to God through Islam was still in its infancy, so it was necessary to prepare the believing exemplar thoroughly, and fear was to be expected, because the opponents of the call plot against it and scheme by night. This is the trial. What is intended of the believer when he faces the trial of fear? He must make fear a pretext for completing the means that prevent the frightening matter from occurring. If he does this, he has succeeded in this trial.

We come to the second trial in this noble verse, which is hunger. Hunger is an overpowering appetite for food, and it is necessary for preserving life. Among the mercies of the Almighty toward the human being is that He provided within his own body a store of nourishment, saved up from a time of plenty to benefit him in a time of hardship. A person keeps surplus nourishment in the form of fat and flesh. When he is hungry and finds no food, he draws on this fat; when the fat is exhausted, he draws on the flesh; and when the flesh is exhausted, the body takes its nourishment from the bone, so that a person may preserve life.

The human being is composed of many systems, and the master of these systems is the brain. As long as life exists in the cells of the brain, everything in you is ready for action. But if those cells die, everything ends. That is why it is said that so-and-so died, then they gave him a particular medicine and life returned to him. They forget the established scientific fact that life does not leave a person unless the brain ceases to function. For this reason, there is a person whose heart may stop, and the physicians treat him with an electric shock that restarts the heart, or they open the chest to massage the heart. But if the cells of the brain die, that is death. All the systems of the body are in the service of that master, the brain.

It is remarkable that you find the master of the human being, the brain, at the top of the body, and in animals likewise the brain is at the top. As for plants, their master is in their roots. The leaves wither first, then the slender branches shrivel, then the trunk, and finally the root dries up when some water does not reach it. But when some water reaches the roots at the appropriate time, they turn green again, grow, and life returns to them. Likewise is the brain in the human being. When a person has exhausted his store of fat and flesh and feeds on the bones, his rescue comes from delivering nourishment to the brain. For this reason, an Arab woman who knew nothing of anatomy said: "Years have passed over us: a year that melted the fat, a year that wasted the flesh, and a year that erased the bone."

We must understand that hunger makes every provision in life sweet to us. If you are hungry, every food becomes delicious. The one who compels people to prepare various kinds of dishes is only the lack of hunger. A person wants to make food appetizing for himself so that he may eat, but if he were hungry, any food would suffice for him. For this reason they said: "The food of the hungry is pleasant, and the bed of the weary is soft." When a person is exhausted, he sleeps on rough ground and sinks into sleep, whereas if he is not exhausted, he keeps tossing on the bed even if it is made of brocade.

So the trial of hunger is that you endure with the necessary food that sustains your life, eating it as fuel for the movement of life and not eating it for pleasure. When a person takes sustenance to secure for himself the fuel of life, any food suffices him. For this reason God prescribed fasting, so that we would be patient under the harm of hunger, because believers may be compelled by some battle to remain for long hours without food. If they are not trained to bear a measure of hunger, they will grow weak and exhausted.

So the Almighty wants to prepare the believer with a complete and sufficient preparation. The believer faces fear and prepares himself; he faces hunger and takes from the sustenance of life only what is necessary.

For this reason you find that societies face economic hardships through austerity. But some societies cannot do so, and you find the people in those societies do not practise austerity. Therefore we say to one who lives a life of luxury: you are not preparing yourself the necessary preparation to face the vicissitudes of time.

And I say, as Ibrahim ibn Adham said:

"Whenever something becomes expensive for me, I leave it, and it becomes cheapest when it has become most expensive."

Whatever thing rises in price, a person does not buy it and leaves it, so it becomes the cheapest thing, because he will not pay money for it to buy it.

As for the third trial, which is the loss of wealth, its source is that the believers will be occupied away from their livelihood by the matter of the call. When they are diverted from the movement of life to confront the enemy, they will be compelled to sacrifice the activity of life that produces wealth, and therefore wealth diminishes, because their movement in life has turned toward resisting the enemies of God. Likewise they will confront the enemy as fighters, and some of them may be martyred. Finally, they face the loss of fruits, and fruits are the goal of every work.

When the Almighty, the Exalted, prepares us in this way, and if we succeed in it, then there is good news for us, because we have been patient through all these troubles: patience through fear, patience through hunger, patience through the loss of wealth, patience through the loss of lives, and patience through the loss of fruits.

So the important thing is that the believer succeeds in all these trials, so that he faces life steadfast and strong. He knows that life is a crossing, and the crossing does not preoccupy him from the goal. For this reason the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted says:

﴿Those who, when a disaster strikes them, say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return."﴾ [2:156]

Al-muṣībah (disaster) is that thing by which a person suffers hardship and pain, and it is derived from the hitting of a target (iṣābat al-hadaf). The believer receives the disaster confident that the reward for it is in proportion to its pain. For this reason, when the disbelievers rejoiced at what befell the Muslims in some battles, Allah sent down this true statement to the believers:

﴿Say: "Nothing will ever befall us except what Allah has decreed for us."﴾ [9:51]

That is, say, O believers, to these foolish disbelievers: nothing will happen to us except what Allah has written.

When we reflect on His saying, the Truthful: "what Allah has decreed for us," it means that the matter will be for our account, and we will receive good reward for it from Allah. The Truthful did not say "what Allah has decreed upon us," because if it were so, it would mean that it is a recompense and punishment from Allah.

Any matter that befalls a person is either one in which he has a part, in which case it is not right for him to lament, since it is he who brought the painful matter upon himself; or it is a disaster in which he has no part, and it happened to him from someone else, for example, in which case he must seek its cause: was it justice or injustice? If it was justice, then it has atoned for the sin; and if it was injustice, then Allah will avenge him against the one who wronged him. Accordingly, the believer in both cases is a winner.

So the believer receives every disaster expecting that good will come to him from it. Every believer must evaluate himself honestly: (Do I have a right over Allah? I am a possession of Allah, and I have no right with Him; whatever He makes to pass over me, He makes it pass in His own dominion.) Whoever does not like this, let him rebel against any disaster and say to it: "Do not afflict me," but he will not be able to avert any disaster. Since we cannot prevent the occurrence of calamities and events, let us accept them as believers, because the Truthful, Glorified and Exalted, by attributing us to Himself, wants to honor us and grant us dignity. He calls us to say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." By this statement we ascribe our ownership to Allah and accept what has happened to us. Here we must bring an example, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness: have you ever seen a person corrupt his own property? Never.

The owner of property works at everything that leads to goodness in his property, and even if people see outwardly that it is corruption, how much more so with Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, when we are His property, and He, Glorified, never exposes His dominion to harm, but establishes it upon wisdom and goodness.

"Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return": that is, we are owned by Allah, and we will return to Him. Even if there is injustice in the calamities of this world inflicted upon us by a person, we will receive the reward for what we were wronged in upon returning to Allah. Thus we belong to Allah at the beginning by ownership, and we belong to Allah at the end in our return; He, Glorified, is the owner of both ends: the beginning and the end. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us that at any disaster that befalls a person, he should say *istirjā'* (seeking restitution), that is, say: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return." He also added that we say: "O Allah, reward me in my disaster and give me something better than it in exchange." If you say it at any disaster that befalls you, you will surely find in what comes after it something better than it. And even if a person forgets to say it at the moment the disaster occurs, then remembers and says it, he receives its reward, as if he had said it at the hour of the disaster.

There is a story about Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her: when her husband Abu Salamah died, and he was filling the hearing and sight (i.e., he was great in her eyes), Umm Salamah grieved deeply over him.
