It was said to her: "Say what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) taught us." She said: "And what did he teach you?" They said: "Say: 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me in my disaster and give me something better than it in exchange.'" She said what was said to her, and behold, after the end of her waiting period, the Prophet (ﷺ) came to her proposing marriage. It was said to her: "Is there anyone better than Abu Salamah, or not?" She said: "I would never have aspired to that," i.e., I would not have expected such a situation.

So, every disaster that a person is exposed to, he must say upon it: "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return. O Allah, reward me in my disaster and give me something better than it in exchange."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 157:

What, then, is the state of those who say this supplication? Behold, Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord, and mercy, and those are the rightly guided.﴾ (2:157)

Let us consider the ultimate of aims, which Allah trains us to pursue, so that we may carry the call, protect the method of truth, and bring down the state of the falsifiers. This is an aim, but it is not the final aim. The final aim is that we do all this so that we may receive the mercies and blessings of Allah in the Hereafter.

So the final aim in every faith and every deed is seeking the pleasure of Allah and His mercy. As the late Shaykh Sayyid Qutb (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Beware lest anything distract you from the blessings, greetings and mercy of Allah, even the triumph of the creed itself."

It is as if the triumph of the creed is a means by which you attain the blessings and mercy from your Lord. Everything other than that is a means leading to an end, and the end of the believer is to be among those whom Allah's saying encompasses:

﴿Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord, and mercy, and those are the rightly guided.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah)

We know that salah (blessing, invocation) in the language means supplication. There is salah from people, salah from the angels, and salah from Allah. He says:

﴿It is He who blesses you, and His angels [do so too].﴾ (33:43, Surat al-Ahzab)

All of us live by the mercies of Allah. Even the disbeliever lives on the earth by the mercy of Allah, takes the means of his life by the mercy of Allah, and the blessings and goods on which he lives come to him by the mercy of Allah. The believer takes the blessings of this world by the mercy of Allah, and Allah increases for him through blessing and tranquility. Tranquility is a great blessing. Whoever lives this life while being at peace with a goal better than this life, this is a great form of tranquility.

So the salah from Allah is the bestowal of mercy and blessing.
The salah from the angels is seeking forgiveness.
The salah from the believers is supplication.

When you supplicate for Muhammad (ﷺ) with goodness, mercy and blessing, it is a supplication for yourself. Why? Because every rank that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attains returns to his ummah and to the whole world.

Who intercedes with Allah on the Day of Gathering, so that Allah may hasten the judgment among the creatures? It is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

So every good that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) attains is good for his ummah. If you pray for him, it is as if you are praying for yourself. When you send blessings upon him once, Allah sends blessings upon you ten times. Is there not good for you in that? ﴿Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord, and mercy, and those are the rightly guided.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah)

The rightly guided are those who keep to the path that leads to the aim, and the aim is blessings from their Lord and mercy. You are now enjoying the blessings of Allah through the means of Allah, and with Allah in the Hereafter you will, by Allah's permission, enjoy the blessings of Allah and the meeting with Allah.

Afterwards the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols (sha'a'ir) of Allah. So whoever performs the Hajj to the House or the 'Umrah, there is no blame upon him for going around them. And whoever volunteers good, indeed Allah is Appreciative (shakir) and All-Knowing.﴾

Al-Safa and al-Marwah are two small hills, known to those who have visited the holy sites and to those who have not. I ask Allah that they see them with the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin), and when they see them, this will be knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin). These two hills were where our lady Hajar, the mother of Isma'il, went back and forth seeking water for her son, after Ibrahim had left them beside the Sacred House of Allah.

And by Allah, what would a woman think when her husband leaves her with her infant in a place where there is no food and no water?

Here Hajar uttered her well-known words:

"To whom are you leaving us? Did Allah command you to do this?"

Our lord Ibrahim said: "Yes." She said: "Then He will not let us perish. She has sufficed herself with the Creator over the created, and she would not have spoken such words except by revelation from the Causer (al-Musabbib). This is the first matter of faith, with attention to the foundation of faith upon which it was established, when Ibrahim, peace be upon him, supplicated to his Lord, saying: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer﴾ (Qur'an 14:37).

When you read "uncultivated" (ghayr dhi zar') know that it means without water, for wherever there is water, there is vegetation. Water is the essential foundation for sustaining life, and when water is absent from a mother and her infant, what would their condition be? Her child became thirsty, and she wanted to search for a spring of water, or a bird descending in a place so she would know there was water there, or to see a caravan travelling with water. Therefore she went out to the highest place and left the valley, and climbed the top of the hill of al-Safa, but found nothing. Then she looked toward the other side, to al-Marwah, and climbed it, but found nothing. She continued going back and forth between al-Safa and al-Marwah seven times. We can imagine her state: a woman of such an age, in such loneliness, with no water with her, and she must have become thirsty just as her infant became thirsty. When exhaustion reached her, her attempts ended, and she returned to where the infant was.

Had her running between al-Safa and al-Marwah been fruitful, and she had found water, we would have said: running alone brought her the water. But it was she who had said earlier: "Then He will not let us perish." And by this saying she had attached herself to the Causer, not to the cause. Had He given her by the direct cause, which is her searching for water, there would have been no proof of her sincerity in her saying: "Then He will not let us perish." The Truth willed that her running end seven times without result, and that she return to her infant; and she found water at the foot of the infant. Thus Hajar was truthful in her certainty, when she was sure that Allah would not let her perish, and Allah willed to say to her: "We know that I will not let you perish, and not by your running, but by the foot of your suckling child, striking it against the earth, whereupon water gushes forth from it." The infant's striking of the earth with his foot was a cause that ordinarily does not act, but Allah willed it as a cause, so that causality would be preserved even if it does not lead to the purpose.

When Hajar found water at the foot of her suckling child, she truly knew that Allah had not let her perish. The running remained a rite (sha'ira) of the Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah, as a perpetuation of a person's faith in the Causer and of not neglecting the cause, and so that a human being approaches every work while believing in the Causer. For this reason we must distinguish between tawakkul (trust in Allah) and tawakul (reliance on chance and neglect). Tawakkul is an act of the heart, not an act of the limbs, while tawakul is the suspension of the limbs. There is no tawakul in Islam; rather, the limbs work and the hearts trust. Such was the tawakkul of Hajar: she worked and trusted in Allah; so Allah provided her with what she wanted through the easiest of causes, which was the striking of the infant's foot on the earth, and that matter remained a rite of the Hajj, namely seven circuits between al-Safa and al-Marwah.

When people neglected the worship of Allah, and the worship of idols entered the Arabian Peninsula, they set up on the hill of al-Safa an idol they named (Isaf), and on al-Marwah an idol they named (Na'ila). They used to go back and forth between Isaf and Na'ila, not between al-Safa and al-Marwah. They had transferred the worship from the purity of monotheism (khalisiyat al-tawhid) to the admixture of paganism (shaa'ibiyat al-wathaniyya).

When Islam came, Allah willed that the Muslims not turn in their prayers toward the Sacred House until the House was purified and made sincerely for Allah. When some believers went to the Ka'bah, they felt uneasy about running between al-Safa and al-Marwah, because Isaf and Na'ila were atop the two hills. It was as if they wished to cut off every connection with the customs of the Jahiliyya, and their faith was too proud to go back and forth between Isaf and Na'ila. So Allah sent down His saying, the Truth: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So whoever performs the Hajj to the House or the 'Umrah, there is no blame upon him for going around them. And whoever volunteers good, indeed Allah is Appreciative and All-Knowing﴾, meaning: do not be uneasy about this matter, for you will run between al-Safa and al-Marwah, not between Isaf and Na'ila as the polytheist idolaters used to do. Therefore the action here is by intention.

The first intention of Hajar's running was faith in Allah and taking the causes, but paganism turned the summit of faith into the depths of disbelief. It was necessary for the Muslims to restore the original intention of faith when visiting the Sacred House by running between al-Safa and al-Marwah. For in Islam we submit to the command of the One who commands. He told us: "Kiss the Black Stone," and at the same time He commanded us to stone the stone that symbolizes Iblis. Thus the lesson lies in the intention, not in the form of the act, and the lesson lies in obeying the command of Allah. It is as if the Truth, through this verse, says to the believers: The polytheists worshipped Isaf and Na'ila, but you, put that matter out of your minds and go to al-Safa and al-Marwah, for al-Safa and al-Marwah are symbols of Allah, and are not symbols of paganism; rather, the misguidance of the polytheists is what bestowed paganism upon them in Isaf and Na'ila. The idolaters, by placing Isaf upon al-Safa and Na'ila upon al-Marwah, wished to take for them the attribute of sanctity of idols. Had al-Safa and al-Marwah not been sacred earlier, they would not have placed their stones upon them, nor would they have brought their idols to place them upon the Ka'bah. This is evidence that the sanctity of these places predates their idols. They protected their paganism by placing Isaf and Na'ila upon al-Safa and al-Marwah.

After the Truth made clear to the believers that al-Safa and al-Marwah are symbols of Allah, He points out that the one who dwells in a place does not defile the place. The proof is that when faith was granted victory, it broke the idols and removed them from the Ka'bah, and the House became pure. And when the believers were uneasy about doing an act of the Jahiliyya, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, reassured them and said: ﴿Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.﴾

The word (safa) means a smooth stone, and it became so from the great number of those who touched it over time. It was said that al-Safa is named after the chosenness (istifa') of Adam, and it was said that al-Marwah is named after a woman, who is Eve; but this is a saying that is reported, and we do not dwell on it much, for it is knowledge that does not benefit and ignorance that does not harm. What matters to us is that it is a place where Hajar went back and forth seeking water for her son. The Truth made running between them one of the symbols of Allah, and symbols (sha'a'ir) are the markers of worship, and they are always applied to physical landmarks: one says, this is the tawaf area, this is the sa'i (course), this is the place of stoning the pillars (marmá al-jamarat), and this is the Sacred Monument (al-mash'ar al-haram).

The word (mash'ar) means the place that has a specific worship. Since al-Safa and al-Marwah are two places, their description as "among the symbols of Allah" has come. ﴿So whoever performs the Hajj to the House or the 'Umrah, there is no blame upon him for going around them.﴾ It is as if Hajj and 'Umrah have something that places them in the status of obligation, and something else that places them in the status of voluntary act. If a Muslim performs Hajj and 'Umrah once, he has fulfilled the obligation, and this does not prevent that repeating Hajj and 'Umrah is an accepted voluntary act, by Allah's permission, for which there is gratitude from Allah.

When we say: "There is no blame upon you for doing such-and-such," it means that if you do it, there is no sin upon you, but it is not wrong to do it, and it is not an obligation to do it. This is what led some people to say that running between al-Safa and al-Marwah is not a pillar of the Hajj. We say to these: this verse came for a reason, namely that they were uneasy about going around in a place where the polytheists used to go around, so He said to them: ﴿there is no blame upon him for going around them.﴾

The negation of blame does not mean that it is valid if you do not do it. No; He, glorified is He, is responding to a situation they were uneasy about. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿going around them﴾ calls for a pause from us. The pilgrim or the one performing 'Umrah runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah, so why did the Truth describe this running as ﴿going around them﴾? To know that, we must clarify the meaning of (taafa), (jaala) and (daara). (Taafa) means "to revolve around a thing." So what is the circuit between al-Safa and al-Marwah, such that the Truth calls it tawaf? The one who revolves around a circle may begin from any point on it as a beginning, so that point becomes an end; so in every circuit around a circle you find that every beginning is an end and every end is a beginning, and any movement from and to one thing makes a circle.

It is true that one who runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah does not revolve, but he goes from al-Safa to al-Marwah, then turns back to al-Safa, then from it to al-Marwah, and so the matter becomes a tawaf. Another example from our daily life: the policeman who patrols the streets and houses at night may go around the whole city, or may go around a single street, which is the place of his watch; this turning in the street from its beginning to its end several times is called a tawaf between them. Thus we understand the meaning of ﴿going around them﴾, that is, walking between them several times from beginning to end.

Thus we find that running between al-Safa and al-Marwah is part of the symbols of the Hajj and the 'Umrah. And we find that the obligatory character of Hajj and 'Umrah is fundamental, and voluntarily repeating Hajj and 'Umrah is good. ﴿And whoever volunteers good, indeed Allah is Appreciative and All-Knowing.﴾ This saying requires that we understand that the one who is appreciative has received a blessing from the one who is appreciated; so what has the Truth received from the repetition of Hajj?

When the believer performs what Allah has made obligatory upon him, he performs the obligation; but when he adds voluntarily out of love for the rite itself, this is an increase for which Allah gives thanks. So the gratitude of Allah, mighty and majestic, indicates that a blessing will come. When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, makes obligatory upon a servant certain duties, the servant is bound by them; and when the servant increases in the same kind of what Allah has made obligatory upon him, this shows his love and passion for the obligation from Allah. And if he loves and is passionate about the obligation from Allah without Allah demanding it of him or binding him to it, but has made it beloved to him, then he deserves that Allah thank him for it; and Allah's gratitude to the servant is a gift without end.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 2, verse 159:

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We have made it clear to the people in the Book — those are cursed by Allah and cursed by the cursers.﴾ [2:159]

When the Truth, glory be to Him, presents this matter, He makes clear to us the recompense for those who conceal what Allah has sent down. Some of the People of the Book concealed the clear proofs that Allah had sent down in the Book they possessed, proofs that establish the truth of Muhammad (ﷺ) in his prophethood. This concealment would inherit evils, and whenever the world suffers harm from their concealment, they will be cursed. Cursing (al-la'n) is expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, alerts the believers in our master Muhammad (ﷺ) that this recompense of expulsion and cursing is not restricted to these people; rather, it extends to and includes everyone who conceals what Allah has sent down of clear proofs. Thus it contains a reality of what happened with the People of the Book, and it also contains a warning to those who believe in Islam not to conceal the proofs of Allah; otherwise they will arrive at what those people arrived at, which is cursing.

The word (al-la'n, cursing) occurs in the Qur'an forty-one times. When it comes as punishment, it is expulsion and removal with anger, which is eternal abiding in the Fire; and when expulsion is removal for discipline, it is not with anger, because the one who disciplines does not become angry at the one he disciplines, rather he becomes angry for the one he disciplines. When expulsion happens after anger, that is evidence that there is no return after it. A person who is left with a silent thing to be punished by, such as the Fire, says to himself: "Perhaps someone will come who will be softened toward my condition and show compassion to me and will take me out of the Fire." He says this to himself, because the thing by which he is punished is silent and has no compassion. But what is the way out if the curse is from Allah, the angels and the people? As the Truth says in another verse:

﴿Those — their recompense is that upon them is the curse of Allah and of the angels and of mankind, all together.﴾ [3:87]

It becomes clear to us here that the curse of Allah is in this world and in the Hereafter, and the cursers from among the people curse them. In the verse we are reflecting upon, the curse is more comprehensive, because (al-la'inun, the cursers) includes people and other than people of the other creatures, as if everyone in existence shares in cursing them. For example, if Allah withholds water from a people because of their disobedience, then the plants curse them because they have been deprived of water, the animals curse them because they have been deprived of water, and the places curse them because they opposed what the places are upon of glorifying Allah. As for the curse of the Hereafter, where there is no seeing of plant or animal, the cursing of them will be issued from Allah, the angels and all mankind. And mankind are the children of Adam until the Hour is established, and among them are disbelievers and believers. How then can the cursing come from those who disbelieved, since they too are cursed?

We say: In this world we find one who deceives another in the religion of Allah, and there is one who is deceived. When matters become clear in the Hereafter, and the deceivers are exposed, and the deceived are left in regret, then those who were followed disown those who followed. The deceiver disowns the deceived, and the deceived disowns the deceiver. And whenever a nation of the deceived enters the Fire, they curse the nation that deceived them; and whenever a deceiving nation enters the Fire, it curses those who submitted to the deception, and they curse one another. The Truth says:

﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [from 2:166].

And He also says:

﴿Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾ [from 7:38].

So cursing exists among the disbelievers toward one another, just as it exists in this world too. Those who disbelieve in the method of Allah, deviate and do wrong, receive the curse from the people of Allah's method, and receive the curse from the wronged among them. Then another situation arises: someone comes who wrongs them, so they curse him and he curses them, and thus all of mankind curses them. Cursing with expulsion, anger and rebuke differs from disciplinary cursing, which takes the form of removal, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did with those who stayed behind in the Battle of Tabuk. The Battle of Tabuk was called the Battle of Hardship (al-'usra), because it came with hardship from every direction: the distance between Tabuk and Medina; another hardship from the shortage of mounts carrying the fighters, for every ten fighters took turns on a single mount; hardship and difficulty in provisions, to the extent that they ate dates with their worms, and they ate fat, grease and rancid tallow; hardship in water, to the extent that they would slaughter a camel to drink the water from its stomach and paunch; and hardship in the scorching, extremely hot air. All conditions were difficult and harsh, and they necessitated that none go out to the expedition except one who was sincere in his certainty.

That expedition was a test and trial for faith in people's souls. Therefore some of them yielded to the whisperings of the self to remain in Medina, and one of them said: "Shall I remain in shade and comfort while the Messenger of Allah is in the heat? By Allah, this will never be!" Then he got up and followed the army of the believers. Another had an orchard with shade and fruits; he looked at his orchard and said: "Are you the one who prevented me from being in the company of the Messenger of Allah? By Allah, you will not be my property after now, and you are for Allah in the way of Allah." A third sat in his house with his beautiful wife before him and trees and crops around him, and said: "Shall I sit in shade, moisture, water and a beautiful woman while the Messenger of Allah is in the scorching heat? By Allah, this will never be!" and he mounted his horse toward the desert to join the Muslim army.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned victorious, those who had not accompanied him on the journey of victory excused themselves, saying they did not possess the means of war: mounts, armor, swords and arrows. The Messenger of Allah accepted their outward excuses and left their inner states to Allah, except for three who spoke the truth and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we were never richer than the hour we refrained from going with you; we had the equipment of war and mounts."

The Messenger of Allah ordered the people not to speak to them or deal with them. Two of them submitted and remained in their houses: Hilal ibn Umayya and Murara ibn al-Rabi'. As for Ka'b ibn Malik, he would go out and meet people, but no one would speak to him. He would go to pray with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and steal glances at the Prophet and greet him, but the Messenger of Allah would not return the greeting; he lowered his gaze and turned away from him, to the extent that Ka'b said: "I would look to see whether the Messenger of Allah moved his lips to return the greeting or not."

Why all of this? The Prophet (ﷺ) intended it as a means of clarifying how disciplinary removal works. The world became constricted for the three. Ka'b went to his cousin Abu Qatada and climbed the wall onto him, because he knew that if he knocked on the door it would not be opened to him. Despite his climbing the wall, the cousin turned away from him, so he said, hoping: "I beseech you by Allah, I beseech you by Allah, I beseech you by Allah," all of which his cousin did not answer. Then he said to him: "You know that I love the Messenger of Allah." His cousin did not answer him, and he continued pleading, asking about the time of pardon, and Abu Qatada said: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

When forty nights had passed over this removal, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) escalated the discipline by ordering the three men, through a messenger he sent to them, not to approach their wives. Isolation had entered a new circle, the circle of the private society where a man and his wife are. Ka'b said to the messenger of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Shall I divorce my wife?" The messenger said: "No, but do not approach her." Some people said to Ka'b: "Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or let your wife go to ask his permission for her to remain with you to serve you; for the wife of Hilal ibn Umayya asked the Messenger of Allah, and he permitted her to serve her husband." Ka'b said: "By Allah, I will not do that, because when the wife of Hilal went to the Messenger of Allah he said to her: 'Let him not approach you,' and she said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, Hilal has no movement toward anything,' so he permitted her to remain to serve him. But I am a young man and I fear that if I ask the Messenger of Allah he will not grant me this right."

Thus was the removal of discipline, and it was not a complete expulsion from the enclosure of faith, as evidenced by the fact that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made those receiving the discipline subject to commands he issued to them. Then the good news of release came after ten days, when the Truth revealed His saying:

﴿And upon the three who were left behind, until when the earth was constricted for them despite its vastness, and their souls were constricted for them, and they thought that there is no refuge from Allah except in Him. Then He turned to them that they might repent. Indeed, Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [9:118]

1. This is a matter we find today in the training of special units in armies. They accustom and train them to eat and drink whatever food or drink they find that sustains their lives, since something may happen that prevents their supply of food or drink, and this is for preserving their lives and defending their homelands..

Thus the Truth (al-Haqq) has not closed the door but has left it open before man, even to one who disbelieved, and even to one who concealed. So let no one think that his past disbelief, his concealment, or his slackness in supporting the Truth will shut the door in his face or stand between him and his Lord. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿Except those who repent, make amends, and make [the truth] clear. Those, I will accept their repentance, and I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ (2:160)

That is: they declare their repentance, and repentance is an inner matter; they set right what they corrupted to the extent of their corruption; and they make things clear to the people to the extent of what they concealed. So the condition of repentance is that every right returns to its owner. Whoever concealed something must make it clear. Concealment does not affect only the relationship between the servant and the Lord; it also harms the servants. And when the Almighty opens the door of repentance to the servant, He says:

﴿He turned to them so that they might repent﴾ (part of 9:118).

The root (t-w-b) (tāba) means returning to God. When the servant repents, he returns to his Lord seeking forgiveness for disobedience and sin. When God turns to a servant, it means that God has accepted his repentance: whereas he had been destined to be punished, God pardons him and does not punish him. So repentance in its entirety is a return to God. When repentance from God is mentioned before repentance from the servants, as in His saying ﴿He turned to them so that they might repent﴾, this means that the Truth prescribed repentance and regulated it in order to open the door of return to Him. There are, then, three stages of repentance:

The first stage: that God prescribed repentance.

The second stage: that the servant repents.

The third stage: that God accepts the repentance.

All of them mean turning back from disobedience and sin.

So whoever commits a sin must make amends for it in the same manner as he committed it. If he committed a sin in secret, it suffices that he repent in secret. But if he violated the limits of God openly, we say to him: it is never right that you disobey God openly before people and become a bad example for people who will thereby become bold and violate the limits of God, and then repent between yourself and God in secret. Your repentance must be public. For this reason the common proverb says: "You strike me in the street and make peace with me in the alley."

To one who violates a limit of God before people, we say: your repentance must be declared before all people. For this reason we avert the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd) because of doubts (shubhāt). But one who boasts of having committed a sin we do not leave alone. For example, one who was witnessed by four people as having committed a major sin such as adultery, who kept committing the sin recklessly until four witnessed against him: can it be reasonable for us to say to him, "We avert it because of doubts"? No. He violated the limit openly, so he must be punished by carrying out the prescribed penalty.

As for those who repent, make amends for what they corrupted, and make clear to the people what they concealed, their recompense is repentance from God.

Part of God's kindness to man is that He prescribed repentance so that people feel the weight of sin, and made it an act of the penitent and an act of the One who accepts repentance, who is the Almighty. He said "they repent" (tābū) and "I turn" (atūbu). All of this is so that a person who commits a sin and then repents does not feel that it is an insurmountable matter. The Truth says: ﴿Those, I will accept their repentance, and I am the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾. He, glorified is He, turns to whoever repents from sin, and turns to all sinners together. He, exalted is He, is "Tawwāb," a word that signifies intensity in the attribute.

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers — upon them is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together.﴾ [2:161]

They are those who persisted in refusing to repent, so their recompense is the curse of Allah, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together. And He, glory be to Him, adds:

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 162:

﴿Abiding therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾

The truth (al-Haqq, God) speaks of the punishment of the disbelievers; He speaks of the Fire as a punishment and of time as eternity (khulud), then He raises eternity to everlastingness (al-abadiyyah). Thereby we know that there is a punishment in the Fire, and an abiding in it, and everlastingness. And because God's mercy has preceded His wrath in the ordaining of punishment, abiding in the Fire is never mentioned with the word "forever" (abadan) except in surah al-Jinn, where He says:

﴿And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger, then for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ (part of verse 23, surah al-Jinn).

Since there is a restricted (muqayyad) statement, every unrestricted (mutlaq) mention of eternity is to be understood in light of it. The fact that the Truth did not use the word "abadan" when mentioning punishment is evidence that His mercy preceded His wrath even in the ordaining of punishment. There is an objection that arises from superficial understanding (sathiyyat al-fahm). When the Truth says:

﴿On the Day when it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission; some of them will be wretched and some happy. As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He wills. And as for those who are happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills—a gift unbroken.﴾ (surah Hud).

The Truth is speaking of the Day of Gathering, and of mankind, its wretched and its happy. Those who are wretched will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing. We may imagine the picture of breathing inside the Fire amid its gloomy atmosphere of flame. A human breathes in order to be refreshed by air; how then would he take it in from the Fire? In that is a great punishment. And the people of the Fire abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure.

Superficial thinkers ask: "God places those who are wretched in the Fire as long as the heavens and the earth endure, and says the same about those who are happy in the Garden." We say to them: the heavens and the earth now differ from the heavens and the earth in the Hereafter. The heavens and the earth in this world are causes and livelihood; but in the Hereafter we do not eat through causes, rather through the Causer. We live in the Hereafter by the word "Be" (kun), and do not live by the causes of plowing, sowing and rain. God will change the heavens and the earth on the Last Day. Read, if you wish, the saying of the Truth:

﴿On the Day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens as well﴾ (part of verse 48, surah Ibrahim).

From this saying we understand that what is meant is the heavens and the earth that have been changed. We note that the Truth, in the matter of the abiding of the wretched, spoke with the exception of will, saying: (except as your Lord wills). So the abiding of the wretched in the Fire is undone and brought to an end by the will of God, because the wretched are not only the disbelievers; among them are also some sinful believers. These sinful believing wretched will enter the Fire and receive their recompense, but after receiving their recompense they will come out. Thus the abiding will end at the end of time, and the meaning of (except as your Lord wills) is that they remain in the Fire until a specified time.

As for the Garden, the exception applies from the beginning. Why? Because the believer who disobeyed God will not enter the Garden from the outset; rather he will spend a period in the Fire and then enter the Garden. Thus the abiding in the Garden, as far as he is concerned, has been diminished from its beginning. As for the wretched, the abiding in the Fire is diminished from its end. So (except as your Lord wills) means that the sinful believer will not enter the Garden from the beginning of the Hereafter. Thus: "except" here comes to exclude time from its beginning for the happy, or to exclude time from its end for the sinful wretched. For this reason you find no contradiction, that contradiction which superficial understanding produces.

As for His saying: (the punishment will not be lightened for them): when a person is punished with something, repetition of the punishment upon him may perhaps make him accustomed to punishment; but reality says that the punishment intensifies upon him. So lightening has no connection with time. As for His saying: (nor will they be reprieved), from it we know that reprieve (inzar) is respite (imhal), and the meaning is that they will not be delayed from their punishment; or (nor will they be looked upon) means that He does not look upon them. There is a verse that conveys this meaning in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Nor will God speak to them, nor look upon them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them﴾ (part of verse 77, surah Al 'Imran).

Because looking gives some tenderness; and why did He say: "nor will they be reprieved"? Because you may turn toward someone and look at him without intention, spontaneously. But the gaze is not directed toward him with compassion, and He, glory be to Him, does not look upon them at all, because a gaze may suggest a kind of pity. Thus (nor will they be reprieved) means: He will never look upon them at all, as if they have been utterly neglected.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 163:

Then the Truth says:

﴿And your God is One God; there is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.﴾

This is the fundamental matter of the Truth. "Your God" (ilahukum) means that the one worshipped is one God. In reality, the true God existed before disbelief came into being.

"There is no god but He" is a second matter, because the heedlessness of people is what led some souls to turn toward other gods.

The Truth's statement, that He, glory be to Him, is "One God" (ilah wahid), means that He has no second. The difference between wahid (one) and ahad (single, indivisible) is that wahid means He has no second, while ahad means He is not composite and not made up of parts. Therefore we cannot describe God as "kull" (a whole) or "kulli" (universal), because "kull" is opposed by "juz'" (part) and "kulli" is opposed by "juz'i" (particular), and "kull" is that which is formed by the gathering of parts. God is singular in His oneness, glory be to Him, exalted above everything, and to Him belongs the highest likeness. I give this example for approximation, not for comparison: a chair is a "whole" made of wood, nails, glue and paint. Can we apply the name "chair" to the wood, or to the nails, or to the glue, or to the paint? No. Every part is not called "the whole"; rather, the whole arises from the gathering of the parts.

The "universal" (kulli) is applied to many things, but each of them realizes the universal. The word "human" (insan) we call a "universal"; its particulars are Muhammad, Zayd, Bakr, Umar and Khalid. We say, "Zayd is a human," and that is a correct statement, and we say, "Umar is a human," and that is a correct statement.

God, glory be to Him and exalted, is not a "universal," because He is One, and He is not a "whole," because He is ahad.

The fundamental matter in religion is "Your God is One God; there is no god but He." The Qur'an does not negate, and say "There is no god but He," except when heedlessness arises that gives divinity to other than God, or gives divinity to God and to partners with Him. The Qur'an negates that and says: "There is no god but He, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful." And there is nothing other than God except a blessing from Him, glory be to Him, or one upon whom a blessing has been bestowed.

Whatever is other than God is either a blessing or one upon whom a blessing is bestowed, and all of these are breaths of the Most Merciful and of the Especially Merciful. Since everything other than God is either a blessing or one upon whom a blessing is bestowed, a blessing is not described as a god, and one upon whom a blessing is bestowed is not called a god, because "one upon whom a blessing is bestowed" means that another has poured his blessings upon him; for blessing is given, and the one blessed is the one to whom it is given. If something is a gift, or is given to someone, it is not valid for it to be a god. But those who are led into temptation are only tempted through means, and the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, is the Causer of all causes.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, draws our attention to serving this matter: He calls us to look at the universe and reflect upon the blessing that exists for us. Then you, O one upon whom God has bestowed this blessing: if you find someone claiming it for himself, give it up and leave it to him, and attribute the blessings to their Originator, who is God. Beware of associating anyone other than Him with God's blessing, for God says, in the Hadith Qudsi:

("I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his partner.")(1)

1. A Hadith Qudsi narrated by Muslim and Ibn Majah.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66), on surah 2, verse 164:

The Truth (al-Haqq) draws our attention to the cosmos, saying:

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ship that runs in the sea with what benefits people, and what God sends down from the sky of water, whereby He gives life to the earth after its death, and disperses in it every kind of creature, and the turning of the winds and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth, are signs for a people who use their reason.﴾

Indeed God, glorified is He, in His mercy created man as one blessed with favours, and created everything in the cosmos as a favour to him. He draws our attention to the proof of this matter through the cosmos itself. He specifies manifestations in the cosmos that no one has claimed to have created or brought into being. So when people who do not believe in the One God come and shift divinity to other than Him, we say to them: this wondrous cosmos, which is embodied in the earth, embodied in the sky, embodied in the alternation of night and day, embodied in the ships that run in the sea, embodied in the water that God sent down from the sky, and embodied in the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth — all these signs, that is, these wondrous matters, draw attention to the fact that their Originator is greater than them.

He, glorified is He, wants to alert the intellect to receive the favour of existence in itself and in the cosmos subjected to it, so that it may infer from these wondrous signs the truth of God's saying: "Your God is One God" [cf. 2:163]. For it is not reasonable that anyone other than God should create all that creation and then remain silent about it! Moreover, no one has claimed to have created them. Since no one has claimed that, and you, O human, did not create them, and despite disbelief and obstinacy, no one has ever claimed this matter at all, then the dominion will remain God's alone until someone says: "I have dominion," and until now no one has dared to say this word. This is evidence that God is One, the Unique. The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know.﴾ (Surah Ghafir [40:57]).

Why? Because mankind was created from the earth, and lives by what is in the earth. So the principle is that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind; for mankind are the children of the earth, and their sustenance comes from it and their continued life is upon it. And it is reasonable that the Truth, glorified is He, created that from which man is created before He created man, and so that man might live, God supplied him with the same kind of that from which he was created. And remember well that we have said that when God presents the matter of creation to man, He presents it in a way that carries immunity against any other matter that contradicts it. Therefore He tells us: the creation of the heavens and the earth and your creation is an unseen matter, and since it is an unseen matter, no one has witnessed it or seen it except the One who created it; so take knowledge of creation from Him. For this reason God, the Exalted, said:

﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor did I take the misleaders as helpers.﴾ (Surah al-Kahf [18:51]).

So we must beware of these misleaders who try to mislead us with matters that are not true. The Truth has known from eternity that there would be those who say: the heavens and the earth were created in such-and-such a way, and man was created by such-and-such a method. When we hear these people we say: these are the misleaders, and God has warned us of them from eternity.

Thus the existence of misleaders is itself the proof of God's truthfulness. These are those who said: the earth was a part of the sun and separated from it, and man's origin is an ape — for if there were no misleaders we would say: "Where, O Lord, is what You said about them, that they are misleaders?"

And when God, the Exalted, presents that He created us from the earth and made our sustenance from it, knowledge comes even from those who disbelieve in God to confirm this matter. When they analysed the human being, they found him composed of sixteen elements, and when they analysed the clay from which crops and fertility come, they found it to be sixteen elements also, matching the elements of the human being, the first of which is oxygen and the last of which is manganese. On this basis, when the Truth says: "I created man from clay," we say to Him: You have spoken truly, O Lord, for You made our sustenance come from what emerges from the clay.

So the matter of the creation of the heavens and the earth must be the starting point of wonder, and you, O human, must take heed of what has been created for you, so that you may infer your Creator, believe, and testify that He is One God. If anyone tries to mislead you and says to you, "There is another god," say: "There is no god but Him, glorified is He."

When the Truth speaks of man, He, glorified is He, speaks of one established in the cosmos, and this one established in the cosmos needs two things: time and place. The place for man is the earth on which he walks and the sky that shades him, and time is what arises from the night and what arises from the day. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, wants to give us the lesson in the alternation of night and day. The meaning of the alternation of night and day is that each of them comes after the other: the day comes after the night, and the night comes after the day.

﴿And He it is who made the night and the day to succeed each other, for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful.﴾ (Surah al-Furqan [25:62]).

So the alternation of night and day means that the day should not be perpetual, i.e., unceasing, and that the night likewise should not be perpetual. For this reason there are other verses in which the Truth bestows this blessing upon us, saying:

﴿Say: Have you considered: if God made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you light? Will you not then listen? Say: Have you considered: if God made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you a night in which you may rest? Will you not then see?﴾ (Surah al-Qasas [28:71–72]).

So you, O one who moves in the cosmos, are subject to what applies to every moving thing: you must have rest in proportion to your movement. Therefore time has been divided into night, in which you rest, and day, in which you move. For this reason the Truth says:

﴿And He it is who made for you the night as a garment and sleep as rest﴾ (part of verse 47, Surah al-Furqan).

And He, glorified is He, knows from eternity that the night, that is the time of rest, cannot be a rest for all people; rather there must be people who carry out matters requiring wakefulness at night, and to these He says:

﴿And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day﴾ (part of verse 23, Surah al-Rum).

He gives an opportunity to those whose eyes remain wakeful all night, so that they may rest by day.

Thus, from the greatness of the Truth is that He made time alternate. For if the night were perpetual and the day were perpetual, life would be corrupted. For this reason we find that the Truth swore by His saying:

﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it is still﴾ (Surah al-Duha [93:1–2]).

So the morning brightness is the place of movement and toil, and the night is the place of stillness, and both must exist together. The Truth, glorified is He, says: "Indeed in the alternation of night and day, and the ships that run in the sea" — and the word "fulk" (ships) is used both for the singular and the plural, as in His saying concerning Noah's ship: "and build the ship under Our eyes" [11:37]. That means he builds one ship, whereas "the ships that run" are all the ships. And how can the running of ships on water be a sign? Man understands that if water were not in this fluid state, ships could not sail upon it; water must be liquid so that ships can run upon it. And before the invention of steam engines, these ships used to run in the sea by the force of the winds. Why? Because water is of two kinds:

* river water;

* sea water.

River waters always flow from high to low towards the outlet, and so it is reasonable that we attribute a ship's movement in them to the current of the water. But if we want to make it sail against the flow of the water, then we need the wind to assist us in that, and we take the word "rih" (wind) to mean air. But "rih" also means force, for God, glorified is He, says:

﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart﴾ (part of verse 46, Surah al-Anfal).

That is, your strength; that is, dispute only results in the dissipation of strength. And the wind was a visible force. When man arrived at inventing the steam engine and ships were operated by it, man dispensed with operating ships by wind. Thus we know that the word "rih" is understood as the winds, and is also understood as absolute force, and thirdly in the sense of scent.

The Qur'an clarifies this for us: when the meaning of "rih" as absolute force is used, we find the Qur'an saying:

﴿If He wills, He stills the wind, so that they remain motionless on its surface﴾ (part of verse 33, Surah al-Shura).

That is, when God wills, He disables the motive force of anything, and He, glorified is He, does so. As for the meaning of "rih" as scent, we find it in the Truth's saying:

﴿And when the caravan departed, their father said: Indeed I find the scent of Joseph﴾ (part of verse 94, Surah Yusuf).

Ya'qub, the father of Yusuf, peace be upon them both, possessed a strong sense of smell; when the caravan left Egypt, his father said: "Indeed I smell the scent of Joseph." And in the countryside we hear someone say: "I will take revenge on so-and-so and not leave a trace (rīha) of him on the earth," meaning he will leave no trace of him on the earth. And why was the word "rā'iha" (scent) used here? It has only been proven recently that scent is the most lasting trace for a living being, as evidenced by the fact that creatures with a strong sense of smell, such as police dogs, track a culprit by his scent to his whereabouts, as if the culprit leaves a trace of his scent at the scene of the crime; all that is required is for someone with a strong sense of smell to be present to track him.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has given us intellect, but He has left to some of us, and to the non-rational, what the majority of us cannot reach. The dog, which is a dumb, unreasoning animal, comes to track things we cannot track, because it is still only in the realm of the senses, whereas man has taken a share of the realm of the senses and a share of the intellect.

And the Truth's saying: "and what God sends down from the sky of water, whereby He gives life to the earth after its death" — does this saying mean that the water is in the sky? No. The water originally is in the earth, but the water of the earth that remains still is not beneficial for our irrigation or for the irrigation of our crops; it is salty, bitter, and brackish, and what exists on the earth of it is only a reserve. Therefore God placed in it chemical materials that keep it from spoiling and keep its properties and nature from changing. Then the extent of water spreads over the land in a ratio of three times, why? Because God wants the surface of the water to spread so widely that it gives evaporation large, vast sources; this evaporation is the process of divine distillation.

The sending down of water from the sky is what we see in the form of rain, but before its descent come several stages: evaporation, condensation, the fertilising of the clouds by the winds, and others. These many stages we have only recently come to know, as evidenced by our attempts to imitate this cycle by evaporating and condensing salt water to extract distilled water; but that has high financial costs, for one cup of distilled water takes time and requires effort and expense, whereas the divine laboratory pours forth for us abundance without limit in its quantities. This laboratory works, and we do not know it.

The water cycle begins with the rising of vapour from the water, and after that it meets a cold zone and falls as fresh water. And from the precision of the Wise Creator, glorified is He, is that He made the level of fresh water always higher than the level of the salt water; for if the level of the salt were higher than the fresh, it would overwhelm it and spoil it, and we would find no water to drink. But the Wise Creator made the level of fresh waters in the rivers higher than the water of the seas and oceans, so that the water flows from the river into the sea; and that causes no harm.

So the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, teaches us that He sent down water from the sky. How does this water descend? This is what we have only recently come to know. And by fresh water God gives life to the earth after its death. And what is death? Death is the cessation of movement. Likewise the earth, when it dries, retains no movement; and we cannot with our senses perceive the movement of the earth during the growth of plants, but God, mighty and majestic, affirms this in His saying:

﴿And you see the earth lifeless, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells﴾ (part of verse 5, Surah al-Hajj).

When rain falls on the earth, its crust swells, and that crust rises to the surface of the earth; then what happens?

{ And it causes to grow from every pair

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 165:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿And among the people are those who take, besides Allah, rivals (andad) whom they love as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah. If only those who have wronged could see, when they see the punishment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ (2:165)

The nidd (rival) is the like and the equal, and the kafir (disbeliever) is one who ascribes to Allah a like and an equal. The polytheists (mushrikun) do not exclude Allah from divinity; rather they associate with Him others as rivals (andad). They love these rivals as they love Allah, or they love them as you love Allah. Just as the believer loves his Lord, the disbeliever loves his god whom he has taken as an object of worship. (But those who believe are stronger in their love for Allah.) Why? Because this is the love about which no one disagrees. But the love of these polytheists for their many false gods varies. When harm touches the polytheist, he supplicates to Allah and not to the false gods, in confirmation of the words of the Exalted:

﴿And when harm touches the human being, he calls upon Us, lying on his side or sitting or standing﴾ (part of 10:12).

The polytheist discovers by his natural disposition (fitrah) the falsehood he has told himself regarding his taking rivals to Allah. Therefore, when the means are exhausted for him and he falls into a dilemma, he does not deceive himself and say: "O idol, help me!" Rather he says: "O Lord, rescue me!" As for the believer, he does not change his love for Allah at all. The believer loves his Lord in ease and in hardship, and on this basis the ones who believe are stronger in their love for Allah, because they do not forget Him, neither in comfort nor in adversity. But the disbelievers do not recognise the true Allah except in calamities. When the matter passes, they behave as the Qur'an describes the conduct of every disbeliever among them:

﴿He passes on as if he had never called Us for a harm that touched him﴾ (part of 10:12), and ﴿and he sets up rivals to Allah in order to mislead from His way. Say: Enjoy your disbelief briefly; indeed you are of the companions of the Fire﴾ (part of 39:8).

They forget Allah and return to sanctifying the false rivals, and by that they wrong themselves. (If only those who have wronged could see, when they see the punishment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment.) These polytheists are surprised by a strange matter they had not reckoned with: they believed in rivals, and on the Day of Resurrection they come to see those rivals, and they are fuel for the Fire tormenting them. Had the stones of the idols they worshipped not come with them, they would have said: "Surely the stones will rescue us from this punishment." Here the Truth, glorified is He, makes clear to them that the stones are not merely with you in the punishment; they are the fuel of the Fire by which you are tormented. In confirmation of His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾ (part of 21:98).

Likewise His saying, the Truth, concerning the Fire:

﴿whose fuel is people and stones﴾ (part of 2:24).

Thereby every hope of the disbelieving polytheists that their false gods will rescue them is cut off. (When they see the punishment) means they see the punishment with certainty of sight (haqq al-yaqin), and they had been told of it beforehand, but they did not believe in the Last Day; yet had they believed in the Day of Resurrection and affirmed it, seeing the punishment with the certainty of sight would have sufficed for them. The Truth, glorified is He, concludes the noble verse with His saying: (that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment). That is, at the moment they see the punishment with the certainty of sight, they will then realise that power belongs to Allah and that He is severe in punishment.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, makes clear what their state will be when they see the punishment, so He says:

﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed, and they see the punishment, and their means of connection are cut off from them. 166﴾

Everyone who adorned disbelief and disobedience for another will disown everyone who made the disobedience of God and associating partners with Him attractive to them, including Satan. The mainstay of their misguidance, he will disown them, and at that time he will say:

﴿Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke it to you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot come to your aid, nor can you come to mine.﴾ (Part of verse 22, Surah Ibrahim.)

Satan will be unable to rescue anyone among the polytheists, and they will not cry out for him so that he comes to rescue them. Even if the polytheists cry out, Satan will not come to save them. Each of them will disown the other: the disbelievers will disown everyone who made associating partners with God attractive to them, or the disbelievers will say to those who made associating partners with God attractive to them: "We are innocent of you and have no connection with you." The verse mentions those who were followed first, because they are the ones who misled others, and then mentions those who followed after that. They see the punishment and their means of connection are cut off, and every soul has become a pledge for what it earned. Satan himself acknowledges that he had no authority except that he called them; whoever responded to him was brought to this destination. Authority is either authority of proof or authority of compulsion, and Satan had no authority of compulsion over the disbelievers; he had only one action without authority, which was that he called them to associate partners with God, and they responded to him. So what happens when their means are cut off? The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Those who followed will say: If only we had a return, we would disown them as they have disowned us. Thus God will show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will not come out of the Fire. 167﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 167:

﴿Those who were followed will say, "If only we had another chance, we would disassociate ourselves from them just as they have disassociated themselves from us." Thus Allah will show them their deeds as regrets upon them. And they will never emerge from the Fire.﴾

The disavowal of those who were followed (ittaba'u) from those who followed them (ittaba'u) will not benefit them, and their wish that there were a return (kara, i.e. a return to the world) so that they might disavow those who led them astray will not avail them. Allah will show them their past deeds as regrets upon them. Regret (hasrah) does not occur except when a person is afflicted with a calamity from which there is no escape. "And they will never emerge from the Fire": that is, their remorse for the evil deeds they committed previously will not benefit them, and this remorse will not avail in bringing them out of the Fire.

Then Allah, Exalted is He, says:

﴿O mankind, eat of what is on the earth [that is] lawful and good, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ [2:168]

Among the mercies of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon His servants is that He did not confine the address to those who believe. Rather, He widened the circle to include believers and others, and said: "O mankind." It is as if He created everything on earth for all of mankind. This is what we have said about it: it is the bounty of lordship (ʿaṭāʾ al-rubūbiyyah) given to all humanity, whether they believe or do not believe. He, glorified is He, created all creation, its believers and its disbelievers, and since He created them and brought them into existence, He directs the address to all of them, believers and disbelievers alike. It is as if the address says to the disbelievers: even if you do not believe in Allah, take from the believers the lawful things and use them, for they benefit you in your worldly life, even if you do not believe in Allah, because it is in your interest to eat what is lawful and good. Allah has not forbidden except what is harmful, and has not permitted except what is good.

Here is a position taken by many who have transgressed against themselves, who wish that the matter of religion, the matter of prohibition and the matter of permission, were false matters. For nothing saves them before themselves except that they find things by which they can deny religion, because they have not been able to bring themselves to what Allah requires. When they are unable to do that, they find no outlet for themselves except to say: the matters of religion are false, including what is permitted and what is forbidden. They say: since Allah has forbidden something, why did He create it in the universe?

It is as if they believe that every creature on earth was created to be eaten, and they do not know that every creature on earth has a purpose. Now they catch snakes and vipers in order to extract their venoms, so that they may kill with them the microbes that kill humans. Before they discovered the benefit of snake venom, they used to ask: "And what is the benefit of creating such snakes?" When Allah compelled them and drove them to benefit from the venom in snakes, to make it a remedy, they realized the wisdom of Allah in creating these kinds. He created them not for us to eat, but for us to be healed by them.

So when you see something forbidden, do not say: why did Allah create it? For you do not know what its purpose is. The purpose of every creature is not that man should eat it; rather, every creature has a purpose which you may not perceive it performing in the universe. This is a matter we use ourselves, for example: when summer comes and we fear for our woolen clothes from insects, we bring something that kills insects, namely naphthalene (al-naftalīn), and we warn our children not to approach it or eat it. Naphthalene is not to be eaten, but it is beneficial in killing harmful insects. Likewise, Phenyk (al-fīnīk): we buy it and put it in a bottle in the house to disinfect any polluted place, and we warn children against it because it is harmful to them, but it is beneficial in cleansing the house of insects. Likewise the creatures whose wisdom in creation we do not know: Allah created them for a specific purpose proper to them, so do not transfer anything of its purpose to another purpose.

If man has not yet understood the benefit of some creatures, then how much more he is ignorant, and he discovers every day a secret of the secrets of Allah's creatures.

For example, they used to look at a kind of fish whose size does not exceed the length of a finger joint, and which never grows, and they were perplexed about its benefit. When we went to Saudi Arabia and saw the places from which we take water, which may spoil, and we found this kind of fish in abundance, we asked them about the reality of this fish. They said: it does not grow and remains at this size, and its task is to purify water in places where man does not purify it. We tested what they said: we threw some food leftovers, and we found these fish coming out from nowhere we knew, seizing these remnants, and not leaving them until they finished them.

Thus the Living, the Self-Subsisting creates creatures to preserve other creatures. He, glorified is He, says to man: do not eat this and eat that, for a wisdom that we may not know.

Another example: the bird known as Abu Qirdan, the friend of the farmer. Its function in life was to eat insects and worms when the land is irrigated. Since this bird disappeared under the influence of pesticides, the danger of worms to crops grew severe, especially the cotton worm. It is a divine equation composed with precise composition. Likewise the fly: some people ask, "What is the wisdom of its existence in life?" They do not know that the fly performs an important role for man, which is eating filth and the diseases in it; and if people protected themselves with cleanliness, the fly would not come to them.

So, everything in existence is arranged with precise order; it is the arrangement of a Creator, All-Knowing, All-Wise. Since the Wise is the One who created, no one should object and say: why did He create such and such? For every creature has a role it performs in the universe.

Therefore the Creator warns people, believers and disbelievers alike, to eat the lawful and good from the earth. He says to the disbeliever: if you reflect upon matters, you will find that everything I have commanded you is for your benefit; and even if you do not believe, I am guiding you to what benefits you. So do not eat except what is lawful and good, and look at what He permitted the believers as food, and eat the like of it.

Reality and history have shown that disbelievers resort to the method of Allah in some matters of judgment in order to solve the problems of their lives; not as a religion of Allah, but as the commands of Allah as a system. So if disbelievers in Allah had wisdom even regarding the affairs of their worldly life, they would take what Allah commanded the believers and follow it.

An example of this: when the Truthful, Exalted is He, forbids the flesh of carrion, that is, what died without being slaughtered, its flesh is harmful to health, because the blood vessels in an animal and in every living creature are of two kinds: either veins or arteries, and the blood, before it goes to the kidneys or the lungs, is corrupt blood. When we slaughter the animal, the corrupt and non-corrupt blood flows out and exits, and the meat becomes pure; but an animal that was not slaughtered was not purified (lam yudhakka), meaning it was not cleansed from the corruption of the blood, and it is harmful to man.

When the Truthful, Exalted is He, says "O mankind," it is as if He is calling the believers: if you reflected, you would have to be careful in your life not to eat except what Allah has permitted to the believers. "And do not follow the footsteps of Satan." That is, do not walk behind Satan. The footstep (khuṭwah) is the distance between the two feet when walking, that is, between one step and the next. Do not make Satan your leader, for Satan's enmity toward you is established beforehand, and you must be wary and suspicious of him; for he disobeyed his Lord, and it is not right to obey him in any matter. "Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy." And Satan's enmity toward man is ancient, dating back to the days of Adam.

Almighty Allah says concerning the commands of Satan:

﴿Indeed, he only orders you to evil and immorality and to say about Allah that which you do not know.﴾ [2:169]

As-su' (evil) is every sin for which there is no prescribed penalty (hadd), such as backbiting (ghiba) or tale-bearing (namima). Al-fahsha' (immorality) is every sin for which there is a prescribed penalty and a punishment. Satan commands you to say about Allah that which you do not know.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 170:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Follow what Allah has sent down," they say, "Rather, we follow what we found our fathers upon." Even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided?﴾

This verse addresses a serious issue in the Islamic community: the imitation of people in the customs of their fathers. Imitation (taqlid) is a natural disposition in a human being, for when a human comes into existence endowed with the energy of life, this energy wants to move, and its movement always follows what it sees in the movement of those who came before it. The small child does not know how to reach for things unless he sees someone in his surroundings doing so. When the child wants to move, he imitates the movements of those around him. That is why you always find children imitating their parents in most of their movements. When children are together with successive generations of different ages, the small child imitates in his primitive movements a mixture of the movements of these generations: he imitates his grandfather, imitates his grandmother, imitates his father and mother, and his siblings, so mixed movements arise that represent all the generations.

Therefore, the child's integration into a family made up of fathers and grandfathers represents in the human being the nature of life connected to the method of movement on earth and the method of heaven. For the child, when he lives with his father alone, may find him busy in the movement of life, which may have distracted him from the values of life or from the method of heaven. But when he sees the father of his father, who is his grandfather, has withdrawn from the movement of life and turned toward the method of values, because he is, as it is thought, close to meeting Allah, then if he did not pray in his youth, he now prays; and if he did not perform acts of obedience before, he now performs them. Thus the child sees the unbridled movement of worldly life and eagerness for it in his father, and finds the turning toward values and worship in his grandfather. That is why you find him perhaps helping his grandfather in obedience: when the child hears the muezzin say "Allah is greatest," he knows that his grandfather wants to pray, so he goes and brings the prayer rug and spreads it out for his grandfather, and stands imitating his grandfather. If it is a girl, we find her imitating her mother or grandmother and putting a covering on her head to pray. So, the integration of generations gives the good of both movements: the movement of the material life and the movement of the values of the method of heaven. That is why the Truth reminds us with favour, saying: ﴿And made for you from your spouses sons and grandchildren﴾ (part of verse 72 of Surah al-Nahl).

Thus, the imitation of later generations of earlier generations is a matter required by the nature of existence. When Allah calls people to follow what He sends down to the messengers, He forbids them to follow the imitation of fathers in all their movements, because the movement of the fathers may have become corrupted through heedlessness of the method or forgetting the method. Therefore He calls us and commands us, glory be to Him: to detach ourselves from these things and follow what Allah has sent down, and not descend to the level of the earth, because the customs and method of the earth may change, but the method of heaven never changes. So follow what Allah has sent down.

When people argue, they say: "Rather, we follow what we found our fathers upon." This is a justificatory claim in existence. Had that been true and truthful, and conforming to reality, Allah would not have repeated the messages after Adam had been taught the entire method that He wants. For if we were following what we found our fathers upon, the sons of Adam would have followed what Adam did, and the sons of the sons of Adam would have followed their fathers, and thus the method of heaven would remain existing and inherited, with no change in it. So what required that the method of heaven change?

This is evidence that people have changed the method. Therefore their saying "we follow what we found our fathers upon" is a fabricated claim, because if they had followed what their fathers were upon, the method of Allah on earth would have remained luminous, unaffected by the heedlessness of people and unaffected by the deviations of the people of the earth from the method of heaven. It is a justification that reveals that what they found their fathers upon agrees with their desires.

As for His saying, the Truth: "Follow" (ittabi'u), meaning: make what has been sent down to you from heaven something followed, and be followers of this method, not followers of anything else, because whatever is other than the method of heaven is a method fashioned by the people of the earth, and it is an untrustworthy method. As for their saying "what we found our fathers upon" (alfaynā 'alayhi ābā'anā), meaning: what we found our fathers upon, and what our eyes opened upon, so we found it a movement to be emulated and followed.

The Truth shows them that this is a mistaken statement, a justificatory statement, and that you are not truthful in it. The lack of truthfulness becomes clear in that if you were followers of the method of heaven, the method would not have changed. This is first. Second, you differ from your fathers in many things: when the sons have a personality and selfhood, we find the sons eager to differ, and we find generations that are dissolute. The father wants one thing and the son wants another. Therefore it is not right for them to say "Rather, we follow what we found our fathers upon," because if that were right, the method of Allah on earth would not have differed, but the method has differed due to the entry of human desires. Nevertheless we see some difference in the behaviour of sons from fathers, and we accept that and say: this is due to the change and difference of generations, meaning that the sons have become possessed of selfhood. Therefore the claim that sons follow fathers is a lie that does not represent reality.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, responds to this claim because it is a justificatory claim with no evidence of truth and no proof from reality. He says: "Even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided?" meaning: would they follow what their fathers were upon even if their fathers did not understand and were not guided?

So the response came from two aspects: from the aspect of understanding (ta'aqqul) and from the aspect of being guided (ihtida'). Both understanding and guidance are negated of the fathers in this verse. You follow them in blind following, without thought. A human does not obey with blind obedience except one whom he is certain has a piercing, absolute insight, and this cannot be attained from one human to another. Absolute obedience is not right to be given to anything except the method of heaven. When it is blind obedience to one whom you trust for his healing, sufficient, wise sight, it is obedience with sight and insight at the same time, because you protect yourself from the error of your sight and the error of your insight, and you commit to following one whom you believe his sight and insight never err. Then it is not blind obedience.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, alerts them that it is not right for you to say that you follow what you found your fathers upon, because your fathers might not understand and might not be guided. If your fathers had understanding or guidance, then following them would be a sound matter, not because you followed your fathers, but because you followed what is reasonable and guidance.

Thus we find that the matter of imitation is an alleged matter, because you never imitate your equals, but you follow the one you believe to be wiser than you, and as long as he is equal to you, it is not right to imitate him in every movement. Rather, the movement must be presented to your mind. Therefore Allah's obligation on His servants arose only after the intellect was complete with maturity (bulugh). He, glory be to Him, does not take the intellect unawares before it matures; rather, Allah does not obligate a servant except when his intellect matures; and He does not obligate him if he has no intellect, and does not obligate him if his strength is not behind his intellect. If a human is sound in strength and intellect, his obligation is complete. He, glory be to Him, obligates only the one with a mature intellect who has the capacity to carry out what his intellect has been guided to, that is, not under compulsion.

So the one who obligates a human according to these matters is one who knows that if the intellect is found mature without compulsion, it must be guided to the matter of truth.

Indeed, the Truth, glory be to Him, has not obligated the human except after all the faculties of his self are complete, because the last faculty to form in a human is the faculty of instinct, that is, that he be fit for procreation and fit for life to extend through him. We said before: the fruit we eat does not become a delicious, ripe fruit until it has performed its first task; its task is not only that a human eat it. Rather, that a viable seed be produced from it for the extension of life. When the seed exists, eating the fruit is then fitting. Likewise the human: he is not fit for the extension of life except after puberty or at the age of puberty.
