Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 187:

The Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿It is made lawful for you on the night of the fast to go in unto your wives. They are a garment for you, and you are a garment for them. God knows that you used to betray yourselves, so He turned to you and pardoned you. So now, have intercourse with them and seek what God has prescribed for you. Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn. Then complete the fast until nightfall. And do not have intercourse with them while you are devoting yourselves to worship in the mosques. These are the limits of God, so do not approach them. Thus God makes His signs clear to the people, that they may become righteous.﴾ 187

After the Truth had set forth the etiquette of supplication, blending it and introducing it into the fast, He, glory be to Him, explains to us the etiquette of dealing between the spouses during the fast. This interweaving and blending of different subjects in the Qur'an comes so that we understand from it that religion is a single, interlocking unity that addresses all human faculties, and He, glory be to Him, never wants one faculty to appear or to dominate over another.

The Truth says: (It is made lawful for you on the night of the fast to go in unto your wives). When you hear (It is made lawful for you), it is as if what is now made lawful had been forbidden before. What God made lawful in this statement was the very thing that was forbidden during the fast, because the fast is abstention during the day from the desire of the belly and the desire of the private parts. So it is as if, before this verse was revealed, going in unto wives during the night of the fast was forbidden; the fast at its beginning was abstention from food from before dawn until the moment of sunset, and there was no closeness between the spouses either at night or by day. Thus intercourse on the night of the fast was forbidden. And eating and drinking were forbidden to them after the night prayer ('Isha') and after sleep, until they broke the fast.

A man came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "I went home and did not find my family had prepared food for me, so I slept. Then I awoke, O Messenger of God, and I knew I could not eat, and so I am suffering from fatigue." So God made two matters lawful: the first matter is going in unto wives at night, and the second matter is the words of the Truth: (Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread of dawn). That is, eat and drink until dawn, even if sleep has overtaken you. This is a new concession for all Muslims, like the first concession that was granted to the traveller or the sick person. The first concession concerned the hardship of the fast for the traveller or the sick person; the new concession is general for every Muslim, and it is a deepening of the meaning of the ruling.

The Truth has deferred this permission somewhat so that every Muslim may perceive the extent of the relief, because he had already fallen into the slip of transgression, and God lifted it from him. Look at the Qur'anic verse as it says: (They are a garment for you, and you are a garment for them. God knows that you used to betray yourselves).

The phrase (you used to betray yourselves) teaches us that a person was not strong enough to fast the whole time from desire of the private parts. When He left you betraying yourselves and then sent down the concession for you, here you feel God's favour upon you.

So some of the concessions by which God grants His servants relief in the obligations are: a concession that comes together with the legislation, and a concession of relief that comes after the legislation has arrived, to alert that, had He not done so, you would have been exposed to betrayal and hardship (God knows that you used to betray yourselves). And observe the boldness of 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, who went to the Prophet and said: "I, O Messenger of God, went as a young man goes," and the one who was hungry also said to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "He is hungry." The legislation came to suit every situation: we abstain by day from the two desires of belly and private parts, and by night God has made lawful for us the two desires of belly and private parts. This relief came only after the betrayal had occurred, to show us God's mercy in that He estimated the condition of the human being.

(It is made lawful for you on the night of the fast to go in unto your wives), and (go in unto) (al-rafath) is enjoyment of the woman, whether it be foreplay or intercourse. (They are a garment for you, and you are a garment for them).

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wants to give us the process of the joining of man and woman through the word of God. (Libas, garment) is what is put on the body for covering, so it is as if the woman is a garment for the man and the man is a garment for the woman, and the first meaning of a garment is covering the nakedness. So the man is a garment for the woman, that is, he covers her nakedness, and she covers his, so it is a reciprocal process; this happens in reality, for they wrap themselves in one garment. That is why He says: (have intercourse with them), that is, bring skin to skin.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to teach us that the woman is a covering garment for the man, and the man is a covering garment for the woman, and the Truth, glory be to Him, wants this garment to remain a covering, such that nothing of either spouse is exposed to others. That is why the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, warns us that something should not happen between a man and his family at night and then the woman speaks of it by day, or the man speaks of it; this matter is governed by the principle of mutual concealment. (They are a garment for you, and you are a garment for them). And since they are a garment for you and you are a garment for them, it is part of the mercy of legislation toward the human being that the man and the woman are joined in one garment, and afterwards we ask them to refrain from contact.

So the words (you used to betray yourselves) were a natural and inevitable matter, and that is why the Truth said after it: (so He turned to you). The meaning of (He turned to you) is a report from God that He has relented, and when God reports that He has relented, that is, He has legislated repentance for them. Repentance, as we know, comes in three stages: God first legislates repentance, then you repent second, then God accepts the repentance third. (And pardoned you), since He has made this process for the wisdom of displaying the sublimity of the legislation in relief, the intention is that it should occur here, and that the pardon should come from Him, glory be to Him.

The Truth says: (So now, have intercourse with them and seek what God has prescribed for you). He did not wish to leave intercourse to its own course, so He said: in intercourse you must remember what God has prescribed, and what God has prescribed is chastity (i'faf) through this union and procreation. The woman intends the chastity of the man so that his eye does not stretch toward another woman, and he also intends by this process to keep her chaste so that she does not look to another. God wants chastity in this matter so that the child may grow up in this union upon firm ground of purity and cleanness.

And so that a man does not doubt the offspring of his own loins as to whether they are his children, and the Truth, glory be to Him, wants the purity of the human being, every offspring must be reckoned to the one who enjoyed, and after the enjoyment he must bear the consequence; it is not proper for a Muslim to enjoy and let another bear the consequence of that, for the Muslim gives every matter its due. (So now, have intercourse with them and seek what God has prescribed for you), that is, what God has prescribed, that marriage is for chastity and procreation. In that is purity for every member of society. That is why the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

("And in the intercourse of one of you there is a charity." They said: "O Messenger of God, does one of us satisfy his desire and have a reward for it?" He said: "Do you see, if he had placed it in what is unlawful, would there have been a burden of sin upon him? So likewise, if he places it in what is lawful, he has a reward.")(1).

The Truth continues: (Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread), that is, until the true dawn becomes clear to you. At the time of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, there were two calls to the dawn prayer: Bilal would call at night, while the night still remained, and Ibn Umm Maktum would call at the very first moment of dawn. That is why the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ("If you hear the call of Ibn Umm Maktum, then refrain.") But one of the Companions, 'Adi ibn Hatim, said: "I placed beside my pillow a white thread and a black thread, and I kept eating until I could distinguish the white thread from the black thread." So he [the Prophet] said to him: "You have a broad nape" (that is, little discernment). So the meaning here is the whiteness of day and the blackness of night.

The Truth continues: (Then complete the fast until nightfall, and do not have intercourse with them while you are devoting yourselves to worship in the mosques). They had understood that intercourse at night, as God had legislated, does not invalidate the fast. But it was necessary to establish rules of conduct within the mosque, or etiquette for the sunnah of i'tikaf (retreat in the mosque) which the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, established in the last ten nights of Ramadan. For this reason the Truth made clear that the permissibility of intercourse between a man and his wife is for one who is not in i'tikaf and outside the nights of Ramadan. As for one who is in retreat in the mosque, that matter is not lawful for him. The meaning of i'tikaf is that you confine your movement during a period of time to your presence in a certain place; that is why they say: "So-and-so is in retreat these days," meaning he has confined his movement during a period of time to a certain place. This does not mean that i'tikaf is restricted to the last ten nights of Ramadan only; rather, a Muslim may observe i'tikaf in God's house at any time.

The scholars differed concerning i'tikaf. Some of them stipulated that the person must be fasting when he enters i'tikaf, and they also stipulated that the i'tikaf be for a specified period, and that it be in the mosque, and they said: if you want to observe i'tikaf, then confine your movement to a place which is God's house.

Many scholars say: when you enter the mosque you receive the reward of i'tikaf so long as you have intended the sunnah of i'tikaf, on condition that you do not speak of any matter of worldly affairs, because you have come from your unrestricted movement on earth to God's house at that moment, so make your moments for God. That is why, when the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, saw a man searching in the mosque for something lost from him, he said to him: ("May God not return it to you, for the mosques were not built for this.")(2).

Why? Because the mosque is a place of worship. That is why I say to anyone who speaks to me in the mosque about anything related to the movement of life: ("Be glad that it will not benefit you"), because you entered the mosque only for worship. The moment you enter the mosque is a moment in which you came to draw near to your Lord and commune with Him, and to live in the embrace of His care, so why do you bring the world with you? Let us have in one of the Companions a fine example; he used to say: "We used to take off the matters of the world along with our sandals." Another Companion added and said to him: "Add, my brother, that we leave our ranks with our sandals."

Look at the precision: the Companion who follows the Prophet does not take off the world with his sandal only at the door of the mosque, but he also takes off his rank in the world. The many hours of the day may occupy you, while the mosque will take from you only a little time, so put your rank with your sandal outside the mosque, and enter without any rank except the rank of your faith in God. Sit in the place you find empty, and do not step over people's necks to reach a particular spot in the mosque. You enter in servitude to God, and your seat may come beside one who serves you, and the young sit beside the elder, and you claim no rank for yourself except your rank with God.

The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to sit wherever the gathering ended for him, that is, when he found a place for himself. This is contrary to our time, when a person reserves a place for another person with a prayer mat, and a person may enter to step over necks and sit in the front row, not knowing that God had already arranged the rows before he came to the mosque. And since we are going to leave our ranks, do not say: "Where shall I sit, and beside whom?" Rather, sit where the gathering ends for you, and do not step over necks. Intend i'tikaf, and do not speak of any matter of worldly affairs, lest you fall under the supplication of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that God not bless you in the lost thing you are seeking and searching for. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to observe i'tikaf in the mosque during the last ten nights of Ramadan. Does that mean i'tikaf is valid only in mosques? No; i'tikaf is valid in any place, but i'tikaf in the mosque is the complete i'tikaf, because in it you take both time and place together.

(And do not have intercourse with them while you are devoting yourselves to worship in the mosques; these are the limits of God, so do not approach them). The meaning of (limit, hadd) is the barrier preventing one thing from mixing with another, and the limits of God are His prohibitions. The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, says:

("...Whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into the unlawful, like a shepherd who grazes around a sanctuary, about to pasture within it. Surely every king has a sanctuary, and surely God's sanctuary on earth is His prohibitions.")(3).

So the prohibitions are those for which God has set a limit, so that we do not transgress it. And we may observe that when God forbids something He says: (so do not approach them), and when He commands something He says, glory be to Him: (so do not transgress them). In that is a mercy from God toward you, O accountable one.

1 Related by Muslim and Abu Dawud, and Ahmad.
2 Related by Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.
3 This hadith was narrated by Imam al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, and it is here part of the hadith.

Thus we find that consuming wealth in circulation is a common matter among people. God wants to regulate it with a system, so He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or send it to the rulers in order that you may consume a portion of the wealth of the people in sin, while you know.﴾ (188)

"As long as my wealth is mine, why should I not consume it?" The command here is for everyone, and wealth is attributed to everyone. Wealth, at the moment it is someone's property, is at the same time wealth from which others benefit.

So it is a common matter for all. But what governs the movement of its circulation? What governs it is the established truth that does not change, and falsehood does not govern it. What is meant by falsehood (al-batil) and truth (al-haqq)? Falsehood is that which passes away, which does not endure, which goes. Truth is that which is established and does not change. So do not consume by falsehood, meaning do not consume what another owns except by a right that God has established by a ruling. So do not steal, do not usurp, do not snatch, do not take bribes, and do not be treacherous regarding the trust you have been entrusted with. If any of that happens, you will have consumed wealth by falsehood.

When you consume by falsehood, you yourself will not be able to exempt others from what you have permitted yourself, and others will also consume by falsehood. As long as you consume by falsehood and others consume by falsehood, people become, all of them, plunder for all of them. But when a person is governed by the case of truth, you take only by truth, and others must give you only by truth. Thereby the whole movement of life is subjected to a law that regulates the established truth that does not change. Why? Because falsehood may have height, but it does not have stability. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿He sends down from the sky water, and valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a rising foam. And from that which they heat in the fire seeking ornament or utensils is foam like it. Thus Allah presents the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but that which benefits people remains on the earth. Thus Allah presents parables.﴾ (17) (Surah al-Ra'd)

When you see rain falling into a watercourse and a valley, you find that this rain has swept away all the straw and filth and carried it off, so it floats on the water with a froth. Likewise, when you put iron in the fire, you find it melts and its dross comes out, and the dross floats on the surface. Thus we find that a thing floating and rising above the surface does not mean that it is true. He, glory be to Him, gives us from perceptible matters what enables us to distinguish through them non-physical matters. Thus you see that falsehood may float and rise, but it does not endure; rather it ends. The colloquial saying goes: "It boils up and sinks down" (yafur wa yaghur).

God wants our movement in life to be clean and noble, a dignified movement. Nothing enters your belly except what you have toiled for, and every person takes his right. Before a person thinks of eating, he must move in order to eat, not wait for the fruit of others' movement. Why? Because this laziness spreads chaos in life. When we see a person who does not work and lives in comfort, eating from the labour of others, this person becomes an example that others follow. He persuades all people to be still rather than move, and they live as dependents on others. This results in the stopping of the movement of life, and this is falsehood that passes away, through which the fruits of the mover's movement end, and here everyone goes hungry.

The truth wants a person to move in order to satisfy his need for food, drink and shelter, and thereby the cycle of life continues. He, glory be to Him, wants to guarantee for us the nobility of movement in life, meaning that you have movement in everything from which you benefit, because your movement will not be limited in its benefit to you alone, but it is a chain of mutually propelling movements. When you spread the nobility of movement, everyone will move toward this nobility. But falsehood produces the opposite: when you consume from the movement of others, you spread chaos in the universe.

Accordingly, lawful movement is not sufficient simply by moving. Rather, you must look to the nobility of movement, that it not be in falsehood, because the one who steals moves in his theft, but his movement is ignoble, and it is unlawful movement. So every stolen thing in existence is the result of a false movement. Likewise usurpation, deception, cheating, dishonesty in work, betrayal of a deposit, and denial of a trust: all of that is falsehood, and every movement outside what God has legislated is falsehood, even helping in a movement outside what God has legislated. All of that is falsehood.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: (And do not consume your wealth among yourselves by falsehood), meaning beware of consuming it by falsehood and then sending it to the rulers so that they justify for you that this falsehood is right for you. There are many people who see in the ruler's action a justification for doing the same thing, and this is a mistaken matter, because every person is responsible for his own movement.

Do not say that the ruler has legislated actions and so lay upon him the responsibility for your deeds. An example of this are those things we call fine arts: dancing, singing and debauchery. Does the governments' permission of them, and their not forbidding them, make them lawful? No, because there is a difference between a civil religion and a divine religion. For this reason you find that corruption arises in life from such conduct.

Those who work at a job that God does not approve are eating their wealth by falsehood, and they put unlawful wealth into the bellies of their innocent children. Those who eat from such things must take careful notice that the one who supports them has brought upon them things of this unlawfulness and falsehood. They must remember their Lord and say: "No, we will not eat from this source, because it is an unlawful and false source, and God has created us, and He, glory be to Him, is responsible for our provision."

I hear many people say: these false works have become matters of life; life has been built upon them, and we can no longer do without them. I say to them: No, you must rebuild your lives anew on lawful work. If one insists on doing unlawful work in order to support those under him, then the one who supports them must take a stance against him that turns him back, and insist on not eating from falsehood.

Imagine what happens when a son refuses to eat from the work of his mother, who dances or sings for example, or the work of his father if he knows that he works by falsehood. The matter will be harsh upon the father or the mother themselves.

Those who say: "This is our provision, and we have no provision other than it," I say to them: God, glory be to Him and exalted, provides whom He wills without reckoning, and no person should suppose that his work is what will provide for him. Rather, God provides for him by means of this work. So if he moves from false work to another lawful work, God will not withhold from him truthful work and lawful provision to sustain himself by.

God, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, addressed this matter when He wanted to make the House of God in Mecca forbidden to the polytheists. There were people who lived on what the polytheists brought in the season of the pilgrimage, and the people of Mecca would sell everything in this economic season to the polytheists who came to the House. When God prohibited the polytheist from entering the Sacred House, what would be the stance of these people?

The first thing that comes to mind is the thought: "How will they live?" Let us reflect on the matter that God wants to fix in the soul of every believer. The Truth says:

﴿Indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this, their year.﴾ (Part of 28, Surah al-Tawbah)

Then He comes to the matter that preoccupies people and says:

﴿And if you fear privation, Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills.﴾ (Part of 28, Surah al-Tawbah)

Thus we see that this matter was not hidden from God. So let no one say that unlawful, false work is the source of my provision, and that I cannot live if I abandon it, whether it be composing or playing music, or composing debauched songs, or dancing, or sculpting statues. We say to him: No, do not make this the source of your provision, for God says to you: ﴿And if you fear privation, Allah will enrich you from His bounty.﴾ And when you fear God, He, glory be to Him, makes a way out for you. (﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect.﴾) You must abandon every work in which there is disobedience to God, and look to the hand of God extended to you with His goodness.

So God's saying: (And do not consume your wealth among yourselves by falsehood) is a warning to people not to put into their bellies and the bellies of those they support anything but wealth from what is right and wealth gained by a noble, clean movement. Let the believer's support always be the saying of the Truth:

﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out. And will provide for him from where he does not expect.﴾ (Surah al-Talaq)

We should know that whoever eats by falsehood hungers in truth, meaning that God tests him with an illness that makes him unable to eat the lawful and good. So you find a person who owns wealth and can eat from everything in the universe of food and drink, but the doctors forbid him to eat from many foods, because eating them is harmful and a danger to his health. The blessing is before him and in his hands, but he cannot eat from it rightfully. At the same time his children, servants and entourage, and everyone they support, enjoy the blessing. We say to such a person: you must have taken something by falsehood, so God has deprived you of what is right. From here we say: "Whoever eats by falsehood hungers in truth." And we also say: "Whoever exploits a means for falsehood, God shows him its ugliness in truth." The one who oppresses people with his strength and his bulging muscles will inevitably have a day come upon him when he becomes weak.

And the woman who sways her waist gracefully will inevitably have a day come upon her when her waist dries up and she is no longer able to move. And the one who dazzles people with the beauty of her eyes right and left will inevitably have a day when she goes blind and sees no one, and people shrink from her ugliness.

Whoever eats by falsehood will hunger in truth, and whoever exploits a means by falsehood, God will show him its ugliness in truth. Write a list in front of you of those you know, and review the life of everyone who has exploited something God created to spread some deviance or made it a means to falsehood, which God will inevitably show him to be falsehood.

I want people to make a list of all those who deviate from God's method and reflect on the course of their lives. Each of us knows his neighbours and colleagues: where do they eat from, and where do they earn? Let him reflect on their lives, know the works of the lawful and the unlawful, and make their lives a lesson for himself and his children: How were they? And what did they become? Then let him look at how the ends of these people came out. Out of our love for these people, we say to them: Take care of your own affairs. You will not deceive God by gathering unlawful wealth and then giving charity from it. God will not accept this deed from you, because God is good and accepts only the good.

We hear of many deviants in life who go on pilgrimage, build mosques and give charity, all with wealth whose source is unlawful. To these we say: God is free of need from your worship and from your unlawful charity. We advise them that God does not expect from you the building of houses for Him from the unlawful, or charity to His servants from wealth acquired by other than what is lawful. Rather, He, glory be to Him, wants from you steadfastness upon the method.

When we reflect on the verse, we find in it a wonder. God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: (And do not consume your wealth among yourselves by falsehood and send it to the rulers). The Truth mentioned the rulers in the verse, because the ruler is the one who legislates and gives legitimacy to wealth, even if it is false. His saying, glory be to Him: (send it, *tudlu*) is derived from (*adla*), and we lower the bucket (*dalw*) to raise water from the well. (*Dalla*) means to bring out the bucket, while (*adla*) means "to lower the bucket." This is why in the story of the devil who misleads man, the Truth said:

﴿So he made them fall by deception. And when they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them.﴾ (Part of 22, Surah al-A'raf)

(And send it, *tudlu*, to the rulers) means that you bribe the rulers so that you may consume a portion of the wealth of the people by falsehood. Strangely, this very text is the text of bribery. Bribery (*al-rishwa*) is derived from (*al-rishaa'*), and *al-rishaa'* is the rope to which the bucket is tied, so one says *adla* and *dalla* in bribery. Why do they lower it to the rulers? They do so so that the rulers will give them the legislative authority to consume people's wealth by falsehood, and that is when we are governed by the laws of men. But when we are governed by the laws of God, then

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 189:

The word al-ahilla (the new moons) is the plural of hilal (the crescent), and it was called hilal because a person, at the moment he sees it, raises his voice in tahlil (the exclamation of glorification). Almighty and Exalted God answers with a reply that contains all the details about the moon, the celestial body which submitted to the activities of the intellect until it discovered it. The ancient Arabs did not know anything about that moon, but they used it for dating, and their knowledge of it did not exceed the limits of its benefit to them. They had not attained the intellectual refinement by which they contemplate the signs of God in the universe. All the signs of the universe are first benefited from, and then the intellect becomes active afterwards, so it knows the cause; and perhaps the intellect does not become active, and the benefit remains the benefit.

God, Glorified is He, wanted to draw our attention to an important principle, which is that He teaches us how to benefit from cosmic signs such as the moon. It is not enough that it appears and disappears and changes its size, because the intellect will not be able to encompass these things. Rather, we benefit from it as a timetable (miqat) and use it to measure time. If we, living in the twentieth century, do not know the causes of the moon's phenomena, scientists have not known them, then how was the state of those who asked about them fourteen centuries ago?

Contemporary scholars have said in their interpretations, for example, that the sun is one million and a quarter times the size of the earth, and the moon is smaller than the earth; and when the earth comes between the sun and the moon, despite the sun's immense size, the earth blocks part of the moon. This blocked part is in proportion to the arc of the earth's shadow that is cast, and this part of the moon becomes dark.

The moon's existence is constant, but when the earth comes between it and the sun, it is the earth that blocks the sunlight from reaching it, and the size of its light increases as the earth moves away from it. When the earth moves completely away from it, it appears in the sky as a full moon. Then the earth returns to block part of the sun from it, and this increases day after day, so the light of the sun reflected onto it decreases accordingly, gradually diminishing until the earth comes between it and the sun, and nothing of it appears. We say: when we do not see the moon neither at night nor during the day, despite its existence in its place, we say it is hidden in the earth's shadow, therefore we do not see it. This phenomenon does not happen to the sun because the sun's body is very large. When it does happen, the effect is small, and it is called an eclipse (kusuf).

When the Arabs turned their attention to the universe, they said: What is the matter with the crescent, that it becomes thus and then grows until it becomes a full moon? Then the Truth, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: They are timetables for the people and for the Hajj﴾. They were asking about the new moons and their cycles, so God cut off the thread of their thinking and gave them the essence and the result, saying: ﴿Say: They are timetables for the people and for the Hajj﴾. This is the matter which the intellect of that time was able to know; as for what lies beyond that, wait until time reveals it, and your ignorance of it does not diminish your benefit.

Every answer to any question in that time contained what the intellect could grasp at the moment of legislation; as for the rest of the answer, the Truth leaves it to time. He gives us only what serves the legislation. For example: they used to say in the past that the earth is a sphere, and science proved that it is so, and we saw it by artificial satellites, and the matter was settled.

When the Arabs asked about the new moons, we were informed by the Truth that they are timetables. The word mawaqit is the plural of miqat, and miqat derives from waqt (time), and waqt is time. We know that every event requires time and place. Therefore time and place are linked to occurrence; there is no time or place except when an event exists.

As for the one who says: How was time before God created creation? We say to him: time came into being for the originated thing, which is creation, and God is eternal. As long as God is eternal and not originated, there is no time or place; do not say when or where, because "when" and "where" are created. And how do we know the time? We know time as a measure of duration, corresponding to a measure of motion and a measure of action. And where is place in this definition? Time sometimes controls place, so time is said to be the origin and place an accident upon it; and at another time place is the origin and time the accident upon it; and at a third time the two are mutually bound, time and place.

In Egypt, if we want to perform Hajj, we begin the ihram at Rabigh, and we call Rabigh the miqat of the people of Egypt, meaning it is the place which whoever passes by without being in ihram may not go beyond.

Thus the miqat has been applied to a place, Rabigh, and upon the arrival of the Egyptian at Rabigh with the intention of Hajj, he enters ihram immediately, whether the time is morning, noon, afternoon, or evening.

But when we begin fasting, time becomes the origin in your fast wherever you go; time determines the times of fasting in Tanta, London, or Tokyo. Thus we know how time can be a miqat.

So sometimes time controls the miqat and place is an accident upon it, sometimes place controls the miqat and time is an accident upon it, and sometimes time and place together control the act, such as the Day of Arafah.

Thus we know the meaning of ﴿timetables for the people﴾: by the crescent we know the beginning of the month of Ramadan, by it we know the Eid al-Fitr, and likewise the season of Hajj, the waiting period of the woman ('iddah), and the sacred months. All these matters we know through the timetables. God willed to make the crescent the means by which we identify these matters, and He made the sun only to guide us to the day, though it has another function in the zodiacal signs (buruj), to which the state of weather, climate and agriculture is linked. Therefore He said:

﴿He it is who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light..﴾ (Surah Yunus).

Observe the precision of the expression, and how God explains to man the reality of light and the reality of radiance. The sun is luminous in itself, whereas the moon is illuminated, because its light comes from another; it is like a shining piece of stone upon which the rays of the sun fall, giving us light. The moon shines by the light of another, and therefore the Truth says in another verse:

﴿And He made therein a lamp and a moon giving light﴾ (Surah al-Furqan).

The lamp in this verse is the sun, which has heat, and God made it with zodiacal signs; as for the moon, it has stations (manazil), and it shines by the light of another. Concerning this, the Truth says:

﴿He it is who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light, and determined for it stations, that you might know the number of years and the reckoning..﴾ (Surah Yunus).

Thus the number of years and their reckoning come from the moon. In our time, when they want to fix the time standards, they establish them by the lunar reckoning; for they have found that reckoning by the moon is more precise than reckoning by the sun, since solar reckoning goes out of step by one day every certain number of years.

To understand the difference between the stations of the moon and the zodiacal signs of the sun: the buruj are names from the Syriac language, namely: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Virgo, Leo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces, and their number is twelve; these are the signs of the sun, and the timing of sowing, weather and climate is linked to them. We must understand that God has secrets in the buruj, as is evident from the fact that Almighty and Exalted God made them an oath when He says: ﴿By the sky containing the buruj﴾.

Therefore you find that the timing by the sun does not vary; the months that come in cold and those that come in heat are the same, and likewise those that come in autumn and spring. Between the solar year and the lunar year there are eleven days, and the lunar year is what is used for the historical dating of the Arab months, and we know the beginning of each month by the crescent:

﴿Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months﴾ (part of verse 36, Surah al-Tawba).

Therefore the obligations of worship were reckoned by the moon, so that the lunar stations would roam through the solar zodiacal signs, and the obligation would come in every climate and weather of the year. Thus you do not fast Ramadan in a perpetual summer, nor in a perpetual winter; rather God alternates the times of worship over all the days of the year. People who live in cold regions, for example, if Hajj were fixed in the summer season, they would not be able to perform the obligation; but the Hajj season revolves through all the months, so when Hajj falls in winter, it facilitates for them the task of performing the obligation in a climate close to the climate of their lands.

Thus we find that God's wisdom required that the times of worship revolve over all the days of the year, so that all people, according to their climatic circumstances, may perform the acts of worship without hardship. Therefore the stations are dispersed among the zodiacal signs, and this is the reason some scholars said: the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) circulates through all the nights of the year, according to the wandering of the stations through the zodiacal signs.

So there are zodiacal signs of the sun, stations of the moon, and positions of the stars, and the positions of the stars are what God swears by in His saying:

﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars, and indeed it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'a).

Perhaps a time will come when God reveals to humanity the effect of the positions of the stars on the lives of creatures, when souls are prepared for that and minds are able to comprehend it. Thus everything in the universe has a system: the sun has zodiacal signs, the moon has stations, and the stars have positions. All the secrets, laws and order of the universe are in these creatures, and God has given us from the secrets of the new moons that they are timetables for the people and for the Hajj. When He, Glorified is He, spoke of Hajj, He wanted to give us a ruling connected with it; for there were tribes of the Arabs known as the Hums, these Hums were strict in their religion and zealous for it, and among them were Quraysh, Kinanah, Khath'am, Jusham, and Banu Sa'sa'a ibn 'Amir. When one of these would perform Hajj, he would not enter his house through the door, because he was disheveled and dusty from performing the rites of Hajj. He would try to enter his house contrary to his usual manner, so he would enter from the back of the house; this was an extremism on their part, which God did not want to legislate, lest he see something he disliked in his wife or family. When God mentioned the rites of Hajj in the Qur'an, He wanted to purify the rites from this custom familiar among the Arabs, and said:

(﴿It is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, but righteousness is [in] one who fears God. So enter houses through their doors and fear God that you may be successful﴾). That is, do not make matters formal; we want the essence of righteousness, which is the good and beneficial thing. It is noted that the word (al-birr) in this verse came in the nominative, because its position in grammatical analysis (i'rab) is the subject of (laysa, "is not"). It differs from the word (al-birr) which came earlier in His saying, ﴿It is not righteousness that you turn your faces toward the east or the west﴾, where it came in the accusative, because its position in grammatical analysis is the predicate, fronted, of (laysa). Orientalists have tried to take this difference in nominative and accusative as an objection against the Holy Qur'an. We say to them: You have little understanding and knowledge of the Arabic language, so what can we do for you? It is correct to make the predicate the subject, saying (Zayd diligent), if we know Zayd and do not know his attribute, so we make Zayd the subject and diligent the predicate. But if we know a diligent person and do not know who he is, we say (The diligent one is Zayd).

Thus sometimes the name is known to you, so you attach the attribute to it; and sometimes you do not know the name but know the attribute, so you attach the name to the attribute. This is the secret of the difference between nominative and accusative in the word (al-birr) in each of the two verses. We say to the Orientalists: every word in the Qur'an has an arrangement and a meaning, so do not approach the Qur'an with ignorance, and then raise objections that do not diminish the value of the Book but reveal your ignorance.

Then what is (al-birr)? We have said: al-birr is the good and beneficial thing. If God had left us to determine (al-birr), our ability to understand the good and the beneficial would differ according to the differences in our minds; you see this as good, and another sees something else, and a third sees the opposite of what you see. Therefore God removes from our hands the explanation of the meaning of righteousness, and specifies for us the qualities of the good and beneficial, for no one deviates and inclines toward something without believing that it is the good and beneficial; therefore the Truth says: ﴿But righteousness is [in] one who fears God. And enter houses through their doors﴾.

Al-Sha'rawi, *Tafsir al-Sha'rawi* (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), commentary on Surah al-Baqarah (2), verse 190:

It was possible for God to make His religion victorious from the very first moment without any intervention by the Muslims. But that would have meant that people would be equal in faith, the first and the last alike. Yet the will of God, glory be to Him, decreed that this religion should have men who would sacrifice their lives and their wealth for it, so that they might attain martyrdom and rise to the rank of the prophets. Therefore the command to fight came late and gradually. The command to fight came in its first stage with the saying of God, exalted is He:

﴿And fight in the way of God those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors.﴾ [2:190]

The occasion of the revelation of this verse was that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions longed for the Sacred House, and they wished to perform the 'umrah (the lesser pilgrimage). They set out in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year after the Hijrah. They wished to perform the 'umrah, but when they had gone and were in a place called al-Hudaybiyah, the Quraysh stood before them and said: "Muhammad and his Companions cannot enter Mecca." Negotiations took place between the two sides, and the Messenger of God then agreed to return that year on condition that he come the following year, and that Mecca be vacated for them for three days in the month of Dhu al-Qa'dah.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had given his Companions the good news that they would enter the Sacred Mosque, with their heads shaved and their hair cut short. This news spread, and the Muslims rejoiced and were glad. Then they were taken by surprise by the negotiations of the Messenger of God and his return, at a distance of about twenty kilometres from Mecca, and the Companions were saddened. Even 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, became angry and said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Are you not the Messenger of God? Are we not upon the truth?" Our master Abu Bakr replied to him, saying: "Hold fast to your stirrup, O 'Umar, for he is indeed the Messenger of God."

This incident also revealed a stance of Umm al-Mu'minin Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, a stance that expresses tenderness, mercy and gentle, soft counsel. When the Messenger of God entered upon her and said to her: "The Muslims are ruined, O Umm Salamah. I commanded them, but they did not comply."

Observe the role of the wife when her husband returns to her troubled. Here her function of providing tranquillity becomes manifest. Umm Salamah said: "Excuse them, O Messenger of God, for they are distressed. Their souls longed to enter the Sacred House of God with their heads shaved and their hair cut short, and then they were deprived of it while they were a few miles away from it. Go to what God has commanded you and do it, and do not speak to anyone. If they see you do it, they will know that it is a firm resolve."

The Messenger of God took the advice of Umm Salamah, did what God had commanded him, and all the Muslims followed him, and the matter ended. Before they returned to Medina, God did not wish to prolong the matter for those who had criticised the stance, lest the rift remain in the hearts of the believers. That is a difficult psychological process, so God did not prolong the cause for them, and He brought the reason, saying to them: "What grieves you about returning to Medina? You have believing brothers in Mecca who have concealed their faith and are mingled among the disbelievers. Had you entered and fought them, you would have fought both believers and disbelievers, and you would have killed your brothers. Had these believing brothers been distinguished in one part of Mecca, I would have permitted you to fight the polytheists as you wished." Read the saying of God, exalted is He:

﴿They are the ones who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque, and the offering detained from reaching its place. And were it not for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, that you might trample them and thereby incur blame without knowledge—that God might admit into His mercy whom He wills. If they had been separated, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.﴾ [48:25]

After the revelation of this verse the Muslims understood that the restraint had been for a reason and a wisdom. When they came the following year, God said to them:

﴿The sacred month for the sacred month, and violations are subject to retribution...﴾ [2:194]

The Truth was reassuring them: those who barred you in Dhu al-Qa'dah of that year, you would fight them, and you would enter in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the following year. The Muslims feared that if they came the next year, the Quraysh might break the covenant and fight them, and the word of the Truth was revealed:

﴿And fight in the way of God those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors.﴾ [2:190]

When we reflect on His saying, exalted is He, "And fight in the way of God," we find that the Truth, glory be to Him, emphasises the phrase "in the way of God," because He wants to put a limit to human tyranny. The intention in fighting must be for the sake of God, not that fighting be done with the intention of domination, arrogance and oppression. There is no fighting for the sake of life, or wealth, or to secure an economic market. Rather, fighting is for raising the word of God and supporting the religion of God. This is the purpose of fighting in Islam.

﴿And fight in the way of God those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, God does not love the transgressors.﴾ The Truth forbids aggression: that is, a Muslim must not fight one who has not fought him, nor transgress.

Suppose that the Quraysh were the ones who fought. Still, people such as women, children and the infirm did not fight the Muslims, even though they were on the side of those who fought. Therefore it is not permissible to fight them. Yes, the reaction is proportionate to the action. So what? Because fighting women and the infirm is aggression, and He, glory be to Him, does not love aggressors. But fighting the believers is only to repel aggression, and there is no initiation of aggression.

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them, and expel them from where they expelled you, and oppression (fitnah) is worse than killing. And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you therein. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾ [2:191]

We hear the word (thaqafa) and the word (thiqaf), and ṯaqāfah is the ease of learning, or that one acquaints oneself with a portion of many things; by this, so-and-so becomes (muthaqqaf), meaning he has a quantity of information and knows something of everything, and then he specializes in one branch of knowledge and knows everything about one thing.

All these meanings are derived from tangible matters. In the Arabic usage, (al-tathqif) is the straightening of a branch. The Arabs would take branches of trees to make them into spears and staves, and a branch may be crooked or have a knot, so the Arab would (thaqqafahu), that is, remove its protrusions and crookedness, then bring the (thiqaf), which is a piece of bent iron, to straighten the crooked branches with it, as the iron-worker does with construction iron.

As if the (muthaqqaf) is one who corrects something crooked in the universe; he knows this and that, and has become one with sound straightening. Thus we find that the meanings of the language and its words are derived from the tangible things before us. His saying (thaqiftumūhum), that is (wajadtumūhum), for (thaqifa al-shay') means he found it.

And the Truth says:

﴿Then if you overtake them in war, disperse those behind them﴾ (part of verse 57, Surat al-Anfal).

That is, (disperse them wherever you find them). The Truth says: (And kill them wherever you overtake them), that is, do not say, "They expelled us from here," but rather expel them from where they expelled you, that is, from whatever place you are in; by that you will not be transgressors. His exalted saying (and expel them from where they expelled you) reminds us of a similar reasoning in another verse, among it His saying:

﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished...﴾ [16:126].

And His saying:

﴿And the recompense of an evil is an evil like it...﴾ [42:40].

When we examine within these texts ("and the recompense of an evil is an evil like it"), this thought may arise: I took my right from one who wronged me, and I avenged myself on him with an act like the act he did to me; is it said that I committed an evil? To understand the matter, we say: the Truth, glory be to Him, sometimes uses the expression (al-mushakalah), which is mentioning a thing by the wording of another because it occurs in its company. Like His saying: (And they schemed, and Allah schemed), Allah does not scheme, but the wording came for mushakalah. Or the noble wording has come in the exacting of your right with the phrase "an evil like it" to alert you that exacting your right by the like of what was done to you is considered an evil if we weigh it against forgiveness and pardon of the wrongdoer. He indicates this, glory be to Him, at the end of this verse, saying: (But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah; indeed He does not love the wrongdoers). Similarly, the end of the preceding verse was: (And if you endure patiently, it is better for the patient).

The Truth says: (And oppression is worse than killing). Fitnah is derived from a tangible matter: the goldsmith takes a piece of gold and puts it in the fire, and it melts; if some foreign metal mixed with the gold, it comes out and the gold remains pure. Thus fitnah is trial and testing. The polytheists did what is worse than killing: they previously tried to subject the believers to torment in order to turn them from their religion, so the believers fled with their religion.

The Truth commands the Muslims, in fighting the people of polytheism, to observe the sanctity of the Sacred House, so that they do not violate it by fighting, except when the people of polytheism fight them.

Thus we find that the first command to fight came only to repel aggression, and the Truth, glory be to Him, wanted to remove from the hands of the enemies of Islam a card they might play against the Muslims. They know that the believers in Islam will respect the sacred months, respect the sacred place, and respect the state of ihram, and so will not fight; perhaps this encouraged the enemies of Islam to fight the Muslims only in the sacred months, thinking the Muslims might hesitate to fight them. So the Truth, glory be to Him, wanted to legislate for them what suits such a matter, and permitted them to fight: if they fight you in the sacred month, fight them in the sacred month; if they fight you in the sacred place, fight them in the sacred place; and if they fight you while you are in ihram, fight them, for sacred things are subject to retaliation (qisas).

Thus the Truth removed the card from the hands of the disbelievers. The Truth, glory be to Him, explains that although fighting in the sacred month, in the sacred place, and in the state of ihram is difficult and severe, fitnah in the religion of God is worse than killing, because fitnah only comes to corrupt people's religion for them. It is true that it does not prevent people from being religious, but it tempts those who have become religious, and they tried to force the early Muslims through torture until they apostatized from the religion, and that was worse than killing because it is fitnah in the religion. It is God who legislated the sacred month; how can the believers be tempted away from the religion of God and forced to associate others with Him, and then you say afterward, "We are in the sacred month"? The sacred month was only sacred because God made it sacred; so fitnah against God is shirk, and it is worse than fighting in the sacred month. Therefore there is no need for anyone to feel scruple about fighting in the sacred month when he is tempted in his religion. Then we know that fighting came only as defense.

After this, does fighting remain defense, as the enemies of Islam wish to make it defense only for those who believed? Or as those who try to defend Islam wish, saying: No, Islam came with defensive fighting only. We say to these: defense of whom? Is it defense of those who believed only? Or of any human being whom we want to protect from what affects the choice of his religion?

It is also defense, and we shall call it defense, but it is defense of those who believed, whom we protect from whoever attacks them; and also of those who did not believe, whom we protect from whoever influences them in choosing their religion, so that we protect their choice, not so that we force them into the religion, but so that we make them free in choosing. The forces that impose a religion on people we remove from the way, and we proclaim the call of Islam; whoever stands against this call, we fight, because he corrupts people's choice of their religion. In this too there is defense.

(And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you therein): because you are more deserving and more fitting to respect God's sanctification of al-Masjid al-Haram. But if they dare to fight in al-Masjid al-Haram, God has permitted you, O Muslims, to fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram as long as they have fought you there. (But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers. But if they desist, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.) How exalted is this religion.

We do not hold them accountable, after they have ended up in faith, for what their hands had committed in daring against the people of faith, as long as they have believed. Therefore we see 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when he passed by the slayer of his brother Zayd ibn al-Khattab, and a man pointed and said: "This is the slayer of Zayd." 'Umar said: "What shall I do with him, when he has embraced Islam? Islam has protected his blood."

The matter ended with his Islam; faith in Allah is dearer to the believer than his blood and his self, and when he believes, the enmity has ended. And this Wahshi, slayer of Hamzah, came before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and all that the Messenger of Allah did was turn his face away from him; yet he neither killed him nor took revenge on him. And Hind, wife of Abu Sufyan, who ate the liver of Hamzah, embraced Islam, and her deed ended with her Islam. Thus Islam is not a religion of rancor, nor vengeance, nor settling of scores; if blood boils in confrontation with disbelief, the belief of the disbeliever in Islam grants him safety. This is the religion.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 2, verse 192:

﴿And if they cease, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Meaning: as long as they have stopped what they were doing of sedition (fitnah) through opposing the call and associating partners with Allah, and have been restrained by the religion that commands them, so that they have refrained from disbelief, then after that we have no claim against them, because Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. It is not right that resentment over what they did to us in the past should spread in our souls; rather we should seek the reward for that from Allah. And as long as they have believed, that is enough for us.

Almighty Allah, after giving us the stages of fighting and its motives, said:

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah (trial, tribulation) and religion is for Allah. But if they cease, then there is to be no aggression except against the wrongdoers.﴾ [2:193]

We have understood that fitnah (trial, tribulation) is a testing and an examination, and Allah says:

﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?﴾ [29:2]

Allah tests faith through fitnah, and sees whether those who proclaim their faith will be patient with the trials it contains or not. Had entering Islam not entailed entering into war or fighting, nor the martyrdom of some believers, the matter would have been an enticement for many people to enter Islam. But Allah has made for them a fitnah in that they may be defeated and some of them may be killed as martyrs. This is so that only the elite who bear the honour of the call and take charge of protecting the earth from corruption enter the religion; thus the believers must be the essence of mankind.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: (And fight them until there is no more fitnah). The meaning of "and religion is for Allah" is that you bring them out of the religion of their own selves, or out of the religions that tyranny has imposed upon them. When we take them from the religions of tyranny, and from the religions that people have made attractive, to the religion of the Creator, this is a good matter for them, and that is a lofty mission. It is as if you, through this lofty mission, want to guide and direct the human mind and prevent it from submitting to an equal of its own, so that it submits to the One who created it. The possessor of such a mind must thank the one who directs him to this right course. For this reason, Allah, the Exalted, makes this truth manifest, saying on the tongue of the Messenger:

﴿Say: "I do not ask you for any reward for it, except that whoever wills may take a way to his Lord."﴾ [25:57]

So if we looked at the Messenger's work from the viewpoint of economics, it would be due that he receive a wage, since he provides us with benefit. Yet despite the benefit he has given, he takes no wage, because he is detached from wages; he knows that a wage from an equal is small however great it be, and he desires his wage from the One who created him. This is aspiration toward the Highest, for none gives a reward for faith except Allah, glory be to Him, who gives without limit.

The Truth concludes this noble verse with His saying: (But if they cease, then there is to be no aggression except against the wrongdoers). That is, if they cease killing you, you will not commit aggression against them; rather, you will repel the aggression of the wrongdoers among them.

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 2, verse 194:

The wrongdoer, when he transgresses, thinks that no one will be able to overpower him. The Truth (al-Haqq) asks us to say to him: "Rather, we will overpower you, and we will transgress against you in the same way you transgressed against us," and He gives us a justification, so He says:

﴿The sacred month for the sacred month, and violations of sanctity are subject to retaliation. So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same way as he transgressed against you. And fear Allah, and know that Allah is with the righteous.﴾

The meaning is that if they fight you in the sacred month, then you fight them in the sacred month. If they violate the sanctity of a time, retaliation occurs in a similar time; if they transgress against the sanctity of a place, retaliation is by the sanctity of a similar place; and if the transgression is against the sanctity of the state of ihram (ihram, the sacred state of pilgrimage), the response is by a similar sanctity of ihram, because retaliation (qisas, the principle of equal retribution) means that you take for the wronged person the like of what the wrongdoer did.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, wants to lighten the impact of the matter on the believers who were turned back at al-Hudaybiyyah in Dhu al-Qa'dah of the sixth year of the Hijrah, and the polytheists sent them back to Madinah. Allah then granted them retaliation by letting them return in Dhu al-Qa'dah in the following year, the seventh year of the Hijrah. If they had been prevented in the sacred month, Allah willed that they return to visit the House in the sacred month, at the same time.

His saying, the Truth: (and violations of sanctity are subject to retaliation) requires us to ask: how is that so, and what is the sacred thing? The sacred thing is that which is forbidden to violate, and the permitted thing is that which is unrestricted and allowed. Does this mean that the one who commits a forbidden act is retaliated against with a similar act? If a man commits adultery with a woman, do we say to him, "We will retaliate against you by committing adultery with you"? No. Retaliation in violations of sanctity applies only to what is permitted. Likewise, if a person steals money from me and I have no proof, but I am convinced that he is the thief, may I retaliate by stealing from him? No. Retaliation applies only to a matter that is known and clear; a hidden matter cannot be retaliated against by the same act.

But suppose one of your relatives whose maintenance is obligatory upon you, and you refrain from supporting this person, which is forbidden for you. Since the matter is public, he may take from your property and eat, and it becomes a case of retaliation. Suppose your wife complains of your stinginess and neglect, as Hind, the wife of Abu Sufyan, complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about her husband's stinginess, and he said to her: "Take from his property, in a reasonable way, what suffices you and your son."

Another example: suppose a guest is in your home and you refuse to honour him, and he seizes the opportunity of your being away from the place where you sit, then takes something and eats it. This is not a transgression against you unless it involves another forbidden matter. After that, the Truth leaves the regulation of these matters to the ruler, so that affairs do not descend into chaos.

His saying, the Truth: (So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same way as he transgressed against you) calls us to vigilance, lest someone deceive us, claiming faith while he intends revenge. We ought to recall the poet's saying:

If the scorpion returns, we return to it,
and the sandal is ready for it.

The Truth concludes the noble verse with His saying: (And fear Allah, and know that Allah is with the righteous), meaning: do not suppose that Allah has given you dominion over them in anything; rather, you and they are all owned by Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 195:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says:

﴿And spend in the cause of God, and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction; and do good, for God loves the good-doers.﴾

This verse came after the verses on fighting, and its meaning is: prepare yourselves for fighting in the cause of God.

As for His saying, ﴿do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction (al-tahlukah)﴾, it requires us to know that the word tahlukah is on the pattern tafa'ulah, and there is no counterpart to it in the Arabic language except this word. No word in the Arabic language is on the pattern tafa'ulah except the word tahlukah. Tahlukah is ruin (al-halak), and ruin is the departure of a thing from its state of being in order, such that one does not know where it goes. An example of this is the ruin of a human being, which occurs by the departure of his soul. The Truth says:

﴿So that whoever perishes might perish upon clear evidence, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence... 42﴾ [al-Anfal].

Ruin is the opposite of life. Man must know that life is not merely the sensation and movement that we see; rather, the life of each thing follows a specific measure. The life of an animal has its law, the life of a plant has its law, and the life of an inanimate thing has its law. The proof is that the Truth, glory be to Him, placed "perishes" before "lives", and He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Everything is perishing except His Face... 88﴾ [al-Qasas].

It is not only we who perish, nor only animals and plants, but everything, including inanimate matter. It is as though inanimate matter perishes like us, and as long as it perishes, it has a life, but not like our life; rather, a life according to its own law. Everything is created for a task it performs, and that is its life.

His saying, ﴿do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾, reveals to us some of the marvels of expressive eloquence in the Qur'an. In a single sentence, it gives you a thing and its opposite, and this is something we do not find in human discourse. In this verse the Truth says to us: ﴿spend in the cause of God﴾, that is, spend in jihad, and then He says: ﴿do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾. Why? Because spending is taking money out to another who performs for you a task that serves in preparing for the cause of God, such as manufacturing weapons, supplies of provisions, or equipping buildings and fortresses. These are the ways of spending money.

The Truth says: ﴿do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction﴾. The verb alqa (to throw) indicates that there is something high and something below it. It is as if God says: do not throw yourselves into destruction. Would one of us throw himself into destruction, or throw himself into destruction among his enemy? No. The hand withheld from spending in the cause of God is what throws its owner into destruction, because if he refrains from that, the enemy will become bold against him, and as long as the enemy has become bold against the believers, he will tempt them in their religion, and if he tempts them in their religion, they have perished. Thus, preparing for war is the surest way to prevent war, and when the enemy sees you strong, he fears you and withdraws from fighting you.

And just as the Truth, glory be to Him, wants from us in the legislation of fighting that we fight, He also commands us to weigh the matter of fighting with precise weighing and decisiveness, so that neither false generosity nor reckless zeal takes us. The meaning is: do not undertake fighting unless it is the overwhelming presumption that you will be victorious. Restraint in advance may require you to measure matters precisely; courage may require you at times to hold back and refrain from fighting, so that you may be victorious afterwards, at the time when preparation for it is complete.

The first meaning makes you spend in the cause of God and not throw your hand into destruction by abandoning fighting. The second meaning is: do not throw your hands into destruction by undertaking fighting without a reason or without adequate preparation. The Truth wants the believers to weigh matters in a way that keeps them from abandoning jihad and thus perishing, because their adversary will become bold against them, and it does not want them to throw their hands into fighting merely out of desire for fighting without preparing for it. This is the firmness of faith. It is one sentence that has given us several meanings.

The Truth concludes the noble verse with His saying: ﴿and do good, for God loves the good-doers﴾. The Truth says: ﴿and do good﴾. Ihsan (excellence), as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us, is: ﴿that you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you﴾ (1).

The problem of people these days is that they imitate "He sees you": they have installed closed-circuit television in large shops so that the progress of work throughout the shop may be monitored. This is the work of men. But look at the loftiness of faith: it commands you to see God, so do not perform work in a merely formal manner that removes blame from you; rather, you must perform the work with the intention of excellence in work.

Ihsan in everything is to perfect it, to such an extent that a person does for others what he would like others to do for him. If people dealt on this basis, all industries would excel. But when deception prevails, you deceive others and others deceive you, and afterwards we all cry out in complaint. We must therefore do good in everything: for example, we must do good in spending, and we will not do good in spending unless we do good in the toil that produces the fruit of what we spend, because toil's fruit is wealth, and there is no spending except with wealth. So you bring out from the proceeds of your toil to spend on what is appropriate.

The scope of ihsan is not confined to fighting alone. The matter here is general. Do not think that it is a matter in one corner of religion that came to serve one part of life; rather, every corner of religion came to serve every part of life. So if ihsan is by means of wealth, this requires that a person do good in his movement on the earth and work at a labor that suffices him and suffices those he supports, and then what he has in excess is what he can do good with.

If wealth is not available, then you must do good by your standing and intercede for others. Standing (jah) has been given its value by Islam, meaning it was made to have worth. So the person of standing must intercede with his standing to help the holders of rights obtain their rights; and the notable must also take the weak person under his protection and shield him from the oppression and injustice of the strong, and with his standing he must establish justice in the environment in which he lives.

Wijahah (distinction) means that a person has respect, weight, or esteem. These things have antecedents in a person's ihsan; he does not acquire them without cause, but a deed preceded them and made for him standing among people. People ordinarily respect only one who has some kind of favor over them, so it is as though it is respect that has been paid for, not free respect. Ihsan may be by knowledge, or by the virtue of strength through aiding the weak, or by granting experience to others, or by relieving a believer's distress.

Thus the forms of ihsan are many, and all of them serve the cause of faith. When the disbeliever sees the believers and each of them doing his work well, this entices him toward faith. If we ask: what has made our contemporary world indifferent to our religion? We will find that the world looks at God's religion through the movement of Muslims, and that movement is in most of its aspects not Islamic. It is true that some of the rational thinkers and philosophers of the West do not take religion from the movement of Muslims, and this is the utmost justice on their part, because perhaps some Muslims are not committed to their religion, so no one should take Islam from a person merely because he is a Muslim.

The adherents of other religions know that there are acts their religion has forbidden. And as long as there are acts that religion has forbidden and prescribed a punishment for, this is evidence that they may occur. When you see an individual who belongs to Islam and steals, do you say: Muslims are thieves? No. You must look at the legislation of Islam: has it criminalized the thief or not? So let no one say: look at the condition of the Muslims. Rather, let us look at the laws of Islam, because God has decreed that men perform acts, good and bad, and therefore He rewards good deeds and punishes evil deeds.

Rational people and thinkers take religion from the principles of religion itself, and do not take it from the conduct of people. It may be that the eye of an observer falls on a violator in a matter the religion forbids. So do not take a wrong act as Islam; take it rather as a departure from Islam.

When the world sees us doing good in everything, we give them the model our forefathers had. Islam was made to spread with that wondrous, legendary tide, so that within half a century it reached the farthest parts of the East and the farthest of the West. Afterwards it receded politically from the earth, but it remains as a religion, and what remains of Islam is this system that draws people to it. Islam has an immunity in its inherent essence; it carries the components of its survival and its fitness. It is what draws non-Muslims to it so that they believe in it, and it is not Muslims who draw people to Islam.

Therefore I say: if the political representation of Islamic nations in the civilized non-Islamic countries had adopted the principles of Islam, it would have been a good model. Look at a single capital of the Western states and you will find more than sixty-three Islamic embassies in it, and each embassy has a staff exceeding twenty. Suppose these people were an Islamic model in conduct and dealings in a non-Islamic capital; then the people of that country would find a committed Islamic community, not seduced by the ornaments of civilization: they do not drink wine, do not dance, do not frequent places of ill repute, and their women do not display themselves. By God, would the conduct of these people not attract attention?

But what happens, unfortunately, is that the people of the West, despite their falsehood, have overcome the sons of Islam, despite their truth, and have led them to their own licentiousness. This blind imitation makes Westerners say: if Islam had immunity, it would have protected its children from falling into what we have fallen into.

Thus the ihsan of Muslims is the greatest propaganda and call to the religion of Islam. The Truth says: ﴿for God loves the good-doers﴾. Love, as we know it, is the inclination of the lover's heart toward the beloved, and this is so with respect to humans. But with respect to the Truth, it is the Creator's affection toward the created with mercy and honor. The Truth, glory be to Him, loves that His servants be upon His character. Just as God has done well in everything He created (﴿He who made everything He created good﴾), He wants from His servants, since He has graced them with a thinking mind that plans, and with capacities that turn thought into action, that the Truth wants us to make our guide in every work that we do it well, so that we become characterized by the character of God. Thus the word ﴿God﴾ spreads, that noble word with which a person greets every beauty in any craft, saying: ﴿God﴾.

Thus the word ﴿God﴾ spreads as a blessing in existence, as a comment on everything good, even he who does not believe in that God also says: ﴿God﴾. It is as if the natural disposition (fitrah) God originated in people speaks that all goodness must be attributed to God, whether God is the one who acts directly, such as causes, cosmic phenomena and laws, or the one who created the doer of the good. All matters return to God.

If those who do not do their deeds well knew what they deprive existence of, they would grieve over themselves. Would that they deprived existence only of the word ﴿God﴾! Rather, they put in place of ﴿God﴾ an evil word, and they spread ugliness in existence, and when ugliness spreads in existence, humanity in general is the loser.

So God's saying: ﴿for God loves the good-doers﴾ is an encouragement to everyone who takes up any work to do it well, so that he may be upon the character of God.

(1) Part of a hadith related by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 196:

After that, the Truth (may He be exalted) says:

﴿And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then [offer] whatever sacrifice is feasible. And do not shave your heads until the sacrifice has reached its place. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [must compensate] with a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice. And when you are safe, whoever enjoys [the benefit of] 'Umrah until Hajj [must offer] what sacrifice is feasible. But whoever does not find [an animal], then fast three days during Hajj and seven when you return; that is ten complete. That is for one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque. And fear Allah, and know that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ [2:196]

The Qur'anic arrangement (nasq) is a wondrous arrangement. You recall that He spoke about fasting, and Ramadan comes before the months of Hajj, so it was natural that He speak about Hajj after speaking about Ramadan, and about the new moons and His making the new moons as timekeeping markers for people and for Hajj. There is also another matter that calls for speaking about Hajj, which is speaking about fighting in the sacred months and about the Sacred House. He, glorified is He, said:

﴿And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there﴾ (part of verse 191, surah al-Baqarah).

So the discussion of Hajj comes in its natural context. When Allah says: (And complete the Hajj and the 'Umrah for Allah), we understand from it that the command to complete something is not given except when the command to perform that act has been revealed, as if you began to act after the legislation of it.
