It is said: so-and-so has (lidd), that is, he has wickedness in his dispute, and he argues with falsehood. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: (Indeed, the most hated of men to Allah is the most contentious opponent).¹

That is, the one who argues with falsehood and has harshness in disobedience; he is a sinner and at the same time harsh in his sinfulness. Why is he the most contentious of opponents? Because the one who confronts you openly makes you take precautions against him, whereas the one who meets you with hypocrisy wants to deceive you. This is violence in dispute. An open opponent is better, because he confronts you with what is in his inner self. But when you confront one who conceals his enmity and shows his love, he will be harsh toward you in his dispute, because he wants to deceive you and plot against you.

﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein.﴾ "Turns away" (tawalla) means departs. That is, he tells you what pleases you, and when he turns away from you, he moves the matter to reality by revealing what he was concealing. The meaning may also be that when he takes charge of something else (from wilaya, authority), then in "tawalla" there is the sense of turning away and withdrawing, and there is also the sense of assuming authority.

﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and livestock.﴾ Without human intervention, the earth was created in the form of goodness, and corruption is an accidental matter that comes from human beings. We know that corruption has not befallen any matter except that humans have had a part in it.

Why have we complained of a shortage of food, but never of a shortage of air? Because humans have no intervention in air, and to the extent that human intervention increases, corruption occurs. We intervened a little in water, and corruption came from that: we did not manage to convey it through good pipes, so it reached us polluted, or chlorine was added to it or removed from it. To the degree that intervention occurs, corruption occurs. In earlier times, a person would go to the direct source of water in the wells and take the natural water that Allah created without human intervention, and there was no pollution or anything else.

Thus, to the extent that a human being is present in the movement of life without being guided by faith in Allah, corruption arises. That is why humanity needed a heavenly method. Other creatures than humans have no method; they were created by instinct and perform their function alone. The beast has never refused to let you ride it, nor to let you load your burdens upon it, nor to let you use it in plowing or irrigation. Even when you slaughter it, it does not refuse you. Why? Because it was created with an instinct by which it performs beneficial movement without choice on its part. If it refuses at some time, that happens only because of an accidental matter, such as illness.

But the one who has choice must have a method that tells him: do this and do not do that. If he is upright in following the method regarding "do" and "do not do," his life proceeds in a balanced way. But if he is not upright, life becomes corrupt. This is what we understand from the words of the Exalted: ﴿When he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein﴾, as if corruption were the thing that needs work. Leave nature and creatures as they are, and you will find them working in order and perfection, going well.

Thus corruption is an accidental matter that comes from the human being who lives without a method, for ﴿when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein.﴾ So it is as if the original state of the earth and what is in it came in the form of goodness. If you do not add to what is good, then do not try to corrupt it. The Exalted said:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption in the land," they say, "We are only reformers." Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they perceive not.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

From here we understand that they supposed the earth needed their movement to reform it, although the earth without their movement is good, because they do not move by the method of Allah.

Thus from this verse we understand that when a person (tawalla), in the sense of turning back, or assuming authority, strives in the land to cause corruption therein, then corruption in the land is an accidental matter arising from human striving without a method from Allah. And as long as the human being has choice, there must be a method above him that protects that choice. If he has no method and follows his desire, he is certainly a corrupter.

Consider the stupidity of one who corrupts the earth: does he think that he alone will benefit from the earth, so that he permits himself to corrupt the earth for others? He forgets the truth: just as he corrupts for others, others corrupt for him. So who loses? We will all lose, then.

﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and livestock...﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

The word "harth" (crops/tilth) has two meanings: sometimes it is applied to crops, and sometimes to women. The first meaning occurs in the words of the Exalted:

﴿And David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field into which the sheep of the people had strayed at night...﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya').

So "harth" in the verse means crops, and crops result from tilling and stirring the earth. Your task, O human, is to till and stir the earth, bring the seed that Allah created into the earth that Allah created, water it with the water that Allah created, and grow in the air that Allah created. For this reason the Almighty calls our attention and alerts us, saying:

﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah).

The second meaning: "harth" is applied to women in the words of the Exalted:

﴿Your wives are a tilth for you...﴾ (part of verse 223, Surah al-Baqarah).

Just as the purpose of tilling crops is to produce plants, so the woman is for bearing children. The Exalted says:

﴿So come to your tilth however you wish.﴾ (part of verse 223, Surah al-Baqarah).

Those who are licentious and permissive wished to extend approaching women to her entire body. We say to them: observe His words, "your tilth," and the tilth is the place of growth, so approaching is only in the place of growth. Do not understand it as a generalization; it is a specification. The Almighty continues describing the one who speaks good words but strives in the land with corruption, saying: ﴿and destroy crops and livestock.﴾ "Livestock" (nasl) means offspring and descendants.

The verse concludes with: ﴿and Allah does not love corruption.﴾ That is, the Almighty wants of you, if you do not contribute the power that Allah gave you in thought and giving, then at least leave the matter as Allah created it, because Allah does not love that you corrupt what He created good in its own essence.

What has preceded in this verse is merely an example of the ways the Islamic call was received in its early days by those who were hypocritically opposing its strong reality, bringing words that pleased and acts that pleased the hypocrite. We know that hypocrisy was evidence of the strength of the Muslims, and for this reason hypocrisy did not arise in Makkah but arose in Madinah. The Almighty said:

﴿And among the people of Madinah are those who have become adept at hypocrisy.﴾ (part of verse 101, Surah al-Tawbah).

Someone may ask: how did this phenomenon appear in the strong faith-environment of Madinah? We say: because Islam in Makkah was weak, and no one flatters the weak, whereas Islam in Madinah became strong, and it is the strong whom people flatter.

Thus the presence of hypocrisy in Madinah was a healthy phenomenon showing that faith had become strong, to the point that one who had no Islam claimed it. These people would say beautiful, pleasing words, and they might do in front of those they flattered acts that pleased whoever saw or heard them, but they did not remain steadfast in the truth. When they turned away, that is, disappeared from the eyes of those they flattered, they returned to their original disbelief, or when they were entrusted with something, they strove in the land with corruption.

¹ Narrated by al-Bukhari. The meaning of (al-aladd al-khasm) is the one most intense in his dispute.

The verse here addresses something that reveals the discernment of the believers: the verse exposed the hypocrite. Al-Akhnas was the chief of hypocrisy, and exposing the hypocrite in this manner shows that behind Muhammad (ﷺ) and the believers who follow Muhammad stands a Lord who informs them of whoever is deceiving them. It also alerts them to the necessity of having discernment, as the Truth says:

﴿And when it is said to him, "Fear Allah," pride takes hold of him in sin. So Hell is sufficient for him, and wretched is the resting place.﴾

He would not be told "Fear Allah" unless it was known that he was a hypocrite. Since they said this to him, that is evidence that their discernment was not deceived by this hypocrisy. We understand from this verse that the believer is shrewd and perceptive (kayyis, one who is intelligent and sharp), and must look at things with the measure of mental alertness. He must not surrender himself merely to outward purity to be given the matter; rather, Allah wants every believer to have individuality and shrewdness.

"And when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah'": it seems that the outward appearance by which he speaks or acts contradicts taqwa, because it is a pleasing speech that does not harmonize with an inner state that is not pleased. It is true that he prays in the first row, is enthusiastic about the causes of religion, and says the fine words that please the Prophet (ﷺ) and please the believers. But it is conduct and speech issuing from a corrupt intention. The meaning of "Fear Allah" is: let your outward be in agreement with your inward. It is not enough to say a speech that pleases, nor to do an action that delights others, because Allah loves that speech be in harmony with action, and that the action of the limbs be in harmony with the intentions of the heart.

Therefore, the believer must have discernment, intelligence, and sharpness, and must see the conduct of the other party, so he does not take things at face value, nor by the mere wording of speech or deed, unless he finds in it a harmony of action with intention. He is not content merely to know this, but must tell the hypocrite the truth of what he sees, so as to shorten the hypocrite's period of hypocrisy. When he says to him, "Fear Allah," the hypocrite understands that his hypocrisy has been exposed, and perhaps after that he will refrain from hypocrisy. In that there is mercy from the believer toward the hypocrite. Whoever sees and perceives, by his intelligence, hypocrisy in anyone here should say to him, "Fear Allah." The intention is to expose his hypocrisy and say to him, "Fear Allah." If one person says to him, "Fear Allah," and another says, "Fear Allah," and a third, and a fourth, he will know completely that his hypocrisy has been exposed, and his speech will no longer please people.

"And when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah,' pride takes hold of him in sin": the restriction of pride to sin here indicates that pride may be without sin. Since Allah has said "pride takes hold of him in sin," there is therefore a pride without sin. Yes, because pride is desirable for the believer, and Almighty Allah has ruled pride for Himself, for His Messenger, and for the believers:

﴿And to Allah belongs honour, and to His Messenger and to the believers.﴾ (Surah al-Munafiqun, 8)

This is honour through truth, not through sin. What is the difference between honour through truth and honour through sin? Let us survey the Noble Qur'an to know the difference. Did not the magicians of Pharaoh say, as Allah related about them:

﴿By the might of Pharaoh, indeed we will be the victors.﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 44)

This is honour through sin and falsehood. Likewise His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿But those who disbelieve are in pride and dissension.﴾ (Surah Sad, 2)

This too is false honour. As for His saying, Almighty and Majestic:

﴿Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of honour, above what they describe.﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 180)

That is true honour. So honour is the power that prevails, which nothing can overcome. As for honour through sin, it is the haughtiness of pride joined with guilt and disobedience. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, says to everyone who desires this kind of honour through sin: if you have honour, no one will be able to overpower you. But O magicians of Pharaoh, O you who said "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed we will be the victors," it was you who fell down prostrate to Moses and said:

﴿We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 47-48)

The might of Pharaoh did not benefit you, because it was honour through sin. Honour through truth came and overcame honour through sin. Therefore, Allah, Glorified and Exalted, makes clear to us that honour, so that it is not through sin, must be directed against the disbeliever in Allah, and be humility toward the believer in Allah:

﴿Humble toward the believers, mighty over the disbelievers.﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah, 54)

Likewise His saying, the Truth:

﴿Forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves.﴾ (Surah al-Fath, 29)

This is the evidence of honour through truth, and its sign is that when it prevails, it is at the height of humility. We have as an example our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who left Makkah because he could not protect the weak among the believers. Then he returned to Makkah as a conqueror by the victory of Allah, and entered Makkah with his head bowed in humility toward Allah, so much so that it almost touched the qurbus (the front arch) of his mount's saddle. That is strength, and it is the opposite of honour through sin, which, when it prevails, becomes tyrannical. Honour through truth, when it prevails, becomes humble.

"And when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah,' pride takes hold of him in sin": that is, pride and haughtiness are joined with sin, and sin is opposition to what Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has commanded. "So Hell is sufficient for him, and wretched is the resting place." What is this honour that leads in the end to the Fire? It is not honour; rather it is humiliation. There is no good in a deed that is followed by the Fire, and no evil in an evil that is followed by Paradise. So if you want to be honoured, consider your end and where you are going.

"So Hell is sufficient for him": that is, this suffices as exposure of his honour through sin. As for the word "mihad" (resting place), its meaning is something smoothed and prepared, that is, comfortable for sitting, walking, and dwelling. That is why they call a child's cradle a mahd. Does a mihad in this form fit punishment? Yes, it fits exactly, because the one who sits in a mihad has no will to get out of it, like a child who has no strength to leave his bed. So he has lost his will and his control over his limbs. If the mihad is in this form in the Fire, then it is "wretched is the resting place."

This is one type of people. In contrast, the Exalted gives us another type of people, and He says:

﴿And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah, and Allah is Kind to the servants.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 207)

(١) Al-Qurbus is the raised, arched part of the saddle.

If you wish, in Surat Yusuf, consider the words of the Exalted:

﴿And they sold him for a cheap price﴾ [Surah Yusuf].

That is, they sold him for a low price. It also comes with the meaning of "bought" (ishtara). The ancient Arab poet 'Antarah ibn Shaddad says: "He plunged into its torrents, and bought and sold."

So (shara) in the language is used in two senses: either it means "sold" (baa'a), or it means "bought" (ishtara). Context and indicators determine which meaning is intended. In 'Antarah's words, "shara wa baa'a" (he bought and sold), we understand that what is meant by "shara" here is "bought," since it stands in contrast to "baa'a." And in the Exalted's words:

﴿And they sold him for a cheap price﴾ [Surah Yusuf],

the context of the verse makes clear that they sold him. This is one of the greatness of the Arabic language: it is a language that wants people who receive the word with their intellect, and who let context govern their understanding of meanings.

(And among the people is one who sells himself (yashri nafsahu) seeking the pleasure of God), and we understand "yashri" here to mean "sells his self." One who sells himself is one who loses it in exchange for something. When a person loses himself, he sacrifices it, and when the sacrifice is in pursuit of God's pleasure, it is martyrdom in His path, the Mighty and Majestic. It is as if he sold himself and received in exchange the pleasure of God.

Similar to this is the saying of the Exalted:

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah].

The Truth gives them Paradise in exchange for their selves and their wealth. So His saying, "And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of God," means he sold himself and took Paradise in exchange for it, if the meaning of "yashri" is "sold."

And what is the meaning if it means "bought"? Here we understand that he bought his self, meaning that he sacrificed everything so that his faithful self would be saved. It is remarkable that this verse has been said, regarding its occasion of revelation, to confirm that it bears both meanings, "sold" and "bought." There is Abu Yahya, who is Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi. He was in Makkah, and he had grown old. He embraced Islam and wished to emigrate. The disbelievers said to him: "You came to Makkah poor, and we sheltered you under our protection, and now you are a man of great wealth, and you want to emigrate with your wealth."

He said to them: "If I leave you with my wealth, will you let me go?"

They said: "Yes."

He said: "Will you guarantee for me a mount and provision until I reach Madinah?"

They said: "That is yours."

He had thus bought his self with this conduct and preserved it in faith by his wealth. When he went to Madinah, Abu Bakr and 'Umar met him and said to him: "The sale has profited, O Abu Yahya."

He said: "And may God profit all your trade."

Sayyidina Abu Bakr and Sayyidina 'Umar said to him: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) told us that Jibril informed him of your story." It is narrated that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "The sale has profited, Abu Yahya." So the meaning of the verse according to this story is that he bought his self with his wealth, and the context of the verse agrees with this same meaning. This is among the benefits of Qur'anic expression, where a single word serves two opposite meanings.

But if the meaning is that he sold himself, then that has a different story. At the Battle of Badr, which was the first battle in Islam, the chiefs of Quraysh had gathered themselves to fight the Muslims in this battle. The Muslims were able to kill some of these chiefs and also captured many of them. Among those killed in this battle was one of the chiefs of Quraysh, Abu 'Uqbah al-Harith ibn 'Amir, and the one who killed him was a companion named Khubayb ibn 'Adi al-Ansari al-Awsi, who was from the tribe of the Aws in Madinah. After that, some disbelievers schemed, and sent to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saying: "O Messenger of God, we have embraced Islam, and we want you to send us people who will teach us Islam." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent them ten of his companions to teach them the Qur'an. The disbelievers betrayed these ten and killed them, except Khubayb ibn 'Adi, who managed to escape with his life, along with another companion named Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah. But Khubayb fell into captivity, and those who captured him recognized that he was the one who had killed Abu 'Uqbah al-Harith at the Battle of Badr. So they sold him to the son of Abu 'Uqbah so that he might kill him in exchange for his father. He did not want to kill him, but instead crucified him alive. When he left him crucified on the wood, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), while in Madinah, said: "Who will take down Khubayb from his cross, and for him is Paradise?"

Al-Zubayr said: "I, O Messenger of God."

And al-Miqdad said: "And I am with him, O Messenger of God."

They went to Makkah and found Khubayb on the cross, and he had died, and around him were forty men of Quraysh guarding him. They seized their moment of heedlessness, went to the cross, took down Khubayb and carried him off. When the people came to their senses, they did not find Khubayb, so they set out tracking the trail to catch up with those who had taken him. Al-Zubayr saw them, so he threw Khubayb on the ground, then looked at him, and behold, the earth swallowed him, so he was named "Swallowed by the Earth" (Bali' al-Ard). After that he turned to them and removed the turban behind which he had been concealing himself, and said: "I am al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, my mother is Safiyyah bint 'Abd al-Muttalib, and my companion is al-Miqdad. If you wish, I will boast against you, meaning each of us will boast of himself; and if you wish, I will fight you, meaning I will combat you; or if you wish, depart." They said: "We depart," and they departed. When al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he gave them the good news of the Paradise to which Khubayb had gone.

So Khubayb sold himself for Paradise. Accordingly, if one attributes the occasion of revelation of the verse to Abu Yahya Suhayb ibn Sinan al-Rumi, then "shara" means "bought," and if one attributes the occasion of revelation to Khubayb, then it means "sold." Thus we find that a single word in the Noble Qur'an bears more than one reality.

As for this Khubayb ibn 'Adi, the daughter of the man who bought him to give him to 'Uqbah so that he might kill him in exchange for his father, Mawiyyah, said of him: "By God, I saw Khubayb eating a bunch of grapes like a man's head! And by God, there was no garden or grapevine in Makkah; it was only a provision that God sent to him."

When they came to kill him, he said: "Let me pray two rak'ahs." He prayed two rak'ahs, then looked at the people and said: "By God, if I did not fear that you would say he prolonged the prayer out of fear of death, I would have prolonged it." And before they killed him he said: "O God, count them, kill them one by one, and leave none of them." Then he cried out and said:

"And I do not care, when I am killed as a Muslim,
On whatever side I fall, for God is my place of death."

That was the last thing he said.

The Truth says: (And God is Kind to His servants). What is the connection between what preceded and "Kind to His servants"? Since God is Kind to His servants, God did not will to make this a general matter for every Muslim, but rather made it rare instances to establish the truth of the faith-based cause, because He does not want all Muslims to sacrifice themselves, but wants to preserve among us people who will carry the call.

After the Almighty has presented the types of people who receive the call with disbelief and hypocrisy, and those who stand opposite them, who receive it with pure faith, He calls out to all the believers, saying:

﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace (al-silm) completely and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ [2:208]

The verse begins with the address to those who have believed in Allah, as if He were saying to them: O you who have believed in Me, listen to My word. Allah does not impose obligations on one who has not believed in Him; rather He addresses those who love Him and have believed in Him. And since they have loved Allah, every believer must turn to the One he loves, for Allah will not give him anything except what makes him happy.

So the obligation from Allah is a making-happy of the one who loves Him: ﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace completely﴾. The word "fi" (in) indicates the sense of enclosure (zarfiyyah), and the meaning of enclosure is that one thing contains another. An example of this is the cup that contains water, so we say: "The water is in the cup." Likewise, the mosque contains those who pray, so we say: "The worshippers are in the mosque."

Enclosure indicates that the container surrounds the contained, and since the container has surrounded the contained, the contained has no way to escape from the container. For this reason, the Almighty gives us a picture of how thoroughly enclosure can be realized when He says:

﴿And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees﴾ [20:71].

Crucifixion is always upon something, and the noble verse wishes to explain to us how crucifixion can be fully embedded in the one crucified. When you want to crucify something upon something, you tie it to the thing it is crucified upon; and if you go to the extreme in tying it, it is as though you had put the crucified inside the one it is crucified upon.

For example: bring a matchstick, place it on your finger, and then tie it firmly with a thread. You will notice that the stick has sunk into your skin. The Almighty says: ﴿Enter into peace completely﴾. The word "as-silm" (السِّلم), "as-salm" (السَّلم), and "as-salam" (السَّلَم) is Islam, and the root is one, because peace (السلم) is the opposite of war, and Islam came to end the war between you and the universe in which you live, for your benefit and the benefit of the universe, so that you may be at peace with Allah, at peace with the universe, at peace with people, and at peace with yourself.

His saying "enter into peace" means: that peace may encompass you. Allah is the God who created the universe, and you must live in peace with Him, since you believe in none but Him as the one God. So we must live in peace with the earth, the heavens, and the universe, because the universe is submissive, subdued, and subjected, and it cannot step outside what has been drawn for it; it works in your service and does not oppose you.

When a person is obedient, everything in existence rejoices in him, because existence is obedient and glorifies Allah. When a person finds a fellow glorifier like himself, he rejoices in him, because he is at peace with the universe. And you are at peace with yourself, because you have a will; and this will—Allah's dominion over all your limbs—does what you want from any organ. But does every organ agree with what you command? That is another matter. For example, your tongue responds to your will, so you say with it: "There is no god but Allah," and others among the polytheists say otherwise, associating with Allah humans and non-humans whom they worship. The atheists said with their tongues, may Allah protect us: "There is no god in the universe," and the tongue did not disobey any of them, because it is subdued to their will.

A person's will over his tongue and all his limbs ends on the Day of Resurrection, and he is witnessed against by his other members: the feet, the hands, the eyes, the ears, and every limb acknowledges what it used to do, because on that day a person has no control over those parts. Rather, all control belongs to the Supreme Creator.

﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer.﴾

When Allah calls the believers to enter into peace completely, the meaning also allows that the Almighty addresses the Muslims not to take some of the religion and leave the other part. He says to them: take Islam entirely and implement it fully, for Islam represents a structure with known foundations and clear rules, so no one should try to take one ruling apart from another, or else imbalance would occur.

For example, you may find a dispute between husband and wife, which may lead to fights and divorce, and afterward you find someone accusing Islam of having given the man a sword drawn over the woman. We say to them: Why do you accuse Islam? Did you enter marriage according to the logic of Islam? If you entered marriage according to the logic of Islam, you would find the organizing rules that preserve the woman's dignity; but there are those who enter marriage without the logic of Islam, and when they fall into crisis they begin calling upon Islam. Did the man choose the one who will share his life by the measure of religion? Did he place before his eyes the conditions for choosing a righteous wife, which came in the noble hadith:

On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "A woman is married for four things: for her wealth, for her lineage, for her beauty, and for her religion. So win the one with religion; may your hands be rubbed with dust."¹

Did the man prefer the woman of religion over others, or did he prefer another criterion? When a man came to propose to a daughter from her father, did the father place the criteria of Islam in consideration when approving this marriage? Did you prefer the one whose religion and character you are pleased with, or did you abandon those rules? You abandoned the rules of Islam, so why do you blame Islam when consequences and outcomes are bad?

If you wish to be held to account, you must take all your affairs by the measure of Islam, and then act in a manner suited to Islam. If you are like that, Islam protects you from everything. Islam supports the forces in the universe and supports the forces within the self, so that you live in peace and do not oppose, because all of that is met by war. War arises only from the opposition of forces: the forces of your self oppose one another in war with yourself, the forces of humans oppose one another in war with humans, and your powers oppose the other powers of the universe, so you oppose nature and oppose the Almighty.

Thus opposition gives rise to war, and war arises only when desires differ. Human desires cannot meet except when they are guarded by the values of one who has no desire. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:

﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted…﴾ [23:71] (Surat al-Mu'minun)

Why? Leave aside the deaf universe around you, or the universe that has no choice in acting or being acted upon by you; it acts or is acted upon for you without choice on its part. But look at humans of your own kind: what makes one person's desire dominate the desires of others?

What has that person possessed that makes you a follower of him, or him a follower of you? In the law of following, the follower can only be one who believes that the one followed is above him, and no human can have this superiority at all. Therefore all humans must follow a power they believe is above them all. When we believe, we enter into peace, and there is no opposition between one power and another power; for I am not subject to you, nor are you subject to me, and both you and I submit to a power higher than me and you. The power we follow in obedience must also be one that has no interest in what it legislates.

Human legislators consider their interests when they legislate: the legislator of communism frames his legislation against capitalism, and the legislator of capitalism frames his against communism. But when the legislator has no benefit from what he legislates, this is the legislation of the Almighty.

When we enter Islam, we all enter, and none of us stays aside; that is the meaning of "enter into peace completely." This is one meaning, and there is another meaning also possible: enter into peace, that is, Islam, with all its obligations, so that you leave no obligation aside from you.

As for the first meaning: if we did not all enter into peace, those who submit would suffer because of those who do not submit, for the one who submits refines his conduct toward others, and the benefit of the Muslim reaches others, while the Muslim suffers from the non-submission of those who have not submitted. So it is in the interest of us all that we all be Muslims. Those who do not perceive this truth interpret the saying of Allah, Exalted:

﴿No harm will come to you from those who have gone astray if you are guided﴾ [5:105]

contrary to its apparent meaning. Part of your guidance is that you make those who have not believed see, so that they believe, because your interest is that you all submit; if you submit, your submission will benefit others, because your conduct will become upright and refined, while whoever has not submitted will have crooked and unrefined conduct, and you will suffer because of him. So it is in your interest to spend a long time and bear great hardship in calling others to enter Islam. Beware of saying that this wastes your life's opportunities. No, it secures for you life's opportunities, and your time is not wasted, because you will protect yourself from the evils of the non-Muslim.

I clearly remember that when we spoke on Surat al-Fatihah, we said: Allah teaches us to say ﴿You alone we worship﴾: "We all, O Lord, worship You, and we will all be made happy by that; and guide us all, O Lord, for if You guide me alone, others would enjoy Your guidance to me while I would suffer from their misguidance. So it is in our interest that we all be guided together."

This is the meaning of "enter into peace completely," that is, all together. As for the meaning of His saying, ﴿No harm will come to you from those who have gone astray if you are guided﴾, it means you will not bear the burden of their misguidance when you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. As for the second meaning: enter Islam so that none of you stays aside. Someone takes some parts of Islam and leaves others, but you want to build your life. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explained that Islam has foundations, namely the five pillars, and beware of taking three pillars and leaving two, for the structure of Islam is built upon five pillars.

One engineer once told me: We can build a structure on three pillars, or four, or five. I said to him: But when you make the building on four pillars and distribute the loads and weights over four foundations, can you, when constructing it, make it three pillars only? He said: No.

I said: Then the building is established from the beginning on the foundations you want, and therefore you distribute the forces over three, four, or five from the start. Allah, glorified and exalted, willed that the foundations of Islam be five, and after that Islam is built; and when Islam is built, beware of taking one brick of Islam without another, but Islam must be taken entirely. The harm that occurs in the Muslim world is the result of the patchwork that happens within the Muslim world: those patchworks which attempt to take some of Islam and leave some, and this is the reason for the weariness and harm, because Islam must be taken all at once. So ﴿Enter into peace completely﴾ means: beware of leaving aside any of its rulings. What wearies those who now belong to the religion is that we want to patch together an Islamic life in lands that take their laws from non-Islamic lands.

Therefore, for us to succeed in our lives, we must take all of Islam. Unfortunately, many rulers of Muslim lands take from Islam only the last part of the verse: ﴿Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you﴾. They take "those in authority among you" and leave "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger."

And I say: Why do you take the last part and leave what precedes it? Allah did not make the obedience to the ruler an independent obedience; rather He said: ﴿Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾ to show that obedience to the ruler is from within the obedience to Allah and obedience to the Messenger. So we do not want patchwork in Islam; take it whole, and you will find rest, and we will find rest with you.

The Almighty, by calling us to enter Islam, wants to protect people from the trial of the difference of their desires; so He lightened and removed from His creatures what they might dispute over, and left them free to pursue the task of deriving the secrets of Allah in His existence through experimental knowledge as they like. If they desire progress, let them work...

¹ Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 2, verse 209:

The Truth (al-Haqq) then says:

﴿And if you slip after clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾

Al-zalla (slip) is disobedience (al-ma'siyah). It is derived from the root (zala), and "zala al-shay'" means it departed from its uprightness. So everything has an uprightness, and departing from it is considered a slip. Al-zalal (slipping) is the sins and disobedience by which one opposes the straight path (al-manhaj al-mustaqim).

(After clear proofs have come to you) He, glory be to Him, makes clear to us that you have absolutely no excuse for slipping, because I have explained everything to you and did not leave you to your minds alone. It is logical that you use your minds correctly so that you manage the movement of the universe in which I have made you successors (istikhlaf). Nevertheless, if heedlessness befalls you, I send the messengers. For this reason He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And We would never punish until We have sent a messenger.﴾ (Qur'an 17:15)

Allah has shown mercy to creation by sending messengers so that they may make clear to humankind the correct path from the crooked path. The Truth, exalted is He, leaves some matters to humans so that they may bring forth thought from themselves, and then He approves of Islam what they have brought, to teach us that reason, when it is natural and logical, is capable of reaching the judgment by its own nature. In the history of Islam we find that our master 'Umar saw things and proposed some suggestions, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agreed to them, and then the Qur'an was revealed in accordance with what 'Umar had said. Someone may ask: was the Prophet (ﷺ) not more deserving of this?

We say: had those opinions come from the Prophet (ﷺ), there would be nothing strange in them, because the Prophet (ﷺ) is infallible (ma'sum) and revelation comes to him. But Allah wants to tell us that when natural reason is pure, it can be guided to the correct judgment, even if no judgment has descended from heaven. For this reason the judgments of our master 'Umar provoke a large number of orientalists, who say: "Do you have nothing but 'Umar? Why do you not say Muhammad?"

We say to them: 'Umar was raised in the school of the Prophet (ﷺ), so what he says he took from the Prophet (ﷺ). 'Umar himself acknowledged this and said: "What is 'Umar without Islam?" We cite 'Umar because he is a human being and not a messenger; what applies to humans applies to him. Revelation does not come to him, and he was not infallible.

So it seems the Truth wanted to bring us close to the capacity for deduction (istinbat) and understanding, so that we all become 'Umar; for 'Umar, by his natural disposition, was guided to what is right, and he would say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Shall we do such-and-such?", and revelation would then come in agreement with his opinion. Thus Allah has not burdened us beyond measure; rather, the obligation came to protect the minds from the desires of the self which obscure them. The affliction of opinion is desire, and were it not for desires, all opinions would agree.

Long ago they gave us an example of the woman who gathered summer and winter in a single night. She married off her son and her daughter, and the four of them lived together in one room: her son with his wife, her daughter with her husband, and the woman with them. She sleeps only a little and goes to her daughter advising her: "Warm your husband and please him, for the weather is cold." Then she goes to her son and says: "Keep away from your wife, for the world is hot."

The place is one and the night is one, but the woman made it summer and winter at the same time, and the cause is the desire of the self. Allah, glory be to Him, shows us this in His saying:

﴿And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted.﴾ (Qur'an 23:71)

So the Truth, glory be to Him, protects us when He legislates for us. Humans grow weary of the legislation of their own selves for themselves, so they try to lessen the error of human legislation, and they legislate things by which they correct what they have; and if you look at the laws they have amended, you will find that the amendment meets Islam or comes close to Islam.

They asked me in America: "Why has Islam not prevailed over all creeds, although you say that Allah says in His Book: ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾? Yet your religion has not prevailed over all religions, and many people remain non-Muslims, whether they are Jews, Christians, or without religion?"

I said: If you would pay attention to the saying of Allah: ﴿though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ and ﴿though the polytheists dislike it﴾, that would show you that the prevalence of Islam has been achieved alongside the existence of disbelievers, and its prevalence alongside the existence of polytheists. Otherwise, if it prevailed with nothing opposing it, against whom would it be disliked? The creed that the people of disbelief dislike is the one that strengthens the existence of Islam. Thus ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it﴾ indicates that the prevalence of Islam means that a disbeliever and a polytheist will both exist, and both will dislike the spread of the religion.

When we see the events of life compelling Western countries, when they discover the error of their legislation, they try to amend the laws, and they find no amendment except to turn to the rulings of Islam. But they did not turn to it as a religion; they turned to it as a system. Their return to Islam is evidence and confirmation of the soundness and validity of Islam's rulings, because if they had taken those rulings as religious rulings, others would have said: "A people fanatical about a religion they believe in, and so they implemented its rulings." But despite their dislike of the religion, they were compelled to adopt its teachings, so it seems they have no solution except to take what Islam has put forward.

Thus the saying of Allah: ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it﴾ is a strength for the system of Islam, not so that you believe in it, but so that you are compelled to resort to it. In Italy, for example, they used to criticize Islam for permitting divorce and regarded it as an avenging of women's rights; but the circumstances of life and family problems compelled them to permit divorce. Did they legislate it because Islam said so? No, but because they found that the solution to their problems comes only from it. And in America, when they launched a fierce campaign against the consumption of alcohol, did they fight it because Islam prohibited it? No, but because the reality of public health demanded that of them. Thus ﴿though the disbelievers dislike it﴾ and ﴿though the polytheists dislike it﴾ mean that they will resort to the system of Islam to resolve their issues. If they do not take it as a religion, they will take it as a system.

﴿If you slip after clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Mighty and Wise.﴾ That is: beware lest you think that by your slipping you have taken your portions from Allah; for your return is to Allah, and He is Mighty, and His might, glory be to Him, is that He prevails and is not prevailed upon. He manages our affairs with mercy and wisdom.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 2, verse 210:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿Are they waiting for anything but that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels, and the matter be decided? And to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ (2:210)

That is: what are they waiting for? Are they waiting for affairs to overtake them, so that they find themselves in a world whose adornment has been taken, and it has turned into stubble scattered by the winds, and the human being stands before the moment of reckoning?

His saying "هل ينظرون" (hal yanzuroon, "are they waiting") is derived from al-nazar (looking). Al-nazar is the seeking of perception of a thing in general, and seeking perception of anything by anything is called nazar. An example of this is that we say to anyone who speaks on any intellectual matter: "Do you not have nazar?" That is, do you possess the power of perception or not?

So nazar is the seeking of perception of a thing. If you seek to see, it is nazar with the eye; if you seek to know and understand, it is nazar with the intellect and the heart. Sometimes nazar is used to mean waiting, which is the seeking of perception of what is expected.

And "هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله" means: are they waiting for anything other than that the Hour should come upon them and surprise them in their particular time? For it will not surprise anyone in the general time, since it will have minor signs and major signs. The meaning of its having minor and major signs is that this is evidence that Allah gives us respite so that we may amend ourselves; He keeps open the door of repentance so long as the sun has not risen from the west.

When we hear His saying, exalted is He, "هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله", we say: what delays their entry into Islam in its entirety? What are they waiting for? Just as you say to a person in front of you: "What are you waiting for?" Likewise, the Truth urges us to enter into submission (al-silm) completely; otherwise, what are you waiting for?

And "إلا أن يأتيهم الله في ظلل من الغمام والملائكة" — when you say "يأتيهم الله" or "جاء ربك" or He, glory be to Him, comes in the Qur'an with something similar to what we know among created beings of coming and arriving, and like the face and the hand, then take it within the frame of "ليس كمثله شيء" (there is nothing like unto Him). Allah exists and you exist: is your existence like His existence? No.

Allah is living and you are living: is your life like His life? No. Allah is All-Hearing and you hear: is your hearing like His hearing? No. Allah is All-Seeing and you see: is your sight like His sight? No. And as long as you believe that He has attributes like those in you, take them with respect to Allah within the frame of "ليس كمثله شيء".

As for those who interpret the intended meaning of "the Face of Allah" as His essence, and "the hand" as His power, and "يد الله فوق أيديهم" (the hand of Allah is over their hands) as His power above their power, we say to them: why these interpretations? If we take it as the Truth said about Himself, but within the frame of "ليس كمثله شيء", we have been spared error: we have neither likened Him to His creation nor emptied a text of its meaning.

Therefore the scholars who verify (al-muhaqqiqun) say: you believe in Allah as He has given you the image of faith in Him, but within a frame that does not differ from what is in "ليس كمثله شيء". And although you may imagine anything, your Lord is contrary to what you imagine, for whatever occurs to your mind, Allah, glory be to Him, is other than that. The human mind only conceives images known to it, and as long as they are images known to it, they are within the creation of Allah, and He, glory be to Him, does not resemble His creation.

When the Truth is manifested, He will surprise those who imagined Allah in any form: He, glory be to Him, is other than what they imagined, and Allah will come to them with a reality that was never in their minds. For if the image of the Truth were in the mind of humans, that would mean they had become capable of conceiving Him, and He who is capable is never made something over which one has power. Among His greatness is that the intellect cannot conceive Him materially. For this reason Allah set forth for us an example that brings the matter near, saying:

﴿And in yourselves; will you not see?﴾ (Surah al-Dhariyat, 51:21)

The spirit present in the kingdom of our body, which, when it leaves a person, he becomes a corpse and returns to decomposing elements and rising vapours — this spirit within each of us no one has been able to conceive, nor determine its place or shape. This spirit, created by Allah, we have not been able to conceive; so how can we conceive the Greatest Creator? "هل ينظرون إلا أن يأتيهم الله" means: with what did not enter their reckoning. Are they waiting until they see that orderly, marvellous universe effaced, and the whole universe scattered, and the sun wound up, and the stars dispersed, and everything in existence changed; and after that they are surprised to find themselves before their Lord? So what are they waiting for?

Therefore they must seize the opportunity before that matter comes, and before the opportunity slips from their hands and the time of their return to Allah ends. Why do they procrastinate about entering into submission completely? What are they waiting for? Are they waiting for Allah to change, or for the method of Allah to change? That will never happen.

We stress once more that when we hear something related to the Truth that resembles what occurs among humans, let us take it within the frame of "ليس كمثله شيء". Just as you have believed that God has an essence unlike essences, you must know that God has attributes unlike attributes, and actions unlike actions. So do not make the essence of Allah different from human essences, and then come to the attributes about which Allah spoke of Himself and make them like human attributes. If Allah comes, do not imagine His coming to be that He leaves one place for another; He, glory be to Him, is in a place without being absent from any place. That is greatness.

So when it is said, "إلا أن يأتيهم الله", do not suppose that His coming is like your coming, for His essence is not like your essence; and because people differ in their ranks, their actions differ, so if people differ in actions according to their ranks, and in attributes according to their ranks, the Truth is exalted above everything and every conception. Let us take everything related to Him within the frame of "ليس كمثله شيء": the action of your Lord differs from your action. Beware of subjecting His action to the law of your action, for your action requires treatment and a time that differs according to your capacity and power, whereas Allah does not do things by treatment such that He takes time for them, but He says: "كن فيكون" (Be, and it is).

It is as though the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, wishes to give us an image of the accomplishment in which human choice has no part to oppose, so He says: when the command comes, every power of a creature is dissolved from that command, and the command belongs to Allah alone.

"فِي ظُلَلٍ مِنَ الْغَمَامِ" (in canopies of clouds): there is something that shades you and there is something you take shade in. What shades you, you have no authority over in its shading you unless you see where its shadow is and go to it; and another thing you can handle yourself, like an umbrella you open in any place you want. The word "ظلل" (zulal) means that it conceals from you the source of light; therefore when Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, wished to depict this for us, He said:

﴿And when a wave covers them like canopies, they call upon Allah﴾ (part of 31:32, Surah Luqman)

That is: the great terror came upon them like a canopy encompassing them. So Allah wishes to inform us that the whole universe will be effaced and the terrifying matter, the grievous matter, will come upon you; the believer had been expecting it, and it will bring him coolness and peace, for he did not believe for its sake; but the disbeliever will be struck with the great terror, for he was taken by surprise by something that was not in his reckoning.

Compare the coming of the matter to one who hopes for it with its coming to one who does not hope for it. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, said: when these canopies and the angels come, the matter has been decided. When you hear "قضي الأمر" (the matter has been decided), know that what is meant is that the opportunity has slipped from people's hands; whoever has not returned to his Lord until now has no opportunity to return. An example of this is what the Truth said in the story of Noah:

﴿And the matter was decided and it came to rest upon al-Judi﴾ (part of 11:44, Surah Hud)

That is: everything has ended, and people no longer have the ability to turn back from what they were in. So Allah says: what are you waiting for? Are you waiting until this day comes upon you? You must seize the opportunity to return to your Lord before the opportunity of returning slips from you. "وإلى الله ترجع الأمور" (and to Allah all matters are returned), and at another place comes "وإلى الله ترجع الأمور" (and to Allah all matters are returned).

There is a difference between "تَرجع الأمور" with a fatha on the ta' and "تُرجع الأمور" with a damma on the ta'. It is as though the matters are moving on their own, and at another time they are driven towards Allah. The one who desires will return to his Lord of his own accord, for he is going towards the good that awaits him; but the one who does not desire, and who did not hope to meet his Lord, will be returned against his will: another force comes and returns him. Whoever does not come willingly comes fearfully.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 211:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says after that:

﴿Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them. And whoever substitutes the favour of Allah after it has come to him—indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

It is as if Allah did not burden the Children of Israel, and wants them to acknowledge against themselves what Allah honoured them with of earlier good. So when you say, "Ask so-and-so what you did with him," it is as if you only order the asking when you are confident, and that he will find no answer except what supports your statement. The Truth informs His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to ask the Children of Israel about the earlier good with which He overwhelmed them; and He, glory be to Him, knows that they, despite their obstinacy, will not be able to speak except in agreement with the matter that the Truth states, and it becomes a proof against them.

And Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, says: ﴿Ask the Children of Israel how many [We gave them]﴾. When you hear "kam" (how many) in a context like this, understand that it is a metaphor for reporting a great quantity, unlike "kam" by which you intend a question. You say: "How many times did you do such-and-such with so-and-so," "How many favours did you do for him," "How much did you neglect him," "How much did you honour him." Therefore, when you hear this "kam," know that its meaning is a great quantity, expressed in a way that indicates a number that cannot be counted.

﴿Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them.﴾ Indeed, the Truth wants to set forth for us an example like a person who eats your goodness and denies your kindness, and complains about you to another person; then you respond: "Did he not convey to you the complaint? Ask him what good I have done for him. I will not speak; rather I will make him speak." You say that only while confident that he cannot change anything.

Did He not split the sea for them? Did He not turn Moses' staff into a serpent? Did Allah not shade them with clouds? Did Allah not give them manna and quails? All of that Allah gave them; yet they did not thank Allah's favour, so His anger descended upon them. He seized them with years of drought and hunger, and seized them with lice, frogs and blood. All of that Allah did with them.

And when the Truth says to His Messenger, ﴿Ask the Children of Israel﴾, the address extends to the community of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. So if one of them comes to you, ask him: "How many signs did Allah give you, and you denied them, hesitated, and were obstinate?" ﴿How many clear signs We gave them﴾: "kam" indicates a great quantity; "min āyah" means a wondrous matter; and "bayyinah" means a clear matter that no one can overlook.

﴿Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them. And whoever substitutes the favour of Allah after it has come to him, indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ And how does a person substitute the favour of Allah? When the favour of Allah reaches a creature, it is obligatory for them to receive it with gratitude; the meaning of gratitude is to attribute it to its Giver, and to be ashamed to disobey the one who bestowed it upon them. If people receive the favour otherwise, then it has been substituted. For this reason the Truth says in another verse: ﴿Have you not seen those who substituted the favour of Allah with disbelief?﴾ Since they have substituted it with disbelief, disbelief has taken the place of faith. Thus what was required was that they meet the favour with faith, by increasing in nearness to Allah; but they substituted the favour with disbelief.

﴿And whoever substitutes the favour of Allah after it has come to him, indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾ One might understand that "severe in punishment" concerns the Hereafter, and perhaps some people are slow to believe in the Hereafter, or are people who do not believe in the Hereafter. Yet if the matter of punishment were limited to the punishment of the Hereafter, people would be made miserable by those who do not believe in the Hereafter, or who delay it, because these people spread corruption in the earth, since they do not fear the Hereafter and do not believe in it, or it does not occur to them.

Whoever believes that there is a coming Hereafter in which there will be reckoning is the one whose conduct will follow the requirement of that faith. As for the one who does not believe there is another day, the world suffers because of him. If Allah did not hasten some kind of punishment upon those who do not believe in the Hereafter or who delay it, people would be made miserable by these who do not believe or delay it.

Every community that does not turn to the method of Allah, and substitutes the favour of Allah with disbelief, must have an immediate punishment from Allah upon them. This is so that people know that whoever is not restrained by faith and fear of the Last Day must be restrained out of fear that punishment will come to him in this world. So the wrongdoer, if he knows that one like him met his punishment and reckoning in this world, will fear to do wrong, even if he does not believe in the Hereafter, because he will be certain that the reckoning is inevitable. For this reason Allah does not postpone all punishment until the Hereafter, but sends down some of it in this world. The Truth says about those who substitute the favour of Allah with disbelief:

﴿And they caused their people to alight at the abode of destruction, [Hell], which they will enter, and wretched is the settling place.﴾ (Surah Ibrahim)

This is the punishment of the Hereafter, and Allah will not leave them in this world without their receiving punishment.

Even those who wrong and act tyrannically while they are Muslims—Allah does not leave them without punishment in this world until they come to Him on the Day of Resurrection; rather, there must come to them from the reality of their worldly life what frightens people from such ends, so that the movement of life among all people is set right; otherwise misery will befall people from these and from those who do not believe in the punishment of the Hereafter.

Some of the righteous used to say: "O Allah, indeed the people have been slow regarding Your Hereafter, and Your forbearance has deceived them, so seize them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent." Because if He, glory be to Him, left their punishment for the Hereafter alone, they would corrupt and become a trial for others among the believers. For this reason Allah willed to place in the method of faith a criminalisation and a punishment that occurs in this world. Why? So that the corruption of one who doubts the matter of the Hereafter does not spread. And the severity of Allah's punishment He has not placed only in the Hereafter, but has placed it in this world as well; for this reason Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, says:

﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed for him is a constricted life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha)

Then the Exalted and Glorified says:

﴿The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve, and they mock those who believe. But those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And God provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾ (2:212)

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wishes to clarify the reality of man in the universe, a reality which indicates that he is the master of that universe, meaning that all species serve him. We know that the inanimate serves the plant, and the inanimate and the plant serve the animal, and the inanimate, the plant and the animal serve man. Thus man is the master of these species.

Reason requires that this master seek a species higher than himself. Just as the species beneath him serve him, so this higher species must be fitting to his mastery, and he will never find anything in existence higher than the species to which he belongs. Therefore it was fitting that man should say: "I want a species that informs me about myself, for I am in dire need of it." So when the messengers came and said: "The One who is higher than you, O man, is God, 'there is nothing like unto Him' and He is exalted above all species," it was incumbent upon man to say: "Welcome!", for knowledge of God solves the riddle for him. The messengers came only to solve for man a riddle he was seeking, and it was incumbent upon man to rejoice at the coming of the messengers. Especially since God, mighty and majestic, does not seek service from him; it is man who needs to worship God so that He subjects creatures to him, and worships Him so that He honours him. Thus the believer is between two matters: between a servant subjected to him, namely what is beneath him of inanimate things, plants and animals, and a bestower, generous and favouring him, who is higher than him. He is God.

So whoever takes one and leaves the other has taken the lower and abandoned the higher, and the Truth says to him: "Take the higher." If you are happy with the bounty of the creatures beneath you and wish to have more of it, how do you not seek more from the One who is higher than you? He is God.

When the Truth says: "The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve," He wants to draw our attention to the fact that the measures of the disbelievers are base and low, because what has been made attractive to them is the lower matter. It is a failure of judgement for a person to take the lower matter and prefer it over the higher. The word *zuyyina* (was made attractive), whenever it occurs in the Qur'an, is in the passive form (the form of the verb whose subject is not named), as in His saying: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: women, children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver...﴾ (3:14).

There is "*zuyyina lil-nas*" (made attractive for people), and in the verse of al-Baqarah under discussion, "*zuyyina lil-ladhina kafaru*" (made attractive for those who disbelieve). Why did the Truth say there "*zuyyina lil-nas*" and why did He say here "*zuyyina lil-ladhina kafaru*"? The Truth said that because those who disbelieve have nothing but the life of this world; the higher they do not believe in. But in the matter of people in general, when God, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires...﴾, He, glorified is He, is telling people: take life in its proper measure. *Zuyyina* means *husnina*, made good. So who made it good? God, mighty and majestic, made it good. How, then, do you forget the One who made it good for you, and made it beautiful and placed it under your control?

You should take it as a means to faith in the One who provided it to you, and whenever you see something beautiful in existence, say: "Glory be to God," and your faith in God increases. As for taking the matter and separating it from the One who created it, that is the base measure.

Or it may be that God, glorified and exalted, is the One who made them attractive by placing in people instincts that incline toward what this worldly life gives. And we say: has He, glorified is He, given instincts without giving a method for elevating those instincts? No; He has elevated the instincts and given the method for elevating them, so do not take this and leave that. Therefore the Truth says:

﴿And the enduring good deeds are better﴾ (18:46).

When the Truth says: "The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve," He exposes those who believe that there is no life after this life. We say to them: this is a base measure, an inaccurate scale, and a sign of folly, because you have gone to the lower and left the higher. It is strange that you have done this and then there are such contradictions between you and those who chose the higher. You are in the lower, and you mock those who turned to the higher. The Truth says: ﴿And they mock those who believe.﴾ Why do they mock them?

*[Editor's note: the following line in the source is a publication note and is not part of the commentary text.]* Review the original and its hadith takhrij by Dr. Ahmad Hashim, vice-president of al-Azhar University.

Because those who believe are committed, and as long as a person is committed he restrains himself from the movements of existence that come to him without restriction. But those people have rushed with all their powers and faculties toward what has been made attractive to them of life.

Thus you find a person living within the level of his lawful income, owning only one suit (*badla*), and another person who steals from others. You find that the second, who lives on the wealth of others, has a fine appearance and dress, and when the two meet you find the one who plunders mocks the one who lives on what is lawful. Why? Because he considers himself to be on a higher measure than him; he sees himself as well dressed and stylish (*al-shiyaka*). So the Truth settles this matter and says: ﴿But those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ Why the Day of Resurrection? Are they not above them now?

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, speaks of the visible view of people, because they do not look at psychological peace, which is the harmony of a person's faculties when he goes to sleep, and who has not tried upon himself a religious lapse or a moral lapse, who does not harm anyone, does not take bribes, does not slander or backbite. How would his state be when he reviews his day's deeds before sleeping? He must be in a happiness that cannot be measured by worldly wealth.

Therefore God did not introduce this sensation into the comparison, but introduced the matter that no one can control: ﴿But those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ So the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed, and when they passed by them they winked at one another, and when they returned to their families they returned jesting, and when they saw them they said, "Indeed, these are misguided," though they had not been sent as guardians over them.﴾ (83:29–33)

Then the Truth says after that:

﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, observing. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ (83:34–36)

That is, have we known how to repay them? We say: Yes, O Lord. Especially since the laughter of the Hereafter is not followed by weeping. ﴿But those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ Note that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, departed from the expected style in this verse. It would have been expected to say: "and those who believe will be above them." But He said: ﴿those who fear God﴾, because faith may be taken as a mere name. It may be well known about you that you are a believer, but with this description alone you will not attain the lofty rank unless your deeds lead you to God-consciousness (*taqwa*).

So do not say: "I am a believer" and another say: "I am a believer," and the believers become a billion people in the world. We say to them: you will not take faith by name, but you will take faith by adherence to the method of heaven. Therefore God did not say: ﴿Those who believe will be above them on the Day of Resurrection,﴾ but said: ﴿Those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection,﴾ to separate the name from the attribute. The Truth concludes the verse with the noble words: ﴿And God provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾

What is provision (*rizq*)? According to the people, provision is everything from which one benefits; everything you benefit from is provision. According to this definition, thieves consider the unlawful to be provision, but it is unlawful provision.

People restrict the word *rizq* to one thing that constantly occupies their minds, which is wealth (*al-mal*). We say to them: No, provision is everything from which one benefits. Everything whose sphere is benefit enters into provision: your knowledge is provision, your character is provision, your standing is provision, and everything you benefit from is provision. When you say that all of that is provision, take God's words:

﴿Those who have been favoured in provision do not return their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so that they are equal therein.﴾ (16:71)

It is as if God wants His creatures to share their provisions with others, and every person who is distinguished and has surplus must return it to people. But people understand provision only as wealth, and do not understand that it applies to everything from which they benefit.

If that is so, what is the meaning of ﴿He provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾? The phrase "without reckoning" must be understood as follows: reckoning requires a reckoner, one reckoned with, and that for which one is reckoned. On this basis, "without reckoning" means: from whom, to whom, and concerning what?

It is provision without reckoning from God. He may provide you according to your effort, and perhaps more; He provides without reckoning, because there is no authority higher than Him to say to Him: why did You give so-and-so more than he deserves?

He provides without reckoning because His treasuries never run out. He provides without reckoning because no law governs Him; He gives by the freedom of power. Exalted is He, He gives the disbeliever until you marvel and say: He gives the disbeliever and does not give the believer, why?

If anyone can call Him to account, let him ask why He does this. He gives seven hundred-fold for one good deed, without reckoning. Reckoning comes only when you take something countable: if you take, for example, a hundred from a thousand, you have subtracted a countable from a countable, so it must decrease, and when you see it decreasing you fear giving. But God is otherwise: He gives a countable without countable limit.

So when you read "without reckoning," say that reckoning, if it occurs from God toward others, means He does not give according to the work but increases it, and He will not reckon with Himself, nor will anyone reckon with Him.

﴿What is with you will be exhausted, and what is with God endures.﴾ (16:96)

Thus "He provides for whom He wills without reckoning" makes every person keep his manners if he sees another given more provision than himself, because he does not know God's wisdom in it. There are many people who, when God gives them a blessing, say: "Our Lord has honoured us," and when He takes away the blessing, say: "Our Lord has humiliated us." Concerning this, the Exalted says:

﴿As for man, when his Lord tests him and honours him and bestows favour upon him, he says, "My Lord has honoured me." But when He tests him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."﴾ (89:15–16)

No! You are mistaken, O you who consider a blessing an honour from God, and you are also mistaken, O you who consider the removal of a blessing a humiliation from God. A blessing is not an honour from God unless God grants you success in using it well, and a blessing is not a humiliation unless God does not grant you success in fulfilling its due. The due of a blessing in every case is thanking the Benefactor and not being preoccupied with it to the neglect of the One who provided it.

We also want to understand that the Exalted's words ﴿And God provides for whom He wills without reckoning﴾ extend to another meaning: He does not want you to estimate your provision by the reckoning of your work's movement alone, for the reckoning of your work's movement may err. An example of this is the farmer who plants and estimates his provision from what the land produces, but a blight may come that destroys everything, as we observe and witness, and the farmer's provision at that time comes from a place that never entered his calculation at all.

Therefore a person must work within the means, but he should not take the means as his reckoning and think that this is his provision, because provision may come by a way that did not enter your reckoning or your calculations. The Truth says concerning this:

﴿And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect.﴾ (65:2–3)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 2, verse 213:

After that, the Almighty Allah tells us in another verse what clarifies and explains the matter of the creed (aqidah) and the procession of the messages upon the earth, in its beginning, its succession and its continuity through messengers who followed one another. So the Almighty Allah says:

﴿Mankind were one community; then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners, and He sent down with them the Book with truth, to judge between people concerning that over which they differed. And none differed over it except those who were given it, after clear proofs had come to them, out of animosity among themselves. So Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ [2:213]

And one may say: If mankind were one community, and Allah ordained the sending of the prophets upon their being one community, then from where did disagreement come into people's lives? We say: This general verse must be understood in light of another, detailed verse, His saying:

﴿And mankind were not but one community, then they differed. And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them concerning that over which they differ.﴾ [10:19] (Surat Yunus).

It is necessary for us, then, to take this verse in the light of the verse of Surat Yunus. When the Almighty Allah addresses the human intellect, He wishes to address it in a way that awakens its mind and its thinking, so that it receives the words of Allah with the whole of its thought, and so that the entire Qur'an is present in your mind, each part serving the others.

(Mankind were one community; then Allah sent the prophets.) Before Allah sent the prophets, mankind was one community following Adam. Allah had conveyed the method (manhaj) to Adam after choosing him and guiding him, and Adam taught his children the method of Allah. So his descendants remained upon faith in one creed, and there did not arise among them anything that would necessitate the difference of their desires. The world was spacious, and its population consisted only of Adam and his children, and the good of the world was wide enough for all who existed. Thus there was no fighting over anything; whoever wanted something took it, and ownership was held in common by all, since no one had private ownership. Whoever wanted to build a house could build it, even on twenty feddans, and whoever wanted to eat fruit or take dates from any orchard could take what he wanted.

An example of this in our daily life: there is the head of a household who brings twenty kilos of oranges and leaves them in front of his children, and every child who wants an orange or more takes what he wants without hindrance. But if the head of the house buys one kilo of oranges, then each child takes only one orange.

So mankind was one community, meaning that greed did not exist, and the desire to monopolize benefits did not exist, which would have caused them to differ. Thus the foundation of disagreement is greed for the goods of this world, and from here desire arises.

It was incumbent upon Adam, peace be upon him, after Allah had conveyed the method to him, to convey it to his children, and for his children to accept the method. But some of his children rebelled against the method, and the desire to monopolize arose from the narrowness of the one who monopolizes and benefits from it, and from here disputes arose. In the story of Habil and Qabil there is what clarifies this:

﴿And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth, when they each offered a sacrifice, and it was accepted from one of them but not accepted from the other. He said, "I will surely kill you." He said, "Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous."﴾ [5:27] (Surat al-Ma'idah).

We know that Adam and Eve were the origin of existence. Eve would bear twins each time, and Adam wished to marry them off to one another. But how could the marriage be arranged when they were all his children and of one generation, and each of them knew that the one in front of him was his brother?

The Shari'ah addressed that problem at that time, and it considered that kinship is by the womb (batn), meaning that whoever is born with his brother in one womb is his brother, whereas whoever was born after or before him is as if not his brother. Therefore Adam and Eve would exchange the marriage of the children according to the distance between the wombs, and the purpose of this separation was that the woman would be as if a stranger to her brother.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both: "That Adam used to marry the male of one womb to the female of another, and that Habil wanted to marry the sister of Qabil, and she was more beautiful than Habil's sister, and Qabil wanted to keep her for himself over his brother. Adam, peace be upon him, ordered him to marry her to him, but he refused. So he ordered them both to offer a sacrifice.
