And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And God does not like corruption.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

If only this category, when alerted to this, would be restrained and return. No. When a sincere, loving, compassionate advisor says to him: *"Fear God,"* pride in sin seizes him!! The other category in society is the one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of God, which takes the form either of giving his life in battle and becoming a martyr, or of preserving himself in a way that brings good to the method of God. So He, glorified be He, said:

﴿And among the people is one who sells himself seeking the pleasure of God, and God is Compassionate to the servants.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

Then Al-Haqq spoke about entering into *al-silm* (peace) completely. Entering into peace, that is Islam, requires us to enter together into every kind of peace in life: peace with yourself, so that your faculties do not conflict, so you do not say a thing that contradicts your heart; peace with the society in which you live; peace with the universe that serves you, whether inanimate, plant, or animal; and peace with your nation in which you live. So He, glorified be He, said:

﴿O you who have believed, enter into peace completely and do not follow the steps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

All this shows us that when Al-Haqq created creation, He set for them the method that guarantees their safety and security in every stage of this life. So if you see a flaw or disorder in the universe, or you see fear or anxiety, know that one of the methods of Islam has been suspended. When the Truth, glorified and exalted, commands us to enter into peace completely, He warns us that if we slip from the method, then God is Almighty and Wise, none overcomes Him and none can prevail over Him. He is the Capable, the Strong, who runs everything with wisdom. So do not think that by slipping from His method you harm God; rather, you harm yourselves and the members of your own kind, because God cannot be overcome.

Al-Haqq, glorified be He, gives us another warning. He draws our attention to the fact that we do not control the Hour. The Hour comes suddenly and unexpectedly, a deafening, overwhelming, convulsive, shaking catastrophe. So beware lest this tremor strike you while you are heedless of it. All of this is so that we also enter into peace on the Last Day. It is as if the Truth, glorified be He, is drawing our attention to the fact that the words of the Qur'an are not mere theoretical words, but the words of the Wise, the All-Aware, which have judged the history of the nations that preceded the call of Muhammad (ﷺ).

How many signs did Al-Haqq send to the Children of Israel, and they hesitated, and what happened among them happened, and they brought misery upon themselves and the society suffered because of them. So the matter is not theoretical speech. God wants us to look deeply into the affairs of life and not to look at surface matters. The adornment of the worldly life must not deceive us from the Hereafter, because the life of this world is short in duration. We must measure the age of the world against our own lifespans in it, and our lifespans in it are short, because some of us die old and some of us die young.

Al-Haqq, glorified be He, shows us that He did not leave His creation without purpose. Rather, He sent them messengers to explain to them the method of God. People were one community united upon the truth until desires stirred in their souls. Yet, in His mercy, God did not leave them to their desires. Rather, the procession of messages continued among mankind, and whenever desires overcame them and corruption spread, Al-Haqq, in His mercy, sent a messenger to alert them, until the final Messenger came, whom God distinguished by the eternity of his method and made the values remain in his nation. The Muhammadan nation became the bearer of the trust of guarding the method that preserves the movement of life on earth, because the Truth, glorified be He, did not entrust any other nation with it. That is why the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was the Seal of the Prophets.

Then God alerted us afterwards that man's destiny, reaching the bliss of God in Paradise, will not come easily or smoothly. Rather, it is a path surrounded by hardships. So you must alert yourselves, train yourselves, and accustom yourselves to bear these hardships and to endure those toils. As the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: *"Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and the Fire is surrounded by desires."*²

Al-Haqq then bestows favour upon His creatures: He gave man, the vicegerent on earth, a mind with which to think, an energy that executes the plans of the mind, and a material universe before him that interacts with him in movement. The mind plans, and the energy executes in the created matter subjected to God. So all the tools of movement belong to God, and you, O man, have no right to create anything in them, except to direct created energies to work on created matter. You do not bring anything into existence.

After that, Al-Haqq asks you, O Muslim, to maintain the movement of life, by setting aside for the one unable to move a share of your movement. Therefore you must move in life with a movement that suffices you and suffices those you support, and suffices the one who is unable to move. In this way, you secure, for every incapable person, the heavens' protection through the movement of the believing brothers who move. He, glorified and exalted, reassures you that if you do this and secure the incapable, He will secure you when incapacity befalls you.

God, glorified be He, has made the state of life a sequence of turns among people. There are no people who are always capable, nor people who are always incapable. Al-Haqq makes those who were capable yesterday incapable today, and those who were incapable yesterday capable today, so that movement is distributed throughout existence. And so that each of us knows that God asks you when you are capable, in order to give to you when you are incapable. That is why He asked us to spend, and spending on others is not possible except after a person has met the necessities of his own life. So it is as if Al-Haqq says to you: you must move in life with a movement that suffices you and suffices you to spend on those you support. Otherwise, if you move only according to your capacity, you may not find anything to spend.

After that, the All-Glorified charges us that every believer must take responsibility for spending on the circle nearest to him, so that every person in life bears responsibility for a sector of society connected to him by a relative bond, such as parents and close relatives. And we should make orphaned weak ones a common responsibility of society, required of everyone, whether they are bound to us by kinship or not. They are all our relatives, because God has charged us to care for them.

But can God's method settle without anyone opposing it? Of course not. That is why Al-Haqq alerts us that we will find peoples who are not pleased that God's method be applied in existence, because they live only on the wrongdoings of people. These are people who will be displeased that God's method be implemented. So be wary of them. That is why Al-Haqq, glorified be He, enjoined fighting, so that we prevent the strife of disbelief from the earth, because disbelief multiplies gods in the universe, and every person will follow his desire, and his god becomes his desire, and gods will multiply with the multiplication of desires. That is why God prescribed fighting for the believers and said: *"and it is hateful to you."* All of this is to guarantee for us the goal He desires, which is entering into peace, safety, and Islam completely. After that, He asks us to strive with our wealth and our souls, and to leave our homelands and families if the faith-movement requires that. So He said:

﴿Indeed, those who have believed and those who have emigrated and struggled in the way of God—those hope for the mercy of God, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

Then Al-Haqq draws our attention to the summit of the planning apparatus in man, to protect it and make it a sound apparatus capable of planning with clarity, wisdom, and strength. This is the mind. He draws our attention to the necessity of keeping away from the mind everything that *yukhammiru* (clouds, numbs) it, that is, covers it from functioning. We keep away from it intoxicants. Why? So that the mind remains, as God wants it, the instrument of choosing between alternatives.

Since the mind is what plans for the energy within man to work on the matter in the universe, this planning mind must remain sound. A person must not try to cloud it, and no one should say: *"I cloud it because of the excess of problems."* No. Because problems do not require just one mind from you, but two minds. So do not come to your single mind to obliterate it with intoxicants. Facing problems requires that we plan with strong planning.

After that, Al-Haqq warns us not to take from the movement of others without sweat and without effort, so He warns us against *al-maysir* (gambling), which is easy gain. The warning against gambling came only to guarantee that every person moves in life with a sound movement in which there is no deception. It is as if all that has preceded is among the illuminations of His words: *"in this world and the Hereafter."* After that, the Truth, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿They ask you about orphans. Say: Improving their condition is best. And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers. And God knows the corrupter from the reformer. And if God had willed, He could have put you in difficulty. Indeed, God is Almighty and Wise.﴾ (Part of verse 220 of Surah al-Baqarah).

We know that orphans may not fall within the circle of the needy, but God alerts us that the matter concerning the orphan is not a matter of needing sustenance, but he needs us to compensate him, through faithful mutual support, for what he lost of a father. This prevents resentment towards children whose fathers have not died. When the orphan finds that all the believers are fathers to him, he feels the solidarity that compensates him for the tenderness of a father and does not suffer the look of pity with which he views his peers who, by the presence of their fathers, are superior to him. In this way, resentment is removed from him.

The early Muslims used to mix their wealth with the wealth of orphans, to ease for themselves and for the movement of the orphan the burden of work. If an orphan came under the guardianship of a person, and that person wanted to give the underage orphan an independent life, independent management, and an independent course in life, that would be hard on the man. That is why God permitted the guardian to mix his wealth with the orphan's wealth, and to make the movement of this wealth part of the movement of his own wealth, so that the guardian experiences no hardship.

When the saying of the Exalted was revealed:

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner.﴾ (Part of verse 152 of Surah al-An'am).

People became scrupulous and asked how they should deal with the orphan, especially since the All-Glorified and Exalted said:

﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies.﴾ (Part of verse 10 of Surah al-Nisa').

People withheld their hands from the affairs of orphans, and wan[ted]

Then the Exalted Lord introduces with us a new matter. If we consider it, we find it to be the foundation of every movement in life and in society: the matter of marriage. He, glorified is He, wants to secure stability and happiness for the being whom He honoured, made a khalifah (vicegerent) on earth, and made all the kinds subservient to his service.

The Truth wants that being to proceed from one methodical source, because conflicting desires are what corrupt the movement of life. So He wanted the whole human collectivity to proceed from one doctrinal source, and He wanted to protect that source from stumbling through the multiplicity of inclinations and desires. Therefore the Truth alerts us to this position. He, glorified is He, wants the soundness of the vessel in which that human being will come into existence, after marriage. Through marriage a human being is born, and life continues through multiplication.

Therefore, precision is necessary in choosing the source from which offspring come. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And do not marry idolatresses until they believe. Indeed, a believing slave woman is better than an idolatress, even if she pleases you. And do not marry [your women to] idolaters until they believe. Indeed, a believing slave is better than an idolater, even if he pleases you. Those invite to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission, and He makes His verses clear to the people that they may remember.﴾ [2:221]

The Truth says: ﴿do not marry idolatresses until they believe﴾. This is the first brick in building the family and building society, because if she is not a believer, what will happen? She will supervise the upbringing of the newborn child in a manner suited to her polytheism. Your task as a father and educator will not be accomplished except after a long period in which matters have been planted in the child. So beware that the man be a believer while the woman is an idolatress, because this disturbs the order of the family. The mother's work with the child affects the earliest formation of his character; it affects his values and the formation of his morals. This begins from the moment he sees and comprehends. The child spends his first years in his mother's embrace, and afterwards he grows up and is in his father's embrace. So if the mother is an idolatress and the father a believer, faith will not reach him except after polytheism has taken from him, become firmly established in him, and gained control over him.

We know that childhood in human beings is the longest childhood among all creatures. There is a childhood that lasts two hours, like the childhood of the fly, and another that lasts a month, but the longest childhood occurs in the human being, because this childhood suits the task that the human being will carry out. All the childhoods before it are childhoods whose task is very easy. It is the human being from whom values will come, so his childhood was long; it continues until the time of reaching puberty. The Truth is the One who says:

﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission as those before them asked permission. Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ [Surah al-Nur, 24:59]

So the child remains a child until he reaches puberty. How many years, then, will pass over the child? And how many years will this child be nourished from the springs of polytheism if his mother is an idolatress? It is a long period, after which it is not possible for him to be a believer whose faculties are not disturbed. And if such a person is made fit to be a believer, his faith will rest on coercion, compulsion, and the guardianship of the father, and such faith will be a formal process, not anchored or founded on a sincere basis.

We know that the fruits whose produce we enjoy do not ripen except when the seed from which a new tree is formed ripens, and before that they are merely unripe fruit with no taste. The Truth wanted to alert us to this matter, so that a person would take care to preserve the fruit until it ripens and has seeds.

A woman does not become a good fruit unless she bears, like herself, a righteous and beneficial son. The Truth wants the new generation to have sound faith; therefore He says: ﴿do not marry idolatresses until they believe﴾. That is: beware that you be deceived by the low, descending standards. Each of you must take the ruling of Allah: ﴿a believing slave woman is better than an idolatress, even if she pleases you﴾, because a person's admiration for a woman apart from faith will be admiration of short duration.

If we gather the moments of enjoying a woman's sensual beauty, their total will not exceed a month out of the total years of marriage. Every week a meeting takes place which may last minutes, and after that beauty fades, and values remain the controlling factor. We find that when a woman marries, and then conception is slow, she suffers in her heart, and so do her family.

If a man has married her for her handsomeness, her good looks, her figure and her eyes, all of this will cool down and calm after a period, and then other measures exist for sustaining life. When a person turns to her and does not find her, he drowns in regret, because she was not in his mind at the time he chose.

Therefore a woman wants to establish herself by having a child, to bind the man to her, and so that society says: "You must bear her for the sake of the children!" After marriage the man wants values other than the sensual values that arose at first. Therefore Allah warns us, saying: ﴿do not marry idolatresses until they believe﴾. The phrase ﴿until they believe﴾ came because Islam erases what came before it; once she has believed, the matter is settled.

Look at the precision of His, glorified is He, words: ﴿do not marry idolatresses until they believe, and a believing slave woman is better than an idolatress﴾. That is: the Muslim slave woman is better than a free idolatress. ﴿Even if she pleases you﴾: the Truth's speech here has come with the standards of sensual admiration, to draw our attention to the fact that we must not neglect eternal standards and take perishable, transient standards.

Then the Truth says: ﴿do not marry idolaters until they believe﴾. This is the counterpart in address, and it is not a mirror image, because He did not address believing women with the prohibition that they not marry idolaters. Rather He said: ﴿do not marry idolaters until they believe﴾. This is a precision of expression here, because the man has the guardianship over being married off (that is, the authority to contract), so He commands him by saying to him: "do not marry [them off]." But the woman has no guardianship to contract herself. We know the legal principle which says: "there is no marriage except with a guardian" (la nikah illa bi-wali), and He did not direct His address to the women, because a woman is governed by her emotions, but her guardian looks at the matter from a number of other angles that govern the situation.

It is true that we ask the virgin girl's permission so that we ensure her emotions are not obstructed from this marriage. But the father or the male guardian measures matters by other measures. If we left the girl with her own measure, the marriage would collapse as soon as her emotion calmed, and when other intellectual measures come, she will not find that marriage suitable for her, and married life will fail. Therefore Islam requires us to consult the woman, so that we do not bring her someone she hates. But the one who marries her to that man is her guardian, because he has the intellectual, social and moral measures which the girl may not consider. Her admiration for the young man may be dazzled by his stature, his good appearance and the attractiveness of his speech, but when the matter enters the movement of life and its turmoil, she may find him a man unworthy of her.

So that the matter is a blend of a daughter's emotion, a father's reason and a mother's experience, it was necessary to consult the girl, and for the father to be enlightened by the mother's opinion. Then the father states his opinion at last. Every marriage that comes about in this manner is a marriage that is granted success, because the standards are all shared, and no standard has gone wrong. The father has formed a judgement based on the daughter's consent. But if the girl refuses while the father's standards are sound, yet the daughter has no acceptance for this man, then this marriage is not valid.

Many marriages have failed because we have not found anyone who applies God's method in entering into marriage. When they do not apply God's method in entering marriage and then meet failure, they cry out calling upon the rules of Islam to save them.

We say to them: Did you enter into marriage according to the religion of God? As long as you have entered marriage by your opinions, detached from God's method, then resolve the matter by your opinions. Religion is only responsible for those who enter with its standards. But if you enter marriage with other than God's standards and then want God, or those who are in charge of God's affairs, to resolve your problems, that is an injustice from you to yourself and to those in charge of God's affairs. And if such problems did not occur, we would have accused God's method, and we would have said: "We have abandoned God's method and we are happy in our lives." Therefore it was necessary that problems occur.

So the saying of the Exalted Lord, ﴿do not marry idolatresses until they believe﴾, is a matter with a cause. But the lesson lies in the generality of its subject, not in the particularity of its cause. Its cause was what is related: there was a companion named Marthad ibn Abi Marthad al-Ghanawi, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Makkah to bring out some Muslims from it. He had been attached to a woman in the pre-Islamic period named ʿInaq, and she loved him. When she saw him she wanted to be alone with him, and he said to her: "Woe to you! Islam has come between us." She said to him: "Marry me." He said to her: "I will marry you, but only after I consult and ask permission of the Prophet (ﷺ)." When he consulted him, the saying of the Exalted came down: ﴿do not marry idolatresses until they believe, and a believing slave woman is better than an idolatress, even if she pleases you﴾.

It is also said that the saying of the Exalted, ﴿a believing slave woman is better than an idolatress, even if she pleases you﴾, was revealed concerning Khansa'(1), a black slave girl belonging to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. Hudhayfah said to her: "O Khansa', you have been mentioned in the Highest Assembly along with your blackness and your ugliness, and Allah has revealed your mention in His Book." Hudhayfah freed her and married her.

The Truth continues, saying: ﴿And do not marry [your women to] idolaters until they believe, and a believing slave is better than an idolater, even if he pleases you﴾. The standards are one in choosing a life partner. It is the desire to build family life on a basis of goodness. The purpose of everything is what determines its value, and not the means determines the value of a thing. You may travel a path that is dangerous but whose goal contains good, and you may travel a path strewn with roses and sweet herbs whose goal is evil. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿Those invite to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and forgiveness by His permission, and He makes His verses clear to the people that they may remember.﴾ Those who invite to the Fire are the people of polytheism. As for Allah, He invites to Paradise, and forgiveness comes by the permission of Allah, that is, by Allah's facilitation and success. We all know the wisdom spoken by the Imam ʿAli, may Allah honour his face: "There is no good in a good after which is the Fire, and no evil in an evil after which is Paradise."

The Truth's saying ﴿that they may remember﴾ recurs often. What does this remembering do? Remembering makes you feel that the matter was already known, and that heedlessness is what came upon you. But when heedlessness is alerted to it, it reminds you of what you had forgotten before. However, if heedlessness is prolonged and the origin is forgotten, that is the catastrophe by which the matter is obliterated.

So remembrance includes stages. The first stage: that you know if you did not know, or that you learn if you were ignorant. The second stage: that you remember if you were forgetful, or harmonise what you know with what you do. Remembrance inspires you to harmonise your knowledge with your conduct, so that you do not fall into ignorance, and ignorance means that you know what contradicts the truth. Allah wanted to protect the person who chose faith when He forbade him to marry one of the people of polytheism.

The Exalted Lord wants to secure for the one whom He made khalifah on earth one doctrine from which human conduct proceeds, because if doctrines are dispersed according to desires, conduct will be dispersed according to desires. When conduct is dispersed, the movement of life becomes contradictory and does not support itself.

Thus the Exalted Lord wills to secure the unity of doctrine without any influence affecting it. He therefore stipulated, in building the first brick of the family, that a believer not marry an idolatress, because in such a case the idolatress will take charge of raising the child for a long period, which, as we have said, is the longest of the childhoods of a living being. And if the father is a believer and the mother an idolatress, the father will be occupied with the movement of life, so most of the values that contradict faith will take root through the mother.

And He wanted

1 Al-Khans: a depression in the bridge of the nose with a slight elevation at the tip of the nose.

The Lord, exalted is He, then addresses the matter of intimacy with women during the period of menstruation, and the legislation comes to regulate this question, because Islam came at a time when there were two currents in society:

One current held that the menstruating woman is a woman who suffers from filth, so her husband may not eat with her, live with her, have intercourse with her, or live with her in one house, and neither may his children. Another current regarded the woman during her menses as an ordinary woman, no different from when she is not menstruating, meaning that she carries on her marital life with her husband without caution or restraint. The situation was thus oscillating between excess and negligence, so Islam came to put an end to this question, and the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an injury, so keep away from women during menstruation, and do not approach them until they have become clean. When they have purified themselves, then come to them as Allah has commanded you. Indeed Allah loves those who turn back in repentance and loves those who purify themselves.  222﴾

When you read "it is an injury," you have taken the ruling from the One who is trusted regarding the rulings, and you do not debate the matter, however much medicine may offer explanations, reasons and causes. Say to it: No; the One who created it said: "It is an injury." Al-mahid (menstruation) is used for the blood, and it is also used to mean the place of menstruation, and it is used to mean the time of menstruation.

The Truth's statement about menstruation, that it is an injury, prepares the mind to receive a ruling concerning this injury, and thus the mind is readied for the danger that the ruling will bring. The ruling of prohibition and restriction came after its rationale had been mentioned first.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, Who is the Creator, willed that the process of menstruation in the woman be a chemical process necessary for her life and for the life of reproduction. He commanded men to keep away from women when they are menstruating, because menstruation is an injury to them. But is menstrual blood an injury to men or to women? It is an injury to both men and women together, because the verse used the word "injury" without restricting whom it refers to. What indicates this is that menstruation brings filth to the man in a sensitive place, which is the site of ejaculation for him, so if microbes reach him they cause him serious diseases.

What happens is that the Truth created the woman's womb, and in her ovaries there is a specific, known number of ova known to Him alone, glorified and exalted is He. When one of the ovaries releases an ovum, it may not be fertilized, and then the lining of the uterus, which is composed of blood tissues, loses its proportion of the hormones that were holding the uterine lining in place, and when the proportion of hormones decreases, menstruation occurs.

Menstruation is blood containing non-living tissues, and the area of the vagina and uterus becomes irritated, because the vagina and uterus area is very sensitive to the growth of microbes that cause infections, both for the woman and for the man if he has intercourse with his wife during menstruation. Menstruation harms the woman in her strength and body; the evidence is that Allah permitted her not to fast and not to pray. So the matter is exhausting and tiring for her, and it is not permissible for a man to burden her more than she already is.

So His saying, exalted is He, "it is an injury," is a generalization that the injury afflicts both the man and the woman. Then the Truth explained that the word "injury" is a rationale that requires a ruling to follow, either permission or prohibition, and since it is an injury, it must be a prohibition.

He, mighty and majestic, says: "So keep away from women during menstruation, and do not approach them." Whoever says that "menstruation" means the place of menstruation builds his view on the claim that what is prohibited is sexual intercourse, but what is above the navel and above the clothing is permissible. So the Truth's statement "and do not approach them" means: do not come to them in the place from which the injury comes, which is the menstrual blood. "Until they have become clean, and when they have purified themselves, then come to them as Allah has commanded you." The word "yatahurna" (become clean) is from "tahur," the verbal noun of "tahara, yatahiru" (to be clean). When we reflect on His saying "fa-idha tatahharna" (when they have purified themselves), we find that He did not say "fa-idha taharna." So what is the difference between "tahara" and "tatahhara"?

"Yatahurna" means that menstruation has ceased for them, while "tatahharna" means they have washed themselves from menstruation. For this reason a disagreement arose among the scholars: can a man have intercourse with his wife as soon as the period of menstruation has ended and the blood has stopped, or must he wait until the woman purifies herself by bathing?

To go beyond the disagreement, we say: the Truth's statement "tatahharna" means they have bathed, so there is no intercourse before the bath. Among the marvels of the words of the Qur'an is that words influence the deduction of a ruling. An example of this is His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed it is a noble Qur'an, in a Book well-guarded, which none touches except the purified.  77–79﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah).

What is meant then? Is it meant that only the angels whom Allah has purified from impurity may touch it, or do humans also have the right to hold the mushaf because they purify themselves? Some scholars said: the matter must be brought under the general principle of purity, so the meaning of "except the purified" is those whom He has purified, meaning those for whom He prescribed purification. Therefore, when the Muslim bathes or performs ablution, two things have occurred to him: the act of purifying himself (tatahhur) and the state of purity (tuhr).

So the act of purifying oneself is in fact ablution or bathing, and purity is by the legislation of Allah. Just as Allah originally purified the angels, He has purified us, the human race, by legislation. In this way we understand the verse in its unrestricted sense and resolve the disagreement. As for the Truth's statement in the verse that we are reflecting upon: "until they have become clean" means until Allah permits them to attain purity, then they bathe in compliance with Allah's legislation for them to purify themselves. "Then come to them as Allah has commanded you" means in the lawful places.

"Indeed Allah loves those who turn back in repentance and loves those who purify themselves." The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, wished to bring you comfort: just as He required you to purify yourself physically, He also accepts from you that you purify yourself spiritually through repentance. So He brought the command both physically and spiritually. Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, brought a new ruling, which puts an end to a problem raised by the Jews.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 223:

The Jews used to spread the claim that if a man approached his wife from behind, even in her qubul (with the qaf vowelled with a damma), the child would be born cross-eyed (ahwal). Al-Qubul (القُبل) is the place of intercourse, and it does not mean anal intercourse, God forbid, as the people of Lot used to practise. Since this misconception raised by the Jews had no basis in truth, God wished to refute this matter and said:

﴿Your wives are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth as you wish, and send ahead for yourselves, and fear God, and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers.﴾ (2:223)

Indeed, God, glorified and exalted, makes room for enjoyment for the man and the woman in whatever manner they choose, on the condition that the act takes place in the place of growth. God used the word (ḥarth, tilth) here to make clear that tilling occurs in the place of growth. (fa'tū ḥarthakum, "go to your tilth"): and what is the ḥarth? The ḥarth is the place where plants are made to grow, and God, exalted is He, said:

﴿And He destroys the tilth and the offspring﴾ (part of 2:205).

So come to the woman in the place of sowing, the sowing of offspring. As for the place from which offspring does not grow, do not approach it. Some people mistakenly understood His saying (fa'tū ḥarthakum annā shi'tum, "go to your tilth as you wish") to mean coming to the woman in any place, and that is an error, because His saying (nisā'ukum ḥarthun lakum, "your wives are a tilth for you") means the place of the growth of crops, and the crop, for both the woman and the man, is the child. So come to her in the place that brings forth offspring, from whichever direction you wish.

God continues: (wa-qaddimū li-anfusikum, "and send ahead for yourselves"). That is: beware of taking the matter as mere sexual enjoyment. God, glorified and exalted, intends by this sexual pleasure to secure the hardships that arise from it, because the offspring that will come from the sexual union will bring hardships and burdens. Had God not linked it to this pleasure, people would have shunned intercourse.

Hence God links the toil and hardship of parents in raising their children with the pleasure of sexual desire, so as to guarantee the survival of the human species. Yet God also warns us not to regard this sexual pleasure as the primary purpose of approaching women, saying (wa-qaddimū li-anfusikum). That means: look closely at this matter, so that it does not become the goal; rather it is a means. So do not turn the means into the end. (wa-qaddimū li-anfusikum): that is, store up for yourselves something that will benefit you in the coming days.

Thus the primary purpose of the sexual act is procreation. (wa-qaddimū li-anfusikum): that is, do not take the fleeting, immediate enjoyment as the goal, but take it for what is to come. And how do we send ahead for ourselves, or what do we do? So that we are not made wretched by the one who comes. You must understand this process: send ahead for yourself something that will give you peace, and do what the Messenger of God (ﷺ) taught us. At the moment you come to this blessing and draw near to your wife, you must mention God and say: (Allāhumma jannibnī al-shayṭān wa-jannib al-shayṭān mā razaqtanī, "O God, keep Satan away from me and keep Satan away from what You provide me"). When the Muslim comes to his family and his child grows up, Satan will have no influence over him. Some scholars said: he cannot be affected by sorcery. Why all this?

Because at the moment you sow it, that is, plant it, you have mentioned the One who causes growth, namely God, mighty and majestic. And since you have mentioned the Creator who causes growth, you have given your son eternal protection. On the contrary, the child whose father forgets God when he approaches his wife will grow up and become prey to the devils.

(wa-qaddimū li-anfusikum): that is, send ahead for yourselves what gives you peace and what prolongs the span of your life and your deeds in this world. For when you approach the matter with the intention of having a child, remembering God and seeking refuge from Satan, the Creator will bless you with a righteous child. This child will pray for you, and will teach his children to pray for you, and their children will pray for you, and the matter will continue in an unbroken chain, so your deeds will not cease until the Hour comes. Here you will have sent ahead for yourself the best of sending ahead.

Suppose you were granted a child and he died, and you were struck with grief, said (inna lillāhi wa-innā ilayhi rāji'ūn, "to God we belong and to Him we return"), and sought reward for him with your Lord. You will have sent him ahead, and he will close for you one of the gates of the Fire. So in every matter you must remember (wa-qaddimū li-anfusikum).

God says: (wa-ttaqū Allāh wa-'lamū annakum mulāqūhu wa-bashshiri al-mu'minīn, "and fear God, and know that you will meet Him, and give good tidings to the believers"). The meaning of (fear God) is: beware of angering your Lord in any of these deeds. And be, O Muslim, in this God-consciousness, certain that you will meet God, and never doubt this meeting. As long as you fear God and are certain that you will meet Him, nothing remains for you except to be given the good news of Paradise.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 224:

After that, the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace between people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

In the verse there are three things. First: that you be righteous (tabarru), meaning that you do righteousness (al-birr). Righteousness may be disliked by a person because it is difficult for the self. Second: that you fear Allah (tattaqu), meaning that you avoid sins; taqwa (God-consciousness) may also be difficult at times. Third: that you make peace between people (tuslihu), meaning that you set right the state of relations (dhat al-bayn). Reconciliation between people may involve hardship, and that is after you refrain from making Allah an object of oath.

When the Truth says: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾, then 'urdah is the barrier, that which stands between two things. 'Urdah also means one who is fit for every matter; it is said: "So-and-so is fit (ʿurdah) for all important tasks," meaning suitable. And 'urdah, as we have known, is what intervenes between two things, as when a person places his hand over his eyes and does not see the light; here the hand is an 'urdah between the person's eyes and the sun. The person thereby shields himself from the light.

It is as if the Truth says: "I do not want you to make the oath an obstacle between a person and doing good, righteousness and God-consciousness." When someone asks you to be kind to one who has wronged you, you may say: "I have sworn that I will not be kind to this person." By doing so you have made the oath by Allah a barrier between you and righteousness. The Truth wants by this statement to alert us that swearing by Him is not permissible for preventing righteousness, maintaining ties of kinship, or reconciling between people. Whoever swears to something and then sees something better than it, let him do the better thing and expiate his oath. Why? Because the believer, when he swears not to do good, places Allah as a barrier between himself and good, and thereby he has contradicted himself by making the barrier the swearing by Allah. Allah is the One who commands righteousness, God-consciousness and reconciliation between people. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths﴾. That is, the Truth wants to protect the acts of righteousness, God-consciousness and reconciliation between people.

If you swear, O believer, not to perform these acts, the Truth wants you to break this oath and perform righteousness, God-consciousness and reconciliation between people, so that you do not contradict the legislation of Allah. When we find a society in which every individual performs righteousness, every person fears Allah by avoiding sins, and every person who sees a dispute between two groups reconciles it, is this not entering into Islam completely? So the Truth wants to preserve for people the springs of goodness and not to block them before themselves.

The Truth is the One who commands that the believer not make the oath a barrier between a person and righteousness, or between a person and God-consciousness, or between a person and reconciling people. Islam is lenient regarding retracting an oath and breaking it in favour of righteousness, and the righteous predecessors (al-salaf al-salih) said: "Breaking an oath is better than persisting in what is not righteous" (la hinth khayr min al-birr). Thus a society in which righteousness is practised, sins are avoided, and disputants are reconciled falls within the scope of:

﴿Enter into peace completely﴾ (part of verse 208, surah al-Baqarah).

A person may make any excuse to keep away from righteousness, God-consciousness or reconciling people, and may even do something that relieves him and makes him think he is obeying the command of Allah. Let us give an example of this. Our master Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, after Mistah ibn Uthathah joined those who spread the slander (al-ifk) by which they accused the Mother of the Believers, Lady ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

The summary of the matter is that ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, was the wife of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). She had gone out with the Noble Messenger on the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq, and the command concerning the hijab had been revealed, so ʿAʾishah went out in a howdah (hawdaj).

The Messenger carried out his expedition and the time to return came. ʿAʾishah lost a necklace of hers. She was light in weight, for food in those days was scarce. ʿAʾishah set out to search for her lost necklace, and when the people lifted her howdah they did not notice that ʿAʾishah was not in it. She found her necklace, but the army of the Messenger of Allah had moved away from her. She thought they would miss her and return for her. Behind the army was Safwan ibn al-Muʿattal al-Sulami, and ʿAʾishah recognised him; he made his mount kneel, and ʿAʾishah rode and returned to Madinah. The talk of the slander spread through ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the head of the hypocrites.

ʿAʾishah was afflicted with grief and sorrow for a long period, and the Truth made clear the falsehood of this talk. What was spread about the Mother of the Believers ʿAʾishah, who was the wife of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), spread before she was known as the daughter of Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr was the true friend of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Had something similar happened to someone other than ʿAʾishah, Abu Bakr's position would have been the same as his position when his relative Mistah ibn Uthathah joined in the talk of the slander with those who joined in it. Then Allah cleared ʿAʾishah and sent down the revelation that establishes the innocence of the Mother of the Believers in the slander. When Allah cleared her, Abu Bakr came, for he had been supporting Mistah, and he cut off his support and said: "By Allah, I will never support him again." Why? Because he had joined in the talk of the slander. The matter, on its surface, appears to be scrupulousness. So he refrained from supporting Mistah ibn Uthathah because Mistah had engaged in the slander. But look at the measures of perfection, excellence and virtues with Allah: the Truth made clear that this is one path and that is another path. The Most High says:

﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear that they will not give to the near of kin, the needy and the emigrants in the way of Allah; let them pardon and overlook. Do you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ (surah al-Nur, 22).

If you love that Allah should forgive you, will you not forgive the one who did a wrong to you? As long as you want Allah to forgive you, forgive people their errors. The Mighty and Majestic said this to Abu Bakr, because he took a position against a man who had engaged in the slander along with those who engaged in it, and yet it reached him that this was not correct.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous﴾. Do not say: "I have sworn by Allah that I will not do that good." No. Do it, for Allah is pleased that you break the oath and expiate it.

﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace between people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ Almighty Allah informs us: "I do not want you to make swearing by Me an obstacle or a barrier against doing good." For example, if someone asks you to be kind to a person who wronged you, do not say: "I swore I would not be kind to him because he does not deserve it." Then you would have made the oath by Allah a barrier to righteousness. It is as if the Exalted Truth wants to say to you: "No, I am lenient regarding the oath by Me; if you swear not to be righteous, or not to fear Allah, or not to maintain ties of kinship, or not to reconcile between two people, I have been lenient about the oath."

The hadith says: "Whoever swears to an oath and then sees that other than it is better, let him do what is better and expiate his oath." Thus Allah, glorified and exalted, protects the doing of righteousness, protects God-consciousness, and protects the acts of reconciling between people. And if you had sworn by Allah not to do them, why? Because when you swear by Allah not to act, and make Allah the one who prevents you, you have contradicted the legislation itself, since Allah is the One who commands righteousness, reconciliation and God-consciousness. So do not make the oath of mankind a barrier to implementing the methodology of the Lord of mankind.

﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle for your oaths that you be righteous and fear Allah and make peace between people﴾. If you swear to abandon an obligatory duty, you must retract the oath: break it and expiate for it. The same ruling applies to one who withholds his possessions, such as a beast, a machine or a car, from people's benefit on the pretext that he has sworn not to lend it to anyone; and this is something that happens often in the countryside.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, concludes the verse with the noble words: ﴿And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ He, glorified is He, is Hearing of the oath you have sworn, and Knowing of your intention, whether it is good or evil. So do not take the oath as a pretext to prevent righteousness, God-consciousness and reconciliation.

1 This hadith was related by Imam Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, from Abu Hurayrah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 225:

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, speaks of oaths (yamin), He gives us a foundational principle for judging whether an oath is binding (yamin haqq) or is mere idle talk (laghw). By the mercy of God, He, glorified and exalted, has taken into account only the oath upon which the heart has resolved, that is, the oath whose swearer intends not to break it. As for the idle oath (laghw al-yamin), God has overlooked it.

For example, the oaths that are common on people's tongues, such as their saying: "By God, if you had not done such-and-such, I would have done such-and-such to you," or "By God, I will visit you," or "By God, that was not my intention," or swearing on the basis of supposition, such as your saying: "By God, this happened," while you are not certain that it actually happened, yet there is no lie in your intention.

As for the perjurious oath (al-yamin al-ghamus), it is the oath and swearing in which you know it to be false, and you swear to the opposite of what you know, such as when you have witnessed someone stealing or killing and you swear by God that he did not steal or did not kill. For all of this, God, glorified and exalted, settles this matter with His saying:

﴿God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned. And God is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾ (2:225)

It was fitting that this verse should come after all that preceded it, because He, glorified, has made clear to us the oath that does not take effect, as if He were saying to us: "Retract it and break it, and I will accept your retraction in exchange for your being righteous, pious and reforming." If He has accepted our retraction from this oath, it is because there is a counterpart for it in doing good. His saying, the Truth: (for what your hearts have earned) carries the same meaning as His saying, exalted is He:

﴿But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have deliberately bound.﴾ (part of 5:89, Surat al-Ma'idah)

That is, the thing bound (ma'qud) in the soul and that has taken root within your self; but the thing that passes over the tongue, God does not hold us accountable for it. (God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths.) The word "ayman" is the plural of "yamin," and "yamin" means the oath or swearing. It was named "yamin" (right hand) because in ancient times, when they made pacts, each man would strike his right hand upon the right hand of his companion, and that is because the right hand is the active member (al-jarihah al-fa'ilah).

And by the way, regarding the active member, beware of thinking that it acts through exercise and training; rather, it acts by its created nature, that is, as God created it, so it is compelled to act according to its creation.

Therefore, when you find a person whose right hand does not work and who carries out his tasks with his left hand, do not try to make him use the right instead of the left, because your attempt is futile and will not avail; the reason he uses the left instead of the right is a natural, created cause. The mechanism in the brain that controls movement is what determines this matter: if it is created in the right half of the brain, the right hand is the one that acts, and if it is created in the left half of the brain, then the left hand is the one that works.

Thus you find that the one who writes with his left hand masters writing with it better, at times, than the one who writes with his right. From here we say that it is an error to try to change the behavior of one who works with his left hand instead of his right, because that is futile and will not reach a result.

Sometimes you find the mechanism controlling the movement of the hands located in the middle and center of the brain, so it sends balanced movements to the right hand and the left hand together. Therefore you find a person who writes with his right and left hands together, at the same speed and with the same proficiency, and performs tasks with ordinary spontaneity. God has manifold affairs in His creation. He thus gives us the proof that He is not bound by rules: He is able to make the right hand work, able to make the left hand work, or make both work together with the same strength, or make both hands incapable of working. It is not a mechanical process outside the will of God; rather, everything is subject to His will, glorified is He.

(God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths.) What is meant by it is the oath. The oath, among its meanings, is strengthening (taqwiyah), and it is derived from "hilf" (alliance), which is that people form an alliance upon a certain action. When we form an alliance upon an action, we divide the action among ourselves, and when we do so, it becomes easy for all of us to carry it out.

(God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned, and God is Forgiving and Forbearing.) And earning (kasb) is a voluntary process, because at the moment you swear by God without intending it, He does not hold you accountable, and this is evidence that God is vast in forgiveness and forbearing.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 226:

Then Allah the Exalted says:

﴿For those who swear off relations with their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. If they return, then indeed Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. 226﴾

Yu'lun (ي ؤلون): that is, they swear that they will not approach their wives for the specific act. A man sometimes wishes to discipline his wife, so he abandons her in bed without an oath and without swearing. Some people cannot refrain from their wives on their own, so they swear not to approach them, so that the oath serves as a restraint and an incentive for him to do so. This practice was familiar among the Arabs before Islam.

A man would withhold himself from intimacy with his wife for whatever period of time he wished. Some of them would swear not to approach their wife for a specified period, and before that period ended, he would swear another oath to extend it for another period, and so on, until the matter became a process of humiliating the woman, confining her, and withholding from her the fulfilment of her right to marital intimacy. This was a violation of the wife's right to enjoy her husband.

Allah the Exalted wishes to put an end to this matter, and He does not end it in favour of one party over the other, but by the justice of the Wise, Merciful Creator toward His servants. It would have been possible for Him to forbid it outright and prohibit people from it entirely. However, He, glory be to Him, knows the hidden things and the nature of human souls. A woman may seek to exploit a man's desire for her, either because of her beauty or to inflame his passion, and so she tries to humble him. Therefore Allah gave the man the right to refrain from his wife for four months; beyond that, a woman cannot bear for her husband to withhold himself from her.

﴿For those who swear off relations with their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. If they return, then indeed Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ Islam wishes to build married life on a realistic foundation, not on winged and unjust ideas that do not hold up before reality. It acknowledges inclinations and refines them, but does not demolish them; it acknowledges instincts and does not suppress them, but regulates them.

There is a difference between regulation (الانضباط, al-inḍibāṭ) and repression (الكبت, al-kabt). Repression leaves the disease an opportunity to spread in secret until it erupts in the impulses of the human soul, erupting unexpectedly and without precaution. Regulation, however, acknowledges instinct and acknowledges inclinations, and only tries to guide them, not destroy them. Humans in all their works follow this theory, even in their industry. For example, those who make steam boilers provide in those boilers, into which gas may be compressed so that it would explode, a vent so that excess pressure may be relieved if it occurs; and they may design within them an automatic system in which the mind does not intervene, but the machine itself governs.

Allah the Exalted established a clear system in His creation, and legislated for them the formation of the family on a sound basis. Islam built this system first on the soundness, purity and unity of belief, so that influences do not scatter among the components of the family. Therefore it forbade the Muslim man to marry a polytheist woman, and forbade the Muslim woman to marry a polytheist man. Then He taught us the meaning of instinctive union between the spouses. Allah the Exalted did not wish to let instinct run free at every time of marital togetherness, so He made menstruation a period in which intercourse is forbidden, and said:

(So keep away from women during menstruation.) (Qur'an 2:222)

Thus Allah regulates sexual relations between the spouses in a sound and clean manner.

Allah the Exalted knows that the human soul is subject to change, because man is a created being who has a beginning and an end, and everything created must undergo change. When a man and a woman meet, this meeting must be defined in the light of God's method, because if the meeting takes place according to human methods and emotions, the outcome will be failure, since human methods are changeable and temporary. Therefore the meeting of a man and a woman must be in the light of God's standards.

Allah knows that the soul has impulses and changing states, and it is very possible that a dispute arises between the spouses, so Allah the Exalted provides an outlet through which the husband may vent for the sake of discipline that seeks refinement and preservation. He legislated for a man, if he sees in his wife a humiliation to him by her beauty and her charm, and a man may have a particular temperament and an unbridled desire for this act, that for a period Allah permitted him to swear not to approach his wife. Allah did not make that period unlimited; rather He restricted it by the oath so that the matter would be regulated.

(Its original source was reviewed and its hadiths were takhrij'd by Dr. Ahmad Umar Hashim, vice-president of al-Azhar University.)

Thus Allah wants treatment, not harshness. If the man were not restrained by an oath, he might change his mind and come to his wife; therefore Allah said: ﴿For those who swear off relations with their wives, there is a waiting period of four months.﴾ That is, you, husband, have the right to swear not to approach your wife for four months, but if the period exceeds four months, it is no longer discipline but harm. The Creator, Mighty and Majestic, wishes to discipline, not to harm. Thus when the period is exceeded, the husband becomes a transgressor and has no right.

Indeed Allah the Exalted is the Creator of inclinations, emotions and instincts, and He legislates for them with sound legislation. He, Mighty and Majestic, leaves us that which guides us to this. In the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, Umar passed through the depth of the night and heard a woman reciting the well-known verses:

The night has stretched out and its sides have grown dark,
and sleeplessness has kept me from a companion I play with.
By Allah, were it not for fear of God's consequences,
the sides of this couch would have been shaken from its edges.

The meaning is that the woman suffers from loneliness for a man, and the suffering nearly drives her to improper conduct, but the fear of Allah is what prevents her from deviation. One may ask how Umar heard this woman while he was walking in the street. I say: a woman in whom these feelings arise sings in the stillness of the night, and when the night is quiet there is no commotion, so what is said inside houses is easy to hear. Did not Umar hear the speech of the woman who was arguing with her daughter about watering the milk?

When al-Faruq heard the words of this woman who suffered from loneliness for a man, he went, with his sound nature and his radiant insight, to his daughter Hafsa, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, and said to her: "How long can a woman endure the absence of a man?" She said: "Six months, or four months."

So Umar established a sunnah which later became a rule: that no soldier of the Muslim soldiers should be away from his family for more than four months. Thus the saying of Allah the Exalted: (For those who swear off relations with their wives, there is a waiting period of four months) preceded the incident of Umar; then Allah left it to the reality of life to show us the truth of what He legislated for us, and Umar came to deduce the ruling from the reality of life.

﴿If they return﴾, that is, if the man returns and wishes to approach his wife before the four months have passed, then the man may expiate his oath and the matter ends. But if the four months pass and the separation exceeds its term, the husband is ordered either to retract the oath or to divorce; if the husband refuses, the judge divorces her. Some jurists said that the passing of four months without his returning and resuming relations makes her divorced with one irrevocable divorce. Therefore Allah says: ﴿And if they resolve on divorce, then indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. 227﴾

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 227:

﴿And if they resolve on divorce, indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ [2:227]. The scholars differed: does the wife become divorced by an irrevocable (bà'in) divorce or by a revocable (raj'i) divorce? The meaning of "revocable divorce" (ṭalāq raj'ī) is drawn from the term itself, namely that the husband has the right to take his wife back (yurāji'ahā) without her permission or consent. As for irrevocable divorce (ṭalāq bā'in), there is no return unless he contracts a new marriage with her for a new bridal gift (mahr). In the case of the divorce resulting from an oath of abstinence (īlā'), the divorce is a minor irrevocable divorce (bayniwnah ṣughrā), which requires a new contract and a new bridal gift, provided that two divorces have not already preceded it. The major irrevocable divorce (bayniwnah kubrā), which is described as "the one of three," is one in which the wife is divorced three times; it is not valid for the husband to take her back unless she marries another husband, lives with him a complete married life, and then he divorces her for whatever reason. After that, her former husband has the right to take her back and return her to himself by a new contract and a new bridal gift, but only after he has been scorched by the jealousy of her marriage to another man. The Almighty and Exalted says, presenting this matter:

﴿For those who swear abstinence from their wives, there is a waiting period of four months. If they go back, indeed Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful. And if they resolve on divorce, indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ [2:226-227] (Surat al-Baqarah).

Islam is a realistic religion: it gives the Muslim husband things that release his anger, and things that enable him to discipline his wife, but Islam does not like the man to go to excess in discipline. If he goes to excess and exceeds the four months, we tell him: there must be a dividing limit.

Then the Almighty and Exalted turns, in the matter of obligations, to speak about divorce, having previously spoken about marriage and ila' (the oath of abstention from intercourse), until He arrives at divorce.

When we reflect on Islam's position on divorce, we find that it speaks in a realistic manner that suits human inclinations, for as long as we are changeable beings, events or feelings that were not in account at the time of marriage may befall the lives of the spouses. It is possible that a person, at the time of marriage, is driven by the intensity of a single faculty, and then, when the reality of life arrives, multiple faculties take possession of him. The sexual impulse may dominate him and drive him to marry, and in pursuit of satisfying his sexual desire he may neglect the rest of his soul's faculties. Then, when he enters the reality of marriage and the ardour and heat of his instincts subside, his soul becomes alert to other standards that he wishes to see in his wife, and he does not find them, and he asks: what has concealed them from him?

What concealed them is the frenzy and violence of the sexual outlook, for he looked at the woman before marriage from one angle only and did not look at the other aspects. For example, the husband may find that the wife's morals clash with his morals, he may find that her thinking and culture clash with his thinking and culture, and perhaps he finds an absence of emotional compatibility between him and her, and no psychological harmony has arisen between them, and emotions, as we know, have no laws.

It is possible that a man is unable to be content with a single sexual feast, so he does not build his life on chastity, but wants his wife to be pure and chaste in her life with him, while he gives himself the freedom to multiply his sexual feasts with more than one woman. Perhaps the reverse happens: a man finds that one woman suffices him, but the woman wants more than one man.

A man may be pure in his way of life while his wife wishes him to bring money from any source, and so they disagree. And a woman may be pure in her way of life and not accept that her husband earn from unlawful money.

From here discord arises. Discord comes when one of the spouses wants their life to be clean, pure and upright, and the other does not see that. Such a picture exists in the reality around us: how many homes suffer when the family unity disappears and one spouse's view of matters differs from the other's.

This is the cause of the discord that arises between spouses when one of them does not content himself with his companion. Had a man and his wife agreed upon chastity, purity and goodness, the affairs of their lives would have been set right. Therefore Islam brings its exalted legislation to suit all the circumstances of life, and the Almighty says:

﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual periods. And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs, if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands have more right to take them back in this [period] if they want reconciliation. And due to the wives is similar to what is expected of them, according to what is reasonable. And the men have a degree over them. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise. 228﴾

The whole verse contains legal obligations, and the first legal ruling is: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual periods﴾. We may note that the ruling did not come in the form of a command but in the form of a statement. He said: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual periods﴾. When the Almighty wants a binding ruling, He does not give it in the imperative form of command, but in the form of a declarative statement. This is firmer and more certain for the command. How so?

This means that when the Almighty commands, the command meets with compliance from those who believe in Him, and compliance is applied in every detail so that no case deviates from it, so it becomes a reality that is related rather than an obligation that is demanded. And since the command has become a reality that is related, it is as if the matter has become a history that is narrated. He says: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual periods﴾. It is also possible to take the verse in another sense, namely that Allah has said: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves﴾, so it is a declarative statement.

We have said that a declarative statement admits of truth and falsehood. Allah has said that, so whoever wishes to confirm the word of Allah should implement the ruling, and whoever wishes to defy Allah by denying Him and not believing Him does not implement the ruling, and he sees in himself the sign of non-belief, which is manifest loss. Is that not more binding than anything else? Similar to this is His saying, the Exalted:

﴿Evil women are for evil men, and evil men for evil women; and good women are for good men, and good men for good women. Those are free from what they say. For them is forgiveness and noble provision. 26﴾ (Surat al-Nur).

Although this is a declarative statement, it is an imperative legislation that admits of obedience and disobedience. Allah asks us that the matter be thus: ﴿Evil women are for evil men﴾, meaning that your Lord wishes that ﴿evil women are for evil men﴾ and that ﴿good women are for good men﴾. That does not mean that reality must be as the verse states; rather, reality will be so if we implement the word of Allah, and it will differ if we disobey Allah and rebel against His law. The same meaning is in His saying:

﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾ (from verse 97 of Surat Al 'Imran).

That is, make whoever enters the Sacred House safe. It is possible that someone disobeys Allah and does not make the Sacred House safe. Thus His saying, the Truth: ﴿And divorced women shall wait by themselves for three menstrual periods﴾ is a legal obligation that deserves implementation by whoever believes in Allah. His saying ﴿yatarabbasna﴾ means "they wait," and the expression here fits the context perfectly. The one who is divorced is the one who waits (mutarabbisah), and "divorced" means that she is disfavoured, and she waits and awaits the end of her waiting period so that she restores her standing by her fitness for marriage to another husband. The noble statement does not end with His saying ﴿yatarabbas﴾, but He said ﴿yatarabbasna bi-anfusihinna﴾ (they wait by themselves), although the one who waits is herself the divorced woman; that is because the conscious, responsible self and the self that commands to evil are in a struggle over the time, which is ﴿three periods﴾. ﴿Qur'ū'﴾ (qurū') is the plural of ﴿qar'﴾ (qar'), which is either the menstrual period or the purity between two menstrual periods. What does the Almighty mean by His saying ﴿three qurū'﴾?

Is it the menstrual period or the purity? It is the purity, because He said ﴿thalātha﴾ (three) with the feminine ta' ending. We know that the ta' comes with the masculine and does not come with the feminine, and ﴿ḥayḍa﴾ (menstruation) is feminine while ﴿ṭuhr﴾ (purity) is masculine. Therefore, ﴿thalātha qurū'﴾ are three consecutive periods of purity. The reason is the establishing of the womb's clearance and giving the spouses a respite in which to reconsider themselves, for perhaps after the first or second purity one of them longs for the other, and matters return to what they were. But if three purities pass, there is no hope or expectation of return.

Then the Almighty says: ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾. What is the meaning of "creation"? Creation is the bringing into existence of a thing that was non-existent, and this thing that was non-existent is either a pregnancy or a menstruation. For the pregnant woman there is a waiting period mentioned in the Almighty's saying:

﴿And for those with children, their term is until they give birth to their load﴾ (from verse 4 of Surat al-Talaq).

As for the woman who is not pregnant, who has no pregnancy, her waiting period is to menstruate and purify three times. There is a third case:

﴿And those who have despaired of menstruation among your women, if you doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated﴾ (from verse 4 of Surat al-Talaq).

That is, the woman whose monthly course has ceased has a waiting period of ﴿three months﴾. The same ruling applies to the young girl who has not yet menstruated, that is, her waiting period is three months. Thus the system of waiting periods has cases:

* If she is not pregnant, her waiting period is three qurū', that is three purities, if she is of those who menstruate.

* If she is pregnant, her waiting period is to give birth to her load.

* If she is not pregnant and has reached the age of despair and no longer menstruates, or is a young girl who has not reached the age of menstruation, both of these have a waiting period of three months.

The Almighty's saying ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾ indicates that the woman has her own testimony concerning the matter that pertains to her and that no one else can witness. She is the one who determines the matter herself, saying: "I am pregnant" or otherwise, and she must not conceal that, for it may be that she is pregnant and afterwards conceals what is in her belly so that she does not have to wait the full length of the pregnancy and marries another man, so that the child is attributed to someone other than his father. Pregnancy usually continues for nine months, but there are exceptions: there is a pregnancy of seven months, and sometimes six months. A woman who has been divorced may marry after three months and claim that she is pregnant by the new husband, and that her pregnancy lasted only seven or six months.

Some of us know the story of the woman who was pregnant for six months. They brought a woman to our master 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, because she had given birth after six months, and he wished to impose the hadd (prescribed punishment) for fornication upon her. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Imam, intervened and said: "How can you impose the hadd upon her, since she gave birth after six months? Have you not read the saying of the Truth, the Almighty?" 'Uthman said: "And what did the Truth say about that?" The Imam then recited Allah's saying:

﴿And mothers breastfeed their children for two complete years﴾ (from verse 233 of Surat al-Baqarah).

That is, she nurses the infant for a period of twenty-four months. In another verse the Truth says:

﴿His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning is thirty months﴾ (from verse 15 of Surat al-Ahqaf).

If we take from the first verse twenty-four months, which is the period of nursing, and subtract it from the thirty months that combine pregnancy and nursing in the second verse, we understand that pregnancy may be six months. Here our master 'Uthman said in astonishment: "By Allah, I had not realised this."

Thus a six-month pregnancy is possible, and from here we understand the wisdom in the Almighty's saying: ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾, so that a woman does not claim that she is not pregnant, marry another man, and attribute to him a child that is not his offspring, which entails more than one problem, among them that the child would not inherit from the first father, and that his unmarriageable relatives would no longer be unlawful to him; his paternal sister would no longer be his sister, and likewise his paternal aunts and maternal aunts, and the balances would be overturned. This is on the side of the original father.

As for the side of the second husband, the child acquires unlawful rights: he will inherit from him, and the unmarriageable relatives of the second man become his unmarriageable relatives, so he enters upon them without right and sees their nakedness, and illegitimate intermingling occurs.

Thus the Truth's saying ﴿And it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs﴾ is a statement by which the Truth wishes that life be founded on purity, honour and chastity, and that no one transgress upon the rights of another. This concerns pregnancy. What then is the case regarding menstruation?

Likewise, it is not lawful for her to conceal her menstruation in order to prolong the waiting period with her husband. The Truth says: ﴿if they believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾. What is the connection of belief here with the legal ruling? It is a firm connection, because pregnancy or menstruation are hidden matters that no apparent law governs; what governs them is the act of faith, and therefore it was said: "The unseen is guarded only by the unseen," and since the thing is hidden, it will be guarded only by the supreme Unseen, who is God, the Exalted.

The Truth continues: ﴿And their husbands have more right to take them back in this [period]﴾. The ba'l (بعل) is the husband, and he is the lord, master and owner. During the period of waiting, the husband has more right to take back his wife into his marriage. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And their husbands have more right to take them back﴾, does that mean there are people who could share with the husband in the taking back? Since the Truth used the word ﴿aḥaqq﴾ (more right), and on its apparent sense it would give the right to non-husbands to take back? No; rather the meaning is that no one here has a right except the husband. Taking back during the waiting period is the husband's right, so the wife may not say "no," nor may the wife's guardian say "no." If the husband wishes to take back his wife and she refuses and declines, his wish must be preferred and given precedence over hers, and he is more entitled than her, and her word is not considered, for she has no right in this matter, having first consented to it. But if the waiting period has ended, the situation differs: a guardian is required, a new contract and a new dower are required, and the wife's consent is a condition.

﴿And their husbands have more right to take them back in this [period] if they want reconciliation﴾. This is "if they want reconciliation." Intention is an unseen act, so this is in effect a warning to the spouses: the legislation permits them to return, but if the husband wants to take her back in order to harm her...

Al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66), on surah 2, verse 229:

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿Divorce is twice; then either retention in kindness or release with good treatment. It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon either of them for what she gives up to be released. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah – it is those who are the wrongdoers.﴾ [2:229]

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, speaks about divorce after having spoken about the divorced woman in her waiting period and how she may be taken back and reconciled. He, glorified is He, speaks about divorce in itself, and divorce (talaq) is derived from release (inlaq) and liberation (tahharur). It is as if it unties a knot that existed, which is the knot of marriage (nikah). The knot of marriage is the bond that God made a strong contract, the solemn covenant, and the Exalted said:

﴿And they have taken from you a solemn covenant﴾ [Surat an-Nisa']

It is a solemn covenant because it makes lawful for each spouse the intimate parts of the other, whereas He did not call faith a solemn covenant; He said of it only "covenant" (mithaq). So it is as if the covenant of marriage is more severe than the covenant of faith. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, wants to train people to solve problems by the easiest means. Therefore He legislated for us that the knot of marriage may be undone, and the ending of a knot is not like its beginning; it is not radical.
