﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, "Are those who know equal to those who do not know?" Only they will be reminded who are people of understanding.﴾ 9 (Surat al-Zumar).

The Almighty instructs His Messenger (ﷺ) to convey to us, the Muslims who believe in his message, that we should compare the one who humbles himself before God during the night, spending it standing and prostrating, hoping for the mercy of his Lord, with the one who calls upon his Lord in adversity and forgets Him in prosperity. Are those who know the rights of God, so that they obey Him and affirm His oneness, equal to those who do not know, so that they neglect reflection and contemplation of the evidences of God's power? The path to remembering God is renewing one's connection with Him and standing before Him, establishing the prayer.

We receive the command to establish the prayer even in the midst of fighting. Therefore, the prayer of fear (ṣalāt al-khawf) was legislated for us. Fighting is the matter that takes a person out of his path of security, so He, glorified be He, says: ﴿But if you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding﴾. Even in the midst of fighting and fear, we do not forget the remembrance of God, for we are most in need of God while confronting the enemy. Therefore it is not proper that the reason which requires us to be with God should become a justification for forgetting God.

Likewise the sick person: as long as he is sick, he is still in the companionship of God, so it is not proper for him to cease the prayer, for there is no excuse for abandoning it. Even if the sick person cannot pray standing, he prays sitting; if he cannot pray sitting, he prays lying on his side, and the ruling continues with him even if he is compelled to pray with the movement of his eyelids. Likewise, if you fear your enemy, pray on foot, meaning walking on your feet, or riding. The word "rijālan" is the plural of "rājil," that is, one who walks on his feet. An example of this is the Almighty's saying:

﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep, distant mountain pass.﴾ 27 (Surat al-Hajj).

People used to perform the obligation of pilgrimage walking on foot, or riding on camels made lean by travel, from every distant place. So the rājil is one who walks on his feet. The feet are created to carry the human being: the one standing among them is carried by them, and they also move the one who moves. If a person is standing, his legs carry him; if he is walking, his legs move. The point here is that prayer is obligatory on believers, whether they are walking on their feet or riding.

God, glorified and exalted, has explained this matter in the prayer of fear by dividing the Muslims into two groups: one group prays with the Prophet (ﷺ) in the first rak'ah, then they complete the prayer on their own, and the other group comes to pray behind the Messenger in the following rak'ah, until the prayer ends for the Messenger (ﷺ). He waits for them until they finish their prayer, and then he gives the salutation with them. Thus the first group took the merit of beginning the prayer with the Messenger, and the other group took the merit of finishing the prayer with the Messenger (ﷺ). This took place at the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa', where each of the two groups stood facing the enemy as a guard during the prayer of the other group.

My view on this matter is that the prayer of fear, in the forms mentioned by the jurists, was for the battles in which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was present, because it is not proper for one army to pray behind the Prophet (ﷺ) while the rest are prevented from praying behind him. Therefore God made the blessing of praying with the Messenger available to both groups.

However, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) departed to the Highest Companion, it is possible for those standing before the enemy to have one imam and the others to have another imam. Thus the division of the prayer behind the imam in the prayer of fear was only because the imam was the supreme Imam, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). God did not wish to bar one group from praying with the Messenger in favour of another, so He divided the single prayer between them. But in our present time, when affairs have become orderly and all people are equal, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is no longer among us, it is valid for each congregation to pray with an imam of its own.

As for the Almighty's words, ﴿But if you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding﴾, we understand from it that the prayer does not lapse even at the moment of meeting the enemy. So when the time for prayer comes, the believer must pray it if he is able; if he is not able, let him say the takbir twice(1) and continue. The Almighty then says: ﴿So remember God as He has taught you that which you did not know﴾, meaning: remember God for having taught you things you did not know. For if He had not taught you, what would you have been doing?

1 See Tafsir al-Qurtubi on the noble verse 239 of Surat al-Baqarah.

Then he returns to the family and to the woman whose husband has died, saying:

﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind should bequeath to their wives a provision for a year, without their being turned out. But if they leave, there is no blame on you for what they do with themselves within what is reasonable. And Allah is Almighty, All-Wise.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah).

So Allah, glorified and exalted, separated with a verse, "Maintain the prayers..." (﴿Maintain the prayers...﴾), a single matter, the matter of separation between spouses, and divided it into two parts. He placed between them the discussion of prayer, to alert us to the unity of the faith-based obligations. Since the Truth speaks about matters whose every aspect is either a chosen discord through divorce, or a decreed parting through death, Allah, glorified and exalted, wanted the person to enter into the act of worship that connects him to Allah, who legislated divorce and prayer and decreed death.

Why did Allah choose prayer over the other acts of worship to interrupt the context of the legislation on divorce and separation? Because prayer is what grants believers tranquility, when matters of marriage and divorce distress them and concern them, whether in the discord of divorces that have occurred or the hardship of separation by death. Their hearts will only be steadied by standing before their Lord to perform the prayer. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the first to do this: whenever a matter distressed him, he would stand to pray.

The believer goes to the Creator, who arranged for him the causes of marriage, divorce and separation, to ask Him to relieve his worry and grief. Since the believer has chosen to go to the One who directs destinies, he should know that Allah, who directs those destinies upon him, has not left them without rulings. Rather, He placed for every matter a fitting judgment. The believer's duty is only to accept the matters of destiny with contentment, and then to go to Allah obediently, humbly and in prayer. For the matter, whether divorce or death, contains fear and separation, whether a chosen separation or the decreed separation of death.

Then comes His saying, exalted be He: (﴿Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer﴾). We understand that what is meant in the verse is the five daily prayers. So what is meant by the middle prayer?

Sometimes a particular and a general matter come together, as in His saying:

﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women, and do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.﴾ (Surat Nuh).

How many times is the father included here? He is included in His saying, "forgive me and my parents," and in His saying, "whoever enters my house," and in His saying, "the believing men and believing women." That is, he is included three times.

So the placing of the general after the particular means that the particular enters into the general, so the command concerning the particular is repeated in a manner suited to its particularity.

His saying, exalted be He, (﴿Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer﴾), conveys this meaning. If we ask: what is the meaning of "maintain"? The answer requires us to understand that we have "preserving" (ḥifẓ), which is opposed to "forgetting," and "preserving" is opposed to "neglecting" (taḍyīʿ). The two meet: whoever preserves something and forgets it has neglected it. Whoever preserves wealth and then squanders it has also neglected it. So all these meanings meet in the loss of a thing. Preserving means that you guarantee the continuance of something you possess. If you memorize a verse of the Qur'an, you must keep it in yourself, and if Allah has blessed you with wealth, you must safeguard it.

His saying, (﴿Maintain the prayers﴾), means: do not neglect them. It may also carry another meaning, namely that you have tasted the sweetness of prayer in nearness to the company of your Lord, and that is more fitting and more deserving that you hold to it more firmly. This statement applies to the five prayers that we know.

His saying, exalted be He, (﴿and the middle prayer﴾), is a mention of the particular after the general, as if Allah commanded the preservation of that particular twice: once within the sphere of the general, and once more singled out by Allah for its specificity. What is the reason here for singling out the middle prayer? The word "wusṭā" is the feminine of "awsaṭ," and "awsaṭ" and "wusṭā" mean the matter between two things in balance, that is, the two sides are equal. The two sides cannot be equal in number among the five prayers unless the prayers are odd (witr), that is, single. For if they were even, we would not know which is the middle among them. Since the intended meaning is the middle of the five, it is the third prayer, preceded by two prayers and followed by two, if you count by the order of the first, second, third, fourth and fifth.

If the consideration is the legislation of the prayer, the first prayer Allah, mighty and majestic, made obligatory is the Ẓuhr prayer. This is the first obligation, then ʿAṣr, then Maghrib, then ʿIshāʾ, then Fajr. If the middle is taken according to legislation, it is the Maghrib prayer, and this is an opinion held by many scholars.

If the middle is taken according to the number of rakʿahs (units) of the prayer, you will find that there is a prayer of two rakʿahs, which is the Fajr prayer, a prayer of four rakʿahs, which is Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr and ʿIshāʾ, and a prayer of three rakʿahs, which is Maghrib. The middle among them is the three-rakʿah prayer, which lies between the even and the four-part prayer, so it is also the Maghrib prayer. If you take it in relation to the day, Ṣubḥ (Fajr) is the beginning of the day, then Ẓuhr after it, then ʿAṣr, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, so the middle is ʿAṣr.

If you take it as the middle between the audible and the silent prayers, it may be either the Fajr prayer or the Maghrib prayer, because the silent prayers are Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, and the audible ones are Maghrib, ʿIshāʾ and Fajr. Between ʿIshāʾ and Ẓuhr comes the Fajr prayer, or the Maghrib prayer, considering that it falls between Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr on one side, and ʿIshāʾ and Fajr on the other.

If you take it because the angels gather in it, since they are at the two ends of the day and the night, that means the ʿAṣr prayer or the Fajr prayer. So the middle comes from the consideration by which you reckon it, whether it is by number or by legislation, or by the number of rakʿahs, or silent or audible, or according to the descent of the angels of day and night. Each of these considerations carries its own ruling.

Why did Allah conceal its identity from us? We say: He concealed it so that each of us would be alert and would know that there is a difference between a thing in itself and a thing that is left vague in relation to others, so that each prayer becomes "the" prayer, which leads to the preservation of all the prayers. Since the middle prayer may be Fajr, Ẓuhr, ʿAṣr, Maghrib or ʿIshāʾ, this is more conducive to preserving all the prayers. The vagueness of the thing has come to spread its clarification. For this reason Allah also concealed the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr), for the same reason and the same cause: instead of being one night of power, it became nights of power.

Likewise, His saying, (﴿Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer﴾), means: the five prayers in general, and each prayer has its own particular characteristic. The Truth, glorified, wants us to stand for each prayer while devoutly obedient (qānitīn). The clear command is (﴿and stand before Allah devoutly obedient﴾), and the root meaning of qunūt in the language is persistence in a thing. The Noble Qur'an has urged and encouraged the constancy of obedience to Allah and the adherence to humility and submission, as we see in the saying of the Noble Truth:

﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, taking heed of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only the people of understanding take heed.﴾ (Surat al-Zumar).

The Truth, glorified, conveys to His Messenger (ﷺ) so that he may convey to us, the Muslim believers in his message, that we should compare the one who humbles himself before Allah during the night, passing it standing and prostrating, hoping for the mercy of his Lord, with the one who calls upon his Lord in hardship and forgets Him in ease. Are those who know the rights of Allah, so that they obey and affirm His oneness, equal to those who do not know, so that they neglect reflection and contemplation of the proofs of Allah's power? The way to the remembrance of Allah is the renewal of one's connection to Him and standing before Him, establishing the prayer.

We receive the command to establish prayer even in the midst of battle. Therefore the prayer of fear was legislated for us. Fighting is the situation that takes a person out of the path of his security, so He, glorified, says: (﴿If you fear, then on foot or riding﴾). Even in the midst of battle and fear we do not forget the remembrance of Allah, for we are most in need of Allah while facing the enemy. Therefore it is not right to make the cause that obliges us to be with Allah a justification for forgetting Allah.

Likewise the sick person: as long as he is sick, he is still in the company of Allah, so it is not right for him to cut off prayer, for there is no excuse for abandoning it. Even the sick person, if he cannot pray standing, prays sitting; if he cannot sit, he prays lying on his side, and the matter continues with him even if he must pray with the movement of his eyelids. Likewise, if you fear your enemy, pray on foot (rijālan), that is, walking on your feet, or riding (rukbānan). Rijālan is the plural of rājil, one who walks on his feet. An example of this is the saying of the Truth:

﴿And proclaim to the people the pilgrimage; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every deep mountain pass.﴾ (Surat al-Hajj).

People used to perform the obligation of pilgrimage on foot or riding on camels made lean by the journey, coming from every distant place. So the rājil is one who walks on his feet. The feet were created to carry the children of Adam: the standing among them, and they move the moving among them. If a person is standing, his two legs carry him, and if he is walking, his two legs move. The meaning here is that prayer is obligatory on believers, whether walking on their feet or riding.

Allah, glorified and exalted, explained this matter in the prayer of fear by dividing the Muslims into two groups: one group prays with the Prophet, peace be upon him, in the first rakʿah, then they complete the prayer alone, and the other group comes to pray behind the Messenger in the rakʿah that follows, until the prayer ends for the Messenger, (ﷺ), and he waits for them until they finish their prayer and gives the salutation with them. Thus the first group takes the excellence of beginning the prayer with the Messenger, and the other group takes the excellence of completing the prayer with the Messenger (ﷺ). This happened in the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa', and each of the two groups stood facing the enemy as guards during the prayer of the other group.

My opinion on this matter is that the prayer of fear in the forms the jurists have mentioned was only for the battles in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was present, because it is not right for one army to pray behind the Prophet (ﷺ) while the rest are prevented from praying behind him. Therefore Allah made the blessing of praying with the Messenger of Allah available to both groups.

But when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed to the Highest Companion, it is possible that there could be an imam for those standing before the enemy and another imam for the others. So the division of prayer behind the imam in the prayer of fear was only because the imam was the Supreme Imam, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah did not will to keep one people from praying with the Messenger while another people prays with him, so He divided the one prayer between them. But in our present time, when affairs have become organized and all people are equal, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is no longer among us, it is therefore permissible for each congregation to pray with its own imam.

As for the Truth's saying, (﴿If you fear, then on foot or riding﴾), we understand from it that the prayer is not dropped even at the meeting with the enemy. If the time of prayer comes, the believer must pray it if he is able; if he is not able, he should say the takbīr twice.(1) Then the Truth continues, saying: (﴿Then remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know﴾), that is, remember Allah for having taught you things you did not know. For if He had not taught you, what would you have been doing?

1 See the tafsir of al-Qurtubi on this noble verse, number 239, Surat al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 240:

Then, after that, the Truth (al-Haqq) returns to the context of discussion concerning the woman whose husband has died, saying:

﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind—a bequest for their wives: provision for a year without being turned out. But if they leave, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable. And Allah is Mighty, Wise.﴾ [2:240]

In an earlier verse, the Truth said:

﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind—they shall wait with themselves for four months and ten days. Then when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And Allah is Aware of what you do.﴾ [2:234] (Surat al-Baqarah).

So we are before two rulings concerning those who die and leave wives behind: the ruling that she waits for herself four months and ten days, and another ruling that, when death or its causes or its precursors come upon the husband, he may advise and bequeath that the wife remain in his house for a full year without being expelled. The four months and ten days are an obligation (fard), and the remainder of the year is a bequest (wasiyyah): if she wishes she takes it, and if she wishes she sets it aside.

(﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind—a bequest for their wives﴾) This is a bequest from the husband when death approaches him.

Thus the woman whose husband has died stands between two rulings: a binding ruling, which is an obligation upon her to remain four months and ten days, and a ruling by which the husband bequeaths that she remain a full year without being turned out, unless she leaves of her own accord. And (﴿without being turned out﴾) means that no one expels her. (﴿But if they leave, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves of what is reasonable. And Allah is Mighty, Wise.﴾) She has the choice to remain for a year according to her husband's bequest, and she has the choice to leave after the four months and ten days.

And Allah says after that:

﴿And for the divorced women is a provision in kindness, a duty upon those who are conscious of Allah.﴾ [2:241]

Every divorced woman, in whatever form her divorce takes, has a provision (mata'). But He, glory be to Him, has explained the provision in each case, as evidence of which He made clear to us: if you have not specified a bridal payment (fareedah) for them, then ﴿provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means﴾ [2:236]. And if you have specified a dowry (mahr) for her, then it is half of what you have specified [cf. 2:237]. Thus Allah has made for every situation a ruling suited to it, and for every divorced woman a provision in the measure that He, glory be to Him, has stated.

Now as we reflect on the words of the Truth thereafter:

﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, so that you may understand.﴾ (2:242)

From what has preceded, we know that the signs (ayat) are the wondrous matters. When Almighty Allah draws the intellect's attention to receive a ruling by way of reasoning (ta'aqqul), pure reason, if it directs its thought to studying the causes of this matter, will end up only at this ruling. For this reason, you find that Almighty Allah leaves some quarrels in dealings and vendettas in disputes to depart from the ruling of what Allah has legislated in any of the matters that have been mentioned earlier, and then harm befalls society as a result of the violation; as if by that He confirms His wisdom in legislating what He has legislated. Otherwise, if no harms resulted from the violations, people would say: there is no need for legislation, and they would abandon legislation without any harm befalling them.

Therefore, when we do not adhere to the legislation, the logic and the cosmic perfection require that harms occur; for if harms did not occur, people would doubt the method of Allah and say: "We have not adhered to Your method, O Lord, and yet there are no harms among us." Thus the harms we find in society draw our attention to the truthfulness of Allah and the perfection of His wisdom in determining His method. And so those who oppose the method of Allah end up confirming the method of Allah.

Then the discussion moves to treating a matter of faith: when God decrees a decree, no created being can escape it. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Have you not seen those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death? So God said to them, "Die," and then He gave them life. Indeed, God is bounteous toward mankind, but most of mankind do not give thanks.﴾ 243

After the Exalted One spoke about what concerns the Muslim family in the case of the end of marriage, whether by divorce or by death, He willed that the Islamic nation know that no one flees from the decree of God except to the decree of God. The Islamic nation is the nation entrusted with carrying the message and method of heaven to earth until the Hour is established, and there will be no further Prophet sent after Muhammad (ﷺ). Such a nation must be trained in a way that suits the mission God has placed upon it. The Exalted One must also set before this nation everything that the processions of the Messengers encountered among the earlier nations, so that they may take lessons from these situations and embody the method, not from theories that are recited but from a reality that has been studied and has occurred in society.

God wanted to draw our attention to the foundation of the matter, which is that He is the Giver of life and none other, and the Giver of life is the One who takes it. He did not place a cause for the gift of life among people. Rather, He alone gives life and causes death. In life and death there is the preservation of the human species, but the preservation of the lives of individuals arises through sustenance, which arises through wealth.

The Truth addresses this matter through a reality that Moses (ʿalayhi al-salām) had already lived with his people, the Children of Israel. We know that the story of Moses with his people took up the broadest of the Qur'an's stories, because they were the nation that wearied the Messengers and wearied the Prophets. It was necessary that the Truth present this entire matter to the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ) from the reality of what had happened. So He said, glory be to Him:

(Have you not seen those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death?). From this statement we know that the reason for leaving was only fear that they would die. As for the cause of this death, the verses do not address it, though the commentators did address it and said lengthy things. Some of them said that they left fleeing from a plague that had struck the land, fearing that they would die, and some said that they left fleeing from an enemy that had been set over them to annihilate them. The point is that they wanted to flee out of fear of death.

Thus the Qur'an addresses this matter from the angle that matters. But what is the cause, and why the departure? That is a matter of no importance, because the Qur'an does not give history. It does not say when the events occurred or their time, nor at whose hand this was, nor does it specify the persons of the matter. The Qur'an does not concern itself with all of that. Those who exhaust themselves searching for the details of those matters in the Qur'anic narrative are only trying to tie things to a particular time, a particular place, and particular persons.

We say to them: If the Qur'an had wished that, it would have done so, and if that had any basis in lesson and admonition, the Truth would have explained it to us. You want to weaken the meaning of the story by those details, because if the meaning of the story is confined to its time, it may be said: The time in which it happened could allow such an event, but the present time no longer allows it. And it may be said: This place where it occurred could allow its occurrence, but other places do not. Likewise, if He had specified it with particular individuals, it would be said: Such stories could only happen at the hands of these individuals, because they are rare occurrences in the universe that do not repeat.

When God leaves in a story its elements of time, place and persons undefined, and makes its places general, He gives it life in every time, in every place, and with every person, and no one can say that it is confined. I always give this example of those who try to determine the time of the People of the Cave, the place of the People of the Cave, the names of the People of the Cave, and the dog of the People of the Cave. We say to these people: You do not enrich the story, because when you specify for it a time, a place, and persons, it will be said: It is only useful for the time in which it occurred.

Therefore, when the Truth wills to leave something undefined, He leaves it undefined in order to generalize, and when He wills to specify, He identifies. An example of this is His saying, exalted is He:

﴿God sets forth an example for those who disbelieved: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, and their husbands did not avail them anything against God, and it was said, "Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾ 10 (Surah al-Tahrim).

The Truth did not specify the name of either of these two women. He mentioned only the important matter, which is that each of them was the wife of a noble Messenger. Nevertheless, Noah (ʿalayhi al-salām) could not withdraw the disbelieving creed from his wife, and Lot (ʿalayhi al-salām) could not withdraw the disbelieving creed from his wife. Rather, each of the two women conspired against her husband, the Messenger, along with her people. Therefore the destination of each of them was the Fire. The lesson from the story is that the choice of belief is left to the human being, so freedom of belief is a clear foundation among the foundations of the method. And He, glory be to Him, also said about the wife of Pharaoh:

﴿God sets forth an example for those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people."﴾ 11 (Surah al-Tahrim).

He did not mention her name, because it is not important to us in the matter. The point is that she was the wife of one who claimed divinity, and yet he could not convince his wife that he was a god. But when He wished to identify, He said about Mary (ʿalayhā al-salām):

﴿And Mary, daughter of ʿImran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our Spirit, and she affirmed the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was among the devout.﴾ 12 (Surah al-Tahrim).

He mentioned her and mentioned her father's name, because the event that happened to her will not be repeated in another woman. So those who try to strengthen the story by mentioning its details, we say to them: You are impoverishing the story. The important thing is that the Exalted One wants to say: They left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death. We want to take a linguistic position on the words of the Truth: (ʾAlam tara), "have you not seen."

When you say to a person "ʾalam tara," it means: did he not see with his own eyes? By God, did the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and the believers with him, and the believers after him until the Hour is established, see this matter? No. It reached them by means of hearing, not seeing. We know that seeing is through the eye, hearing is through the ear, tasting is through the tongue, smelling is through the nose, and touching is through the hand. These are the means that give the intellect perception and sensation so that it may yield meanings. On this, read His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that you might give thanks.﴾ 78 (Surah al-Nahl).

So the means of knowledge comes from the senses, and the chief of the senses is the eye, because it is possible to hear something from someone through his own experience, but when you see it yourself, the experience becomes yours alone. That is why it is said: "He who has seen is not like he who has heard." So when the Truth wishes to say, "Do you not know, O you whom I address with the Qur'an, the news of these people?", He, glory be to Him, brings it in this form: (Have you not seen those who left their homes), meaning: have you not known? And knowing here is by what means? By hearing.

Why did He, glory be to Him, not shorten the distance and say (Have you not heard?) instead of (Have you not seen?) In His saying (Have you not seen), He informs you of something that preceded your existence or came after your existence, so you must receive it as you receive what you have seen, because God, who created the senses, is more truthful than the senses. That is why the saying of the Exalted One came in Surah al-Fil:

﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ 1 (Surah al-Fil).

We know that the Prophet (ﷺ) was born in the Year of the Elephant and did not see that event, so how does God say to him, "Have you not seen?" Does the meaning of that equal "Have you not known?" or "Have you not heard from me?" and not "Have you not heard?" It is so that He may affirm to him that He will tell him of an event he did not witness, but the Truth will inform him of it, and God's informing him is as if he saw it. It is as if God is saying: This is a matter settled, and the moment I inform you of it, it is as though you saw it.

In our lives we hear people say: So-and-so is ʾalmaʿī (sharp-witted). It means that he speaks to you in a way as though he had seen or heard:

"The ʾalmaʿī, who makes you think a thought,
as though he had seen and as though he had heard."

The Truth speaks to us about these people, saying: (Have you not seen those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death, so God said to them, "Die," and then He gave them life). He, glory be to Him, informs us that the thing they flee from overtakes them, because no one can guard against the decree of God. Therefore God caused them to die and then gave them life so that they might take warning. If God had delayed the giving of life until the Day of Resurrection, the lesson would not have had effect, because after the Day of Resurrection there is no consideration and no obligation, and all of that would have no value. His saying, exalted is He, (fearing death) is an explanation of the cause of the departure. The Exalted One wanted to show them that this is a matter in which caution does not avail. You left out of fear of death, and I will cause you to die, and what you were seeking after death, I will bring about for you something other than it. Therefore He gave them life with a different life, so that they might be grieved and fulfill their appointed term. (Then He gave them life) so that He might show you that the matter of death is in His hand, glory be to Him, whether their fear of death came from their enemies or from plague and pestilence. The matter in its essence does not differ. Had the verse mentioned that they left out of fear of a plague, we would not have understood from it the possibility that they left out of fear of their enemies. So leaving the direct cause of the matter unspecified gave it richness.

His saying, exalted is He, (and they were thousands) shows us the extent of the failure and foolishness they were in, for how could they leave in fear of enemies while they were thousands in number? Not one of these thousands arose to say to them: Death and life are in the hand of God. (Have you not seen those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death, so God said to them, "Die").

When you command a subordinate with an order, you must have the power to carry it out. Would it be that if you say to someone, "Die," he will die? If he kills himself, he has killed himself, and there is a great difference between dying and being killed. Death comes without a cause from the dead person, but killing may happen through suicide or by some other means. The point is that it is the killing of a soul, not death.

The Truth clarifies the difference between killing and dying when He says:

﴿Muhammad is only a Messenger; Messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm God at all, and God will reward the grateful.﴾ 144 (Surah Al ʿImran).

This verse came in the context of drawing lessons from the defeat at Uhud, when it spread among the Muslims that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had been killed, and some of them thought of apostasy. The saying of the Truth came explaining that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is a Prophet who was preceded by Messengers who brought the method, and the Muslim nation that God entrusted with the completed method should not have its faith shaken by the death of the noble Messenger, because whoever turns back and apostatizes will not harm God at all. Rather, the reward will be for the grateful, those who recognize the favor of God's method.

We should know that the Truth brought up death as the counterpart of killing, and He made clear the matter of death in the next verse when He said:

﴿It is not for any soul to die except by God's permission, a term decreed. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him of it, and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him of it, and We will reward the grateful.﴾ 145 (Surah Al ʿImran).

So the matter of death is bound to God's will, His complete power, and His determination of every term at a known time that neither advances nor delays, and every person will meet the result of his deeds. Whoever works only for this world will receive his reward in it, and whoever works for the Hereafter, God will reward him in his worldly life and in his Hereafter.

Therefore the command proceeds from the Truth in His saying: (So God said to them, "Die," and then He gave them life). It was not by their will that they brought about their death, or the matter of their return to life. Rather it was a command of subjugation (taskhīr), by which they die through the complete power of His will, represented in (Be, and it is) (kun fa-yakun, the divine word of creation). And they return to life with the complete ... (ṭalāqa al-)

Following the discussion of the attempt by some of the Children of Israel to flee from God's decree, when God caused them to die by His ordaining and then brought them back to life by His ordaining, this is a clear lesson for the believers, for whom the command to fight in the way of God is about to come. So, O believers, do not be concerned if fighting brings you death, for death comes at any time. Thus says the Truth:

﴿And fight in the way of God, and know that God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

This is the clear command to fight in the way of God without fear of death. Why? Because the Giver of life and the Writer of the term is All-Hearing, All-Knowing: All-Hearing of the words of the one who fights, and All-Knowing of his intentions.

In earlier times, jihad was a heavy burden on the mujahid, for he bore the expense of his own self, bore the mount, a horse or a camel, and bore his weapon. Every mujahid had to prepare his equipment for war. If he allowed himself to die, then it was all the more fitting that he allow himself to give up his wealth and prepare his equipment for war. On this basis, fighting with both self and wealth was a necessary matter.

As for the Exalted One's saying, (And fight in the way of God), meaning: fight with your selves. Then he turned to wealth, saying:

﴿Who is it that will lend to God a goodly loan, so that He will multiply it for him manifold? And God withholds and extends, and to Him you will be returned.﴾

Whenever you hear (who is it that will lend to God), that is a great matter. For when you lend to a person, it is as if you are lending to God. But the matter is not clear, why? Because that person will benefit directly. But when you spend in the way of God, there is no specific person whom you are giving to; rather, you are giving to the general meaning in the matter of religiosity, and your dealing in it is with God. It is as if you are lending to God when you spend from your wealth to prepare yourself for war.

The Truth, glory be to Him, wants to alert us with the word "loan" that He is asking of us an act that is not easy for the human soul, and He, glory be to Him, knows what the souls have been disposed to. In the language, "qard" means to nibble a thing with the fang, and He, glory be to Him, knows that the act of lending is a difficult matter. And so that He might show people that He knows its difficulty, He came with His saying: (yuqriḍu, lends), meaning He who determines its difficulty, and He assigns the reward according to the degree of difficulty.

(Who is it that will lend to God a goodly loan?) And what is the goodly loan? And if you lend to a servant of God's servants, would the loan not be goodly?

Firstly, if you lend to a servant of God's servants, it is as if you have lent to God. True, you give the person that which eases his relief in a distressing situation, and true also that in the act of jihad you are not giving a specific person but are giving God directly. He, glory be to Him, informs us: whoever lends to My servants, it is as if he has lent to Me. How? Because God is the One who brought every servant of His into existence, so when a servant is in need, his need is made a claim upon his provision in this world. So when a servant gives to his needy brother, it is as if he is lending to God, who has undertaken the provision of that needy person.

His saying, glory be to Him: (God lends) indicates to us that the loan is not lost, because a loan is something you take out of your wealth in hope that you will recover it. He, glory be to Him, reassures you that it is He who will borrow from you and that He will return what He has borrowed, but not in the form of what you advanced; rather in the form of an investment multiplied many times over. The principal is preserved and invested. Therefore He says: (Who is it that will lend to God a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him manifold?) These are many multiples by the measures of God, mighty and majestic, not by our measures as humans.

The expression "a goodly loan" here indicates to us that the source of the money from which you lend must be lawful. Therefore it was said to the woman who gives charity from the wealth of fornication: (Would that she had not committed fornication and had not given charity).

It has also been said: the reward of a loan is greater than that of charity, although in charity a person gives up the whole thing, whereas a loan is a debt which its owner retrieves. Because the pain in giving charity occurs once: you give it and you lose hope in it. But with a loan, your soul remains attached to it, so whenever you show patience once, a good deed comes to you. Also, the one to whom charity is given may not be needy, but the borrower is none but needy.

Lending from the wealth you have causes the wealth to diminish, so God gives you manifold multiples as a result of this loan, which is entirely fitting for His saying: (And God constricts and expands, and to Him you will be returned), meaning: on the day you go to Him and each of us takes his due in the reckoning. That is, the wealth from which you lend decreases in outward appearance, but God increases it and expands it manifold, and in the Hereafter the reward will be abundant.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, moves on to another matter, opening it with His words ( Have you not considered ), to affirm that the report which follows is a fact as certain as something seen with the eye. He says:

﴿Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs: "Raise up for us a king, and we will fight in the way of Allah." He said: "Would you perhaps, if fighting is prescribed for you, not fight?" They said: "And what reason do we have not to fight in the way of Allah, when we have been driven out of our homes and our children?" But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.﴾ [2:246]

He, glorified be He, conveys this to us by way of hearing about it, and we must receive it as though we were seeing it with our own eyes. So what do we see? ( Have you not considered the chiefs ). What is the meaning of al-mala' (the chiefs, the notables)? It derives from mala'a, meaning a vessel became full, so that there is no room left to bear any addition, and the container has been occupied by its contents to such an extent that it can no longer make room for anything else. The word al-mala' is applied to the nobles of a people. The nobles are as though they are the ones who fill the life of existence around them, and no one else can compete with them. Al-mala' are the eminent figures of the people, who sit together for consultation.

( Have you not considered the chiefs of the Children of Israel after Moses ), meaning: has there not come to you the news of the people's leading figures and nobles after Moses, peace be upon him, for example in the era of Joshua ( Yusha' ) or Ezekiel ( Hizqil ) or Samuel ( Shamwil ), or any one of them? That does not concern us, because the Qur'an does not mention which era they were in. What matters is that they were after Moses, peace be upon him. ( When they said to a prophet of theirs: "Raise up for us a king, and we will fight in the way of Allah." )

The nobles of the Children of Israel gathered for consultation, then went to the prophet who was contemporary with them and said to him: "Raise up for us a king." From this we understand that they did not have a king. And what do we gain from mentioning that they had a prophet, but no king?

We understand from this that prophethood was supervising the implementation of affairs but did not directly handle the affairs, whereas kingship is what directly handles affairs. Had prophethood directly handled affairs, they would not have asked their prophet to raise up for them a king. The reason for this is that the one who directly handles affairs is exposed to the resentment of many people, and it is his lot to fail in managing some matters. So instead of directing their failure at the highest authority, they transfer it to someone lower, namely the king. For this reason they asked the prophet to bring a king who would re-manage affairs, so that prophethood would remain a reference for truth and would not become a target of blame for anything. Allah, the Exalted, informs us that He said to the prophet of the Children of Israel:

You are the ones who requested fighting, and you are the chiefs, that is, the nobles of the people, and you have brought the reason that necessitates fighting, namely that you were driven out of your homes and your children. That is, your humiliation has reached the point that you no longer have homes, and your humiliation has reached the point that you no longer have children after your enemy took them captive. So the cause for requesting fighting exists. Nevertheless, their prophet said to them: ( Would you perhaps, if fighting is prescribed for you, not fight? ) Their prophet made the condition clear to them and said: I fear that I may bring you a king so that you fight in the way of Allah, and then Allah prescribes fighting upon you, and when the matter becomes a fait accompli, we find that you have no resolve to fight and you falter.

But they said: ( And what reason do we have not to fight in the way of Allah, when we have been driven out of our homes and our children? ). Look at the precision in their words: ( in the way of Allah ), and attaching that way to their having been driven out of their homes and their children! They wanted to reverse the matter and say: fighting in the way of Allah is what follows after experience has bitten them regarding what they love, of homes and children. So Allah is the refuge in every matter, and He accepted their saying and counted their fighting as being in His way.

Their expulsion from their homes was something understandable, but how could they be expelled from their children? Perhaps they had left their children to the enemy, and perhaps the enemy had taken them prisoner. But it was they who were driven out of their homes, and regarding their relationship with the children, the words of the poet apply:

When you depart from a people who have decided
that you should not leave them, it is the departing ones who are they.

Consider the scrutiny: they were the chiefs of the Children of Israel, and they went to a prophet and said to him: "Raise up for us a king," so that they might make it a legitimate war, so that they could fight in the way of Allah. The prophet said what he said, and they responded to him with: ( And what reason do we have not to fight in the way of Allah? ), meaning: how could we not fight in the way of Allah?

The command to fight came to them in His words, exalted is He: ( When fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away ). His words ( was prescribed ) [kutiba, passive] are used because it was they who requested the legislation of fighting, so Allah placed them within the contract, and the expression came with kutiba (was prescribed), not with kataba (He prescribed). Nevertheless, they turned away, that is, they turned their backs on fighting.

Their prophet had the right to doubt their capacity to fight, and to say to them: ( Would you perhaps, if fighting is prescribed for you, not fight? ). But did they all turn away from fighting? No. There were among them those to whom the words of the poet apply:

The one who has made the truth bitter
has not left a generation free of the people of truth.

There were among them those who did not turn away from the obligation to fight, but they were a few. This is a required preparation, so that when the multitude recedes and everyone scatters from around you, beware of saying: ( I am few ), because the measures are not by the number of the gathering, but by the support of Allah, the Exalted.

Your enemy may be numerous, yet have no stock of high divinity, while you may be few in number, yet have a stock of high divinity. This is what the Truth wants to draw our attention to with His words: ( But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few ). The phrase ( except a few ) came to serve a point, which is why at the end of the story He says:

﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah.﴾ [2:249]

That is, victory comes by the permission of Allah. So the visible thing is one, but the viewpoint of those who see it differs according to the measure of their faith. You see a beautiful flower, and seeing is a shared thing among all people. Another sees it, and it delights you, so you preserve it and leave it as an adornment for yourself and for others, while another person sees it and plucks it, not caring whose it is. Thus you know that the inclination of action differs from one person to another. The enemy may appear numerous before us while we are few, and we all see the enemy as numerous and see ourselves as few, but the perceptions differ. I will reckon myself together with my Lord, while another sees them as many and says: "We cannot overcome them," because he has taken his Lord out of the calculation.

( But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except a few of them, and Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers ). So turning away is a wronging of the self, because wrongdoing in its simplest meaning is to transfer a right to other than its owner. You were driven out of your homes and remained in this state, so you wronged yourself, and you wronged your children who were taken from you and you did not reclaim them, and above all of that you wronged your religious cause.

Thus those who turned away were wrongdoers to themselves, to their families, to their community, and to the doctrinal cause. His saying, the Truth: ( And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers ), is a sign that Allah is aware of those who falter in secret, who wanted to kill the morale of the people, and who in this age are called the "fifth column," who undermine morale without anyone seeing them, but Allah knows them.

These people among the Children of Israel asked their prophet to raise up for them a king, and it would have been enough for the prophet sent to them to choose a king for them, so that they might fight under his banner. But they increased in dragging their feet and obstinacy, and wanted to shift the matter to a different footing, one that is not among the issues of religion.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿And their Prophet said to them, "Indeed, Allah has sent Ṭālūt (Saul) to you as king." They said, "How can he have kingship over us when we are more deserving of kingship than him, and he has not been given abundance of wealth?" He said, "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him broadly in knowledge and physique. And Allah gives His kingship to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing."﴾

It was they who asked their Prophet to send them a king. It would have sufficed, then, for their Prophet to choose a person and appoint him as king over them. But their Prophet wanted to instill in them respect for the one sent as their king. He said to them: "(Indeed, Allah has sent Ṭālūt to you as king)." The Prophet who said this belonged to them; he was one of them, and when they asked him to send them a king, they knew that he was trustworthy in this matter.

The courtesy of prophethood is manifest in the way he conveyed it. He said: "(Indeed, Allah has sent Ṭālūt to you as king)." He wanted to reassure them that the matter of choosing Ṭālūt as king was not from him, because he was a human being like them, and he wanted to remove his own human element from this affair. So he said: "(Indeed, Allah has sent Ṭālūt to you as king)." What, then, was their response? "(They said, 'How can he have kingship over us when we are more deserving of kingship than him, and he has not been given abundance of wealth?')" This was the beginning of obstinacy and contentiousness, and the shifting of the matter to something that is not among the affairs of religion.

They wanted nobility and wealth. They should have taken the matter as one in which kingship had come for their benefit, since they were the ones who requested a king to lead them in war. Thus the choice of a king was for them and in their interest; why, then, do they imagine that the choice was against them and not in their interest? Another point we understand from their words "(How can he have kingship over us)" is that Ṭālūt was not one of the notable figures. Usually, when a matter becomes pressing for a group, they think about who should lead, and there are typically a number of prominent personalities around whom thought revolves, and the group assumes that the choice could fall on one of them. But the choice of heaven fell on Ṭālūt, contrary to what that group had expected. Ṭālūt came from among the common folk, as evidenced by their saying "(How can he have kingship)," meaning he had not previously been given kingship.

They belonged to two lineages: the lineage that took prophethood, which is the lineage of Benjamin (Binyamin), and the lineage that took kingship, which is the lineage of Levi son of Jacob (Ya'qub). When he said to them "(Indeed, Allah has sent Ṭālūt to you as king)," they began searching for his genealogical record, and found him belonging neither to this nor to that, and therefore they said: "(How can he have kingship over us)." This shows us that when people want a particular situation, they do not want the man suited to the situation, but rather the man suited to their own inclinations, as evidenced by their saying "(How can he have kingship over us when we are more deserving of kingship than him)."

Does kingship come through arrogance or pride? Since Ṭālūt was a man from among the common people, the Almighty wants to establish a principle for every believer: when you want to make a choice, beware lest lineage, descent, or status deceive you, but choose the most fitting from among the people of expertise, not from among the people of trust. They overlooked that the matter they asked of their Prophet requires two qualities: a man of physical stature and a man of knowledge, and Allah chose for them Ṭālūt, a man who was both of stature and knowledgeable.

When we reflect on the context of the verses, we find that Allah first said to them "(He has sent to you)" so that no one among them would be embarrassed that Ṭālūt was preferred over him. But when contention arose, He said: "(Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you)," and by this statement He confirms that among you there is no one who possesses both physical stature and knowledge. Likewise, there is none among the learned among you who possesses physical stature: "(Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him broadly in knowledge and physique)." They should have received Allah's choice of Ṭālūt for kingship with acceptance and contentment, so what of the fact that He has increased him in knowledge and physique?

The breadth in knowledge and physique is the qualification suited to the task for which they wanted a king. Therefore the Almighty says: "(And Allah gives His kingship to whom He wills)," as if the Almighty is saying to them: Do not think that you are the ones who nominate the suitable king for us. It is enough for you that you asked me to send you a king; so leave the choice to my standards to select the suitable king.

The Almighty concludes the verse by saying: "(And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing)," meaning that for every station there is a fitting word, and for every position a fitting man, and He, glory be to Him, knows who is suited for this task and who is suited for that. And this is not out of constraint or a lack of men, but out of abundance and knowledge.

They received this divine choice with contention, and contention is a kind of obstinacy, which is only ended by a visible, observable matter that compels by proof. Therefore it was necessary for a miracle to come. ﴿And their Prophet said to them, "Indeed, the sign of his kingship is that there will come to you the chest (Ark) in which is tranquility from your Lord and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, carried by the angels. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers."﴾

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 2, verse 248:

God sent with the king Talut a sign that proves he is a king chosen by God. Their prophet said to them: "The sign of his kingship is that the ark (al-tabut) will come to you." That is, the sign indicating his kingship is "that the ark will come to you." From this statement we infer that the ark had been absent and lost, that it was a well-known matter among them, and that they were eager for its return.

What is the ark (al-tabut)? The ark is mentioned in the Qur'an in two places. One is the verse we are now discussing; the other is in the words of the Exalted:

﴿When We inspired to your mother that which is inspired: "Put him into the chest and put it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his. And I cast upon you love from Me, and that you may be raised under My eye."﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha).

Thus we know the ark from the days of the story of Moses, when he was an infant and his mother feared for him; God inspired her: "If you fear for him, then cast him into the river." Is this the very ark that the verses we are discussing speak of?

It is most likely that it is, because since it comes in its unqualified form, it is the well-known ark, as if the matter by which Moses was saved has a history with Moses, Pharaoh, their prophet and Talut. From this process we take that the relics connected with great events in the history of belief must be given attention, and we should not call them idolatrous or pagan, because they are linked to a matter of creed, to historical matters, and to sacred things. Consider the ark, in which is a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, carried by the angels. This is evidence that it is something great and important.

Thus, the relics that are connected with the events of belief and the events of prophethood are important for faith, and it is as if the Qur'an says: leave them as they are, and take from them admonition and lesson, because they remind you of sacred things. The ark had been lost, and that is evidence that an enemy overcame the lands they had settled, and an enemy, when it raids a land, first tries to efface the sacred things that bind the land to its belief. If the ark was thus sacred to them, the enemies must have taken it. These enemies are the ones who drove them out of their homes, they being thousands fleeing from death. And if they drove them out of their homes, it is all the more certain that they forced them to leave the ark behind.

God, glory be to Him, reassures them that the sign of Talut's kingship is the coming of the ark, which you long for, and to which your sacred things are bound.

(That the ark will come to you, in it is tranquility from your Lord.) It is as if psychological peace will come to you with this ark, because when a person finds the ark that a prophet was saved by, and among the things we will come to know later, a person breathes in his connection to heaven, and it is a material connection that makes the soul at rest. For example, reflect on your feelings when you are told: "This is the Mushaf from which our master Uthman used to read." It is a Mushaf like any other Mushaf, but its distinction is that our master Uthman used to read from it; you find yourself at peace when you see it. Likewise, when you go to the Palace of the Caliphate in Turkey and are told: "This is the sword with which Imam Ali used to fight." You look at the sword and find its weight and heft equal to ten swords, and you marvel how our master Ali, may God honour his face, carried it and how he fought with it.

Likewise, when you are told: "This is a hair of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, or the kohl-pot with which he used to apply kohl," there is no doubt that such sights will leave radiance and tranquility in your soul. And when a person with some doubts and fears sees them, belief settles in his soul. From all this I say: the rulers should not regard sacred objects as a form of shirk and idolatry; rather they should give them care and attention and display them to the people, so that they become a source of tranquility and security of soul for people. They should advise people not to be tempted by them, but to leave them so that they remind us of a matter connected with our creed and with our Prophet.

Now look at the Qur'an's account of the ark. God, the Truth, did not say that the ark would come complete, nor did He say that it is the ark in which Moses was placed; rather He said: (in it is tranquility from your Lord and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind), as if the family of Moses and Aaron had preserved the relics of their prophets. Also His saying: (carried by the angels) confirms for us that there is no doubt that the relic carried by the angels must be something great that requires exceptional care: (that the ark will come to you as the sign of his kingship).

We note in His saying "that the ark will come to you" that He attributed the coming to the ark. Was it part of the sign that the ark would come to them while they sat waiting? Since the ark is carried by the angels, the people will not see them, because they are unseen beings, so no one will see them; rather the people will see the ark coming toward them. For this reason the Truth attributed the act of coming to the ark. This scene shakes hearts and makes the hardest-hearted people fall down in prostration, saying: ("Talut, you are the king, and we will not dispute with you.") We now want to know which things of Moses' relics the family of Moses could have preserved, and which relics of Aaron the family of Aaron preserved from Aaron, peace be upon him.

Some people said it is the staff of Moses, which is the relic that remained with the family of Moses, and that is reasonable, because it is one of the instruments of Moses' miracle, peace be upon him. Was it not the miracle that turned into a living, slithering serpent and swiftly swallowed what the magicians had made? Such a miraculous instrument cannot be neglected by Moses, nor by the believers in him after what happened through it. And it is not reasonable that the family of Moses would squander a staff about which God spoke, saying:

﴿"And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?" He said: "It is my staff; I lean upon it."﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, verses 17–18).

There is a long story that the discussion of this staff took up; how then would Moses and his people casually squander it? Surely they preserved it, revered it, and made it one of their glories.

The Truth, glory be to Him, shows us that these people were men of obstinacy, contention and reluctance: they do not believe in matters unless they are tangible, like the ark that comes to them alone, carried by the angels, yet they do not see the angels; they saw only the ark moving toward them. ("That the ark will come to you, in it is tranquility from your Lord and a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind, carried by the angels. Surely in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.") There is no sign more wondrous than the coming of the ark to establish the truth of the prophet's word that God has sent Talut as king; if they do not believe in this matter, they should review their faith.

The Qur'anic context shows that God confounded them with the argument, confounded them with the sign, and confounded them with the Qur'an, as evidenced by His omitting what should have been said, namely: "So they accepted Talut as king." Talut organized the war; he stood up, divided the troops and arranged them, and none of these details are mentioned in the verses.

And the Truth says afterwards:

﴿So when Talut set out with the troops, he said: "Indeed, Allah is going to test you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is indeed of me, except one who scoops up a handful with his hand." But they drank from it, except for a few of them. And when he crossed it, he and those who believed with him, they said: "We have no power today against Jalut and his troops." Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said: "How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of Allah! And Allah is with the patient."﴾ 249

Al-fasl (the separation) is to isolate one thing from another, and similar to that is the words of the Most High:

﴿And when the caravan departed, their father said: "Indeed, I sense the smell of Yusuf."﴾ (Surah Yusuf, 12:94).

("Fassalat al-'ir") means it left Egypt and went out of it. We use the word (fasl) in the classification of books, and by it we mean a quantity of interrelated information that forms one unit. When the fusul (sections) are joined together in books they become abwab (chapters), and when chapters on one field of knowledge are arranged together we call it: this is (kitab) (a book).

We also use the word (fasl) to describe a group of students close in age and academic level, and we divide them into a first, second and third class, according to the capacity of the classrooms and the number of students. And thus we understand the meaning of the Truth's saying: (So when Talut set out with the troops), that is, he separated them from the rest who were not fighters, and divided them into organised groups, each group having a task.

The word (junud) (troops) is the plural of (jund), which is singular but denotes a group. The root of the word is (jannad), meaning hard, firm, strong ground, and since the troops are presumed to have roughness and strength, they were given the name: jund. Although the word (jund) is singular, it denotes a people, like (rahat) and (ta'ifa), and they call it a collective noun (ism jam'). (So when Talut set out with the troops, he said: Indeed Allah is going to test you with a river), that is, when he went out to the place where the army was encamped, he began the first of his duties as king. He wanted to test them, for they were a people who had stood against his appointment as king, so he wanted to establish his rule on firm ground. So he said to them, on the authority of the Truth: (Indeed Allah is going to test you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is indeed of me, except one who scoops up a handful with his hand, but they drank from it, except for a few of them).

He made clear to them: you are about to undertake a mission for Allah in the way of Allah, and it is He, glory be to Him, who will administer the test, not I, because the test is in proportion to the mission; I am merely overseeing the execution of the command, and Allah is testing you with a river: whoever drinks from it is not of us, except one who scoops up a handful with his hand.

And when you hear the word (mubtalikum) (testing you), do not interpret it as a calamity, but interpret it as a test, in which one may succeed and one may fail.

The test here is with a river. Since the test was with a river, this word must have a position and a psychological effect upon them; they must have been thirsty, for otherwise, had they not been thirsty, the river would not have been a trial. (Indeed Allah is going to test you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me).

They were thirsty, and when they see the water they will rush to it, drinking eagerly and quenching themselves, yet the Truth tests their steadfastness by demanding that they refrain from drinking from it. The test came in preventing them from what their souls yearn for. (Whoever drinks from it is not of me). Why?

Because when they see what they love and desire, they will rush to it and forget the command of Allah. One who forgets the command of Allah and prefers himself is not to be trusted to be among the troops of Allah. But the one who sees the water and refrains from it while being in need of it, is patient and in control of himself, and he will be among the troops of Allah, for he has preferred what Allah seeks over what his belly seeks, and he is worthy of being tested. Nevertheless, Allah did not make the test harsh; He permitted what quenches thirst and did not forbid it to them altogether. (Indeed Allah is going to test you with a river. Whoever drinks from it is not of me, and whoever does not taste it is indeed of me, except one who scoops up a handful with his hand). He allowed them a handful that suffices to relieve the thirst and preserves life; He permitted them what necessity requires. But what is the connection of this test to the operation they are about to undertake?

Indeed, the military operation they are about to enter, they will face hardship, they will be exposed to the exhaustion of provisions, and they are also liable to be besieged by their enemy. A fighting man in such circumstances must strengthen himself against his desires and take from his provisions and water only in proportion to what is necessary to sustain life. Therefore, one handful suffices to sustain life. It is as though the training here is a necessity for the mission. So did they do that?

The news comes to us from the Truth: (But they drank from it, except for a few of them). Thus the sifting is completed. At the beginning, they had already turned away and avoided fighting, except for a few; and here a few of the few refrained from drinking. These are the sieves of selection or the filters of testing: one may be strong enough to bear half the hardship, another strong enough for a third of it, and a third for a quarter of it. Only a few remained of them, but they were the few suited to the mission; those who remained steadfast in faith.

And see how the filters of testing operate in jihad in the way of Allah: so that none carries the banner of jihad except the trustworthy one who knows its rights. (So when he crossed it, he and those who believed with him, they said: "We have no power today against Jalut and his troops"), that is, when they crossed the river and passed all the preceding tests, some of them said: (We have no power today against Jalut and his troops). Some of them feared the final test, but those who believed in Allah did not fear. The Truth says: (Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said: How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of Allah! And Allah is with the patient).

The perceptions differed though the sights were the same. Those who crossed the river divided into two parts: one part saw Jalut and his troops, and the other part also saw them, and they did not divide at the seeing, but they divided at the feelings that followed the seeing: one part feared and one part did not fear. Those who feared said: (We have no power today against Jalut and his troops). Fear of Jalut and his troops entered their souls, so they said: (We have no power today against Jalut and his troops). They passed through three stages: the first is the perception of Jalut and his troops; the second is an apprehensive feeling about the strength of Jalut and his troops; and the last is an inclination toward fear of Jalut and his troops. But the part that did not fear also saw the scene, and there came concerning them the saying of Allah: (Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said: How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of Allah!).

It is as though they brought their Lord into their reckoning, so they belittled their enemy, whereas the earlier group isolated itself from its Lord, so they saw themselves as few and feared. The mere supposition of the believing group that they would meet Allah produced this conviction in them; and if this is the state of mere supposition, what then of certainty? (How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of Allah, and Allah is with the patient). We know that there are battles in which the one more capable of patience wins, and our evidence for that is the saying of the Truth:

﴿When you said to the believers: "Will it not suffice you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 3:124).

This is the promise; but if you are patient, how much will the reinforcement be? The Truth says:

﴿Yes! If you are patient and fear Allah, and they come at you immediately, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked.﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 3:125).

So the start with three thousand to support the people of faith increases the number of reinforcement to five thousand if they are patient and fear Allah. Thus the reinforcement comes in proportion to patience; because the tenderness of Divine power toward you increases at the moment it finds you bearing hardship, so it shows mercy to you and gives you a greater share. Allah wants His servant to exhaust his own means of strength, and when the means are exhausted with manliness and steadfastness, the help of Allah comes to you, and Allah says to His angels: this one deserves to be helped, so help him. That is why the saying of the Truth came on the tongues of the believers: (How often has a small company overcome a large company by the permission of Allah, and Allah is with the patient). And the Truth says afterwards:

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 250:

﴿When they went forth against Goliath (Jalut) and his hosts, they said: "Our Lord, pour upon us patience, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people."﴾

This is the faith-charged resolve of one who wishes to face his enemy. He calls out: "Our Lord" (rabbana). He did not say "O Allah," but says "Our Lord," because the Rabb is the One who takes charge of nurturing and giving, whereas what is required of the servant with regard to "Allah" is worship and obligations. Therefore the believer calls upon his Lord in a difficult situation, saying "O our Lord," meaning: O You who created us, who take charge of us, and who supply us with the means. The believers with Talut said: "Our Lord, pour upon us patience."

When we reflect on the phrase "pour upon us patience," it conveys to us that they asked that Allah fill their hearts with patience, and that the effect of patience be the firming of their feet ("and make our feet firm"), so that they might face the enemy with faith. At the end of patience and the firming of feet comes the victory of Allah for the believers over the disbelieving people. The result of resolve grounded in faith and of fighting comes in His saying, the Truth: ﴿So they routed them by Allah's permission, and David killed Goliath, and Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom and taught him of what He willed. And were it not for Allah's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would be corrupted; but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds.﴾ (2:251)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 251:

Indeed, the Truth informs us that He gave victory to the believers in Him. The Truth uses the word (they routed them) [hazamūhum], and it indicates the flight of the one who should have been the attacker. The fighter should always be the attacker, advancing constantly. So when he resorts to fleeing, here we pause to ascertain his situation: is this flight a tactical withdrawal (taḥarruf li-qitāl), a turning aside and a shift to another position which is better suited for fighting in? If that is the case, then it is not defeat. But if the flight is not for a counterattack or a stratagem against the enemy, and was instead out of fear, then here it is defeat.

And God's saying: ﴿So they routed them by God's permission﴾ indicates that the soldiers of Goliath (Jālūt) were not all killed, but rather those who were killed were the leaders of disbelief among them, as evidenced by His saying afterwards: ﴿And David killed Goliath﴾. Goliath was the commander of the army of the disbelievers, who fled, so David pursued him and killed him. For the first time the name (David, Dāwūd) appears to us in this long story, a name of which we had no idea before, and the idea of him will come after this story in the saying of the Exalted:

﴿And We certainly gave David bounty from Us. O mountains, echo with him, and the birds; and We made iron pliable for him. [Saying:] Make full coats of mail and measure well the links, and act righteously. Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do.﴾ (Surah Saba': 10–11).

So David's beginning came out of this battle after the killing of Goliath. David was the brother of ten, and he was the youngest of them. The Prophet said to the people: whoever enters the battle against Goliath must come with the armour of Moses fitted to his measure. Here David's father displayed the armour before all his sons, and it did not fit any of them except the youngest, who was David. The armour fitted his measure, and David entered the battle and killed Goliath, the commander of the polytheists, and God's wisdom willed that the youngest of the believers should be the one to kill the greatest of the army of the polytheists.

This battle was the beginning of David's history, and this battle brought him the great victory. Then God bestowed upon him kingship and wisdom, and made the mountains and the birds echo and return with him the glorification and exaltation of God. All of that was the result of the killing of Goliath. David loved the armour, and his hope became that God would teach him the craft of making coats of mail, and for this reason he took no profession in his life except making coats of mail. God made iron soft for him so that he could shape from it whatever he wished, as came in His saying:

﴿And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you, to protect you from your violence.﴾ (Part of verse 80, Surah al-Anbiya').

This is evidence that a person loves the thing that is connected to the elevation of his status. The killing of Goliath was indeed the beginning for David. (﴿And David killed Goliath, and God gave him kingship and wisdom and taught him of what He willed. And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted; but God is full of bounty to the worlds.﴾) Here the Truth brings a cosmic principle in existence, namely that war is a social necessity, and that the Truth repels people by means of people. And that were it not for the existence of one power against another power, the world would be corrupted; for if a single power dominated the universe, it would be corrupted.
