What sustains the universe is that there exist in it balanced powers: a power which is confronted by another power. For this reason we find the world always guarded by two superpowers, and if there were one power, error would prevail everywhere. If we reflect on history from the earliest times, we would find this duality of powers preserving stability in the world.

At the beginning of Islam, the two superpowers were Persia in the East and Rome in the West. Now, Russia has fallen from the scale of the world's balance, and Germany and Japan are racing to balance the power of America.

Indeed, God's saying: ﴿And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾ came as a sequel to the story of the conflict between the Children of Israel and their enemies who expelled them from their homelands. When we reflect on this story from its beginning, we find that they first asked God for permission to fight. God sent them a king to fight under his banner; and the sign of this king's truthfulness was that God would bring the Ark (al-tābūt). Then came a social matter which people usually arrive at by sound judgment even without revelation: that when a person sets out to undertake a matter, he must prepare for it with human means, and once he has fully prepared with all the means, he then turns to God's help, because the means, as we have said, come from the hand of God. So do not reject the hand of God with its means in order to seek God's help in His essence; rather, take the means first, for they come from the hand of your Lord.

The Truth also teaches us that among the means is the testing (tamḥīṣ) of those who defend the truth, a testing which shows us the strength of their steadfastness in the trial of faith; for a person may say a word with his tongue, but when he is faced with action, his soul may whisper to him not to fulfil it. And indeed a few of the people succeeded in the multiple trials. And indeed the battle took place; these believers defeated their enemies, and David triumphed by killing Goliath.

So this is a case in which God repelled some people by means of others, and the Truth expresses it as a general principle: (﴿And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾). Repelling (daf') is turning back what is intended; so if it was intended for people that evil should exist, God repels it. Thus God repels, but by the hands of His creatures, as He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Fight them; God will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people.﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah, 14).

It is God's repelling of the believers so that they fight the disbelievers, and the Truth punishes the disbelievers by the hands of the believers. And when we reflect on the wise saying: (﴿And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾) we find a prior premise preparing for this saying: they were expelled from their homes and their children, and this was the justification for fighting. You will find another verse also saying:

﴿Those who have been expelled from their homes without right, only because they say, "Our Lord is God." And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of God is mentioned much. And God will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, God is Strong and Exalted in Might.﴾ (Surah al-Ḥajj, 40).

The context differs between the two verses: the context in Surat al-Baqarah concerns people who are actually fighting, while the context in Surat al-Ḥajj concerns people who believed in the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and went out, being the oppressed (al-mustaḍʿafūn), from Mecca to join their brothers in faith in the abode of faith, in order to regroup and enter Mecca victorious.

It is true that we find a comprehensive unity between the two verses, namely the going out from homelands. So at times the defence is by fleeing in order to return (tafirru li-takirr), that is, you leave the abode of disbelief as an emigrant in order to gather your affairs, you and those with you, and return to your land as a fighter and conqueror. And at other times the defence is by actually fighting; the verse we are reflecting upon here indicates that they fought in fact, and the second verse indicates that they went out of Mecca to return to it as conquerors. The going out itself is a kind of repelling. Why? Because if the early Muslims had remained in Mecca, their opponents might have destroyed them, and nothing of Islam would have remained; so they went to Medina and established the Islamic state, then returned victorious and conquering:

﴿When the help of God and the victory has come.﴾ (Surah al-Naṣr, 1).

The context in the two verses is one, but the result differs. Here the Truth says: (﴿And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾). Why would the earth be corrupted? Because the meaning of God's repelling people by means of others is that there are people who have become accustomed to corruption, and opposing them are people who went out against those accustomed to corruption in order to return them to righteousness. The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, gives us the cause in the second verse, saying:

﴿And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of God is mentioned much.﴾ (Part of verse 40, Surah al-Ḥajj).

The ṣawāmiʿ (monasteries/hermitages) are what today corresponds to the monastery (dayr) of the Christians, and they used to worship God in them, because there is a worshipper who acts by the general obligation, and another worshipper who has bound himself to something beyond what God has obligated him with. Those who worship God in this way sit in remote places away from people, which they call ṣawāmiʿ, and they resemble the monastery today. The general meaning of worship for the Christians is worship in churches, and this is what is meant by biyaʿ, while the specific meaning is worship in ṣawāmiʿ.

So (﴿monasteries [ṣawāmiʿ]﴾ here are for the elite of the religious, and churches or biyaʿ for the general religious. The Truth's saying: (﴿and synagogues [ṣalawāt]﴾), from ṣalūt, is the place of worship for the Jews, and (﴿mosques [masājid]﴾) are the mosques of the Muslims.

As for His saying, (﴿the earth would have been corrupted﴾) in this verse, and His saying there (﴿there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques﴾), it means that the earth will be corrupted if the monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques are not established; because they are what connect the created being with the Creator. And as long as those places are what connect the created being with the Creator, then if they are demolished, people will be heedless of their Lord, and the causes of this world will tempt them.

So the monasteries, churches, and hermitages, when they existed, and the mosques now, are the guardians of values in existence, because they constantly remind you of servitude and protect you from vanity; they are part of prostration, which is the utmost submission to the Lord. By them we submit to God five times in the day and night; so if there is any vanity in the servant, it must melt away, and the servant knows that the whole universe is a bounty from God upon the servants. So let no vanity enter you, O Muslim. When vanity does not enter you, you use the means of God for the things God desires. As for your taking God's means for things other than what God desires, that is an insolence from you. If God has empowered your hand to move, why do you disobey God with it and strike people with it? God has empowered your tongue to speak, so why do you harm others with the word? God has given you the blessing, so do not use it in disobedience.

God, the Exalted, said in this verse: (﴿the earth would have been corrupted﴾), and He explained that in His saying: (﴿And were it not for God's repelling some people by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of God is mentioned much﴾). These places are what preserve the foundations of values in religion. ("The foundations of values in religion") are not "all the values in religion." For this reason we have said that the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has made for Islam five pillars, upon which Islam was built. We must establish the structure of Islam upon these five pillars; do not say that Islam is these five pillars. No; Islam is built upon them only, for they are the columns or foundations upon which Islam was built. When you lay the foundation of a house and erect the columns, this house is not thereby fit for dwelling; rather, you must build the rest of the structure. So Islam is built upon these foundations.

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, clarifies this by commanding the preservation of the places of these values, because mosques, as we speak in Islamic usage, are the meeting place of the luminous outpourings of the Truth upon His creation; whoever wants the outpouring of the Truth with its light goes to the mosque. So that the earth may not be corrupted, these places of worship must exist. Thus once the Truth mentioned the result, and once He mentioned the cause.

And why does God repel some people by means of others? Because there are people who want evil and people who want good; whoever wants evil repels whoever wants good. And if the battle occurs with this description, then the hand of God does not abandon the believing side seeking good, for He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿God will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, God is Strong and Exalted in Might.﴾ (Part of verse 40, Surah al-Ḥajj).

That is, the battle does not last long. For this reason we said previously that the battles we see in the universe do not include a battle between two rights, because there are not two rights in existence; the Truth is one, so let no one say, "I am upon the truth and my opponent is upon the truth." No, there is only one truth. A battle, if it occurs, occurs between truth and falsehood, or between falsehood and falsehood. The battle between truth and falsehood does not last long, because falsehood is bound to vanish. What lasts longest among battles is the battle between falsehood and falsehood, for neither of them is more deserving of God's support: this one is on corruption and that one is on corruption, and He, glory be to Him, crushes this corruption by that corruption. And when this corruption is crushed by that corruption, the two wings of corruption in the universe come to an end. And then there come after that people who are not from

Then the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, says:

﴿These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth, and indeed you are among the messengers. [2:252]﴾

We know that "Tilka" (these) is a demonstrative by which Allah addresses His Messenger ﷺ, pointing to the verses that preceded, which show the greatness of the Truth and His self-subsistence. The Truth had said earlier:

﴿Have you not considered those who left their homes, and they were thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, "Die," and then He restored them to life. Indeed, Allah is bounteous to the people, but most of the people are not grateful. [2:243]﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah).

And when they asked to fight, and that He send them a king, and He sent him to them, and He sent them the Ark, in which was tranquility (sakinah), are these not other signs? And after that the Truth willed that the killing of Jalut (Goliath), the huge giant, should come about at the hands of Dawud (David), the small youth. Is this not a sign? And another sign is that a small group, by their own admission, when they said: "How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah" — this small group entered the battle and defeated the multitude. Is this not a sign?

Did the Messenger ﷺ know the signs that preceded his mission? No, but it was from Allah's informing him, along with the acknowledgment of everyone, especially those who disbelieved in Muhammad ﷺ, that he could neither read nor write, nor sat with a teacher, and no one had spoken to him at all. Even on the journey he made for trade, others accompanied him. Had they seen him sitting with anyone teaching him something, they would have broadcast that Muhammad had sat with so-and-so and learned such-and-such. But no one said this, because it had never happened at all. Therefore, his ﷺ informing them of what they themselves know in their own possession is a part of the secrets of his miracle: he knew the earlier reports despite not having read, not having written, and not having received knowledge from anyone. Some of the polytheists disputed and said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to sit with a youth at al-Marwah, teaching him these reports." Then the true word came down refuting this fabrication:

﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue. [16:103]﴾ (Surat al-Nahl).

Thus the Truth established that their argument is false and their claim is a lie on their part, because the one they alleged taught the Messenger was a non-Arab. The Truth, glorified is He, says to Muhammad ﷺ: "These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth." The phrase "āyāt Allāh" means wondrous things. "Natlūhā" means We make one word follow another, and it comes from "waliya," meaning it came after it without a separation. "Natlūhā ʿalayka bil-ḥaqq" — and "al-ḥaq" is that which occurs in its proper place, where it does not change from it, so it never contradicts itself.

Suppose an incident happened before you, and you were asked about it a thousand times throughout your life; you would find that your answer never differs about it, because you are relating a reality you saw. But if the story were a lie, you would find that your account of it changes the second time, because you do not remember what you said the first time, since you are not narrating a reality that holds you and to which you are bound. Likewise, the Truth does not change, does not contradict, and does not conflict.

"These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth." Since the Truth, glorified is He, is the One who says them, He will say them to you truly, and then others will know that you have known what they have, of what they conceal in their books and say to one another. Here they will know that you are among the messengers. For this reason we find in the "mā kānāt" of the Qur'an, in which He, exalted is He, says "mā kunt" (you were not), "mā kunt," and "mā kunt," and like His saying, the Truth:

﴿And you were not on the western side when We decreed to Musa the command, nor were you among the witnesses. [28:44]﴾ (Surat al-Qasas).

That is, O Muhammad, you were not present with Musa at the western side of the mountain when Allah entrusted him with the matter of the message, and you were not a contemporary of Musa nor a witness to his conveying the message. So how would your people deny you while you recite to them the reports of the earlier ones? A similar example is His saying, the Truth:

﴿That is from the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens, which of them would be charged with Maryam, nor were you with them when they disputed. [3:44]﴾ (Surat Al 'Imran).

What the Qur'an related to you, O Muhammad, of the glorious reports about those whom Allah chose is from the unseen which Allah revealed to you. You were not present with them while they drew lots with arrows to determine by lot who would take charge of Maryam's affairs, nor were you with them as they disputed over attaining this noble honor. A similar example is the saying of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿And you were not on the side of the mount when We called, but it is a mercy from your Lord, that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, that they may remember. [28:46]﴾ (Surat al-Qasas).

That is, O Messenger, you were not present on the side of the mount when We called Musa at the appointed time, and his Lord spoke to him and conversed with him. But Allah informed you of this through revelation, as a mercy to you and to your nation, and so that you would convey it to a people to whom no messenger had come before you, that perhaps they would remember and believe. A similar example is the saying of the Truth:

﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor faith, but We made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, you guide to a straight path. [42:52]﴾ (Surat ash-Shura).

The Qur'an is a revelation sent down from Allah, which makes the believers know the light of guidance and the obligations of the Truth, and guides whoever chooses guidance. And indeed, O Muhammad, you call by this Qur'an to a straight path. Every "mā kunt" in the Noble Qur'an is evidence that what Jibril, as a messenger from Allah to you and a bearer of revelation from Allah, informed you of is the truth; you learned it, O Muhammad, in a special manner and along a particular method, although you had not read a book nor sat with a teacher. What you tell them of verses agrees with what they have, and it would have been incumbent upon them to say that the one who taught you this is Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, and they should have acknowledged and testified that you are among the messengers.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 253:

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Those messengers, We preferred some of them above others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and some of them He raised by degrees. And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, the clear proofs, and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit. Had Allah willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another, after the clear proofs had come to them. But they differed: some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. Had Allah willed, they would not have fought one another; but Allah does what He wills.﴾ [2:253]

The Truthful, glorified and exalted is He, points to the messengers by His saying: "Those messengers" (tilka al-rusul). "Al-rusul" is the plural of a singular which is "rasul" (messenger). The rasul is the one charged with the message (risala). The risala is a sentence of speech that carries a meaning to a goal. Since "al-rusul" is a group, why did the Truth not say "these messengers" (ha'ula' al-rusul) and instead say "those messengers" (tilka al-rusul)? So that the Noble Qur'an may show you that the messengers, however they differ, are sent from one God and with one method. And as we knew before, the indication with "tilka" is an indication of something distant. When we point to something near, we say "dha" (this), and when we use the form of indication with address, we say "dhaka" (that). When we point to a feminine, we say "ti", and when we address a feminine, we say "tika". And the "lam" (la), as we knew, here is for distance or for elevated rank.

So His saying, the Truth: "Those messengers" is an indication to the messengers whom Sayyidina Muhammad (ﷺ) knows, or the messengers who preceded in the Qur'anic context. The Qur'anic context that preceded spoke of Musa (peace be upon him), and of Isa (peace be upon him), and the context spoke of the messengers of firm resolve (ulu al-azm).

If you want the Qur'anic order here, it points to what preceded in this surah; and if you want the order of revelation, the indication is to those whom the messengers among the earlier messengers knew. The connection here is that the Truth ended the previous verse with His saying there: "And indeed you are among the messengers" (wa innaka lamina al-mursalin). And since "wa innaka lamina al-mursalin" conveys that the Prophet (ﷺ) is a part of a general totality, it is as if He says: Beware lest you think that since they all agree in being messengers, or that they are messengers of Allah, they are also equal in rank. No, rather each one of them has his general rank in excellence and a specific rank in preference. They are all messengers from Allah, but the Truth gives each one of them a specific rank in preference.

So why did Allah's saying "And indeed you are among the messengers" confirm for us that Sayyidina Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among the messengers? Do not take this matter on the basis that all the messengers are equal in standing and say they are alike in merit. No. Allah has preferred some of them over others.

And what is preference (tafdil)?

Preference is that you come to another and give him a distinction. When you give him a merit over others, a person may say to you: "This is favouritism" (muhabat). Therefore we say to whoever says that: Adhere to precision, and know that preference is favouring another with a distinction for the sake of wisdom, whereas favouritism (muhabah) is favouring another with a distinction for the sake of desire and passion. For example, if we want to choose someone for a great post, we choose a number of personalities who may fit the qualifications and we say: "This one is suitable, and this one is suitable, and this one is suitable," and "this one has merits over that one," and so on. If we look at them and evaluate them for the sake of wisdom and competence, this is preference. But if we choose one because he is a relative or a son-in-law or otherwise, this is desire and favouritism.

Preference is that you favour and give a merit, but for wisdom; whereas favouritism is that you favour and give a merit, but for a desire in yourself. For example, suppose you bought a steam boat and rode it with your small son, with the steam boat's driver. Your small son wanted to drive the steam boat, sat in the driver's place and began to steer. But high waves came and the sea became turbulent, so you rose quickly, took the boy, and ordered the driver to take over the command. Here the boy may cry out. Is this favouritism on your part toward the driver? No. If it were favouritism, it would have been toward your son. But you preferred the driver for a wisdom you know, which is that he is more knowledgeable in steering than the small boy. So if you look at the basis of favouring and the basis of distinguishing for wisdom, this is preference; but in favouritism, desire is the ruler.

All the works of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, proceed from wisdom, because He, glorified is He, has no desire and no passion; so all of us are equal in relation to Him. So He, glorified is He, when He gives a merit or gives good or gives excellence, the purpose in it is some wisdom.

And when the Truth said: "And indeed you are among the messengers," He followed it with the noble statement: "Those messengers, We preferred some of them above others," and He gave us examples of preference, saying: "Among them are those to whom Allah spoke." When you hear "Among them are those to whom Allah spoke," Musa (peace be upon him) comes to mind immediately; otherwise Allah, majestic and exalted, has also spoken to the angels.

Then the Truth says: "and some of them He raised by degrees." Then He said: "And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, the clear proofs." He, glorified is He, first specified Musa (peace be upon him) by the predominant attribute, saying: "to whom Allah spoke," and likewise specified Sayyidina Isa (peace be upon him) as one to whom He gave the clear signs. Between Musa (peace be upon him) and Isa (peace be upon him), the Truth said: "and some of them He raised by degrees," and the address in the verses is to Muhammad (ﷺ). So there is speech about another, addressed to Muhammad (ﷺ).

When identification comes by name or by the predominant attribute, the subject is specified; but when it comes by attribute and leaves it to the listener's discernment to return the attribute to its owner, it is understood that His saying "and We raised some of them by degrees" applies in truth only to Muhammad (ﷺ) alone. He, glorified is He, placed it in the middle between Musa (peace be upon him) and Isa (peace be upon him), although the Messenger (ﷺ) did not come in the middle, but came as the last of the prophets; yet you find that his method (ﷺ) is the middle. Judaism has excessed in materialism without spirituality, and Christianity has excessed in spirituality without materiality, and the world needs a middle course between the material and the spiritual; so Muhammad (ﷺ) came, and it is as if Muhammad (ﷺ) is the pivot of the balance in the question of existence.

And if we want to know the bases of preference, we find a messenger whom Allah sends to his village, like Sayyidina Lut for example, and there is a messenger whose mission is limited or whose lifespan of mission is limited; but there is one messenger of whom it was said: "You are sent to humankind and jinn, and to everyone among humankind and jinn until the Hour arises," and that is Muhammad (ﷺ).

So if preference is the field of work, it belongs to Sayyidina Muhammad (ﷺ). And if we look at the miracles which Allah sent down to His messengers so that they might establish for people the truth of their communication from their Lord, we find that all the miracles came as cosmic miracles, that is, material sensory miracles, whoever sees them believes in them. Whoever saw the staff of Musa striking the sea so that it split, this is a material miracle in which the people of Musa believed; and whoever saw Isa (peace be upon him) healing the blind and the leper has witnessed a material miracle and believed in it. But do these miracles now have any existence other than the report about them? No, they have no existence.

But when Allah wills to bring Muhammad (ﷺ) a miracle, He does not bring him a miracle of the kind of sensory things (al-mahassat)(1) which happen once and end. He, glorified is He, sent Muhammad (ﷺ) until the Hour arises, so his mission is unlimited, and his miracle (ﷺ) must be non-sensory but rational, because reason is the common measure among all. For that reason his miracle was the Qur'an. Every person can now say: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and that is his miracle.

The miracle of our Messenger (ﷺ) is a perceptible reality. And regarding the field of applying the method, we find that the messengers did not come to legislate; they only conveyed the rulings from Allah, and it was not for them to legislate. But Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) is the only messenger to whom Allah said:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [59:7].

So He, has specially singled him out with legislation too. Is this not a distinction? The purpose of the heavenly method is to lay down the laws that govern the movement of life in the vicegerency on earth, and those laws are of two types: one type came from Allah, and in this all the messengers are equal; but there is a second type of law, in which Allah delegated to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the right to lay down legislation to suit what he sees, and this is a preference for the Messenger (ﷺ).

So when Allah, exalted is He, says: "and some of them He raised by degrees," this applies only to Sayyidina Muhammad (ﷺ). And this is more than naming explicitly. Let me give an example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: you gave your son an ordinary pen, to your second son a pen of higher value, to your third son a watch, and the fourth son you bought a very expensive gift. Then you come to the children and say: "I bought for so-and-so a fountain pen, and for so-and-so a ballpoint pen, and I bought for so-and-so a watch, and to some of them I bought a precious gift." So "some of them" here is recognized as the fourth son whose name you did not mention, so he has been specified and defined.

"Those messengers, We preferred some of them above others; among them are those to whom Allah spoke." And when you say "to whom Allah spoke," beware of neglecting a universal principle that governs every attribute of Allah found in humans. I speak and Allah speaks; but is His speech like my speech? If you believe my existence is like His existence, then make my speech like His speech; but if my existence is not like His existence, how can my speech be like His speech?

Someone may say: speech is sound, vocal cords and other things. We say to him: No. You do not take what pertains to Allah, glorified is He, except within the frame of "There is nothing like unto Him" (laysa kamithlihi shay'), and we take every attribute that comes from Allah through Allah, and we do not place an attribute from ourselves, and afterwards we do not compare it with an attribute of humans. Allah has life and you have life; but is the life of any of us like His life, glorified is He? No, His life is essential, and the life of each of us is granted and taken away, so it is not like His life.

And when the Truth says:

﴿Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne. You have not, besides Him, any protector or intercessor. Will you not then remember?﴾ [32:4].

So is the sitting of the Truth like the sitting of creation? Or is the throne of the Creator like the throne of the created? Of course not. We, the believers, take every attribute of Allah within the frame of declaring Him far above imperfection: Glory be to Allah, "There is nothing like unto Him"; so Allah's istiwa' is not like the istiwa' of humans, and the sitting of the Truth is not like the sitting of a human being.

And we give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example, both before and after: suppose a friend invited you to eat at his house, then an elder of the people invited you to eat at his house; you will certainly find the food varying in quality and kinds among every hundred tables of those who invited you. So if humans themselves differ in descriptive matters according to their stations, capacities and abilities, then when you elevate the attribute to the Creator of all things, you are certain that He, glorified is He, is exalted above all others, and "There is nothing like unto Him."

So "Allah spoke" (kallama Allah) means that He informed His Messenger by whatever means of communication. "Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and some of them He raised by degrees, and We gave Jesus son of Mary the clear proofs, and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit." The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, always emphasises in speaking of Sayyidina Isa that Isa son of Mary is supported by the Holy Spirit, because the matters Sayyidina Isa faced required that the Holy Spirit always be with him; therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says of him:

﴿And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I am raised alive﴾ [19:33].

In his birth, Sayyidina Isa faced a problem, because he was born in a manner other than the manner of people's birth, and his mother was accused; the Qur'an came and cleared her, declared her innocent, and placed the matter in its true station; and likewise in his death, when they wanted to kill him.

And when we look at
1 Note that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had great sensory miracles; see the book: al-Furqan... by Ibn Taymiyyah...

The sacrifice demanded involves either a person giving of himself or giving of his wealth. For this reason it is fitting here to speak of spending (nafaqah), which is the giving of wealth, especially since in ancient times it was the fighter who had to equip his means of fighting: his horse, his lance, his sword, his arrows, and so he needs spending. The Truth speaks about this matter because the command concerns preserving the cell of faith (khaliyyat al-iman) portrayed in the heavenly method (al-manhaj al-samawi) brought by the messengers, so that this method remains on earth until people return to it when evil or falsehood strikes them. So He says:

﴿O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided you before there comes a Day in which there is no trade, no friendship, and no intercession. And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers.﴾ (254)

We know that every call from the Truth that begins with His saying (O you who have believed) indicates only that what comes after this address is an obligation upon those who have believed in God, and not an obligation upon people in general; for God does not impose an obligation upon the one who disbelieves in Him. God imposes obligations only upon the one who believes in Him, and whoever has passed through that and reached faith's certainty is fit to be addressed by God. It is as though he finds in the Divine words a call saying to him: O you who believed in Me as a God, Wise, Powerful, Legislator for you, I want you to do this matter.

So faith in God is the ground (hathiyyah) of every ruling. So you do it why? Do not say: Because its wisdom is such and such. No. Rather say: Because God in whom I believe commanded me to these acts, whether I understand the wisdom in them or not. Indeed, perhaps your readiness to carry out a command God has given, while you do not understand its wisdom, is stronger in faith than your carrying out a command whose wisdom you know.

If a person were told by a physician: The wine you drink corrupts your liver and does such and such to you, and afterwards he abstained from wine, it is true that his abstention coincided with obedience to God; but did he abstain because God said so? No, he did not abstain because God said, but because the physician said. So his faith in the physician is greater than his faith in the Lord of the physician. The believer, however, says: I do not drink wine because God has forbidden it. And why should I wait until the physician tells me that your liver will be ruined by wine? Mercy lies in the disease not coming in the first place.

The Truth says: (O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided you), meaning: I do not ask you to spend on Me, but spend from My provision to you; for provision comes from a person's activity, and a person's activity needs energy that moves in a thing or a matter, and this movement comes in an arrangement of thought, and this thought was arranged by the One who created it. The limbs that act, the hand that moves, and the foot that walks were created by God, and the matter with which you act is created by God. Let us take the farmer as an example: we find that the earth containing the elements was created by God. So man works with the intellect God created, and plans with the limbs God created, to bring him the energy by which he works upon matter that God created, so that it gives man its good. So what then belongs to man?

Yet even if some good comes to a person from all this, He, glory be to Him, does not say: "It is Mine." Rather I grant it to you, O human, but give Me My right in it. And My right I will not take for Myself, but it belongs to your poor brother. The Truth says:

﴿I do not want provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me.﴾ (Adh-Dhariyat 57)

Beware of saying: What concern is the poor man to me? You must know that poverty (maskanah) is an accident (ard), and an accident may befall you yourself. Do not assume that you will always be the giver, but assume that something may happen to you that makes you take rather than give. The Truth says to you: Give to the poor while you are rich; for He, glory be to Him, will say to people: that they should give to you while you are poor. So consider God's ruling at the hour when it is demanded of you, so that it protects you at the hour when it is demanded for you, and thus the matter is balanced.

Although He, glory be to Him, is the One who provides, He wants you, O servants, to help one another and to love one another, so that rancour is erased from your hearts; for the weak person, weak naturally, not weak through begging, laziness or professional idleness, but weak through inability to work, bearing this is the responsibility of the believers. Glory be to Him and exalted, He makes the strong responsible for helping you when you are weak.

When you see, while you are weak, that the strong who have been given capacity have not forgotten you, and have mentioned you with what they have, then you know you are in a supportive environment that wishes you good. If you see a blessing reaching others which you cannot attain, you do not envy it at all, nor do you harbour spite against its giver; rather you wish, from the sweetness of its effect on your soul, because it came to them out of need, that God had empowered you to return it, and thus society becomes one of mutual solidarity and cooperation.

So when God, exalted is He, says (spend from what We have provided you), you are not donating to God's essence; rather you spend from what He provided you. And of God's grace upon you is that He honoured the effect of your work and attributed it to you, even if your brother is in need. So He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Who is it that would lend to God a goodly loan so He will multiply it for him many times over? And God withholds and extends [provision], and to Him you will be returned.﴾ (Al-Baqarah 245)

The Truth, glory be to Him, has regarded spending in the way of God as a loan from the servant to the Lord, the Creator, the Bestower of every provision. And so that we understand the meaning of spending (nafaqah), I say: we have said before that the word is derived from the root (n-f-q), and it is said: the market was spent (nafaqat al-suq), meaning it ended quickly and the goods in it were exchanged at their fixed prices. We know that trade means an exchange between commodities and prices. The commodity (silʿah) is that which is benefited from directly, and the price (thaman) is that which is not benefited from directly.

So when you are hungry, would it suffice you to have a mountain of gold? This mountain of gold you do not benefit from directly; but your benefit from a loaf of bread is a direct benefit, and likewise a full cup of water, you benefit from directly, and the clothes you wear, you benefit from directly. So that which is benefited from directly is called a commodity, and that which is not benefited from directly we call a price. Therefore the Truth says to us, as a warning and admonition against pride in wealth:

﴿O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided you before there comes a Day in which there is no trade, no friendship, and no intercession. And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers.﴾ (254)

(Al-Baqarah)

The Truth, glory be to Him, alerts us to spend from His provision to us before the Last Day comes, a day in which there is no trade, meaning no room for exchanging prices for commodities or the reverse. Likewise on that day there will be no (khullah), and khullah means pure affection, the relationship that exists between two people so that each becomes connected to the other by love; because each of you is separate from the other, even if affection binds you together, and on the Last Day every person will be occupied with his own affair.

The Last Day has no trade, no buying, no friendship, and no intercession, and these are the outlets on which a person might lean. You do not possess a price with which to buy, and no one else possesses a commodity in the Hereafter; so this door is closed. Likewise there is no friendship or intercession, and this intercession is permitted only: if one is among those whom God has permitted to intercede, it is in God's hand. The word (shafiʿ) is derived from (al-shafʿ) and (al-watr): the odd is one, the even is two, so the intercessor joins his voice to mine so that this need may be fulfilled with so-and-so. A person seeks intercession through someone who has standing with the one interceded with, until what he seeks is carried out for him. But these means do not exist in the Hereafter. So there is no trade, no friendship, and no intercession; so if you spend, you have guarded yourselves against that day, so seize the opportunity before there comes a day in which there is no trade, no friendship, and no intercession.

These are the doors of salvation presumed by humans, which are closed on that great day. It is as though the Truth, glory be to Him, says: I have not missed an opportunity for My creatures; My creatures are those who wronged themselves and placed themselves in this position, so I have not wronged them. Therefore the Truth concludes the verse with His saying: (And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers).

The commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 255:

After Allah, glorified and exalted be He, spoke of the messengers, of disagreement, of fighting to establish the path of truth, and of spending, He now clarifies for us the correct faith-based outlook in whose light all these matters came. The procession of all the divine messages came for the sake of this method, and so He, glorified be He, said:

﴿Allah—there is no god but Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation does not tire Him. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ 255

Let us now pause in reflection at His true saying: (Allah, there is no god but Him). The word (Allah) is a proper name denoting the Necessarily Existent (wājib al-wujūd). When we say (Allah), the mind turns to the Essence that necessarily exists.

What is meant by (necessarily existent)? Existence is of two kinds: that which is necessary (wājib), and that which is contingent (mumkin). The necessary kind is that which must exist. When Allah, the Exalted, informed us of His name (Allah), He gave us the notion that this word is one by which He challenges that anything else be named with it. Had we all been believers, our respect for this challenge would have arisen from faith. But here are disbelievers, rebels and atheists who say: (Allah is a myth). Yet, does any of them dare to name himself (Allah)?

None of them does this, because Allah has issued this challenge, and none has dared to enter into this test. The reluctance of the disbelievers and atheists to enter this test is evidence that their disbelief is not firmly rooted in their souls. Had their disbelief been sound, they would have said: "We will name ourselves and see what happens." But this has not happened.

Thus (Allah) is the name of the Necessarily Existent, possessing all the attributes of perfection. Then He brought the fundamental matter, which is His saying, exalted be He: (there is no god but Him). Here we find negation and we find affirmation: negation in (there is no god), and affirmation in (but Him). Negation is takhliyah (clearing away), and affirmation is tahliyah (adorning). He, glorified be He, cleared Himself of any partner, then affirmed His oneness for us. And (there is no god but Him) means: there is no one worthy of worship except Allah. We know that some of mankind, in times of heedlessness, have worshipped idols and worshipped the stars. But were these gods in truth, or in falsehood? They were gods in falsehood. The evidence for the truth of this proposition, which is (there is no god but Allah), meaning there is no one worthy of worship but Allah, is that none of those gods objected to the truth of this proposition. Thus this statement is truth and sincerity.

If anyone claims otherwise, we say to him: Allah has informed us that there is no one worthy of worship besides Him, because He is the One who created and the One who provides, and He said: "I am the One who created." If this statement is true, then He is truthful in it, and we worship none but Him. If this statement is not true, and some other than Him is the One who created this universe, then where is this One who created, and who then left the one who did not create to take the universe from Him and say: "I am the One who created the universe"? This is a matter of one of two things. The first: there is no other god besides Him, so the matter is settled. The second: were there other gods, and then one came and said: "I am the god, and there is no god but me." Where are those other gods? Did they not know of this story?

If they did not know of it, they are not fit to be gods. And if they knew of it, why did they not say: "No. We are the gods, and this speech is a lie"? And just as Allah sent messengers with miracles, He would have had to send a messenger with miracles. So the one who makes a claim, if no opponent appears against him, the claim is established until a challenger arises.

Thus the statement (there is no god but Allah) carries its own proof of truthfulness: either this statement is true and sincere, and the matter ends, or it is not true, and then where is the god who created and who ought to be worshipped, after hearing the one who came to take this matter from him? And after that we hear from him no sound and no movement, he does not speak, and we know nothing of him, so what is his state? Either he did not know, and so is not fit to be a god, or he knew and did not will, and then he has no power. Therefore our Lord, glorified be He, brings this matter from another angle, saying:

﴿Say: If there were gods with Him, as they say, they would surely have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne. Glory be to Him, exalted far above what they say, with supreme exaltation.﴾ (Surah al-Isra' 42–43).

If those alleged gods had any manifestations of power, they would have gone to Allah, glorified be He, and denied His divinity. And if there were a god other than Allah, a battle would have occurred between the gods, but this has not happened. So the word (there is no god but Allah) is true in itself, even according to those who deny it, and the proof in it is the absence of any challenger to this claim, because if no challenger exists, it is established that He, glorified be He, is the only God. And if a challenger were to exist, we say: where is he? Let me give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: suppose we are in a gathering, and then we find a wallet, so we display it to those present, and we find no owner for it. Then one who was with us came out and said: "O people, while I was sitting with you my wallet was lost." And since none of us claimed it for himself, it is therefore his wallet.

Thus (there is no god but Allah) is a proposition filled with sincerity and truth, and Allah is the Worshipped One toward whom worship is directed, and worship is obedience. The meaning of "worshipper" is one who obeys, and every obedience entails a command and entails a prohibition. Since worship entails a command and entails a prohibition, the one commanded and the one prohibited must be capable of doing and capable of not doing. So when we say to him: do such-and-such as a method of faith, he is capable of not doing it. And when we say to him: do not do it, he is capable of doing it. For if he were not capable of not doing, would one say to him "do"? No, one would not say that to him. And if he were not capable of doing, would one say to him "do not"? That would not be possible.

Thus it must be that he is capable of both this and that, otherwise the command and the prohibition would be futile, with no purpose behind them. Therefore, when they wished to restrict Islam to the ritual acts of worship, which are the testimony that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and the prayer, the fasting, the zakat and the hajj, they said: "Is this all of Islam?" and said: "It is a religion that relies only on outward appearances." We said to them: No, Islam is every movement in life that suits the vicegerency of man on earth, because Allah says in His noble Book:

﴿He produced you from the earth and made you inhabit it﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah Hud).

("And made you inhabit it") means He asked you to cultivate it. So every movement in life that leads to the cultivation of the earth is part of worship. Do not take worship to be only fasting and prayer, for the prayer, the fasting and the others are the pillars upon which the movement of life will stand, on which Islam will be built. If you made Islam to be only these pillars, you would have made Islam a foundation without a structure. These are the pillars on which Islam is built. So Islam is everything that suits the vicegerency of man on earth. This is clarified and confirmed by the saying of Allah, exalted be He:

﴿He produced you from the earth and made you inhabit it﴾ (part of verse 61, Surah Hud).

And some people come out to us saying: "We have nothing but to worship and not to work." We say to any of them: how much time does the prayer take from you in a day? An hour, for example. And zakat, how much does it take from you, in the year, one day? And the fast, how much time does it take from you? The daylight hours of the days of one month. And the obligation of hajj, does it take from you more than one journey in your lifetime? So by Allah, what do you do with the rest of your life after that, which is much? You do not take more than an hour a day for prayer, and you do not take more than a day a year for paying zakat, and you spend a month a year fasting its daylight hours, and you perform hajj once in your life. Then what do you do with the rest of the time? You eat and you wear clothes; you seek a loaf of bread for food, so who will make it for you? This loaf passes through stages until it becomes a morsel you eat, and it requires more knowledge, more movement, and more energy.

The shop that only sells it and does not bake it needs a glass front or something similar, and there must be someone working there who goes with his cart to the bakery to fetch the bread, carries it to the shop and sells it. And if you look at the oven, you will find several stages of delivering and receiving the flour, then to the dough, and to the fire fuelled by diesel, and workers who do this need someone to plan for them. And before that, the flour was just grains, and they were ground to become flour, and there are engineers who run the mills that grind and who work on their maintenance. And after that, the land in which the wheat grew, and how it was ploughed, prepared for planting, irrigated, fertilised, sown, and harvested, and how the husks and ears were threshed, and how they are then winnowed to separate the grains from the chaff, and the grains are packed, and so on?

Consider how much effort went into the loaf of bread you eat, how many energies and how many men at work. So how can you accept that they make it for you while you only sit to pray and fast? No, beware of taking the work of others without effort of your own.

Another example: you wear a robe. How much spinning, weaving and thread did this robe take? So do not sit idle, and benefit from the movement of those who move in life, and say: "I was created only for worship." This is not worship; rather, worship is that you obey Allah in all He commands, and that you refrain from all He forbids, within the framework of His saying, exalted be He: (He produced you from the earth and made you inhabit it). Every work counts as worship, otherwise you will be a "good-for-nothing" (tanbal) in existence. True faith requires you to benefit from your work and not depend on the work of others.

Allah, glorified and exalted be He, has appointed us as vicegerents on earth in order that we cultivate it. And among the goodness of worship is that we perfect every work, and by this we do not only establish the pillars of Islam, but establish the pillars and the structure together. Thus we will have discharged the responsibility of faith, and every act of ours will correspond to our saying: (there is no god but Allah).

We have known that the word (Allah) is the proper name denoting the Necessarily Existent, and it is the name Allah chose for Himself and informed us of, and Allah has many names, as related in the hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: Allah has names, ninety-nine names... [the commentary continues]

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 256:

Then the Exalted and Majestic Lord says:

﴿There is no compulsion in religion. The right course has become clear from the wrong. So whoever disbelieves in the Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold, which will never break. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾

The Truthful Lord (al-Haqq subhanahu wa ta'ala) clarifies for us, the believing servants and all of mankind, that: "There is no compulsion in religion." Ikrah (compulsion) is to force another to do an act which he does not see as good for him to do. That is, the person being compelled does not see any good in it until he does it.

But there are things we do with those around us for their benefit: for example, forcing children to study, and this is for the children's good; and forcing sick children to take medicine. Such matters are not compulsion; rather, they are things we do for the benefit of those around us, because no one is pleased to remain ill.

Compulsion is to force another to do an act in which he does not see good by the standard of sound reason. Therefore the Truthful Lord says: "There is no compulsion in religion." The meaning of this verse is that Allah did not compel His creation, though He is their Creator, to a religion. It was possible for Allah to subdue the chosen human being, as He subdued the heavens and the earth, the animals, the plants and the inanimate objects, and no one could disobey His command. So He, glorified is He, says:

﴿Had Allah willed, He would have guided all mankind.﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd 13:31).

But the Truth wants to know whoever comes to Him as a loving, free chooser, not one who is overpowered. Coming under coercion establishes His power, but does not establish His being beloved. Whoever comes to Him willingly, while able not to come, that is a proof of love. So He, exalted is He, says: "There is no compulsion in religion," meaning: I did not establish the principle of compulsion, and if I willed, everyone on earth would believe, all of them together. Do the messengers whom He sent, glorified is He, volunteer to compel people? No. The Messenger came to convey from Allah, not to compel people; and He, glorified is He, has made His creatures free to choose. Otherwise, had He compelled them, He would not have sent the messengers. Therefore the Lord, mighty and majestic, says:

﴿And had your Lord willed, all those on earth would have believed, all of them together. Would you then compel mankind until they become believers?﴾ (Surah Yunus 10:99).

The Messenger has the task of conveying from Allah, because Allah did not want His creatures compelled to adopt religion. Therefore the one who conveys from Him does not compel His creatures to adopt religion. However, there is a confusion here. There is a difference between compulsion regarding religion and compulsion regarding what religion requires, and this is where the disagreement arises.

You say to a Muslim: "Why do you not pray?" He says to you: "There is no compulsion in religion," claiming to be cultured, and brings you this verse to silence you with it. So you say to him: No. "There is no compulsion in religion" concerns belief and faith. But if you believe and declare that you have believed in Allah and have become a Muslim with us, you must know that if you break one of the rulings of Islam, we demand that you fulfil it. You are free to believe or not to believe, but when you have committed yourself to faith, you bear the responsibility of carrying out what faith requires; otherwise your conduct is counted as one of the conduct of Islam. So if you drink wine, you are free, because you are a disbeliever, for example. But do you believe and then drink wine?! No. By that you break one of the limits of Allah, and you deserve the punishment.

And since, as a sensible, rightly guided person, you have come to know what Islam requires, you must carry out what Islam requires. Therefore Allah did not impose obligation on a human being before his mind matured through puberty, lest it be said that Allah took someone to faith and bound him to it before his intellect was complete. Rather, He left obligation until the human being matures and is complete. When he enters the sphere of obligation, he knows its requirements, and he is free to enter faith or not to enter it; but if he enters, he will be held to account. So let no one, when he hears one of the rulings of religion, say: "There is no compulsion in religion," because this verse was revealed concerning the basic creed. If you follow this creed, it becomes incumbent upon you to fulfil its requirements. The enemies of Islam wanted to escalate this matter, and they said falsely and fabricatedly: Islam spread by the sword.

We say to them: Allah willed that Islam should begin weak, and that those who first embraced it should be persecuted with every kind of persecution; they were tortured, expelled from their homes, their wealth and their families, and they were unable to do anything. So the period of weakness that Islam passed through at first was an intended period.

We also say to them: Who compelled and forced the first bearer of the sword to bear the sword?! The Muslims were weak and overpowered, unable to protect themselves. You fall into contradictions when you say that Islam was spread by the sword. They speak of the jizya, rejecting it. We say: What is the jizya that Islam took from non-Muslims as a tax for their defence? The Muslims used to take the jizya from the lands entered by the Islamic conquest, meaning that there were people who remained upon their religion. And as long as there are people who remain upon their religion, this is proof that Islam did not compel anyone.

Allah's saying "There is no compulsion in religion" has as its reason that the right course is clear and the wrong course is clear; and as long as the matter is clear, compulsion does not arise. For compulsion comes at a time of confusion, and there is no confusion here. Therefore the Truth says: "The right course has become clear from the wrong." And since the right course is distinct from the wrong, there is no compulsion. But Allah gives you the proofs, and you, O human being, with your intellect, can choose, so that you know that if you enter the religion you will be bound by it and held to account for entering it. So do not enter except while believing and certain that this is the Truth, because it will entail that you accept the rulings of the religion upon you.

("There is no compulsion in religion; the right course has become clear from the wrong.") Al-rushd (the right course) is the path of salvation, and al-ghayy (the wrong course) is the path of destruction. The Truth, clarifying the right and the wrong, says in another verse of the Noble Qur'an:

﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant in the earth without right; and if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they see the way of right guidance, they will not take it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf 7:146).

The Truth teaches us that those who are arrogant in the earth without right will not be able to attain the sight of Allah's signs and the proofs of His power; and even if they see the correct path, they will not walk in it, and if they witness the way of misguidance, they will take to it, because they deny the signs of the Most Merciful and are heedless of them.

Al-ghayy also means losing the way. When a person walks in the desert and loses the way, it is said of him: "So-and-so has gone astray" (ghawa), that is, he has lost the correct direction of travel, and he may be exposed to many dangers, such as meeting wild beasts and other things. The Truth clarifies the way of rushd in another utterance, in His saying:

﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth, or whether their Lord intends for them rushd (right guidance).﴾ (Surah al-Jinn 72:10).

The jinn assumed, as some of the company of mankind assumed, that Allah would not raise anyone after death, or would not send a messenger from among mankind to guide the universe. The jinn sought to reach the heaven and found it filled with guards of angels and blazing meteors. The jinn do not know the secret of guarding the heaven, nor whether there is evil in it for mankind or whether Allah intended for them good and guidance. So rushd, with the rā' vocalised with a ḍamma and the shīn with a sukūn (ruhd), and rashad, with the rā' and the shīn both vocalised with a fatḥa, both clarify the path leading to salvation. Its opposite is al-ghayy.

The Truth continues: "So whoever disbelieves in the Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold." First: we notice that the Truth here has placed disbelief in the Taghut before belief in Allah, because the matter requires takhliya (emptying) first and tahliya (filling) second. A person must empty himself of the Taghut, so that he does not enter claiming to believe in Allah while the Taghut is in his heart. Before we iron the garment, we wash it and clean it; emptying comes before filling.

And what is the Taghut? It is from the root ṭ-gh-y (ṭagha, to transgress), and the word ṭāghūt is an intensive form of transgression. He did not say ṭāgh, but ṭāghūt, like jabarūt. The Taghut may be applied to Satan; it may be applied to those who grant themselves the right to legislate, declaring disbelief and attributing to whomever they wish faith according to their whims, and giving things by temporal authority of their own; it is also applied to sorcerers and charlatans, and to anyone who transgresses and exceeds the limit in anything. So the word ṭāghūt is an intensive form, and this intensification may take many colours: sometimes the transgressor is a satan, sometimes a priest, sometimes a sorcerer or charlatan, and sometimes a ruler.

The root ṭ-gh-w indicates that the one described by it is one whose obedience to him increases his transgression. When he tests you in a small matter and you obey him in it, he increases in transgression over you through that obedience. The Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So he made light of his people and they obeyed him; indeed they were a corrupt people.﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf 43:54).

He then increases the matter until he becomes a tyrant, and no one begins his work with overt, lofty transgression; rather the matter starts step by step, like any oppressive dictatorial regime. It begins by "feeling the pulse"; if the people endure, the regime grows in harshness until it becomes a taghut. So the Taghut is the one whom obedience increases in transgression. It is applied to Satan, because he is the foundation; to those who speak in the name of religion for temporal power (whether they are priests or others); and to those who practise sorcery and charlatanry, because they transgressed by what they knew; they use things by which they weary people. The word has come here in the intensive form because it includes all these meanings. If we survey the word in the Qur'an, we find that al-Ṭāghūt occurs in the masculine in some places, and it occurs in the feminine in one verse of the Qur'an:

﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it, and turn in repentance to Allah, for them is good news; so give good news to My servants.﴾ (Surah al-Zumar 39:17).

This verse has clarified that they have abandoned every kind of transgression and its categories; that is, those who avoid the many colours of transgression are those who direct pure worship to Allah, and for them is good news. "So whoever disbelieves in the Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold." The word istamsaka (has grasped firmly) differs from masaka (held). For istamsaka indicates that there is striving in the grasping, and the one who adheres to religion needs striving in adhering; because Satan will not leave him. It is not enough to hold; you must hold firmly. Whenever Satan whispers to you about something, you must hold firmly to religion. This shows that there is struggle and back-and-forth.

"Has grasped the handhold" (al-'urwa): the 'urwa is the hook or handle, as we say "the handle of the bucket" (′urwat al-dalw), which you grip from it. This is usually made of braided, sturdy rope. Al-wuthqā is the feminine of al-awthaq, that is, a matter that is trusted. His saying "has grasped the most trustworthy handhold" may be a comparison with the handle of the bucket, because a person uses the bucket to bring water, and by water is the life of the body; and by religion is the life of values.

"Has grasped the most trustworthy handhold": it is as if, when the word 'urwa comes, the bucket comes to mind, and the bucket brings water, and by water is the life of the body. So these give us clear imaginative suggestions. "Has grasped the most trustworthy handhold." And since it is a trustworthy handhold, which is religion and faith in Allah, and since it is religion and the rope of Allah, it is trustworthy; and since it is trustworthy, there is no severance (infiṣām) for it. We must know that there is infiṣām and inqiṣām, the first with fā' and the second with qāf.

Infiṣām (breaking off, dislocation): it prevents internal connection, as when a hand is broken but remains hanging. Inqiṣām (snapping apart): that each part goes far from the other, that is, there is separation. The Truth says: "There is no infiṣām for it, and Allah is Hearing and Knowing," which suggests that the operation of the Taghut will always be a whisper, and this whisper is the sound that entices with smooth speech. That is why the expression "the whisper of Satan" (waswasat al-shayṭān) was taken from the whisper of ornaments (waswasat al-ḥulī), and the whisper of gold is the ringing of gold, that is, an alluring whisper like the whisper of Satan. And Allah is Knowing of every matter.

God says next:

﴿Allah is the Protector (walī) of those who believe; He brings them out of the darknesses into the light. As for those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Taghut (false deities/tyrants); they bring them out of the light into the darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; therein they will abide forever.﴾ [2:257]

Indeed, Allah is the Protector of those who believe, as long as... ﴿Whoever disbelieves in the Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most reliable handhold﴾. It is as though the Truth were explaining this by this verse: as long as the servant is connected to the most reliable handhold and holds fast to it, and this is one that has no severance, then his guardianship has become Allah's. The word walī, when you hear it, comes from (waliya), meaning that one thing follows another without a separation: this comes right after that. And since it follows it without any separation, it is the nearest to it. And since it is the nearest to it, it is the first to rush to rescue. A person may walk with me, and if my foot slips I call out to him, because he is the nearest to me, and he is the one who will come to my aid.

So there is no separation, and since there is no separation, he is the first you call upon, and the first to whom you turn without having to cry out to him; for you do not say to the one beside you, "Take my hand"; rather he takes your hand of his own accord, without even noticing. Thus the phrase ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾, when you consider it, is found to harmonise also with ﴿All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾. He does not want you to call out to Him, because there is someone you shout to for rescue, but you will not shout to Him, because He is All-Hearing and All-Knowing: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾.

The word walī also comes from mawlā and from wāli. ﴿Walī of those who believe﴾ means He is the one who takes charge of their affairs, as you say: "The wāli is the one who has taken charge of the subjects' matters." The word mawlā is sometimes applied to a master and sometimes to his servant, and therefore the poet says:

"Your mawlā, O my mawlā, is seeking a need"

that is, your servant, O my master, is seeking a need. It is used in interrelated meanings, because we have said walī means "near." If the servant is in need of something, who is the first to help him? His master. And if the master calls, who is the first to answer him? His servant. So it is applied to the master, applied to the servant, and applied to the governor: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾. His saying, ﴿those who believe﴾, means a group containing many individuals, as if He wants those who believe to make their belief one thing, not many; or that the protection of Allah for each individual is protection for all the believers. And as long as they are believers, there is no conflict among the protections, because they all proceed from and act upon one belief, one method, one saying, one action, and one movement.

And how is ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe﴾? He is their walī, meaning their helper, their lover, their answerer, and their supporter. He is their walī by the proofs He made clear to them for belief. Is there any love greater than this? Did He leave us to search for the proofs, or did He draw our attention to the proofs?

This is one of the forms of Allah's protection. Before we believed, He placed the proofs for us; when we believed, He stood by us with help; and if our enemies fight us, He is with us; and after that the protection continues until He gives us the fullest reward in the Hereafter. So He is a walī in every stage: before belief, a walī through the proofs; with belief, a continuing support, our helper against our enemies and His; and in the Hereafter, our walī through love and giving, giving us an unlimited gift. Thus His protection never ends.

﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of the darknesses into the light﴾. He, glory be to Him, brings them out of the darknesses of ignorance into the light of faith, because darknesses usually obliterate what is seen. You cannot see anything unless there is light coming from the thing seen, that is, rays reaching you. If there is darkness, it means no rays come from things, so you do not see them; and when light comes, you distinguish things. This is in sensible matters; and likewise in matters of values: ﴿He brings them out of the darknesses into the light, and those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Taghut; they bring them out of the light into the darknesses.﴾

Have they entered the light, O our Lord? We may understand that what is meant here is the apostates whom Satan whispered to and led into the darknesses of disbelief after they had been believers; or ﴿they bring them out of the light into the darknesses﴾, meaning they stand between them and the light and prevent them from faith, as one person says:

"Did you not know that my father expelled me from his inheritance?" That means he had the right to inherit, and his father expelled him from the inheritance. This applies to those who abandoned faith and preferred the darknesses. The Qur'an clarifies the matter of coming out of darkness into light, and from disbelief into faith, in other passages, such as the words of our master Joseph to the two young men who were with him in prison:

﴿And there entered with him into the prison two youths. One of them said, "Indeed, I see myself pressing wine," and the other said, "Indeed, I see myself carrying bread on my head, of which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you are among the doers of good." He said, "No food will come to you that you are provided with except that I will inform you of its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah and are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers."﴾ (Surah Yusuf)

Was Joseph then in the religion of the disbelieving people and afterward left it? No; he had never entered into the religion of the people who do not believe in Allah. That religion was before him, but he left it, refused to enter it, and adhered to the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him. In the expression there is what emphasises freedom of choice. There is another verse in which the Truth says:

﴿And Allah created you, then causes you to die; and among you is one who is returned to the feeblest age so that he knows, after knowledge, nothing. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent.﴾ (Surah al-Nahl)

The meaning of the verse is that Allah created us all and decreed for each of us a term: some of us die young, and some of us reach the feeblest age, and return to weakness, their cells of vigour diminish, and they no longer know what they used to know. The verse does not mean that a person exists in the feeblest age and then is returned to childhood. When the Truth says, ﴿those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Taghut; they bring them out of the light into the darknesses﴾, the Truth has mentioned "protectors" here in connection with the Taghut, because, as we have said, the Taghut has many forms: Satan is a taghut, the Dajjal is a taghut, the sorcerer is a taghut. The Truth gave the predicate in the singular, "the Taghut," for a plural subject, "their protectors," and described these protectors of the Taghut as bringing those who disbelieved out of the light into the darknesses.

Allah made the Taghut singular and used the plural for the individuals whom the Taghut moves into the darknesses. Why did Allah not say here "tawāghīt" instead of "Taghut"? The word Taghut is treated here as we say "so-and-so is just" or "the two men are just" or "the men are just." On this analogy the word Taghut came: Satan, the Dajjal, the soothsayer, the sorcerer, and the ruler who rules by other than Allah's command are all taghut. The verse kept to the singular and masculine. The word Taghut applies to one, two, or a group; that is, those who bring out into the darknesses from the light are the protectors of the Taghut, or those who have taken the taghuts as protectors, and they are abiding forever in the Fire. Entry into the Fire applies to the taghuts and also to the followers of the taghuts, as the Truth says in His Book:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell; you will be its certain entrants.﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya')

The followers of the taghuts, and the taghuts, are in the Fire of Hell. May Allah protect us and you from its punishment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 258:

The Almighty wishes to give us a realistic picture in the universe of His saying: "Allah is the Protector (wali) of those who believe." He is the Protector and the Helper, so He says:

﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said, "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west." So the one who disbelieved was overwhelmed. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ [2:258]

When you hear "Have you not considered" (ألم تر), you know that it is composed of a hamza, which is (أ), and a negative particle, which is (لم), and the negated verb is (تر). The hamza here comes for denunciation (inkar), and denunciation is a negation with reproach. But it has not entered upon an affirmative verb such that it would be said that it denies the verb after it, just as you say to a child: "Do you hit your father!" Here the hamza has come not to ask a question but to deny this deed, because the verb after it is affirmative, which is (تضرب), and the hamza has come before it, so it is called "the hamza of denunciation" (hamzat inkar) for reproach. Thus denunciation is: negation with reproach when it enters upon a negated verb.

Since denunciation is a negation and the verb after it is negated, it is as if you have negated the negation, and so you have affirmed it. It is as if He, glorified is He, when He says to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Have you not considered" (ألم تر), the meaning is "you have seen." Why did He not say to him: "Have you seen" (أرأيت)? He came with the negative form so that it would have greater impact, for the coming of the affirmative may be a prompting of the one being questioned. When a friend says to you: "You did not ask about me, and you neglect me," you may reply to him saying: "Did I not help you when you were weak? Did I not take you by the hand when you were sick?"

You had already offered your services to this friend, but you want to deny the negation that he is stating, and thus we know that the negation of a negation is an affirmation. Therefore we take from His saying, exalted is He, in this expression (ألم تر) the meaning: you saw. Seeing is by the eye. Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was the first addressee of the Noble Qur'an from his Lord, see this event in the days of Abraham? Certainly not. So "Have you not considered" (ألم تر) here comes to mean: "Have you not known?"

Why did He come with "Have you not considered" here? He came with it so that we know that when Allah says "Have you not known," it is as if you are seeing what He informs you of, and you must take it as confirmed as if you had seen it with your own eye. The eye is one of your senses, and the sense may deceive, but your Lord does not deceive. So "Have you not considered" means: "Have you not known with certain knowledge (علم اليقين)," and it is as if you had seen what Allah informs you of. Therefore He, exalted is He, says to the Messenger:

﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾ [105:1] (Surat al-Fil).

The Messenger was born in the Year of the Elephant, so he did not see this event, yet it is as if Allah informs him of it and says to him: "Have you not known?" And it is as if He says to him: "Know with certain knowledge as if you see it, for your Lord is more trustworthy than your eyes." When it is said "Have you not considered" (ألم تر), what is meant is "Have you not considered such-and-such." But the Truth said: "Have you not considered to the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord" (ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه), and the use of the particle "to" (إلى) here points to a strange matter that has occurred. An example of this is what we sometimes say: "Have you not seen how Zayd does such-and-such?" It is as if what Zayd did is a strange matter, and it draws attention to attending to the end of the matter, because "to" (إلى) indicates reaching an endpoint, as if the matter has reached the extreme of wonder. So do not take it as if you had merely seen it, but look at its outcome in what happened.
