The Truth says here: "Have you not considered to the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord," and "to" (إلى) has come here to show that this is a matter that has reached a far extreme of wonder, and indeed it has reached a far extreme of wonder. Glorified and exalted is He, He did not tell us who that man was who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because identifying him does not concern us, whether he was Nimrod or someone else.

If some exegetes go to the saying that he was a king named Nimrod, we say to them: "Thank you for your effort, but if Allah had wished to specify the man's name, He would have specified it for us." What concerns us is that he was one who rose up against Allah's Messenger Abraham (peace be upon him) and disputed with him on this matter, and identifying him here is not necessary. When the Almighty wishes a matter to be general and possible to occur at any time or place, Allah does not specify it, so any person in any place may argue with any believer. It is not so with any specification or determination. An example of this is those who want to know the story of the People of the Cave, asking: where, when, how many were they, and who were they?

We say: if one of these questions were answered, the story would be spoiled, because if we specify its time, someone will come and say to you: "The time in which the story took place allowed such a thing." If we specify the place, another will say: "The place allowed this matter." If we specify the persons by their names, so-and-so and so-and-so, a third will say: "Such personalities could produce such behavior. And how can we have the strength of faith of these?"

The Truth did not specify the time, the place, or the persons, and brought them in an undetermined form to show that any youths in any time and any place who say what they say, and if He had specified them in one, the purpose would be spoiled. Let us consider the precision of the Truth when He struck an example for those who disbelieved with the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, when He, majestic and exalted, said:

﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, so they availed them nothing against Allah, and it was said, "Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾ [66:10] (Surat al-Tahrim).

He did not specify for us the name of either of these two women, but mentioned only the important matter, which is that each of them was the wife of a noble messenger, yet each of them insisted on disbelief, so they both entered the Fire. But when the Truth, exalted is He, wished to single out an event that will never recur at any time or place, He mentioned Mary with clear specification and naming when He said:

﴿And Mary, daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit, and she affirmed the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was of the devoutly obedient.﴾ [66:12] (Surat al-Tahrim).

Why did the Truth specify Mary by name and the event? Because the occurrence cannot be repeated by any other woman. Specification here is obligatory, because no woman will bear a child without a husband except this one. But if the matter will recur at any time or place, He, glorified is He, mentions its general description. An example of this is the saying of the Truth: "Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham" (ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم), and He did not tell us who he is. The word "argued" (حاجّ) originally is (حاجج), like (قاتل) and (شارك). When there are two identical letters, we make the first one sukun and assimilate the second into it for lightness, so it becomes (حاج), and (حاج) is from the pattern (فاعل), which comes for mutuality (المشاركة), and so that we understand the meaning of "mutuality" (المشاركة), here is this example:

We say: "Zayd fought (قاتل) 'Amr," or we say: "'Amr fought Zayd," and the meaning of that is that each of them fought, and both are doer and object at the same time, but we give precedence to the aspect of doer in one, and the aspect of object in the second, even though each of them is both doer and object.

Another example: when we say "Zayd partnered (شارك) 'Amr," and "'Amr partnered Zayd," so the mutuality comes from both: this is doer and this is object, but we usually give the agent quality to the one who initiated, and the object quality to the second, even if the second is also a doer. Therefore the poet, when he wants to describe the condition of a person walking in a place full of many snakes, and wary that a snake might bite him, said:

The feet have made peace with the snakes from him,
the viper and the cobra (الشجاع القشعما).

Here the poet describes for us a person who walked in a place full of snakes, and a person usually fears that a snake will bite him, but this person described in this verse, we find that the snakes have made peace with his foot, that is, they did not bite him because he did not provoke them, and snakes usually do not bite except one who initiates them by provocation. We find here that the doer is the snakes, because they made peace with his foot. It is also correct to say that the foot is what made peace with the snakes.

We know from the rules of the language what we studied in the past, which is called (البدل), and the apposition (البدل) takes the ruling of what it replaces. If the replaced element is nominative, the apposition comes nominative; if the replaced element is accusative, the apposition comes accusative; and if the replaced element is genitive, the apposition is likewise. Here in this verse the word "the snakes" (الحيات) came nominative, but "the viper" (الأفعوان) came accusative in the verse, although it is an apposition to the nominative "the snakes," because he noticed in it also the quality of object, so he put it in the accusative. Also it is possible to read "the snakes" in the accusative and "the foot" in the nominative, because each of them is both doer and object in terms of making peace.

Likewise in the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: "Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord." We note that the word "Abraham" (إبراهيم) comes in the noble verse in the accusative with a fatha, that is, the quality of object predominates over it. So who argued with Abraham? It is a certain person, and he is the doer, because he is the one who initiated the argument. Thus the noble verse guides us, and the verse describes that man: "because Allah had given him kingship," that is, that man had been granted kingship by Allah, and this man argued with Abraham about his Lord. It is as if this man is the one who began the argument, saying to Abraham: "Who is your Lord?"

Abraham (peace be upon him) said: "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death." This is the excellence of the Qur'an in leaving a matter in trust that the hearer will refer everything to its origin. So the saying of the Truth: "When Abraham said, 'My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death,'" it is as if the one who argued with Abraham asked him: "Who is your Lord?" and Abraham said: "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death."

We may note that this verse came after the saying of the Truth in the previous verse: "Allah is the Protector of those who believe," and protection (الولاية) is help, support, and aid. He, glorified is He, wishes to show us how Allah aided Abraham against the one who argued with him. However, the one who argued with Abraham entered into labyrinths of sophistry after he heard Abraham's saying: "My Lord is the one who gives life and causes death." The Truth brought "gives life and causes death" because that is a matter which no one has claimed to have done, and no one has claimed to be a partner in it; even the disbelievers, if you ask them: "Who created?" they say: "Allah."

So this is a settled matter. However, the adversary who argued with Abraham wanted to move the argument to a sophistic shift. Sophistry, as we know, is speech that prolongs disputation without end.

The man who argued with Abraham (peace be upon him) said: "If your Lord is the one who gives life and causes death, then I give life and cause death."

Abraham (peace be upon him) asked him: "How do you give life and cause death?"

The man said: "I am able to kill whichever prisoners I have and able not to kill them, so the one I did not kill, it is as if I gave him life, and the one I killed, I caused him to die."

Our master Abraham did not say, "Let us first agree what is life? And what is death?" Because Abraham, the Friend of the Merciful, did not wish to prolong this disputation, so he brought him a matter that would bridle him from the beginning and end the argument, and he said to him: "Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west," and "the one who disbelieved was overwhelmed." Thus our master Abraham ended this argument. It was possible for our master Abraham to enter into an argument with him and say: "What is life?"

We know that life is giving matter that which makes it moving, sensitive, willing, and choosing, while death is the departure of the soul from the body. The one who kills a person only takes his soul out of his body, and killing differs from death, because death is the departure of the soul from the body without a wound, or breaking of structure, or an act that a person does to his body such as suicide.

A person may be sitting in his place and his life ends and he dies, and no one before that is able to say to him: "Die," and he dies. This is death. But the taking of the soul by a grievous wound or breaking of structure is killing and not death. Therefore Allah makes killing the counterpart of death, in His saying, exalted is He:

{Muhammad is not but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all, and Allah will reward the grateful. And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah, a decree with a specified term. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof; and We will reward the grateful}

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-Baqarah, verse 259:

The Truth (al-Haqq) expounds the matter from which Abraham turned aside, which is death and life. So He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Or like the one who passed by a town, and it was fallen down upon its roofs. He said, "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then resurrected him. He said, "How long have you remained?" He said, "I have remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you have remained a hundred years. But look at your food and your drink, they have not spoiled; and look at your donkey. And We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones, how We raise them and then clothe them with flesh." And when it became clear to him, he said, "I know that Allah is over all things competent." ﴾ 259

When we look at the beginning of the verse, we find it begins with (أو) "or". What follows "or" is coordinated with what precedes it, so it is as if the Truth is saying to us: "Or (have you not seen) like the one who passed by a town."

When you hear the word (قرية) "town/village", it denotes a gathering of people living in a limited place, and we understand that the one who passed by this town was not one of its inhabitants; rather, he passed by it as a traveller on a journey. We also notice that the Truth, glorified is He, did not wish to tell us the name of the town or the name of the one who passed by it.

Some said: he was Irmiya ibn Hilqiya, or he was al-Khidr, or he was Uzayr. We have said before that when the Truth leaves something unspecified, its meaning is: do not individualize the matter, so that it may happen to anyone.

(Or like the one who passed by a town). They said: it is Bayt al-Maqdis. (And it was fallen down upon its roofs). To understand the meaning of "fallen down upon its roofs", we should know that when I say (أنا خويان) "I am empty", meaning (أنا بطني خاوية) "my stomach is empty" — that is, (جوعان) "I am hungry" — then (خاوية) "empty" is meant to say that it is a town empty of inhabitants. Its buildings may be standing, but there are no people in them. The Truth, by His saying about that town that it is "fallen down upon its roofs", and (العرش) "roof/throne" is applied to the tent-structure of a dwelling, and as we know it is also applied to the ceiling. So when He says "fallen down upon its roofs", it means the roof collapsed first, then the walls fell upon it, just as we say in our colloquial language: (جاب عاليها على واطيها) "he brought its high part down onto its low part".

When a person passes by a town like this one, its sight must be something striking. He said: (How will Allah bring this to life after its death?), as if he were asking about the town, and about the causing to die and the bringing to life of the people who inhabited the town. When the Truth mentions the town in the Qur'an, He sometimes intends to speak about its people, such as His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿And ask the town in which we were, and the caravan in which we came, and indeed we are truthful.﴾ (Surah Yusuf, 82).

When the sons of Ya'qub, peace be upon him, returned from Egypt and left their younger brother with Yusuf, peace be upon him, they said to their father: send someone who will bring you the testimony of the people of Egypt, and ask your companions who were with us in the caravan yourself, and they will tell you that we left our brother in Egypt. But the question of the one who passed by the fallen town is a question about its people.

(How will Allah bring this to life after its death?) When you hear (أنّى) "how/whence", it comes sometimes with the meaning (كيف) "how", and sometimes with the meaning (من أين) "from where"; and what suits it here is that the question be as follows: "How does Allah bring this to life after its death?" His saying this indicates that he is a believer, for he does not doubt that the matter of bringing to life is from Allah; rather, he wants to know the manner. It is as if he is a believer that Allah is the One who gives life and causes death. And this will come in the story of our master Abraham:

﴿Show me how You give life to the dead.﴾ (From verse 260, Surah al-Baqarah).

He does not doubt that Allah gives life to the dead; rather, he wants to see how this matter is accomplished. For the one who wants to know the manner of a thing must be amazed at the existence of this thing, so he asks: how was this thing made? Just as we see the Pyramids, and we do not doubt that the Pyramids were built in this form, but we only ask: how did they build them? How did they move the stones, so massive, to the top, when there were no scaffolds or mechanical cranes? So we are merely amazed, and amazement is a branch of faith in the event.

Asking about the manner means certainty about the event. So the Truth's saying (أنّى يُحيي هذه الله) means: how does Allah bring this town to life after its death? It is as if the speaker does not doubt that Allah gives life, but he wants the manner; and the manner is not the seat of faith, for Allah has not forbidden us from learning the manner, since He knows that we believe He is able to bring this event into being.

I give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: a clothes designer, when he tailors beautiful garments that you see, you are certain that he is their maker, but you are only amazed at the precision of the craftsmanship, and you say to him: by God, how did you make this? As if you have fallen in love with the craft! So you long to know how it came to be. How much more so the craft of the Truth, blessed and exalted is He? You are astonished and amazed in order to live in the shade of the secret flowing from the Creator into the created, and you want to delight in these blessings.

Another example, and to Allah belongs the highest example, before and after: you see, for instance, a painting that a painter has drawn, and you say to him: by God, how did you mix these colours? You do not doubt that he mixed the colours; rather, you want to make yourself happy by knowing how he painted it. Thus his saying and Abraham's saying, in asking about giving life and causing death in what comes, does not mean that he is not a believer; rather, he is a lover and longing to know the manner, so as to live in the atmosphere of the aesthetic creativity that brought this craft into being.

We know that the bringing to life of people will entail the bringing to life of the town, for man is the initiator of the movement that populates existence, and people have life and have death, and the town with its debris, its walls and its roofs has life and has death. When the servant asked this question, Allah wanted the answer to be a lived experience within the questioner himself; therefore the Qur'an says (فأماته الله مائة عام) "So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years."

The questioner wanted to know the manner, and his request is a sign of faith, so that it might afterward become faith grounded in an observed reality. (فأماته الله مائة عام) Allah has placed the matter and the experience in the questioner himself, and this is Allah's report. He caused him to die for a hundred years. The "year" ('am) is the cycle (al-hawl), and they named the cycle "year" because the sun swims (ta'um) through the whole sphere in this period, and "swimming" is gliding, and the Truth says:

﴿And each, in an orbit, is swimming.﴾ (From verse 40, Surah Yasin).

That is why we call it a year. (فأماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه قال كم لبثت قال لبثت يوما أو بعض يوم) So it is as if Allah spoke to him, as He spoke to Musa, or he heard a voice, or an angel, or that someone present saw the experience. The essential point is that there was a question and an answer. The Truth, glorified is He, informs us of a dialogue that took place concerning this matter: the question is: "How long have you remained?" The man answered: "I have remained a day or part of a day."

The man's answer means that he was in doubt, for he found the day nearly finished or finished, or that when he saw the sun shining he gave this answer: (لبثت يوما أو بعض يوم) "I have remained a day or part of a day", or he may have said that because he cannot control the estimation of time. Was he truthful in his saying or lying? He was truthful, for he had seen nothing in himself that had changed by which to judge the amount of change. If he had shaved his beard, for example, and then got up to find his beard had grown long, or he had slept with black hair and then got up with white hair, then any changes in him would have been felt by him; but he found no change.

So what was the Truth's answer? The Truth said: (بل لبثت مائة عام) "Rather, you have remained a hundred years." Here we are before two parties, and the matter almost becomes a riddle: one party says: "I have remained a day or part of a day", and the Lord says: "Rather, you have remained a hundred years." We want to solve this riddle. The Truth, glorified is He, is truthful and free from any flaw, and the believing servant is truthful within the limits of what he saw of his own condition.

We want evidence for this, and evidence for that. We want evidence of the servant's truthfulness in his saying "I have remained a day or part of a day." And we want from the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, a proof of reassurance, not a proof of demonstration, that the man had died for a hundred years and returned to life.

We say: in the story there is what supports "I have remained a day or part of a day", and what supports "Rather, you have remained a hundred years". The man had with him his donkey, and he had with him his food and drink of juice, grapes and figs. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, said: "you have remained a hundred years", and to demonstrate truthfulness in both matters together He said: (فانظر إلى طعامك وشرابك لم يتسنّه) "But look at your food and your drink, they have not spoiled." The man looked at his food and drink and found that the food and drink had not changed, and this is evidence that he had only remained a day or part of a day; and thus the man's truthfulness was established, and the matter of "a hundred years" remained.

So the Truth said: (وانظر إلى حمارك ولنجعلك آية للناس) "and look at your donkey, and We will make you a sign for the people." This saying indicates that here is something wondrous, and Allah wanted to show him, by a look at the donkey, evidence of the truth of a hundred years having passed. The man found his donkey had turned into scattered bones, and this cannot happen in a short time. For the death of a donkey is something that may happen in a day; but that its body should rot, then its flesh turn to ash, and then the bones remain scattered, that is a matter that requires a long time, which only a hundred years could contain. So looking at the donkey is evidence of the truth of a hundred years having passed, and looking at the food is evidence of the truth of "a day or part of a day."

So the matter is then a wondrous matter: how time was folded in the matter of the food, and how time was stretched out in the matter of the donkey. He, glorified is He, shows us that He is the Withholder and the Extender: He withholds time in regard to one thing, and extends time in regard to another thing, and the two things exist together. That process cannot be except by a free power that the cosmic laws do not possess; rather, it is He who possesses the laws.

The Truth, glorified is He, said: (ولنجعلك آية للناس) "and We will make you a sign for the people." So who are the people for whom Allah would make the matter of the one who passed by a town a sign? There had to be people in the story, but the town was fallen down upon its roofs, and there was no person or building in it. Were they the people who had been in the town, or others? Some exegetes said this, and others said the opposite view.

The most truthful thing that can connect to Allah's truthfulness in His saying "and We will make you a sign for the people" is Allah's withholding of time in regard to one thing and extending it in regard to another. And 'Uzayr, as the majority of scholars said, is the one who passed by a town. This 'Uzayr was one of the four who memorized the Torah, for only four memorized the Torah: Musa, 'Isa, 'Uzayr and Yusha'. Allah showed him the bones and how He raises them and lifts them, so that they are joined together, then clothes them with flesh; that is, He showed him the process of giving life visibly. And in this is an answer to the question: (أنّى يُحيي هذه الله بعد موتها) "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?"

The Truth says: (وانظر إلى العظام كيف ننشزها) "and look at the bones, how We raise them." (ننشزها) means We lift them. 'Uzayr saw every bone of his donkey being lifted from the ground, and he witnessed each bone being put back in its place. After the skeleton of the donkey was formed, the journey of clothing the bones with flesh began, and after that comes life.

'Uzayr found an answer within himself, and found an answer in the donkey. After that he remembered his town from which he had set out, and wished to return to it. When he returned, he found its condition had changed in a manner consistent with the passing of a hundred years. In that town there was a female servant belonging to their household, that is, a slave-woman in his family, and this slave-woman had become blind and had become paralysed. When he entered and said: "I am 'Uzayr", the slave-woman said: "'Uzayr went a hundred years ago, and we do not know where he went or whether he returned." He said: "I am 'Uzayr." She said: "Indeed 'Uzayr has a sign: this sign is that his supplication is answered." And she did not forget herself. She said: "If you are 'Uzayr, then ask Allah to return my sight to me and to bring me out of this sitting-state of mine." 'Uzayr called upon Allah, and she was healed. When she was healed, she looked at him and found him to be 'Uzayr, so she went to her people and announced that 'Uzayr had returned. After that 'Uzayr went to his son, and found him a man who had passed a hundred years of age, while 'Uzayr was still a young man at about fifty years of age.

Therefore you find the poet speaking in riddle: "And what son has seen his father while he is in the weakness of his age?" The intended riddle is 'Uzayr, whom Allah caused to die when he was fifty, then Allah brought him back to life in his very age after a hundred years, and 'Uzayr met his son. The son said: "I used to hear that my father had a mark between his shoulders (a mole). When he uncovered..."

Then follows a story about Abraham as well, after the argument with the man was carried over to the sun, so the man who disbelieved was confounded. As for Abraham, peace be upon him, he believes in God's power, but he wants to know the modality (kayfiyyah). Abraham, peace be upon him, was not doubtful, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:

("We have more right to doubt than Abraham, when he said: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.﴾ He said: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾ He said: ﴿Yes, but that my heart may be at rest.﴾")(1).

Its origin was reviewed and its hadiths were takhrij'd (traced to their sources) by Dr. Ahmad Umar Hashim, vice-president of al-Azhar University.

We Muslims have not doubted this matter.

Therefore, Abraham, peace be upon him, did not doubt, all the more so, by the explicit evidence of the verse when the Truth, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when Abraham said, "My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead." He said, "Have you not believed?" He said, "Yes, but that my heart may be at rest." He said, "Take four birds and incline them toward you. Then put on each hill a portion of them; then call them, they will come to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise." 260﴾

Abraham, peace be upon him, asks: "How do You give life to the dead?" That is, he seeks the state in which the process of giving life takes place. Abraham, peace be upon him, is not speaking about the fact of resurrection; rather, his doubt, peace be upon him, was whether God, glorified is He, might not respond to his request to show him and inform him of the manner in which the dead are brought to life. Let us give this example, and to God belongs the highest example, before and after, and the example is to bring the matter closer to minds, because God is exalted above any likeness.

When one of us says to an engineer, "How did you build this house?" the questioner refers to an event and to something produced, namely the house that was built. Does knowledge of the modality fall within the belief of faith? No.

Let us first know what 'aqidah (creed) means. 'Aqidah is: a matter that is bound (ma'qud). If that is so, how does he say, "that my heart may be at rest"? Is this evidence that Abraham, before the question and before it was granted to him, did not have a tranquil heart? No. Abraham was a believer, but he wanted his tranquility to increase, because he turned over in his mind the manner in which the process of giving life takes place, yet he did not know in what form it would occur.

Thus tranquility came for a specific purpose, in a particular modality, which would bring him out of the labyrinths of imagined and conceived modalities. And since you want the modality, and this modality cannot be explained to you in words, there must rather be a practical, real experiment: ﴿Take four birds and incline them toward you.﴾ "Incline" (ṣurrahunna) means: gather them and bring them close to you, so that you may verify the identities of the birds and the form of each bird, so that you do not imagine that another bird has come to you. The commentators said: the four birds are: the peacock (gharab), the peacock (ṭāwūs), the rooster (dīk), and the dove (ḥamāmah), and each bird had a different form.

﴿Then put on each hill a portion of them; then call them, they will come to you in haste.﴾ Did Our master Abraham carry out this process, or did he suffice with God explaining the modality to him? The Qur'an did not address this narrative, so either God told him the modality, and if he wished to verify it, let him do so, or he was certain without carrying out that process. The Qur'an did not tell us whether our master Abraham carried out this process or not. The Truth says, addressing Abraham with the steps of the experiment: ﴿then call them, they will come to you in haste.﴾ It would have been expected to say: "they will come to you flying" (ṭayarānan).

How do birds hasten (yas'ā)? Birds fly in the sky and in the air. But the Truth wanted by this to leave no room for confusion of the matter, so He said "in haste" (sa'yan), that is, the bird will come before him walking. The Truth moved the matter from flying to hastening, so that our master Abraham might verify it. Therefore, so that you may verify, O Abraham, and your tranquility may increase, We brought them as birds of different kinds, and you are the one who cut them, you are the one who placed a portion on each hill, then you are the one who called the birds and they came to you in haste.

Here is a remark on the freedom of power (ṭalāqat al-qudrah), and on the difference between the necessary power of the Necessary Existent (wājib al-wujūd), who is the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, and the granted power from the Necessary Existent, who is God, glorified is He, to the contingent being who is man. This one has power, and that one has power. The power of God is necessary power, and the power of man is possible (contingent) power. The power of God is not taken from Him by anyone, while the power of man is taken from him by God. Man is one of the human race, and human beings differ in their capacities; when one of them has power, there is another who has no power, that is, he is incapable. The capable one among men can transfer the effect of his power to the incapable; for example, a capable man may carry a chair for someone who cannot carry it to sit on. But the power of the Truth differs.

As if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, were saying: I transfer from My power to one who has no power, so he becomes capable. I say to the thing: "Be," and it is. This is what we understand from His words, glorified is He, to Abraham: ﴿then call them, they will come to you in haste.﴾ Abraham, as one of the human race, is incapable of the modality of giving life, but the Truth gives him the power to call the birds, and the birds come in haste.

The Truth gives Abraham the power to call the birds, and the birds come in haste. This is the difference between necessary power and possible power. The power of the contingent is not transferred by anyone to one who lacks it, but the power of the Necessary Existent transfers it to one who has no power, so he becomes capable. This is why the wise word comes with the attributes of Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him:

﴿And a messenger to the Children of Israel, [who will say]: "Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord: that I will create for you from clay [in the form of] a bird, then breathe into it and it will be a bird by permission of Allah. And I heal the blind and the leper, and I give life to the dead, by permission of Allah. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers."﴾ (Surah Aal 'Imran).

The attributes of Jesus son of Mary occur only by permission from God. Jesus' power to make from clay what is in the form of a bird, and if he breathes into it by God's permission it would become a bird, and likewise the healing of the blind and leper and the giving of life to the dead—all of that is by permission of whom? By permission of God. Likewise was the matter in the experiment of our master Abraham, therefore the Truth said to him: ﴿And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.﴾ Indeed God is Exalted in Might (al-'Azīz), that is, no one overcomes Him. And He is Wise (al-Ḥakīm), that is, He places everything in its proper place.

Thus the Truth sets out the story of life and the story of death in a material experiment, so that the heart of our master Abraham may be at rest. The story of life and death came because the doubt among those who were contemporaries of the Muhammadan call concerned the matter of resurrection from death, and all their speech leads to that. They marvelled at the occurrence of this matter:

﴿They say: "When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?"﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun).

And in another statement:

﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation."﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin).

The Truth, glorified is He, commanded Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to answer this: Say, O Muhammad: "He who originated them the first time will give them life"; for He created them from nothing. Therefore the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. And to Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (Surah al-Rum).

Indeed God, glorified and exalted is He, is capable of beginning creation without a model, then repeating it after death; and repeating it is easier for Him than beginning it, by the measure of those who believe that repeating a thing is easier than beginning it. God has absolute power over His creation, He is the Victorious in His dominion, and He is the Wise in His action and His decree.

Indeed, one who repeats only repeats something existing, whereas one who begins does so from non-existence. So the easier is repetition, while beginning is beginning from non-existence, and both are from the power of the Truth, glorified and exalted is He. This matter establishes the Last Day, because belief in the Last Day is the doctrinal balance; if it settles in the heart, the human being with all his limbs turns toward the actions that proceed by the light of God's method, so that the human attains the fullest reward.

When a person understands that there is a reckoning, a recompense, and a resurrection, he knows that he has not been left loose in this world, nor has he escaped the One God, the Subduer. For man there is a return: we say to the one who is deceived by what God has given him: No, you will not escape the hand of God; rather, there is a return for you by death and a return by resurrection. When that return is firmly established in the minds of Muslims, every person will settle his account in light of this return. And after the matter of life and death was settled, the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, willed to bring something that is the fruit of life in the living being, and the first manifestation of life is sensation and movement. Movement in existence God willed for man, because He, the Truth, willed man for the vicegerency on earth. Vicegerency on earth requires that man populate the earth, as God, glorified and exalted is He, said:

﴿Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. He has produced you from the earth and made you inhabitants therein.﴾ (Verse 61, Surah Hud).

The vicegerency of man on earth requires that he move and populate the earth. When God wants us to move and populate the earth, there must be works that organize this movement, and there must be many arts founded on construction. God distributes the active capacities of these many arts and makes them talents that are thoughtful and planned in human beings. The Truth, glorified is He, did not make one person a collection of talents; rather God scattered talents among creation, and each one took a certain talent.

Why? Because God wanted the world to be complementary and not repetitive; complementarity suggests interdependence. If you know something subject to your talent, and I do not know it, I am obliged to join with you; and I may also know something that you do not know, so you are obliged to join with me. This kind of joining is not a joining of favour; it is a necessary joining of coexistence.

But if each one became a collection of talents, he would be independent of other human beings and would live alone by himself, and his need of human society would end. It is as though God, when He distributed the causes of excellence among creation, wanted them to complement one another and join one another, not as a joining of favour but as a necessary joining of coexistence, because one wants what the other produces by his talent, and the other wants from another person what is gifted in him. Therefore people are in good condition when they differ, because each of them needs the other.

For this reason we find no progress in any society unless the talents in that society are different and mutually supporting. When there are people with uniform talents, they must fight one another; but when each person needs the talent of the other, they coexist, because life does not run except by the whole. Therefore when a group is equal in talents, they must perish, because they compete over them and each wants to monopolize them for himself. But in complementary talents, no one among them says: "Why is so-and-so better than me?", because he knows it is necessary that there be the engineer, the physician, and the craftsman. Therefore you find existence organized by its own natural organization, which establishes a base and establishes a summit; the small summit is carried by the large base. If you reversed the pyramid, it would become a problem, because the matter in that case would be pressed on many sides that have no foundation and rest on nothing. Therefore it is wise, if you see in society one who has risen to the summit, to help him remain outstanding, and not to contend with him so that you all fall; for there must be differentiation so that complementarity may arise.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, presents this matter to us in a social aspect and an economic aspect, to show us that the origin of existence must be established upon a social matter and an economic matter. Why? Because man is first occupied with preserving his life, then with preserving his kind. The preservation of human life is by sustenance, and the preservation of his kind is by marriage. The preservation of life by sustenance requires movement in life, and the Truth honours its fruit. When the Truth wants to soften the heart of the one who moves toward his weak brother, He says:

﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ (Verse 245, Surah al-Baqarah).

As we have struck the example before, and to God belongs the highest example, we said: Indeed...

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 2, verse 261:

After establishing the matter of resurrection, revival and death, the Truth, glory be to Him, speaks about that important matter in social and economic structure, so that it stands before us. And the Truth, glory be to Him, moves us on in order to give us the Islamic economic and social entity. So He, majestic is His affair, says:

﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that sprouts seven ears; in each ear is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ [2:261]

Allah attributes wealth to humans who act and move, because they acquired these possessions through their movement. In another place in the Qur'an, the Truth says:

﴿And give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾ (part of verse 33, Surah al-Nur).

All wealth is the wealth of Allah, and man has acquired it through movement. Allah honours this movement, and Allah's honouring of man is the law of benefit (al-nafa'iyya). So He made the wealth that remains from your movement your property, O human. But if Allah wants this wealth, He will take it. And among Allah's favours upon man is that when He, glory be to Him, asks man for some of the wealth that remains from his movement, He asks for it as a loan, and returns it multiplied afterwards.

Therefore, spending in the way of Allah, Allah returns it multiplied, and as long as Allah multiplies it, He increases it. So do not grieve and do not fear for your wealth, because you have given it to One who is All-Powerful, All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. He is the Truth who is able to give each one according to what He wills, glory be to Him; He gives according to the intention of the servant and the amount of his spending.

This verse addresses the matter of miserliness (shuhh) in the human soul: a person may have some surplus, and his soul clings to it and withholds, fearing that if he spends from it, it will diminish.

Here the matter of faith says to you: spend, for He, glory be to Him, will increase you, and the Truth will give you as He gives you from the earth that you cultivate. You plant a single grain. Does it give you one grain? No. A grain of wheat produces a number of stalks, and each stalk has an ear containing many grains. So if the earth, which is created by Allah, multiplies for you what you give it, will the One who created it not multiply the return to you? And if some of Allah's creation multiplies for you, how much more so Allah, majestic and exalted is He?

The barren earth with its elements gives you back. When you take a measure (kayla) of wheat from your storehouse to sow it in the ground, is it said that you have reduced your storehouse by the amount of that measure? No; because you will plant it, and you await how many grains will come. This is barren earth, created by Allah. If what is created by Allah has been able to give you seven hundred for one grain, will not the One who created this earth give you multiples of that?

He is abundant in giving. The Truth has attributed to the spenders the wealth with which Allah has provided them, saying: ﴿those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah﴾. The phrase ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ is a general expression; its meaning may be jihad, or the channels of charity, because all of this is in the way of Allah. For when the weak person finds himself in a cohesive society, and finds that the one with strength has extended the effect of his strength and activity to him, would he resent the strong? No, because his good comes to him. We give an example from the countryside, we say:

The cow that gives milk for an hour walks through the neighbourhood. Everyone prays for Allah to protect her and says: "May Allah keep her safe for you." Why? Because her owner gives everyone around him from her milk, her cheese and her butter, so everyone prays for her. Her owner does not tie her up, does not fodder her, and is not preoccupied with her, and the good that comes from her goes to all the family. When we find a society of this kind, where the weak finds in the strong a helper, here the weak says: "I am in a complete world."

And if one person has strength and another has weakness, the weak does not resent; rather he says: "The good of others reaches me." Likewise the giver is reassured that if he becomes incapable one day, he will find someone to support him, since strength is transient, as long as man is among transient things. He may be strong today and weak tomorrow.

Therefore, the word of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿the likeness of those who spend their wealth﴾ is a law by which Allah intends to combat miserliness in the souls of created beings. He says to each of us: look with a conscious gaze; the earth does not diminish your storehouse when you give it a measure of wheat! It is true that you reduced a measure from your storehouse to plant it, but you expect to take from the earth multiples of it. And beware of thinking that what the earth gives you is trustworthy, while what Allah gives you is not something you trust.

﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that sprouts seven ears; in each ear is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ The verse addresses miserliness and affirms that charity does not diminish what a person has; rather it will increase it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 262:

And after that, the Exalted says:

﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, then do not follow what they have spent with reminders (of their generosity) or injury, for them is their reward with their Lord, and there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾ [2:262]

This is another snapshot in which the Truth clarifies: beware, when you spend your wealth in the way of Allah while hoping for Allah's bounty, of reminding the one you give to or harming him. Al-mann (reminding, or taunting over a favour) is to reproach the one you have benefited with your kindness, to show him that you have made a right of yours binding upon him, and that you have become a possessor of favour over him. As they say in the countryside (ta'ayyar bihā, "to reproach him with it"), and the poet says:

"And if a man bestows a favour upon me, then reminds me of it once before a base man..."

Therefore, it is part of faithful good manners in a person that he forgets that he gave, and forgets that he spent, and does not let any of his family know of his kindness to the poor or of his charity to him, especially the children, who do not understand the logic of Allah in things. For when my son knows that I give so-and-so to my neighbour, he may point it out and taunt the neighbour's son; perhaps his vanity will take him so that he reproaches him. This matter can only be appreciated by one who is charged with the obligation and who knows the ruling with its rationale from Allah.

The Truth clarifies for us: beware of following the spending with reminder or injury, for if you follow it with reminder, what then is the situation? The one to whom you gave charity dislikes it, and resentment is born in him, and hatred is born in him. Therefore, when they said: "Guard against the evil of one to whom you have done good," they explained it as: guarding against that person's evil is by not mentioning your kindness to him; beware of mentioning it to him, for that begets resentment in him.

Therefore you find many people saying: "How much I did for so-and-so and so-and-so, this much and that much, and then they turned against me and denied it." And I say to everyone who says this: as long as you remember what you bestowed upon them, it is part of Allah's justice that they deny it. Had you dealt with Allah, they would not have denied it. So as long as you have not dealt with Allah, you will be met with denial of what you spent.

It is as if the Exalted wishes, through the first verse, to make the heart of the spender generous, so that he extends his hand with spending. Therefore He said: ﴿then do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury; for them is their reward with their Lord, and there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾

The Truth, glorified and exalted, reassured us in the first verse that charity and spending do not diminish wealth but increase it, and the Truth gave us the example of the land which yields, for one grain, seven hundred grains. Then the Truth clarifies for us that the bane of spending is that it be accompanied by (al-mann) or (al-adha), for that corrupts the matter of the sincere reaching of the weak and helpless. Therefore the Truth, glorified, says:

﴿Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah, then do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury, for them is their reward with their Lord﴾ (part of verse 262, Surat al-Baqarah).

Observe the precision of expression in His noble saying: (then do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury). The speech would be sound if it came as follows: (those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah and do not follow what they have spent with reminders or injury), but the Truth, glorified, has used "thumma" (then) here, because it has a place. The one who spends wealth may not remind at the moment of giving, but the one who spends may delay the reminder; so the Truth, glorified, alerts every believer:

The spending must remain unaccompanied by reminder, and the spender must keep far from reminder always, so that he does not refrain from reminder only at the time of giving, but the absence of reminder must continue even after the giving, however long the time.

"Thumma" comes with this meaning because there is a time gap in which a person delays in doing reminder. The Truth prohibits reminder in a continuous and lasting manner, not only at the moment of giving but also after the giving. Shawqi, prince of poets, may Allah have mercy on him, when he wrote poetry on the bearing of burdens, placed verses on bearing psychological burdens, and said:

Did you bear a debt in your life once?
Did you ever bear a grief in your ribs one day?
Did you bear a reminder repeated in the day,
while the night was from one who bestowed kindness upon you?

And after Shawqi enumerated the aspects of the heavy burdens in life, he said:

That is life, and these are its burdens,
by which iron was weighed and became light.

As if reminder is then a great psychological burden. The Truth, glorified, reassures those who spend their wealth without reminder or injury in the way of Allah that they have a reward with their Lord. The word (al-ajr) (reward) and the clarification from the Lord are a reassurance that the matter has been entrusted to one trustworthy in its performance, and capable of this performance. As for the one who reminds or injures, he has taken his reward through the reminder or the injury, and has no reward with Allah; for the one who reminds or injures has not conceived of the Lord of the weak, but has conceived of the weak.

The one who spends in the way of Allah, when he conceives of the Lord of the weak, and that the Lord of the weak is the One who brought him into existence and placed weakness upon him, he believes that Allah is the Guarantor of the weak one's provision. When the strong spends on the weak, he is only discharging on Allah's behalf. Therefore we find in the sayings of those brought near:

("We place the charity in the hand of Allah before we place it in the hand of the weak.") Let us look at what our lady Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, did. She would polish the dirham and perfume it. When it was said to her: "What are you doing?" she said: "I polish a dirham and perfume it, because I intended to give it in charity." It was said to her: "Will you give it in charity polished and perfumed?"

Al-Zahra', daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, said: "Because I know that it falls into the hand of Allah before it falls into the hand of the poor. The reward is with the One who magnifies it, raises it, and elevates its value, and He is the Creator, the Giver."

Let us reflect on the words of the Truth: (there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve). Why did Allah not say: "no fear from them"? Because the Truth wants to clarify for us by His saying (there is no fear upon them) that there is a third element that will intervene. It is an intervention by a person who may appear to the spending person as loving him, and says: "Save for the coming days, save for your children."

For such an element the Truth says: (there is no fear upon them), that is, beware, O possessor of such an opinion, of intervening in the name of love, and let your words be spared; for the one who spends in the way of Allah finds giving and protection from Allah. There is no fear upon the one who spends in the way of Allah, and not only that, but the Truth says of those who spend in the way of Allah without reminder or injury: (nor will they grieve), meaning that in the dealings of the Truth with them there will come what gladdens them, that they gave charity, either through the swiftness of replacement for them, or through the contentment of the soul, or through the provision of averted harm. The bane of people is that they always look to the provision of acquisition, that is, that people measure provision by what money enters for them, and do not measure the matter by the provision of averting, and the provision of averting is the place of blessing.

Suppose a man's salary is fifty pounds, and then Allah averts from him expenses that would demand a hundred pounds, as when he comes home and finds his child exhausted and his fever high, so Allah grants the man's heart tranquillity, and he asks his wife to prepare a cup of tea for the boy and gives him a tablet of aspirin, and the fever passes and the matter ends.

Another man comes home and finds his child exhausted and his fever high, and the fever continues for more than a day, so Allah casts terror into his heart, and fancies and illusions about the illness come to the man's mind, so he takes his son to the doctor and spends fifty or a hundred pounds.

The first man: Allah healed his son with a piastre. The second: Allah healed his son with many pounds. The provision of the first man is the provision of averting. For just as Allah provides through acquisition, Allah provides through averting, that is, He averts the expense and repels the calamity. And there is a man whose income is a hundred pounds, and Allah brings him expenses that take two hundred, and there is a man whose income is fifty pounds, and Allah averts from him expenses that exceed a hundred pounds. Which of them is better?

It is the one from whom Allah averted expenses that exceed his capacity. So people should look at the provision of averting just as they look at the provision of acquisition. His saying, the Truth, concerning those who spend in His way without reminder or injury: (there is no fear upon them, nor will they grieve), this saying is evidence that Allah will bring the outcome of spending without reminder or injury in a way that gladdens the believer's heart, either by blessing in provision or by averting expenses from him; so the believing heart says: "This is the blessing of the charity I gave."

Indeed, he gave something in charity, and Allah raised and averted from him something harmful, so the believing heart rejoices at that. After that, the Exalted alerts us to an important matter: if you, O believer, cannot give with your wealth, then give with your speech, for if you cannot give people your wealth, then meet them with good response. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

("Guard yourselves against the Fire even with half a date; and whoever cannot find it, then with a good word.")(1)

1. Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Zakat.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 263:

The Almighty sets out the matter in this verse:

﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by harm. And Allah is Rich, Forbearing.﴾

What is the meaning of "a kind word" (qawl ma'ruf)? We customarily find that al-ma'ruf (that which is known and acceptable) is the opposite of al-munkar (that which is denounced), as if good were a matter recognized by natural disposition, and as if what is commonly recognized is always of the kind of beauty and of the kind of goodness, while what the soul rejects is of the kind of evil and of the kind of ugliness. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿a kind word﴾. It is as though it is in the nature of beauty and of goodness to be recognized, and in the nature of its opposite to be denounced. So a kind word means that you respond to the beggar in a graceful way, such that his soul is not filled with resentment against you, and such that you do not rebuke him for having asked you. And if the beggar has frowned at you with the frown of one in need, then forgive him for that. Why?

Because there is a person whose back is lashed by the whips of need, who sees you as possessing wealth, ease, or abundance of property, and who may exceed a little in speech towards you, and perhaps go beyond the courtesy of conversation with you; so you must bear with him.

And if you, O servant, commit the sins that anger Allah, and the Truth forbears towards you and forgives them for you and does not punish you for them, then when a person does something to you, be likewise a possessor of kind words, forgiveness and forbearance. The Almighty says to us: ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?﴾

We all love that Allah should forgive us, and therefore we must forgive others, especially the needy. When the Truth says ﴿And Allah is Rich, Forbearing﴾, there is in that a warning to the capable one who deprives the poor, as if He were saying to him: You have only deprived yourself, O capable one, of the reward of Allah. When you, O capable one, deprive a poor man, it is you who are deprived, because Allah is independent of you. And He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Here you are, those who are called to spend in the way of Allah, but some of you are stingy; and whoever is stingy is only stingy against himself. And Allah is the Rich, and you are the poor. And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, then they will not be like you.﴾ (Surah Muhammad, 38)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 264:

Indeed Allah is Rich (ghani) in His absolute power; He is Rich and Able to replace the stingy people with a people who spend from the provision Allah has bestowed upon them in the way of Allah. Whoever withholds from giving has only denied himself the gate of mercy. Therefore the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿O you who have believed, do not nullify your charities with reminders [of your generosity] and injury, like one who spends his wealth to be seen by the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like that of a smooth stone upon which is dust; then a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They are unable to do anything with what they have earned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾ [2:264]

The one who gives charity and follows his charity with reminders and injury is in fact nullifying his charity, and his loss becomes a double loss. The first loss is that he has actually diminished his wealth, because Allah will not compensate him, since he followed the charity with what nullifies it, namely reminders and injury. The other loss is the deprivation of reward. So the one who spends in order that people may say of him that he spends should know that the Truth makes clear to us that reward is given on the principle that the one who pays the reward is the one for whom you did the deed.

Man, with his limited power, gives the reward to the one for whom he has done a deed. Whoever acts so that people will say he acted should seek his reward from the limited capacity of human beings. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us about the one who does a good deed or gives charity so that it will be said of him that he did it: on the Day of Resurrection he will come and find no reward for himself. There has come in the noble hadith:

("A man whom Allah gave various kinds of wealth came with it, and He made him recognize His blessings, and he recognized them. Allah said: 'What did you do with them?' He said: 'I left no thing in which You love to be spent except that I spent in it for You.' He said: 'You have lied; you only intended that it be said, "So-and-so is generous," and it has been said.' Then he was commanded, and he was dragged on his face until he was thrown into the Fire.") (1)

So beware lest you say: "I spent, and Allah did not expand my provision." For Allah may test and try you, so do not give charity for the sake of expanding your provision. Allah's giving to the believer is not in this world alone; rather, Allah may want not to give you in the perishing world and to preserve the giving for you in the enduring one, which is the Hereafter. "And it is better and more enduring."

The Truth says: (and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day; his example is like that of a smooth stone upon which is dust). The safwan is the smooth stone, which is called in colloquial speech the "zulta" (pebble). It is said of a bald man "safwan," meaning his head is smooth like a marwa (stone). A smooth thing is one that has no pores which the perceiving eye can grasp; a person only perceives these pores by placing the stone under a microscope. When a thing is smooth, dust may settle on it, then rain comes down upon the dust and the dust slides off the smooth thing. Had the stone had some roughness, some of the dust would have remained among the protrusions. So the one who spends his wealth to be seen by people is like the safwan on which dust accumulates, and rain falls on the dust and removes it all, so the matter becomes: (they are unable to do anything with what they have earned), that is, they have lost the ability to possess anything, because Allah has made what they did of deeds "scattered dust."

These are like the smooth stone with dust upon it, on which a heavy rain (wabil), that is, a strong downpour, falls, and leaves it bare. Those are the characteristics of those who intended by their spending to be seen by people, so Allah nullifies their recompense, because Allah does not grant them success in good and reward.

1 From a hadith in which al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim," and Muslim narrated it.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi) on Surah 2, verse 265:

And God brings in the counterpart: those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of God. He says:

﴿And the likeness of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of Allah and for the firming of their own souls is like a garden on a height: a heavy rain strikes it, and it yields its produce twofold; and if no heavy rain strikes it, then a light rain. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

Seeking the pleasure of God in spending means that showing-off (riya', ostentation) is removed from the sphere of giving, so that it is purely for His sake, glory be to Him. As for "firming from their own souls" (tathbitan min anfusihim), it also concerns their own selves. It is as if the faithful soul clashes with the appetitive soul (al-nafs al-shahwaniyya). Whenever the faithful soul seeks something, the appetitive soul tries to prevent it, and the faithful soul prevails over the appetitive soul and gives victory to God.

What is meant by "firming from their own souls" is that the believer is steadfast in loving his self with a deeper love, not a foolish love. Thus the act of spending must first be spending in the way of God, and it is firming the self by which the believer first gives his blood, and then firms his self by giving his wealth. In this way the firming is confirmed, as the noble verse depicts it:

﴿Like a garden on a height: a heavy rain strikes it, and it yields its produce twofold; and if no heavy rain strikes it, then a light rain.﴾ (from verse 265 of Surat al-Baqarah)

As we have learned, the word "garden" (jannah) in the language refers to a place in which there is dense green vegetation to the extent that it covers whoever enters it. From it comes the word (jann), meaning "to cover," and whoever enters this garden becomes covered.

The Truth wishes to strike for us the example that clarifies the second category of those who spend in the way of God, seeking His pleasure and firming their faithful selves against the appetitive self. Each of them is like one who enters a garden dense with crops, and this garden is located on a high rise. When the garden is on a high rise, it means that it is surrounded by places that are low and lower than it. So what does rain do to this garden that is on a rise? The Truth has informed us of what happens to such a garden before modern science advanced and discovered the effects of groundwater on agriculture.

This garden on a rise does not suffer what the level land suffers. On level land, groundwater may reach the capillary roots of plants and spoil them by stagnation, so these roots cannot absorb the nutrients the plant needs, and the plant first pales to yellowing and then dies. The garden on a rise receives the water that falls on it from the rain and has drainage channels on all the low sides around it, and this garden is irrigated by the most recent means of irrigation that science has reached. It takes water from above, that is, from the rain, so the water falls on the leaves to perform a first function, which is washing the leaves.

As we know, the leaves of a plant are like the lungs of a human; their task is breathing. When rainwater falls on them, it washes these leaves, which allows them to perform their role in what we in the modern age call chlorophyll photosynthesis. After that the water descends to the roots to dissolve the elements the soil needs for the plant's nourishment, so the roots take what they need of the nourishment dissolved in the water, and the excess water drains off into the low channels. These are the most recent methods of modern agriculture, and they have discovered that the yield is multiplied by them.

The Truth informs us that whoever spends his wealth seeking the pleasure of God and firming his own self is like this garden, which is watered by a divine method. If a heavy rain falls on it, it takes what it needs of it and the rest of the rain moves away from it. ("If no heavy rain strikes it, then a light rain"): the drizzle (tal) is a light rain and mist that is sufficient for it to yield twice its produce. And if "double" means the amount equal to a thing twice, then "twofold" equals the thing four times.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 266:

God strikes a parable for us, to make clearer the condition of one who spends his wealth to be seen by people. He asks His believing servants, and He knows them best. So He says, exalted is His majesty:

﴿Would any one of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines beneath which rivers flow, with every kind of fruit in it for him, and then old age strikes him while he has weak offspring, and then a fiery whirlwind strikes it and it is burned? Thus God makes the signs clear to you, that you might give thought.﴾

The Truth, glory to Him, makes us partners in the image, as if He wants to take from us a clear testimony. So: would any one of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines beneath which rivers flow, with every kind of fruit in it for him? We know that palm trees and grapevines were among the most important fruits and produce of the society in which the Noble Qur'an was revealed. We also know that there are orchards containing palm trees and grapevines, to which the owner adds trees of peaches and other fruits. For this reason, the Truth speaks about the People of the Garden:

﴿And present to them the parable of two men: We had made for one of them two gardens of grapevines, and We had surrounded them with palm trees, and placed between them a field of crops. Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fall short therein at all, and We caused a river to gush forth within them. And he had fruit, so he said to his companion while speaking with him: "I am greater than you in wealth and stronger in men." And he entered his garden while wronging himself. He said: "I do not think this will ever perish. And I do not think the Hour will occur. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than it as a destination."﴾ (Surah al-Kahf).

It is as if the two gardens here contain many things: in them are grapevines, and God added to them the gift of palm trees, then crops. This is called in the language 'atf al-'amm 'ala al-khass, or 'atf al-khass 'ala al-'amm (conjunction of the general over the specific, or of the specific over the general), so that a thing is mentioned twice: once by its particularity, and once within the generality of other things. When the Truth, glory to Him, speaks of the Garden of the Hereafter, He says once:

﴿God has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah).

God has prepared for those who believe in Him, who fight in the way of supporting His religion and raising His word, gardens through which rivers flow, and that is the great triumph and success. And again the Truth speaks of the Garden of the Hereafter, saying:

﴿And the foremost, the first of the emigrants and the helpers, and those who followed them with good conduct—God is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah).

The mention of the rivers that flow beneath the Garden comes once preceded by (min) "from", and once not preceded by (min). When the mention of those rivers beneath the Garden comes preceded by (min), this suggests that their source is intrinsic to them and the water is owned by them.

When the mention of those rivers flowing beneath the Garden comes not preceded by (min), this means that the source of these rivers is not intrinsic to them, but it flows beneath them by the will of God, so no one dares to withhold water from this Garden that God has prepared for the believers. When the Truth draws us into the question:

﴿Would any one of you wish to have a garden of palm trees and grapevines beneath which rivers flow, with every kind of fruit in it for him, and then old age strikes him while he has weak offspring, and then a fiery whirlwind strikes it and it is burned? Thus God makes the signs clear to you, that you might give thought.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

This Garden, with this description and abundant good in it, but its owner is struck by old age, and the vigour of youth is no longer in his health. He is surrounded by good while he is most in need of that good, because he has reached old age and has no strength with which to work. Thus his soul is attached to the bounty of this Garden, not for himself only but for his weak offspring. This is the summit of the depiction of need for good, not for the self alone but for the weak children as well.

We are before a man surrounded by three circumstances. The first circumstance: the Garden, containing every kind of good.

The second circumstance: old age, weakness, and inability to work.

The third circumstance: weak offspring.

Then a fiery whirlwind strikes this Garden and it is burned. What grief would the man then have? It is a severe grief. Likewise is the grief of one who does good to be seen by people. The whirlwind, as we know, is a violent wind accompanied by thunder, lightning and rain, and it may contain fire, if the electrical charges result from the collision of clouds or carry fiery projectiles from an erupting volcano. Thus is the condition of one who spends his wealth to be seen by people: a beginning of greed and an end of despair, that is, something hopeless.

So every believing person must remember, at the moment he spends, this trial that stirs greed, and that outcome filled with despair. It is a severe calamity. The poet depicts it saying:

So I became, from Layla this morning, like one who grasps
at water, which has betrayed him through the gaps of his fingers.

Another says:

Like a cloud that flashed lightning over thirsty people,
then when they saw it, it dispersed and cleared away.

The one who seeks to be seen loses all his needs, and cannot control anything of what he has earned.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 267:

Then the Truth (al-Haqq) says, after that:

﴿O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned and from what We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim at the defective therefrom to spend from it, while you would not accept it yourselves except with closed eyes. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.﴾

This verse gives images that occur in human society. These images occurred in the society of Madinah after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had established the state of Islam there. Some people would bring a cluster (ʿadhq) of palm dates and hang it in the mosque so that whoever wished could eat from it. The ʿadhq is a strong branch of the palm that carries many small stalks on which the dates hang. Some of them would bring a cluster that was not ripe, or one of the ḥashf, which is the worst of dates. Allah wished to spare them this situation, so that they would not assign to Allah what they dislike, and so He sent down this wise statement: ﴿O you who have believed, spend from the good things you have earned﴾.

Spending must come from good, lawful earnings. Do not bring wealth from an unlawful source in order to spend from it on good causes. Allah is good and accepts only what is good. Spending should not come from the worthless and inferior part of wealth.

The Truth, glorified and exalted, specifies the means of spending from His bounty when He says: ﴿and from what We have produced for you from the earth﴾. He, glorified be He, always reminds us when He says: ﴿spend from the good things you have earned﴾. Do not think that earning is the origin of provision. No, earning is a movement granted to you by Allah. You, O servant, move by an energy granted to you by Allah, with a thought bestowed upon you by Allah, on an earth that Allah has subjected for you. These are the many tools that Allah has singled you out with, and there is nothing in them that you own of your own self. Yet the Truth respects the human being's movement and striving for provision, so He says: ﴿spend from the good things you have earned﴾.

The Truth warns us against choosing the bad and unsuitable from the product of our labour to spend from, by His saying, glorified be He: ﴿And do not aim at the defective therefrom to spend from it﴾. That is, it is neither proper nor fitting for us to take for ourselves the good of our earnings and give Allah the inferior and bad of our earnings, because none of us is content to take for his food or for his dependents this bad and unsuitable thing to spend from or to eat. ﴿while you would not accept it yourselves except with closed eyes. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾. That is, you, O believing servant, will not be content to eat the bad unless you close your eyes, or its price is lowered for you, such as when the seller offers you something of middling quality or something inferior at a price below that of the good.

Allah, the Truth, glorified and exalted, wished to clarify for us through these images the aspects of spending:

* Spending does not diminish wealth; rather, it increases it seven hundredfold.

* Spending must not be nullified by a person through reminders of kindness and harm.

* A kind word is better than charity followed by reminder or harm.

* Spending must not be for the sake of being seen by people; rather, it is to seek the pleasure of Allah.

These noble verses address the afflictions of spending: whether the affliction of stinginess, or the affliction of reminding and harming, or spending for the sake of display before people, or spending from inferior wealth.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, while Allah promises you His forgiveness and bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ (2:268)

Indeed, Shaytan may whisper to you that spending is a cause of impoverishment for you, and he tries to divert you from spending in the paths of good, and he entices you toward sins and indecency. When the wealthy man withholds his hand from the needy, he enters into the heart of the needy the resentment (al-hiqd). And any society in whose heart resentment enters, you find all evils spreading within it. The Truth addresses these matters with His saying:

﴿Indeed, the life of this world is but play and amusement; but if you believe and fear Allah, He will give you your rewards and will not ask you for your wealth. If He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy, and He would bring out your resentments.﴾ (Surah Muhammad, 47:36-37)

Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, does not ask you to return His gift of wealth to you. Rather, the Truth seeks the purification of wealth through spending it in the way of Allah, so that it increases and grows, and so that resentment is removed from society; for when resentment enters a society, then upon that society is peace (i.e., it is lost). Society does not recover from this resentment except by being struck by a strong blow that shakes it, so that it awakens to the necessity of removing resentment from it. Therefore Allah warns us not to listen to Shaytan:

﴿The Shaytan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, while Allah promises you His forgiveness and bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:268)

So whoever listens to the words and promise of Shaytan, and does not listen to the promise of Allah, becomes like one who preferred the enemy of Allah over Allah. May Allah protect us and you from such a position. Indeed, Shaytan has whispered to you about poverty if you spend, and human experience with Shaytan confirms to the human being that Shaytan is a liar and a misleader, and human experience with faith in Allah confirms to the human being that Allah is abounding in forgiveness and generous in giving to His servants. And wisdom requires that we know which paths we are guided to and walk upon.

Then the Truth (Allah) says:

﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good. And none will be reminded except the people of understanding.﴾ (269)

Wisdom (hikmah) is placing a thing in its beneficial place. So it is as if the Truth says: everything I have commanded you with is itself wisdom, because I want to secure your life in this world for those weak offspring you leave behind, and to secure for you the happiness of the Hereafter. If the believing servant does what Allah commands, this is placing things in their proper places, and it is taking hold of wisdom.

Allah also wished to make man aware through his tenderness toward his children, because a person may pass through a period in which the matters of his own self become insignificant to him, and he is occupied only with the affairs of his children. He may go hungry so that the children may be fed, and he may go without clothing so that he may clothe them. We have the clear example in our master Ibrahim, the Friend of the Merciful (khalil al-Rahman), peace be upon him. His Lord tested him at the beginning of his life with being burned in the fire, and because Ibrahim was strong in faith, Allah made the fire cool and safe.

Allah tested him at the end of his life with the vision of slaughtering his son, and because Ibrahim was great in faith, he submitted to the command of the Merciful, who ransomed Isma'il with a great ram. A person in his later years has a greater attachment to his children than to himself. Thus was the ascent in Allah's trials of our master Ibrahim, peace be upon him. For this reason Allah wished to strike this chord for mankind, and He said:
