﴿And let those fear [Allah] who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them. So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ (An-Nisa' 4:9)

Indeed, the Truth, glory be to Him, wants His servants to secure their children through righteous deeds and sound speech.

Another example: when the Truth wished to protect the wealth of orphans, and informed us of the entry of Musa, peace be upon him, with the righteous servant who had been given knowledge from Allah, He says:

﴿So they set out until, when they came to the people of a town and asked them for food, they refused to entertain them. And they found within it a wall about to collapse, so he [al-Khadir] set it up straight. [Musa] said, "If you had wished, you could have taken for it a payment."﴾ (Al-Kahf 18:77)

Musa, peace be upon him, did not know the knowledge of the righteous servant, that under the wall there was a treasure belonging to two orphans. Their father had been a righteous man, and the people of this town were miserly; they had refused to feed the righteous servant and Musa, peace be upon him. Therefore it was necessary to rebuild the wall, so that the treasure would not be exposed in a town of miserly people, who would seize it, and so that the two boys would not take the treasure of their father, who had been a righteous man, before they were grown.

Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches us to secure our children through righteous deeds, and this is the very wisdom that those whose minds are capable of reaching the depth of sound reasoning do not attain.

Our master al-Hasan al-Basri gives us the example of righteous action when he says to whoever enters upon him seeking a need: "Welcome to one who comes carrying my provision to the Hereafter without a fee." Indeed, al-Hasan al-Basri had been given of wisdom such that he does not view good by the measure of its time, but by the measure of what returns to him after the time has passed.

I have also previously given the example of the student who strives and exhausts himself in his lessons to attain success, while his brother loves comfort and idleness for himself. Then we find that the one who exerted himself is the one who rises in society, while the one who accepted idleness for himself becomes a vagabond in society.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 270:

And after that, the Truthful One (al-Haqq), glory be to Him, says:

﴿And whatever you spend of expenditure or whatever vow you vow, indeed Allah knows it. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.﴾

We have already understood spending (nafaqah). So what is the matter of vowing (nadhr)? Vowing is that you bind yourself to something of the same kind as what Allah has legislated (shara'a), beyond what Allah has made obligatory (awjaba). So if you vow to pray to Allah a number of rak'ahs every night, this is a vow of the same kind as what Allah has legislated, because Allah has legislated prayer and made it obligatory as five obligatory prayers. If you vow beyond what Allah has made obligatory, this is the vow. It is said of the one who vows something of the same kind as what Allah has legislated beyond what Allah has made obligatory: indeed this is a sign that worship has become sweet to him, so he loves it and is enamoured of it, and a sign that he has come close to knowing the measure of his Lord, and that his Lord deserves from him more than what He has obligated upon him. Thus Allah, in His obligating, was merciful to us, for if He had obligated what He deserves from us, not one of us would have been able to fulfil the right of Allah.

So when you, O believing servant, make a vow, you bind yourself to something of the same kind as what Allah has legislated for you, beyond what Allah has obligated upon you. You are free to commit yourself to a vow or not. But if you utter a vow, it is binding, why? Because you have obligated yourself to it. Therefore it is part of wisdom that a person not entangle himself and not be excessive in vowing, because at the time of fulfilment he may not be able to do it.

And the people of closeness to Allah say to one who breaks a vow after having made it: Have you tested your Lord and found Him unworthy of the continuation of affection? None of us would dare to do that, because Allah is worthy of deep affection. For this reason it is better for a person to be patient before he vows anything.

We now stop at the appended phrase of the verse: (And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers). Indeed, the wrongdoers are those who wrong themselves, for the Truth has informed us that a person's wronging is only to himself, and He said to us:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong people at all, but people wrong themselves.﴾ (Surah Yunus [10:44]).

And among the gravest wronging of oneself is spending for show (riya'), or spending in acts of disobedience, or failing to fulfil a vow. For whoever does that there are no helpers who will ward off the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 271:

Then the Truth says, after that:

﴿If you disclose your charities, how excellent they are; and if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you, and He will remove from you some of your misdeeds. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

So if you display the charity, then how excellent what you do is; so that you may be an example for others, and so that you may ward off resentment from the community. And if you conceal the charity and give it to the poor, then Allah will, by that, expiate from you some of your misdeeds, and Allah is Acquainted with the intention behind publicising charity and behind concealing charity. The closing phrase of this noble verse serves both the matter of displaying charity and the matter of concealing charity. The Truth is Aware of the intention of the one who displays his charity. If he is wealthy, then he should display his charity in order to protect his honour from people falling into speaking about him; for when people know of the wealthy man, they must know of the wealthy man's spending, otherwise people may attribute to the wealthy man the bounty that Allah has given him, and not reckon to him the expenditure in the way of Allah. Why? Because Allah wishes to protect people's honour from other people.

As for a person who is not visibly wealthy, it is commendable that he conceal his charity. And if you display your charity, as you have said, so that people may follow your example, and there is no show-off (riya') in your mind, then this too is desirable. The Truth says: (And Allah is Acquainted with what you do), meaning that Allah rewards according to the degree of the servant's intention, whether in displaying or in concealing.

By surveying the verses that address spending, one finds that He, glory be to Him, blocks off before the human soul every outlet of miserliness (shuh), and cuts off every path by which it would be enticed to stinginess, if it wished to withhold what Allah has given it. The Creator who bestowed upon the creature what He bestowed asks it to spend. If we look at the matter from the standpoint of logic, we find it natural; for Allah does not ask His creatures to spend from what they have created, but He asks them to spend from what He has created for them.

When a human being in this existence is asked by faith to spend, it necessarily follows that he must have something to spend, and he cannot have something to spend unless he owns something beyond his need and the need of his dependants, and that is achieved only through the fruit of work. Therefore, Allah's command to the believer to spend requires that He first command him to work according to his capacity, not according to his need. If every capable person worked only according to his need, how would the necessities of life come to exist for one who cannot work?

So the Truth wants us to work according to our capacity in labour, in order to provide for ourselves and for those under our care; and whatever exceeds that, we give to those who cannot work.

Someone might say: If Allah wished to soften the hearts of those who spend toward the helpless, why did He not make the helpless able to work too?

We say to the proponent of this view: When the Truth creates, He creates a complete and harmonious cosmos, to which causes submit. Perhaps the fact that causes submit to him leads him to transgress, so that he thinks he has become the creator of everything. When the earth responds to him if he ploughs and sows, and when the water responds to him if he lowers his bucket, and when all causes respond to him, he may imagine himself to be the origin of existence. So Allah wills to make the power that acts within causes so that they produce; He, glory be to Him, wills to make it an accident (ʿaraḍ) of this existence, and does not make it a necessary attribute of the human being. So sometimes you find him capable, and sometimes you find him incapable.

If he were capable by his own essence, there would be no incapable person. Therefore, the existence of those unable to move in life draws people's attention to the fact that they are not originators of this existence, and that the One who gave them power can strip them of it and restore it to others; so the one who was incapable yesterday becomes capable today, and the one who was capable yesterday becomes incapable today, and thus the human being remains mindful of the bestowing Power who has made him vicegerent on earth.

Accordingly, the difference between the believer and the disbeliever in the movement of life is that they share one thing, and then the believer is distinguished by another. They share that each of the believers and the disbelievers works in the causes of life to produce what sustains him and those he supports; that is a common measure between believer and disbeliever. The disbeliever confines himself to this cause of work, working for himself and for those he supports.

But the believer shares this with him and adds that he works for something else: that some surplus from him may be directed to one who cannot work, seeking the reward for it from Allah.

For this reason we have said previously: when the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of zakat, He spoke of it once as something required to be paid, and spoke of it again as something required as an end, saying: (And those who are active in zakat). He did not say "those who pay zakat." The believers do not work with the aim of zakat except that they work according to their capacities, to sustain themselves and those they support; then some surplus comes from them from which they pay zakat.

And the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, says concerning zakat:

﴿And establish prayer and give zakat; and whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

So the outcome of the matter is that zakat becomes an aim for them whenever they undertake any work. By this divine command zakat has become an end in itself; it is one of the pillars of Islam, and by it the believer is distinguished from the disbeliever.

When the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, addressed the sources of miserliness in the human soul, He made clear that the first thing the human soul encounters is that a person fears spending because it diminishes what he has. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) warned against miserliness in his saying: "Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection; and beware of miserliness, for miserliness destroyed those before you, driving them to shed their blood and make lawful their prohibitions."(1) It is so; but the Truth, glory be to Him, made clear to every believer that it diminishes what you have, yet it increases you in what is with Allah; so if it diminishes the fruit of your action, it has completed you by Allah's action for you. And when it completes you by Allah's action for you, you must compare a created, incapable power with a creating, capable Power.

He, glory be to Him, draws our attention to look carefully at one of His creations, the earth, in which we plant a single seed, one grain, and it yields seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. If a person at first looked at what he places in the earth when he ploughs and sows and thought it diminishes his stores, he would not sow or plant; but when he looked at what the earth gives, seven hundredfold, he came forward to sowing and to ploughing, undeterred, because it would repay him many times over what he gave.

If the earth, which is created by Allah, gives this bounty, how then would the bounty of the Creator of the earth be?

﴿The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

Thus, by this parable the Truth has blocked the outlet of miserliness for the human soul. Another matter that the verses address is that a person may feel embarrassed in his society before a beggar who asks him; in his greed for his wealth he does not like to spend, and in his concern for his standing among people he does not like to refuse; so he gives, but with irritation, and perhaps his irritation extends to rebuking and scolding the one who asked. So the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, said, to close that situation:

﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need, Forbearing.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

Allah's saying (a kind word and forgiveness) indicates that the one asked has been upset by the beggar's request and angered by the embarrassment, and the Truth asks such a person to forgive the one who asks this lapse, if he has regarded the request as a fault:

﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Free of need, Forbearing.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah).

After that, the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, addresses (reproach, al-mann), which spoils the gift, because it makes the recipient humbled and broken, while the giver wishes to be in the dignity of giving and the elevation of the one who spends. He says: if you do that, the charity will extend from you to others and benefit them, but you are the loser, because you will gain nothing thereby, even if the beggar has benefited. So, out of concern for yourself, do not follow charity with reproach or injury.

Then the Truth comes to treat another outlet of miserliness in the human soul: a person may like to give, but when his hand reaches out to give, it is hard for him to spend the good part of his good wealth; so he keeps it for himself and sets aside the things his soul is averse to, to offer them as charity. So He, glory be to Him, forbids us this, saying:

﴿And do not aim at the bad of it to spend from it, while you yourselves would not take it except with closed eyes.﴾ (Part of verse 267, Surah al-Baqarah).

That is, if such a thing were given to you, you would not accept it except by shutting your eyes and overlooking its flaw, as though you did not see its defect, in order to take it. So what you would not accept for yourself, it is not right that you give to another. Then, after the Qur'an has spoken of the outlets of miserliness in the human soul, it makes clear to us that what produces these outlets and nourishes them is none other than Satan:

﴿Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 268).

If you equate the promise of Satan with the promise of Allah to you of good pleasure, then there is loss and ruin. So review your faith, and make the promise of Satan repelled before Allah's promise to you of bounty and forgiveness.

Then He speaks of the time of charity and of the state of giving it openly or secretly, and the intention in your heart is what tips one action over another. If you are a wealthy person, then protect your honour from people's talk, and give openly in what is obligatory upon you, to shield your honour from their remarks. And if you wish to give voluntarily, there is no harm in doing so privately, so that "your left hand does not know what your right hand has spent." It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: voluntary charity given in secret is better than its public form by seventy times, and obligatory charity given openly is better than given in secret by twenty-five times.

It is as if Allah has opened before the human soul every outlet of giving and closed the outlets of miserliness. Look next at the Truth, glory be to Him, as He protects the weak believers by placing them under the protection of the strong believers. O servant who believes, know that when you receive the command of Allah, you do not receive it as though it were always required of you; rather, you must receive the ruling as something that may, through the changing circumstances of others, become required of you. If you are wealthy, do not believe that Allah always demands it of you; but consider that if you come, through the vicissitudes of life, to be poor, the ruling will become required of you. So assess the state of it being required of you now, because you are wealthy, as the state in which it will be required for you if vicissitudes befall you and you become poor thereby.

Thus the legislation is both for you and against you. Do not regard it as always against you, for if you regard it as always against you, you isolate yourself from the vicissitudes of life, and the vicissitudes of life persist, and no one can ever be free of them. Therefore, glory be to Him, He commanded the believer to sponsor his believing brother.

(1) Related by Muslim.

Look at the aspirations of faith within the human soul, even toward those who do not share your faith. If you are asked to give the obligatory charity to your believing brother, you are also asked to give voluntarily to one who is not a believer. This is a feature of Islam found in no other religion: it protects even the non-believer. For this reason, the Truth (al-Haqq) says:

﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend is for yourselves, and you spend only seeking the Face of Allah. And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.﴾ [2:272]

What is the origin of this matter?

The origin of this matter is that some of the early converts to Islam had relatives who had not embraced Islam. These relatives were poor, and the Muslims wished to give these poor relatives some of their wealth, but they were reluctant to do so, so they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this matter.

Here is Asma' bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, whose mother Qutaylah was still a disbeliever. Asma' asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to give some of her wealth to her mother so that she might live and be sustained. Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed His words: (It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills). It is narrated from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, that she said: "My mother came to me while she was a polytheist in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I sought a ruling from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). I said: 'My mother has come to me, and she is desirous (of my help). Shall I maintain good ties with my mother?' He said: '(Yes), maintain good ties with your mother'" (1). Some of the believers had wanted to constrain their relatives who had not believed, so that they would believe, but the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, revealed the gracious word: (It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills).

This is a sublime religion. It is a religion that wants us to sustain the creature on earth with the bounty of Lordship (rububiyyah), even if that creature does not meet us in the bounty of Godhead (uluhiyyah), because the bounty of Godhead is a obligation, while the bounty of Lordship is provision and nurture.

Provision and nurture are required for everyone who is on the earth, because we know that no one in existence summoned himself into existence; rather, his Creator brought him into existence. And since the Most Generous Creator is the One who brought the servant into existence, whether believer or disbeliever, He is the one who guarantees his provision. Provision is one thing, and the domain of faith in Allah is another thing. Therefore the Truth says: (It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills).

Or perhaps the verse, when it was revealed urging spending, was addressed to the fact that some people were lazy, and some believers would deliberately choose the inferior part of their wealth to spend.

And if Islam came to confront the human soul with all its changing states and all its thoughts, it is no wonder that it treats them in this respect and returns them to what is correct if a thought arises in them that harms believing conduct. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to love that, whenever any command was revealed, the Muslims would turn to it with ardent attentiveness; when he saw negligence in any of that, he was saddened, so Allah clarifies to him: it is incumbent upon you to convey the command of Allah concerning spending, and it is not upon you, after that, that they obey. (It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills).

Someone may say: since Allah is the One who guides, we should leave people in whatever state of faith or disbelief they are in, and our duty is only to convey. To the proponents of this view we say: consider what the Qur'an provides concerning a single matter. This matter we are discussing is guidance. Let us survey all the verses, and we will find that those who hold that guidance is from Allah, and that it is not proper for Him to punish one who disobeys, have a viewpoint; and those who say that He, glorified is He, may punish them because He left them the choice, have a viewpoint. So what is the differing viewpoint, such that the matter reaches an equal level of understanding?

When Allah, the Exalted, speaks in His revealed Qur'an, He asks us to reflect upon it, and reflecting upon it means not looking at the surface of the text but looking at the underlying dimension of the text. (Will they not then reflect?) means: do not look at the face, but look at what faces the face, which is the back.

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ (part of 4:82).

And Allah, the Exalted, has said:

﴿As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾ (part of 41:17).

How can Allah have guided them, and then afterward they prefer blindness over guidance? Thus the meaning of (We guided them) is: He pointed them to good. And when He pointed them to good, He left within them the power to choose between alternatives, so they could choose this, or they could choose that. When Allah guided them and pointed them out, they preferred blindness over guidance. And Allah says to His Messenger in two other texts of the Noble Qur'an:

﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ (part of 28:56).

Thus He negated guidance from him. And in another verse, the Truth affirmed guidance for him, where He says:

﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ (part of 42:52). How does Allah affirm one act for one agent and then negate the very act from that same agent? We say to them: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is obligated to point people to the method of Allah, but he is not obligated to compel them to the method of Allah, because that is not his work. So when Allah says (Indeed, you do not guide), it means you do not force by compulsion and coercion whom you love; rather, you (guide), meaning you only point out, and upon you is conveyance, and upon Us is the reckoning.

Therefore the Truth's words (It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills) contain no proof for a compulsion of faith, which some who wish to slip away from the method of Allah want to use as an entry point for psychological evasion. We say to them: there is a difference between the guidance of indication and the guidance of help. Allah guides the believer and guides the disbeliever, that is, He points them out; but whoever believes in Him, He guides with the guidance of help, guides him with the guidance of success, and guides him with the guidance of making acts of obedience light for him.

(It is not upon you to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills; and whatever good you spend is for yourselves.) This is a matter that deals with stinginess logically: every giver's giving returns to himself, and there is no giver whose giving does not return to him except Allah. He alone is the one whose giving does not return to His creatures upon Him, because He, glorified is He, from eternity and before creating creation, possesses all the attributes of perfection. The giving of a human returns to the human, and the giving of our Lord returns to us.

For this reason some of the predecessors who had a flash of faith said: "I have never done good to anyone at all." It was said to him: "Do you say that, when you did such-and-such for so-and-so and such-and-such for so-and-so?" He said: "I only did it for myself." It was as if, when he did good for others, he saw that he was doing it for himself. We have said previously that the knower of Allah (al-Hasan al-Basri) would, when someone came to him asking, brighten his face and rejoice, and say: "Welcome to one who has come carrying my provision to the Hereafter without a wage."

Thus he saw that he was giving to him, even though he was taking from him. So Allah, the Truth, glorified and exalted, addresses this matter with (and whatever good you spend is for yourselves), meaning: beware lest you think that I ask you to give to others. I have asked you to spend so that I may increase you in spending and giving. Then He says: (And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you in full). The meaning of tawfiyah is complete fulfilment. Do not think that you are spending on one who denies your kindness, for whatever good you have spent, Allah is Knowing of it. So make your spending with the one who denies, and do not make your spending with the one who praises, for by that you have taken your reward from the one who praises you, and with Allah there is no reward for you.

I used to always say to those who complain of people's ingratitude and forgetting of kindness: "You are deserving of that, because you kept them in mind the hour you spent upon them; had you kept Allah in mind, that would never have happened from them." (And whatever good you spend is for yourselves, and you spend only seeking the Face of Allah.) Is this verse a commendation of the believers' deeds, or a report intended as a command? It is both together: it means, spend seeking the Face of Allah. (And whatever good you spend will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.) You will not be wronged by creation, and you will not be wronged by the Creator. As for creation, you have secured your religion and your honour when you discharge some of Allah's rights from your wealth, so no one will transgress against you to say what they say; and as for with Allah, He, glorified is He, repays good manifold, many times over what you have spent.

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Then the Exalted Lord speaks of one of the avenues of charitable spending that existed in the early days of Islam:

﴿For the poor who are confined in the way of Allah and cannot travel about the land. The ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their abstinence. You will know them by their mark; they do not beg of people persistently. And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah knows it.﴾ [2:273]

When we hear a prepositional phrase (jarr wa majrur) with which a noble verse begins, we know there is something it is attached to. What is "for the poor" attached to? Here it is the spending: that is, spending is for the poor who are confined in the way of Allah. And if we ask what "uhsiru" (confined, restricted) means, we find that there is "hasar" and there is "ahsar," and both carry the sense of prevention, except that prevention sometimes comes from something you cannot repel, and sometimes from something you are able to repel.

For example, one who is sick and is restricted from traveling about the land: did he have the ability to do that? No. But one who wanted to travel the land and was prevented by another person like himself is prevented, so the matter ultimately returns to prevention. Prevention may come from the self itself, or from the action of others. Thus, "they were confined in the way of Allah": they were confined because the disbelievers constricted the avenues of life for them, or they confined themselves to jihad and did not wish to occupy themselves with anything else, since Islam still needed a people who would strive. These are the People of the Suffah. "For the poor who are confined in the way of Allah, who cannot travel about the land," their inability arises either from a matter outside their will, or from a matter in their intention, which is to stand guard in the way of Allah. Both are permissible.

The Ansar would bring dates and leave them in their clusters, hanging them on ropes tied to the pillars of the mosque. Whenever one of the People of the Suffah became hungry, he would take his staff and strike a cluster of dates, so some of the dates would fall and he would eat. Some would bring the inferior dates and the shees (poor, dry dates) and place them there, and this is what Allah referred to when He said: ﴿And do not aim at the bad of it to spend from, while you would not take it yourselves except with closed eyes.﴾ [2:267]

When we consider the words of the Truth, ﴿they cannot travel about the land,﴾ "daraba" (to strike) is an action of a limb with force upon something affected by that striking. And what is "daraba fi al-ardh" (striking in the land)? The Exalted Lord wishes to show us that struggle in life must be at the utmost level of strength; when you go out into the land, you must strike it with plowing and with sowing. You do not take it with ease or gentleness. Therefore the Truth says: ﴿It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its tracts and eat of His provision, and to Him is the resurrection.﴾ [67:15]

Indeed, the earth is made subservient by the Truth, Glorified and Exalted, to man: he strives in it, travels in it, and eats of the provision of Allah that comes out of it.

When Allah, Glorified be He, describes those who are confined in the way of Allah and cannot travel about the land, saying ﴿the ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their abstinence﴾, meaning the ignorant one, by their circumstances, assumes they are rich. The cause of this assumption is their leaving off asking. And if abstinence (ta'affuf) is leaving off asking, then Allah says after it: ﴿You will know them by their mark; they do not beg of people persistently.﴾ The "simah" (mark) is the distinguishing sign that indicates the state of its bearer. It is as though you would find in them humility, submissiveness and shabby appearance even if they do not ask or request; yet you recognize them from their state, which deserves that one spend on them. And if abstinence is leaving off asking, then Allah says after it: ﴿they do not beg of people persistently﴾, so it is as though He permits mere asking but forbids insistence and importunity in it. And if they had asked a mere request without insistence or importunity, would this not be evidence that they are not wealthy? Yes, but He said: ﴿the ignorant man thinks them wealthy because of their abstinence.﴾ So there is no asking, no asking in its absolute sense, and all the more so no insistence in asking; the evidence is that the Truth says: ﴿You will know them by their mark﴾, and if they had asked we would have recognized them by their asking. Thus the verse indicates that what is negated is asking in general. As for the word "ilhaf" (insistence), it came for one of the meanings toward which the miraculous style aims. What is it?

As we said, "simah" is the distinguishing mark indicating the state of its bearer. It is as though you would find humility, submissiveness and shabby appearance even if they do not ask; that is, you recognize them from their wretched condition. So if the one who asks does ask afterward, his asking is considered insistence, because his state already indicates need. And since his state indicates need, he should have been provided for without having to ask; so if he asks even a mere request, it is as though he has insisted and pressed the matter.

Also, the Truth wants the believer to have penetrating insight into his brother, so that he perceives his circumstances by looking at him and does not let him ask. For if you recognize by "simah," you are intelligent and perceptive; but if you do not recognize by "simah" and wait until he says it and asks you, then you are deficient in perceptive insight. Thus the Exalted Lord wants the believer to be perceptive in looking, so that he can discern in the faces of his believing brothers who bears the concern of need and who carries the thoughts of want. When he knows this, he possesses faith-based discernment.

There is a lesson in that incident: one of the knowers of Allah was visited when someone knocked on his door. He went out, then came back in and went out again carrying something, gave it to the visitor, then returned weeping. His wife said to him: "What makes you weep?" He said: "So-and-so knocked on my door." She said: "And you gave him, so what made you weep?" He said: "Because I left him until he asked me."

The knower of Allah wept because he felt the responsibility of what he should have recognized through his insight and should have learned about the circumstances of his brothers. For this reason Allah legislated the Friday gatherings, so that a person may check on each of his brothers: what has kept him back, sickness or need? Debt or calamity? And so that he does not force him to humiliate himself and ask. When he does this, he possesses the discernment of faith.

﴿And whatever good you spend, indeed Allah knows it.﴾ You must know that before you give, Allah has already known that you will give; the matter is reckoned with Him by a measure, and the conduct of His creation comes in accordance with His decree, and what He decreed in the past necessarily applies now. He, Glorified be He, has decreed, because He knew that His servant would do it, and he has done it. Every act has a time in which it occurs and a manner in which it occurs. And time is either night or day.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says, explaining the circumstances of spending and the times in which it takes place, in His saying:

﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly, they will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾ (2:274)

The matter of spending requires two things: either you spend secretly, or you spend openly. The time is night and day. So Allah has confined time and circumstance to two things: night and day. Beware, then, of holding back a gift you intend to give, saying: "I will do it by day, or I will do it at night, because that is better," and making excuses that give you room to delay giving. The Truth wants the expenditure to reach the poor from you, by night or by day. The question of night and day in respect of time, and the question of secrecy and openness in respect of manner, have no bearing on the sincerity of intention in giving.

﴿Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and openly⦆. Does the verse say: "Those who spend their wealth by night or by day?" No. It has required of each of us that his spending be by night and by day, and said: ﴿secretly and openly﴾. So spend by night, spend by day, spend secretly, and spend openly. Do not limit spending to night or to day, to a time, or to a manner, or to a state.

Allah, the Truth, has encompassed the time of spending, night and day, and has also encompassed the manner in which spending takes place, secretly and openly, so that spending may spread at every time and in every form. Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says of these people: ﴿they will have their reward with their Lord﴾, and this statement indicates the generality of those from whom spending may come, by night or by day, secretly or openly.

Some people have said that it was revealed on a specific occasion: that Imam ʿAli, may Allah ennoble his face and be pleased with him, had four dirhams, so he gave one in charity by day, one by night, one secretly, and one openly, and the verse was revealed concerning that occasion. However, the word of Allah ﴿they will have﴾ indicates the generality of the subject, not the specificity of the cause. It is as if the reward that Allah, glory be to Him, has ordained for that act is common to everyone from whom this deed can come.

The word of Allah ﴿they will have their reward with their Lord﴾: here we find that the word ﴿ajr﴾ (reward) gives us a glimpse into the believer's stance toward all acts of spending, because a reward (ajr) is only for work that has a price for something, and it is a wage for labor. The one you hire offers you nothing but effort, and this effort may produce something valued, that is, a thing that has a price. So the saying of Allah ﴿they will have their reward with their Lord﴾ indicates that the believer must regard everything that comes from work as something Allah asks him to spend from.

Allah does not give him the price of what he spent; rather, Allah gives him the reward of the work. Why? Because the believer who travels through the earth plans with his thought, and thought is created by Allah; he carries out the plan he devised with his thought through his energies and his apparatus, and his energies and apparatus are created by Allah; he interacts with the material he works upon, and all of it is created by Allah. So what does man possess in all of this? Neither the thought that plans, nor the energy that acts, nor the material that is acted upon: all of it belongs to Allah. Therefore you alone have the reward of your work, because you exercise a thought created by Allah, with an energy created by Allah, upon a material created by Allah. If something results from it that Allah wishes you to take and give to your poor, needy brother, then He gives you the reward of your work, not the price of your work. But if a created being equal to you, a human, takes the proceeds of your work from you, then he gives you the price of what he took from you. So the price (thaman) is from an equal created being, and the reward (ajr) is from the Highest Creator, because you possess nothing in all of that.

Then the Truth says: ﴿and no fear will there be upon them, nor will they grieve﴾. Fear is caution about something that is coming. So who is the one fearing? Who is the one feared? And who is the one about whom fear is felt? ﴿And no fear will there be upon them﴾ from whom?

It is permissible that ﴿no fear will there be upon them﴾ refers to fear from themselves. A student may fear for himself that he will fail; the self is one, fearing and feared for: it is fearful now and will be feared for afterward. When the pupil fears he will fail, it is not said that the one who fears is the very same as the one who is feared for, because this one is in his state, and that one is in his state.

Or ﴿no fear will there be upon them﴾ refers to fear from others. It is possible that around many wealthy people there are foolish people who, when they see these people's hands extended with goodness to others, wink at them to hold back, fearing they will become poor, saying to them: "Prepare for the age, for behind you are your dependents." But people of goodness do not listen to these fools.

So ﴿no fear will there be upon them﴾ is neither from themselves nor from the fools around them. The Truth continues: ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, meaning there is no fear upon them now, and no sorrow in them when they are confronted with the realities of goodness that Allah, glory be to Him, has stored up for them; rather, they will rejoice.

Afterwards, Allah the Exalted addresses an issue among the most dangerous issues of the age. This issue the Qur'an had to address, because it speaks of spending (nafaqah) and of giving (infaq), and there is no doubt that this requires a spender and one on whom it is spent, because he is incapable. Suppose that people became stingy and did not spend. What then is the position of the incapable one who finds nothing? His position does not go beyond two matters: either he goes off to borrow, and if no one agrees to lend him, he takes up usury (riba) and increase, or else how would he live?

So the verses we are concerned with address the economic structure in an Islamic nation that is generous, or in an Islamic nation that is miserly and niggardly. Why?

Because the One who created the creatures has made a precise reckoning for that creation, such that if you counted what the wealthy owe in zakat, and counted what is needed by the one who is unable, because he has a natural incapacity to work, you would find that the incapable ones need exactly what overflows from the capable ones, with no increase or decrease. Otherwise there would be an error, God forbid, in the reckoning of the Creator, and that can never occur.

When we look at societies in their formation, we find that a wealthy person in one place has become averse to his place and has chosen to live in another place. People wonder why he left that place while he is in ease, prosperity and wealth. Perhaps if he were poor we would say he sought wider means, but why did he leave this place while he is wealthy and in such ease? They did not perceive that God, who created the creatures, manages His dominion by directing the thoughts that occur to people's minds, so you find that his place has become averse to him, his soul has been filled with unease, and he chose to go to another place.

Were we to have precise statistical instruments and reckon the needy in the environment he moved from, we would find an amount of wealth exceeding the needs of those living in that environment; so God directed it to another place that needs such a quantity of it. Thus you find the exchange organized. If you see a needy person, or a person who wants to practise usury, know that there is a shortfall in the known right of God, and I do not say in the unknown right. That is, the wealthy person was miserly with what he is obliged to spend on the needy.

When the Qur'an confronts this matter, it confronts it by disparaging usurious dealing in a way that makes the upright human nature recoil from it, and the Exalted says:

﴿Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, "Trade is but like usury," and Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may keep what is past, and his affair is up to Allah; but whoever returns to it — those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ [2:275]

Look at the word (yakulun, "consume"). Are all the needs of life eating? No. The needs of life are many; eating is one of them, but eating is the most important of them, because it is the means of sustaining the self. And (riba) is the surplus, and since it is the surplus, it means he does not need to eat it, so this is a rebuke to him.

The Truth wants to disgrace this matter, so He says: they have a mark (simah). The scholars have said: is this in the Hereafter, by which they are distinguished on the Gathering, as the Truth says:

﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾ [55:41].

So those who do not pray have a distinguishing sign, and those who do not pay zakat have another distinguishing sign, such that when you see them you recognise them by their marks, and that they are of whatever category of the disobedient. It is as though, when they rise on the Day of Resurrection, they rise staggering like one who is being struck and beaten by Satan's touch so that he falls, or else this is a matter that occurs to them in this world. Let us examine this matter:

(Those who consume usury will not stand except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity.) We want to know the word (takhabbut, "staggering"), the word (shaytan, "Satan"), and the word (mass, "touch"). (Takhabbut) is striking without evenness and guidance. You say: so-and-so staggers, meaning his movement is not regular, not logical, a movement with no controlling principle; that is takhabbut. (Shaytan) is a kind of creation of God, for God told us that He created humans and jinn, and among the jinn are shayatin and unrestricted jinn, and the shaytan is the disobedient one of the jinn. We have not seen Satan, but we have known of him through the information of the Truth in which we believed, which said: I have a hidden creation, and therefore I named it jinn, from concealment, and from it comes majnun, meaning one whose mind is concealed; and the disobedient of this creation is called (shaytan).

So our belief in him is not from sense perception, but from belief in the unseen, of which those we believe in informed us. When we find something called faith, we must know that it relates to something not perceived by the senses, because for what is perceived by the senses one is not told to believe in it, since it is witnessed to you. I do not say: I believe that the lamp is shining now; I do not believe that we are gathered in the mosque now; I do not say that, because this is a witnessed and sensed reality. So the matter of faith relates to the unseen, such as belief in the existence of the angels. Now, having believed in the unseen, we find the Truth, glorified and exalted, giving us an image of Satan, and when He gives us an image of Satan, or of the distinguishing head of Satan, just as our own heads are what distinguish us, He speaks of the tree of zaqqum, saying:

﴿Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire. Its emerging fruit is like the heads of devils﴾ [37:64–65].

The tree of zaqqum is in the Hereafter, in the Fire, so we do not see it, and we do not see the heads of devils. How then does God liken what we have not seen to what we have not seen, likening an unknown thing to an unknown thing? We say: yes, and that is intended for the miraculousness of the Qur'an, for Satan has a frightful imagined form. The proof is that if you asked the caricaturists of the world to draw a picture of Satan, without giving them the features of a specific form, each of them would draw, according to his imagination, an entity extremely ugly: this one depicts him as ugly in one respect, and that one depicts him as ugly in another respect, such that if you gathered the drawings, no drawing would match another.

So each one finds horrible the image he draws. And when we give the prize to whoever drew the picture of Satan, do we give it to the most beautiful picture or the ugliest? We give it to the one with the most extreme ugliness. So the image of Satan is a frightful, ugly form. Had he come in one single form of ugliness, people would differ about that form, for it might be ugly to you and not ugly to another. But when God releases people's imaginations in conceiving ugliness, ugliness becomes manifest and clear in the works of each person, so the image becomes more complete and fuller, and the more complete and fuller is that ugliness be widespread in all of them.

The Truth says: (like one who is being beaten by Satan's touch). We have said that Satan is the disobedient of the jinn, and we have said that our Lord, glorified and exalted, has told us much that the shayatin have attachment and connection with many humans:

﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in burden﴾ [72:6].

(They do not stand except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan's touch.) It is as though Satan has touched human makeup with a touch that corrupts the soundness of its faculties. Human makeup has a soundness of faculties with one another; every movement has its soundness. When Satan touches it, the coordination of the faculties is corrupted, so its psychological faculties become unsound and out of harmony with one another, and its movement becomes irregular and illogical.

What is the connection between this image and the process of usury? If you want a distinguishing mark in the Hereafter, then when you see someone struck down, know that he is among the people of usury. That is in the Hereafter; in this world you also find that he has an illogical, hysterical movement. How?

Look at the world now. God created the world in a form of completeness. This person has capacities and talents, and that one has other talents and capacities, until the holder of these capacities needs the holder of those capacities, and the universe is completed. Had every person been an identical unit, everyone would have been independent of everyone. Had individuals been equal in talents, people would not have needed one another. But talents differ, because if you excel in one art of life, others have excelled in other arts you need; if they need you in what you excel at, you need them in what they excel at, and thus the world is completed. Likewise God created the universe: hot regions, cold regions, regions with minerals, regions with agriculture, so that the world is compelled to complete itself and compelled to live together. That is why the Truth says in Surah al-Rahman:

﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures﴾ [55:10].

(He laid it out) for whom? (The earth): what earth, and what creatures? The whole earth, and all creatures. If it is confined by barriers, it becomes corrupt. Preventing a human from freedom of movement from place to place corrupts human movement in the universe. A person may wish to move to virgin land to cultivate it, but the people of that land refuse. Had the whole earth been for all creatures, so that if work became scarce in one place you could go to another place without restrictions upon you, but those restrictions arose from temporal authorities that hold places for themselves, that is what corrupts the universe. There are environments complaining of scarce food, and environments complaining of a shortage of workers for a ruined land that is fit for cultivation. Had the whole earth been for all creatures, there would be no inability.

We note what is said: population density or the population explosion, while there are places that need people and people who need places. Why this imbalance? This imbalance arises from the fact that human conduct is not logical in this universe. The universe we live in has various intellectual advancements and inventive ambitions that have risen to the planets and conquer space, and every home has entertainment devices. Would logic not require that the world live happy and at rest?

Logic would require that the world live at rest and calm, because every day it invents things that give it the greatest fruit with the least effort in the shortest time, so what more do we want? But does the world we live in accord with logic in this reality? No. Rather, we find that the richest and best-endowed economic countries in the world are those in which people suffer anxiety, are full of turmoil, where deviance spreads, and where they complain of high rates of madness among their populations.

So the world is not logical. And this staggering confirms what the Truth says: (except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan's touch). It is a hysterical movement in the universe, indicating that it is a universe not at rest, a universe not in harmony with its aspirations and inventions.

Should this universe, with its intelligent people, not seek the cause of this, and ask why we suffer all this misery while we have these inventive ambitions? They should have searched. The calamity is general; it does not afflict only the backward or developing countries, but also the developed ones. Thinkers should have convened conferences to examine this question. If the matter is general, encompassing all lands, advanced and backward, we must seek a common cause, and not seek a cause that may exist among one people and not among another, for if we searched we would say: it exists in this environment. But it exists likewise in all environments, so the common factor must exist.

The sustenances in the universe divide into two kinds: a sustenance from which we benefit directly, and a sustenance that is the cause of what we benefit from directly. I eat a loaf of bread; this is called direct sustenance. I drink water, which is direct sustenance; I clothe myself with a garment, which is also direct sustenance; I dwell in a house, which is fourthly direct sustenance; I light a lamp, which is direct sustenance. But money brings direct sustenance and does not replace direct sustenance. If I had a mountain of gold and I were hungry, what would I do with it? So a loaf of bread is better than it. This is direct sustenance; money or gold I buy with it this and that, but l

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 2, verse 276

He, glory be to Him, means to say: Beware lest interest (ribā) deceive you by its wording, for words deceive people. You named it (ribā, "increase") from a superficial, outward view, because ribā is increase, while zakāh diminishes. In ribā, a hundred becomes a hundred and ten, for example, according to the interest rate, whereas in zakāh a hundred becomes ninety-seven and a half (97.5), on money and trade goods, and it differs from that in crops and other things. On the surface, ribā increased and zakāh decreased. But this decrease and that increase exist only in your terminology and your customs. Almighty and Exalted God erases the increase and makes the decrease grow. So He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿God deprives interest of blessing and makes charities grow. And God does not love every ungrateful sinner.﴾

The word yamḥaq (erases) comes from maḥq, meaning to be lost state after state, that is, it is not lost suddenly but slips away into loss without one's awareness. From it comes al-māḥaq, meaning the waning of the crescent moon. "God erases interest" means He makes it appear splendid to its owner, and then ruin creeps into him from where he does not perceive.

If we examine closely the environments around us, we find the confirmation of this. How many people have practised ribā, and we saw them and knew them, and afterwards we came to know how their lives ended. ("God erases interest and makes charities grow.") He says in another verse:

﴿And whatever you give in ribā so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with God.﴾ (part of verse 39, Surah al-Rūm).

So beware lest you think that you deceive God by this... What is the counterpart?

﴿And whatever zakāh you give, seeking the Face of God, those are the ones who multiply.﴾ (part of verse 39, Surah al-Rūm).

The "muḍʿifūn" (those who multiply) are those who make a thing into manifold multiples. When the Truth says, "God erases interest," do not belittle the attribution of the act to God. The attribution of an act to its doer must take its manner from the essence of the doer. If it is said to you, "So-and-so, the weak man, slaps you," or "So-and-so, the boxer, slaps you," you must measure this slap by its doer. So if God is the One who said, "God erases," is there any erasure beyond this? No, it is not possible.

Also, when God says, "God erases interest and makes charities grow," in the Qur'an that is recited, which is miraculous, preserved, and challenged by its preservation, this is a guarded matter: "God erases interest and makes charities grow." Because the One who said it is God, in the Book of God that is preserved, recited in worship, meaning the matter is on the tongues of all the masses and in the hearts of all believers. Would God state a matter that He preserves with such preservation, only for the reality of time to come and refute it? No, it is not possible. A person preserves only the document that supports him! I preserve only the promissory note that concerns me! Since He is its Preserver, and He is the One who said:

﴿Indeed, We sent down the Reminder, and indeed We are its guardians.﴾ (Surah al-Ḥijr, 9).

This means that He, glory be to Him, will issue within it matters, and these matters He has undertaken to preserve, and He undertakes to preserve them only so that they may be a proof of His truthfulness in saying them. Something that contains no proof, we do not preserve. He, glory be to Him, is the One who said:

﴿And indeed Our host, they are the victorious.﴾ (Surah al-Ṣāffāt, 173).

This is a Qur'anic matter which God has undertaken to preserve, so the reality of life must come to confirm it. If the reality of life does not confirm it, what then is the position? Shall we deny the Qur'an? Far be it from us to deny the Qur'an, which was spoken by the Truth, there is no god but Him, to govern a universe from behind it.

(God deprives interest of blessing and makes charities grow, and God does not love every ungrateful sinner.) Why did the Truth say "kaffār" (ungrateful, intensive form) and not "kāfir," and why did He say "athīm" (sinner, intensive form) and not merely "āthim"? Because He wants to return the judgment to God, and as long as he wants to return the judgment to God, he has committed two disbeliefs: a disbelief because he did not acknowledge this, and a disbelief because he rejected the judgment of God. And he is "athīm," not merely "āthim," and in this is the intensive form, so that we may infer that the matter we are discussing is a social, civilizational, universal matter, and if it is not as God intended it, the pillars of the whole society will be shaken.

The Qur'an, having explained to us the bitterness of excess in (kuffar) and in (athim), now brings the opposite, so that we may perceive the sweetness of that opposite. An example of this is what the poet says:

"The face is like the dawn, whitened,
and the hair is like the night, blackened.
Two opposites, when they come together, become beautiful,
and the opposite reveals the beauty of its opposite."

So it is as if God, after speaking of the disbelievers and the sinner, brings us back to the sweetness of faith, saying:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds, establish prayer, and give zakat, they will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will be upon them, nor will they grieve.﴾ (2:277)

We have said that the word (ajr, reward) implies that no creature owns a commodity; rather, all of us are hired workers. Why? Because we employ a brain created by God, with energy created by God, in matter created by God. So what do you, O human, own except your action? And since you own nothing but your action, you have a reward (﴿for them is their reward with their Lord﴾). The phrase (with their Lord) has a noteworthy aspect: when your wage is with an equal to you, he may consume you; but your wage with a Lord who has taken charge of your upbringing will never be lost.

The Truth continues: (﴿and no fear will be upon them﴾), neither from themselves against themselves, nor from their loved ones against them; (﴿nor will they grieve﴾), because whatever good has escaped them will be found present before them.

After that, the Truth says:

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 278:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains of interest, if you should be believers.﴾

When the Truth (al-Haqq) says, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, we know that the address by faith is the basis (haythiyya) of every obligation that follows it. When the Truth calls out and says, ﴿O you who have believed﴾, it means: O you who have believed in Me as a God who is All-Powerful, All-Wise, Mighty over you, dominant over My command; your disobedience does not harm Me, and your obedience does not benefit Me. So if you have believed in Me, and I am a God who is All-Powerful and All-Wise, then listen to Me regarding the rulings that I love for you.

Therefore every ﴿O you who have believed﴾ in the Qur'an is the basis (haythiyya) of every ruling that comes after it. You act on what Allah commands you, and if someone asks you and says to you: Why did you do this? Say to him: I did it because I am a believer, and the One who commanded me is the One whose wisdom and power I have believed in. You do not enter the maze of the causes (ʿilal) of the rulings, because you have believed that Allah is a Wise and Powerful God who sent down those obligations to you. Beware of entering the maze of the cause (ʿilla) of the rulings. Why? Because there are things whose cause may be hidden from you. Would you postpone them until you know the cause?

Did we postpone the prohibition of the flesh of swine until it is established today through analysis that it is harmful? No. If it is established today through analysis that it is harmful, then we become more confident in every ruling Allah has obligated us with, even if we have not been guided to its cause. The Truth says: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah﴾. Among the wonders of the word ﴿fear (ittaqū)﴾ is that it comes in things that seem contradictory, but they actually converge. ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah﴾, and it does not say here: fear the Fire, as it says in another verse: ﴿fear the Fire﴾. So how can He say ﴿fear Allah﴾ and say ﴿fear the Fire﴾? Because the meaning of ﴿fear (ittaqū)﴾ is: make a shield (wiqāya) between yourselves and your Lord.

How do we make a shield between ourselves and our Lord, when what is required of us in terms of faith is that we join ourselves to the methodology of Allah so that we are always in the company (maʿiyya) of Allah? We say: Allah, glory be to Him, has attributes of majesty (ṣifāt jalāl), such as the Subduer (al-Qahhār), the Avenger (al-Muntaqim), the Compeller (al-Jabbār), the Possessor of Bounty (Dhū al-Ṭawl), and Severe in Punishment (Shadīd al-ʿiqāb). So He asks His believing servant to make a shield between himself and His attributes of majesty. The Fire is one of the hosts of the attributes of majesty. When He, glory be to Him, says ﴿fear Allah﴾, it means: make a shield between yourselves and the attributes of majesty, of which the Fire is one of the hosts. So ﴿fear Allah﴾ is like ﴿fear the Fire﴾, meaning: make a shield between yourselves and the Fire.

The Truth continues: ﴿and give up what remains of interest, if you should be believers﴾. ﴿Give up (dharū)﴾ means: leave, abandon, forget, and seek good from Allah concerning what remains of interest, if you are truly believers in Allah. It is as if Allah wanted to make this a decisive purification, after which the believer is born pure and clean.

It is a command from the Truth: leave the interest that you have not yet received, because what you have received is governed by His words ﴿so he keeps what is past﴾. As for what you have not received, leave it: ﴿fear Allah and give up what remains of interest, if you should be believers﴾. If you say that the contract was concluded before the prohibition, and the contract has made the right to that gain yours, remember that you have not taken possession of this right so that it becomes in your hand, and do not say that my economic life depends on it. The arrangement of economic life was not established by agreement on this interest, but it is established by taking possession of it, and you have not taken possession of it.

The Truth continues:

﴿And if you do not do so, then be informed of war from Allah and His Messenger. But if you repent, you shall have your principal; you do no wrong, nor are you wronged.﴾ (2:279)

In this verse there is a universal matter that many people overlook. A system has come to protect one group from the injustice of another group, and this system came only after the group of usurers (murabin) had wronged the group of poor and oppressed people. It is enough for these oppressed people, who were exploited by the usurers, that the Qur'an should grant them justice and bring the matter of riba (usury) to an end in a way that gives those who practised usury what has already passed, because they had built their lives upon it.

As for ﴿فأذنوا بحرب﴾ (fa-'dhanu bi-harb, "then be informed of war"): the root ا-ذ-ن (alif, dhal, nun) is the source of the whole word-family, derived from al-udhn (ear, hearing). The ear is the first foundation of information (i'lam), because a person is not presumed to be a reader first; he cannot be a reader unless he hears, so information can arise only through hearing. When the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of the instruments of human knowledge, He said:

﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that you may give thanks.﴾ (16:78)

Accordingly, when the science of physiology came to examine this, they found it exactly as Allah described it. A newborn infant, when a human finger is brought near its eyes, does not blink, because its eyes have not yet performed their function; but if one shouts beside its ear, it reacts.

We know that the first organ to perform its function for the human infant is his ear, and it is also the organ that performs its function for a person whether awake or asleep. The eye closes in sleep and does not see, but the ear is ready at all times to hear, because it is the instrument of summoning (al-istidt'a'). Thus the word al-adhan (call to prayer) and al-udhn (ear) all come from the function of hearing. Allah, glory be to Him, said:

﴿And it has listened to its Lord and it must [obey]﴾ (84:5)

What is the meaning of ﴿أذنت﴾ (adhinat, "it listened")? When you hear from an equal, you may comply or you may not; but when you hear from a capable God, there is no escape for you but to comply. It is as if Allah is saying: the earth splits when it hears My command to split. As soon as the earth hears the command of the Truth, it acts, and it is right that it should act; it has listened to the command of Allah, that is, it submitted, because the one who addresses it is Allah.

Thus the whole word-family here comes from al-udhn (ear). Therefore Allah says to those who do not do what Allah has commanded regarding usury: ﴿فإن لم تفعلوا فأذنوا بحرب من الله ورسوله﴾ ("If you do not, then be informed of war from Allah and His Messenger"). As for the war of Allah, we say nothing about it except the words of Allah:

﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾ (74:31)

No one can take precautions against it. As for the war of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that is the apparent matter. It is as if Allah, glory be to Him, is dispatching against the usurers a tremendous expedition from His hosts, which none knows except Him; and the hosts of the war of the Messenger are the believers in his message, who must be a force against every manifestation of corruption in the universe, in order to purify their lives from the filth of usury.

Thus Allah set an end to this mode of dealing, so that wealth may be purified of that usury. When the Truth says ﴿فلكم رؤوس أموالكم لا تظلمون ولا تُظلَمون﴾ ("you shall have your principal; you do no wrong, nor are you wronged"), the meaning is that He, glory be to Him, makes clear by this statement that the usurers have no right to double or two-fold, nor to multiplied increases. Then ﴿لا تظلمون﴾ ("you do no wrong") applies to you who practised usury: you must not take from them anything beyond the principal.

But what is the place of ﴿ولا تُظلمون﴾ ("nor are you wronged"), and who would wrong them? Perhaps a weak person who was wronged by them earlier may take from them some of the principal, claiming that since they exploited him, taking from him an amount beyond the principal, he may now take back. The legislation wants to prevent the former wrongdoer, ending his injustice, and to aid the later wronged person, giving him his right. Glory be to Him, He does not wish to direct an injustice in order to exploit one who was wronged, so that he wrongs the one who wronged him first; rather, by this ruling He wills to end this kind of injustice absolutely, and to make everyone equal in benefiting from the advantages of the ruling.

Many theories that come to overturn a system in some society aim at the group that did the wronging, and do not content themselves with restraining them from injustice; rather they empower the wronged to wrong those who wronged him. That is injustice (ijhaf) in society, and this is what people must pay close attention to, because Allah, who gave you justice, O wronged one, against your wrongdoer by preventing his injustice toward you, here you must respect His ruling when He says ﴿فله ما سلف﴾ ("he keeps what has passed"), and with this statement the matter is concluded.

Then He, glory be to Him, resumes the command with a new justice that brings you and him together on a footing of equality, without injustice from you, O formerly wronged one, on the pretext that he wronged you. Societies that follow this system ("you do no wrong, nor are you wronged") are walking a moderate path, not one of directed injustice. We blame a people for having done wrong, then we bring another people to make them wrong; no. Rather, everyone is on an equal footing from now on.

The corruption of any system in society comes from directing injustice from a new faction against an old faction; thus injustice remains in place: one group wronged, and then a group that had been wronged comes to wrong the group that previously wronged. We say to them: that is directed injustice, and we want justice to be ordered and to encompass all members of society, so that each person takes his right. The one who wronged previously, we have prevented from his wrongdoing, and the one who was overcome previously, we have granted justice, and thus all are on an equal footing; so that society may walk a just course governed by a faith-based principle. We do not reward the one who disobeyed Allah concerning us with anything more than that we obey Allah concerning him.

And after that the Qur'an comes to open a new door of hope before those who have been wronged. It puts an end to those who were previously oppressors: it ruled for them the principal (ra's al-mal) and forbade them from taking more than the principal, so their hearts were softened toward these people. That is to say, it is not an inescapable necessity that you take your principal right now; rather, you must give the debtor respite and grant him time if he is in hardship. And if you rise high in certain, faithful maturity and are content with God as a substitute for every compensation that escapes you, then you must go beyond and forgo even your principal, which God has ruled for you, so that you may elevate yourselves through it and give it to one who cannot pay. Then the word of the Truth comes:

﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be respite until a time of ease; but that you remit it as charity is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ [2:280]

As for "And if the debtor is in hardship" (wa-in kana dhu 'usra): it rules that the creditor has his principal, but suppose the debtor is in hardship. Here is an issue raised by some orientalists who claim they have studied Arabic. They studied it as a craft (sina'a), but the linguistic faculty (malaka) eluded them, because language is not merely a craft. Language is a natural disposition (tab'), language is a faculty (malaka), language is a sentiment (wijdan). They say that the Qur'an misses some of the rules that its language lays down. For example, they brought this verse: ﴿And if the debtor is in hardship, then let there be respite until a time of ease; and that you remit it as charity is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

Some orientalists said: we want to investigate with the scholars of the Qur'an the predicate (khabar) of "kana" in His words "wa-in kana dhu 'usra". Indeed, we do not find the predicate of "kana", and his Arabic faculty is lacking, because if he had studied Arabic he should have known that "kana" requires a subject and a predicate: a subject in the nominative and a predicate in the accusative, and this is what is called the incomplete "kana" (kana al-naqisa). He should also have understood that it may come complete (tamma), meaning it has no predicate and is satisfied with the nominative alone. This requires a simple explanation.

Every verb indicates an event and a time. The word "kana", when you hear it, indicates existence and an absolute event in which the state of its subject is not specified: kana mujtahidan? kana kasulan? For example, it indicates the existence of something in absolute terms, that is, it has no state. This means that "kana" indicates absolute existential time, that is, the bare incomplete meaning, and an absolute thing is not made clear unless it is restricted. So if you want to indicate a restricted existence, so that the meaning becomes clear and manifest, you must bring it a predicate, as when you say: kana Zayd mujtahidan (Zayd was diligent). Here a particular thing has come into existence, namely Zayd's diligence. Thus "kana" here is incomplete, requiring a predicate to complete it and give it a particular existence. But if the matter is not so, and we want existence only, then "kana" is complete, that is, it is satisfied with its nominative alone, as when you say: "the absent one returned, so there was joy" (fa-kana al-farah), i.e., joy came into being; or "the sun rose, so there was light" (fa-kana al-nur). And the poet says:

wa-kānat wa-laysa al-subḥu fīhā bi-abyaḍa
wa-aḍḥat wa-laysa al-layl fīhā bi-aswada

So His words "wa-in kana dhu 'usra" mean: "if there is found one in hardship", i.e., if there is found a person who has no ability to repay, then "respite" (fa-nazira) from the creditor "until a time of ease" (ila maysara), i.e., until he becomes at ease; and the principal in this case is a "goodly loan" (qardan hasanan). Whenever he is patient with him for a moment, God gives him reward for it.

We should know that the reward of a goodly loan is greater than the reward of charity, because when you give charity you have cut off your soul's hope from it, and you do not occupy yourself with it, and you receive reward for it all at once. But when you give a loan, your heart remains attached to it; the more intense the attachment and the love of wealth that blows upon you, and you remain patient, the more reward you receive. Therefore you must note that when a loan is a goodly loan, and the borrower is truly excused, because there is a difference between one who is truly excused and one who is excused falsely. The one truly excused is the one who strives hard to settle his debt, but circumstances stand before him and prevent it. As for the one falsely excused, he finds with him what would settle his debt, but he procrastinates in paying, and the money stays with him benefiting him, and in this he is a wrongdoer.

Therefore test yourself: you will find that every debt that occupies your heart, know that its owner was eager to pay and did not pay; and every debt that was coolness and peace upon your heart, know that its owner is truly excused and cannot pay; and perhaps you feel shy to pass by him, lest your mere sight embarrass him. These debts do not remain long, because the Messenger judged this matter with a ruling, when he (ﷺ) said: "Whoever takes people's wealth intending to repay it, God will repay it on his behalf, and whoever takes it intending to destroy it, God will destroy him" (1).

So as long as at the hour he takes it he intends to repay, God makes the way of repayment easy for him; and whoever takes it intending to destroy it, God does not make it easy for him to pay, because he cannot leave money with which to settle his debt. And there is an incident in the life of the Messenger (ﷺ) that explains this hadith: a man died owing a debt, and when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) learned that he was in debt, he said to his companions: "Pray over your brother."

So he did not pray over him himself, but asked his companions to pray. Why did he not pray? Because of the earlier statement: "Whoever takes people's wealth intending to repay it, God will repay it on his behalf." Since he died without repaying, it follows that he had in his intention to procrastinate. Yet the Messenger (ﷺ) did not prevent his companions from praying over him.

And the Messenger (ﷺ) deals with the one in hardship with the generosity of faith, saying:

"Whoever gives respite to one in hardship, or remits it for him, God will shade him in His shade on a day when there is no shade but His shade" (2).

The meaning of "anzara" (grants respite) is that he gives him time and postpones collecting the debt from him, so he does not pursue him, does not imprison him over his debt, does not hound him; and if he rises high in certain faith, he says to him: "Go, God will compensate me and you," and the matter ends. Therefore the Truth says: "but that you remit it as charity is better for you, if you only knew," and the fruit is the goodly recompense from God. So either you grant respite and postpone, or you give away part of the debt or all of it, and you are free to do what you wish. Look at the precision of the Truth in settling this economic question, which was the preoccupation of the pre-Islamic environment.

We have already learned from what preceded that Islam built the economic process on support and giving, and the Exalted spoke of it in the verses of spending that came earlier, from His words: "The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is like a grain..." And He spoke at length about spending. Spending includes what is obligatory upon you of zakat, and what you volunteer yourself. The one who gives something beyond what God has obligated, He, glory be to Him, considers it a right of the poor, but an unspecified right. Therefore, when we came to His words, glory be to Him:

﴿Indeed the God-fearing are in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them; indeed they were before that doers of good, sleeping little of the night;﴾ (Surat al-Dhariyat)

Does Islam require of us that we sleep only a little of the night? No; the Muslim may pray the 'isha' and sleep, then rise for the dawn prayer, this is what Islam requires. But the Truth, glory be to Him, here speaks of the doers of good (muhsinin) who have entered the station of ihsan with God.

﴿Indeed the God-fearing are in gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them; indeed they were before that doers of good, sleeping little of the night, and at the dawn hours they seek forgiveness;﴾ (Surat al-Dhariyat)

Does legislation oblige the believer to rise at the pre-dawn to seek forgiveness? No; the Muslim must perform the obligations, but if the Muslim desires to enter the station of ihsan, he must know the way:

﴿and at the dawn hours they seek forgiveness﴾ (Surat al-Dhariyat)

The discourse here is about the station of ihsan. And the Truth adds about the people of this station:

﴿and in their wealth is a right for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (Surat al-Dhariyat)
