God, glory be to Him, has specified in the wealth of those who enter the station of ihsan a right for the beggar and the deprived, but God did not specify the value of this right or its form, whether it is known or unknown. But when God spoke of the believers He said, glory be to Him:

﴿And those in whose wealth is a known right, for the beggar and the deprived﴾ (Surat al-Ma'arij)

Thus we find in the wealth of the owner of the station of ihsan a right for the beggar and the deprived, but in the wealth of the owner of faith there is a known right, which is zakat. The station of ihsan exceeds the station of faith, because the right in the believer's wealth is known, whereas in the station of ihsan there is in their wealth a right for kindness to the poor even if it is not known, i.e., not specified.

We have seen that some jurists considered zakat, since it is a right of the poor over the rich, that if the rich withholds what amounts to the nisab of theft, his hand is cut off, because he has taken the right of the poor. The nisab of theft is a quarter dinar of gold. Thus Islam builds its social matters either upon unobligatory spending or obligatory spending. When people's souls are stingy, and they cannot donate the amount beyond what is obligatory, and love of their wealth becomes firmly established in their souls such that they do not give it up, God, glory be to Him, says to each of them:

You have not given up your wealth, and I have forbidden usury. How then shall we meet to lay a sound foundation for society? I will keep your wealth for you and withhold from you the interest of usury, and thus we meet halfway: I take none of your wealth, and I take nothing from others beyond this wealth.

The Truth, glory be to Him, explained the verse of debt, and this verse took the longest space among the verses of the Qur'an. Why? Because upon debt the economic affairs of society are built for one who has no financial resource by which to direct the movement of his life. When the Truth set down the verse of debt, He did not set it down in a dry, rigid, legislative manner, but set it down in an affective manner. That is, He blended legislation with feeling, He mixed the rigidity of law with the spirit of Islam, so He did not make it a dry process.

When human legislators legislate, they lay down the law dryly, for example: whoever kills is killed, and so on. But the Truth says otherwise even in the most severe disputes, which are disputes over blood, so He said, glory be to Him:

﴿Then whoever is pardoned something by his brother, let there be follow-up in kindness and payment to him with good conduct; that is a lightening from your Lord and a mercy﴾ (part of verse 178, Surat al-Baqara)

1 Narrated by al-Bukhari and Ahmad from Abu Hurayra.
2 Narrated by Ahmad and Muslim from Abu al-Yusr.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 2, verse 281:

Before the Exalted reveals the verse of debt (ayat al-dayn), He says:

﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah. Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ [2:281]

We have already clarified that taqwa of Allah requires that you perform the actions that shield you from the attributes of majesty (sifat al-jalal) in Allah. We have also clarified that when Allah said: (Fear the Fire) (ittaqu al-nar), it meant that we should do what places between us and the Fire a shield, so the Fire is among the things connected to the attributes of majesty. And here the Exalted says: (Fear a Day), so do we fear the Day itself, or do we fear what arises within the Day? Indeed, the Day is a container of time, and times are not feared in themselves, but a person fears what happens within time.

However, if something within time is frightening, then the fear is directed at the entire Day, because it is a Day of terror; everything in it is alarming and frightening. May Allah protect us and you from its terror. And observe the extreme precision of the Qur'an in His words: (you will be returned to Allah in it).

Return on this Day does not happen by the choice of the servants, but by the will of Allah. When the Exalted speaks of the believers who do righteous deeds, He says of their return to Allah on the Day of Resurrection:

﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is hard except for the humble [khashi'in], who are certain that they will meet their Lord and that they will return to Him.﴾ [2:45-46]

The meaning of that is that the believing servant longs to return to Allah, because he desires to attain success.

As for those who do not believe, the Truth says about them:

﴿The Day they will be pushed toward the Fire of Hell with a violent push.﴾ [52:13]

The return of those who do not believe is a compelled return, not a desired one. And the Truth says of this Day: (Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 282:

After that, Allah, glorified is He, legislates for the debt, saying, glorified is He:

﴿O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write it down between you with justice. And let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write, and let the one who has the obligation dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not diminish anything from it. But if the one who has the obligation is of limited understanding or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice. And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of the two errs, the other can remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are summoned. And do not be weary of writing it, whether it is small or large, for its term. That is more just in the sight of Allah and more suitable as evidence and closer to avoiding doubt, except when it is an immediate commerce that you conduct among yourselves; then there is no blame upon you that you not write it. And take witnesses when you conclude a sale. And let no harm befall a scribe or a witness. And if you do, indeed it is disobedience in you. And fear Allah; Allah teaches you, and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ [2:282]

It is the longest verse in the Qur'an, and Allah opens it with His saying: (O you who believe). This opening, as we know, suggests that the ruling that follows it has faith as its basis. As long as you have believed in Allah, you apply what He has obligated you with, because Allah does not obligate a disbeliever. Man, as we said earlier, is free to turn to faith in Allah or not to turn to it.

If a person turns to faith, then he should receive every ruling from Allah with commitment. We give this example, and to Allah belongs the highest example: when a person is sick, he is free to go to the doctor or not to go. But when a person goes to the doctor and the doctor prescribes medicine for him, the person does not ask the doctor, who is a creature like himself: why did you prescribe these medicines? The doctor may reply: you were free to come to me or not come, but since you have come to me, listen to the instruction and carry it out. The doctor does not explain the chemical reactions and equations, no. The doctor diagnoses the illness and prescribes the medicine. So what of us when we turn to the Supreme Creator with faith?

We carry out His commands, glorified is He, and Allah does not command the believer except out of wisdom, and afterward the traces of wisdom may become apparent to the believer, and the believer's confidence in his faith in Allah increases. The Truth says: (O you who believe, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down). When we reflect on the Truth's saying (tadayantum, you contract a debt), we find in it (dayn), and there is (din), and the meaning of din includes recompense, and the meaning of din includes the methodology of heaven, while ad-dayn is borrowing until a due date for repayment. Thus we find three clear meanings: ad-din: which is the Day of Recompense; and din: which is the heavenly methodology; and ad-dayn: which is the money borrowed.

Allah, by His saying (tadayantum bi-dayn), wants to remove confusion between two meanings, leaving one meaning, which is borrowing, so He said (bi-dayn). The interaction here is in the matter of debt, not in recompense or in methodology. And the Truth specifies the debt with a specified term. Allah intended by the word (musamma, specified) further specification, for there is a difference between a term tied to a time and a term tied to an event that will occur. If you say: my term is the arrival of the pilgrims. This is an event within a time, and no one can guarantee the arrival of the pilgrims, for the airplane may be delayed, or some of the pilgrims may fall ill, so the rest are held in quarantine.

But if you say: my term is two months or three months, this means the term is the time itself. Therefore it is not valid for anyone to postpone his debt to something that happens in time, because it is possible that that thing does not happen in that time. Contracting a debt for a specified term requires specifying the time, and the Truth clarifies for us: (When you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down). And the word (fa-uktubuhu, then write it down) is the lifting of hardship between loved ones. It is a heavenly legislation, so do not let one of you take the ease of friendship, saying to his companion: we are friends. It is a heavenly legislation that tells you: write the debt, and do not say: we are friends. For one of you may die, and if you do not write the debt, what hardship will the children, the widows, or the heirs face?

Thus the Truth's obligation to write the debt is the implementation of a command from Allah that achieves the lifting of hardship among loved ones. Many people think that Allah intends by the writing the protection of the creditor. No. What is intended by that, and what is important, is the protection of the debtor, because if the debtor knows that the debt is documented against him, he is keen to work to pay his debt; but if the debt is not documented, it is possible that he becomes lazy about working and about settling the debt. In that case he and his family obtain their need once, then the wealthy society withholds from the poor society and does not lend to him, and they take the debtor's inability to pay as a pretext for that. This person who has not paid his debt falls into the circle of bearing a doubled burden, because he has narrowed the door of the good loan.

Allah wants to keep the wheel of economic life turning for those who do not possess, because the one who possesses can run his own life, while the one who does not possess is the one in need. For this reason there is a proverb in the Egyptian countryside that says: whoever takes and gives, the money becomes his money. He borrows and repays, so everyone trusts him, and they see him as honest, they see him as diligent, they see him as sincere, and they know of him that when he takes, he fulfills, and then all the money becomes his money.

Thus, Allah, glorified is He, by writing the debt, wants to protect the movement of life for the one who does not have means, because the one who has means does not need the loan. Therefore the command came from the Truth, glorified is He: (When you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down). And who writes the debt?

Notice the precision: neither you, O creditor, write it, nor you, O debtor, but there must come a scribe other than the two, for this third party has no interest in the debt transaction (and let a scribe write it down between you with justice). In this there is clarification that a person who knows writing, if he is asked to write a debt, should not refuse to do so. Why? Because the verse of debt was revealed when writing was scarce among the Arabs; there were only a few who knew writing, so there was intense demand for whoever knew writing.

But if none of those who know writing is asked to write the debt, what should he do? The Truth commands him to volunteer, and in this comes the clear command (so let him write). Because when a matter requires a person to act, and the circumstance does not allow experimentation, the Sharia obliges him to appoint himself to the work.

Suppose you are in a boat, and then a storm comes and sweeps away the one who holds the rudder of the boat, or he is unable to manage the rudder. Here, whoever knows must step forward to steer the rudder; he appoints himself to the work, and there is no room for experimentation. When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, presented the matter of famine in the story of our master Yusuf, He said:

﴿You will sow for seven years in succession; so what you harvest, leave in its ear, except a little of what you eat. Then there will come after that seven hard years which will consume what you have prepared for them, except a little of what you store.﴾ [Yusuf 12:47–48].

And Yusuf said:

﴿Appoint me over the treasuries of the land; indeed, I am a knowing guardian.﴾ [Yusuf 12:55].

The matter is famine, so it does not bear experimentation, and he is competent for this task, possessing the gift of preservation and knowledge, so he appointed himself to the work. Likewise here (and let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him): if he is asked, and even if he is not asked and it becomes incumbent upon him, then (so let him write).

This is the reason for both matters. And since writing is for documenting the debt, who is the weak party? It is the debtor, and the writing is evidence against him for the creditor. Therefore Allah specifies who dictates: the one who has the obligation, that is, he dictates the wording that will be evidence against him (and let the one who has the obligation dictate). And why does the creditor not dictate? Because the debtor is usually in a position of weakness; perhaps when the moment of writing the due date arrives, the creditor might shorten this date, and the debtor might be too embarrassed to speak and remain silent, because he is in a position of weakness. Allah chooses the one who is in a position of weakness to dictate the wording of the debt, so he dictates at his ease, and it is guaranteed that he is not seized by the sword of need at any point.

But what do we do when the one who owes the debt is of limited understanding, or weak, or unable to dictate himself? The Truth lays down the rules (and if the one who has the obligation is of limited understanding or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate with justice). The safih (of limited understanding) is one who has reached the stage of men but does not possess the capacity to dispose of his affairs. The da'if (weak) is one who does not have the capacity that makes him mature in intellectual maturity for dealing, such as a small child, or an elder who has reached such old age that he knows nothing after his knowledge, or one who cannot dictate, that is, a mute, so his guardian, trustee, or executor dictates for him.

Then comes the additional documentation, in the saying of the Exalted: (And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses, so that if one of the two errs, the other can remind her). Let us look at the precision in documentation when the Truth says: (And bring to witness); we bring witnesses and write, because by this documentation He, glorified is He, wants to secure economic life for the one who does not possess; for when need is secured for the one who does not possess, the wheel turns and the movement of economic life proceeds, because the one who possesses is few, and the one who does not possess is many. Every serious and beneficial idea needs a hundred people to implement the plan.

The single pocket that spends needs a hundred to carry out, and for this reason the multitude are those who do not possess, so that the system of life may run; because Allah does not want the system of life to be a favor from creatures to creatures, rather Allah wants the system of life to be a necessary system. The worker who does not support a family may not go out to work, so the Truth ties the worker's going out to his need. He needs food and the care of himself and his family, so he goes out to work out of necessity, and through repetition of the matter he comes to love his work, and when he loves the work he loves the work for its own sake.

Thus he moves from need to work, to loving work for its own sake, and when he loves work for its own sake, the wheel of life turns. The Truth, glorified is He, in defining the witnesses by this saying: (And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men).

Why did the Truth say (shahidayn, two witnesses) and not (shahidan)? Because the mere witness may be false, so the Truth came with the intensive form. As if he is a witness whom people know for the justice of his testimony, until he becomes a shahid (a true witness). He is a person whose just testimony has been repeated, and people have entrusted him with it, and this is evidence that he is a shahid. And if there are not two men as witnesses, the Truth specifies for us (then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses).

The Truth, glorified and exalted, has required of us, according to our capacity, that is, those with whom we are content. The Truth gave the reason for the two women being in place of one man as follows: (so that if one of the two errs, the other can remind her); because testimony is contact with a society, so that you witness in it and know what is happening, and the woman is mostly far from all that.

The principle regarding women is that they have no connection with such matters, and no business in these transactions; so if circumstances force the testimony of a woman, let it be a man and two women, because the default in the thinking of a woman is that she is not preoccupied with the economic society surrounding her, so one of them may err or forget, and the other reminds her, and both of them review this situation, because it is not the duty of a woman to mingle with the multitude of people, especially regarding business matters.

Then the Truth says: (And let not the witnesses refuse when they are summoned). Just as the Truth said about the scribe that he should not refuse to document the debt, so too is the testimony regarding this debt. How is the testimony: is it in the performance or the bearing? There are two stages: a stage of bearing, and a stage of performance.

When we ask someone, saying: come and bear witness to this debt, he has no right to refuse, and this is the bearing. And after we have documented the debt, we will summon this witness before the judge, and—

Then, after that, the Almighty (al-Haqq, subhanahu wa ta'ala) teaches us the intense concern for documentation, so He says:

﴿And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken into possession. But if one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted discharge his trust and let him fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it—his heart is indeed sinful. And Allah is All-Knowing of what you do.﴾ [2:283]

Travel, as we know, is a departure from the monotony of life in one's homeland, and the monotony of life in one's homeland makes a person know thoroughly the foundations of his life. But travel takes a person out of the monotony of life, so he is not able to do many of the things he is able to do while residing. So suppose that you are traveling, and you are compelled to borrow, and there is no scribe and no witness; then what is the position?

Behold, the Truth makes it clear to you: "a pledge taken into possession." So Allah has not left the matter of debt even in travel; He has not legislated only for residence, but the Truth has also legislated for travel: "a pledge taken into possession." Likewise, writing and testimony are for residence, and the pledge taken into possession in travel—its purpose is to protect a person against the pressures of society.

But does the Almighty prohibit the aspiration to altruism? Does the Almighty prohibit the manliness of dealing? Does the Almighty prohibit noble qualities from permeating people? No. The Almighty says: "But if one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted discharge his trust." This is the aspiration of faith; Allah has not closed the matter of nobility and altruism in dealing. Writing the debt, calling witnesses, and taking a pledge are not an obligation, because Allah said: "But if one of you entrusts another, let him who is entrusted discharge his trust."

Also, one might understand that the one entrusted is the debtor. Here we say: No, the matter is different. Here there is a pledge, and that means there are two matters: the first is the debt, and the second is the pledge taken into possession, which is in exchange for the debt. So one is trusted with the pledge in his hand, and the other is trusted with the debt. Therefore the wise saying is intended for the one who holds the pledge and the one who holds the debt, and it means that the one with the pledge discharges his trust, and the other discharges his debt. When we rise to this level of dealing, a person's restraint is not in documentation external to the self, but in faith-based documentation within the self. But can we guarantee that faith-based documentation exists in every person?

Can we guarantee circumstances? We do not guarantee circumstances. Faith-based trustworthiness may exist at the time of receiving and taking, but we cannot guarantee that it will exist at the time of returning. A man may come to you and say: "I have a hundred pounds; take it as a trust with you."

The meaning of "trust" (amanah) is that there is no document and no witnesses, and conscience is the judge. If you wish, you may acknowledge these hundred pounds, and if you wish, you may deny them. The man who does this with you is in fact asking you to record the hundred pounds in a faith-based conscience. It is permissible that you say to him at the moment he does this: "Yes, I will keep the hundred pounds for you with utmost trust," and your intention is to return it to him when he asks for it. But you do not guarantee the circumstances of life for yourself, as a human subject to changes. Life may press on you so that you delay in returning the trust, or make you deny it, and you say to the one who entrusted you: "Get away from me; I do not own myself at the time of returning, though I owned myself at the time of receiving."

Trust is the general matter in the universe, though it is now specifically related to the noble verse we are discussing, and the Almighty presents it with its generality to the whole universe, so He says:

﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it. Indeed, he has been unjust and ignorant.﴾ [33:72]

The whole universe feared for itself from bearing the trust, and this means that the trust will be subject to change and choice, and no creature in the universe has guaranteed for itself the ability to fulfill it at the time of returning. The creatures declared their refusal to bear the trust, as if they said: "We, O our Lord, want to be subjugated and compelled, with no choice for us." Therefore we find the whole universe carrying out its task as Allah willed it, except for man, who accepted, with his intellect and thinking, to bear the trust of choice, and with the tongue of his state or the tongue of his speech said: "I am able to bear the trust, because I can choose among alternatives."

Here we remind man: you may be strong at the moment of bearing, but what about your condition at the time of returning? Therefore Allah said of man: "And man bore it; indeed, he has been unjust and ignorant." Man wronged himself when he bore the trust and did not fulfill it, so he is unjust. And he is ignorant because he estimated the time of bearing and did not estimate the time of returning, or he guaranteed it and then backed out and violated what he had pledged to himself to fulfill.

So, although a person may be confident that he will return the trust, he is still subject to changes. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said: "And do not be weary of writing it, whether small or large, to its term; that is more just in the sight of Allah." So writing is an opportunity for a person to protect himself from weakness at the time of returning. Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, wants to document the matter with a documentation that does not make you, O servant, subject only to your faith-based conscience, but you are subject also to documentation outside your faith, and that is by writing the debt, small or large, to its term.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: "And do not conceal testimony." This word, "and do not conceal," is an expressive act, because the word "testimony" (shahadah) means the thing you have witnessed; as long as you have witnessed something, it is established, and what is established never changes. Therefore the person who recounts a true account does not differ in his telling of it even if he narrates it a thousand times, because he draws on a reality.

But the liar draws on something other than reality, so he says a word, forgets that he lied before, and so tells another lie, because he does not draw on a reality. The word of testimony concerns a witnessed, established matter, and as long as the matter is witnessed and established, it presses on the soul of the one who sees it to come out. So beware of suppressing it by concealment, because the word "concealment" means that something is trying to come out while you try to hide it. Therefore the Truth says: "And do not conceal testimony." It is as if the natural, innate faith-nature presses on its owner to make him utter what he witnessed, because it is established.

Therefore the command comes from the Truth: "And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it—his heart is indeed sinful." A person may ask: is the concealing here an attribute of the heart or of the person who did not state the testimony? The poet says:

Indeed, speech is in the heart, and the tongue was only made a indicator of it.

Whenever Allah affirms something, He brings the limb related to the matter, so you say: "I saw it with my eye, heard it with my ear, gave it with my hand, and walked to it with my foot." You mention the limb that has a role in this matter.

When the Truth says: "for whoever conceals it—his heart is indeed sinful," all the limbs submit to the heart. "And Allah is All-Knowing of what you do": that is, your concealment of the truth will change nothing of the reality of Allah's knowledge. When the matter of debt and its documentation and circumstances ends, whether in the ordinary homeland or during travel, Allah guarantees to the person moving in life a noble and pure movement.

If these are not present, then interests stop and suffer paralysis. The one who cannot move—what does he do in life? His heart fills with malice toward the one who has wealth, and when his heart fills with malice toward the wealthy, he dislikes the blessing in him, and when the destitute dislikes the blessing in his wealthy brother, the blessing itself dislikes to go to one who dislikes the blessing in his brother. These are matters that the Truth, glory be to Him, has arranged, some connected to others.

Blessing loves the one blessed (with the mīm pronounced and the ʿayn with fatḥa) more than the blessed one loves the blessing, and it goes to the one whom Allah has blessed with it, with passion. So whoever dislikes the blessing in the blessed one, the blessing resists him, as if it says to him: "You will not obtain any good from me." Let every person try it.

Love the blessing in others, and you will find the blessings of all at your service; if you love the blessing in another, it comes to you to serve you. Also, the believer must know that some blessings are not the product of toil and effort; a blessing may be mere grace from Allah, who favors some of His creation over others, so when you dislike it in the one blessed, you have objected to Allah's decree regarding the blessing. And when you object to Allah's decree regarding the blessing, the Truth, glory be to Him, does not let you benefit from it at all.

If you see a relative withholding his blessing from his relatives, know that they dislike the blessing in him. Had they loved it, the blessing would have run to them. The divine method wants to make people a solidly interdependent and complementary body, so that when I see the blessing in you and I obtain from it, I love it in you, and when I love the blessing in you, giving comes to me from this blessing, and you find no difference between the wealthy and the destitute. You find no difference between wealthy and destitute except in a society that does not implement Allah's rule in anything.

We have said this regarding the situation of a person compelled to usury because he did not find anyone to lend him a good loan, and did not find anyone to pay him the obligation of zakat from Allah sufficient for his need, so he was compelled to take usury. Thereby the usurious society enters into war with Allah, and does anyone have the strength to enter into war with Allah? No. And the usurious society enters into war with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prohibited usury and said at the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Every usury is abolished, but you have your principal; you do not wrong and you are not wronged. Allah has decreed that there is no usury, and the usury of Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib is entirely abolished."

This is the characteristic of the sublimity of heavenly legislation: human legislation protects its author's relatives from legislation, but heavenly legislation imposes its applications first upon the relatives. The model in this was our master Umar ibn al-Khattab. When Umar wished to establish legislation, he would gather his family and relatives and say:

"I will do such and such. By Him in whose hand is my soul, whoever opposes me in any of this, I will make him an example for the Muslims." Umar declared it before the people. And why did Umar announce this? Because many people flatter those in authority, and those in authority may not be aware of it; we may find a man who enters upon a people on the basis that he is so-and-so son of so-and-so, and by intimidation this person settles his affairs among people in spite of them. And the ruler may know nothing of such conduct.

But when the ruler announces to the people and to his relatives that there is no distinction whatsoever in what is legislated, and that the law applies to himself and his family, then whoever exploits the name of a ruler or fabricates something, the responsibility falls on the one who did it and on the one for whom it was done, and thereby affairs are set right. But when the facts come out about the exploitation by the rulers' relatives after the end of the rulers' terms, then we say: why did we not know everything from the beginning? And where were the facts at the time?

The Muslim ruler must announce to the governed that the laws are applied to him first and to those he supports. Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at the Farewell Pilgrimage: "And the usury of the Jahiliyyah is abolished, and the first usury I abolish is our usury, the usury of Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, for it is entirely abolished."(1)

At the Battle of Badr, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought out his own household to fight, because if he had brought out none of his household, one of the disbelievers would have said: "He is protecting his household." And if the reward of martyrdom is Paradise, why would he send distant people forward and not send his beloved ones to fight?

But here is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) giving precedence to his relatives and beloved ones; he is the one who knows his Lord, regarding the matter of martyrdom and how it spares a person the hardships of life and admits him to Paradise. Thus favoritism in early Islam was favoritism for what remains, not like the favoritism of fools for what perishes.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) teaches us this and strikes the hands of the usurers, this is the war—

1 Narrated by Muslim in the sermon of the Farewell Pilgrimage.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 2, verse 284:

He, glorified is He, says after that:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it. Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾

The verse opens by placing (lillah, "to Allah") before what is in the heavens and the earth. The Truth, glorified is He, says: (To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth). That is the container in which created things exist. No one claims that the heavens and the earth belong to him. But among what is in the heavens or on the earth there are things that created beings do claim as their own. When we look at the bounties of the earth, we find that at times they are owned by people, by what Allah has given them as ownership. And humans who have ascended to the sky and moved about in its atmosphere, with what they have moved about of artificial satellites and spacecraft, may declare their ownership of these satellites and those craft.

The Truth draws our attention here with His words (To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth), and it clarifies for us that, if it appears that Allah has given the ownership of causation to His creatures, He has given this ownership only as a loan, which is taken back from them. Either they depart from it and die, or it departs from them and is taken from them by sale, gift, usurpation, or plunder.

The word (lillah) indicates exclusivity and indicates restriction. Everything in existence is ultimately in Allah's hand, and no one claims, by the causal means Allah has granted him, that he owns anything. Why? Because the human owner does not even possess himself so as to endure.

We have not seen anyone whom the changes of circumstance have not touched. And as long as changes touch every human being, we must know that Allah wants His creatures to show compassion to one another, to complete one another, and Allah wants His creatures to cooperate. The Truth does not do this because the matter has slipped out of His hand, God forbid. No! Allah informs us: "To Me belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and I am able to make the matter a rotation among people."

Therefore we say to those who reach a high rank in wealth, or status, or any field: beware when blessing is complete for you. Why? Because if blessing completes for you in height, wealth, health, and children, you are among the things subject to change, and as long as it has been completed and reached its end while you are without doubt subject to change, the blessing will turn toward less. So when a person ascends to the peak while he is changeable, he must descend from that peak. Hence the poet says:

When a thing is completed, its deficiency appears;
Expect its decline once it is said to be complete.

History carries to us the story of the Arab woman who entered upon the caliph and said to him: "May Allah complete His blessing upon you." Those sitting around the caliph heard her and rejoiced and declared their happiness. But the caliph said to them: "By Allah, you did not understand what she says. She is saying: May Allah complete His blessing upon you, for if it is completed, it will cease, because changes pursue creation." Thus the caliph understood the woman's intention.

And the poet says:

My soul, which possesses things, is itself departing;
How then should I grieve over a thing that has gone from it?

The possessing soul is itself departing; so how does one grieve over a thing that has been lost from him?

The Truth, glorified is He, asks us always to be mindful of one clear matter: that the whole universe belongs to Allah, and that all of humankind, with their selves and their souls, and what appears of them and what is hidden, are not concealed from Allah. The Truth, glorified is He, does not call us to account merely according to what He knows, but calls us to account for what has been recorded against us.

Every person reads his own book. He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And every person We have fastened his bird of fortune to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find spread open. "Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this day as an accountant."﴾ (Surat al-Isra')

Reckoning means that a person has a credit, and against him there is also a debit. The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, explains to us (his and against him) by the balance as we know balances among us, and He, glorified is He, says:

﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth. So those whose scales are heavy – they are the successful. And those whose scales are light – they are the ones who have lost themselves for what they used to deny of Our verses.﴾ (Surat al-A'raf)

The reckoning of the Truth is precise and just. Those whose good deeds weigh heavy in the pan are those who attain the Garden of Paradise, and those who sold themselves to Satan and the desire of the soul have their evil deeds weigh heavy, so they become people of the Fire.

So we are before two kinds of people: those whose side of good weighs heavy in the reckoning, and those whose side of evil and wickedness weighs heavy in the reckoning. But what about those whose two pans are equal in their deeds, whose good deeds are balanced by their evil? They are the people of the A'raf, who receive forgiveness from Allah, because the forgiveness of Allah, who is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, has preceded His wrath, exalted is He. And if the matter of the people of the A'raf had not come in the Qur'an, someone would say: Allah has told us the account of those whose scales are heavy, and the accounts of those whose scales of good are light, but He has not told us the account of those whose evils are equal to their good deeds.

But the Forbearing, the All-Aware has clarified for us the account of every matter, and clarified for us that forgiveness precedes wrath with Him. Therefore, in reckoning, the Truth does not suffice with knowledge alone, but with clear and precise recording. So the Truth, glorified is He, reassures us, saying:

﴿Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Surat al-Furqan 70)

The Truth reassures us that what we do of good we find in the pan of the scale, and reassures us also that He, glorified is He, will recompense us for what evil of the wicked has befallen us, and that we will take from their good deeds to be added to our scale. So reassurance came from two sides: the Truth reassured us about the good we have done, so it is not forgotten that it enters into our reckoning; and He reassured us also about the evil of the wicked that has befallen us, and the Truth will take from their good deeds to add them to us.

In the world we find many people whom Allah loves for a quality of goodness in them, and this good quality may be hidden so that no one sees it, but Allah, from whom nothing hidden is concealed, sees this quality in the person, and loves him for its sake. And the Truth sees that this man's good deeds are few, so He causes some of creation to strike this man with their evils and wrongs, so that he takes from their good deeds to increase the good deeds of this man.

The meaning of (whether you show what is in yourselves) is that you turn the inner feelings into practical inclinations. But does the meaning of (or conceal it) mean that you do not turn inner feelings into practical inclinations? No. Not everything has a practical inclination. An example of that is love: a person may love and not find the capacity for an inclination by which he declares that he is consumed by his love; and likewise the one who harbors resentment may not find the capacity for an inclination by which he declares his resentment. So there are actions that settle in the hearts. Does Allah hold a person accountable for what has settled in the souls?

This matter requires extreme precision, because we find that some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood before this verse in a way that made some of them weep. This is Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who, when he heard this verse, said: "If Allah takes us to account for what we have concealed in our souls, we will surely be destroyed." And he wept until his sobbing was heard. This matter reached Ibn Abbas, and he said: "May Allah have mercy on Abu Abd al-Rahman; his fellow Muslims found what he found from this verse." Then Allah revealed after it: (Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity) to the end of the surah.

Let us know that the impulses of the soul are many. There is something called (hajis) (a passing thought), and another thing called (khatir) (an idea that crosses the mind), and what is called (hadith al-nafs) (inner discourse), and there is (hamm) (resolve in the sense of contemplation), and there is ('azm) (determination). These are five states, and the first four of these states contain nothing blameworthy in themselves; rather, the last one, in which the intention becomes clear, must be given attention, and each state must be treated in detail.

The (hajis) is the thought that strikes all at once; the (khatir) is that which passes through, that is, moves through the soul for a little while; (hadith al-nafs) is that the soul keeps turning it over; (hamm) is gathering the means and asking the soul about all the means by which a person carries out his desires; and ('azm) (intention) is reaching the end and beginning to execute the matter.

The intention (qasd) is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: (And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it). Many scholars have stopped at this statement, and some scholars have asked: is the verse that comes after it, in which He says (Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity), an abrogation of the verse preceding it?

But we know that the verse is a report, and reports are not abrogated; rather, rulings are what are abrogated. On that basis, the intention and the determination to carry out the matter is what is meant by the Truth's saying: (And whether you show what is in yourselves or conceal it, Allah will call you to account for it). This is what Allah will call us to account for.

When the Truth, glorified is He, says: (Then He forgives whom He wills), who are they? Allah has made clear whom He wills to forgive: they are those who repent, those who turn back to Allah. They are those of whom the Truth said:

﴿Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (Surat al-Furqan)

The replacement of an evil deed by a good deed is a matter at which the accountable person must pause to see the bounty of Allah, because whoever commits an evil and is pained by it, and grieves over it, then as the evil he committed pained him, Allah writes for him a good deed. But one who has not committed an evil is not alarmed by this. Some of the knowers say: "An act of disobedience that leaves one with humility and brokenness is better than an act of obedience that leaves one with pride and arrogance."

You will find that the general goodness in existence may be from among those who were excessive against themselves in some matter they committed and then repented of, but it still troubles them.

One of them may be strong in everything, except that he is weak before one matter, and his weakness before this one matter led him to disobey Allah through it, while he strives earnestly in the areas where he is not weak to greatly increase his good deeds, so that Allah erases and removes this by that. So the general goodness in existence may be from among those with evil deeds who were excessive against themselves in one area, and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wills to make them turn toward areas of goodness, saying: perhaps this will carry that.

But the one who remains so placid that no disobedience stings him, and matters remain lukewarm in his soul. Therefore we must look at those who were excessive against themselves not from one angle, but from many angles, and we must show them courtesy and call upon Allah to pardon them for what we know of them, and to bless them in what they have offered, so that Allah may remove from them the burdens of what they did.

Some scholars see in the Truth's saying: (Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills) that Allah has made forgiveness a matter connected to the worshipper of Allah: if you wish that Allah forgive you, then increase good deeds so that Allah replaces your evil deeds with good deeds. And if you wish to be punished, and this is a thing no one wishes, then do not do good deeds.

This matter makes us know that the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, when He asks us to believe in Him, He gives us control of the reins. And by merely our believing in Him, we receive from Him the reins of choice. The proof is clear in the sacred hadith: From Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Allah, mighty and majestic, says:

("I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me within himself, I remember him within Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than theirs; and if he draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; and if he draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; and if he comes to Me walking, I come to him running.")(1)

So by merely your believing, Allah has given you control of the reins. If you wish Allah to draw near to you a cubit, then you draw near to Him a span; the reins are in your hand. And if you wish that your Lord draw near to you a fathom, then you draw near a cubit. And if you wish that your Lord come to you running in haste, then you go to Him walking. The moment Allah sees you coming and turning toward Him, it is as if He says to you: No… rest yourself; I am the one who comes to you.

Therefore we said earlier, regarding prayer, that when you believe, O servant, in Allah, and after that He calls out to you...

1 Narrated by Muslim from Abu Hurairah in the Book of Remembrance (Kitab al-Dhikr).

Then, after that, God Almighty says:

﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each one believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return."﴾ [2:285]

When we reflect on this noble verse, we find that the first belief in God was from the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord." After that comes the belief of those to whom the Messenger conveyed the call ("and the believers"). After that, the belief of the Messenger merges with the belief of the believers ("Each one believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers, and they say, 'We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return.'").

That is, both the Messenger and the believers believed in God. The first belief is the belief of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and the belief of the believers is also in the message that the Messenger brought, based on the distribution of the subject of (āmana, "believed") between the Messenger and the believers. Then God unites the Messenger and the believers in one belief, and this is natural, because the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, believed in God first, and afterwards the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, conveyed to us, and we believed in God and in him, and then the belief merged, so our belief became the belief of the Messenger and the belief of the Messenger became our belief. This is what the true word clarifies: "Each one believes in God."

Thus, the Messenger in his first stage preceded others in believing in God, and the Messenger is required, even when he believes in God, to believe that he is the Messenger of God. Did the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, not say: "I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him"? And when something in his own conduct pleased him, the Messenger would say: "I bear witness that I am the Messenger of God..." He would say it joyfully.

An example of this is what is narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "In Medina there was a Jew who used to lend me money on my dates until harvest time. Jabir had land on the road to Ruma, and it stopped bearing for a year (1). The Jew came to me at harvest time (3), and I had nothing from it, so I began asking him to give me respite until the next year (i.e., asking him to grant me time until a second year), but he refused. I informed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of this, and he said to his companions: 'Come, let us ask the Jew to grant Jabir respite.' They came to my palm grove, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, spoke to the Jew, and the Jew said, 'Abu al-Qasim, I will not grant him respite.' When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw this, he stood up and walked through the palm grove, then came back and spoke to him again, but he refused. I brought a little fresh dates and placed them before the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he ate, then said: 'Where is your shelter, Jabir?' I told him, and he said: 'Spread it out for me there.' I spread it out, and he entered and slept, then woke up. I brought him another handful, and he ate from it. Then he stood up, spoke to the Jew, but he refused. So he walked among the fresh dates in the second grove and then said: 'Jabir, harvest and pay what is owed.' He stood among the harvest, and I harvested from it what I owed, and there was a surplus. I went out and came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and gave him the good news. He said: 'I bear witness that I am the Messenger of God.'" (4)

And God, glorified and exalted, bears witness that there is no god but He:

﴿God bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those of knowledge, upholding justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [3:18] (Surah Al Imran).

So God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the Messenger of God bears witness that there is no god but God, and he also bears witness that he is the Messenger of God, conveying that to the believers, and the faith structure is completed. Therefore the True One says of that: "Each one believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers." The True One says "each" with tanwin, meaning each of the Messenger and the believers.

He, glorified be He, lists the elements of faith: "Each one believes in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers, and they say, 'We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return.'" We know that belief in God and everything related to belief must be unseen (ghayb); there is no belief in something perceived at all. Perceptible things do not admit belief, because they are witnessed. The elements of faith in this verse are:

Belief in God, which is unseen. Belief in the angels, who are unseen creations of God; had God not informed us that He has creatures called angels, we would not have known of them. The Truth informed us that He created the angels, who do not disobey God in what He commands them and do what they are commanded, and they are unseen. Were it not for that, we would not know of the matter of the angels. Belief in the books and the messengers.

Someone may say: Are the messengers unseen? Are the heavenly books unseen? The messengers are human beings, and the books are witnessed. To such a speaker we say: No, none of us has seen the Book descend upon the Messenger, which means that the process of revelation of the Book to the Messenger is unseen, known to God and believed in by the believers.

How do we believe in all the messengers without distinguishing between any of them? We say: the messengers who convey from God only convey a method from God, which contains beliefs that differ according to the ages, and contains rulings that differ according to the ages and the circumstances of the matters in them.

Thus the doctrinal foundation in all the messages is one matter, but what is required in the movement of life differs, because the affairs of life differ, and when the affairs of life differ, the True One, glorified be He, sends down the suitable legislation. But the foundation is one, and the communication is from the Creator, there is no god but He. Therefore the wise word comes: "We make no distinction between any of His messengers," so we do not distinguish between the messengers in that they convey from God what their methods of conveyance agree on in terms of belief, and what they differ on in terms of rulings suited to the affairs of each age.

Then the True One says: "And they say, 'We hear and we obey.'" So hearing is the reaching of the call, and obedience is responsiveness to what is required, that the believer carries out every command and refrains from every prohibition in every matter related to the movement of the universe. Those who want to isolate religion from the movement of life say: religion concerns acts of worship such as prayer, fasting, zakat, and hajj. Then they try to separate the movement of life from religion.

To these we say: You speak of a religion that has reached you that did not come to organize the movement of life, but came to give the spiritual dose that was missing among the Jews, namely the spiritual dose. But the Islamic religion came as the seal of religions, organizing the movement of life, so every matter in life and every movement in it falls within the bounds of obedience. When we read the noble Qur'an, we find the wise word:

﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of God and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ [62:9] (Surah Al Jumu'ah).

So the True One, glorified be He, commands the believers and takes them out of one movement of life into another. He did not take them from emptiness; rather He called them to declare collective allegiance, which is a declaration by every believer of servitude to God before the rest of creation. After the believers finish the prayer, what does the True One say to them? He says to them:

﴿And when the prayer is ended, disperse in the land and seek of God's bounty, and remember God much that you may prosper.﴾ [62:10] (Surah Al Jumu'ah).

So dispersing in the land is a movement in life, just as the call was to hasten to the remembrance of God. Thus every movement in life falls within the framework of obedience. So "We hear and we obey" means: we hear the whole method, but when we hear the method and obey, do we have the ability to obey the whole method, or do we have lapses?

Since no one will complete all obedience and we have lapses, the True One says:

"Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final return." So the goal and the end all return to You, and You are the True God; therefore we, the servants, ask You for forgiveness until we meet You, and we are confident that Your mercy has preceded Your wrath.

1 "Fa-jalasat": the land was delayed in bearing fruit; in another narration: "fa-kharasat," meaning it departed from its usual custom regarding dates.
2 "Fa-khalā": the lender was delayed a year.
3 "Al-judhādh": (with kasra or fatha on the jim, with the dhal marked, and it may be left unmarked) the time of cutting the dates from the palm trees.
4 Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Foods, and Muslim in the Book of Faith.

I need to translate this passage, but I should flag one issue first: the Arabic text ends with a footnote number and a hadith citation ("رواه الطبراني في معجمه الكبير عن ثوبان") that appears to be attached to the earlier hadith. Also the passage is cut off mid-word ("إ"). I'll translate exactly what is given, including the footnote and the truncated ending.

---

Allah the Exalted says:

﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It shall have what it has earned, and it shall bear what it has acquired. "Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear. Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."﴾ [2:286]

(Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity) He, glorified is He, has not imposed upon you anything except what is within your capacity. Why? Because events, with respect to the resolve of the human soul, fall into three categories. The first category: that which we have no ability to do, and this is far from being an obligation. The second category: that which we are able to do, but with hardship, meaning it exhausts our capacity a little. The third category: obligation within capacity. Thus (Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity) means that the Truth does not burden the soul except with an obligation in which its capacity is wider than the obligation. Allah has obligated every Muslim with prayer, five obligatory prayers each day, and their times are filled with prayer, and it would have been possible for them to be ten; the evidence is that there are people who perform voluntary prayers. And He, glorified is He, obligated every Muslim with fasting for a month; is there not someone who fasts three months? The same applies to zakat; there are those who would give out all their wealth to Allah, and do not limit themselves to what is obligatory upon them of zakat.

So this is within capacity, and it is possible to increase. Therefore things are of three kinds: a thing that does not enter into capacity, so there is no obligation with it; a thing that enters into capacity with some hardship; and a thing within capacity. When the Truth obligates, He obligates what is within capacity. And since He obligated what is within capacity, if you voluntarily do an additional matter, that is a different subject: (Whoever volunteers good, it is better for him) as long as you volunteer from the same kind as what was obligated.

Thus obligation is within capacity; otherwise, had it not been within capacity, you would not have voluntarily added more. He, glorified is He, says: (Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity), and then comes after that to teach us, saying: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear), and He is the One who said: (Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity). So He, glorified is He, obligates us with what we are able to do and can bear.

It has been narrated that when Allah heard His Messenger and the believers saying: (Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that You laid upon those before us), He said: "I have done so."

And when they said: (Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no ability to bear), He said: "I have done so." He, glorified is He, did not obligate us except with what is within capacity, which is the common measure among all believers. There are people whose resolve is wider than that of others, and whoever has a wide resolve enters into the acts of worship that he increases in the category of voluntary acts, while whoever does not have a wide resolve performs only the obligatory duties required of him. When something arises for a person that makes the ruling beyond his capacity, Allah lightens the obligation; the traveler, the Shari'ah says to him: you are leaving your ordinary life and going to places where you have no settled residence, therefore the Truth lightens the obligation upon you; so you may break your fast during Ramadan, and you may shorten the prayer.

The Truth, glorified is He, knows that capacity may become constricted, so He, majestic is His glory, lightens the ruling of obligation and grants concessions when capacity is constrained. An example of this is the saying of the Truth:

﴿Now Allah has lightened [the burden] for you, and He knows that among you is weakness. So if there are among you one hundred steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ [8:66].

The ratio in fighting before this verse was one to ten, and the Truth lightened it, making it one to two because of weakness. Thus we see that He, glorified is He, will lighten the obligation if it exceeds capacity. Many people err in interpretation; they say about some obligations that they are beyond their capacity. To these we say: No. Do not determine the capacity yourself and then measure the obligation by it; rather, look: did the Truth obligate you or did He not? If the Truth has obligated you, then judge that He obligated you with what is within capacity, and all the obligations of the Most Merciful are within capacity: (Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. It shall have what it has earned, and it shall bear what it has acquired).

(Lahā) indicates ownership and specificity, and it is what benefits the soul and earns it reward; (ʿalayhā) indicates burden. We note that every (lahā) came with (kasabat), and every (ʿalayhā) came with (iktasabat), except in one verse in which the Truth says:

﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and is encompassed by his sin—those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever﴾ [2:81].

Here is a pause regarding style: (kasaba) means there is a difference in the actual, active treatment between it and the word (iktasabat), because (iktasaba) contains the form (iftaʿala), meaning it involves effort, and one performs an act from which one takes treatment; whereas (kasaba) is a natural matter. So (kasaba) is other than (iktasaba), and all acts of goodness come as kasb, not iktisab.

An example of this: when a man looks at his wife and sees her beauty, does he contrive something, or is that a natural matter? It is natural. But when a man looks at non-mahram women, he watches whether anyone sees the glance? Has anyone seen him among the people? Will he receive mockery and ridicule for that act or not? Why? Because he has committed a contrived act.

Another example: a person eats from his own wealth or from his father's wealth; he eats as a natural matter. But whoever enters an orchard and wants to steal from it exerts himself in that act, and wants to conceal himself. So the person of evil contrives, while the person of good, his acts are easy with no contrivance in them... Evil is what needs contrivance.

The greatest calamity is that evil does not need contrivance, because its owner has come to dullness of the faith-sense, and evils become easy for him, because he has become accustomed to them greatly. The Truth says: (Yes, whoever earns an evil deed and is encompassed by his sin). Indeed, sin encompasses him from every side, and there is no outlet left, and he does not contrive until it becomes a faculty in him for evil. So the thief, for example, at the beginning of his work fears and watches, but when stealing becomes his profession, he carries the tools of theft and his sense becomes numb.

In the first stage of evil, the people of evil are ashamed of doing evil, and that is evidence that their consciences and hearts still have some good in them; but when they regard evil as a trade and a faculty, here is the calamity, and sin surrounds each of them and encircles him and leaves him no path to Allah to repent.

So the one who plays games of chance, or whom the sin of indecency has encircled, may say joyfully: "Last night's gathering was wonderful," whereas the one who commits the error for the first time says: "It was a black night, I wish it had not happened," and keeps reproaching himself and blaming his soul, because he has become exhausted and worn himself out, because he committed the error.

Thus the saying of the Truth: (It shall have what it has earned and it shall bear what it has acquired) makes clear to us that doing evil is what requires effort. If the matter moves from iktasabat to kasabat, this is the great catastrophe, and his sin has encompassed him. Each soul bears what it has acquired. The wise person is one who increases what is for his soul and not what is upon it, because the one who says that is the Truth, the Knowing, the Owner, to whom is the final return, and there is no escape from this matter. Then the Truth says, on the tongue of His believing servants: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err). And one may say: The Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, reassured us, saying: "My nation has been relieved of error, forgetfulness, and what they were compelled to do"(1). How then does the Qur'an bring something lifted from the Islamic nation so that people call upon their Lord to lift it from them?

To such a speaker we respond: Did anyone tell you that the lifting of error, forgetfulness, and compulsion was from the very beginning? Perhaps the lifting happened after the Messenger and the earlier believers made their supplication. Since it was "rufiʿa" (with damm on the rāʾ, kasra on the fāʾ, and fatḥa on the ʿayn), this means it existed, so let no one say: "How do you supplicate for something that does not exist?" Or this indicates the utmost purity of faith, that Allah should not be disobeyed except by error or forgetfulness, and that it is neither proper nor fitting that He be disobeyed intentionally; because the one who truly knows the worth of Allah should not disobey Allah except by forgetfulness or error, since the Creator is the Bestower of all blessings, and then He obligated us, and we should not intend disobedience. Therefore the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, named what happened from Adam a disobedience, even though He says:

﴿And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found in him no determination﴾ [20:115].

And Allah called forgetting in the story of Adam a disobedience: (And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred) [20:121]. Thus forgetting was first a disobedience, but Allah honored the nation of Muhammad and lifted forgetting from it. And in the matter of Adam there is a point that the believer must pay attention to: Adam was created by the hand of Allah, while we are created through the law of procreation; Adam received the obligation directly from Allah, not through a messenger, and was obligated with one matter only, which was not to eat from the tree.

So if Adam was created directly by Allah and obligated directly by Allah, and was not obligated except with one matter, which was not to approach this tree, and there were not many obligations, then what did he forget, and what did he remember? It is disobedience, then. Forgetting was disobedience for Adam because he was created by the hand of Allah.

﴿He said: "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to what I created with My two hands?"﴾ [38:75].

Therefore it was not fitting that he forget this single obligation, nor was it proper for him to forget. Perhaps our master Adam was made to forget for a wisdom known to Allah, perhaps so that he would populate the earth in which Allah made him a successor; but as for the nation of Muhammad, when we say: (Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err), it is as though we say, O Lord, we esteem You with the esteem You deserve, and we do not dare to disobey You deliberately, and if we disobey, the disobedience is only forgetting or error, and this is recognition of the worth of the Truth, glorified is He.

But what is forgetting? And what is error?

First, there is (akhṭa'a) and there is (khaṭi'a), and (al-khiṭʾ) is only sin, because it is deliberately doing what should not be done. You know a rule and you err, whereas one who erred may not know the rule, so you correct his error because he has deviated from the correct. An example: when you learn in school that the subject is marfūʿ and the object is manṣūb, and in the middle of the year they correct the rule for you until it settles in your mind; but in exam days, does the teacher correct you or hold you accountable? He holds you accountable, because you studied this rule all year. So there is khaṭi'a and there is akhṭa'a; one who errs once does so unintentionally, because there is no rule I violated, or I did not know the rule but spoke in error, because they did not tell me, or they told me once and I did not remember—that is, the matter has not settled as a faculty in my soul. For the pupil errs regarding subject and object for a long time, and after that he matures and language becomes a faculty in him, provided he is persistent in maintaining it.

At first the pupil would say: "Qaṭaʿa Muḥammadun al-ghuṣn" (Muhammad cut the branch), without vowelling it, but would pause on the final consonant of his pronunciation of the name Muhammad; and when he remembers the rule he says "Muḥammadu" with raf', and "al-ghuṣna" with naṣb, why? Because three rules come to his mind: this is a subject, and the subject's ruling is raf', so it is marfūʿ; he passes through a rational process, but after passing through it he reads it correctly, and may not even recall the rule, because the matter has become a linguistic faculty in him. This linguistic faculty is what we call "automatic."

An example is the boy learning sewing: look how much time passes until he learns how to hold the thread so as to pass it through the eye of the needle, and his teacher may hit him more than once so that he learns it; the thread-end bends because it is long, so he shortens it, then it does not enter the eye, so he twists it so it enters; he takes a long time, then makes the stitch and it comes out irregular, and after that he continues for a while, then he performs all these actions spontaneously while talking with others, because these actions have become an innate faculty, that is, a mechanical act.

Training in mental work according to specific rules, like learning language, we call a faculty; while training in the work of the limbs—such as threading the needle—we call automatism.
